retrieved_context.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
retrieved_context.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
retrieved_context.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

hits.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
hits.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since late 2021, Russia’s GRU-aligned Sandworm APT (Seashell Blizzard) has deployed an initial-access subgroup dubbed BadPilot to stealthily breach high-value telecom, oil and gas, shipping, arms-manufacturing and government networks worldwide by exploiting critical CVSS 9.8 vulnerabilities—Zimbra CVE-2022-41352, Exchange CVE-2021-34473 and Outlook CVE-2023-23397—and, from early 2024, remote-monitoring-and-management flaws such as Fortinet FortiClient EMS CVE-2023-48788 and ScreenConnect CVE-2024-1709 (CVSS 10.0). Following initial access, BadPilot establishes persistence via its custom LocalOlive web shell or legitimate RMM tools (“ShadowLink”) configured as Tor hidden services, harvests credentials, performs lateral movement, exfiltrates data and stages follow-on operations. These agile, low-noise TTPs have underpinned Sandworm’s high-impact campaigns—from NotPetya and 2018 Olympic disruptions to multiple destructive power-grid outages in Ukraine and an attack on Denmark’s energy sector—advancing Russia’s strategic objectives. Critical organizations must therefore enforce timely patching of Internet-facing services, continuous asset monitoring and robust defense-in-depth controls.
hits.title: Microsoft: Russia's Sandworm APT Exploits Edge Bugs Globally

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: Symantec has warned that extortion actors, notably the Clop ransomware operation (aka Snakefly/TA505/FIN11), have been exploiting a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability in the MOVEit Transfer web application (CVE-2023-34362) since May 27, 2023, enabling supply-chain attacks across multiple organizations; although first patched on May 31, additional vulnerabilities (CVEs pending) were disclosed on June 9. Attackers deploy a bespoke web shell, Lemurloot (detected as JS.Malscript!g1, Trojan.Gen.2, WS.Malware), to authenticate via hard-coded credentials, execute SQL statements to alter or delete database elements, exfiltrate records and Azure settings, and manipulate user accounts. With proof-of-concept code now public, secondary threat actors face elevated risk of exploitation and data theft. Clop has since threatened data leaks unless ransoms are paid, reflecting its shift from encryption to extortion. Symantec mitigations include file-based and ML detections, network-based attack signatures, and Data Center Security policy controls that harden MS SQL, IIS and sandbox environments to prevent web-shell deployment and unauthorized software execution.
hits.title: MOVEit Vulnerabilities: What You Need to Know | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Since at least 2020, Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a novel GRU-affiliated Russian group—now named Cadet Blizzard (formerly DEV-0586)—that has executed destructive cyber campaigns against government, law enforcement, NGO and IT service providers primarily in Ukraine, Europe and Latin America, peaking January–June 2022 with the WhisperGate MBR-wiper and website defacements, then re-emerging in January 2023 to renew hack-and-leak operations under the “Free Civilian” forum; Cadet Blizzard leverages exploitation of perimeter web servers (notably CVE-2021-26084 Confluence, Exchange CVE-2022-41040/ProxyShell), living-off-the-land tactics for lateral movement (Impacket modules, PowerShell get-volume, reg save), credential harvesting via renamed procdump64 dumps of LSASS, persistence with commodity and custom web shells (P0wnyshell, reGeorg, PAS variants), and socket-based tunneling tools (NetCat, GOST) often via scheduled tasks; operational mistakes have limited scale compared to Forest or Seashell Blizzard yet still risk significant network disruption, data exfiltration and strategic intelligence leakage; defenders should prioritize patching exposed web services, monitor for known IoCs and anomalous web-shell activity, LSASS and registry dumps, unusual scheduled tasks or renamed tunneling binaries, and collaborate with CERT-UA and global partners for timely threat intelligence sharing and incident response.
hits.title: Cadet Blizzard emerges as a novel and distinct Russian threat actor | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: In Q1 2023, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) found that over 60 percent of Russian state-backed phishing campaigns were aimed at Ukraine, led by FROZENBARENTS (aka Sandworm, GRU Unit 74455), which abused globally compromised EXIM mail servers, SMS-delivered phishing links and fake Windows update payloads deploying the Rhadamanthys stealer, then maintained persistence via webshells and Adminer to exfiltrate data to the CyberArmyofRussia_Reborn Telegram channel across government, defense, energy (notably the Caspian Pipeline Consortium), transport, education and humanitarian sectors while conducting information operations. Simultaneously, FROZENLAKE (APT28) leveraged reflected XSS on Ukrainian government sites to redirect users to phishing domains hosted on free services, with harvested credentials sent to compromised Ubiquiti devices; Belarusian PUSHCHA continued targeted low-volume campaigns against regional webmail providers; and IRA-linked actors deployed coordinated YouTube Shorts and Blogger posts to amplify pro-Wagner, anti-Ukrainian narratives. Financially motivated Cuba ransomware affiliates pivoted to intelligence collection using RomCom malware via ChatGPT/OpenAI-spoofed domains against conference attendees. TAG’s takedowns and Safe Browsing protections, coupled with targeted Gmail alerts, underscore the need for organizations to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, patch mail servers, monitor for unauthorized EXIM access, and guard against reflected XSS and SMS phishing.
hits.title: Ukraine remains Russia’s biggest cyber focus in 2023

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Google has released Chrome 120.0.6099.129/130 updates to patch an actively exploited high-severity zero-day (CVE-2023-7024), a heap-based buffer overflow in the WebRTC framework that enables crashes or arbitrary code execution, discovered by TAG researchers Clément Lecigne and Vlad Stolyarov on December 19, 2023. This marks the eighth Chrome zero-day exploited in the wild this year—following type confusion flaws in V8 (CVE-2023-2033, CVSS 8.8; CVE-2023-2136, CVSS 9.6; CVE-2023-3079, CVSS 8.8; CVE-2023-4762, CVSS 8.8), a heap overflow in WebP (CVE-2023-4863, CVSS 8.8), a heap overflow in libvpx (CVE-2023-5217, CVSS 8.8) and an integer overflow in Skia (CVE-2023-6345, CVSS 9.6)—amid a record 26,447 CVEs disclosed in 2023, 115 of which have been weaponized by threat actors and ransomware groups using remote code execution, security-feature bypass, buffer manipulation, privilege escalation and input-validation flaws. Given WebRTC’s cross-browser support, impacts on Firefox and Safari remain under assessment. Administrators and end users should immediately upgrade Chrome for Windows, macOS and Linux and apply forthcoming patches for Chromium-based browsers (Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi) to mitigate potential compromise.
hits.title: Urgent: New Chrome Zero-Day Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild - Update ASAP

hits.text: Government-backed actors have rapidly weaponized CVE-2023-38831, a logic flaw in WinRAR versions prior to 6.23 that abuses Windows ShellExecute’s handling of filenames with embedded spaces to trigger default extension resolution and execute unintended “.cmd” or “.bat” payloads; although RARLabs patched the bug in August 2023, public proof-of-concepts surfaced within hours, enabling multiple APTs and financially motivated groups to launch spear-phishing and drive-by campaigns. TAG observed Russian GRU-linked FROZENBARENTS (aka SANDWORM) in September luring energy sector and financial targets with a faux Ukrainian drone-training PDF that dropped a packed Rhadamanthys infostealer, FROZENLAKE (aka APT28) using a free hosting redirect chain and a decoy Razumkov Centre invite to deploy a BAT-delivered reverse SSH shell and IRONJAW PowerShell stealer, and Chinese-linked ISLANDDREAMS (aka APT40) targeting Papua New Guinea via Dropbox-hosted archives that sideload an XOR-encoded DLL to load a Donut-generated BOXRAT backdoor in-memory. These operations underscore the urgency of immediate patch deployment, throttled n-day mitigation, Google Safe Browsing/Gmail defenses, and ongoing monitoring for exploit indicators to prevent credential theft, unauthorized code execution, and persistent C2 channels.
hits.title: Government-backed actors exploiting WinRAR vulnerability

canonical_entities: regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea
hits.text: In early 2018 McAfee Advanced Threat Research uncovered Operation Honeybee, a North Korean–linked campaign—tracked to the persona snoopykiller@mail.ru and control domains navermail.byethost3.com/nihon.byethost11.com—targeting humanitarian aid groups and regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea with malicious Microsoft Word documents named “Honeybee” that exploited politically themed and generic “not compatible” lures to execute VBA macros embedding a custom‐alphabet Base64 payload. Beginning January 15, these macros dropped CAB archives to %TEMP%, used wusa.exe or expand.exe for UAC bypass, then hijacked cliconfg.exe via a malicious NTWDBLIB.dll to install a persistent COMSysApp service loading ipnet.dll from %SystemRoot%\System32. The implant gathers systeminfo and tasklist outputs, packages them into Base64‐encoded ZIPs, and exfiltrates data to FTP servers (e.g., 1113427185.ifastnet.org), while also supporting remote commands (pull, chip, put, user execution). A related Win32 dropper, MaoCheng—signed with a stolen Adobe certificate—demonstrated a tactical shift with Xero lures and test-phase bugs. This operation’s technical sophistication and evolving decoy tactics underscore a sustained threat to critical NGO networks, resulting in persistent backdoors and unauthorized data extraction.
hits.title: McAfee Uncovers Operation Honeybee, a Malicious Campaign Targeting Humanitarian Aid Groups | McAfee Blog

hits.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
hits.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

hits.text: McAfee Mobile Research Team uncovered Xamalicious, a new Android backdoor built with Xamarin that abuses accessibility permissions to harvest device metadata, query a C2 server for a second-stage payload, and dynamically inject an assembly DLL to perform unauthorized ad-clicking, app installs and other financially motivated actions; this threat has been embedded in 25 apps—ranging from horoscope and gaming to utility tools—on Google Play since mid-2020, amassing over 327,000 installations across Brazil, Argentina, the UK, Australia, the US, Mexico and Europe. To evade detection, Xamalicious encrypts all C2 traffic as JWE tokens (RSA-OAEP/128CBC-HS256), self-updates its APK to transform into spyware or a banking trojan, and links back to the Cash Magnet ad-fraud campaign; its use of non-Java frameworks like Xamarin underscores heightened obfuscation. Google Play Protect now blocks or auto-removes infected apps. Separately, a malicious WhatsApp-based phishing campaign in India distributes fake SBI APKs invoking SMS permissions to capture credentials, banking and identity data, then exfiltrates them for unauthorized transactions.
hits.title: New Sneaky Xamalicious Android Malware Hits Over 327,000 Devices

canonical_entities: Western nation’s military mission in Ukraine
hits.text: In February–March 2025, Russia-linked espionage group Shuckworm (aka Gamaredon/Armageddon) targeted a Western nation’s military mission in Ukraine using a multi-stage PowerShell-centric campaign initiated via an infected removable drive and malicious .lnk file. Obfuscated VBScript (~.drv) deployed through mshta.exe and wscript.exe created registry-named payloads: one performing WMI ping checks to mil.gov.ua before resolving dynamic C2 addresses via Teletype, Telegra.ph, t.me, check-host.net and Cloudflare tunnels (e.g., 107.189.19.218), and another altering Explorer registry keys to hide system files and propagate shortcuts across USB and network shares. The attackers then delivered an updated PowerShell infostealer (GammaSteel) alongside reconnaissance scripts that captured screenshots, systeminfo, process lists and host metadata, exfiltrating sensitive documents (*.docx, *.pptx, *.pdf) using PowerShell web requests with certutil-computed MD5 hashes and fallback cURL over Tor to mask origin. This campaign underscores Shuckworm’s shift from VBS to PowerShell, leveraging in-registry script storage and heavy obfuscation to evade detection, with indicators including anomalous UserAssist entries, unusual mshta/wscript invocations and atypical C2 resolution patterns.

hits.text: ESET researchers uncovered the Iran-aligned APT35 (aka Ballistic Bobcat, Charming Kitten, TA453/PHOSPHORUS) deploying a novel Sponsor backdoor across at least 34 opportunistic victims—primarily Israeli organizations in sectors from automotive to telecommunications, plus medical targets in Brazil and the UAE—by scanning for and exploiting Exchange CVE-2021-26855 vulnerabilities since September 2021, wrapping up their CISA AA21-321A/PowerLess campaign before dropping Sponsor via innocuously named batch files that deploy configuration files (config.txt, node.txt) to disk, install a persistent Windows service (“SystemNetwork”/“Update”) when run with an “install” argument, then periodically RC4-decrypt and call back to embedded C2 relays, all while leveraging open-source tooling (Mimikatz, Chisel, GO Simple Tunnel, Plink, RevSocks and Merlin) for lateral movement and data exfiltration; ESET has catalogued five Sponsor versions through June 2022, underscoring Ballistic Bobcat’s modular, short-duration, narrowly targeted “Sponsoring Access” campaign and highlighting the need for Exchange patching, service and file monitoring for batch deployments, and detection of RC4-encrypted config lookups to disrupt ongoing espionage operations.

hits.text: Operation RoundPress, attributed with medium confidence to Russian state-sponsored APT28 (Fancy Bear), has since 2023 exploited stored and reflected XSS flaws in widely used webmail platforms—initially leveraging Roundcube CVE-2020-35730 to inject malicious JavaScript into email bodies, then CVE-2023-43770 and additional n-day vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra in early 2024—to execute upon email open without clicks or redirects. Through spear-phishing emails crafted with timely political or news excerpts, the hidden script auto-fills victim credentials via invisible input fields, scrapes DOM content—including emails, contacts, webmail settings, login history, 2FA tokens and passwords—and exfiltrates data via HTTP POST to hardcoded C2 servers. Targets span high-value government entities in Greece, Ukraine, Serbia and Cameroon, military units in Ukraine and Ecuador, defense contractors in Ukraine, Bulgaria and Romania, and critical infrastructure in Ukraine and Bulgaria. The lack of persistence mechanisms confines execution to session scope but underscores the necessity for timely patching of XSS vulnerabilities, disabling HTML rendering in webmail clients, enforcing strict input sanitization and multifactor authentication, and monitoring anomalous outbound traffic to mitigate credential theft and data exfiltration.
hits.title: Government webmail hacked via XSS bugs in global spy campaign

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
retrieved_context.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Since late 2021, Russia’s GRU-aligned Sandworm APT (Seashell Blizzard) has deployed an initial-access subgroup dubbed BadPilot to stealthily breach high-value telecom, oil and gas, shipping, arms-manufacturing and government networks worldwide by exploiting critical CVSS 9.8 vulnerabilities—Zimbra CVE-2022-41352, Exchange CVE-2021-34473 and Outlook CVE-2023-23397—and, from early 2024, remote-monitoring-and-management flaws such as Fortinet FortiClient EMS CVE-2023-48788 and ScreenConnect CVE-2024-1709 (CVSS 10.0). Following initial access, BadPilot establishes persistence via its custom LocalOlive web shell or legitimate RMM tools (“ShadowLink”) configured as Tor hidden services, harvests credentials, performs lateral movement, exfiltrates data and stages follow-on operations. These agile, low-noise TTPs have underpinned Sandworm’s high-impact campaigns—from NotPetya and 2018 Olympic disruptions to multiple destructive power-grid outages in Ukraine and an attack on Denmark’s energy sector—advancing Russia’s strategic objectives. Critical organizations must therefore enforce timely patching of Internet-facing services, continuous asset monitoring and robust defense-in-depth controls.
retrieved_context.title: Microsoft: Russia's Sandworm APT Exploits Edge Bugs Globally

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: ESET researchers have identified SwiftSlicer, a new Go-written destructive wiper attributed to the Sandworm APT, on a Ukrainian organization’s network on January 25 via malicious Group Policy, indicating full Active Directory compromise; detected as WinGo/KillFiles, SwiftSlicer deletes shadow copies and recursively overwrites files in %CSIDL_SYSTEM%\drivers, %CSIDL_SYSTEM_DRIVE%\Windows\NTDS and other drives with 4,096-byte random blocks before forcing a reboot. This deployment method mirrors earlier HermeticWiper and CaddyWiper attacks—CaddyWiper was used against Ukrinform—and follows a wave of RansomBoggs ransomware linked to Sandworm two months prior. Sandworm’s near-decade track record of disruptive campaigns against Ukrainian critical infrastructure includes BlackEnergy, GreyEnergy, the original Industroyer, and a thwarted Industroyer2 in April, underscoring the imperative to harden Active Directory, monitor Group Policy changes, and maintain secure, offline backups.
retrieved_context.title: SwiftSlicer: New destructive wiper malware strikes Ukraine

retrieved_context.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
retrieved_context.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

retrieved_context.text: McAfee Mobile Research Team uncovered Xamalicious, a new Android backdoor built with Xamarin that abuses accessibility permissions to harvest device metadata, query a C2 server for a second-stage payload, and dynamically inject an assembly DLL to perform unauthorized ad-clicking, app installs and other financially motivated actions; this threat has been embedded in 25 apps—ranging from horoscope and gaming to utility tools—on Google Play since mid-2020, amassing over 327,000 installations across Brazil, Argentina, the UK, Australia, the US, Mexico and Europe. To evade detection, Xamalicious encrypts all C2 traffic as JWE tokens (RSA-OAEP/128CBC-HS256), self-updates its APK to transform into spyware or a banking trojan, and links back to the Cash Magnet ad-fraud campaign; its use of non-Java frameworks like Xamarin underscores heightened obfuscation. Google Play Protect now blocks or auto-removes infected apps. Separately, a malicious WhatsApp-based phishing campaign in India distributes fake SBI APKs invoking SMS permissions to capture credentials, banking and identity data, then exfiltrates them for unauthorized transactions.
retrieved_context.title: New Sneaky Xamalicious Android Malware Hits Over 327,000 Devices

canonical_entities: Western nation’s military mission in Ukraine
retrieved_context.text: In February–March 2025, Russia-linked espionage group Shuckworm (aka Gamaredon/Armageddon) targeted a Western nation’s military mission in Ukraine using a multi-stage PowerShell-centric campaign initiated via an infected removable drive and malicious .lnk file. Obfuscated VBScript (~.drv) deployed through mshta.exe and wscript.exe created registry-named payloads: one performing WMI ping checks to mil.gov.ua before resolving dynamic C2 addresses via Teletype, Telegra.ph, t.me, check-host.net and Cloudflare tunnels (e.g., 107.189.19.218), and another altering Explorer registry keys to hide system files and propagate shortcuts across USB and network shares. The attackers then delivered an updated PowerShell infostealer (GammaSteel) alongside reconnaissance scripts that captured screenshots, systeminfo, process lists and host metadata, exfiltrating sensitive documents (*.docx, *.pptx, *.pdf) using PowerShell web requests with certutil-computed MD5 hashes and fallback cURL over Tor to mask origin. This campaign underscores Shuckworm’s shift from VBS to PowerShell, leveraging in-registry script storage and heavy obfuscation to evade detection, with indicators including anomalous UserAssist entries, unusual mshta/wscript invocations and atypical C2 resolution patterns.
retrieved_context.title: Shuckworm Targets Foreign Military Mission Based in Ukraine | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Unit 42 researchers identified two North Korea–linked campaigns, Contagious Interview (CL-STA-0240) and Wagemole (CL-STA-0241), active since December 2022 and March 2023 respectively, that exploit job-seeking and recruitment processes to compromise targets: Contagious Interview poses as anonymous employers, lures software developers into installing malicious NPM packages hosted on free GitHub repos, and deploys the BeaverTail JavaScript stealer/loader to harvest browser-stored cryptocurrency wallet and credential data before retrieving the cross-platform InvisibleFerret Python backdoor for follow-on intrusion, while Wagemole involves DPRK operators submitting fraudulent resumes and conducting unauthorized remote employment with U.S. and global organizations to facilitate espionage or funnel wages to weapons programs; both campaigns leverage open-source supply-chain tactics, Node.js execution, code obfuscation and minimal detection footprints to enable cryptocurrency theft, staging for additional attacks and sensitive data exfiltration, underscoring the need for rigorous vetting of employers, candidates and development-environment artifacts.
hits.title: Hacking Employers and Seeking Employment: Two Job-Related Campaigns Bear Hallmarks of North Korean Threat Actors

hits.text: Researchers have observed a North Korean “Contagious Interview” campaign leveraging a macOS malware family dubbed Ferret—first documented in December 2023 and again in December 2024/January 2025—to lure targets via fake virtual job‐interview links that prompt installation of shell scripts, persistence agents and a Google Chrome update imposter; these installers drop the BeaverTail JavaScript loader, which in turn deploys the Python backdoor InvisibleFerret to harvest web‐browser credentials and crypto‐wallet data. Variants in the campaign include FROSTYFERRET_UI, FRIENDLYFERRET_SECD, MULTI_FROSTYFERRET_CMDCODES and, as of February 3, the newly revealed under‐the‐radar FlexibleFerret, suggesting DPRK actors are honing evasion and expanding beyond job‐seeker targeting to developers more broadly. Apple’s recent XProtect signature update aims to block known variants, but organizations should urgently apply patches, monitor for anomalous shell script execution, persistence agent installs and spoofed update processes, and inspect network traffic for BeaverTail/InvisibleFerret command-and-control indicators to disrupt this evolving threat.
hits.title: Ferret Malware Added to 'Contagious Interview' Campaign

hits.text: North Korea–linked Contagious Interview actors have deployed three fake cryptocurrency consulting firms—BlockNovas LLC, Angeloper Agency and SoftGlide LLC—to lure candidates with bogus job interviews and video coding assessments, distributing the BeaverTail JavaScript stealer/loader that contacts lianxinxiao[.]com C2 to deliver the InvisibleFerret Python backdoor on Windows, Linux and macOS and, in some chains, the OtterCookie payload; they’ve also leveraged ClickFake Interview video lures to push FROSTYFERRET and GolangGhost, hosted a Hashtopolis password-cracking system on mail.blocknovas[.]com, and run a “Kryptoneer” crypto-wallet connector on attisscmo[.]com. Operating under aliases CL-STA-0240, DeceptiveDevelopment, Famous Chollima and others, the group obfuscated traffic via Astrill VPN, residential proxies and five Russian IP ranges masked by VPN/proxy/RDP layers from Khasan and Khabarovsk, used AI-generated personas across LinkedIn, Facebook, GitHub and more, and even advertised a senior software engineer role targeting Ukrainian professionals in December 2024. Their campaign enabled AnyDesk installation and led to at least one MetaMask compromise in September 2024; on April 23, 2025, the US FBI seized blocknovas.com, highlighting urgent needs to harden remote-hiring vetting, monitor anomalous C2 communications and enforce multi-factor authentication on crypto and recruitment platforms against DPRK’s evolving “Wagemole” salary-siphoning and potential DPRK–Russia infrastructure collaboration.
hits.title: North Korean Hackers Spread Malware via Fake Crypto Firms and Job Interview Lures

canonical_entities: Exfiltration of SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations
hits.text: North Korean state-sponsored APT Slow Pisces (aka Jade Sleet, TraderTraitor, PUKCHONG) is executing a sophisticated three-stage campaign against cryptocurrency developers by posing as recruiters on LinkedIn, distributing benign PDF job descriptions with embedded coding challenges, and redirecting targets to malicious GitHub repositories containing Python and JavaScript code laced with YAML deserialization and EJS escapeFunction backdoors; once activated under specific conditions, these backdoors deploy in-memory RN Loader and RN Stealer payloads to collect system information, establish C2 communications, and exfiltrate SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations with minimal forensic footprint—building on past successes that netted over $1 billion in 2023 and $1.5 billion in 2024—and highlighting the urgent need for enhanced vetting on professional platforms, proactive detection of unsafe deserialization and templating flaws, and memory-based threat monitoring to defend the cryptocurrency sector.
hits.title: Slow Pisces Group Targets Developers Using Coding Challenges Laced with Python Malware

hits.text: Since January 2021, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has tracked a government-backed North Korean campaign that leverages social engineering via X (formerly Twitter) and encrypted messaging apps to befriend security researchers and deliver malicious files containing at least one unpatched 0-day in a popular software package; upon exploitation the custom shellcode performs anti-virtual-machine checks, captures system data and screenshots, and exfiltrates them to C2 infrastructure (e.g., 23.106.215[.]105, www.blgbeach[.]com), with the latest vulnerability reported and patched on September 12, 2023 (see TAG’s published RCA). In parallel, the actors published a seemingly benign Windows tool called GetSymbol on GitHub (https://github.com/dbgsymbol/) that quietly downloads debugging symbols—and arbitrary code—from attacker domains, requiring full OS reinstalls for compromised hosts. TAG has added malicious sites to Safe Browsing, issued government-backed attacker alerts to targeted Gmail and Workspace users, and urges researchers to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, keep software up to date, and verify system integrity after using third-party tools.
hits.title: Active North Korean campaign targeting security researchers

hits.text: ESET researchers have retrospectively identified WinorDLL64.dll—a backdoor payload for the Wslink loader (WinorLoaderDLL64.dll) first uncovered in 2021—that operates as an in-memory server using MemoryModule and is protected by Oreans Code Virtualizer; although the initial compromise vector remains unknown, sparse detections in Central Europe, North America and the Middle East and a South Korean VirusTotal submission triggered YARA alerts based on its unique filename. Communicating over the loader’s established AES-256-CBC encrypted TCP channel, WinorDLL64 implements at least 16 commands—including comprehensive system profiling, secure file exfiltration, overwrite and deletion, process and RDP session management, unrestricted PowerShell execution, directory compression for data theft, and connection latency measurement—facilitating reconnaissance, persistence and lateral movement. Low-confidence attribution to North Korea–aligned Lazarus (HIDDEN COBRA) derives from targeting of South Korean victims, shared VS2010 LTCG build signatures and code/behavior overlap with 2018 GhostSecret (FE887FCAB66D7D7F79F05E0266C0649F0114BA7C) and Bankshot implants; this underscores Lazarus’s organized, modular arsenal and highlights the need to detect anomalous in-memory loaders and encrypted session anomalies.
hits.title: WinorDLL64: A backdoor from the vast Lazarus arsenal?

canonical_entities: registered variables in the Windows Registry
hits.text: In June 2024, HP’s Threat Research team led by Patrick Schlapfer intercepted a low-grade phishing campaign leveraging HTML smuggling via an AES-encrypted HTML attachment containing JavaScript-embedded decryption logic—a novel twist on typical encrypted archives—which, when decrypted, mimicked a legitimate website but dropped a fully commented, French-language VBScript that registered variables in the Windows Registry, staged a JavaScript payload as a scheduled task, and invoked a PowerShell script to deploy the freely available AsyncRAT infostealer. Schlapfer and co-lead Alex Holland’s analysis, including comparison with generative-AI–produced code, concluded the well-structured, human-readable script was likely authored by gen-AI by a low-skill newcomer benefitting from reduced entry barriers, with no obfuscation or complex infrastructure beyond a single C2 server. This first definitive proof of AI-generated malware in the wild underscores the need for defenders to adapt detection strategies to AI-crafted droppers, monitor anomalous AES-in-JavaScript decryption patterns, and anticipate more sophisticated AI-generated payloads poised to emerge within the next two years, thereby heightening the risk to network and endpoint security.
hits.title: AI-Generated Malware Found in the Wild - SecurityWeek

retrieved_context.text: North Korean state-sponsored APT Slow Pisces (aka Jade Sleet, TraderTraitor, PUKCHONG) is executing a sophisticated three-stage campaign against cryptocurrency developers by posing as recruiters on LinkedIn, distributing benign PDF job descriptions with embedded coding challenges, and redirecting targets to malicious GitHub repositories containing Python and JavaScript code laced with YAML deserialization and EJS escapeFunction backdoors; once activated under specific conditions, these backdoors deploy in-memory RN Loader and RN Stealer payloads to collect system information, establish C2 communications, and exfiltrate SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations with minimal forensic footprint—building on past successes that netted over $1 billion in 2023 and $1.5 billion in 2024—and highlighting the urgent need for enhanced vetting on professional platforms, proactive detection of unsafe deserialization and templating flaws, and memory-based threat monitoring to defend the cryptocurrency sector.
retrieved_context.title: Slow Pisces Group Targets Developers Using Coding Challenges Laced with Python Malware

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

retrieved_context.text: Since January 2021, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has tracked a government-backed North Korean campaign that leverages social engineering via X (formerly Twitter) and encrypted messaging apps to befriend security researchers and deliver malicious files containing at least one unpatched 0-day in a popular software package; upon exploitation the custom shellcode performs anti-virtual-machine checks, captures system data and screenshots, and exfiltrates them to C2 infrastructure (e.g., 23.106.215[.]105, www.blgbeach[.]com), with the latest vulnerability reported and patched on September 12, 2023 (see TAG’s published RCA). In parallel, the actors published a seemingly benign Windows tool called GetSymbol on GitHub (https://github.com/dbgsymbol/) that quietly downloads debugging symbols—and arbitrary code—from attacker domains, requiring full OS reinstalls for compromised hosts. TAG has added malicious sites to Safe Browsing, issued government-backed attacker alerts to targeted Gmail and Workspace users, and urges researchers to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, keep software up to date, and verify system integrity after using third-party tools.
retrieved_context.title: Active North Korean campaign targeting security researchers

retrieved_context.text: ESET researchers have retrospectively identified WinorDLL64.dll—a backdoor payload for the Wslink loader (WinorLoaderDLL64.dll) first uncovered in 2021—that operates as an in-memory server using MemoryModule and is protected by Oreans Code Virtualizer; although the initial compromise vector remains unknown, sparse detections in Central Europe, North America and the Middle East and a South Korean VirusTotal submission triggered YARA alerts based on its unique filename. Communicating over the loader’s established AES-256-CBC encrypted TCP channel, WinorDLL64 implements at least 16 commands—including comprehensive system profiling, secure file exfiltration, overwrite and deletion, process and RDP session management, unrestricted PowerShell execution, directory compression for data theft, and connection latency measurement—facilitating reconnaissance, persistence and lateral movement. Low-confidence attribution to North Korea–aligned Lazarus (HIDDEN COBRA) derives from targeting of South Korean victims, shared VS2010 LTCG build signatures and code/behavior overlap with 2018 GhostSecret (FE887FCAB66D7D7F79F05E0266C0649F0114BA7C) and Bankshot implants; this underscores Lazarus’s organized, modular arsenal and highlights the need to detect anomalous in-memory loaders and encrypted session anomalies.
retrieved_context.title: WinorDLL64: A backdoor from the vast Lazarus arsenal?

canonical_entities: registered variables in the Windows Registry
retrieved_context.text: In June 2024, HP’s Threat Research team led by Patrick Schlapfer intercepted a low-grade phishing campaign leveraging HTML smuggling via an AES-encrypted HTML attachment containing JavaScript-embedded decryption logic—a novel twist on typical encrypted archives—which, when decrypted, mimicked a legitimate website but dropped a fully commented, French-language VBScript that registered variables in the Windows Registry, staged a JavaScript payload as a scheduled task, and invoked a PowerShell script to deploy the freely available AsyncRAT infostealer. Schlapfer and co-lead Alex Holland’s analysis, including comparison with generative-AI–produced code, concluded the well-structured, human-readable script was likely authored by gen-AI by a low-skill newcomer benefitting from reduced entry barriers, with no obfuscation or complex infrastructure beyond a single C2 server. This first definitive proof of AI-generated malware in the wild underscores the need for defenders to adapt detection strategies to AI-crafted droppers, monitor anomalous AES-in-JavaScript decryption patterns, and anticipate more sophisticated AI-generated payloads poised to emerge within the next two years, thereby heightening the risk to network and endpoint security.
retrieved_context.title: AI-Generated Malware Found in the Wild - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: McAfee Mobile Research Team uncovered Xamalicious, a new Android backdoor built with Xamarin that abuses accessibility permissions to harvest device metadata, query a C2 server for a second-stage payload, and dynamically inject an assembly DLL to perform unauthorized ad-clicking, app installs and other financially motivated actions; this threat has been embedded in 25 apps—ranging from horoscope and gaming to utility tools—on Google Play since mid-2020, amassing over 327,000 installations across Brazil, Argentina, the UK, Australia, the US, Mexico and Europe. To evade detection, Xamalicious encrypts all C2 traffic as JWE tokens (RSA-OAEP/128CBC-HS256), self-updates its APK to transform into spyware or a banking trojan, and links back to the Cash Magnet ad-fraud campaign; its use of non-Java frameworks like Xamarin underscores heightened obfuscation. Google Play Protect now blocks or auto-removes infected apps. Separately, a malicious WhatsApp-based phishing campaign in India distributes fake SBI APKs invoking SMS permissions to capture credentials, banking and identity data, then exfiltrates them for unauthorized transactions.
retrieved_context.title: New Sneaky Xamalicious Android Malware Hits Over 327,000 Devices

hits.text: Researchers have observed a North Korean “Contagious Interview” campaign leveraging a macOS malware family dubbed Ferret—first documented in December 2023 and again in December 2024/January 2025—to lure targets via fake virtual job‐interview links that prompt installation of shell scripts, persistence agents and a Google Chrome update imposter; these installers drop the BeaverTail JavaScript loader, which in turn deploys the Python backdoor InvisibleFerret to harvest web‐browser credentials and crypto‐wallet data. Variants in the campaign include FROSTYFERRET_UI, FRIENDLYFERRET_SECD, MULTI_FROSTYFERRET_CMDCODES and, as of February 3, the newly revealed under‐the‐radar FlexibleFerret, suggesting DPRK actors are honing evasion and expanding beyond job‐seeker targeting to developers more broadly. Apple’s recent XProtect signature update aims to block known variants, but organizations should urgently apply patches, monitor for anomalous shell script execution, persistence agent installs and spoofed update processes, and inspect network traffic for BeaverTail/InvisibleFerret command-and-control indicators to disrupt this evolving threat.
hits.title: Ferret Malware Added to 'Contagious Interview' Campaign

hits.text: North Korea–linked Contagious Interview actors have deployed three fake cryptocurrency consulting firms—BlockNovas LLC, Angeloper Agency and SoftGlide LLC—to lure candidates with bogus job interviews and video coding assessments, distributing the BeaverTail JavaScript stealer/loader that contacts lianxinxiao[.]com C2 to deliver the InvisibleFerret Python backdoor on Windows, Linux and macOS and, in some chains, the OtterCookie payload; they’ve also leveraged ClickFake Interview video lures to push FROSTYFERRET and GolangGhost, hosted a Hashtopolis password-cracking system on mail.blocknovas[.]com, and run a “Kryptoneer” crypto-wallet connector on attisscmo[.]com. Operating under aliases CL-STA-0240, DeceptiveDevelopment, Famous Chollima and others, the group obfuscated traffic via Astrill VPN, residential proxies and five Russian IP ranges masked by VPN/proxy/RDP layers from Khasan and Khabarovsk, used AI-generated personas across LinkedIn, Facebook, GitHub and more, and even advertised a senior software engineer role targeting Ukrainian professionals in December 2024. Their campaign enabled AnyDesk installation and led to at least one MetaMask compromise in September 2024; on April 23, 2025, the US FBI seized blocknovas.com, highlighting urgent needs to harden remote-hiring vetting, monitor anomalous C2 communications and enforce multi-factor authentication on crypto and recruitment platforms against DPRK’s evolving “Wagemole” salary-siphoning and potential DPRK–Russia infrastructure collaboration.
hits.title: North Korean Hackers Spread Malware via Fake Crypto Firms and Job Interview Lures

hits.text: Unit 42 researchers identified two North Korea–linked campaigns, Contagious Interview (CL-STA-0240) and Wagemole (CL-STA-0241), active since December 2022 and March 2023 respectively, that exploit job-seeking and recruitment processes to compromise targets: Contagious Interview poses as anonymous employers, lures software developers into installing malicious NPM packages hosted on free GitHub repos, and deploys the BeaverTail JavaScript stealer/loader to harvest browser-stored cryptocurrency wallet and credential data before retrieving the cross-platform InvisibleFerret Python backdoor for follow-on intrusion, while Wagemole involves DPRK operators submitting fraudulent resumes and conducting unauthorized remote employment with U.S. and global organizations to facilitate espionage or funnel wages to weapons programs; both campaigns leverage open-source supply-chain tactics, Node.js execution, code obfuscation and minimal detection footprints to enable cryptocurrency theft, staging for additional attacks and sensitive data exfiltration, underscoring the need for rigorous vetting of employers, candidates and development-environment artifacts.
hits.title: Hacking Employers and Seeking Employment: Two Job-Related Campaigns Bear Hallmarks of North Korean Threat Actors

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: LNK files in the Windows Startup folder
HTTP POST exfiltration with Base64 encoding
hits.text: Cisco Talos analysts have uncovered PS1Bot, a sophisticated multi‐stage malware framework active throughout 2025 that leverages malvertising campaigns—delivering SEO‐styled ZIPs like “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”—to drop a JavaScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) which retrieves modular PowerShell and C# components in memory via Invoke-Expression, minimizing disk footprint and evading AV. Once executed, PS1Bot establishes persistence by creating randomly named PS1 scripts in %PROGRAMDATA% and corresponding LNK files in the Windows Startup folder that poll a C2 “/transform” endpoint for obfuscated payloads, using the host’s C: drive serial number to generate unique communication URLs. The framework’s on‐demand modules include information stealers, keyloggers, screen capture tools and advanced crypto wallet extractors that scan for seed-phrase wordlists in multiple languages, compress findings and exfiltrate via HTTP POST with Base64 encoding. Continuous sample updates and code overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet‐linked families suggest shared development resources or actor collaboration, highlighting the need for defenses that detect anomalous PowerShell IEX activity, monitor suspicious JavaScript downloaders and Startup LNK creations, and inspect outbound HTTP traffic for drive‐serial based URLs and wallet data exfiltration.
hits.title: Threat Actors Attacking Windows Systems With New Multi-Stage Malware Framework PS1Bot

hits.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
hits.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

hits.text: At least four distinct campaigns exploited CVE-2023-37580, a reflected XSS zero-day in Zimbra Collaboration Suite, to siphon emails, attachments, user credentials and authentication tokens from government organizations worldwide before the July 5 hotfix and July 25 official patch; in chronological order, unidentified actors targeted Greece on June 29 via malicious URLs that, when clicked during active Zimbra sessions, deployed a data-theft framework and auto-forward rules, Winter Vivern’s APT leveraged unique exploit links to hit Moldova and Tunisia between July 11 and 25, another group used a phishing-style XSS link in Vietnam to harvest webmail credentials and exfiltrate them to a compromised government domain, and on August 25 unknown attackers employed an N-day variant to steal tokens from Pakistan’s mail servers; Google’s Threat Analysis Group warns these campaigns underscore the urgency of promptly applying open-source fixes, hardening mail-server code to prevent XSS, and maintaining vigilant patch management as attackers continuously monitor public repositories for unpatched vulnerabilities.
hits.title: APTs Swarm Zimbra Zero-Day to Steal Government Info Worldwide

Apple’s recent XProtect signature update aims to block known variants, but organizations should urgently apply patches, monitor for anomalous shell script execution, persistence agent installs and spoofed update processes, and inspect network traffic for BeaverTail/InvisibleFerret command-and-control indicators to disrupt this evolving threat.
hits.title: Ferret Malware Added to 'Contagious Interview' Campaign

hits.text: North Korea–linked Contagious Interview actors have deployed three fake cryptocurrency consulting firms—BlockNovas LLC, Angeloper Agency and SoftGlide LLC—to lure candidates with bogus job interviews and video coding assessments, distributing the BeaverTail JavaScript stealer/loader that contacts lianxinxiao[.]com C2 to deliver the InvisibleFerret Python backdoor on Windows, Linux and macOS and, in some chains, the OtterCookie payload; they’ve also leveraged ClickFake Interview video lures to push FROSTYFERRET and GolangGhost, hosted a Hashtopolis password-cracking system on mail.blocknovas[.]com, and run a “Kryptoneer” crypto-wallet connector on attisscmo[.]com. Operating under aliases CL-STA-0240, DeceptiveDevelopment, Famous Chollima and others, the group obfuscated traffic via Astrill VPN, residential proxies and five Russian IP ranges masked by VPN/proxy/RDP layers from Khasan and Khabarovsk, used AI-generated personas across LinkedIn, Facebook, GitHub and more, and even advertised a senior software engineer role targeting Ukrainian professionals in December 2024. Their campaign enabled AnyDesk installation and led to at least one MetaMask compromise in September 2024; on April 23, 2025, the US FBI seized blocknovas.com, highlighting urgent needs to harden remote-hiring vetting, monitor anomalous C2 communications and enforce multi-factor authentication on crypto and recruitment platforms against DPRK’s evolving “Wagemole” salary-siphoning and potential DPRK–Russia infrastructure collaboration.
hits.title: North Korean Hackers Spread Malware via Fake Crypto Firms and Job Interview Lures

hits.text: Unit 42 researchers identified two North Korea–linked campaigns, Contagious Interview (CL-STA-0240) and Wagemole (CL-STA-0241), active since December 2022 and March 2023 respectively, that exploit job-seeking and recruitment processes to compromise targets: Contagious Interview poses as anonymous employers, lures software developers into installing malicious NPM packages hosted on free GitHub repos, and deploys the BeaverTail JavaScript stealer/loader to harvest browser-stored cryptocurrency wallet and credential data before retrieving the cross-platform InvisibleFerret Python backdoor for follow-on intrusion, while Wagemole involves DPRK operators submitting fraudulent resumes and conducting unauthorized remote employment with U.S. and global organizations to facilitate espionage or funnel wages to weapons programs; both campaigns leverage open-source supply-chain tactics, Node.js execution, code obfuscation and minimal detection footprints to enable cryptocurrency theft, staging for additional attacks and sensitive data exfiltration, underscoring the need for rigorous vetting of employers, candidates and development-environment artifacts.
hits.title: Hacking Employers and Seeking Employment: Two Job-Related Campaigns Bear Hallmarks of North Korean Threat Actors

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: In May 2023, after U.S. authorities secured convictions against three high-level operators and declared the Russia-based cybercrime enterprise Fin7 “no more,” security experts began spotting first signs of its resurrection in April 2024 when Blackberry reported a typosquatting-based malware intrusion against a major automotive firm; since January 2024, Silent Push analyst Zach Edwards has mapped over 4,000 Fin7-linked hosts—rented largely on the pro-Russia Stark Industries Solutions platform—employing typosquatting, booby-trapped ads, malicious browser extensions and spear-phishing domains to mimic hundreds of brands from American Express and Microsoft 365 to CNN and Zoom, as well as popular free software tools such as 7-zip, PuTTY and Python, all “aged” on innocuous templates for six to nine months before weaponization; eSentire and Malwarebytes also observed sponsored Google ads pushing phony extensions in May and April 2024, and Fin7 has even deployed domains targeting Louvre and Olympic tourists, building on its 2013–present campaign that has extorted some $3 billion from victim organizations, underscoring the urgent need for renewed law enforcement focus and proactive domain-monitoring defenses.
hits.title: The Stark Truth Behind the Resurgence of Russia’s Fin7 – Krebs on Security

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: North Korean APT Lazarus has launched “Operation In(ter)ception,” a macOS-focused cyberespionage campaign that lures engineering professionals with a fake Coinbase job posting and deploys a signed universal macOS executable (Intel and Apple Silicon) that drops three components—a decoy PDF (Coinbase_online_careers_2022_07.pdf), a FinderFontsUpdater.app bundle and a downloader named safarifontagent—before phoning home to a new, currently nonresponsive C2 at concrecapital[.]com/%user%.jpg. Identified by ESET in late July and using a February-2022 developer certificate for “Shankey Nohria” revoked by Apple on August 12, the malware mirrors a May sample but introduces fresh C2 infrastructure and was first uploaded from Brazil. A companion Windows variant, spotted by Malwarebytes on August 4, follows the same decoy routine. This marks another evolution in Lazarus’s longstanding impersonation tactics—previously targeting engineers via spear-phishing and defense-sector ruses—while the group simultaneously diversifies into cryptocurrency heists (prompting Tornado Cash sanctions) and VHD ransomware operations to fund the North Korean regime.
hits.title: APT Lazarus Targets Engineers with macOS Malware | Threatpost

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since January 2021, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has tracked a government-backed North Korean campaign that leverages social engineering via X (formerly Twitter) and encrypted messaging apps to befriend security researchers and deliver malicious files containing at least one unpatched 0-day in a popular software package; upon exploitation the custom shellcode performs anti-virtual-machine checks, captures system data and screenshots, and exfiltrates them to C2 infrastructure (e.g., 23.106.215[.]105, www.blgbeach[.]com), with the latest vulnerability reported and patched on September 12, 2023 (see TAG’s published RCA). In parallel, the actors published a seemingly benign Windows tool called GetSymbol on GitHub (https://github.com/dbgsymbol/) that quietly downloads debugging symbols—and arbitrary code—from attacker domains, requiring full OS reinstalls for compromised hosts. TAG has added malicious sites to Safe Browsing, issued government-backed attacker alerts to targeted Gmail and Workspace users, and urges researchers to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, keep software up to date, and verify system integrity after using third-party tools.
hits.title: Active North Korean campaign targeting security researchers

hits.text: ESET researchers have retrospectively identified WinorDLL64.dll—a backdoor payload for the Wslink loader (WinorLoaderDLL64.dll) first uncovered in 2021—that operates as an in-memory server using MemoryModule and is protected by Oreans Code Virtualizer; although the initial compromise vector remains unknown, sparse detections in Central Europe, North America and the Middle East and a South Korean VirusTotal submission triggered YARA alerts based on its unique filename. Communicating over the loader’s established AES-256-CBC encrypted TCP channel, WinorDLL64 implements at least 16 commands—including comprehensive system profiling, secure file exfiltration, overwrite and deletion, process and RDP session management, unrestricted PowerShell execution, directory compression for data theft, and connection latency measurement—facilitating reconnaissance, persistence and lateral movement. Low-confidence attribution to North Korea–aligned Lazarus (HIDDEN COBRA) derives from targeting of South Korean victims, shared VS2010 LTCG build signatures and code/behavior overlap with 2018 GhostSecret (FE887FCAB66D7D7F79F05E0266C0649F0114BA7C) and Bankshot implants; this underscores Lazarus’s organized, modular arsenal and highlights the need to detect anomalous in-memory loaders and encrypted session anomalies.
hits.title: WinorDLL64: A backdoor from the vast Lazarus arsenal?
