hits.text: Following the sale of INC ransomware source code in March 2024 and its initial appearance in August 2023, researchers in July 2024 uncovered Lynx ransomware, a Windows-only, C++-based RaaS variant that shares ~48% of INC’s functions (70.8% among common routines) and has been deployed against U.S. and U.K. retail, real estate, architecture, financial and environmental service firms via phishing, malicious downloads and underground forums; employing AES-128-CTR and Curve25519 Donna for encryption with a .lynx extension, it conducts double-extortion by exfiltrating victims’ data (published on lynxblog[.]net under a policy excluding governments, hospitals and non-profits) before encrypting all files by default—killing processes, encrypting network shares and hidden disks, deleting shadow copies and backups, leveraging the Restart Manager API to target in-use files, and printing a OneNote report—then dropping a README.txt ransom note; this evolution of RaaS underscores the need for organizations to adopt robust cybersecurity measures, including anti-phishing training, backup hardening, dynamic and behavioral detections via Palo Alto Networks’ Cortex XDR Anti-Ransomware and Advanced WildFire, and vigilant monitoring of Indicators of Compromise such as published SHA256 hashes to mitigate high-profile, code-reused ransomware campaigns.
hits.title: Lynx Ransomware: A Rebranding of INC Ransomware

hits.text: Since at least September 2023, the China-aligned Evasive Panda APT (aka BRONZE HIGHLAND/Daggerfly) has conducted a dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora by compromising both the Kagyu International Monlam Trust’s website and the official Monlam translation-software supply chain—first implanting obfuscated JavaScript into jquery.js on the festival site that verifies victims’ first three IP octets via an MD5 hash salted with “1qaz0okm!@#,” serves a faux “Aw, Snap!” error page to users in India, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Australia and the U.S., and lures them to download a malicious “certificate.exe” or “.pkg” downloader; that loader side-loads memmgrset.dll (http_dy.dll) to fetch a JSON config from update.devicebug[.]com and ultimately deploys the undocumented Nightdoor backdoor alongside the group’s modular MgBot implant, while a trojanized Monlam software installer (Windows autorun.exe abusing MonlamUpdate.exe for DLL side-loading of RPHost.dll, and macOS Mach-O downloaders) has delivered further downloaders and payloads—retrieved from tibetpost[.]net and a direct IP—to %TEMP%\default_ico.exe for additional Nightdoor and MgBot installation.
hits.title: Evasive Panda leverages Monlam Festival to target Tibetans

hits.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
hits.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: Exfiltration of SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations
hits.text: North Korean state-sponsored APT Slow Pisces (aka Jade Sleet, TraderTraitor, PUKCHONG) is executing a sophisticated three-stage campaign against cryptocurrency developers by posing as recruiters on LinkedIn, distributing benign PDF job descriptions with embedded coding challenges, and redirecting targets to malicious GitHub repositories containing Python and JavaScript code laced with YAML deserialization and EJS escapeFunction backdoors; once activated under specific conditions, these backdoors deploy in-memory RN Loader and RN Stealer payloads to collect system information, establish C2 communications, and exfiltrate SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations with minimal forensic footprint—building on past successes that netted over $1 billion in 2023 and $1.5 billion in 2024—and highlighting the urgent need for enhanced vetting on professional platforms, proactive detection of unsafe deserialization and templating flaws, and memory-based threat monitoring to defend the cryptocurrency sector.
hits.title: Slow Pisces Group Targets Developers Using Coding Challenges Laced with Python Malware

retrieved_context.text: McAfee’s Advanced Threat Research team uncovered “Operation Sharpshooter,” a global cyber-espionage campaign targeting nuclear, defense, energy and financial organizations via weaponized Office documents masquerading as recruitment materials; an initial macro‐enabled loader drops an in‐memory implant that retrieves a second‐stage backdoor dubbed “Rising Sun,” which leverages source code from Lazarus Group’s 2015 Duuzer Trojan to perform account, file/directory, process and system/network discovery, process injection and automated encrypted exfiltration over C2 channels (e.g., 34.214.99.20/view_style.php); from October to November 2018 McAfee telemetry identified at least 87 predominantly English-speaking targets, with key IOCs including hashes such as 8106a30bd35526bded384627d8eebce15da35d17 and document URLs like hxxp://208.117.44.112/Strategic Planning Manager.doc, detectable by McAfee signatures RDN/Generic Downloader.x and Rising-Sun, and mitigated by monitoring macro executions, anomalous process injections and outbound C2 traffic while the broader community assesses attribution and monitors for follow-on exploitation.
retrieved_context.title: ‘Operation Sharpshooter’ Targets Global Defense, Critical Infrastructure | McAfee Blog

retrieved_context.text: ESET researchers have traced the China-aligned hacker group FishMonger, aka Aquatic Panda, and its global espionage campaign “FishMedley” back to the iSoon APT contractor (Axun Information Technology) operating under the Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security and PLA, following the U.S. DOJ’s addition of key members to the FBI’s Most Wanted list; FishMonger’s modus operandi relies on compromising high-privilege user accounts—likely harvested via phishing or credential theft—to gain domain administrator access, then deploying publicly available modular backdoors and loaders (ShadowPad, Spyder loader, SodaMaster) and the RPipeCommander reverse shell rather than zero-day exploits, enabling sustained infiltration of governmental bodies, Catholic charities, NGOs and think tanks across Taiwan, Hungary, Turkey, Thailand, the U.S. and France; while technically unsophisticated, the group’s efficient use of known tools has yielded consistent exfiltration of confidential data, underscoring the need for potential targets to hunt for these specific indicators of compromise and strengthen monitoring of privileged accounts.
retrieved_context.title: Chinese Hacker Group Tracked Back to iSoon APT Operation

retrieved_context.text: Moses Staff, an Iran-linked APT active since September 2021, has conducted politically motivated sabotage campaigns—initially against Israeli organizations and later targets in India, Germany, the U.S., Italy, Chile, Turkey and the UAE—by exploiting known public-facing server vulnerabilities (e.g., Microsoft Exchange), moving laterally with PsExec, WMIC and PowerShell, and deploying a two-stage destructive toolkit: a Python-based loader (PyDCrypt) that installs a custom DiskCryptor variant (DCSrv) to encrypt files and disrupt operations without ransom demands, and, as newly documented by Cybereason, the StrifeWater RAT masquerading as calc.exe to establish early footholds, harvest system metadata (machine name, OS version, CPU architecture, user privileges, time zone), execute commands, capture screens, maintain persistence via scheduled tasks, and download auxiliary modules before self-removal—all while communicating with hard-coded C2 IPs, URLs and domain names—to evade detection; organizations should urgently patch exposed servers, monitor anomalous calc.exe and scheduled-task activity, and enhance EDR rules to detect PyDCrypt, DCSrv and StrifeWater behaviors to thwart data exfiltration and infrastructure damage.
retrieved_context.title: Iranian APT group uses previously undocumented Trojan for destructive access to organizations

retrieved_context.text: In August, the DPRK–linked APT TA444 (aka APT38, BlueNoroff, BlackAlicanto, Coperenicum, Sapphire Sleet and Stardust Chollima) deployed SpectralBlur, a custom post-exploitation macOS backdoor that leverages command-and-control instructions to upload/download files, spawn a shell, update its configuration, delete files or enter hibernation/sleep mode; Proofpoint researcher Greg Lesnewich identified code overlaps with the KandyKorn macOS data stealer—earlier tied to Lazarus Group phishing campaigns against blockchain engineers—linking both tools through shared strings and infrastructure. This rapid iteration of proprietary macOS malware underscores TA444’s dedicated development capability and signals an intensified DPRK espionage focus on Apple users, particularly within the cryptocurrency sector, demonstrating persistent operational tempo and advanced post-exploitation tactics.
retrieved_context.title: North Korea Debuts 'SpectralBlur' Malware Amid macOS Onslaught

canonical_entities: Palo Alto Networks Cortex XDR Anti-Ransomware
retrieved_context.text: Following the sale of INC ransomware source code in March 2024 and its initial appearance in August 2023, researchers in July 2024 uncovered Lynx ransomware, a Windows-only, C++-based RaaS variant that shares ~48% of INC’s functions (70.8% among common routines) and has been deployed against U.S. and U.K. retail, real estate, architecture, financial and environmental service firms via phishing, malicious downloads and underground forums; employing AES-128-CTR and Curve25519 Donna for encryption with a .lynx extension, it conducts double-extortion by exfiltrating victims’ data (published on lynxblog[.]net under a policy excluding governments, hospitals and non-profits) before encrypting all files by default—killing processes, encrypting network shares and hidden disks, deleting shadow copies and backups, leveraging the Restart Manager API to target in-use files, and printing a OneNote report—then dropping a README.txt ransom note; this evolution of RaaS underscores the need for organizations to adopt robust cybersecurity measures, including anti-phishing training, backup hardening, dynamic and behavioral detections via Palo Alto Networks’ Cortex XDR Anti-Ransomware and Advanced WildFire, and vigilant monitoring of Indicators of Compromise such as published SHA256 hashes to mitigate high-profile, code-reused ransomware campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Lynx Ransomware: A Rebranding of INC Ransomware

retrieved_context.text: Since its emergence in 2013, Iran-linked APT35 (aka Charming Kitten/Phosphorus) has executed a series of high-value espionage campaigns—beginning with a 2014 social-media spying operation—and continued in 2019 with spear-phishing against U.S., French and Middle East academic institutions before Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit seized control of 99 APT35 domains; in late 2020 the group targeted oncology, genetics and neurology researchers in Israel and the U.S. via its “BadBlood” PDF-based spear-phishing campaign, while in 2021 it chained Exchange Server flaws (ProxyShell) for network intrusion and demonstrated TTP overlaps with Momento ransomware (CVE-2021-21972 exploiter); in January 2022 it performed mass Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) scans—over 80 percent of attempts originated in the U.S.—and later deployed a stealthy .NET-based PowerShell backdoor (“PowerLess”) that runs in-process to avoid detection, followed by Hyperscrape, a Windows .NET mailbox exfiltration tool for Outlook, Gmail and Yahoo! that quietly harvests emails once the actor possesses valid credentials or session cookies, and a companion Telegram dump utility; APT35 maintains persistence for intelligence collection or monetizes access when systems lack strategic value, underscoring the need for timely patching, multi-factor authentication and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: An In-Depth Look at APT35 aka Charming Kitten

canonical_entities: dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora
retrieved_context.text: Since at least September 2023, the China-aligned Evasive Panda APT (aka BRONZE HIGHLAND/Daggerfly) has conducted a dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora by compromising both the Kagyu International Monlam Trust’s website and the official Monlam translation-software supply chain—first implanting obfuscated JavaScript into jquery.js on the festival site that verifies victims’ first three IP octets via an MD5 hash salted with “1qaz0okm!@#,” serves a faux “Aw, Snap!” error page to users in India, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Australia and the U.S., and lures them to download a malicious “certificate.exe” or “.pkg” downloader; that loader side-loads memmgrset.dll (http_dy.dll) to fetch a JSON config from update.devicebug[.]com and ultimately deploys the undocumented Nightdoor backdoor alongside the group’s modular MgBot implant, while a trojanized Monlam software installer (Windows autorun.exe abusing MonlamUpdate.exe for DLL side-loading of RPHost.dll, and macOS Mach-O downloaders) has delivered further downloaders and payloads—retrieved from tibetpost[.]net and a direct IP—to %TEMP%\default_ico.exe for additional Nightdoor and MgBot installation.
retrieved_context.title: Evasive Panda leverages Monlam Festival to target Tibetans

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
retrieved_context.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: Exfiltration of SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations
retrieved_context.text: North Korean state-sponsored APT Slow Pisces (aka Jade Sleet, TraderTraitor, PUKCHONG) is executing a sophisticated three-stage campaign against cryptocurrency developers by posing as recruiters on LinkedIn, distributing benign PDF job descriptions with embedded coding challenges, and redirecting targets to malicious GitHub repositories containing Python and JavaScript code laced with YAML deserialization and EJS escapeFunction backdoors; once activated under specific conditions, these backdoors deploy in-memory RN Loader and RN Stealer payloads to collect system information, establish C2 communications, and exfiltrate SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations with minimal forensic footprint—building on past successes that netted over $1 billion in 2023 and $1.5 billion in 2024—and highlighting the urgent need for enhanced vetting on professional platforms, proactive detection of unsafe deserialization and templating flaws, and memory-based threat monitoring to defend the cryptocurrency sector.
retrieved_context.title: Slow Pisces Group Targets Developers Using Coding Challenges Laced with Python Malware

hits.text: Security researchers at McAfee first observed Operation Sharpshooter in October–November 2018, a sophisticated phishing campaign targeting 87 critical‐infrastructure organizations—predominantly in the United States—including nuclear, defense, energy and financial firms, via recruitment‐style Microsoft Word attachments containing weaponized macros that load an in‐memory downloader to fetch a second‐stage implant dubbed Rising Sun; this implant, which exfiltrates host data to a command server, incorporates publicly available Lazarus Group source code as a likely false flag rather than evidence of Lazarus involvement. canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has uncovered a supply chain attack by the North Korean group Diamond Sleet in which a legitimate CyberLink Corp. multimedia installer was trojanized—tracked as LambLoad (SHA-256 166d1a6ddcde4e859a89c2c825cd3c8c953a86bfa92b343de7e5bfbfb5afb8be) and signed with a valid CyberLink code-signing certificate—and hosted on CyberLink’s own update infrastructure; the loader enforces a narrow execution window, checks for EDR processes (CrowdStrike’s csfalconservice.exe, FireEye’s xagt.exe, Tanium’s taniumclient.exe) to evade detection, then downloads, decrypts, and in-memory loads a second-stage payload masquerading as a PNG file (SHA-256 089573b3a1167f387dcdad5e014a5132e998b2c89bff29bcf8b06dd497d4e63d; decrypted PE 915c2495e03ff7408f11a2a197f23344004c533ff87db4b807cc937f80c217a1) from compromised domains before calling back for commands; observed since October 2023 on over 100 devices across Japan, Taiwan, Canada, and the US and targeting IT, defense, and media organizations for espionage and data theft, Microsoft has alerted CyberLink, notified Defender for Endpoint customers, reported the payload to GitHub for takedown, blacklisted the abused certificate, published detections (Trojan:Win32/LambLoad; Diamond Sleet activity group alerts), provided hunting queries and IOCs, and recommended cloud-delivered protection, network protection, automated remediation, attack surface reduction rules, and immediate isolation and credential resets upon compromise.
hits.title: Diamond Sleet supply chain compromise distributes a modified CyberLink installer | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: On December 4 Fortra issued a private advisory on CVE-2024-0204, a critical authentication bypass in its GoAnywhere MFT 7.x, and silently patched it on December 7 in version 7.4.1 but only publicly disclosed the flaw today; now Horizon3’s Attack Team has released a proof-of-concept exploit that leverages a path traversal vulnerability to access the /InitialAccountSetup.xhtml endpoint and create unauthorized administrator accounts on unpatched instances, prompting defenders to immediately upgrade or delete/replace the InitialAccountSetup.xhtml file, restart services, and monitor the GoAnywhere “Admin Users” list for new entries. While Fortra reports no confirmed exploits in the wild, the public PoC is expected to trigger widespread scanning and compromises, echoing Clop’s January 2023 campaign that abused a GoAnywhere RCE (CVE-2023-0669) to breach over 100 organizations—including Community Health Systems, Procter & Gamble, Rubrik and the City of Toronto—and underscoring a broader pattern of MFT platform assaults seen in the 2020 Accellion FTA, 2021 SolarWinds Serv-U and 2023 MOVEit Transfer incidents.
hits.title: Exploit released for Fortra GoAnywhere MFT auth bypass bug

hits.text: Since at least 2015, Mandiant has identified APT42—an IRGC-linked Iranian state-sponsored threat actor also known as APT35—conducting over 30 spear-phishing operations across 14 countries against government officials, policymakers, journalists, academics and dissidents, evolving tactics from 2020 Oxford vaccinologist-themed pharmaceutical lures to 2021 fake interview requests using compromised U.S. media accounts for 37-day MFA-intercepting credential harvesting, and February 2022 phishes posing as a British news agency targeting political science professors; beyond credential theft via shortened URLs and PDF attachments directing victims to spoofed login portals, APT42 deploys custom Android spyware—spread via SMS links to messaging/VPN apps—to exfiltrate calls, SMS, audio recordings, images and GPS data in real time, while on Windows it employs lightweight custom malware for initial access, privilege escalation, reconnaissance, lateral movement through follow-on phishing, and persistence via scheduled tasks and registry keys; Mandiant further correlates APT42’s TTPs with November 2021 PHOSPHORUS BitLocker ransomware attempts against Fortinet FortiOS SSL VPN and unpatched Exchange servers, highlighting the group’s multi-platform espionage-to-ransom capabilities and real-world threat to high-value targets.
hits.title: New Iranian hacking group APT42 deploys custom Android spyware

hits.text: In Q1 2023, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) found that over 60 percent of Russian state-backed phishing campaigns were aimed at Ukraine, led by FROZENBARENTS (aka Sandworm, GRU Unit 74455), which abused globally compromised EXIM mail servers, SMS-delivered phishing links and fake Windows update payloads deploying the Rhadamanthys stealer, then maintained persistence via webshells and Adminer to exfiltrate data to the CyberArmyofRussia_Reborn Telegram channel across government, defense, energy (notably the Caspian Pipeline Consortium), transport, education and humanitarian sectors while conducting information operations. Simultaneously, FROZENLAKE (APT28) leveraged reflected XSS on Ukrainian government sites to redirect users to phishing domains hosted on free services, with harvested credentials sent to compromised Ubiquiti devices; Belarusian PUSHCHA continued targeted low-volume campaigns against regional webmail providers; and IRA-linked actors deployed coordinated YouTube Shorts and Blogger posts to amplify pro-Wagner, anti-Ukrainian narratives. Financially motivated Cuba ransomware affiliates pivoted to intelligence collection using RomCom malware via ChatGPT/OpenAI-spoofed domains against conference attendees. TAG’s takedowns and Safe Browsing protections, coupled with targeted Gmail alerts, underscore the need for organizations to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, patch mail servers, monitor for unauthorized EXIM access, and guard against reflected XSS and SMS phishing.
hits.title: Ukraine remains Russia’s biggest cyber focus in 2023

While Fortra reports no confirmed exploits in the wild, the public PoC is expected to trigger widespread scanning and compromises, echoing Clop’s January 2023 campaign that abused a GoAnywhere RCE (CVE-2023-0669) to breach over 100 organizations—including Community Health Systems, Procter & Gamble, Rubrik and the City of Toronto—and underscoring a broader pattern of MFT platform assaults seen in the 2020 Accellion FTA, 2021 SolarWinds Serv-U and 2023 MOVEit Transfer incidents.
retrieved_context.title: Exploit released for Fortra GoAnywhere MFT auth bypass bug

retrieved_context.text: Since at least 2015, Mandiant has identified APT42—an IRGC-linked Iranian state-sponsored threat actor also known as APT35—conducting over 30 spear-phishing operations across 14 countries against government officials, policymakers, journalists, academics and dissidents, evolving tactics from 2020 Oxford vaccinologist-themed pharmaceutical lures to 2021 fake interview requests using compromised U.S. media accounts for 37-day MFA-intercepting credential harvesting, and February 2022 phishes posing as a British news agency targeting political science professors; beyond credential theft via shortened URLs and PDF attachments directing victims to spoofed login portals, APT42 deploys custom Android spyware—spread via SMS links to messaging/VPN apps—to exfiltrate calls, SMS, audio recordings, images and GPS data in real time, while on Windows it employs lightweight custom malware for initial access, privilege escalation, reconnaissance, lateral movement through follow-on phishing, and persistence via scheduled tasks and registry keys; Mandiant further correlates APT42’s TTPs with November 2021 PHOSPHORUS BitLocker ransomware attempts against Fortinet FortiOS SSL VPN and unpatched Exchange servers, highlighting the group’s multi-platform espionage-to-ransom capabilities and real-world threat to high-value targets.
retrieved_context.title: New Iranian hacking group APT42 deploys custom Android spyware

retrieved_context.text: In Q1 2023, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) found that over 60 percent of Russian state-backed phishing campaigns were aimed at Ukraine, led by FROZENBARENTS (aka Sandworm, GRU Unit 74455), which abused globally compromised EXIM mail servers, SMS-delivered phishing links and fake Windows update payloads deploying the Rhadamanthys stealer, then maintained persistence via webshells and Adminer to exfiltrate data to the CyberArmyofRussia_Reborn Telegram channel across government, defense, energy (notably the Caspian Pipeline Consortium), transport, education and humanitarian sectors while conducting information operations. Simultaneously, FROZENLAKE (APT28) leveraged reflected XSS on Ukrainian government sites to redirect users to phishing domains hosted on free services, with harvested credentials sent to compromised Ubiquiti devices; Belarusian PUSHCHA continued targeted low-volume campaigns against regional webmail providers; and IRA-linked actors deployed coordinated YouTube Shorts and Blogger posts to amplify pro-Wagner, anti-Ukrainian narratives. Financially motivated Cuba ransomware affiliates pivoted to intelligence collection using RomCom malware via ChatGPT/OpenAI-spoofed domains against conference attendees. TAG’s takedowns and Safe Browsing protections, coupled with targeted Gmail alerts, underscore the need for organizations to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, patch mail servers, monitor for unauthorized EXIM access, and guard against reflected XSS and SMS phishing.
retrieved_context.title: Ukraine remains Russia’s biggest cyber focus in 2023

hits.text: Security researchers at McAfee first observed Operation Sharpshooter in October–November 2018, a sophisticated phishing campaign targeting 87 critical‐infrastructure organizations—predominantly in the United States—including nuclear, defense, energy and financial firms, via recruitment‐style Microsoft Word attachments containing weaponized macros that load an in‐memory downloader to fetch a second‐stage implant dubbed Rising Sun; this implant, which exfiltrates host data to a command server, incorporates publicly available Lazarus Group source code as a likely false flag rather than evidence of Lazarus involvement. McAfee analysts Ryan Sherstobitoff and Asheer Malhotra note that Rising Sun’s multi‐step execution—weaponized document, in‐memory downloader, intelligence‐gathering implant—highlights the continued efficacy of social‐engineering vectors, while experts from CipherCloud, Positive Technologies and Lucy Security emphasize that defenses must go beyond spam filters to include ongoing user awareness training, holistic people-and-technology security models, robust data protection, network visibility and rapid incident response to detect and halt such advanced, evolving threats.
hits.title: Operation Sharpshooter targets infrastructure around the world | TechTarget

canonical_entities: automated encrypted exfiltration over C2 channels
hits.text: McAfee’s Advanced Threat Research team uncovered “Operation Sharpshooter,” a global cyber-espionage campaign targeting nuclear, defense, energy and financial organizations via weaponized Office documents masquerading as recruitment materials; an initial macro‐enabled loader drops an in‐memory implant that retrieves a second‐stage backdoor dubbed “Rising Sun,” which leverages source code from Lazarus Group’s 2015 Duuzer Trojan to perform account, file/directory, process and system/network discovery, process injection and automated encrypted exfiltration over C2 channels (e.g., 34.214.99.20/view_style.php); from October to November 2018 McAfee telemetry identified at least 87 predominantly English-speaking targets, with key IOCs including hashes such as 8106a30bd35526bded384627d8eebce15da35d17 and document URLs like hxxp://208.117.44.112/Strategic Planning Manager.doc, detectable by McAfee signatures RDN/Generic Downloader.x and Rising-Sun, and mitigated by monitoring macro executions, anomalous process injections and outbound C2 traffic while the broader community assesses attribution and monitors for follow-on exploitation.
hits.title: ‘Operation Sharpshooter’ Targets Global Defense, Critical Infrastructure | McAfee Blog

canonical_entities: Palo Alto Networks Cortex XDR Anti-Ransomware
hits.text: Following the sale of INC ransomware source code in March 2024 and its initial appearance in August 2023, researchers in July 2024 uncovered Lynx ransomware, a Windows-only, C++-based RaaS variant that shares ~48% of INC’s functions (70.8% among common routines) and has been deployed against U.S. and U.K. retail, real estate, architecture, financial and environmental service firms via phishing, malicious downloads and underground forums; employing AES-128-CTR and Curve25519 Donna for encryption with a .lynx extension, it conducts double-extortion by exfiltrating victims’ data (published on lynxblog[.]net under a policy excluding governments, hospitals and non-profits) before encrypting all files by default—killing processes, encrypting network shares and hidden disks, deleting shadow copies and backups, leveraging the Restart Manager API to target in-use files, and printing a OneNote report—then dropping a README.txt ransom note; this evolution of RaaS underscores the need for organizations to adopt robust cybersecurity measures, including anti-phishing training, backup hardening, dynamic and behavioral detections via Palo Alto Networks’ Cortex XDR Anti-Ransomware and Advanced WildFire, and vigilant monitoring of Indicators of Compromise such as published SHA256 hashes to mitigate high-profile, code-reused ransomware campaigns.
hits.title: Lynx Ransomware: A Rebranding of INC Ransomware

hits.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.
hits.title: Follina Exploited by State-Sponsored Hackers | Threatpost

hits.text: Since its emergence in 2013, Iran-linked APT35 (aka Charming Kitten/Phosphorus) has executed a series of high-value espionage campaigns—beginning with a 2014 social-media spying operation—and continued in 2019 with spear-phishing against U.S., French and Middle East academic institutions before Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit seized control of 99 APT35 domains; in late 2020 the group targeted oncology, genetics and neurology researchers in Israel and the U.S. via its “BadBlood” PDF-based spear-phishing campaign, while in 2021 it chained Exchange Server flaws (ProxyShell) for network intrusion and demonstrated TTP overlaps with Momento ransomware (CVE-2021-21972 exploiter); in January 2022 it performed mass Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) scans—over 80 percent of attempts originated in the U.S.—and later deployed a stealthy .NET-based PowerShell backdoor (“PowerLess”) that runs in-process to avoid detection, followed by Hyperscrape, a Windows .NET mailbox exfiltration tool for Outlook, Gmail and Yahoo! that quietly harvests emails once the actor possesses valid credentials or session cookies, and a companion Telegram dump utility; APT35 maintains persistence for intelligence collection or monetizes access when systems lack strategic value, underscoring the need for timely patching, multi-factor authentication and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at APT35 aka Charming Kitten

hits.text: Operation RoundPress, attributed with medium confidence to Russian state-sponsored APT28 (Fancy Bear), has since 2023 exploited stored and reflected XSS flaws in widely used webmail platforms—initially leveraging Roundcube CVE-2020-35730 to inject malicious JavaScript into email bodies, then CVE-2023-43770 and additional n-day vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra in early 2024—to execute upon email open without clicks or redirects. Through spear-phishing emails crafted with timely political or news excerpts, the hidden script auto-fills victim credentials via invisible input fields, scrapes DOM content—including emails, contacts, webmail settings, login history, 2FA tokens and passwords—and exfiltrates data via HTTP POST to hardcoded C2 servers. Targets span high-value government entities in Greece, Ukraine, Serbia and Cameroon, military units in Ukraine and Ecuador, defense contractors in Ukraine, Bulgaria and Romania, and critical infrastructure in Ukraine and Bulgaria. The lack of persistence mechanisms confines execution to session scope but underscores the necessity for timely patching of XSS vulnerabilities, disabling HTML rendering in webmail clients, enforcing strict input sanitization and multifactor authentication, and monitoring anomalous outbound traffic to mitigate credential theft and data exfiltration.
hits.title: Government webmail hacked via XSS bugs in global spy campaign

canonical_entities: RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022
Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
hits.text: Trend Micro’s analysis of RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022 reveals a predominantly human-operated ransomware campaign that hit the manufacturing sector hardest (followed by education and banking) with the highest attack attempts observed in the U.S., France, and Brazil—driven in part by a high-profile 2021 breach of a Taiwanese hardware manufacturer. Initial access is achieved via malspam delivering multi-stage payloads that leverage IcedID and TrickBot for footholds, deploy Cobalt Strike beacons and PyXie RAT for code execution and data exfiltration, use SMB to propagate a VATET loader for lateral movement, and employ Mimikatz and LaZagne for credential harvesting. Upon execution, RansomEXX evades defense by disabling tools (T1562.001), skipping encryption of critical Windows paths, file names, and extensions, and terminating hundreds of business and security processes to maximize impact (T1486, T1490), then encrypts data and demands ransom. Recommended mitigations include strict audit and asset inventory, hardened configurations and least-privilege access, macro and email sandboxing to block malspam entry, regular patching and virtual patching, multifactor authentication, advanced behavior-based detection (e.g., Trend Micro Vision One™), and continuous employee training and red-team testing to disrupt the ransomware kill chain and protect against future RansomEXX intrusions.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: RansomEXX | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: In August 2025 the FBI issued a public service announcement that FSB-linked Berserk Bear (aka Blue Kraken, Crouching Yeti, Dragonfly, Koala Team) has been exploiting the seven-year-old Cisco IOS/IOS XE Smart Install remote code execution/DoS vulnerability (CVE-2018-0171) to compromise critical infrastructure worldwide. Since Cisco first detected opportunistic attacks in November 2021, the group has collected configuration files from thousands of unpatched devices associated with U.S. critical infrastructure sectors, covertly modified those configs to maintain persistent unauthorized access, and conducted network reconnaissance targeting ICS-related protocols and applications. Cisco Talos reports that the campaign, referred to as Static Tundra, has aggressively hit telecommunications, higher education, and manufacturing networks across North America, Asia, Africa, and Europe, deploying custom SNMP tools and the SYNful Knock firmware implant—originally identified by FireEye in 2015—to evade detection and embed for years. The FBI’s warning underscores the urgent need for organizations to patch CVE-2018-0171, disable Smart Install, and implement comprehensive hardening, as other state-sponsored actors are likely conducting similar network device compromise campaigns.
hits.title: FBI warns of Russian hackers exploiting 7-year-old Cisco flaw

hits.text: In August, the DPRK–linked APT TA444 (aka APT38, BlueNoroff, BlackAlicanto, Coperenicum, Sapphire Sleet and Stardust Chollima) deployed SpectralBlur, a custom post-exploitation macOS backdoor that leverages command-and-control instructions to upload/download files, spawn a shell, update its configuration, delete files or enter hibernation/sleep mode; Proofpoint researcher Greg Lesnewich identified code overlaps with the KandyKorn macOS data stealer—earlier tied to Lazarus Group phishing campaigns against blockchain engineers—linking both tools through shared strings and infrastructure. This rapid iteration of proprietary macOS malware underscores TA444’s dedicated development capability and signals an intensified DPRK espionage focus on Apple users, particularly within the cryptocurrency sector, demonstrating persistent operational tempo and advanced post-exploitation tactics.
hits.title: North Korea Debuts 'SpectralBlur' Malware Amid macOS Onslaught

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: deployed a webshell on the router’s web server
Credentials from Password Stores: Security Account Manager
hits.text: Dragos researchers, in collaboration with Ukraine’s CSSC, unearthed FrostyGoop—an ICS-specific malware first spotted in April and used in January to disrupt central heating in over 600 Lviv apartment buildings—marking the first known malware to leverage Modbus TCP for read/write operations on operational technology. Attackers gained initial access in April 2023 by exploiting a MikroTik router vulnerability, deployed a webshell on the router’s web server, and maintained persistence via Tor and L2TP tunnels to Moscow-based IPs. After spending months conducting reconnaissance, they extracted credentials by dumping the SAM registry hive in December, then directly issued scripted Modbus commands—read from a JSON configuration file—to publicly exposed ENCO heating controllers, even downgrading firmware to disable monitoring and force inaccurate measurements that halted heating services for nearly two days amid subzero temperatures. This incident underscores the threat posed by internet-exposed ICS devices—over 46,000 globally using Modbus—and highlights poor network segmentation, unpatched ICS CVEs, and the ease with which FrostyGoop’s protocol-agnostic payload can be repurposed against diverse industrial controllers, necessitating immediate network segmentation, firmware monitoring, and patch management in OT environments.
hits.title: ICS malware FrostyGoop disrupted heating in Ukraine, remains threat to OT worldwide

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
hits.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

hits.text: McAfee researchers at RSA Conference 2019 revealed that Operation Sharpshooter—a previously disclosed December 2018 espionage campaign first observed via October 25 weaponized macro-laden Dropbox documents—actually began as early as September 2017, using embedded shellcode in Microsoft Word to deploy a modular, in-memory second-stage implant dubbed “Rising Sun.” Rising Sun, which reuses source code from the Lazarus Group’s Duuzer backdoor, performs reconnaissance, encrypts and exfiltrates system data (computer names, IP addresses, native OS details) and communicates with multiple newly identified command-and-control servers. Initially detected in 87 global organizations—50 percent in U.S. defense, nuclear, energy and financial sectors—the ongoing campaign has expanded to target financial services, government and critical infrastructure in Germany, Turkey, the U.K. and the U.S., exhibiting TTP overlaps and code reuse linking it to Lazarus operations. These findings underscore the need for strengthened macro and memory-resident malware defenses, proactive C2 infrastructure takedown efforts and enhanced attribution methodologies.
hits.title: RSAC 2019: New Operation Sharpshooter Data Reveals Higher Complexity, Scope | Threatpost

canonical_entities: regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea
hits.text: In early 2018 McAfee Advanced Threat Research uncovered Operation Honeybee, a North Korean–linked campaign—tracked to the persona snoopykiller@mail.ru and control domains navermail.byethost3.com/nihon.byethost11.com—targeting humanitarian aid groups and regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea with malicious Microsoft Word documents named “Honeybee” that exploited politically themed and generic “not compatible” lures to execute VBA macros embedding a custom‐alphabet Base64 payload. Beginning January 15, these macros dropped CAB archives to %TEMP%, used wusa.exe or expand.exe for UAC bypass, then hijacked cliconfg.exe via a malicious NTWDBLIB.dll to install a persistent COMSysApp service loading ipnet.dll from %SystemRoot%\System32. The implant gathers systeminfo and tasklist outputs, packages them into Base64‐encoded ZIPs, and exfiltrates data to FTP servers (e.g., 1113427185.ifastnet.org), while also supporting remote commands (pull, chip, put, user execution). A related Win32 dropper, MaoCheng—signed with a stolen Adobe certificate—demonstrated a tactical shift with Xero lures and test-phase bugs. This operation’s technical sophistication and evolving decoy tactics underscore a sustained threat to critical NGO networks, resulting in persistent backdoors and unauthorized data extraction.

hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
hits.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

canonical_entities: dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora
hits.text: Since at least September 2023, the China-aligned Evasive Panda APT (aka BRONZE HIGHLAND/Daggerfly) has conducted a dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora by compromising both the Kagyu International Monlam Trust’s website and the official Monlam translation-software supply chain—first implanting obfuscated JavaScript into jquery.js on the festival site that verifies victims’ first three IP octets via an MD5 hash salted with “1qaz0okm!@#,” serves a faux “Aw, Snap!” error page to users in India, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Australia and the U.S., and lures them to download a malicious “certificate.exe” or “.pkg” downloader; that loader side-loads memmgrset.dll (http_dy.dll) to fetch a JSON config from update.devicebug[.]com and ultimately deploys the undocumented Nightdoor backdoor alongside the group’s modular MgBot implant, while a trojanized Monlam software installer (Windows autorun.exe abusing MonlamUpdate.exe for DLL side-loading of RPHost.dll, and macOS Mach-O downloaders) has delivered further downloaders and payloads—retrieved from tibetpost[.]net and a direct IP—to %TEMP%\default_ico.exe for additional Nightdoor and MgBot installation.

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: deployed a webshell on the router’s web server
Credentials from Password Stores: Security Account Manager
retrieved_context.text: Dragos researchers, in collaboration with Ukraine’s CSSC, unearthed FrostyGoop—an ICS-specific malware first spotted in April and used in January to disrupt central heating in over 600 Lviv apartment buildings—marking the first known malware to leverage Modbus TCP for read/write operations on operational technology. Attackers gained initial access in April 2023 by exploiting a MikroTik router vulnerability, deployed a webshell on the router’s web server, and maintained persistence via Tor and L2TP tunnels to Moscow-based IPs. After spending months conducting reconnaissance, they extracted credentials by dumping the SAM registry hive in December, then directly issued scripted Modbus commands—read from a JSON configuration file—to publicly exposed ENCO heating controllers, even downgrading firmware to disable monitoring and force inaccurate measurements that halted heating services for nearly two days amid subzero temperatures. This incident underscores the threat posed by internet-exposed ICS devices—over 46,000 globally using Modbus—and highlights poor network segmentation, unpatched ICS CVEs, and the ease with which FrostyGoop’s protocol-agnostic payload can be repurposed against diverse industrial controllers, necessitating immediate network segmentation, firmware monitoring, and patch management in OT environments.
retrieved_context.title: ICS malware FrostyGoop disrupted heating in Ukraine, remains threat to OT worldwide

hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails
hits.text: Attackers are leveraging the six-year-old CVE-2017-11882 Microsoft Office RCE vulnerability via malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails to initiate a multi-stage infection chain that delivers the Agent Tesla RAT and advanced keylogger. Once a user opens the Excel file on an unpatched Office build, it connects to a malicious server to retrieve a heavily obfuscated VBS script, which in turn downloads a JPEG containing a Base64-encoded DLL. The VBS launches PowerShell to extract and load the DLL, then abuses RegAsm.exe—disguised as a legitimate registry utility—to inject a thread that fetches and executes the Agent Tesla payload. Deployed Agent Tesla uses clipboard and window hooking for keystroke logging, screen capture and browser, mail and FTP credential theft, exfiltrating data via attacker-controlled Telegram bots. Zscaler’s detailed IoCs—including malicious URLs, file hashes and Telegram endpoints—underscore the critical need for organizations to patch legacy Office versions, deploy email defenses, and monitor for the described artifacts to prevent credential compromise and system takeover.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit 6-Year-Old Microsoft Office Bug to Spread Spyware

hits.text: Silent Push researchers uncovered FIN7’s largest-ever infrastructure, identifying over 4,000 malicious IOFA domains and associated IP addresses used to fuel a global phishing and malware campaign that hit high-profile targets such as the Louvre, Meta and Reuters. Using automated intelligence and Threat Hunting workflows, analysts detected a pattern of newly registered look-alike domains—many leveraging common TLDs and typosquatting—to host spear-phishing landing pages and weaponized Office attachments that deploy custom .NET droppers and Cobalt Strike beacons. Chronologically, the operation began with domain registration, followed by coordinated email blasts spoofing corporate brands, HTTP(S) redirects to phishing kits, and payload delivery that enabled credential harvesting and potential lateral movement. Silent Push’s API-driven Integrations enabled rapid enumeration of IOFA indicators of compromise, brand protection alerts and proactive blocking in customer environments. Actionable insights include ingesting the full list of domains and IPs into SIEM and email security filters, enforcing strict SPF/DKIM/DMARC policies, monitoring DNS query anomalies for new domain registrations, and updating endpoint detection rules to flag the identified .NET loader behaviors.
hits.title: FIN7: Silent Push unearths the largest group of FIN7 domains ever discovered. 4000+ IOFA domains and IPs found. Louvre, Meta, and Reuters targeted in massive global phishing and malware campaigns.

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: targeted cyber-espionage campaign against telecommunications organizations in Egypt, Sudan and Tanzania
telecommunications organizations in Egypt, Sudan and Tanzania
hits.text: In November 2023, Iran-linked espionage group Seedworm (aka MuddyWater and subordinate to MOIS) launched a targeted cyber-espionage campaign against telecommunications organizations in Egypt, Sudan and Tanzania using its Go-based MuddyC2Go framework alongside both living-off-the-land and custom tools to maintain persistence, harvest credentials and exfiltrate data. Researchers observed a PowerShell-based MuddyC2Go DLL launcher named “vcruntime140.dll” sideloaded by the legitimate Java executable jabswitch.exe into csidl_common_appdata\javax, which read C2 URIs (“End” and “Status” values under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip) before invoking Invoke-WebRequest to contacts servers such as 95.164.38.99:443 and 45.150.64.39:443; the backdoor was executed via a scheduled task (“Microsoft\Windows\JavaX\Java Autorun”), while Impacket’s WMIExec, Revsocks (94.131.3.160:443), and SimpleHelp (146.70.124.102) were leveraged for lateral movement, SAM hive dumps, drive reconnaissance and remote administration alongside AnyDesk and a custom keylogger. This activity followed a prior Seedworm intrusion earlier in 2023 into at least one victim using SimpleHelp-driven PowerShell, proxy tools, LSASS dumping and JumpCloud deployment, confirming group attribution. Seedworm’s blend of custom C2 innovation and publicly available/proxy tools underscores the necessity for defenders to monitor for anomalous PowerShell invocations to suspect domains, unexpected Java sideloading, scheduled task creations, unauthorized SimpleHelp or AnyDesk services, Venom Proxy processes, and registry modifications in telecom-grade networks to detect and disrupt its persistent espionage operations.
hits.title: Seedworm: Iranian Hackers Target Telecoms Orgs in North and East Africa | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: In August 2025 Microsoft Threat Intelligence revealed that Storm-2460, associated with the Play ransomware group, has resumed exploiting CVE-2025-29824—a zero-day elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Common Log File System patched in April—to gain SYSTEM privileges on unpatched hosts across IT, financial and real estate organizations in the US, Europe, South America and the Middle East. The campaign begins with an in-memory dropper masquerading as the open-source ChatGPT Desktop app that decrypts and launches PipeMagic, a modular backdoor first observed in December 2022 and now updated with persistence and lateral-movement enhancements targeting Saudi Arabian and Brazilian manufacturing entities. PipeMagic communicates with its TCP C2 over a named pipe, self-updates by storing distinct payload modules in memory via doubly linked lists for staging, execution and communication (plus an additional dynamic list), then leverages the CLFS exploit to escalate privileges before deploying Play ransomware. Although the campaign’s footprint remains limited, the combination of a zero-day exploit and a sophisticated modular backdoor underscores a heightened risk; organizations are urged to immediately apply the April patch for CVE-2025-29824, enable tamper and network protection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, run EDR in block mode, enforce full automated investigation and remediation, and leverage cloud-delivered machine-learning protections to block novel variants.
hits.title: PipeMagic Backdoor Resurfaces as Part of Play Ransomware Attack Chain

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: In early April, Palo Alto Networks’ Advanced WildFire and Cortex XDR uncovered SnipBot—a new v5.0 iteration of the RomCom RAT family—employing advanced window message–based control-flow obfuscation and anti-sandbox checks (filename hash and HKCU\…\RecentDocs entries) in a multi-stage chain beginning with a PDF-labeled EXE downloader signed using a likely stolen certificate; the downloader contacts xeontime[.]com for config-pdf.dll, which uses registry-based COM hijacking to load keyprov.dll from drvmcprotect[.]com into explorer.exe, decrypts payloads stored in HKCU\Software\AppDataSoft\Software, and opens a TCP listener on port 1342 for commands to update, delete, or execute modules. The main backdoor single.dll (mutex “SnipMutex”) supports 27 encrypted commands for drive and process enumeration, file upload/download, and remote module execution, facilitating network pivoting and targeted file exfiltration. Active since December 2023 (RomCom activity since 2022), SnipBot’s tactics, stolen certificates, unique obfuscation, and sophisticated loader underscore a high-risk threat actor likely focused on intelligence gathering; Palo Alto products classify its samples, URLs, and domains as malicious to prevent compromise.
