retrieved_context.text: Since at least August 2023, threat actors have exploited CVE-2023-4966 (CitrixBleed), a 7.5-rated flaw in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway, culminating in an October 16–19 breach at Comcast Xfinity that exposed 35,879,455 customers’ usernames, hashed passwords, names, contact details, last four SSN digits, dates of birth and security Q&A; despite Citrix’s October 10 patch and Comcast’s claim of prompt mitigation, attackers used publicly available proofs-of-concept and rumored Python automation scripts to extract session tokens from device memory, hijack active sessions and bypass authentication, a tactic linked by ReliaQuest to at least five threat groups including LockBit; this incident highlights the necessity not only of timely patching and reboots but also of invalidating all active and persistent session tokens, enforcing multi-factor authentication, resetting credentials and maintaining continuous 24x7 monitoring to prevent further data exfiltration and ransomware deployment.
retrieved_context.title: Comcast Xfinity Breached via CitrixBleed; 35M Customers Affected

hits.text: In mid-March 2025, Kaspersky uncovered Operation ForumTroll, a state-sponsored APT espionage campaign targeting Russian media outlets, educational institutions and government organizations via personalized, short-lived phishing links opened in Google Chrome that automatically triggered a zero-day sandbox-escape exploit (CVE-2025-2783) exploiting a logical error at the Windows–Chrome boundary and chained to an unrecovered RCE payload to install sophisticated malware (Trojan.Win64.Agent, Trojan.Win64.Convagent.gen). Kaspersky’s exploit detection technologies rapidly identified and reverse-engineered the sandbox escape, enabling immediate reporting to Google and the release of Chrome 134.0.6998.177/.178 on March 25, 2025, effectively neutralizing the exploit. Key IoCs include primakovreadings[.]info and detections under Exploit.Win32.Generic, PDM:Exploit.Win32.Generic, PDM:Trojan.Win32.Generic and UDS:DangerousObject.Multi.Generic; defenders should apply the Chrome update, monitor for these indicators and maintain heightened vigilance against targeted phishing lures.
hits.title: Operation ForumTroll: APT attack with Google Chrome zero-day exploit chain

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: Our GReAT team uncovered Operation ForumTroll—a state-sponsored APT campaign targeting Russian media, academic and government personnel—delivering previously unknown malware via phishing emails masquerading as Primakov Readings invitations containing two malicious links; clicking either on a Windows PC using Chrome or any Chromium-based browser silently triggers a zero-day exploit (CVE-2025-2783), exploiting a logic flaw at the Chrome-Windows interface to bypass the browser’s sandbox and deploy the payload without further user interaction. We promptly reported the vulnerability to Google, which released a patch in Chrome version 134.0.6998.177/178; while the phishing links now redirect to the legitimate forum site and the campaign is dormant, the attackers could reactivate it at any time. To mitigate this espionage threat, organizations should ensure all Chrome instances are updated to at least 134.0.6998.177/.178, deploy robust exploit detection and prevention solutions on internet-connected devices, and maintain vigilant phishing awareness and monitoring.
hits.title: CVE-2025-2783 in Operation ForumTroll APT

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Google has released Chrome 120.0.6099.129/130 updates to patch an actively exploited high-severity zero-day (CVE-2023-7024), a heap-based buffer overflow in the WebRTC framework that enables crashes or arbitrary code execution, discovered by TAG researchers Clément Lecigne and Vlad Stolyarov on December 19, 2023. This marks the eighth Chrome zero-day exploited in the wild this year—following type confusion flaws in V8 (CVE-2023-2033, CVSS 8.8; CVE-2023-2136, CVSS 9.6; CVE-2023-3079, CVSS 8.8; CVE-2023-4762, CVSS 8.8), a heap overflow in WebP (CVE-2023-4863, CVSS 8.8), a heap overflow in libvpx (CVE-2023-5217, CVSS 8.8) and an integer overflow in Skia (CVE-2023-6345, CVSS 9.6)—amid a record 26,447 CVEs disclosed in 2023, 115 of which have been weaponized by threat actors and ransomware groups using remote code execution, security-feature bypass, buffer manipulation, privilege escalation and input-validation flaws. Given WebRTC’s cross-browser support, impacts on Firefox and Safari remain under assessment. Administrators and end users should immediately upgrade Chrome for Windows, macOS and Linux and apply forthcoming patches for Chromium-based browsers (Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi) to mitigate potential compromise.
hits.title: Urgent: New Chrome Zero-Day Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild - Update ASAP

canonical_entities: regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea
hits.text: In early 2018 McAfee Advanced Threat Research uncovered Operation Honeybee, a North Korean–linked campaign—tracked to the persona snoopykiller@mail.ru and control domains navermail.byethost3.com/nihon.byethost11.com—targeting humanitarian aid groups and regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea with malicious Microsoft Word documents named “Honeybee” that exploited politically themed and generic “not compatible” lures to execute VBA macros embedding a custom‐alphabet Base64 payload. Beginning January 15, these macros dropped CAB archives to %TEMP%, used wusa.exe or expand.exe for UAC bypass, then hijacked cliconfg.exe via a malicious NTWDBLIB.dll to install a persistent COMSysApp service loading ipnet.dll from %SystemRoot%\System32. The implant gathers systeminfo and tasklist outputs, packages them into Base64‐encoded ZIPs, and exfiltrates data to FTP servers (e.g., 1113427185.ifastnet.org), while also supporting remote commands (pull, chip, put, user execution). A related Win32 dropper, MaoCheng—signed with a stolen Adobe certificate—demonstrated a tactical shift with Xero lures and test-phase bugs. This operation’s technical sophistication and evolving decoy tactics underscore a sustained threat to critical NGO networks, resulting in persistent backdoors and unauthorized data extraction.
hits.title: McAfee Uncovers Operation Honeybee, a Malicious Campaign Targeting Humanitarian Aid Groups | McAfee Blog

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Symantec has warned that extortion actors, notably the Clop ransomware operation (aka Snakefly/TA505/FIN11), have been exploiting a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability in the MOVEit Transfer web application (CVE-2023-34362) since May 27, 2023, enabling supply-chain attacks across multiple organizations; although first patched on May 31, additional vulnerabilities (CVEs pending) were disclosed on June 9. Attackers deploy a bespoke web shell, Lemurloot (detected as JS.Malscript!g1, Trojan.Gen.2, WS.Malware), to authenticate via hard-coded credentials, execute SQL statements to alter or delete database elements, exfiltrate records and Azure settings, and manipulate user accounts. With proof-of-concept code now public, secondary threat actors face elevated risk of exploitation and data theft. Clop has since threatened data leaks unless ransoms are paid, reflecting its shift from encryption to extortion. Symantec mitigations include file-based and ML detections, network-based attack signatures, and Data Center Security policy controls that harden MS SQL, IIS and sandbox environments to prevent web-shell deployment and unauthorized software execution.
hits.title: MOVEit Vulnerabilities: What You Need to Know | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: After a year-long investigation researchers at Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs dissected the Ngioweb botnet—first observed in 2017—which uses a loader network and roughly 15 n-day exploits to deploy malware that contacts C2 domains generated via a domain generation algorithm (augmented by DNS TXT records to resist sinkholing), evaluates device traffic capacity, and links compromised Zyxel, Reolink, Alpha Technologies and, increasingly, Netgear routers (now 10 % of bots) to over 180 “backconnect” C2 nodes that provide at least 80 % of the 35,000 residential proxies in the NSOCKS[.]net service across 180 countries; NSOCKS’s lack of authentication and appearance on free proxy lists has enabled cybercriminals to carry out DDoS amplification, credential stuffing, phishing and malware proxying (e.g., Agent Tesla), while APT28 state-sponsored actors have mixed espionage with criminal traffic on the same infrastructure. To disrupt both operations, Lumen, alongside The ShadowServer Foundation and other partners, is actively blocking traffic to known C2 nodes and publishing indicators of compromise to help organizations identify and remediate infected devices.
hits.title: Botnet fueling residential proxies disrupted in cybercrime crackdown

hits.text: In early April, Palo Alto Networks’ Advanced WildFire and Cortex XDR uncovered SnipBot—a new v5.0 iteration of the RomCom RAT family—employing advanced window message–based control-flow obfuscation and anti-sandbox checks (filename hash and HKCU\…\RecentDocs entries) in a multi-stage chain beginning with a PDF-labeled EXE downloader signed using a likely stolen certificate; the downloader contacts xeontime[.]com for config-pdf.dll, which uses registry-based COM hijacking to load keyprov.dll from drvmcprotect[.]com into explorer.exe, decrypts payloads stored in HKCU\Software\AppDataSoft\Software, and opens a TCP listener on port 1342 for commands to update, delete, or execute modules. The main backdoor single.dll (mutex “SnipMutex”) supports 27 encrypted commands for drive and process enumeration, file upload/download, and remote module execution, facilitating network pivoting and targeted file exfiltration. Active since December 2023 (RomCom activity since 2022), SnipBot’s tactics, stolen certificates, unique obfuscation, and sophisticated loader underscore a high-risk threat actor likely focused on intelligence gathering; Palo Alto products classify its samples, URLs, and domains as malicious to prevent compromise.
hits.title: Inside SnipBot: The Latest RomCom Malware Variant

hits.text: Since mid-September, unknown cybercriminals have been conducting large-scale brute-force attacks against internet-exposed instances of Foundation Accounting Software—widely used by construction sub-industries such as plumbing, HVAC and concrete—by targeting the default “sa” administrator and a second high-privilege account within the MSSQL database accessible via TCP port 4243 (opened for Foundation’s mobile app). After an observed peak of roughly 35,000 rapid login attempts to obtain valid credentials, the attackers enable an extended stored procedure (e.g., xp_cmdshell) to execute OS-level commands and scripts, automating lateral movement and data theft across multiple unrelated victims. Huntress has identified just 33 hosts left with unchanged default passwords, alerted all impacted and at-risk customers, and urges organizations to rotate all Foundation credentials, remove direct internet exposure, and disable the exploited stored procedure to mitigate further compromise.
hits.title: Threat Actors Target Accounting Software Used by Construction Contractors - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

hits.text: In May 2023, after U.S. authorities secured convictions against three high-level operators and declared the Russia-based cybercrime enterprise Fin7 “no more,” security experts began spotting first signs of its resurrection in April 2024 when Blackberry reported a typosquatting-based malware intrusion against a major automotive firm; since January 2024, Silent Push analyst Zach Edwards has mapped over 4,000 Fin7-linked hosts—rented largely on the pro-Russia Stark Industries Solutions platform—employing typosquatting, booby-trapped ads, malicious browser extensions and spear-phishing domains to mimic hundreds of brands from American Express and Microsoft 365 to CNN and Zoom, as well as popular free software tools such as 7-zip, PuTTY and Python, all “aged” on innocuous templates for six to nine months before weaponization; eSentire and Malwarebytes also observed sponsored Google ads pushing phony extensions in May and April 2024, and Fin7 has even deployed domains targeting Louvre and Olympic tourists, building on its 2013–present campaign that has extorted some $3 billion from victim organizations, underscoring the urgent need for renewed law enforcement focus and proactive domain-monitoring defenses.
hits.title: The Stark Truth Behind the Resurgence of Russia’s Fin7 – Krebs on Security

hits.text: CISA has added CVE-2022-22047—a high-severity (CVSS 7.8) elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Client Server Runtime Subsystem used since Windows 7 through Windows 11 and Server 2008–2022—to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and is urging federal agencies to install Microsoft’s July 5 Patch Tuesday update by August 2 after evidence emerged of in-the-wild exploitation; initially disclosed as a zero-day by Microsoft’s security team, the CSRSS bug enables adversaries who already hold local or physical access—or who gain remote code execution via malware or specially crafted Office/Adobe documents and macros—to escalate to SYSTEM privileges for lateral movement, although FortiGuard Labs rates the overall business threat as “medium” given the prerequisite foothold and available patch, while Trend Micro’s ZDI notes such elevation flaws are typically paired with a separate RCE vector and Microsoft has signaled future default blocking of VBA macros to mitigate this attack chain.
hits.title: CISA Urges Patch of Exploited Windows 11 Bug by Aug. 2 | Threatpost

canonical_entities: Scanning the Internet for IoT devices with open Telnet/SSH ports
Use of default or weak credentials
Encrypted SOCKS5 tunneling to proxy infrastructure
hits.text: Researchers have uncovered that since early 2024 a previously undocumented botnet, dubbed Ngioweb, has been systematically scanning the Internet for IoT devices—primarily DVRs, IP cameras and home routers—with open Telnet/SSH ports and default or weak credentials, exploiting known firmware vulnerabilities to deploy a lightweight Go-based loader that establishes encrypted SOCKS5 tunnels back to a resilient NSOCKS residential proxy network of over 150,000 infected nodes. Once a device is compromised, Ngioweb drops a persistent agent that connects to fast-flux C2 domains via HTTPS, retrieves updated encryption keys and proxy configuration, and registers the node for NSOCKS’ tiered subscription service (starting at $25/month), which reportedly generates upwards of $500K in monthly revenue by fueling large-scale credential-stuffing campaigns, ad fraud and DDoS-for-hire operations. The actors behind Ngioweb continually rotate fallback C2 domains, employ encryption and obfuscation to evade signature-based detection, and monitor infection success rates in real time, enabling rapid retooling and expansion. Defenders are urged to enforce strong, unique credentials on all IoT assets, disable unused management interfaces, apply timely firmware updates, implement network segmentation and deploy behavioral analytics or honeypots to detect anomalous outbound proxy traffic.
hits.title: Ngioweb Botnet Fuels NSOCKS Residential Proxy Network Exploiting IoT Devices

hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.

retrieved_context.text: In mid-March 2025, Kaspersky uncovered Operation ForumTroll, a state-sponsored APT espionage campaign targeting Russian media outlets, educational institutions and government organizations via personalized, short-lived phishing links opened in Google Chrome that automatically triggered a zero-day sandbox-escape exploit (CVE-2025-2783) exploiting a logical error at the Windows–Chrome boundary and chained to an unrecovered RCE payload to install sophisticated malware (Trojan.Win64.Agent, Trojan.Win64.Convagent.gen). Kaspersky’s exploit detection technologies rapidly identified and reverse-engineered the sandbox escape, enabling immediate reporting to Google and the release of Chrome 134.0.6998.177/.178 on March 25, 2025, effectively neutralizing the exploit. Key IoCs include primakovreadings[.]info and detections under Exploit.Win32.Generic, PDM:Exploit.Win32.Generic, PDM:Trojan.Win32.Generic and UDS:DangerousObject.Multi.Generic; defenders should apply the Chrome update, monitor for these indicators and maintain heightened vigilance against targeted phishing lures.
retrieved_context.title: Operation ForumTroll: APT attack with Google Chrome zero-day exploit chain

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: Our GReAT team uncovered Operation ForumTroll—a state-sponsored APT campaign targeting Russian media, academic and government personnel—delivering previously unknown malware via phishing emails masquerading as Primakov Readings invitations containing two malicious links; clicking either on a Windows PC using Chrome or any Chromium-based browser silently triggers a zero-day exploit (CVE-2025-2783), exploiting a logic flaw at the Chrome-Windows interface to bypass the browser’s sandbox and deploy the payload without further user interaction. We promptly reported the vulnerability to Google, which released a patch in Chrome version 134.0.6998.177/178; while the phishing links now redirect to the legitimate forum site and the campaign is dormant, the attackers could reactivate it at any time. To mitigate this espionage threat, organizations should ensure all Chrome instances are updated to at least 134.0.6998.177/.178, deploy robust exploit detection and prevention solutions on internet-connected devices, and maintain vigilant phishing awareness and monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CVE-2025-2783 in Operation ForumTroll APT

retrieved_context.text: Since mid-September, unknown cybercriminals have been conducting large-scale brute-force attacks against internet-exposed instances of Foundation Accounting Software—widely used by construction sub-industries such as plumbing, HVAC and concrete—by targeting the default “sa” administrator and a second high-privilege account within the MSSQL database accessible via TCP port 4243 (opened for Foundation’s mobile app). After an observed peak of roughly 35,000 rapid login attempts to obtain valid credentials, the attackers enable an extended stored procedure (e.g., xp_cmdshell) to execute OS-level commands and scripts, automating lateral movement and data theft across multiple unrelated victims. Huntress has identified just 33 hosts left with unchanged default passwords, alerted all impacted and at-risk customers, and urges organizations to rotate all Foundation credentials, remove direct internet exposure, and disable the exploited stored procedure to mitigate further compromise.
retrieved_context.title: Threat Actors Target Accounting Software Used by Construction Contractors - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
retrieved_context.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
retrieved_context.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.

hits.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
hits.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
hits.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

canonical_entities: LNK files in the Windows Startup folder
HTTP POST exfiltration with Base64 encoding
hits.text: Cisco Talos analysts have uncovered PS1Bot, a sophisticated multi‐stage malware framework active throughout 2025 that leverages malvertising campaigns—delivering SEO‐styled ZIPs like “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”—to drop a JavaScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) which retrieves modular PowerShell and C# components in memory via Invoke-Expression, minimizing disk footprint and evading AV. Once executed, PS1Bot establishes persistence by creating randomly named PS1 scripts in %PROGRAMDATA% and corresponding LNK files in the Windows Startup folder that poll a C2 “/transform” endpoint for obfuscated payloads, using the host’s C: drive serial number to generate unique communication URLs. The framework’s on‐demand modules include information stealers, keyloggers, screen capture tools and advanced crypto wallet extractors that scan for seed-phrase wordlists in multiple languages, compress findings and exfiltrate via HTTP POST with Base64 encoding. Continuous sample updates and code overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet‐linked families suggest shared development resources or actor collaboration, highlighting the need for defenses that detect anomalous PowerShell IEX activity, monitor suspicious JavaScript downloaders and Startup LNK creations, and inspect outbound HTTP traffic for drive‐serial based URLs and wallet data exfiltration.
hits.title: Threat Actors Attacking Windows Systems With New Multi-Stage Malware Framework PS1Bot

hits.text: McAfee Mobile Research Team uncovered Xamalicious, a new Android backdoor built with Xamarin that abuses accessibility permissions to harvest device metadata, query a C2 server for a second-stage payload, and dynamically inject an assembly DLL to perform unauthorized ad-clicking, app installs and other financially motivated actions; this threat has been embedded in 25 apps—ranging from horoscope and gaming to utility tools—on Google Play since mid-2020, amassing over 327,000 installations across Brazil, Argentina, the UK, Australia, the US, Mexico and Europe. To evade detection, Xamalicious encrypts all C2 traffic as JWE tokens (RSA-OAEP/128CBC-HS256), self-updates its APK to transform into spyware or a banking trojan, and links back to the Cash Magnet ad-fraud campaign; its use of non-Java frameworks like Xamarin underscores heightened obfuscation. Google Play Protect now blocks or auto-removes infected apps. Separately, a malicious WhatsApp-based phishing campaign in India distributes fake SBI APKs invoking SMS permissions to capture credentials, banking and identity data, then exfiltrates them for unauthorized transactions.
hits.title: New Sneaky Xamalicious Android Malware Hits Over 327,000 Devices

canonical_entities: military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia
hits.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.
hits.title: Operation Lotus Blossom: A New Nation-State Cyberthreat?

canonical_entities: malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails
hits.text: Attackers are leveraging the six-year-old CVE-2017-11882 Microsoft Office RCE vulnerability via malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails to initiate a multi-stage infection chain that delivers the Agent Tesla RAT and advanced keylogger. Once a user opens the Excel file on an unpatched Office build, it connects to a malicious server to retrieve a heavily obfuscated VBS script, which in turn downloads a JPEG containing a Base64-encoded DLL. The VBS launches PowerShell to extract and load the DLL, then abuses RegAsm.exe—disguised as a legitimate registry utility—to inject a thread that fetches and executes the Agent Tesla payload. Deployed Agent Tesla uses clipboard and window hooking for keystroke logging, screen capture and browser, mail and FTP credential theft, exfiltrating data via attacker-controlled Telegram bots. Zscaler’s detailed IoCs—including malicious URLs, file hashes and Telegram endpoints—underscore the critical need for organizations to patch legacy Office versions, deploy email defenses, and monitor for the described artifacts to prevent credential compromise and system takeover.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit 6-Year-Old Microsoft Office Bug to Spread Spyware

retrieved_context.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
retrieved_context.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.

canonical_entities: LNK files in the Windows Startup folder

retrieved_context.text: Cisco Talos analysts have uncovered PS1Bot, a sophisticated multi‐stage malware framework active throughout 2025 that leverages malvertising campaigns—delivering SEO‐styled ZIPs like “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”—to drop a JavaScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) which retrieves modular PowerShell and C# components in memory via Invoke-Expression, minimizing disk footprint and evading AV. Once executed, PS1Bot establishes persistence by creating randomly named PS1 scripts in %PROGRAMDATA% and corresponding LNK files in the Windows Startup folder that poll a C2 “/transform” endpoint for obfuscated payloads, using the host’s C: drive serial number to generate unique communication URLs. The framework’s on‐demand modules include information stealers, keyloggers, screen capture tools and advanced crypto wallet extractors that scan for seed-phrase wordlists in multiple languages, compress findings and exfiltrate via HTTP POST with Base64 encoding. Continuous sample updates and code overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet‐linked families suggest shared development resources or actor collaboration, highlighting the need for defenses that detect anomalous PowerShell IEX activity, monitor suspicious JavaScript downloaders and Startup LNK creations, and inspect outbound HTTP traffic for drive‐serial based URLs and wallet data exfiltration.

retrieved_context.text: McAfee Mobile Research Team uncovered Xamalicious, a new Android backdoor built with Xamarin that abuses accessibility permissions to harvest device metadata, query a C2 server for a second-stage payload, and dynamically inject an assembly DLL to perform unauthorized ad-clicking, app installs and other financially motivated actions; this threat has been embedded in 25 apps—ranging from horoscope and gaming to utility tools—on Google Play since mid-2020, amassing over 327,000 installations across Brazil, Argentina, the UK, Australia, the US, Mexico and Europe. To evade detection, Xamalicious encrypts all C2 traffic as JWE tokens (RSA-OAEP/128CBC-HS256), self-updates its APK to transform into spyware or a banking trojan, and links back to the Cash Magnet ad-fraud campaign; its use of non-Java frameworks like Xamarin underscores heightened obfuscation. Google Play Protect now blocks or auto-removes infected apps. Separately, a malicious WhatsApp-based phishing campaign in India distributes fake SBI APKs invoking SMS permissions to capture credentials, banking and identity data, then exfiltrates them for unauthorized transactions.
retrieved_context.title: New Sneaky Xamalicious Android Malware Hits Over 327,000 Devices

canonical_entities: military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia
retrieved_context.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.

canonical_entities: malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails
retrieved_context.text: Attackers are leveraging the six-year-old CVE-2017-11882 Microsoft Office RCE vulnerability via malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails to initiate a multi-stage infection chain that delivers the Agent Tesla RAT and advanced keylogger. Once a user opens the Excel file on an unpatched Office build, it connects to a malicious server to retrieve a heavily obfuscated VBS script, which in turn downloads a JPEG containing a Base64-encoded DLL. The VBS launches PowerShell to extract and load the DLL, then abuses RegAsm.exe—disguised as a legitimate registry utility—to inject a thread that fetches and executes the Agent Tesla payload. Deployed Agent Tesla uses clipboard and window hooking for keystroke logging, screen capture and browser, mail and FTP credential theft, exfiltrating data via attacker-controlled Telegram bots. Zscaler’s detailed IoCs—including malicious URLs, file hashes and Telegram endpoints—underscore the critical need for organizations to patch legacy Office versions, deploy email defenses, and monitor for the described artifacts to prevent credential compromise and system takeover.

hits.text: Between March and July 2025, DPRK-linked Kimsuky operators executed at least 19 highly tailored spear-phishing attacks against Western, Central, Eastern and Southern European embassies in Seoul, spoofing real diplomats and embedding password-protected ZIPs delivered via Dropbox, Daum or Google Drive. Victims unwittingly launched malicious .LNK shortcuts that triggered obfuscated PowerShell scripts to decode and in-memory execute a Confuser-Core-obfuscated XenoRAT (MoonPeak) payload—identified by GUID 12DE1212-167D-45BA-1284-780DA98CF901 and mutex “Dansweit_Hk65-PSAccerdle”—leveraging scheduled tasks for persistence. Reconnaissance data (OS build, IP, process list) was exfiltrated as base64-encoded text files over HTTPS to the attackers’ private GitHub repo via the Contents API, while C2 instructions (e.g., onf.txt) directed dynamic payload rotations hosted on Dropbox with rapid header-fix GZIP routines. This ongoing campaign provided full system control—including keystroke logging, screenshots and remote shells—and underscores the need to monitor abnormal GitHub API usage, cloud-based archive downloads and anomalous PowerShell invocations.
hits.title: The Coordinated Embassy Hunt: Unmasking the DPRK-linked GitHub C2 Espionage Campaign

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.

canonical_entities: Exfiltration of SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations
hits.text: North Korean state-sponsored APT Slow Pisces (aka Jade Sleet, TraderTraitor, PUKCHONG) is executing a sophisticated three-stage campaign against cryptocurrency developers by posing as recruiters on LinkedIn, distributing benign PDF job descriptions with embedded coding challenges, and redirecting targets to malicious GitHub repositories containing Python and JavaScript code laced with YAML deserialization and EJS escapeFunction backdoors; once activated under specific conditions, these backdoors deploy in-memory RN Loader and RN Stealer payloads to collect system information, establish C2 communications, and exfiltrate SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations with minimal forensic footprint—building on past successes that netted over $1 billion in 2023 and $1.5 billion in 2024—and highlighting the urgent need for enhanced vetting on professional platforms, proactive detection of unsafe deserialization and templating flaws, and memory-based threat monitoring to defend the cryptocurrency sector.
hits.title: Slow Pisces Group Targets Developers Using Coding Challenges Laced with Python Malware

hits.text: Since at least 2019, the North Korea–affiliated APT group Kimsuky has conducted spear-phishing campaigns using malicious lure documents to deploy a potent mix of backdoors and RATs—most notably the Windows/Android DLL AppleSeed (aka JamBog), its Golang-based AlphaSeed variant (leveraging the chromedp library for DevTools-driven C2), Meterpreter, TightVNC and TinyNuke (Nuclear Bot)—to establish C2 via HTTP, SMTP or headless‐Chrome, drop additional payloads and exfiltrate files, keystrokes and screenshots; evidence shows some intrusions since October 2022 delivered both AppleSeed and AlphaSeed via a JavaScript dropper. Active for over a decade—initially targeting South Korean entities before expanding globally in 2017—and recently sanctioned by the U.S. for intelligence gathering to further North Korea’s strategic objectives, Kimsuky has also created fraudulent LinkedIn and GitHub personas to secure remote tech contracts, generating revenue and facilitating multi-pronged blockchain and cryptocurrency theft to evade sanctions and support regime priorities.
hits.title: Kimsuky Hackers Deploying AppleSeed, Meterpreter, and TinyNuke in Latest Attacks

hits.text: ESET researchers disclosed MoustachedBouncer, a Belarus-aligned cyberespionage group active since at least 2014 targeting foreign embassies in Belarus, employing two parallel malware frameworks: the email-based NightClub (SMTP/IMAP C2) and its 2020-onward successor Disco (Go/.NET) delivered via adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) at ISP level—likely leveraging Belarus’s SORM lawful interception—to redirect Windows captive portal checks to a fake Windows Update page. This page loads jdrop.js to prompt a malicious installer, which schedules SMB-delivered OfficeBroker payloads from attacker-injected Google Cloud IPs. Both frameworks support plugins for screenshots, audio recording and file theft. ESET observed compromises of embassies from four continents and assesses medium confidence in state alignment and low confidence in cooperation with Winter Vivern. Recommendations include out-of-band encrypted VPNs to thwart ISP-level interception.

hits.text: In November 2023, Iran-linked espionage group Seedworm (aka MuddyWater and subordinate to MOIS) launched a targeted cyber-espionage campaign against telecommunications organizations in Egypt, Sudan and Tanzania using its Go-based MuddyC2Go framework alongside both living-off-the-land and custom tools to maintain persistence, harvest credentials and exfiltrate data. Researchers observed a PowerShell-based MuddyC2Go DLL launcher named “vcruntime140.dll” sideloaded by the legitimate Java executable jabswitch.exe into csidl_common_appdata\javax, which read C2 URIs (“End” and “Status” values under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip) before invoking Invoke-WebRequest to contacts servers such as 95.164.38.99:443 and 45.150.64.39:443; the backdoor was executed via a scheduled task (“Microsoft\Windows\JavaX\Java Autorun”), while Impacket’s WMIExec, Revsocks (94.131.3.160:443), and SimpleHelp (146.70.124.102) were leveraged for lateral movement, SAM hive dumps, drive reconnaissance and remote administration alongside AnyDesk and a custom keylogger. This activity followed a prior Seedworm intrusion earlier in 2023 into at least one victim using SimpleHelp-driven PowerShell, proxy tools, LSASS dumping and JumpCloud deployment, confirming group attribution. Seedworm’s blend of custom C2 innovation and publicly available/proxy tools underscores the necessity for defenders to monitor for anomalous PowerShell invocations to suspect domains, unexpected Java sideloading, scheduled task creations, unauthorized SimpleHelp or AnyDesk services, Venom Proxy processes, and registry modifications in telecom-grade networks to detect and disrupt its persistent espionage operations.
hits.title: Seedworm: Iranian Hackers Target Telecoms Orgs in North and East Africa | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea
hits.text: In early 2018 McAfee Advanced Threat Research uncovered Operation Honeybee, a North Korean–linked campaign—tracked to the persona snoopykiller@mail.ru and control domains navermail.byethost3.com/nihon.byethost11.com—targeting humanitarian aid groups and regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea with malicious Microsoft Word documents named “Honeybee” that exploited politically themed and generic “not compatible” lures to execute VBA macros embedding a custom‐alphabet Base64 payload. Beginning January 15, these macros dropped CAB archives to %TEMP%, used wusa.exe or expand.exe for UAC bypass, then hijacked cliconfg.exe via a malicious NTWDBLIB.dll to install a persistent COMSysApp service loading ipnet.dll from %SystemRoot%\System32. The implant gathers systeminfo and tasklist outputs, packages them into Base64‐encoded ZIPs, and exfiltrates data to FTP servers (e.g., 1113427185.ifastnet.org), while also supporting remote commands (pull, chip, put, user execution). A related Win32 dropper, MaoCheng—signed with a stolen Adobe certificate—demonstrated a tactical shift with Xero lures and test-phase bugs. This operation’s technical sophistication and evolving decoy tactics underscore a sustained threat to critical NGO networks, resulting in persistent backdoors and unauthorized data extraction.
hits.title: McAfee Uncovers Operation Honeybee, a Malicious Campaign Targeting Humanitarian Aid Groups | McAfee Blog

canonical_entities: diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine
hits.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.

canonical_entities: regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea
retrieved_context.text: In early 2018 McAfee Advanced Threat Research uncovered Operation Honeybee, a North Korean–linked campaign—tracked to the persona snoopykiller@mail.ru and control domains navermail.byethost3.com/nihon.byethost11.com—targeting humanitarian aid groups and regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea with malicious Microsoft Word documents named “Honeybee” that exploited politically themed and generic “not compatible” lures to execute VBA macros embedding a custom‐alphabet Base64 payload. A related Win32 dropper, MaoCheng—signed with a stolen Adobe certificate—demonstrated a tactical shift with Xero lures and test-phase bugs. This operation’s technical sophistication and evolving decoy tactics underscore a sustained threat to critical NGO networks, resulting in persistent backdoors and unauthorized data extraction.

hits.text: Since at least 2019, the North Korea–affiliated APT group Kimsuky has conducted spear-phishing campaigns using malicious lure documents to deploy a potent mix of backdoors and RATs—most notably the Windows/Android DLL AppleSeed (aka JamBog), its Golang-based AlphaSeed variant (leveraging the chromedp library for DevTools-driven C2), Meterpreter, TightVNC and TinyNuke (Nuclear Bot)—to establish C2 via HTTP, SMTP or headless‐Chrome, drop additional payloads and exfiltrate files, keystrokes and screenshots; evidence shows some intrusions since October 2022 delivered both AppleSeed and AlphaSeed via a JavaScript dropper. Active for over a decade—initially targeting South Korean entities before expanding globally in 2017—and recently sanctioned by the U.S. for intelligence gathering to further North Korea’s strategic objectives, Kimsuky has also created fraudulent LinkedIn and GitHub personas to secure remote tech contracts, generating revenue and facilitating multi-pronged blockchain and cryptocurrency theft to evade sanctions and support regime priorities.
hits.title: Kimsuky Hackers Deploying AppleSeed, Meterpreter, and TinyNuke in Latest Attacks

hits.text: Between March and July 2025, DPRK-linked Kimsuky operators executed at least 19 highly tailored spear-phishing attacks against Western, Central, Eastern and Southern European embassies in Seoul, spoofing real diplomats and embedding password-protected ZIPs delivered via Dropbox, Daum or Google Drive. Victims unwittingly launched malicious .LNK shortcuts that triggered obfuscated PowerShell scripts to decode and in-memory execute a Confuser-Core-obfuscated XenoRAT (MoonPeak) payload—identified by GUID 12DE1212-167D-45BA-1284-780DA98CF901 and mutex “Dansweit_Hk65-PSAccerdle”—leveraging scheduled tasks for persistence. Reconnaissance data (OS build, IP, process list) was exfiltrated as base64-encoded text files over HTTPS to the attackers’ private GitHub repo via the Contents API, while C2 instructions (e.g., onf.txt) directed dynamic payload rotations hosted on Dropbox with rapid header-fix GZIP routines. This ongoing campaign provided full system control—including keystroke logging, screenshots and remote shells—and underscores the need to monitor abnormal GitHub API usage, cloud-based archive downloads and anomalous PowerShell invocations.
hits.title: The Coordinated Embassy Hunt: Unmasking the DPRK-linked GitHub C2 Espionage Campaign

ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.

hits.text: Researchers have identified a new ransomware strain dubbed Magniber—an affiliate of both the Magnitude exploit kit and Cerber ransomware—exclusively targeting users in South Korea and the Asia-Pacific region following Magnitude’s reemergence on October 15, 2017, after a brief hiatus during which its Cerber distribution waned. FireEye and Trend Micro findings reveal that Magniber leverages malvertising and IE memory corruption vulnerability CVE-2016-0189 to deliver a binary payload encrypted in reverse RC4 with 30-byte keys, unpacks it in memory, then executes an AES-128 encryption routine that renames files with a “.ihsdj” extension before self-deletion. It employs a GetSystemDefaultUILanguage check to exit on non-Korean systems and generates four callback URLs via a 19-character pseudorandom string to evade virtual machines. Organizations should prioritize patching IE CVE-2016-0189, deploy ad blockers and updated exploit kit defenses, and monitor for Magnitude EK activity in APAC environments.
hits.title: New Magniber Ransomware Targets South Korea, Asia Pacific | Threatpost

canonical_entities: LNK files in the Windows Startup folder
HTTP POST exfiltration with Base64 encoding
hits.text: Cisco Talos analysts have uncovered PS1Bot, a sophisticated multi‐stage malware framework active throughout 2025 that leverages malvertising campaigns—delivering SEO‐styled ZIPs like “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”—to drop a JavaScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) which retrieves modular PowerShell and C# components in memory via Invoke-Expression, minimizing disk footprint and evading AV. Once executed, PS1Bot establishes persistence by creating randomly named PS1 scripts in %PROGRAMDATA% and corresponding LNK files in the Windows Startup folder that poll a C2 “/transform” endpoint for obfuscated payloads, using the host’s C: drive serial number to generate unique communication URLs. The framework’s on‐demand modules include information stealers, keyloggers, screen capture tools and advanced crypto wallet extractors that scan for seed-phrase wordlists in multiple languages, compress findings and exfiltrate via HTTP POST with Base64 encoding. Continuous sample updates and code overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet‐linked families suggest shared development resources or actor collaboration, highlighting the need for defenses that detect anomalous PowerShell IEX activity, monitor suspicious JavaScript downloaders and Startup LNK creations, and inspect outbound HTTP traffic for drive‐serial based URLs and wallet data exfiltration.
hits.title: Threat Actors Attacking Windows Systems With New Multi-Stage Malware Framework PS1Bot

canonical_entities: malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails
hits.text: Attackers are leveraging the six-year-old CVE-2017-11882 Microsoft Office RCE vulnerability via malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails to initiate a multi-stage infection chain that delivers the Agent Tesla RAT and advanced keylogger. Once a user opens the Excel file on an unpatched Office build, it connects to a malicious server to retrieve a heavily obfuscated VBS script, which in turn downloads a JPEG containing a Base64-encoded DLL. The VBS launches PowerShell to extract and load the DLL, then abuses RegAsm.exe—disguised as a legitimate registry utility—to inject a thread that fetches and executes the Agent Tesla payload. Deployed Agent Tesla uses clipboard and window hooking for keystroke logging, screen capture and browser, mail and FTP credential theft, exfiltrating data via attacker-controlled Telegram bots. Zscaler’s detailed IoCs—including malicious URLs, file hashes and Telegram endpoints—underscore the critical need for organizations to patch legacy Office versions, deploy email defenses, and monitor for the described artifacts to prevent credential compromise and system takeover.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit 6-Year-Old Microsoft Office Bug to Spread Spyware

hits.text: Google has released Chrome 120.0.6099.129/130 updates to patch an actively exploited high-severity zero-day (CVE-2023-7024), a heap-based buffer overflow in the WebRTC framework that enables crashes or arbitrary code execution, discovered by TAG researchers Clément Lecigne and Vlad Stolyarov on December 19, 2023. This marks the eighth Chrome zero-day exploited in the wild this year—following type confusion flaws in V8 (CVE-2023-2033, CVSS 8.8; CVE-2023-2136, CVSS 9.6; CVE-2023-3079, CVSS 8.8; CVE-2023-4762, CVSS 8.8), a heap overflow in WebP (CVE-2023-4863, CVSS 8.8), a heap overflow in libvpx (CVE-2023-5217, CVSS 8.8) and an integer overflow in Skia (CVE-2023-6345, CVSS 9.6)—amid a record 26,447 CVEs disclosed in 2023, 115 of which have been weaponized by threat actors and ransomware groups using remote code execution, security-feature bypass, buffer manipulation, privilege escalation and input-validation flaws. Given WebRTC’s cross-browser support, impacts on Firefox and Safari remain under assessment. Administrators and end users should immediately upgrade Chrome for Windows, macOS and Linux and apply forthcoming patches for Chromium-based browsers (Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi) to mitigate potential compromise.
hits.title: Urgent: New Chrome Zero-Day Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild - Update ASAP

hits.text: ESET Research uncovered Operation AkaiRyū, a spearphishing-driven cyberespionage campaign conducted by the China-aligned MirrorFace APT (now assessed as a subgroup under the APT10 umbrella) against a Central European diplomatic institute between June and September 2024, using Expo 2025-themed lures referencing prior NGO communications to deliver password-protected Word documents and malicious links; this marks MirrorFace’s first known European targeting. Analysis revealed a significant TTP refresh: the revival of the ANEL (UPPERCUT) backdoor—previously exclusive to APT10—for file manipulation, payload execution and screenshots; a heavily customized AsyncRAT variant stealthily run inside Windows Sandbox via a complex execution chain; continued deployment of the HiddenFace backdoor; and abuse of Visual Studio Code’s remote tunnels for covert access and arbitrary code execution. Attackers abused legitimate McAfee and JustSystems applications to load ANEL, evading detection, while data exfiltration methods remain unclear. ESET’s forensic collaboration with the victim and JSAC presentation in January 2025 provide actionable insights to monitor for ANEL indicators, sandboxed RAT executions, VS Code tunnel anomalies and Expo-themed spearphishing.
hits.title: ESET Research uncovers Operation AkaiRyū: China-aligned MirrorFace targets European diplomats using Expo 2025 as a lure | | ESET

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

hits.text: New research reveals that over 80,000 Hikvision cameras worldwide remain unpatched against the critical CVE-2021-36260 command-injection flaw (NIST score 9.8/10) disclosed last fall, allowing remote code execution and potential espionage by state-linked groups such as MISSION2025/APT41, APT10 and unknown Russian actors trading stolen credentials on dark-web forums; systemic deficiencies—default or hardcoded passwords, no auto-update mechanism, poor forensics and lack of security-by-design—have left devices in 100+ countries (including the U.S., despite an FCC “unacceptable risk” designation) continuously discoverable via Shodan or Censys and ripe for exploitation, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to inventory IoT assets, change default credentials, deploy available patches and improve visibility and update processes to mitigate geopolitical and operational impact.

hits.text: North Korean state-sponsored APT Slow Pisces (aka Jade Sleet, TraderTraitor, PUKCHONG) is executing a sophisticated three-stage campaign against cryptocurrency developers by posing as recruiters on LinkedIn, distributing benign PDF job descriptions with embedded coding challenges, and redirecting targets to malicious GitHub repositories containing Python and JavaScript code laced with YAML deserialization and EJS escapeFunction backdoors; once activated under specific conditions, these backdoors deploy in-memory RN Loader and RN Stealer payloads to collect system information, establish C2 communications, and exfiltrate SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations with minimal forensic footprint—building on past successes that netted over $1 billion in 2023 and $1.5 billion in 2024—and highlighting the urgent need for enhanced vetting on professional platforms, proactive detection of unsafe deserialization and templating flaws, and memory-based threat monitoring to defend the cryptocurrency sector.

hits.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.

hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.

hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.

hits.text: Dragos researchers, in collaboration with Ukraine’s CSSC, unearthed FrostyGoop—an ICS-specific malware first spotted in April and used in January to disrupt central heating in over 600 Lviv apartment buildings—marking the first known malware to leverage Modbus TCP for read/write operations on operational technology. Attackers gained initial access in April 2023 by exploiting a MikroTik router vulnerability, deployed a webshell on the router’s web server, and maintained persistence via Tor and L2TP tunnels to Moscow-based IPs. After spending months conducting reconnaissance, they extracted credentials by dumping the SAM registry hive in December, then directly issued scripted Modbus commands—read from a JSON configuration file—to publicly exposed ENCO heating controllers, even downgrading firmware to disable monitoring and force inaccurate measurements that halted heating services for nearly two days amid subzero temperatures. This incident underscores the threat posed by internet-exposed ICS devices—over 46,000 globally using Modbus—and highlights poor network segmentation, unpatched ICS CVEs, and the ease with which FrostyGoop’s protocol-agnostic payload can be repurposed against diverse industrial controllers, necessitating immediate network segmentation, firmware monitoring, and patch management in OT environments.
hits.title: ICS malware FrostyGoop disrupted heating in Ukraine, remains threat to OT worldwide

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.

hits.text: Since at least August 2023, threat actors have exploited CVE-2023-4966 (CitrixBleed), a 7.5-rated flaw in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway, culminating in an October 16–19 breach at Comcast Xfinity that exposed 35,879,455 customers’ usernames, hashed passwords, names, contact details, last four SSN digits, dates of birth and security Q&A; despite Citrix’s October 10 patch and Comcast’s claim of prompt mitigation, attackers used publicly available proofs-of-concept and rumored Python automation scripts to extract session tokens from device memory, hijack active sessions and bypass authentication, a tactic linked by ReliaQuest to at least five threat groups including LockBit; this incident highlights the necessity not only of timely patching and reboots but also of invalidating all active and persistent session tokens, enforcing multi-factor authentication, resetting credentials and maintaining continuous 24x7 monitoring to prevent further data exfiltration and ransomware deployment.

retrieved_context.text: ESET Research uncovered Operation AkaiRyū, a spearphishing-driven cyberespionage campaign conducted by the China-aligned MirrorFace APT (now assessed as a subgroup under the APT10 umbrella) against a Central European diplomatic institute between June and September 2024, using Expo 2025-themed lures referencing prior NGO communications to deliver password-protected Word documents and malicious links; this marks MirrorFace’s first known European targeting. Analysis revealed a significant TTP refresh: the revival of the ANEL (UPPERCUT) backdoor—previously exclusive to APT10—for file manipulation, payload execution and screenshots; a heavily customized AsyncRAT variant stealthily run inside Windows Sandbox via a complex execution chain; continued deployment of the HiddenFace backdoor; and abuse of Visual Studio Code’s remote tunnels for covert access and arbitrary code execution. Attackers abused legitimate McAfee and JustSystems applications to load ANEL, evading detection, while data exfiltration methods remain unclear. ESET’s forensic collaboration with the victim and JSAC presentation in January 2025 provide actionable insights to monitor for ANEL indicators, sandboxed RAT executions, VS Code tunnel anomalies and Expo-themed spearphishing.
retrieved_context.title: ESET Research uncovers Operation AkaiRyū: China-aligned MirrorFace targets European diplomats using Expo 2025 as a lure | | ESET

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
