canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: In early April, Palo Alto Networks’ Advanced WildFire and Cortex XDR uncovered SnipBot—a new v5.0 iteration of the RomCom RAT family—employing advanced window message–based control-flow obfuscation and anti-sandbox checks (filename hash and HKCU\…\RecentDocs entries) in a multi-stage chain beginning with a PDF-labeled EXE downloader signed using a likely stolen certificate; the downloader contacts xeontime[.]com for config-pdf.dll, which uses registry-based COM hijacking to load keyprov.dll from drvmcprotect[.]com into explorer.exe, decrypts payloads stored in HKCU\Software\AppDataSoft\Software, and opens a TCP listener on port 1342 for commands to update, delete, or execute modules. The main backdoor single.dll (mutex “SnipMutex”) supports 27 encrypted commands for drive and process enumeration, file upload/download, and remote module execution, facilitating network pivoting and targeted file exfiltration. Active since December 2023 (RomCom activity since 2022), SnipBot’s tactics, stolen certificates, unique obfuscation, and sophisticated loader underscore a high-risk threat actor likely focused on intelligence gathering; Palo Alto products classify its samples, URLs, and domains as malicious to prevent compromise.
hits.title: Inside SnipBot: The Latest RomCom Malware Variant

canonical_entities: regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea
hits.text: In early 2018 McAfee Advanced Threat Research uncovered Operation Honeybee, a North Korean–linked campaign—tracked to the persona snoopykiller@mail.ru and control domains navermail.byethost3.com/nihon.byethost11.com—targeting humanitarian aid groups and regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea with malicious Microsoft Word documents named “Honeybee” that exploited politically themed and generic “not compatible” lures to execute VBA macros embedding a custom‐alphabet Base64 payload. Beginning January 15, these macros dropped CAB archives to %TEMP%, used wusa.exe or expand.exe for UAC bypass, then hijacked cliconfg.exe via a malicious NTWDBLIB.dll to install a persistent COMSysApp service loading ipnet.dll from %SystemRoot%\System32. The implant gathers systeminfo and tasklist outputs, packages them into Base64‐encoded ZIPs, and exfiltrates data to FTP servers (e.g., 1113427185.ifastnet.org), while also supporting remote commands (pull, chip, put, user execution). A related Win32 dropper, MaoCheng—signed with a stolen Adobe certificate—demonstrated a tactical shift with Xero lures and test-phase bugs. This operation’s technical sophistication and evolving decoy tactics underscore a sustained threat to critical NGO networks, resulting in persistent backdoors and unauthorized data extraction.
hits.title: McAfee Uncovers Operation Honeybee, a Malicious Campaign Targeting Humanitarian Aid Groups | McAfee Blog

canonical_entities: LNK files in the Windows Startup folder

hits.text: Cisco Talos analysts have uncovered PS1Bot, a sophisticated multi‐stage malware framework active throughout 2025 that leverages malvertising campaigns—delivering SEO‐styled ZIPs like “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”—to drop a JavaScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) which retrieves modular PowerShell and C# components in memory via Invoke-Expression, minimizing disk footprint and evading AV. Once executed, PS1Bot establishes persistence by creating randomly named PS1 scripts in %PROGRAMDATA% and corresponding LNK files in the Windows Startup folder that poll a C2 “/transform” endpoint for obfuscated payloads, using the host’s C: drive serial number to generate unique communication URLs. The framework’s on‐demand modules include information stealers, keyloggers, screen capture tools and advanced crypto wallet extractors that scan for seed-phrase wordlists in multiple languages, compress findings and exfiltrate via HTTP POST with Base64 encoding. Continuous sample updates and code overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet‐linked families suggest shared development resources or actor collaboration, highlighting the need for defenses that detect anomalous PowerShell IEX activity, monitor suspicious JavaScript downloaders and Startup LNK creations, and inspect outbound HTTP traffic for drive‐serial based URLs and wallet data exfiltration.

canonical_entities: Visual Basic macros in MS Word documents
hits.text: Operation Honeybee, first observed in August 2017 and publicly detailed in March 2018, is a cross-border cyber-espionage campaign attributed to the Honeybee actor that weaponizes Korean-themed MS Word documents containing Visual Basic macros to deploy the SYSCON backdoor against humanitarian aid organizations and government entities across South Korea, Vietnam, Singapore, Argentina, Japan, Indonesia and Canada. Upon opening the malicious document (e.g., “manual.doc”), the Document_Open() macro opens a handle to an embedded, encoded CAB file, decodes it to %temp%\setup.cab, drops two DLLs (NTWDBLIB.dll and cliconfg.exe) and a Win32 executable dropper signed with a stolen Adobe Systems certificate, then reaches out to the 1113427185.ifastnet.org command-and-control server to fetch the main payload. The backdoor leverages the same unique SYSCON key used in prior operations, bypasses User Access Control via the dropped DLLs and executable, escalates privileges, and exfiltrates system information—including running process lists and sensitive files—over FTP, posing a significant data-theft threat to targeted organizations.
hits.title: Operation Honeybee - A Cyber Attack Leveraging a SYSCON Backdoor Using MS Word Documents

hits.text: CISA has added CVE-2022-22047—a high-severity (CVSS 7.8) elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Client Server Runtime Subsystem used since Windows 7 through Windows 11 and Server 2008–2022—to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and is urging federal agencies to install Microsoft’s July 5 Patch Tuesday update by August 2 after evidence emerged of in-the-wild exploitation; initially disclosed as a zero-day by Microsoft’s security team, the CSRSS bug enables adversaries who already hold local or physical access—or who gain remote code execution via malware or specially crafted Office/Adobe documents and macros—to escalate to SYSTEM privileges for lateral movement, although FortiGuard Labs rates the overall business threat as “medium” given the prerequisite foothold and available patch, while Trend Micro’s ZDI notes such elevation flaws are typically paired with a separate RCE vector and Microsoft has signaled future default blocking of VBA macros to mitigate this attack chain.
hits.title: CISA Urges Patch of Exploited Windows 11 Bug by Aug. 2 | Threatpost

hits.text: Google has released Chrome 120.0.6099.129/130 updates to patch an actively exploited high-severity zero-day (CVE-2023-7024), a heap-based buffer overflow in the WebRTC framework that enables crashes or arbitrary code execution, discovered by TAG researchers Clément Lecigne and Vlad Stolyarov on December 19, 2023. This marks the eighth Chrome zero-day exploited in the wild this year—following type confusion flaws in V8 (CVE-2023-2033, CVSS 8.8; CVE-2023-2136, CVSS 9.6; CVE-2023-3079, CVSS 8.8; CVE-2023-4762, CVSS 8.8), a heap overflow in WebP (CVE-2023-4863, CVSS 8.8), a heap overflow in libvpx (CVE-2023-5217, CVSS 8.8) and an integer overflow in Skia (CVE-2023-6345, CVSS 9.6)—amid a record 26,447 CVEs disclosed in 2023, 115 of which have been weaponized by threat actors and ransomware groups using remote code execution, security-feature bypass, buffer manipulation, privilege escalation and input-validation flaws. Given WebRTC’s cross-browser support, impacts on Firefox and Safari remain under assessment. Administrators and end users should immediately upgrade Chrome for Windows, macOS and Linux and apply forthcoming patches for Chromium-based browsers (Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi) to mitigate potential compromise.
hits.title: Urgent: New Chrome Zero-Day Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild - Update ASAP

retrieved_context.text: ESET Research uncovered Operation AkaiRyū, a spearphishing-driven cyberespionage campaign conducted by the China-aligned MirrorFace APT (now assessed as a subgroup under the APT10 umbrella) against a Central European diplomatic institute between June and September 2024, using Expo 2025-themed lures referencing prior NGO communications to deliver password-protected Word documents and malicious links; this marks MirrorFace’s first known European targeting. Analysis revealed a significant TTP refresh: the revival of the ANEL (UPPERCUT) backdoor—previously exclusive to APT10—for file manipulation, payload execution and screenshots; a heavily customized AsyncRAT variant stealthily run inside Windows Sandbox via a complex execution chain; continued deployment of the HiddenFace backdoor; and abuse of Visual Studio Code’s remote tunnels for covert access and arbitrary code execution. Attackers abused legitimate McAfee and JustSystems applications to load ANEL, evading detection, while data exfiltration methods remain unclear. ESET’s forensic collaboration with the victim and JSAC presentation in January 2025 provide actionable insights to monitor for ANEL indicators, sandboxed RAT executions, VS Code tunnel anomalies and Expo-themed spearphishing.
retrieved_context.title: ESET Research uncovers Operation AkaiRyū: China-aligned MirrorFace targets European diplomats using Expo 2025 as a lure | | ESET

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: In early April, Palo Alto Networks’ Advanced WildFire and Cortex XDR uncovered SnipBot—a new v5.0 iteration of the RomCom RAT family—employing advanced window message–based control-flow obfuscation and anti-sandbox checks (filename hash and HKCU\…\RecentDocs entries) in a multi-stage chain beginning with a PDF-labeled EXE downloader signed using a likely stolen certificate; the downloader contacts xeontime[.]com for config-pdf.dll, which uses registry-based COM hijacking to load keyprov.dll from drvmcprotect[.]com into explorer.exe, decrypts payloads stored in HKCU\Software\AppDataSoft\Software, and opens a TCP listener on port 1342 for commands to update, delete, or execute modules. The main backdoor single.dll (mutex “SnipMutex”) supports 27 encrypted commands for drive and process enumeration, file upload/download, and remote module execution, facilitating network pivoting and targeted file exfiltration. Active since December 2023 (RomCom activity since 2022), SnipBot’s tactics, stolen certificates, unique obfuscation, and sophisticated loader underscore a high-risk threat actor likely focused on intelligence gathering; Palo Alto products classify its samples, URLs, and domains as malicious to prevent compromise.
retrieved_context.title: Inside SnipBot: The Latest RomCom Malware Variant

canonical_entities: regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea
retrieved_context.text: In early 2018 McAfee Advanced Threat Research uncovered Operation Honeybee, a North Korean–linked campaign—tracked to the persona snoopykiller@mail.ru and control domains navermail.byethost3.com/nihon.byethost11.com—targeting humanitarian aid groups and regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea with malicious Microsoft Word documents named “Honeybee” that exploited politically themed and generic “not compatible” lures to execute VBA macros embedding a custom‐alphabet Base64 payload. Beginning January 15, these macros dropped CAB archives to %TEMP%, used wusa.exe or expand.exe for UAC bypass, then hijacked cliconfg.exe via a malicious NTWDBLIB.dll to install a persistent COMSysApp service loading ipnet.dll from %SystemRoot%\System32. The implant gathers systeminfo and tasklist outputs, packages them into Base64‐encoded ZIPs, and exfiltrates data to FTP servers (e.g., 1113427185.ifastnet.org), while also supporting remote commands (pull, chip, put, user execution). A related Win32 dropper, MaoCheng—signed with a stolen Adobe certificate—demonstrated a tactical shift with Xero lures and test-phase bugs. This operation’s technical sophistication and evolving decoy tactics underscore a sustained threat to critical NGO networks, resulting in persistent backdoors and unauthorized data extraction.
retrieved_context.title: McAfee Uncovers Operation Honeybee, a Malicious Campaign Targeting Humanitarian Aid Groups | McAfee Blog

canonical_entities: LNK files in the Windows Startup folder
HTTP POST exfiltration with Base64 encoding
retrieved_context.text: Cisco Talos analysts have uncovered PS1Bot, a sophisticated multi‐stage malware framework active throughout 2025 that leverages malvertising campaigns—delivering SEO‐styled ZIPs like “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”—to drop a JavaScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) which retrieves modular PowerShell and C# components in memory via Invoke-Expression, minimizing disk footprint and evading AV. Once executed, PS1Bot establishes persistence by creating randomly named PS1 scripts in %PROGRAMDATA% and corresponding LNK files in the Windows Startup folder that poll a C2 “/transform” endpoint for obfuscated payloads, using the host’s C: drive serial number to generate unique communication URLs. The framework’s on‐demand modules include information stealers, keyloggers, screen capture tools and advanced crypto wallet extractors that scan for seed-phrase wordlists in multiple languages, compress findings and exfiltrate via HTTP POST with Base64 encoding. Continuous sample updates and code overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet‐linked families suggest shared development resources or actor collaboration, highlighting the need for defenses that detect anomalous PowerShell IEX activity, monitor suspicious JavaScript downloaders and Startup LNK creations, and inspect outbound HTTP traffic for drive‐serial based URLs and wallet data exfiltration.
retrieved_context.title: Threat Actors Attacking Windows Systems With New Multi-Stage Malware Framework PS1Bot

retrieved_context.text: New research reveals that over 80,000 Hikvision cameras worldwide remain unpatched against the critical CVE-2021-36260 command-injection flaw (NIST score 9.8/10) disclosed last fall, allowing remote code execution and potential espionage by state-linked groups such as MISSION2025/APT41, APT10 and unknown Russian actors trading stolen credentials on dark-web forums; systemic deficiencies—default or hardcoded passwords, no auto-update mechanism, poor forensics and lack of security-by-design—have left devices in 100+ countries (including the U.S., despite an FCC “unacceptable risk” designation) continuously discoverable via Shodan or Censys and ripe for exploitation, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to inventory IoT assets, change default credentials, deploy available patches and improve visibility and update processes to mitigate geopolitical and operational impact.
retrieved_context.title: Cybercriminals Are Selling Access to Chinese Surveillance Cameras | Threatpost

canonical_entities: Visual Basic macros in MS Word documents
retrieved_context.text: Operation Honeybee, first observed in August 2017 and publicly detailed in March 2018, is a cross-border cyber-espionage campaign attributed to the Honeybee actor that weaponizes Korean-themed MS Word documents containing Visual Basic macros to deploy the SYSCON backdoor against humanitarian aid organizations and government entities across South Korea, Vietnam, Singapore, Argentina, Japan, Indonesia and Canada. Upon opening the malicious document (e.g., “manual.doc”), the Document_Open() macro opens a handle to an embedded, encoded CAB file, decodes it to %temp%\setup.cab, drops two DLLs (NTWDBLIB.dll and cliconfg.exe) and a Win32 executable dropper signed with a stolen Adobe Systems certificate, then reaches out to the 1113427185.ifastnet.org command-and-control server to fetch the main payload. The backdoor leverages the same unique SYSCON key used in prior operations, bypasses User Access Control via the dropped DLLs and executable, escalates privileges, and exfiltrates system information—including running process lists and sensitive files—over FTP, posing a significant data-theft threat to targeted organizations.
retrieved_context.title: Operation Honeybee - A Cyber Attack Leveraging a SYSCON Backdoor Using MS Word Documents

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.

hits.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
hits.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: McAfee Mobile Research Team uncovered Xamalicious, a new Android backdoor built with Xamarin that abuses accessibility permissions to harvest device metadata, query a C2 server for a second-stage payload, and dynamically inject an assembly DLL to perform unauthorized ad-clicking, app installs and other financially motivated actions; this threat has been embedded in 25 apps—ranging from horoscope and gaming to utility tools—on Google Play since mid-2020, amassing over 327,000 installations across Brazil, Argentina, the UK, Australia, the US, Mexico and Europe. To evade detection, Xamalicious encrypts all C2 traffic as JWE tokens (RSA-OAEP/128CBC-HS256), self-updates its APK to transform into spyware or a banking trojan, and links back to the Cash Magnet ad-fraud campaign; its use of non-Java frameworks like Xamarin underscores heightened obfuscation. Google Play Protect now blocks or auto-removes infected apps. Separately, a malicious WhatsApp-based phishing campaign in India distributes fake SBI APKs invoking SMS permissions to capture credentials, banking and identity data, then exfiltrates them for unauthorized transactions.
hits.title: New Sneaky Xamalicious Android Malware Hits Over 327,000 Devices

canonical_entities: spear-phishing attacks against European embassies in Seoul (March–July 2025)
exfiltrated ... over HTTPS to the attackers’ private GitHub repo via the Contents API
hits.text: Between March and July 2025, DPRK-linked Kimsuky operators executed at least 19 highly tailored spear-phishing attacks against Western, Central, Eastern and Southern European embassies in Seoul, spoofing real diplomats and embedding password-protected ZIPs delivered via Dropbox, Daum or Google Drive. Victims unwittingly launched malicious .LNK shortcuts that triggered obfuscated PowerShell scripts to decode and in-memory execute a Confuser-Core-obfuscated XenoRAT (MoonPeak) payload—identified by GUID 12DE1212-167D-45BA-1284-780DA98CF901 and mutex “Dansweit_Hk65-PSAccerdle”—leveraging scheduled tasks for persistence. Reconnaissance data (OS build, IP, process list) was exfiltrated as base64-encoded text files over HTTPS to the attackers’ private GitHub repo via the Contents API, while C2 instructions (e.g., onf.txt) directed dynamic payload rotations hosted on Dropbox with rapid header-fix GZIP routines. This ongoing campaign provided full system control—including keystroke logging, screenshots and remote shells—and underscores the need to monitor abnormal GitHub API usage, cloud-based archive downloads and anomalous PowerShell invocations.
hits.title: The Coordinated Embassy Hunt: Unmasking the DPRK-linked GitHub C2 Espionage Campaign

canonical_entities: Western nation’s military mission in Ukraine
hits.text: In February–March 2025, Russia-linked espionage group Shuckworm (aka Gamaredon/Armageddon) targeted a Western nation’s military mission in Ukraine using a multi-stage PowerShell-centric campaign initiated via an infected removable drive and malicious .lnk file. Obfuscated VBScript (~.drv) deployed through mshta.exe and wscript.exe created registry-named payloads: one performing WMI ping checks to mil.gov.ua before resolving dynamic C2 addresses via Teletype, Telegra.ph, t.me, check-host.net and Cloudflare tunnels (e.g., 107.189.19.218), and another altering Explorer registry keys to hide system files and propagate shortcuts across USB and network shares. The attackers then delivered an updated PowerShell infostealer (GammaSteel) alongside reconnaissance scripts that captured screenshots, systeminfo, process lists and host metadata, exfiltrating sensitive documents (*.docx, *.pptx, *.pdf) using PowerShell web requests with certutil-computed MD5 hashes and fallback cURL over Tor to mask origin. This campaign underscores Shuckworm’s shift from VBS to PowerShell, leveraging in-registry script storage and heavy obfuscation to evade detection, with indicators including anomalous UserAssist entries, unusual mshta/wscript invocations and atypical C2 resolution patterns.
hits.title: Shuckworm Targets Foreign Military Mission Based in Ukraine | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: In February 2022, CISA, the FBI, US Cyber Command CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA issued a joint advisory on Iranian Ministry of Intelligence–linked APT MuddyWater (aka MERCURY, Earth Vetala, Static Kitten, Seedworm, TEMP.Zagros), active since 2018 and focused on cyber espionage, intellectual property theft and ransomware against defense, oil & gas, government and telecom sectors across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America. Exploiting publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and open-source tools, MuddyWater delivers malicious PDFs with embedded links that display error messages prompting users to download Excel maldocs or Windows executables; these files host VBA macros that drop WSF scripts to execute PowerShell and VB payloads, leverage LoLBins, and stage RATs and malware families including PowGoop, Canopy, Small Sieve, POWERSTATS and Mori while communicating with C2 over HTTP and DNS and persisting via Registry Run keys. Cisco Talos observed regional campaigns in Turkey (Nov 2021), Pakistan (Aug 2021) and Armenia (Jun 2021) using decoy documents, signaling tokens and a consistent TTP set, suggesting a conglomerate of subgroups migrating techniques across regions. The resultant network access and data exfiltration underscore the imperative for proactive DFIR readiness, deployment of XDR/MDR platforms, rigorous vulnerability management, macro execution restrictions, PowerShell/LoLBin monitoring and ongoing user awareness training reinforced by incident response tabletop exercises.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at Iranian APT "MuddyWater"

PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
retrieved_context.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: McAfee Mobile Research Team uncovered Xamalicious, a new Android backdoor built with Xamarin that abuses accessibility permissions to harvest device metadata, query a C2 server for a second-stage payload, and dynamically inject an assembly DLL to perform unauthorized ad-clicking, app installs and other financially motivated actions; this threat has been embedded in 25 apps—ranging from horoscope and gaming to utility tools—on Google Play since mid-2020, amassing over 327,000 installations across Brazil, Argentina, the UK, Australia, the US, Mexico and Europe. To evade detection, Xamalicious encrypts all C2 traffic as JWE tokens (RSA-OAEP/128CBC-HS256), self-updates its APK to transform into spyware or a banking trojan, and links back to the Cash Magnet ad-fraud campaign; its use of non-Java frameworks like Xamarin underscores heightened obfuscation. Google Play Protect now blocks or auto-removes infected apps. Separately, a malicious WhatsApp-based phishing campaign in India distributes fake SBI APKs invoking SMS permissions to capture credentials, banking and identity data, then exfiltrates them for unauthorized transactions.
retrieved_context.title: New Sneaky Xamalicious Android Malware Hits Over 327,000 Devices

canonical_entities: spear-phishing attacks against European embassies in Seoul (March–July 2025)
exfiltrated ... over HTTPS to the attackers’ private GitHub repo via the Contents API
retrieved_context.text: Between March and July 2025, DPRK-linked Kimsuky operators executed at least 19 highly tailored spear-phishing attacks against Western, Central, Eastern and Southern European embassies in Seoul, spoofing real diplomats and embedding password-protected ZIPs delivered via Dropbox, Daum or Google Drive. Victims unwittingly launched malicious .LNK shortcuts that triggered obfuscated PowerShell scripts to decode and in-memory execute a Confuser-Core-obfuscated XenoRAT (MoonPeak) payload—identified by GUID 12DE1212-167D-45BA-1284-780DA98CF901 and mutex “Dansweit_Hk65-PSAccerdle”—leveraging scheduled tasks for persistence. Reconnaissance data (OS build, IP, process list) was exfiltrated as base64-encoded text files over HTTPS to the attackers’ private GitHub repo via the Contents API, while C2 instructions (e.g., onf.txt) directed dynamic payload rotations hosted on Dropbox with rapid header-fix GZIP routines. This ongoing campaign provided full system control—including keystroke logging, screenshots and remote shells—and underscores the need to monitor abnormal GitHub API usage, cloud-based archive downloads and anomalous PowerShell invocations.
retrieved_context.title: The Coordinated Embassy Hunt: Unmasking the DPRK-linked GitHub C2 Espionage Campaign

canonical_entities: Western nation’s military mission in Ukraine
retrieved_context.text: In February–March 2025, Russia-linked espionage group Shuckworm (aka Gamaredon/Armageddon) targeted a Western nation’s military mission in Ukraine using a multi-stage PowerShell-centric campaign initiated via an infected removable drive and malicious .lnk file. Obfuscated VBScript (~.drv) deployed through mshta.exe and wscript.exe created registry-named payloads: one performing WMI ping checks to mil.gov.ua before resolving dynamic C2 addresses via Teletype, Telegra.ph, t.me, check-host.net and Cloudflare tunnels (e.g., 107.189.19.218), and another altering Explorer registry keys to hide system files and propagate shortcuts across USB and network shares. The attackers then delivered an updated PowerShell infostealer (GammaSteel) alongside reconnaissance scripts that captured screenshots, systeminfo, process lists and host metadata, exfiltrating sensitive documents (*.docx, *.pptx, *.pdf) using PowerShell web requests with certutil-computed MD5 hashes and fallback cURL over Tor to mask origin. This campaign underscores Shuckworm’s shift from VBS to PowerShell, leveraging in-registry script storage and heavy obfuscation to evade detection, with indicators including anomalous UserAssist entries, unusual mshta/wscript invocations and atypical C2 resolution patterns.
retrieved_context.title: Shuckworm Targets Foreign Military Mission Based in Ukraine | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: New research reveals that over 80,000 Hikvision cameras worldwide remain unpatched against the critical CVE-2021-36260 command-injection flaw (NIST score 9.8/10) disclosed last fall, allowing remote code execution and potential espionage by state-linked groups such as MISSION2025/APT41, APT10 and unknown Russian actors trading stolen credentials on dark-web forums; systemic deficiencies—default or hardcoded passwords, no auto-update mechanism, poor forensics and lack of security-by-design—have left devices in 100+ countries (including the U.S., despite an FCC “unacceptable risk” designation) continuously discoverable via Shodan or Censys and ripe for exploitation, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to inventory IoT assets, change default credentials, deploy available patches and improve visibility and update processes to mitigate geopolitical and operational impact.
retrieved_context.title: Cybercriminals Are Selling Access to Chinese Surveillance Cameras | Threatpost

retrieved_context.text: In February 2022, CISA, the FBI, US Cyber Command CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA issued a joint advisory on Iranian Ministry of Intelligence–linked APT MuddyWater (aka MERCURY, Earth Vetala, Static Kitten, Seedworm, TEMP.Zagros), active since 2018 and focused on cyber espionage, intellectual property theft and ransomware against defense, oil & gas, government and telecom sectors across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America. Exploiting publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and open-source tools, MuddyWater delivers malicious PDFs with embedded links that display error messages prompting users to download Excel maldocs or Windows executables; these files host VBA macros that drop WSF scripts to execute PowerShell and VB payloads, leverage LoLBins, and stage RATs and malware families including PowGoop, Canopy, Small Sieve, POWERSTATS and Mori while communicating with C2 over HTTP and DNS and persisting via Registry Run keys. Cisco Talos observed regional campaigns in Turkey (Nov 2021), Pakistan (Aug 2021) and Armenia (Jun 2021) using decoy documents, signaling tokens and a consistent TTP set, suggesting a conglomerate of subgroups migrating techniques across regions. The resultant network access and data exfiltration underscore the imperative for proactive DFIR readiness, deployment of XDR/MDR platforms, rigorous vulnerability management, macro execution restrictions, PowerShell/LoLBin monitoring and ongoing user awareness training reinforced by incident response tabletop exercises.
retrieved_context.title: An In-Depth Look at Iranian APT "MuddyWater"

hits.text: On June 30, 2025, Qantas Airlines discovered that hackers had exploited a vulnerability in a third-party call-center platform to access personally identifiable information (PII) for approximately six million customers—names, email addresses, phone numbers, birth dates and frequent-flyer numbers—but not passports or payment data—before the breach was contained shortly thereafter; in response, Qantas has launched a dedicated support line and webpage, tightened IT monitoring and access controls, and is investigating alongside federal authorities.  Cybersecurity experts from CyberCX attribute “all the hallmarks” of the attack to the advanced persistent threat group Scattered Spider (aka UNC3944, 0ktapus/Roasted Oktapus, Scatter Swine, Octo Tempest, Muddled Libra), which the FBI recently warned is increasingly targeting aviation, while government minister Tony Burke cautioned Australians to resist cold calls or unsolicited emails and to verify Qantas communications via published contact channels to thwart follow-on phishing campaigns.  Apollo Information Systems CISO Andy Bennett highlights attackers’ use of AI to amalgamate PII from multiple breaches for highly personalized social‐engineering, underscoring the need for rigorous vendor security assessments, proactive threat hunting and cross-sector collaboration under Australia’s $1.67 billion cybersecurity strategy and new critical-infrastructure legislation.
hits.title: Qantas Airlines Breached, Impacting 6M Customers

hits.text: On June 30, threat actors exploited a vulnerability in a third-party call-center platform used by Qantas to exfiltrate 5.7 million unique customer records—none of which involved direct compromise of Qantas’s own systems—and on July 7 the airline confirmed a likely extortion attempt when the hacker made contact; after deduplication Qantas found 4 million records contained names, email addresses and Frequent Flyer details, 1.2 million contained only names and emails, and 1.7 million included additional data such as addresses (1.3 million), dates of birth (1.1 million), phone numbers (900 000), gender (400 000) and meal preferences (10 000), while no credit card, financial or passport information was stored on the breached platform. The company has begun notifying affected customers, deployed enhanced security controls, and is collaborating closely with the Australian Cyber Security Centre, the National Cyber Security Coordinator and the Australian Federal Police to investigate the supply-chain weakness, reinforce third-party risk management, and bolster monitoring and incident response capabilities to mitigate future breaches.
hits.title: Qantas Confirms 5.7 Million Impacted by Data Breach - SecurityWeek

hits.text: In a joint advisory, US, Australian and Canadian agencies warn that financially motivated group Scattered Spider (UNC3944, aka Muddled Libra/Scatter Swine/Starfraud) has leveraged advanced social engineering against help-desk personnel to harvest compromised credentials from hacking forums, deploy RMM tools, create fake social-media personas, and target VMware ESXi servers and Snowflake environments—running thousands of concurrent queries to exfiltrate data to MEGA.nz and Amazon S3—before encrypting systems with DragonForce ransomware and deploying RattyRAT; although recent UK arrests have paused UNC3944 operations, other actors including UNC6040, UNC2165 (RansomHub), UNC4393 (Basta) and UNC2465 (DarkSide/LockBit) are now replicating these TTPs, extending attacks to backup platforms by deleting routines and tampering with permissions to thwart recovery, often exploiting weak credentials, misconfigurations, API/UI flaws and RCE vulnerabilities; defenders are urged to adopt identity-centric security, layered MFA, Zero Trust principles, robust patching, segmentation and proactive disruption of human-driven intrusion paths.
hits.title: Scattered Spider Activity Drops Following Arrests, but Others Adopting Group's Tactics

hits.text: During Q2 2025, CrowdStrike Services observed eCrime group SCATTERED SPIDER expand its long-established insurance and retail campaigns to include U.S. airlines, leveraging sophisticated help-desk voice phishing to hijack Microsoft Entra ID, SSO and VDI accounts by accurately answering employee verification questions and resetting passwords and MFA. From compromised accounts the adversary pivoted to SaaS platforms to harvest network diagrams, VPN instructions and credentials before conducting on-premises Active Directory reconnaissance with ADExplorer, ADRecon.ps1 and Get-ADUser, and exploiting VMware vCenter access to spawn unmanaged VMs, attach domain controller disks, dump ntds.dit and install protocol-tunneling tools (Chisel via trycloudflare[.]com, ngrok, MobaXterm, Pinggy, Rsocx, Teleport). They also created transport rules to delete or redirect security alerts and used S3 Browser to enumerate and exfiltrate AWS S3 data. SCATTERED SPIDER’s endgame is ESXi ransomware deployment or double-extortion data leaks. To detect and disrupt these tactics, organizations should ingest high-priority logs—VMware vCenter/ESXi, firewall, DNS and web proxy—into CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM, enable correlation rules and integrate cloud security for rapid identification and response.
hits.title: SCATTERED SPIDER Escalates Attacks Across Industries | CrowdStrike

hits.text: Scattered Spider, active since May 2022, has evolved from SIM-swapping and typosquatted credential harvesting to sophisticated social-engineering-driven cloud intrusions, most recently impersonating a CFO via public personal data to trick help-desk staff into resetting their Oracle Cloud device, then mapping Entra ID (Azure AD) privileges and SharePoint data, breaching Horizon VDI, VPN, and on-premise environments, reactivating a decommissioned VM, extracting NTDS.dit and over 1,400 secrets from CyberArk vaults using scripts and tools like ngrok, abusing AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, EC2 Serial Console, IAM role enumeration and Teleport for persistence, assigning Exchange Administrator roles to monitor senior employee inboxes, and deleting Azure Firewall policy rules in a tug-of-war over tenant control that required Microsoft intervention, inflicting millions in operational disruption (e.g., MGM Resorts, Marks & Spencer, Hawaiian Airlines) and exposing critical lapses in help-desk verification and privileged access management; organizations should deploy phishing-resistant MFA, enforce least-privilege and strict identity proofing for help-desks, monitor cloud and endpoint activity, and conduct regular social-engineering training to mitigate Scattered Spider’s fast, multi-vector ransomware preparation tactics.
hits.title: Anatomy of a Scattered Spider attack: A growing ransomware threat evolves

hits.text: Since mid-2022, Unit 42 has attributed over 100 high-value cryptocurrency and BPO incidents to Muddled Libra—a fluid subset of the Scattered Spider collective—initially executing structured smishing and 0ktapus phishing campaigns (leveraging over 200 realistic mobile-auth portals) against large business process outsourcers, then evolving in 2023 into an ALPHV/BlackCat affiliate with multi-million-dollar extortion demands, later resuming high-profile attacks in late 2024 and expanding through May 2025 into software automation, telecom, hospitality, finance and retail verticals; their adaptable tradecraft blends social engineering of IT helpdesks to reset passwords and MFA, inside BPO access, legitimate remote management tools for CRM exfiltration, NSOCKS/TrueSocks anonymizing proxies, custom virtual machines, the open-source “bedevil” rootkit on VMware vCenter, email-forwarding rules to hijack incident response communications, and AI-driven voice spoofing for vishing, with members cycling via Discord and Telegram to refresh niche skills and spawn offshoots such as Scatter Swine and Octo Tempest, while leveraging deep incident response framework knowledge to persist in environments and repeatedly reclaim stolen data before affiliating with DragonForce for ransomware; defenders should deploy interwoven modern security architectures (Cortex XSIAM/XDR, Advanced URL Filtering, DNS Security, App-ID), enforce strict access controls, conduct rigorous awareness training, and maintain vigilant MITRE-mapped monitoring (T1566, T1556, T1215, T1562) to thwart these multifaceted, evolving extortion campaigns.
hits.title: Threat Group Assessment: Muddled Libra (Updated May 16, 2025)

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

Credentials from Password Stores: Security Account Manager
hits.text: Dragos researchers, in collaboration with Ukraine’s CSSC, unearthed FrostyGoop—an ICS-specific malware first spotted in April and used in January to disrupt central heating in over 600 Lviv apartment buildings—marking the first known malware to leverage Modbus TCP for read/write operations on operational technology. Attackers gained initial access in April 2023 by exploiting a MikroTik router vulnerability, deployed a webshell on the router’s web server, and maintained persistence via Tor and L2TP tunnels to Moscow-based IPs. After spending months conducting reconnaissance, they extracted credentials by dumping the SAM registry hive in December, then directly issued scripted Modbus commands—read from a JSON configuration file—to publicly exposed ENCO heating controllers, even downgrading firmware to disable monitoring and force inaccurate measurements that halted heating services for nearly two days amid subzero temperatures. This incident underscores the threat posed by internet-exposed ICS devices—over 46,000 globally using Modbus—and highlights poor network segmentation, unpatched ICS CVEs, and the ease with which FrostyGoop’s protocol-agnostic payload can be repurposed against diverse industrial controllers, necessitating immediate network segmentation, firmware monitoring, and patch management in OT environments.
hits.title: ICS malware FrostyGoop disrupted heating in Ukraine, remains threat to OT worldwide

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
hits.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
retrieved_context.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

hits.text: On June 30, 2025, Qantas Airlines discovered that hackers had exploited a vulnerability in a third-party call-center platform to access personally identifiable information (PII) for approximately six million customers—names, email addresses, phone numbers, birth dates and frequent-flyer numbers—but not passports or payment data—before the breach was contained shortly thereafter; in response, Qantas has launched a dedicated support line and webpage, tightened IT monitoring and access controls, and is investigating alongside federal authorities.  Cybersecurity experts from CyberCX attribute “all the hallmarks” of the attack to the advanced persistent threat group Scattered Spider (aka UNC3944, 0ktapus/Roasted Oktapus, Scatter Swine, Octo Tempest, Muddled Libra), which the FBI recently warned is increasingly targeting aviation, while government minister Tony Burke cautioned Australians to resist cold calls or unsolicited emails and to verify Qantas communications via published contact channels to thwart follow-on phishing campaigns.  Apollo Information Systems CISO Andy Bennett highlights attackers’ use of AI to amalgamate PII from multiple breaches for highly personalized social‐engineering, underscoring the need for rigorous vendor security assessments, proactive threat hunting and cross-sector collaboration under Australia’s $1.67 billion cybersecurity strategy and new critical-infrastructure legislation.
hits.title: Qantas Airlines Breached, Impacting 6M Customers

hits.text: In a joint advisory, US, Australian and Canadian agencies warn that financially motivated group Scattered Spider (UNC3944, aka Muddled Libra/Scatter Swine/Starfraud) has leveraged advanced social engineering against help-desk personnel to harvest compromised credentials from hacking forums, deploy RMM tools, create fake social-media personas, and target VMware ESXi servers and Snowflake environments—running thousands of concurrent queries to exfiltrate data to MEGA.nz and Amazon S3—before encrypting systems with DragonForce ransomware and deploying RattyRAT; although recent UK arrests have paused UNC3944 operations, other actors including UNC6040, UNC2165 (RansomHub), UNC4393 (Basta) and UNC2465 (DarkSide/LockBit) are now replicating these TTPs, extending attacks to backup platforms by deleting routines and tampering with permissions to thwart recovery, often exploiting weak credentials, misconfigurations, API/UI flaws and RCE vulnerabilities; defenders are urged to adopt identity-centric security, layered MFA, Zero Trust principles, robust patching, segmentation and proactive disruption of human-driven intrusion paths.
hits.title: Scattered Spider Activity Drops Following Arrests, but Others Adopting Group's Tactics

hits.text: During Q2 2025, CrowdStrike Services observed eCrime group SCATTERED SPIDER expand its long-established insurance and retail campaigns to include U.S. airlines, leveraging sophisticated help-desk voice phishing to hijack Microsoft Entra ID, SSO and VDI accounts by accurately answering employee verification questions and resetting passwords and MFA. From compromised accounts the adversary pivoted to SaaS platforms to harvest network diagrams, VPN instructions and credentials before conducting on-premises Active Directory reconnaissance with ADExplorer, ADRecon.ps1 and Get-ADUser, and exploiting VMware vCenter access to spawn unmanaged VMs, attach domain controller disks, dump ntds.dit and install protocol-tunneling tools (Chisel via trycloudflare[.]com, ngrok, MobaXterm, Pinggy, Rsocx, Teleport). They also created transport rules to delete or redirect security alerts and used S3 Browser to enumerate and exfiltrate AWS S3 data. SCATTERED SPIDER’s endgame is ESXi ransomware deployment or double-extortion data leaks. To detect and disrupt these tactics, organizations should ingest high-priority logs—VMware vCenter/ESXi, firewall, DNS and web proxy—into CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM, enable correlation rules and integrate cloud security for rapid identification and response.
hits.title: SCATTERED SPIDER Escalates Attacks Across Industries | CrowdStrike

hits.text: Scattered Spider, active since May 2022, has evolved from SIM-swapping and typosquatted credential harvesting to sophisticated social-engineering-driven cloud intrusions, most recently impersonating a CFO via public personal data to trick help-desk staff into resetting their Oracle Cloud device, then mapping Entra ID (Azure AD) privileges and SharePoint data, breaching Horizon VDI, VPN, and on-premise environments, reactivating a decommissioned VM, extracting NTDS.dit and over 1,400 secrets from CyberArk vaults using scripts and tools like ngrok, abusing AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, EC2 Serial Console, IAM role enumeration and Teleport for persistence, assigning Exchange Administrator roles to monitor senior employee inboxes, and deleting Azure Firewall policy rules in a tug-of-war over tenant control that required Microsoft intervention, inflicting millions in operational disruption (e.g., MGM Resorts, Marks & Spencer, Hawaiian Airlines) and exposing critical lapses in help-desk verification and privileged access management; organizations should deploy phishing-resistant MFA, enforce least-privilege and strict identity proofing for help-desks, monitor cloud and endpoint activity, and conduct regular social-engineering training to mitigate Scattered Spider’s fast, multi-vector ransomware preparation tactics.
hits.title: Anatomy of a Scattered Spider attack: A growing ransomware threat evolves

hits.text: On June 30, threat actors exploited a vulnerability in a third-party call-center platform used by Qantas to exfiltrate 5.7 million unique customer records—none of which involved direct compromise of Qantas’s own systems—and on July 7 the airline confirmed a likely extortion attempt when the hacker made contact; after deduplication Qantas found 4 million records contained names, email addresses and Frequent Flyer details, 1.2 million contained only names and emails, and 1.7 million included additional data such as addresses (1.3 million), dates of birth (1.1 million), phone numbers (900 000), gender (400 000) and meal preferences (10 000), while no credit card, financial or passport information was stored on the breached platform. The company has begun notifying affected customers, deployed enhanced security controls, and is collaborating closely with the Australian Cyber Security Centre, the National Cyber Security Coordinator and the Australian Federal Police to investigate the supply-chain weakness, reinforce third-party risk management, and bolster monitoring and incident response capabilities to mitigate future breaches.
hits.title: Qantas Confirms 5.7 Million Impacted by Data Breach - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Since mid-2022, Unit 42 has attributed over 100 high-value cryptocurrency and BPO incidents to Muddled Libra—a fluid subset of the Scattered Spider collective—initially executing structured smishing and 0ktapus phishing campaigns (leveraging over 200 realistic mobile-auth portals) against large business process outsourcers, then evolving in 2023 into an ALPHV/BlackCat affiliate with multi-million-dollar extortion demands, later resuming high-profile attacks in late 2024 and expanding through May 2025 into software automation, telecom, hospitality, finance and retail verticals; their adaptable tradecraft blends social engineering of IT helpdesks to reset passwords and MFA, inside BPO access, legitimate remote management tools for CRM exfiltration, NSOCKS/TrueSocks anonymizing proxies, custom virtual machines, the open-source “bedevil” rootkit on VMware vCenter, email-forwarding rules to hijack incident response communications, and AI-driven voice spoofing for vishing, with members cycling via Discord and Telegram to refresh niche skills and spawn offshoots such as Scatter Swine and Octo Tempest, while leveraging deep incident response framework knowledge to persist in environments and repeatedly reclaim stolen data before affiliating with DragonForce for ransomware; defenders should deploy interwoven modern security architectures (Cortex XSIAM/XDR, Advanced URL Filtering, DNS Security, App-ID), enforce strict access controls, conduct rigorous awareness training, and maintain vigilant MITRE-mapped monitoring (T1566, T1556, T1215, T1562) to thwart these multifaceted, evolving extortion campaigns.
hits.title: Threat Group Assessment: Muddled Libra (Updated May 16, 2025)

hits.text: HC3’s November 2022 alert warns of human-operated Lorenz ransomware, first observed in February 2021 and linked to earlier sZ40 and ThunderCrypt activity, which specifically targets large healthcare organizations by customizing its executable code and following a kill chain of initial access, extended reconnaissance, lateral movement to Windows domain controllers for administrator credential theft, then encryption and extortion. Operators demand $500,000–$700,000 and employ a non-typical leak site where stolen data is first offered for sale to other threat actors, then distributed in password-protected archives or, if sales fail, released publicly. With relatively limited public intelligence on Lorenz, HC3 emphasizes that victims should address common ransomware vectors—phishing, exploitation of known vulnerabilities, remote-access compromise and distributed attacks—by reinforcing patch management, intrusion detection, access controls and incident-response planning, especially in light of concurrent Hive ransomware warnings issued by HHS, FBI and CISA.
hits.title: Lorenz Ransomware Targets Large Healthcare Orgs, HC3 Warns | TechTarget

hits.text: On March 4 JetBrains released patches for two critical TeamCity authentication-bypass flaws (CVE-2024-27198 and CVE-2024-27199) that allow unauthenticated remote attackers to create admin accounts or tokens, but misaligned disclosure with Rapid7—whose researchers publicly detailed the bugs hours after the fixes—triggered mass exploitation: by March 6 LeakIX recorded rogue user creation on approximately 1,400 servers and GuidePoint Security linked the BianLian ransomware group to CVE-2024-27198–driven initial access. Despite JetBrains’ efforts to obfuscate patches and limit reverse engineering time, unpatched customers reported at least two file-encryption incidents and one DDoS-prep compromise. This chain of events underscores the necessity of coordinated vendor–researcher disclosure, accelerated patch deployment, and enhanced patch hardening to mitigate rapid exploit development and reduce organizational exposure.
hits.title: Recent TeamCity Vulnerability Exploited in Ransomware Attacks - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: harvest subscriber location, billing and communications metadata
hits.text: On Sept. 25, 2024, the Wall Street Journal disclosed that the Chinese state-sponsored APT Salt Typhoon has stealthily infiltrated multiple U.S. cable and broadband ISPs—likely via firmware and supply-chain compromises in core networking gear—to establish long-term persistence, harvest subscriber location, billing and communications metadata for espionage, and pre-position disruptive capabilities against federal, military and Fortune 100 users; this campaign, echoing Volt Typhoon’s telecom backdoors, Flax Typhoon’s 200,000-device IoT botnet, Brass Typhoon’s cross-domain implants and Mustang Panda’s telco intrusions, signals a shift from surveillance to offensive “blink-the-lights” or infrastructure-crippling attacks in a Taiwan contingency, driving urgent recommendations for carriers to enforce threat-intelligence sharing, secure firmware, tighten supply-chain controls and bolster routing security.
hits.title: China's 'Salt Typhoon' Cooks Up Cyberattacks on US ISPs

retrieved_context.text: On June 30, 2025, Qantas Airlines discovered that hackers had exploited a vulnerability in a third-party call-center platform to access personally identifiable information (PII) for approximately six million customers—names, email addresses, phone numbers, birth dates and frequent-flyer numbers—but not passports or payment data—before the breach was contained shortly thereafter; in response, Qantas has launched a dedicated support line and webpage, tightened IT monitoring and access controls, and is investigating alongside federal authorities.  Cybersecurity experts from CyberCX attribute “all the hallmarks” of the attack to the advanced persistent threat group Scattered Spider (aka UNC3944, 0ktapus/Roasted Oktapus, Scatter Swine, Octo Tempest, Muddled Libra), which the FBI recently warned is increasingly targeting aviation, while government minister Tony Burke cautioned Australians to resist cold calls or unsolicited emails and to verify Qantas communications via published contact channels to thwart follow-on phishing campaigns.  Apollo Information Systems CISO Andy Bennett highlights attackers’ use of AI to amalgamate PII from multiple breaches for highly personalized social‐engineering, underscoring the need for rigorous vendor security assessments, proactive threat hunting and cross-sector collaboration under Australia’s $1.67 billion cybersecurity strategy and new critical-infrastructure legislation.
retrieved_context.title: Qantas Airlines Breached, Impacting 6M Customers

retrieved_context.text: In a joint advisory, US, Australian and Canadian agencies warn that financially motivated group Scattered Spider (UNC3944, aka Muddled Libra/Scatter Swine/Starfraud) has leveraged advanced social engineering against help-desk personnel to harvest compromised credentials from hacking forums, deploy RMM tools, create fake social-media personas, and target VMware ESXi servers and Snowflake environments—running thousands of concurrent queries to exfiltrate data to MEGA.nz and Amazon S3—before encrypting systems with DragonForce ransomware and deploying RattyRAT; although recent UK arrests have paused UNC3944 operations, other actors including UNC6040, UNC2165 (RansomHub), UNC4393 (Basta) and UNC2465 (DarkSide/LockBit) are now replicating these TTPs, extending attacks to backup platforms by deleting routines and tampering with permissions to thwart recovery, often exploiting weak credentials, misconfigurations, API/UI flaws and RCE vulnerabilities; defenders are urged to adopt identity-centric security, layered MFA, Zero Trust principles, robust patching, segmentation and proactive disruption of human-driven intrusion paths.

retrieved_context.text: During Q2 2025, CrowdStrike Services observed eCrime group SCATTERED SPIDER expand its long-established insurance and retail campaigns to include U.S. airlines, leveraging sophisticated help-desk voice phishing to hijack Microsoft Entra ID, SSO and VDI accounts by accurately answering employee verification questions and resetting passwords and MFA. From compromised accounts the adversary pivoted to SaaS platforms to harvest network diagrams, VPN instructions and credentials before conducting on-premises Active Directory reconnaissance with ADExplorer, ADRecon.ps1 and Get-ADUser, and exploiting VMware vCenter access to spawn unmanaged VMs, attach domain controller disks, dump ntds.dit and install protocol-tunneling tools (Chisel via trycloudflare[.]com, ngrok, MobaXterm, Pinggy, Rsocx, Teleport). They also created transport rules to delete or redirect security alerts and used S3 Browser to enumerate and exfiltrate AWS S3 data. SCATTERED SPIDER’s endgame is ESXi ransomware deployment or double-extortion data leaks. To detect and disrupt these tactics, organizations should ingest high-priority logs—VMware vCenter/ESXi, firewall, DNS and web proxy—into CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM, enable correlation rules and integrate cloud security for rapid identification and response.
retrieved_context.title: SCATTERED SPIDER Escalates Attacks Across Industries | CrowdStrike

hits.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.
hits.title: Operation Lotus Blossom: A New Nation-State Cyberthreat?

hits.text: Between late 2022 and early 2023, the Chinese-affiliated APT15 (aka Flea/Nickel) executed a targeted espionage campaign against foreign ministries in the Americas—alongside a finance department, a regional products firm, and an outlier European victim—deploying a novel Backdoor.Graphican that abuses the Microsoft Graph API and OneDrive for dynamic C2, an evolution of its Ketrican/BS2005 malware. Graphican disables Internet Explorer 10’s first-run wizard, leverages a global IWebBrowser2 COM object to authenticate via Graph API, enumerates the “Person” OneDrive folder, decrypts its first subfolder name into the C2 address, generates a Bot ID from host attributes, registers with the server, and polls for commands to spawn shells, upload/download files, launch hidden processes, or run PowerShell with exfiltration. Concurrently, Flea rolled out updated and legacy Ketrican variants, living-off-the-land binaries, and open-source tools—EWSTEW for Exchange mail harvesting; Mimikatz, Pypykatz, Safetykatz; LaZagne; Quarks PwDump; SharpSecDump; K8Tools; EHole; and web shells such as AntSword, Behinder, China Chopper, Godzilla—while exploiting CVE-2020-1472 for privilege escalation. This persistent-access operation highlights Flea’s sustained evolution of custom tools for geopolitical intelligence gathering and introduces a C2 technique poised for adoption by other threat actors.
hits.title: Graphican: Flea Uses New Backdoor in Attacks Targeting Foreign Ministries | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: masquerading as industry-branded webinars and software packages
hits.text: Since October 2023—shortly after the Hamas attack—Iranian state-sponsored actor MuddyWater (aka SeedWorm/TEMP.Zagros) has escalated its longstanding (since 2021) tactic of abusing the legitimate Atera Agent remote monitoring and management (RMM) tool to stealthily deliver malware via trojanized MSI installers masquerading as industry-branded webinars and software packages; this low-profile approach blends malicious payload deployment and persistence into normal admin traffic, enabling long-term espionage against Middle East and global targets in telecommunications, government and oil sectors, and facilitating covert data exfiltration; Harfang Lab researchers have cataloged over 40 unique SHA-256 indicators covering Atera Agent binaries and malicious ZIP archives; organizations are advised to enforce strict application allow-listing, monitor unexpected RMM activity, validate digital signatures, audit endpoint logs for anomalous MSI executions, segment RMM traffic and integrate the provided IOCs into SIEM and endpoint detection tools to detect and mitigate this evolving threat.
hits.title: MuddyWater Hackers Abusing Legitimate RMM Tool to Deliver Malware

hits.text: ReversingLabs discovered that SqzrFramework480, a .NET library published to NuGet in January 2024 under the guise of a Bozhon Precision Industry Technology Co. robot-calibration and GUI framework, contains undocumented routines to harvest industrial system data—capturing primary-screen screenshots every minute in a continuous loop, sending heartbeat ping packets to verify a remote exfiltration server’s availability, opening sockets for data transfer, and extracting credentials, configuration settings and proprietary information from cameras and robotic arms—and, although each function alone is innocuous, their orchestration strongly suggests a supply-chain espionage campaign targeting developers using Bozhon tools; with over 2,400 downloads to date, no clear activation vector beyond explicit invocation by consuming code, and Bozhon unresponsive to inquiries, organizations relying on this package are urged to enforce strict dependency vetting, implement real-time monitoring for anomalous socket and screenshot activity, and report similar findings to NuGet administrators.
hits.title: Suspicious NuGet Package Harvesting Information From Industrial Systems - SecurityWeek
