Variants in the campaign include FROSTYFERRET_UI, FRIENDLYFERRET_SECD, MULTI_FROSTYFERRET_CMDCODES and, as of February 3, the newly revealed under‐the‐radar FlexibleFerret, suggesting DPRK actors are honing evasion and expanding beyond job‐seeker targeting to developers more broadly. Apple’s recent XProtect signature update aims to block known variants, but organizations should urgently apply patches, monitor for anomalous shell script execution, persistence agent installs and spoofed update processes, and inspect network traffic for BeaverTail/InvisibleFerret command-and-control indicators to disrupt this evolving threat.
retrieved_context.title: Ferret Malware Added to 'Contagious Interview' Campaign

retrieved_context.text: North Korea–linked Contagious Interview actors have deployed three fake cryptocurrency consulting firms—BlockNovas LLC, Angeloper Agency and SoftGlide LLC—to lure candidates with bogus job interviews and video coding assessments, distributing the BeaverTail JavaScript stealer/loader that contacts lianxinxiao[.]com C2 to deliver the InvisibleFerret Python backdoor on Windows, Linux and macOS and, in some chains, the OtterCookie payload; they’ve also leveraged ClickFake Interview video lures to push FROSTYFERRET and GolangGhost, hosted a Hashtopolis password-cracking system on mail.blocknovas[.]com, and run a “Kryptoneer” crypto-wallet connector on attisscmo[.]com. Operating under aliases CL-STA-0240, DeceptiveDevelopment, Famous Chollima and others, the group obfuscated traffic via Astrill VPN, residential proxies and five Russian IP ranges masked by VPN/proxy/RDP layers from Khasan and Khabarovsk, used AI-generated personas across LinkedIn, Facebook, GitHub and more, and even advertised a senior software engineer role targeting Ukrainian professionals in December 2024. Their campaign enabled AnyDesk installation and led to at least one MetaMask compromise in September 2024; on April 23, 2025, the US FBI seized blocknovas.com, highlighting urgent needs to harden remote-hiring vetting, monitor anomalous C2 communications and enforce multi-factor authentication on crypto and recruitment platforms against DPRK’s evolving “Wagemole” salary-siphoning and potential DPRK–Russia infrastructure collaboration.
retrieved_context.title: North Korean Hackers Spread Malware via Fake Crypto Firms and Job Interview Lures

retrieved_context.text: Unit 42 researchers identified two North Korea–linked campaigns, Contagious Interview (CL-STA-0240) and Wagemole (CL-STA-0241), active since December 2022 and March 2023 respectively, that exploit job-seeking and recruitment processes to compromise targets: Contagious Interview poses as anonymous employers, lures software developers into installing malicious NPM packages hosted on free GitHub repos, and deploys the BeaverTail JavaScript stealer/loader to harvest browser-stored cryptocurrency wallet and credential data before retrieving the cross-platform InvisibleFerret Python backdoor for follow-on intrusion, while Wagemole involves DPRK operators submitting fraudulent resumes and conducting unauthorized remote employment with U.S. and global organizations to facilitate espionage or funnel wages to weapons programs; both campaigns leverage open-source supply-chain tactics, Node.js execution, code obfuscation and minimal detection footprints to enable cryptocurrency theft, staging for additional attacks and sensitive data exfiltration, underscoring the need for rigorous vetting of employers, candidates and development-environment artifacts.
retrieved_context.title: Hacking Employers and Seeking Employment: Two Job-Related Campaigns Bear Hallmarks of North Korean Threat Actors

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

retrieved_context.text: In May 2023, after U.S. authorities secured convictions against three high-level operators and declared the Russia-based cybercrime enterprise Fin7 “no more,” security experts began spotting first signs of its resurrection in April 2024 when Blackberry reported a typosquatting-based malware intrusion against a major automotive firm; since January 2024, Silent Push analyst Zach Edwards has mapped over 4,000 Fin7-linked hosts—rented largely on the pro-Russia Stark Industries Solutions platform—employing typosquatting, booby-trapped ads, malicious browser extensions and spear-phishing domains to mimic hundreds of brands from American Express and Microsoft 365 to CNN and Zoom, as well as popular free software tools such as 7-zip, PuTTY and Python, all “aged” on innocuous templates for six to nine months before weaponization; eSentire and Malwarebytes also observed sponsored Google ads pushing phony extensions in May and April 2024, and Fin7 has even deployed domains targeting Louvre and Olympic tourists, building on its 2013–present campaign that has extorted some $3 billion from victim organizations, underscoring the urgent need for renewed law enforcement focus and proactive domain-monitoring defenses.
retrieved_context.title: The Stark Truth Behind the Resurgence of Russia’s Fin7 – Krebs on Security

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: North Korean APT Lazarus has launched “Operation In(ter)ception,” a macOS-focused cyberespionage campaign that lures engineering professionals with a fake Coinbase job posting and deploys a signed universal macOS executable (Intel and Apple Silicon) that drops three components—a decoy PDF (Coinbase_online_careers_2022_07.pdf), a FinderFontsUpdater.app bundle and a downloader named safarifontagent—before phoning home to a new, currently nonresponsive C2 at concrecapital[.]com/%user%.jpg. Identified by ESET in late July and using a February-2022 developer certificate for “Shankey Nohria” revoked by Apple on August 12, the malware mirrors a May sample but introduces fresh C2 infrastructure and was first uploaded from Brazil. A companion Windows variant, spotted by Malwarebytes on August 4, follows the same decoy routine. This marks another evolution in Lazarus’s longstanding impersonation tactics—previously targeting engineers via spear-phishing and defense-sector ruses—while the group simultaneously diversifies into cryptocurrency heists (prompting Tornado Cash sanctions) and VHD ransomware operations to fund the North Korean regime.
retrieved_context.title: APT Lazarus Targets Engineers with macOS Malware | Threatpost

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Since January 2021, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has tracked a government-backed North Korean campaign that leverages social engineering via X (formerly Twitter) and encrypted messaging apps to befriend security researchers and deliver malicious files containing at least one unpatched 0-day in a popular software package; upon exploitation the custom shellcode performs anti-virtual-machine checks, captures system data and screenshots, and exfiltrates them to C2 infrastructure (e.g., 23.106.215[.]105, www.blgbeach[.]com), with the latest vulnerability reported and patched on September 12, 2023 (see TAG’s published RCA). In parallel, the actors published a seemingly benign Windows tool called GetSymbol on GitHub (https://github.com/dbgsymbol/) that quietly downloads debugging symbols—and arbitrary code—from attacker domains, requiring full OS reinstalls for compromised hosts. TAG has added malicious sites to Safe Browsing, issued government-backed attacker alerts to targeted Gmail and Workspace users, and urges researchers to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, keep software up to date, and verify system integrity after using third-party tools.
retrieved_context.title: Active North Korean campaign targeting security researchers

retrieved_context.text: ESET researchers have retrospectively identified WinorDLL64.dll—a backdoor payload for the Wslink loader (WinorLoaderDLL64.dll) first uncovered in 2021—that operates as an in-memory server using MemoryModule and is protected by Oreans Code Virtualizer; although the initial compromise vector remains unknown, sparse detections in Central Europe, North America and the Middle East and a South Korean VirusTotal submission triggered YARA alerts based on its unique filename. Communicating over the loader’s established AES-256-CBC encrypted TCP channel, WinorDLL64 implements at least 16 commands—including comprehensive system profiling, secure file exfiltration, overwrite and deletion, process and RDP session management, unrestricted PowerShell execution, directory compression for data theft, and connection latency measurement—facilitating reconnaissance, persistence and lateral movement. Low-confidence attribution to North Korea–aligned Lazarus (HIDDEN COBRA) derives from targeting of South Korean victims, shared VS2010 LTCG build signatures and code/behavior overlap with 2018 GhostSecret (FE887FCAB66D7D7F79F05E0266C0649F0114BA7C) and Bankshot implants; this underscores Lazarus’s organized, modular arsenal and highlights the need to detect anomalous in-memory loaders and encrypted session anomalies.
retrieved_context.title: WinorDLL64: A backdoor from the vast Lazarus arsenal?

hits.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
hits.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since late 2021, Russia’s GRU-aligned Sandworm APT (Seashell Blizzard) has deployed an initial-access subgroup dubbed BadPilot to stealthily breach high-value telecom, oil and gas, shipping, arms-manufacturing and government networks worldwide by exploiting critical CVSS 9.8 vulnerabilities—Zimbra CVE-2022-41352, Exchange CVE-2021-34473 and Outlook CVE-2023-23397—and, from early 2024, remote-monitoring-and-management flaws such as Fortinet FortiClient EMS CVE-2023-48788 and ScreenConnect CVE-2024-1709 (CVSS 10.0). Following initial access, BadPilot establishes persistence via its custom LocalOlive web shell or legitimate RMM tools (“ShadowLink”) configured as Tor hidden services, harvests credentials, performs lateral movement, exfiltrates data and stages follow-on operations. These agile, low-noise TTPs have underpinned Sandworm’s high-impact campaigns—from NotPetya and 2018 Olympic disruptions to multiple destructive power-grid outages in Ukraine and an attack on Denmark’s energy sector—advancing Russia’s strategic objectives. Critical organizations must therefore enforce timely patching of Internet-facing services, continuous asset monitoring and robust defense-in-depth controls.
hits.title: Microsoft: Russia's Sandworm APT Exploits Edge Bugs Globally

hits.text: Symantec has warned that extortion actors, notably the Clop ransomware operation (aka Snakefly/TA505/FIN11), have been exploiting a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability in the MOVEit Transfer web application (CVE-2023-34362) since May 27, 2023, enabling supply-chain attacks across multiple organizations; although first patched on May 31, additional vulnerabilities (CVEs pending) were disclosed on June 9. Attackers deploy a bespoke web shell, Lemurloot (detected as JS.Malscript!g1, Trojan.Gen.2, WS.Malware), to authenticate via hard-coded credentials, execute SQL statements to alter or delete database elements, exfiltrate records and Azure settings, and manipulate user accounts. With proof-of-concept code now public, secondary threat actors face elevated risk of exploitation and data theft. Clop has since threatened data leaks unless ransoms are paid, reflecting its shift from encryption to extortion. Symantec mitigations include file-based and ML detections, network-based attack signatures, and Data Center Security policy controls that harden MS SQL, IIS and sandbox environments to prevent web-shell deployment and unauthorized software execution.
hits.title: MOVEit Vulnerabilities: What You Need to Know | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

hits.text: Sea Turtle, also known as Cosmic Wolf, Marbled Dust, Teal Kurma and UNC1326, has been conducting a stealthy, Türkiye-linked cyber espionage campaign since at least January 2017, recently targeting Dutch ISPs, telecom, IT-service and media providers as well as Kurdish websites via supply-chain and island-hopping attacks to harvest politically sensitive personal data and potential dissident communications. First detailed by Cisco Talos in April 2019 for state-sponsored DNS hijacking to redirect legitimate domain queries to attacker-controlled servers, the group elevated its upstream foothold tactics in late 2021 by exploiting known telecom and IT vulnerabilities across Armenia, Cyprus, Greece, Iraq and Syria, per Microsoft. Between 2021 and 2023 PwC observed deployment of “SnappyTCP,” a simple Linux/Unix reverse-TCP web shell (with and without OpenSSL/TLS) for persistence and C2, and Hunt & Hackett’s 2023 incident revealed credential-theft via a compromised cPanel account used to deploy SnappyTCP, tar and expose email archives publicly for direct exfiltration. Organizations should enforce strong password policies, 2FA, login-rate limiting, SSH monitoring and timely patching to mitigate this ongoing espionage threat.
hits.title: Sea Turtle Cyber Espionage Campaign Targets Dutch IT and Telecom Companies

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
hits.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

hits.text: Russia’s APT29 (aka Cozy Bear/Nobelium) has been exploiting a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in JetBrains TeamCity (CVE-2023-42793, CVSS 9.8) since September—shortly after JetBrains issued a patch and Rapid7 published a proof-of-concept—to gain initial access to SDLC management servers, escalate privileges, move laterally, deploy stealthy backdoors that persist through updates, and potentially manipulate build pipelines or insert malicious updates in SolarWinds-style supply-chain attacks; CISA, FBI, NSA and international partners warn that around 800 internet-exposed instances remain vulnerable (with uncounted internally reachable servers also at risk), and that North Korea’s Lazarus and Andariel groups have similarly weaponized the same flaw, prompting Fortinet to report multi-actor post-exploit techniques in live incidents; mitigation guidance urges immediate upgrading to TeamCity 2023.05.4, removal of public exposure, comprehensive IoC-based threat hunting across servers and build agents, and full compromise assessments to eradicate entrenched backdoors.
hits.title: Global TeamCity Exploitation Opens Door to SolarWinds-Style Nightmare

canonical_entities: U.S. energy, oil and gas utilities
U.S. law firm Hunter Taubman Fischer & Li
Indicator Removal on Host: Clear Windows Event Logs
hits.text: Lynx ransomware, emerging in July 2024 as the INC ransomware successor under a Ransomware-as-a-Service model, employs a sophisticated double-extortion strategy—exfiltrating data prior to encryption and threatening publication on a leak site—and reuses significant INC source code. Between July and November 2024, it disrupted U.S. energy, oil and gas utilities, then in January–February 2025 breached Italy’s CONAD retail chain, U.S. law firm Hunter Taubman Fischer & Li, and Idaho retailer Zamzows, Inc., compromising internal documents and sensitive client and customer data. Initial access leverages phishing (T1566.001), drive-by compromises (T1195) and zero-day exploits; execution via user execution (T1204.002) and scripting interpreters (T1059.001); persistence through autostart mechanisms (T1070.001); exfiltration over C2 channels (T1041); and impact via file encryption (T1486) appending “.LYNX.” Operators use CLI flags (--file, --dir, --mode, --stop-processes, --encrypt-network, --hide-cmd, --no-print, --kill, --safe-mode) to granularly control encryption, terminate SQL, Veeam, Backup, Exchange, Java and Notepad processes/services, delete shadow copies, empty recycle bins, change wallpapers and print ransom notes directing victims to a Tor-based chat. Detection and prevention hinge on hardening email gateways, patching public-facing systems, monitoring anomalous process/service terminations, restricting unauthorized command-line encryption tools, and blocking known SHA256 hashes to disrupt this high-impact, automated RaaS operation.
hits.title: Lynx Ransomware: INC Ransomware Reincarnated - Threat Actors

canonical_entities: month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment
hits.text: In November 2023, Russian state-sponsored group Nobelium (aka Midnight Blizzard/APT29) executed a month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment by conducting a password-spray brute-force attack against a legacy non-production test tenant lacking multi-factor authentication, enabling pivoting to a small subset of high-value accounts—including leadership, cybersecurity and legal team mailboxes—from which they exfiltrated emails and attachments; discovered on January 12, 2024, the campaign underscores the risk of poorly secured account configurations rather than software vulnerabilities, prompting Microsoft to notify impacted employees, reaffirm its MFA mandate, and reinforce zero-trust controls. This incident, following Nobelium’s SolarWinds and 2021 support-tool intrusions, highlights the necessity of enforcing MFA, minimizing default permissions, and hardening non-prod assets to mitigate advanced persistent threats.
hits.title: Russian hackers stole Microsoft corporate emails in month-long breach

hits.text: ReversingLabs discovered that SqzrFramework480, a .NET library published to NuGet in January 2024 under the guise of a Bozhon Precision Industry Technology Co. robot-calibration and GUI framework, contains undocumented routines to harvest industrial system data—capturing primary-screen screenshots every minute in a continuous loop, sending heartbeat ping packets to verify a remote exfiltration server’s availability, opening sockets for data transfer, and extracting credentials, configuration settings and proprietary information from cameras and robotic arms—and, although each function alone is innocuous, their orchestration strongly suggests a supply-chain espionage campaign targeting developers using Bozhon tools; with over 2,400 downloads to date, no clear activation vector beyond explicit invocation by consuming code, and Bozhon unresponsive to inquiries, organizations relying on this package are urged to enforce strict dependency vetting, implement real-time monitoring for anomalous socket and screenshot activity, and report similar findings to NuGet administrators.
hits.title: Suspicious NuGet Package Harvesting Information From Industrial Systems - SecurityWeek

retrieved_context.text: Russia’s APT29 (aka Cozy Bear/Nobelium) has been exploiting a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in JetBrains TeamCity (CVE-2023-42793, CVSS 9.8) since September—shortly after JetBrains issued a patch and Rapid7 published a proof-of-concept—to gain initial access to SDLC management servers, escalate privileges, move laterally, deploy stealthy backdoors that persist through updates, and potentially manipulate build pipelines or insert malicious updates in SolarWinds-style supply-chain attacks; CISA, FBI, NSA and international partners warn that around 800 internet-exposed instances remain vulnerable (with uncounted internally reachable servers also at risk), and that North Korea’s Lazarus and Andariel groups have similarly weaponized the same flaw, prompting Fortinet to report multi-actor post-exploit techniques in live incidents; mitigation guidance urges immediate upgrading to TeamCity 2023.05.4, removal of public exposure, comprehensive IoC-based threat hunting across servers and build agents, and full compromise assessments to eradicate entrenched backdoors.
retrieved_context.title: Global TeamCity Exploitation Opens Door to SolarWinds-Style Nightmare

canonical_entities: U.S. energy, oil and gas utilities
U.S. law firm Hunter Taubman Fischer & Li
Indicator Removal on Host: Clear Windows Event Logs
retrieved_context.text: Lynx ransomware, emerging in July 2024 as the INC ransomware successor under a Ransomware-as-a-Service model, employs a sophisticated double-extortion strategy—exfiltrating data prior to encryption and threatening publication on a leak site—and reuses significant INC source code. Between July and November 2024, it disrupted U.S. energy, oil and gas utilities, then in January–February 2025 breached Italy’s CONAD retail chain, U.S. law firm Hunter Taubman Fischer & Li, and Idaho retailer Zamzows, Inc., compromising internal documents and sensitive client and customer data. Initial access leverages phishing (T1566.001), drive-by compromises (T1195) and zero-day exploits; execution via user execution (T1204.002) and scripting interpreters (T1059.001); persistence through autostart mechanisms (T1070.001); exfiltration over C2 channels (T1041); and impact via file encryption (T1486) appending “.LYNX.” Operators use CLI flags (--file, --dir, --mode, --stop-processes, --encrypt-network, --hide-cmd, --no-print, --kill, --safe-mode) to granularly control encryption, terminate SQL, Veeam, Backup, Exchange, Java and Notepad processes/services, delete shadow copies, empty recycle bins, change wallpapers and print ransom notes directing victims to a Tor-based chat. Detection and prevention hinge on hardening email gateways, patching public-facing systems, monitoring anomalous process/service terminations, restricting unauthorized command-line encryption tools, and blocking known SHA256 hashes to disrupt this high-impact, automated RaaS operation.
retrieved_context.title: Lynx Ransomware: INC Ransomware Reincarnated - Threat Actors

canonical_entities: month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment
retrieved_context.text: In November 2023, Russian state-sponsored group Nobelium (aka Midnight Blizzard/APT29) executed a month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment by conducting a password-spray brute-force attack against a legacy non-production test tenant lacking multi-factor authentication, enabling pivoting to a small subset of high-value accounts—including leadership, cybersecurity and legal team mailboxes—from which they exfiltrated emails and attachments; discovered on January 12, 2024, the campaign underscores the risk of poorly secured account configurations rather than software vulnerabilities, prompting Microsoft to notify impacted employees, reaffirm its MFA mandate, and reinforce zero-trust controls. This incident, following Nobelium’s SolarWinds and 2021 support-tool intrusions, highlights the necessity of enforcing MFA, minimizing default permissions, and hardening non-prod assets to mitigate advanced persistent threats.
retrieved_context.title: Russian hackers stole Microsoft corporate emails in month-long breach

retrieved_context.text: ReversingLabs discovered that SqzrFramework480, a .NET library published to NuGet in January 2024 under the guise of a Bozhon Precision Industry Technology Co. robot-calibration and GUI framework, contains undocumented routines to harvest industrial system data—capturing primary-screen screenshots every minute in a continuous loop, sending heartbeat ping packets to verify a remote exfiltration server’s availability, opening sockets for data transfer, and extracting credentials, configuration settings and proprietary information from cameras and robotic arms—and, although each function alone is innocuous, their orchestration strongly suggests a supply-chain espionage campaign targeting developers using Bozhon tools; with over 2,400 downloads to date, no clear activation vector beyond explicit invocation by consuming code, and Bozhon unresponsive to inquiries, organizations relying on this package are urged to enforce strict dependency vetting, implement real-time monitoring for anomalous socket and screenshot activity, and report similar findings to NuGet administrators.
retrieved_context.title: Suspicious NuGet Package Harvesting Information From Industrial Systems - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
hits.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since late 2021, Russia’s GRU-aligned Sandworm APT (Seashell Blizzard) has deployed an initial-access subgroup dubbed BadPilot to stealthily breach high-value telecom, oil and gas, shipping, arms-manufacturing and government networks worldwide by exploiting critical CVSS 9.8 vulnerabilities—Zimbra CVE-2022-41352, Exchange CVE-2021-34473 and Outlook CVE-2023-23397—and, from early 2024, remote-monitoring-and-management flaws such as Fortinet FortiClient EMS CVE-2023-48788 and ScreenConnect CVE-2024-1709 (CVSS 10.0). Following initial access, BadPilot establishes persistence via its custom LocalOlive web shell or legitimate RMM tools (“ShadowLink”) configured as Tor hidden services, harvests credentials, performs lateral movement, exfiltrates data and stages follow-on operations. These agile, low-noise TTPs have underpinned Sandworm’s high-impact campaigns—from NotPetya and 2018 Olympic disruptions to multiple destructive power-grid outages in Ukraine and an attack on Denmark’s energy sector—advancing Russia’s strategic objectives. Critical organizations must therefore enforce timely patching of Internet-facing services, continuous asset monitoring and robust defense-in-depth controls.
hits.title: Microsoft: Russia's Sandworm APT Exploits Edge Bugs Globally

hits.text: ESET researchers have identified SwiftSlicer, a new Go-written destructive wiper attributed to the Sandworm APT, on a Ukrainian organization’s network on January 25 via malicious Group Policy, indicating full Active Directory compromise; detected as WinGo/KillFiles, SwiftSlicer deletes shadow copies and recursively overwrites files in %CSIDL_SYSTEM%\drivers, %CSIDL_SYSTEM_DRIVE%\Windows\NTDS and other drives with 4,096-byte random blocks before forcing a reboot. This deployment method mirrors earlier HermeticWiper and CaddyWiper attacks—CaddyWiper was used against Ukrinform—and follows a wave of RansomBoggs ransomware linked to Sandworm two months prior. Sandworm’s near-decade track record of disruptive campaigns against Ukrainian critical infrastructure includes BlackEnergy, GreyEnergy, the original Industroyer, and a thwarted Industroyer2 in April, underscoring the imperative to harden Active Directory, monitor Group Policy changes, and maintain secure, offline backups.
hits.title: SwiftSlicer: New destructive wiper malware strikes Ukraine

hits.text: Government-backed actors have rapidly weaponized CVE-2023-38831, a logic flaw in WinRAR versions prior to 6.23 that abuses Windows ShellExecute’s handling of filenames with embedded spaces to trigger default extension resolution and execute unintended “.cmd” or “.bat” payloads; although RARLabs patched the bug in August 2023, public proof-of-concepts surfaced within hours, enabling multiple APTs and financially motivated groups to launch spear-phishing and drive-by campaigns. TAG observed Russian GRU-linked FROZENBARENTS (aka SANDWORM) in September luring energy sector and financial targets with a faux Ukrainian drone-training PDF that dropped a packed Rhadamanthys infostealer, FROZENLAKE (aka APT28) using a free hosting redirect chain and a decoy Razumkov Centre invite to deploy a BAT-delivered reverse SSH shell and IRONJAW PowerShell stealer, and Chinese-linked ISLANDDREAMS (aka APT40) targeting Papua New Guinea via Dropbox-hosted archives that sideload an XOR-encoded DLL to load a Donut-generated BOXRAT backdoor in-memory. These operations underscore the urgency of immediate patch deployment, throttled n-day mitigation, Google Safe Browsing/Gmail defenses, and ongoing monitoring for exploit indicators to prevent credential theft, unauthorized code execution, and persistent C2 channels.
hits.title: Government-backed actors exploiting WinRAR vulnerability

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

canonical_entities: multi-year espionage campaign uncovered by Mandiant
hits.text: In a multi-year espionage campaign uncovered by Mandiant, the Chinese UNC3886 group exploited a critical VMware vCenter Server zero-day (CVE-2023-34048) from late 2021 until its October 2023 patch, triggering vmdird service crashes and removing core dumps to stealthily gain privileged access, then delivering VirtualPita and VirtualPie backdoors via malicious vSphere Installation Bundles on ESXi hosts; they subsequently chained the VMware Tools authentication bypass flaw (CVE-2023-20867) to escalate privileges, harvest and exfiltrate files from guest VMs. UNC3886—targeting defense, government, telecom and technology sectors in the US and APJ—also abused a Fortinet firewall zero-day (CVE-2022-41328) to deploy Castletap and Thincrust implants, demonstrating advanced reverse-engineering of FortiOS. This campaign highlights the urgent need for rapid patching of virtualization and firewall platforms, deployment of EDR solutions and preservation of forensic artifacts to detect and thwart such sophisticated attacks.
hits.title: Chinese hackers exploit VMware bug as zero-day for two years

hits.text: Since at least 2020, Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a novel GRU-affiliated Russian group—now named Cadet Blizzard (formerly DEV-0586)—that has executed destructive cyber campaigns against government, law enforcement, NGO and IT service providers primarily in Ukraine, Europe and Latin America, peaking January–June 2022 with the WhisperGate MBR-wiper and website defacements, then re-emerging in January 2023 to renew hack-and-leak operations under the “Free Civilian” forum; Cadet Blizzard leverages exploitation of perimeter web servers (notably CVE-2021-26084 Confluence, Exchange CVE-2022-41040/ProxyShell), living-off-the-land tactics for lateral movement (Impacket modules, PowerShell get-volume, reg save), credential harvesting via renamed procdump64 dumps of LSASS, persistence with commodity and custom web shells (P0wnyshell, reGeorg, PAS variants), and socket-based tunneling tools (NetCat, GOST) often via scheduled tasks; operational mistakes have limited scale compared to Forest or Seashell Blizzard yet still risk significant network disruption, data exfiltration and strategic intelligence leakage; defenders should prioritize patching exposed web services, monitor for known IoCs and anomalous web-shell activity, LSASS and registry dumps, unusual scheduled tasks or renamed tunneling binaries, and collaborate with CERT-UA and global partners for timely threat intelligence sharing and incident response.
hits.title: Cadet Blizzard emerges as a novel and distinct Russian threat actor | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

hits.text: In Q1 2023, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) found that over 60 percent of Russian state-backed phishing campaigns were aimed at Ukraine, led by FROZENBARENTS (aka Sandworm, GRU Unit 74455), which abused globally compromised EXIM mail servers, SMS-delivered phishing links and fake Windows update payloads deploying the Rhadamanthys stealer, then maintained persistence via webshells and Adminer to exfiltrate data to the CyberArmyofRussia_Reborn Telegram channel across government, defense, energy (notably the Caspian Pipeline Consortium), transport, education and humanitarian sectors while conducting information operations. Simultaneously, FROZENLAKE (APT28) leveraged reflected XSS on Ukrainian government sites to redirect users to phishing domains hosted on free services, with harvested credentials sent to compromised Ubiquiti devices; Belarusian PUSHCHA continued targeted low-volume campaigns against regional webmail providers; and IRA-linked actors deployed coordinated YouTube Shorts and Blogger posts to amplify pro-Wagner, anti-Ukrainian narratives. Financially motivated Cuba ransomware affiliates pivoted to intelligence collection using RomCom malware via ChatGPT/OpenAI-spoofed domains against conference attendees. TAG’s takedowns and Safe Browsing protections, coupled with targeted Gmail alerts, underscore the need for organizations to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, patch mail servers, monitor for unauthorized EXIM access, and guard against reflected XSS and SMS phishing.
hits.title: Ukraine remains Russia’s biggest cyber focus in 2023

hits.text: In May 2023, after U.S. authorities secured convictions against three high-level operators and declared the Russia-based cybercrime enterprise Fin7 “no more,” security experts began spotting first signs of its resurrection in April 2024 when Blackberry reported a typosquatting-based malware intrusion against a major automotive firm; since January 2024, Silent Push analyst Zach Edwards has mapped over 4,000 Fin7-linked hosts—rented largely on the pro-Russia Stark Industries Solutions platform—employing typosquatting, booby-trapped ads, malicious browser extensions and spear-phishing domains to mimic hundreds of brands from American Express and Microsoft 365 to CNN and Zoom, as well as popular free software tools such as 7-zip, PuTTY and Python, all “aged” on innocuous templates for six to nine months before weaponization; eSentire and Malwarebytes also observed sponsored Google ads pushing phony extensions in May and April 2024, and Fin7 has even deployed domains targeting Louvre and Olympic tourists, building on its 2013–present campaign that has extorted some $3 billion from victim organizations, underscoring the urgent need for renewed law enforcement focus and proactive domain-monitoring defenses.

hits.text: Russia’s APT29 (aka Cozy Bear/Nobelium) has been exploiting a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in JetBrains TeamCity (CVE-2023-42793, CVSS 9.8) since September—shortly after JetBrains issued a patch and Rapid7 published a proof-of-concept—to gain initial access to SDLC management servers, escalate privileges, move laterally, deploy stealthy backdoors that persist through updates, and potentially manipulate build pipelines or insert malicious updates in SolarWinds-style supply-chain attacks; CISA, FBI, NSA and international partners warn that around 800 internet-exposed instances remain vulnerable (with uncounted internally reachable servers also at risk), and that North Korea’s Lazarus and Andariel groups have similarly weaponized the same flaw, prompting Fortinet to report multi-actor post-exploit techniques in live incidents; mitigation guidance urges immediate upgrading to TeamCity 2023.05.4, removal of public exposure, comprehensive IoC-based threat hunting across servers and build agents, and full compromise assessments to eradicate entrenched backdoors.
hits.title: Global TeamCity Exploitation Opens Door to SolarWinds-Style Nightmare

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

hits.text: Since at least April 2024 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a Russia-affiliated cyberespionage actor dubbed Void Blizzard (aka LAUNDRY BEAR) conducting high-volume, targeted operations against government, defense, transportation, media, NGO and healthcare organizations—particularly in NATO member states and Ukraine—by leveraging stolen credentials procured via commodity infostealer ecosystems for password spray attacks and Exchange/SharePoint Online access, then automating bulk email and file collection (and in some cases Teams messages) via cloud APIs and tools like AzureHound; in April 2025 the actor evolved to adversary-in-the-middle spear phishing using a typosquatted domain and the open-source Evilginx framework with a malicious QR-coded PDF to harvest Entra authentication data; this widespread success underscores that even unsophisticated TTPs pose major intelligence risks to critical sectors, so organizations should enforce sign-in risk policies and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO/passkeys), centralize identity management with Conditional Access, monitor risky sign-ins and mailbox auditing, apply least-privilege credential hygiene, and promptly rotate credentials after infostealer detections to disrupt Void Blizzard’s operations.

canonical_entities: Scanning the Internet for IoT devices with open Telnet/SSH ports
Use of default or weak credentials
Encrypted SOCKS5 tunneling to proxy infrastructure
hits.text: Researchers have uncovered that since early 2024 a previously undocumented botnet, dubbed Ngioweb, has been systematically scanning the Internet for IoT devices—primarily DVRs, IP cameras and home routers—with open Telnet/SSH ports and default or weak credentials, exploiting known firmware vulnerabilities to deploy a lightweight Go-based loader that establishes encrypted SOCKS5 tunnels back to a resilient NSOCKS residential proxy network of over 150,000 infected nodes. Once a device is compromised, Ngioweb drops a persistent agent that connects to fast-flux C2 domains via HTTPS, retrieves updated encryption keys and proxy configuration, and registers the node for NSOCKS’ tiered subscription service (starting at $25/month), which reportedly generates upwards of $500K in monthly revenue by fueling large-scale credential-stuffing campaigns, ad fraud and DDoS-for-hire operations. The actors behind Ngioweb continually rotate fallback C2 domains, employ encryption and obfuscation to evade signature-based detection, and monitor infection success rates in real time, enabling rapid retooling and expansion. Defenders are urged to enforce strong, unique credentials on all IoT assets, disable unused management interfaces, apply timely firmware updates, implement network segmentation and deploy behavioral analytics or honeypots to detect anomalous outbound proxy traffic.
hits.title: Ngioweb Botnet Fuels NSOCKS Residential Proxy Network Exploiting IoT Devices

hits.text: Since at least May 2023, BlackBerry researchers have identified a technically sophisticated Chinese-speaking threat actor—dubbed Silent Skimmer—that after over a year skimming card data from Asia/Pacific e-commerce and point-of-sale sites has expanded its campaign to North and Latin America, compromising organizations across multiple sectors by exploiting known web application vulnerabilities—most notably CVE-2019-18935 in Progress Software’s Telerik UI previously used by China’s Hafnium and Vietnam’s XE Group—on IIS servers to upload a malicious DLL and achieve remote code execution; using a multi-stage toolkit comprising privilege escalation exploits, a remote access tool, stagers/downloaders, and post-exploit utilities along with open-source binaries and scripts to inject card-skimming code into payment pages; and dynamically rotating short-lived, regionally co-located Microsoft Azure VPS-based C2 servers (each active less than a week) to blend exfiltration traffic with normal operations, mirroring Magecart tactics that have impacted hundreds of thousands of sites (e.g., British Airways, Ticketmaster, Newegg), and highlighting the imperative for prompt patching of third-party components, comprehensive web-app security audits, and vigilant monitoring of anomalous C2 infrastructure to thwart credential and payment data theft.

attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
hits.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

canonical_entities: Defense evasion via virtual machine execution
deployment of a VirtualBox VM running Windows XP to execute encryption, thereby evading host defenses
hits.text: Ragnar Locker, active since December 2019 and first flagged by the FBI in April 2020, is a hybrid ransomware strain and operator gang responsible for breaching 52 organizations across 10 critical infrastructure sectors—including energy, manufacturing, financial services, government, IT and agriculture—employing double-extortion by exfiltrating sensitive data before encryption and threatening public leaks if ransoms go unpaid. Intrusions begin with RDP access via brute-force or stolen credentials, privilege escalation through CVE-2017-0213, and deployment of a VirtualBox VM running Windows XP to execute encryption, thereby evading host defenses; they delete shadow copies, disable antivirus (e.g., Sophos, Veeam) and remote management tools (Kaseya, ConnectWise), and spread laterally via PowerShell. Obfuscation is achieved through junk code, encrypted PE-embedded configs (".keys"), runtime string decryption, locale checks to avoid CIS targets and a custom Salsa20 cipher with a bespoke 64-byte key matrix appending “_RAGNAR_” to footers. Major attacks include Campari Group (2 TB, $15 M), Energias de Portugal (10 TB, 1 580 BTC), Capcom (1 TB) and Dassault Falcon Jet, with the FBI warning of heightened risks to food/agriculture during planting/harvest. Ragnar Locker pressures victims to avoid law enforcement, yet paying ransoms funds criminality and fails to guarantee data deletion; mitigation requires hardened RDP/MFA, patching CVE-2017-0213, network segmentation, behavioral EDR, offline backups and timely incident reporting to the FBI.
hits.title: Ragnar Locker Ransomware (Everything You Need To Know)

canonical_entities: multi-year espionage campaign uncovered by Mandiant
hits.text: In a multi-year espionage campaign uncovered by Mandiant, the Chinese UNC3886 group exploited a critical VMware vCenter Server zero-day (CVE-2023-34048) from late 2021 until its October 2023 patch, triggering vmdird service crashes and removing core dumps to stealthily gain privileged access, then delivering VirtualPita and VirtualPie backdoors via malicious vSphere Installation Bundles on ESXi hosts; they subsequently chained the VMware Tools authentication bypass flaw (CVE-2023-20867) to escalate privileges, harvest and exfiltrate files from guest VMs. UNC3886—targeting defense, government, telecom and technology sectors in the US and APJ—also abused a Fortinet firewall zero-day (CVE-2022-41328) to deploy Castletap and Thincrust implants, demonstrating advanced reverse-engineering of FortiOS. This campaign highlights the urgent need for rapid patching of virtualization and firewall platforms, deployment of EDR solutions and preservation of forensic artifacts to detect and thwart such sophisticated attacks.

retrieval_events.query: What tactics did the BadPilot campaign use to achieve its objectives?

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
retrieved_context.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Since late 2021, Russia’s GRU-aligned Sandworm APT (Seashell Blizzard) has deployed an initial-access subgroup dubbed BadPilot to stealthily breach high-value telecom, oil and gas, shipping, arms-manufacturing and government networks worldwide by exploiting critical CVSS 9.8 vulnerabilities—Zimbra CVE-2022-41352, Exchange CVE-2021-34473 and Outlook CVE-2023-23397—and, from early 2024, remote-monitoring-and-management flaws such as Fortinet FortiClient EMS CVE-2023-48788 and ScreenConnect CVE-2024-1709 (CVSS 10.0). Following initial access, BadPilot establishes persistence via its custom LocalOlive web shell or legitimate RMM tools (“ShadowLink”) configured as Tor hidden services, harvests credentials, performs lateral movement, exfiltrates data and stages follow-on operations. These agile, low-noise TTPs have underpinned Sandworm’s high-impact campaigns—from NotPetya and 2018 Olympic disruptions to multiple destructive power-grid outages in Ukraine and an attack on Denmark’s energy sector—advancing Russia’s strategic objectives. Critical organizations must therefore enforce timely patching of Internet-facing services, continuous asset monitoring and robust defense-in-depth controls.
retrieved_context.title: Microsoft: Russia's Sandworm APT Exploits Edge Bugs Globally

canonical_entities: Scanning the Internet for IoT devices with open Telnet/SSH ports
Use of default or weak credentials
Encrypted SOCKS5 tunneling to proxy infrastructure
retrieved_context.text: Researchers have uncovered that since early 2024 a previously undocumented botnet, dubbed Ngioweb, has been systematically scanning the Internet for IoT devices—primarily DVRs, IP cameras and home routers—with open Telnet/SSH ports and default or weak credentials, exploiting known firmware vulnerabilities to deploy a lightweight Go-based loader that establishes encrypted SOCKS5 tunnels back to a resilient NSOCKS residential proxy network of over 150,000 infected nodes. Once a device is compromised, Ngioweb drops a persistent agent that connects to fast-flux C2 domains via HTTPS, retrieves updated encryption keys and proxy configuration, and registers the node for NSOCKS’ tiered subscription service (starting at $25/month), which reportedly generates upwards of $500K in monthly revenue by fueling large-scale credential-stuffing campaigns, ad fraud and DDoS-for-hire operations. The actors behind Ngioweb continually rotate fallback C2 domains, employ encryption and obfuscation to evade signature-based detection, and monitor infection success rates in real time, enabling rapid retooling and expansion. Defenders are urged to enforce strong, unique credentials on all IoT assets, disable unused management interfaces, apply timely firmware updates, implement network segmentation and deploy behavioral analytics or honeypots to detect anomalous outbound proxy traffic.
retrieved_context.title: Ngioweb Botnet Fuels NSOCKS Residential Proxy Network Exploiting IoT Devices

retrieved_context.text: Since at least May 2023, BlackBerry researchers have identified a technically sophisticated Chinese-speaking threat actor—dubbed Silent Skimmer—that after over a year skimming card data from Asia/Pacific e-commerce and point-of-sale sites has expanded its campaign to North and Latin America, compromising organizations across multiple sectors by exploiting known web application vulnerabilities—most notably CVE-2019-18935 in Progress Software’s Telerik UI previously used by China’s Hafnium and Vietnam’s XE Group—on IIS servers to upload a malicious DLL and achieve remote code execution; using a multi-stage toolkit comprising privilege escalation exploits, a remote access tool, stagers/downloaders, and post-exploit utilities along with open-source binaries and scripts to inject card-skimming code into payment pages; and dynamically rotating short-lived, regionally co-located Microsoft Azure VPS-based C2 servers (each active less than a week) to blend exfiltration traffic with normal operations, mirroring Magecart tactics that have impacted hundreds of thousands of sites (e.g., British Airways, Ticketmaster, Newegg), and highlighting the imperative for prompt patching of third-party components, comprehensive web-app security audits, and vigilant monitoring of anomalous C2 infrastructure to thwart credential and payment data theft.
retrieved_context.title: Payment Card-Skimming Campaign Now Targeting Websites in North America

retrieved_context.text: ESET researchers have identified SwiftSlicer, a new Go-written destructive wiper attributed to the Sandworm APT, on a Ukrainian organization’s network on January 25 via malicious Group Policy, indicating full Active Directory compromise; detected as WinGo/KillFiles, SwiftSlicer deletes shadow copies and recursively overwrites files in %CSIDL_SYSTEM%\drivers, %CSIDL_SYSTEM_DRIVE%\Windows\NTDS and other drives with 4,096-byte random blocks before forcing a reboot. This deployment method mirrors earlier HermeticWiper and CaddyWiper attacks—CaddyWiper was used against Ukrinform—and follows a wave of RansomBoggs ransomware linked to Sandworm two months prior. Sandworm’s near-decade track record of disruptive campaigns against Ukrainian critical infrastructure includes BlackEnergy, GreyEnergy, the original Industroyer, and a thwarted Industroyer2 in April, underscoring the imperative to harden Active Directory, monitor Group Policy changes, and maintain secure, offline backups.
retrieved_context.title: SwiftSlicer: New destructive wiper malware strikes Ukraine

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
retrieved_context.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: Defense evasion via virtual machine execution
deployment of a VirtualBox VM running Windows XP to execute encryption, thereby evading host defenses
retrieved_context.text: Ragnar Locker, active since December 2019 and first flagged by the FBI in April 2020, is a hybrid ransomware strain and operator gang responsible for breaching 52 organizations across 10 critical infrastructure sectors—including energy, manufacturing, financial services, government, IT and agriculture—employing double-extortion by exfiltrating sensitive data before encryption and threatening public leaks if ransoms go unpaid. Intrusions begin with RDP access via brute-force or stolen credentials, privilege escalation through CVE-2017-0213, and deployment of a VirtualBox VM running Windows XP to execute encryption, thereby evading host defenses; they delete shadow copies, disable antivirus (e.g., Sophos, Veeam) and remote management tools (Kaseya, ConnectWise), and spread laterally via PowerShell. Obfuscation is achieved through junk code, encrypted PE-embedded configs (".keys"), runtime string decryption, locale checks to avoid CIS targets and a custom Salsa20 cipher with a bespoke 64-byte key matrix appending “_RAGNAR_” to footers. Major attacks include Campari Group (2 TB, $15 M), Energias de Portugal (10 TB, 1 580 BTC), Capcom (1 TB) and Dassault Falcon Jet, with the FBI warning of heightened risks to food/agriculture during planting/harvest. Ragnar Locker pressures victims to avoid law enforcement, yet paying ransoms funds criminality and fails to guarantee data deletion; mitigation requires hardened RDP/MFA, patching CVE-2017-0213, network segmentation, behavioral EDR, offline backups and timely incident reporting to the FBI.
retrieved_context.title: Ragnar Locker Ransomware (Everything You Need To Know)

canonical_entities: multi-year espionage campaign uncovered by Mandiant
retrieved_context.text: In a multi-year espionage campaign uncovered by Mandiant, the Chinese UNC3886 group exploited a critical VMware vCenter Server zero-day (CVE-2023-34048) from late 2021 until its October 2023 patch, triggering vmdird service crashes and removing core dumps to stealthily gain privileged access, then delivering VirtualPita and VirtualPie backdoors via malicious vSphere Installation Bundles on ESXi hosts; they subsequently chained the VMware Tools authentication bypass flaw (CVE-2023-20867) to escalate privileges, harvest and exfiltrate files from guest VMs. UNC3886—targeting defense, government, telecom and technology sectors in the US and APJ—also abused a Fortinet firewall zero-day (CVE-2022-41328) to deploy Castletap and Thincrust implants, demonstrating advanced reverse-engineering of FortiOS. This campaign highlights the urgent need for rapid patching of virtualization and firewall platforms, deployment of EDR solutions and preservation of forensic artifacts to detect and thwart such sophisticated attacks.

canonical_entities: exfiltrates credentials, contacts and email content via HTTP POST
hits.text: In Operation RoundPress, the Sednit group (aka APT28/Fancy Bear) has since 2023 employed spear-phishing emails embedding XSS exploits against high-value webmail portals—initially abusing CVE-2020-35730 in Roundcube and, from 2024, expanding to zero-day CVE-2024-11182 in MDaemon plus known flaws CVE-2023-43770 in Roundcube, CVE-2024-27443 in Zimbra, and an old XSS in Horde—to inject obfuscated SpyPress JavaScript that exfiltrates credentials, contacts and email content via HTTP POST, sets persistent Sieve-based forwarding rules and even bypasses two-factor authentication; predominantly targeting governmental and defense entities in Eastern Europe (notably Ukraine, Bulgaria and Romania) with additional victims in Africa, Europe and South America; these campaigns, attributed to Sednit with medium confidence through reusable domains and email addresses, underline the critical need to patch webmail software promptly, enforce robust email filtering, monitor C&C traffic and audit server-side mail rules.
hits.title: Operation RoundPress targeting high-value webmail servers

hits.text: Active since at least 2004 and linked to the Russian GRU, APT28 (Fancy Bear, Forest Blizzard, Sednit, Sofacy) has been exploiting XSS vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra mail servers across Europe, Africa and South America since September 2023 under “Operation RoundPress,” targeting governments tied to the Ukraine conflict—such as Ukraine’s government and defense firms in Bulgaria and Romania—and more broadly French organizations after France’s recent attribution of a dozen government and other entities, including a decade-old TV5Monde attack. Employing CVE-2020-35730 (Roundcube; CISA KEV June 2023), CVE-2023-43770 (Roundcube; KEV February 2024) and zero-day CVE-2024-11182 (MDaemon), APT28 injects malicious JavaScript implants (“SpyPress”) via phishing emails that bypass spam filters and execute in the victim’s browser context to steal webmail credentials through hidden forms or counterfeit login pages, harvest messages and contacts, create forwarding rules, and defeat two-factor authentication. ESET’s findings highlight the convenience of remote-triggered webmail XSS, the prevalence of unpatched servers, and the urgent need for organizations to apply KEV-listed patches, enforce robust email filtering, and monitor for anomalous mailbox behaviors to mitigate email exfiltration and credential compromise.
hits.title: Russian APT Exploiting Mail Servers Against Government, Defense Organizations - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Microsoft’s latest joint report with Dutch intelligence exposes a year-long espionage campaign by the Russia-linked APT “Void Blizzard,” which has systematically purchased stolen credentials from infostealer markets to fuel password-spraying attacks against European and North American government and defense contractors—particularly NATO states and Ukraine—before pivoting in recent weeks to adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) spear-phishing via a typo-squatted Microsoft Entra login page and malicious QR code for a sham European defense summit. Leveraging the open-source Evilginx framework, the group captures usernames, passwords and session cookies, then abuses legitimate cloud APIs such as Exchange Online and Microsoft Graph to enumerate mailboxes (including shared folders), automate bulk exfiltration of emails, files and, in some cases, Microsoft Teams chats, and uses AzureHound to harvest Entra ID tenant configurations. Since mid-2024, Void Blizzard’s straightforward playbook—steal credentials, infiltrate Exchange or SharePoint Online, and automate data downloads—has compromised telcos, defense suppliers, digital services providers, healthcare and IT firms, posing an elevated risk of wartime intelligence siphoning for Kremlin military and diplomatic operations.
hits.title: Russian Government Hackers Caught Buying Passwords from Cybercriminals - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. More recently, the group shifted to adversary-in-the-middle spear-phishing using a typosquatted “micsrosoftonline[.]com” domain and an Evilginx-based phishing page delivered through malicious QR codes in forged European Defense and Security Summit PDF invitations, automating bulk data collection via Exchange, Microsoft Graph and Teams web client. Overlaps with Forest Blizzard, Midnight Blizzard and Secret Blizzard indicate coordinated Russian strategic espionage, and a September 2024 pass-the-cookie breach of a Dutch police account underscores their evolving cookie-theft capabilities—highlighting urgent needs for phishing-resistant MFA and hardened Entra ID configurations.
hits.title: Russian Hackers Breach 20+ NGOs Using Evilginx Phishing via Fake Microsoft Entra Pages
