hits.text: Since at least April 2024 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a Russia-affiliated cyberespionage actor dubbed Void Blizzard (aka LAUNDRY BEAR) conducting high-volume, targeted operations against government, defense, transportation, media, NGO and healthcare organizations—particularly in NATO member states and Ukraine—by leveraging stolen credentials procured via commodity infostealer ecosystems for password spray attacks and Exchange/SharePoint Online access, then automating bulk email and file collection (and in some cases Teams messages) via cloud APIs and tools like AzureHound; in April 2025 the actor evolved to adversary-in-the-middle spear phishing using a typosquatted domain and the open-source Evilginx framework with a malicious QR-coded PDF to harvest Entra authentication data; this widespread success underscores that even unsophisticated TTPs pose major intelligence risks to critical sectors, so organizations should enforce sign-in risk policies and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO/passkeys), centralize identity management with Conditional Access, monitor risky sign-ins and mailbox auditing, apply least-privilege credential hygiene, and promptly rotate credentials after infostealer detections to disrupt Void Blizzard’s operations.
hits.title: New Russia-affiliated actor Void Blizzard targets critical sectors for espionage | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine
hits.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.
hits.title: Hackers with Russian Blizzard Steal Data from Rival Networks

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
hits.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: deployed a webshell on the router’s web server
Credentials from Password Stores: Security Account Manager
hits.text: Dragos researchers, in collaboration with Ukraine’s CSSC, unearthed FrostyGoop—an ICS-specific malware first spotted in April and used in January to disrupt central heating in over 600 Lviv apartment buildings—marking the first known malware to leverage Modbus TCP for read/write operations on operational technology. Attackers gained initial access in April 2023 by exploiting a MikroTik router vulnerability, deployed a webshell on the router’s web server, and maintained persistence via Tor and L2TP tunnels to Moscow-based IPs. After spending months conducting reconnaissance, they extracted credentials by dumping the SAM registry hive in December, then directly issued scripted Modbus commands—read from a JSON configuration file—to publicly exposed ENCO heating controllers, even downgrading firmware to disable monitoring and force inaccurate measurements that halted heating services for nearly two days amid subzero temperatures. This incident underscores the threat posed by internet-exposed ICS devices—over 46,000 globally using Modbus—and highlights poor network segmentation, unpatched ICS CVEs, and the ease with which FrostyGoop’s protocol-agnostic payload can be repurposed against diverse industrial controllers, necessitating immediate network segmentation, firmware monitoring, and patch management in OT environments.
hits.title: ICS malware FrostyGoop disrupted heating in Ukraine, remains threat to OT worldwide

retrieved_context.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
retrieved_context.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
retrieved_context.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.

retrieved_context.text: Dragos researchers, in collaboration with Ukraine’s CSSC, unearthed FrostyGoop—an ICS-specific malware first spotted in April and used in January to disrupt central heating in over 600 Lviv apartment buildings—marking the first known malware to leverage Modbus TCP for read/write operations on operational technology. Attackers gained initial access in April 2023 by exploiting a MikroTik router vulnerability, deployed a webshell on the router’s web server, and maintained persistence via Tor and L2TP tunnels to Moscow-based IPs. After spending months conducting reconnaissance, they extracted credentials by dumping the SAM registry hive in December, then directly issued scripted Modbus commands—read from a JSON configuration file—to publicly exposed ENCO heating controllers, even downgrading firmware to disable monitoring and force inaccurate measurements that halted heating services for nearly two days amid subzero temperatures. This incident underscores the threat posed by internet-exposed ICS devices—over 46,000 globally using Modbus—and highlights poor network segmentation, unpatched ICS CVEs, and the ease with which FrostyGoop’s protocol-agnostic payload can be repurposed against diverse industrial controllers, necessitating immediate network segmentation, firmware monitoring, and patch management in OT environments.
retrieved_context.title: ICS malware FrostyGoop disrupted heating in Ukraine, remains threat to OT worldwide

hits.text: Active since at least 2004 and linked to the Russian GRU, APT28 (Fancy Bear, Forest Blizzard, Sednit, Sofacy) has been exploiting XSS vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra mail servers across Europe, Africa and South America since September 2023 under “Operation RoundPress,” targeting governments tied to the Ukraine conflict—such as Ukraine’s government and defense firms in Bulgaria and Romania—and more broadly French organizations after France’s recent attribution of a dozen government and other entities, including a decade-old TV5Monde attack. Employing CVE-2020-35730 (Roundcube; CISA KEV June 2023), CVE-2023-43770 (Roundcube; KEV February 2024) and zero-day CVE-2024-11182 (MDaemon), APT28 injects malicious JavaScript implants (“SpyPress”) via phishing emails that bypass spam filters and execute in the victim’s browser context to steal webmail credentials through hidden forms or counterfeit login pages, harvest messages and contacts, create forwarding rules, and defeat two-factor authentication. ESET’s findings highlight the convenience of remote-triggered webmail XSS, the prevalence of unpatched servers, and the urgent need for organizations to apply KEV-listed patches, enforce robust email filtering, and monitor for anomalous mailbox behaviors to mitigate email exfiltration and credential compromise.
hits.title: Russian APT Exploiting Mail Servers Against Government, Defense Organizations - SecurityWeek

hits.text: In Operation RoundPress, the Sednit group (aka APT28/Fancy Bear) has since 2023 employed spear-phishing emails embedding XSS exploits against high-value webmail portals—initially abusing CVE-2020-35730 in Roundcube and, from 2024, expanding to zero-day CVE-2024-11182 in MDaemon plus known flaws CVE-2023-43770 in Roundcube, CVE-2024-27443 in Zimbra, and an old XSS in Horde—to inject obfuscated SpyPress JavaScript that exfiltrates credentials, contacts and email content via HTTP POST, sets persistent Sieve-based forwarding rules and even bypasses two-factor authentication; predominantly targeting governmental and defense entities in Eastern Europe (notably Ukraine, Bulgaria and Romania) with additional victims in Africa, Europe and South America; these campaigns, attributed to Sednit with medium confidence through reusable domains and email addresses, underline the critical need to patch webmail software promptly, enforce robust email filtering, monitor C&C traffic and audit server-side mail rules.

hits.text: Microsoft’s latest joint report with Dutch intelligence exposes a year-long espionage campaign by the Russia-linked APT “Void Blizzard,” which has systematically purchased stolen credentials from infostealer markets to fuel password-spraying attacks against European and North American government and defense contractors—particularly NATO states and Ukraine—before pivoting in recent weeks to adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) spear-phishing via a typo-squatted Microsoft Entra login page and malicious QR code for a sham European defense summit. Leveraging the open-source Evilginx framework, the group captures usernames, passwords and session cookies, then abuses legitimate cloud APIs such as Exchange Online and Microsoft Graph to enumerate mailboxes (including shared folders), automate bulk exfiltration of emails, files and, in some cases, Microsoft Teams chats, and uses AzureHound to harvest Entra ID tenant configurations. Since mid-2024, Void Blizzard’s straightforward playbook—steal credentials, infiltrate Exchange or SharePoint Online, and automate data downloads—has compromised telcos, defense suppliers, digital services providers, healthcare and IT firms, posing an elevated risk of wartime intelligence siphoning for Kremlin military and diplomatic operations.
hits.title: Russian Government Hackers Caught Buying Passwords from Cybercriminals - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. hits.text: ESET researchers uncovered the Iran-aligned APT35 (aka Ballistic Bobcat, Charming Kitten, TA453/PHOSPHORUS) deploying a novel Sponsor backdoor across at least 34 opportunistic victims—primarily Israeli organizations in sectors from automotive to telecommunications, plus medical targets in Brazil and the UAE—by scanning for and exploiting Exchange CVE-2021-26855 vulnerabilities since September 2021, wrapping up their CISA AA21-321A/PowerLess campaign before dropping Sponsor via innocuously named batch files that deploy configuration files (config.txt, node.txt) to disk, install a persistent Windows service (“SystemNetwork”/“Update”) when run with an “install” argument, then periodically RC4-decrypt and call back to embedded C2 relays, all while leveraging open-source tooling (Mimikatz, Chisel, GO Simple Tunnel, Plink, RevSocks and Merlin) for lateral movement and data exfiltration; ESET has catalogued five Sponsor versions through June 2022, underscoring Ballistic Bobcat’s modular, short-duration, narrowly targeted “Sponsoring Access” campaign and highlighting the need for Exchange patching, service and file monitoring for batch deployments, and detection of RC4-encrypted config lookups to disrupt ongoing espionage operations.

hits.text: In Operation RoundPress, the Sednit group (aka APT28/Fancy Bear) has since 2023 employed spear-phishing emails embedding XSS exploits against high-value webmail portals—initially abusing CVE-2020-35730 in Roundcube and, from 2024, expanding to zero-day CVE-2024-11182 in MDaemon plus known flaws CVE-2023-43770 in Roundcube, CVE-2024-27443 in Zimbra, and an old XSS in Horde—to inject obfuscated SpyPress JavaScript that exfiltrates credentials, contacts and email content via HTTP POST, sets persistent Sieve-based forwarding rules and even bypasses two-factor authentication; predominantly targeting governmental and defense entities in Eastern Europe (notably Ukraine, Bulgaria and Romania) with additional victims in Africa, Europe and South America; these campaigns, attributed to Sednit with medium confidence through reusable domains and email addresses, underline the critical need to patch webmail software promptly, enforce robust email filtering, monitor C&C traffic and audit server-side mail rules.
hits.title: Operation RoundPress targeting high-value webmail servers

hits.text: Active since at least 2004 and linked to the Russian GRU, APT28 (Fancy Bear, Forest Blizzard, Sednit, Sofacy) has been exploiting XSS vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra mail servers across Europe, Africa and South America since September 2023 under “Operation RoundPress,” targeting governments tied to the Ukraine conflict—such as Ukraine’s government and defense firms in Bulgaria and Romania—and more broadly French organizations after France’s recent attribution of a dozen government and other entities, including a decade-old TV5Monde attack. Employing CVE-2020-35730 (Roundcube; CISA KEV June 2023), CVE-2023-43770 (Roundcube; KEV February 2024) and zero-day CVE-2024-11182 (MDaemon), APT28 injects malicious JavaScript implants (“SpyPress”) via phishing emails that bypass spam filters and execute in the victim’s browser context to steal webmail credentials through hidden forms or counterfeit login pages, harvest messages and contacts, create forwarding rules, and defeat two-factor authentication. ESET’s findings highlight the convenience of remote-triggered webmail XSS, the prevalence of unpatched servers, and the urgent need for organizations to apply KEV-listed patches, enforce robust email filtering, and monitor for anomalous mailbox behaviors to mitigate email exfiltration and credential compromise.
hits.title: Russian APT Exploiting Mail Servers Against Government, Defense Organizations - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Microsoft’s latest joint report with Dutch intelligence exposes a year-long espionage campaign by the Russia-linked APT “Void Blizzard,” which has systematically purchased stolen credentials from infostealer markets to fuel password-spraying attacks against European and North American government and defense contractors—particularly NATO states and Ukraine—before pivoting in recent weeks to adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) spear-phishing via a typo-squatted Microsoft Entra login page and malicious QR code for a sham European defense summit. Leveraging the open-source Evilginx framework, the group captures usernames, passwords and session cookies, then abuses legitimate cloud APIs such as Exchange Online and Microsoft Graph to enumerate mailboxes (including shared folders), automate bulk exfiltration of emails, files and, in some cases, Microsoft Teams chats, and uses AzureHound to harvest Entra ID tenant configurations. Since mid-2024, Void Blizzard’s straightforward playbook—steal credentials, infiltrate Exchange or SharePoint Online, and automate data downloads—has compromised telcos, defense suppliers, digital services providers, healthcare and IT firms, posing an elevated risk of wartime intelligence siphoning for Kremlin military and diplomatic operations.
hits.title: Russian Government Hackers Caught Buying Passwords from Cybercriminals - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Since at least April 2024 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a Russia-affiliated cyberespionage actor dubbed Void Blizzard (aka LAUNDRY BEAR) conducting high-volume, targeted operations against government, defense, transportation, media, NGO and healthcare organizations—particularly in NATO member states and Ukraine—by leveraging stolen credentials procured via commodity infostealer ecosystems for password spray attacks and Exchange/SharePoint Online access, then automating bulk email and file collection (and in some cases Teams messages) via cloud APIs and tools like AzureHound; in April 2025 the actor evolved to adversary-in-the-middle spear phishing using a typosquatted domain and the open-source Evilginx framework with a malicious QR-coded PDF to harvest Entra authentication data; this widespread success underscores that even unsophisticated TTPs pose major intelligence risks to critical sectors, so organizations should enforce sign-in risk policies and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO/passkeys), centralize identity management with Conditional Access, monitor risky sign-ins and mailbox auditing, apply least-privilege credential hygiene, and promptly rotate credentials after infostealer detections to disrupt Void Blizzard’s operations.
hits.title: New Russia-affiliated actor Void Blizzard targets critical sectors for espionage | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. More recently, the group shifted to adversary-in-the-middle spear-phishing using a typosquatted “micsrosoftonline[.]com” domain and an Evilginx-based phishing page delivered through malicious QR codes in forged European Defense and Security Summit PDF invitations, automating bulk data collection via Exchange, Microsoft Graph and Teams web client. Overlaps with Forest Blizzard, Midnight Blizzard and Secret Blizzard indicate coordinated Russian strategic espionage, and a September 2024 pass-the-cookie breach of a Dutch police account underscores their evolving cookie-theft capabilities—highlighting urgent needs for phishing-resistant MFA and hardened Entra ID configurations.
hits.title: Russian Hackers Breach 20+ NGOs Using Evilginx Phishing via Fake Microsoft Entra Pages

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
hits.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

canonical_entities: military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia
hits.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.
hits.title: Operation Lotus Blossom: A New Nation-State Cyberthreat?

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.

hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: registered variables in the Windows Registry
hits.text: In June 2024, HP’s Threat Research team led by Patrick Schlapfer intercepted a low-grade phishing campaign leveraging HTML smuggling via an AES-encrypted HTML attachment containing JavaScript-embedded decryption logic—a novel twist on typical encrypted archives—which, when decrypted, mimicked a legitimate website but dropped a fully commented, French-language VBScript that registered variables in the Windows Registry, staged a JavaScript payload as a scheduled task, and invoked a PowerShell script to deploy the freely available AsyncRAT infostealer. Schlapfer and co-lead Alex Holland’s analysis, including comparison with generative-AI–produced code, concluded the well-structured, human-readable script was likely authored by gen-AI by a low-skill newcomer benefitting from reduced entry barriers, with no obfuscation or complex infrastructure beyond a single C2 server. This first definitive proof of AI-generated malware in the wild underscores the need for defenders to adapt detection strategies to AI-crafted droppers, monitor anomalous AES-in-JavaScript decryption patterns, and anticipate more sophisticated AI-generated payloads poised to emerge within the next two years, thereby heightening the risk to network and endpoint security.
hits.title: AI-Generated Malware Found in the Wild - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.

Phishing emails with ISO or 7z archives
hits.text: In the second half of 2023, ESET telemetry recorded a dramatic uptick in AceCryptor CaaS operations — detections tripled from ~13,000 to over 42,000 endpoints and unique AceCryptor-packed Rescoms RAT incidents soared from under 100 to more than 32,000 — marking Rescoms’ debut as a primary payload. Unlike H1’s focus on Peru, Mexico and Egypt, H2 campaigns heavily targeted European companies, with Poland alone accounting for 26K+ attacks, followed by Ukraine, Spain, Serbia, Bulgaria and Slovakia. Adversaries employed typosquatted domains and abused previously compromised corporate mailboxes to send multi-language, B2B-styled emails containing ISO or 7z archives named “offer/inquiry,” which unpacked AceCryptor to deploy Rescoms for browser and email credential harvesting. Repeated use of identical binaries reduced unique sample counts (23K→17K) despite higher encounter rates, and embedded Rescoms license IDs linked the waves to a single actor. While the overall use of Danabot and RedLine Stealer with AceCryptor decreased by over 60%, other families like SmokeLoader, STOP ransomware and Vidar remained active. The operations aimed at initial access for further ransomware or data exfiltration, underscoring the critical need for strict email hygiene and advanced endpoint security.
hits.title: Rescoms rides waves of AceCryptor spam

hits.text: Since mid-September, unknown cybercriminals have been conducting large-scale brute-force attacks against internet-exposed instances of Foundation Accounting Software—widely used by construction sub-industries such as plumbing, HVAC and concrete—by targeting the default “sa” administrator and a second high-privilege account within the MSSQL database accessible via TCP port 4243 (opened for Foundation’s mobile app). After an observed peak of roughly 35,000 rapid login attempts to obtain valid credentials, the attackers enable an extended stored procedure (e.g., xp_cmdshell) to execute OS-level commands and scripts, automating lateral movement and data theft across multiple unrelated victims. Huntress has identified just 33 hosts left with unchanged default passwords, alerted all impacted and at-risk customers, and urges organizations to rotate all Foundation credentials, remove direct internet exposure, and disable the exploited stored procedure to mitigate further compromise.
hits.title: Threat Actors Target Accounting Software Used by Construction Contractors - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: exfiltrates credentials, contacts and email content via HTTP POST
retrieved_context.text: In Operation RoundPress, the Sednit group (aka APT28/Fancy Bear) has since 2023 employed spear-phishing emails embedding XSS exploits against high-value webmail portals—initially abusing CVE-2020-35730 in Roundcube and, from 2024, expanding to zero-day CVE-2024-11182 in MDaemon plus known flaws CVE-2023-43770 in Roundcube, CVE-2024-27443 in Zimbra, and an old XSS in Horde—to inject obfuscated SpyPress JavaScript that exfiltrates credentials, contacts and email content via HTTP POST, sets persistent Sieve-based forwarding rules and even bypasses two-factor authentication; predominantly targeting governmental and defense entities in Eastern Europe (notably Ukraine, Bulgaria and Romania) with additional victims in Africa, Europe and South America; these campaigns, attributed to Sednit with medium confidence through reusable domains and email addresses, underline the critical need to patch webmail software promptly, enforce robust email filtering, monitor C&C traffic and audit server-side mail rules.
retrieved_context.title: Operation RoundPress targeting high-value webmail servers

retrieved_context.text: Active since at least 2004 and linked to the Russian GRU, APT28 (Fancy Bear, Forest Blizzard, Sednit, Sofacy) has been exploiting XSS vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra mail servers across Europe, Africa and South America since September 2023 under “Operation RoundPress,” targeting governments tied to the Ukraine conflict—such as Ukraine’s government and defense firms in Bulgaria and Romania—and more broadly French organizations after France’s recent attribution of a dozen government and other entities, including a decade-old TV5Monde attack. Employing CVE-2020-35730 (Roundcube; CISA KEV June 2023), CVE-2023-43770 (Roundcube; KEV February 2024) and zero-day CVE-2024-11182 (MDaemon), APT28 injects malicious JavaScript implants (“SpyPress”) via phishing emails that bypass spam filters and execute in the victim’s browser context to steal webmail credentials through hidden forms or counterfeit login pages, harvest messages and contacts, create forwarding rules, and defeat two-factor authentication. ESET’s findings highlight the convenience of remote-triggered webmail XSS, the prevalence of unpatched servers, and the urgent need for organizations to apply KEV-listed patches, enforce robust email filtering, and monitor for anomalous mailbox behaviors to mitigate email exfiltration and credential compromise.
retrieved_context.title: Russian APT Exploiting Mail Servers Against Government, Defense Organizations - SecurityWeek

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s latest joint report with Dutch intelligence exposes a year-long espionage campaign by the Russia-linked APT “Void Blizzard,” which has systematically purchased stolen credentials from infostealer markets to fuel password-spraying attacks against European and North American government and defense contractors—particularly NATO states and Ukraine—before pivoting in recent weeks to adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) spear-phishing via a typo-squatted Microsoft Entra login page and malicious QR code for a sham European defense summit. Leveraging the open-source Evilginx framework, the group captures usernames, passwords and session cookies, then abuses legitimate cloud APIs such as Exchange Online and Microsoft Graph to enumerate mailboxes (including shared folders), automate bulk exfiltration of emails, files and, in some cases, Microsoft Teams chats, and uses AzureHound to harvest Entra ID tenant configurations. Since mid-2024, Void Blizzard’s straightforward playbook—steal credentials, infiltrate Exchange or SharePoint Online, and automate data downloads—has compromised telcos, defense suppliers, digital services providers, healthcare and IT firms, posing an elevated risk of wartime intelligence siphoning for Kremlin military and diplomatic operations.
retrieved_context.title: Russian Government Hackers Caught Buying Passwords from Cybercriminals - SecurityWeek

retrieved_context.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. More recently, the group shifted to adversary-in-the-middle spear-phishing using a typosquatted “micsrosoftonline[.]com” domain and an Evilginx-based phishing page delivered through malicious QR codes in forged European Defense and Security Summit PDF invitations, automating bulk data collection via Exchange, Microsoft Graph and Teams web client. Overlaps with Forest Blizzard, Midnight Blizzard and Secret Blizzard indicate coordinated Russian strategic espionage, and a September 2024 pass-the-cookie breach of a Dutch police account underscores their evolving cookie-theft capabilities—highlighting urgent needs for phishing-resistant MFA and hardened Entra ID configurations.
retrieved_context.title: Russian Hackers Breach 20+ NGOs Using Evilginx Phishing via Fake Microsoft Entra Pages

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

retrieved_context.text: Since at least April 2024 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a Russia-affiliated cyberespionage actor dubbed Void Blizzard (aka LAUNDRY BEAR) conducting high-volume, targeted operations against government, defense, transportation, media, NGO and healthcare organizations—particularly in NATO member states and Ukraine—by leveraging stolen credentials procured via commodity infostealer ecosystems for password spray attacks and Exchange/SharePoint Online access, then automating bulk email and file collection (and in some cases Teams messages) via cloud APIs and tools like AzureHound; in April 2025 the actor evolved to adversary-in-the-middle spear phishing using a typosquatted domain and the open-source Evilginx framework with a malicious QR-coded PDF to harvest Entra authentication data; this widespread success underscores that even unsophisticated TTPs pose major intelligence risks to critical sectors, so organizations should enforce sign-in risk policies and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO/passkeys), centralize identity management with Conditional Access, monitor risky sign-ins and mailbox auditing, apply least-privilege credential hygiene, and promptly rotate credentials after infostealer detections to disrupt Void Blizzard’s operations.
retrieved_context.title: New Russia-affiliated actor Void Blizzard targets critical sectors for espionage | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Since at least December 2020, EleKtra-Leak—identified by Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 researchers William Gamazo and Nathaniel Quist—has programmatically harvested AWS IAM credentials exposed on public GitHub repositories within four minutes of exposure, exploiting blind spots in GitHub’s secret scanning and AWSCompromisedKeyQuarantine policy; the adversary conducts account reconnaissance, blocklists victim accounts to deter analysis, configures security groups, then launches behind-VPN c5a.24xlarge EC2 instances from private, non-Marketplace AMIs to mine Monero, operating as many as 474 unique instances between August 30 and October 6, 2023, and fetching bespoke mining software via Google Drive. Evidence suggests overlap with a January 2021 cryptojacking campaign targeting unsecured Docker services using the same custom miner. Despite AWS’s two-minute quarantine response, the campaign maintains continuous fluctuations in compromised accounts, underscoring its rapid, large-scale cryptojacking impact. To mitigate risk, organizations must immediately revoke exposed API keys, remove them from GitHub, and audit repository cloning events for suspicious activity.

canonical_entities: ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates
hits.text: Unit 42 has observed a sharp rise in post-intrusion WastedLocker ransomware attacks by the Evil Corp group—already known for Dridex—against large U.S. organizations in sectors from manufacturing to legal services, with initial compromise typically via ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates that deploy a SocGholish JavaScript loader to profile systems and invoke PowerShell-based Cobalt Strike payloads; attackers then leverage WMI and PsExec for lateral movement, identify high-value and backup systems, elevate privileges, disable Windows Defender, delete shadow copies, install WastedLocker as a service, and encrypt files using a “.<victim_name>wasted” extension while appending ransom notes (“.<victim_name>wasted_info”) with contact addresses on ProtonMail, Airmail and others. Palo Alto Networks’ WildFire, Cortex XDR (anti-ransomware and behavioral threat protection), NGFW DNS signatures and AutoFocus tagging detect and prevent WastedLocker activity; organizations are urged to implement robust, off-site backup strategies and hardened cybersecurity controls to mitigate this high-impact targeted ransomware threat.
hits.title: Threat Assessment: WastedLocker Ransomware

canonical_entities: Palo Alto Networks NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention
hits.text: Unit 42 researchers have uncovered a new, substantially upgraded variant of the Kazuar .NET backdoor—previously observed in 2017 as a second-stage payload by Russian Federal Security Service–linked Pensive Ursa (Turla/Uroburos)—that re-emerged in July 2023 targeting Ukrainian defense organizations via a multi-stage Capibar loader to steal Signal messages, cloud and source-control credentials and other high-value data. This variant adds robust anti-analysis checks (Assembly.Location byte-array loader validation, faked 2008 compilation timestamps), extensive string encryption (multiple custom and ConfuserEx ciphers), hybrid AES payload encryption with RSA-encrypted IV/key plus HMAC-MD5 integrity, and obfuscation of IOCs. It supports 45 discrete commands for system profiling, credential theft and automated task workflows in a multithreaded solver component that writes AES- and RSA-protected result files. Kazuar also implements multiple injection modes (inject, browser- and svchost.exe-centric zombify, combined fallback, remote proxy, single and headless) and uses GUID-derived pseudorandom directories and mutexes to evade detection, while hard-coded agent and build identifiers enable variant tracking. Code overlap with Sunburst underscores its sophistication. Unit 42 has released detailed IOCs, artifacts and a GitHub appendix, and recommends Palo Alto Networks NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention, Cortex XDR, XSIAM, Advanced WildFire and Unit 42 incident response engagement to detect, hunt and mitigate this persistent threat.
hits.title: Over the Kazuar’s Nest: Cracking Down on a Freshly Hatched Backdoor Used by Pensive Ursa (Aka Turla)

canonical_entities: Scanning the Internet for IoT devices with open Telnet/SSH ports
Use of default or weak credentials
Encrypted SOCKS5 tunneling to proxy infrastructure
hits.text: Researchers have uncovered that since early 2024 a previously undocumented botnet, dubbed Ngioweb, has been systematically scanning the Internet for IoT devices—primarily DVRs, IP cameras and home routers—with open Telnet/SSH ports and default or weak credentials, exploiting known firmware vulnerabilities to deploy a lightweight Go-based loader that establishes encrypted SOCKS5 tunnels back to a resilient NSOCKS residential proxy network of over 150,000 infected nodes. Once a device is compromised, Ngioweb drops a persistent agent that connects to fast-flux C2 domains via HTTPS, retrieves updated encryption keys and proxy configuration, and registers the node for NSOCKS’ tiered subscription service (starting at $25/month), which reportedly generates upwards of $500K in monthly revenue by fueling large-scale credential-stuffing campaigns, ad fraud and DDoS-for-hire operations. The actors behind Ngioweb continually rotate fallback C2 domains, employ encryption and obfuscation to evade signature-based detection, and monitor infection success rates in real time, enabling rapid retooling and expansion. Defenders are urged to enforce strong, unique credentials on all IoT assets, disable unused management interfaces, apply timely firmware updates, implement network segmentation and deploy behavioral analytics or honeypots to detect anomalous outbound proxy traffic.
hits.title: Ngioweb Botnet Fuels NSOCKS Residential Proxy Network Exploiting IoT Devices

canonical_entities: Palo Alto Networks NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention
hits.text: Since its debut in 2017 as an advanced .NET second-stage backdoor, Kazuar—attributed to Russian FSB–linked Pensive Ursa (Turla)—reemerged in July 2023 targeting Ukraine’s defense sector alongside a new Capibar first-stage loader, marking its first wild appearance since late 2020. This upgraded variant features extensive stealth and anti-analysis countermeasures—fake 2008 compilation timestamps, custom multi-layer string encryption, assembly-location checks and GUID-based pseudorandom directory and mutex generation—and boasts 45 C2-driven commands for comprehensive system profiling, data collection and credential theft from cloud platforms, source control and Signal. It supports six injection modes (inject, zombify, combined, remote, single and non-interactive), a multithreaded architecture for asynchronous task execution, and a hybrid AES–RSA encryption scheme for task/result files, complicating forensic recovery. Organizations can detect and block Kazuar with Palo Alto Networks NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention, Cortex XDR/XSIAM and WildFire, and engage Unit 42 Incident Response teams for targeted hunting and mitigation guidance.
hits.title: Over the Kazuar’s Nest: Cracking Down on a Freshly Hatched Backdoor Used by Pensive Ursa (Aka Turla)

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
hits.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
retrieved_context.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
retrieved_context.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

retrieved_context.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. More recently, the group shifted to adversary-in-the-middle spear-phishing using a typosquatted “micsrosoftonline[.]com” domain and an Evilginx-based phishing page delivered through malicious QR codes in forged European Defense and Security Summit PDF invitations, automating bulk data collection via Exchange, Microsoft Graph and Teams web client. Overlaps with Forest Blizzard, Midnight Blizzard and Secret Blizzard indicate coordinated Russian strategic espionage, and a September 2024 pass-the-cookie breach of a Dutch police account underscores their evolving cookie-theft capabilities—highlighting urgent needs for phishing-resistant MFA and hardened Entra ID configurations.
retrieved_context.title: Russian Hackers Breach 20+ NGOs Using Evilginx Phishing via Fake Microsoft Entra Pages

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

hits.text: Water Ouroboros is a Ransomware-as-a-Service operation that exploits public-facing Oracle WebLogic vulnerabilities (CVE-2019-2725, CVE-2017-10271, CVE-2019-2729) or drive-by installers for initial access (T1190, T1189), then executes remote Windows commands (wmic.exe, bcdedit.exe, wbadmin.exe, vssadmin.exe) to delete backups and disable recovery (T1490, T1562.001) before encrypting fixed, removable and network drives via a Go-based custom routine that uses RTLGenRandom to generate a symmetric key, protects it with embedded RSA public keys (App_ExportKey), appends “.locked” (unless suppressed with –E), excludes over 60 file extensions, and accepts credentials (c {user}:{pass}), logging (–a), non-aggressive (–A) and size filters (–m). Post-infection, actors maintain access via compromised admin accounts (T1078), disable security tools (PCHunter, ProcessHacker), dump credentials from registry hives (T1003.002), move laterally over RDP/SMB (T1021.001/002), discover assets via AdFind (T1595.002) and exfiltrate data over C&C (SharpRhino RAT/T1071.001, T1041). With 136 incidents in the US and notable impacts on construction, IT, manufacturing and healthcare SMBs, the campaign underscores the need for timely patching, hardened public-facing apps, least-privilege access, MFA, robust backups and advanced threat detection.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Water Ouroboros | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 has identified a first-of-its-kind collaboration between North Korea’s state-sponsored Jumpy Pisces (linked to the Reconnaissance General Bureau) and the Play ransomware gang, revealing a blurring of nation-state and criminal operations: Jumpy Pisces gained initial access in May via a compromised user account, spent months conducting lateral movement and persistence using Sliver C2, custom DTrack info-stealer, a bespoke Mimikatz variant, RDP privileged-account creation tools and a trojanized binary that exfiltrates browser history, autofill data and credit-card details from Chrome, Edge and Brave, then in early September Play deployed its ransomware payload using the same account; Unit 42 attributed the joint operation with moderate confidence based on shared access credentials, continuous Sliver communications until deployment and Play’s known TTPs, though it remains unclear whether Jumpy Pisces acted as a Play affiliate or initial-access broker—this nexus not only underscores the need for defenders to monitor Sliver C2 indicators, credential-theft and RDP hardening but also signals a potential trend of North Korean actors increasingly leveraging underground ransomware networks to fund operations, raising the stakes for global cyber defenses.
hits.title: Play ransomware attack tied to North Korean nation-state actor | TechTarget

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

retrieved_context.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
retrieved_context.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: Steal cloud account credentials (AWS IAM credentials exposed in public repositories)
harvested AWS IAM credentials exposed on public GitHub repositories
hits.text: Since at least December 2020, EleKtra-Leak—identified by Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 researchers William Gamazo and Nathaniel Quist—has programmatically harvested AWS IAM credentials exposed on public GitHub repositories within four minutes of exposure, exploiting blind spots in GitHub’s secret scanning and AWSCompromisedKeyQuarantine policy; the adversary conducts account reconnaissance, blocklists victim accounts to deter analysis, configures security groups, then launches behind-VPN c5a.24xlarge EC2 instances from private, non-Marketplace AMIs to mine Monero, operating as many as 474 unique instances between August 30 and October 6, 2023, and fetching bespoke mining software via Google Drive. Evidence suggests overlap with a January 2021 cryptojacking campaign targeting unsecured Docker services using the same custom miner. Despite AWS’s two-minute quarantine response, the campaign maintains continuous fluctuations in compromised accounts, underscoring its rapid, large-scale cryptojacking impact. To mitigate risk, organizations must immediately revoke exposed API keys, remove them from GitHub, and audit repository cloning events for suspicious activity.
hits.title: EleKtra-Leak Cryptojacking Attacks Exploit AWS IAM Credentials Exposed on GitHub

canonical_entities: Palo Alto Networks NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention
hits.text: Unit 42 researchers have uncovered a new, substantially upgraded variant of the Kazuar .NET backdoor—previously observed in 2017 as a second-stage payload by Russian Federal Security Service–linked Pensive Ursa (Turla/Uroburos)—that re-emerged in July 2023 targeting Ukrainian defense organizations via a multi-stage Capibar loader to steal Signal messages, cloud and source-control credentials and other high-value data. This variant adds robust anti-analysis checks (Assembly.Location byte-array loader validation, faked 2008 compilation timestamps), extensive string encryption (multiple custom and ConfuserEx ciphers), hybrid AES payload encryption with RSA-encrypted IV/key plus HMAC-MD5 integrity, and obfuscation of IOCs. It supports 45 discrete commands for system profiling, credential theft and automated task workflows in a multithreaded solver component that writes AES- and RSA-protected result files. Kazuar also implements multiple injection modes (inject, browser- and svchost.exe-centric zombify, combined fallback, remote proxy, single and headless) and uses GUID-derived pseudorandom directories and mutexes to evade detection, while hard-coded agent and build identifiers enable variant tracking. Code overlap with Sunburst underscores its sophistication. Unit 42 has released detailed IOCs, artifacts and a GitHub appendix, and recommends Palo Alto Networks NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention, Cortex XDR, XSIAM, Advanced WildFire and Unit 42 incident response engagement to detect, hunt and mitigate this persistent threat.
hits.title: Over the Kazuar’s Nest: Cracking Down on a Freshly Hatched Backdoor Used by Pensive Ursa (Aka Turla)

canonical_entities: Palo Alto Networks NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention
hits.text: Since its debut in 2017 as an advanced .NET second-stage backdoor, Kazuar—attributed to Russian FSB–linked Pensive Ursa (Turla)—reemerged in July 2023 targeting Ukraine’s defense sector alongside a new Capibar first-stage loader, marking its first wild appearance since late 2020. This upgraded variant features extensive stealth and anti-analysis countermeasures—fake 2008 compilation timestamps, custom multi-layer string encryption, assembly-location checks and GUID-based pseudorandom directory and mutex generation—and boasts 45 C2-driven commands for comprehensive system profiling, data collection and credential theft from cloud platforms, source control and Signal. It supports six injection modes (inject, zombify, combined, remote, single and non-interactive), a multithreaded architecture for asynchronous task execution, and a hybrid AES–RSA encryption scheme for task/result files, complicating forensic recovery. Organizations can detect and block Kazuar with Palo Alto Networks NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention, Cortex XDR/XSIAM and WildFire, and engage Unit 42 Incident Response teams for targeted hunting and mitigation guidance.
hits.title: Over the Kazuar’s Nest: Cracking Down on a Freshly Hatched Backdoor Used by Pensive Ursa (Aka Turla)

canonical_entities: military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia
hits.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.
hits.title: Operation Lotus Blossom: A New Nation-State Cyberthreat?

hits.text: Scattered Spider, active since May 2022, has evolved from SIM-swapping and typosquatted credential harvesting to sophisticated social-engineering-driven cloud intrusions, most recently impersonating a CFO via public personal data to trick help-desk staff into resetting their Oracle Cloud device, then mapping Entra ID (Azure AD) privileges and SharePoint data, breaching Horizon VDI, VPN, and on-premise environments, reactivating a decommissioned VM, extracting NTDS.dit and over 1,400 secrets from CyberArk vaults using scripts and tools like ngrok, abusing AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, EC2 Serial Console, IAM role enumeration and Teleport for persistence, assigning Exchange Administrator roles to monitor senior employee inboxes, and deleting Azure Firewall policy rules in a tug-of-war over tenant control that required Microsoft intervention, inflicting millions in operational disruption (e.g., MGM Resorts, Marks & Spencer, Hawaiian Airlines) and exposing critical lapses in help-desk verification and privileged access management; organizations should deploy phishing-resistant MFA, enforce least-privilege and strict identity proofing for help-desks, monitor cloud and endpoint activity, and conduct regular social-engineering training to mitigate Scattered Spider’s fast, multi-vector ransomware preparation tactics.
hits.title: Anatomy of a Scattered Spider attack: A growing ransomware threat evolves

canonical_entities: exfiltrates browser history, autofill data and credit-card details
hits.text: Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 has identified a first-of-its-kind collaboration between North Korea’s state-sponsored Jumpy Pisces (linked to the Reconnaissance General Bureau) and the Play ransomware gang, revealing a blurring of nation-state and criminal operations: Jumpy Pisces gained initial access in May via a compromised user account, spent months conducting lateral movement and persistence using Sliver C2, custom DTrack info-stealer, a bespoke Mimikatz variant, RDP privileged-account creation tools and a trojanized binary that exfiltrates browser history, autofill data and credit-card details from Chrome, Edge and Brave, then in early September Play deployed its ransomware payload using the same account; Unit 42 attributed the joint operation with moderate confidence based on shared access credentials, continuous Sliver communications until deployment and Play’s known TTPs, though it remains unclear whether Jumpy Pisces acted as a Play affiliate or initial-access broker—this nexus not only underscores the need for defenders to monitor Sliver C2 indicators, credential-theft and RDP hardening but also signals a potential trend of North Korean actors increasingly leveraging underground ransomware networks to fund operations, raising the stakes for global cyber defenses.
hits.title: Play ransomware attack tied to North Korean nation-state actor | TechTarget

canonical_entities: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts: Logon Script (Windows)
hits.text: Blitz is a modular two-stage Windows malware discovered in 2024 and actively developed into early 2025 by a Russian-speaking actor using the moniker sw1zzx who distributed backdoored Standoff 2 game cheat packages (Nerest_CrackBy@sw1zzx_dev.zip and Elysium_CrackBy@sw1zzx_dev.zip) via a Telegram channel. The first stage is a stealthy downloader (ieapfltr.dll) retrieved through a PowerShell one-liner from pastebin/paste.rs URLs after passing anti-sandbox and VM detection checks (timing loops, floating-point instruction counters, processor count and screen resolution heuristics), which then establishes persistence via HKCU\Environment\UserInitMprLogonScript and HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run. Upon reboot, the downloader connects to a FastAPI-based C2 infrastructure hosted on a Hugging Face Space to fetch the second-stage Blitz bot that performs keylogging, screenshot capture, denial-of-service attacks on web servers and can deploy an XMRig Monero miner as follow-up. This campaign leverages Hugging Face Spaces for file hosting and C2 communications, and the malware developer promoted cheats on social media before announcing departure in May 2025; Hugging Face subsequently locked the account and blocked blob IDs. The impact includes credential theft, resource exploitation, unauthorized cryptocurrency mining and potential service disruption, and Palo Alto Networks’ Advanced WildFire, URL Filtering, DNS Security, Threat Prevention, Cortex XDR and XSIAM effectively detect and block Blitz activities, with Unit 42 standing by for incident response.
hits.title: Blitz Malware: A Tale of Game Cheats and Code Repositories

canonical_entities: creates a scheduled task for persistence
hits.text: On Aug. 17, 2023, the Zero Day Initiative publicly reported an RCE vulnerability in WinRAR (CVE-2023-40477) originally disclosed to the vendor on June 8; just four days later, an actor using the alias whalersplonk published a fake PoC on GitHub that repurposed a GeoServer CVE-2023-25157 exploit script to launch an infection chain rather than trigger the WinRAR flaw. Analysis of poc.py shows it writes a batch file to %TEMP%, executes an encoded PowerShell script that downloads c.ps1 and, subsequently, a VenomRAT v6.0.3 payload named Windows.Gaming.Preview.exe from checkblacklistwords[.]eu, installs it under %APPDATA%\Drivers, creates a scheduled task for persistence, enables keylogging to %APPDATA%\MyData\DataLogs_keylog_offline.txt, and contacts C2 at 94.156.253.109:4449. This RAT supports HVNC, stealer, grabber and commands such as plu_gin, HVNCStop, loadofflinelog, keylogsetting, filterinfo, and Po_ng. The malicious domain was registered at least 10 days before the CVE’s disclosure, indicating pre-positioned infrastructure aimed at opportunistically compromising researchers or other miscreants, not end users directly. Although the fake PoC repo was removed by the time of analysis, Palo Alto Networks WildFire and Advanced URL Filtering had already auto-categorized the domain as malicious and blocked the chain. Unit 42 researchers, alongside CTA partner Broadcom/Symantec, have published full IoCs and SHA lists on GitHub to support proactive defenses across WinRAR’s 500 million-strong user base.
hits.title: Fake CVE-2023-40477 Proof of Concept Leads to VenomRAT

hits.text: Unit 42 researchers identified a critical risk in Google Workspace’s domain-wide delegation feature whereby any Google Cloud Platform (GCP) identity with token-generation privileges can request access tokens for a delegated service account and thus impersonate Workspace users; in a typical attack, a malicious insider (for example, a developer with editor rights or an external attacker wielding a stolen Compute Engine default service account token) abuses domain-wide delegation scopes to access Gmail, Drive, Calendar and Docs data or perform actions on behalf of any user, enabling full domain compromise and lateral movement from GCP into Workspace. The vulnerability stems from a mismatch between GCP’s permission model and the high sensitivity of domain-wide delegation, and detection requires correlating GCP audit logs for service account key creation with Google Workspace authorization logs. Recommended mitigations include placing delegated service accounts at higher levels in the GCP resource hierarchy to restrict which identities can generate tokens, enforcing least-privilege roles and specific OAuth scopes, and leveraging Google’s Recommender API and audit-log monitoring; Palo Alto Networks customers are protected via Cortex XDR and Prisma Cloud.
hits.title: Exploring a Critical Risk in Google Workspace's Domain-Wide Delegation Feature

hits.text: Symantec has warned that extortion actors, notably the Clop ransomware operation (aka Snakefly/TA505/FIN11), have been exploiting a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability in the MOVEit Transfer web application (CVE-2023-34362) since May 27, 2023, enabling supply-chain attacks across multiple organizations; although first patched on May 31, additional vulnerabilities (CVEs pending) were disclosed on June 9. Attackers deploy a bespoke web shell, Lemurloot (detected as JS.Malscript!g1, Trojan.Gen.2, WS.Malware), to authenticate via hard-coded credentials, execute SQL statements to alter or delete database elements, exfiltrate records and Azure settings, and manipulate user accounts. With proof-of-concept code now public, secondary threat actors face elevated risk of exploitation and data theft. Clop has since threatened data leaks unless ransoms are paid, reflecting its shift from encryption to extortion. Symantec mitigations include file-based and ML detections, network-based attack signatures, and Data Center Security policy controls that harden MS SQL, IIS and sandbox environments to prevent web-shell deployment and unauthorized software execution.
hits.title: MOVEit Vulnerabilities: What You Need to Know | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Blitz is a modular two-stage Windows malware discovered in 2024 and actively developed into early 2025 by a Russian-speaking actor using the moniker sw1zzx who distributed backdoored Standoff 2 game cheat packages (Nerest_CrackBy@sw1zzx_dev.zip and Elysium_CrackBy@sw1zzx_dev.zip) via a Telegram channel.
