This campaign leverages Hugging Face Spaces for file hosting and C2 communications, and the malware developer promoted cheats on social media before announcing departure in May 2025; Hugging Face subsequently locked the account and blocked blob IDs. The impact includes credential theft, resource exploitation, unauthorized cryptocurrency mining and potential service disruption, and Palo Alto Networks’ Advanced WildFire, URL Filtering, DNS Security, Threat Prevention, Cortex XDR and XSIAM effectively detect and block Blitz activities, with Unit 42 standing by for incident response.

hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

retrieved_context.text: Symantec has warned that extortion actors, notably the Clop ransomware operation (aka Snakefly/TA505/FIN11), have been exploiting a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability in the MOVEit Transfer web application (CVE-2023-34362) since May 27, 2023, enabling supply-chain attacks across multiple organizations; although first patched on May 31, additional vulnerabilities (CVEs pending) were disclosed on June 9. Attackers deploy a bespoke web shell, Lemurloot (detected as JS.Malscript!g1, Trojan.Gen.2, WS.Malware), to authenticate via hard-coded credentials, execute SQL statements to alter or delete database elements, exfiltrate records and Azure settings, and manipulate user accounts. With proof-of-concept code now public, secondary threat actors face elevated risk of exploitation and data theft. Clop has since threatened data leaks unless ransoms are paid, reflecting its shift from encryption to extortion. Symantec mitigations include file-based and ML detections, network-based attack signatures, and Data Center Security policy controls that harden MS SQL, IIS and sandbox environments to prevent web-shell deployment and unauthorized software execution.
retrieved_context.title: MOVEit Vulnerabilities: What You Need to Know | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: Steal cloud account credentials (AWS IAM credentials exposed in public repositories)
harvested AWS IAM credentials exposed on public GitHub repositories
retrieved_context.text: Since at least December 2020, EleKtra-Leak—identified by Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 researchers William Gamazo and Nathaniel Quist—has programmatically harvested AWS IAM credentials exposed on public GitHub repositories within four minutes of exposure, exploiting blind spots in GitHub’s secret scanning and AWSCompromisedKeyQuarantine policy; the adversary conducts account reconnaissance, blocklists victim accounts to deter analysis, configures security groups, then launches behind-VPN c5a.24xlarge EC2 instances from private, non-Marketplace AMIs to mine Monero, operating as many as 474 unique instances between August 30 and October 6, 2023, and fetching bespoke mining software via Google Drive. Evidence suggests overlap with a January 2021 cryptojacking campaign targeting unsecured Docker services using the same custom miner. Despite AWS’s two-minute quarantine response, the campaign maintains continuous fluctuations in compromised accounts, underscoring its rapid, large-scale cryptojacking impact. To mitigate risk, organizations must immediately revoke exposed API keys, remove them from GitHub, and audit repository cloning events for suspicious activity.
retrieved_context.title: EleKtra-Leak Cryptojacking Attacks Exploit AWS IAM Credentials Exposed on GitHub

canonical_entities: Palo Alto Networks NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention
retrieved_context.text: Unit 42 researchers have uncovered a new, substantially upgraded variant of the Kazuar .NET backdoor—previously observed in 2017 as a second-stage payload by Russian Federal Security Service–linked Pensive Ursa (Turla/Uroburos)—that re-emerged in July 2023 targeting Ukrainian defense organizations via a multi-stage Capibar loader to steal Signal messages, cloud and source-control credentials and other high-value data. It supports 45 discrete commands for system profiling, credential theft and automated task workflows in a multithreaded solver component that writes AES- and RSA-protected result files. Kazuar also implements multiple injection modes (inject, browser- and svchost.exe-centric zombify, combined fallback, remote proxy, single and headless) and uses GUID-derived pseudorandom directories and mutexes to evade detection, while hard-coded agent and build identifiers enable variant tracking. Unit 42 has released detailed IOCs, artifacts and a GitHub appendix, and recommends Palo Alto Networks NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention, Cortex XDR, XSIAM, Advanced WildFire and Unit 42 incident response engagement to detect, hunt and mitigate this persistent threat.

hits.text: Since at least May 2023, BlackBerry researchers have identified a technically sophisticated Chinese-speaking threat actor—dubbed Silent Skimmer—that after over a year skimming card data from Asia/Pacific e-commerce and point-of-sale sites has expanded its campaign to North and Latin America, compromising organizations across multiple sectors by exploiting known web application vulnerabilities—most notably CVE-2019-18935 in Progress Software’s Telerik UI previously used by China’s Hafnium and Vietnam’s XE Group—on IIS servers to upload a malicious DLL and achieve remote code execution; using a multi-stage toolkit comprising privilege escalation exploits, a remote access tool, stagers/downloaders, and post-exploit utilities along with open-source binaries and scripts to inject card-skimming code into payment pages; and dynamically rotating short-lived, regionally co-located Microsoft Azure VPS-based C2 servers (each active less than a week) to blend exfiltration traffic with normal operations, mirroring Magecart tactics that have impacted hundreds of thousands of sites (e.g., British Airways, Ticketmaster, Newegg), and highlighting the imperative for prompt patching of third-party components, comprehensive web-app security audits, and vigilant monitoring of anomalous C2 infrastructure to thwart credential and payment data theft.
hits.title: Payment Card-Skimming Campaign Now Targeting Websites in North America

canonical_entities: online payment and PoS web applications
hits.text: BlackBerry’s Research and Intelligence Team has uncovered “Silent Skimmer,” a year-long, financially motivated campaign by a Chinese-fluent actor exploiting Internet Information Services (IIS) vulnerabilities to breach online payment and PoS web applications across Asia-Pacific, North America and Latin America, achieving initial foothold before leveraging open-source and living-off-the-land tools for privilege escalation and executing a PowerShell-based RAT (server.ps1); this malware connects to geolocated VPS C2 servers to download additional utilities, deploy web shells and inject scrapers into checkout pages, stealthily harvesting payment data via reverse proxies and Cobalt Strike beacons. In parallel, Sophos detailed a “pig butchering” crypto scam using dating-app social engineering and liquidity-mining lures—no malware required—to trick victims into connecting wallets to malicious Ethereum contracts, netting actors millions; these findings highlight the urgent need for patching IIS, monitoring PowerShell and Cobalt Strike activity, enforcing least-privilege controls, detecting web shells, and training users against DeFi phishing.
hits.title: Silent Skimmer: A Year-Long Web Skimming Campaign Targeting Online Payment Businesses

hits.text: The SnapMC group, newly identified by NCC Group, uses its mc.exe exfiltration tool to rapidly compromise unpatched VPNs and webserver apps—exploiting CVE-2019-18935 in Telerik UI for ASPX.NET and SQL injection flaws—to steal sensitive data and demand extortion within a 24-hour contact window and 72-hour negotiation deadline, often escalating pressure before expiration. Without deploying ransomware, SnapMC publishes a list of exfiltrated records and threatens breach disclosures to customers and media if victims fail to comply, exemplifying a streamlined “smash-and-grab” model that requires minimal technical effort. Observations of related exploits—such as CVE-2019-7418 against SonicWall and CVE-2021-1609 on Cisco VPN routers—underscore the critical need for timely patching, zero-trust network access (ZTNA) policies, cloud access security broker (CASB) controls, and a ready incident response plan to detect and mitigate these accelerated data-extortion attacks.
hits.title: 30 Mins or Less: Rapid Attacks Extort Orgs Without Ransomware

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since mid-2016, a cyber espionage operation dubbed Magic Hound, attributed to Iranian government–linked actors including COBALT GYPSY and showing overlaps with Rocket Kitten (Operation Saffron Rose/Ajax Security Team/Operation Woolen-Goldfish) and Newscasters (Charming Kitten/NewsBeef), has targeted energy, government and technology organizations in and tied to Saudi Arabia by distributing Word and Excel documents embedding malicious macros that launch PowerShell downloaders and droppers to deploy a custom toolkit—comprising executable and document loaders, IRC bots and the multi-platform Python-based PupyRAT—for full system access and data exfiltration; analysis by Palo Alto Networks and SecureWorks revealed domain and tool reuse with the Shamoon 2 wiper campaign, and bait lures mimicking holiday greetings, job offers and official Ministry of Health and Commerce communications, underscoring the need for enhanced macro-enablement policies, network segmentation and proactive IOC monitoring of associated domains and IRC traffic.
hits.title: Iranian hackers behind the Magic Hound campaign linked to Shamoon

hits.text: Between late 2022 and early 2023, the Chinese-affiliated APT15 (aka Flea/Nickel) executed a targeted espionage campaign against foreign ministries in the Americas—alongside a finance department, a regional products firm, and an outlier European victim—deploying a novel Backdoor.Graphican that abuses the Microsoft Graph API and OneDrive for dynamic C2, an evolution of its Ketrican/BS2005 malware. Graphican disables Internet Explorer 10’s first-run wizard, leverages a global IWebBrowser2 COM object to authenticate via Graph API, enumerates the “Person” OneDrive folder, decrypts its first subfolder name into the C2 address, generates a Bot ID from host attributes, registers with the server, and polls for commands to spawn shells, upload/download files, launch hidden processes, or run PowerShell with exfiltration. Concurrently, Flea rolled out updated and legacy Ketrican variants, living-off-the-land binaries, and open-source tools—EWSTEW for Exchange mail harvesting; Mimikatz, Pypykatz, Safetykatz; LaZagne; Quarks PwDump; SharpSecDump; K8Tools; EHole; and web shells such as AntSword, Behinder, China Chopper, Godzilla—while exploiting CVE-2020-1472 for privilege escalation. This persistent-access operation highlights Flea’s sustained evolution of custom tools for geopolitical intelligence gathering and introduces a C2 technique poised for adoption by other threat actors.
hits.title: Graphican: Flea Uses New Backdoor in Attacks Targeting Foreign Ministries | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

hits.text: Researchers at NCC Group have identified SnapMC as a new rapid-strike extortion group that eschews file encryption in favor of pure data theft, leveraging the Acunetix vulnerability scanner to pinpoint and exploit unpatched PrintNightmare LPE, Telerik UI for ASPX.NET RCE and SQL-injection flaws in VPN and web-server applications, then running SQL export scripts, compressing stolen CSVs with 7zip and exfiltrating them via the MinIO client—all within 30 minutes—before delivering standard extortion emails. By making data theft the primary leverage, SnapMC renders backup-based recovery moot and heightens the risk that victims who pay ransoms will face repeated extortion or public data sale, as seen with Sodinokibi, Netwalker, Mespinoza and Conti, and echoed by Coveware’s advice never to pay. Effective defenses include prompt patching of known CVEs, deploying well-configured web application firewalls around vulnerable services like Telerik and maintaining rigorous vulnerability management to thwart this growing threat.
hits.title: SnapMC hackers skip file encryption and just steal your files

canonical_entities: enforce persistence via a scheduled task
uploads victim public keys to a C2 server
hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence Center has attributed the emerging H0lyGh0st ransomware, active since June 2021 and tracked as DEV-0530, to financially motivated North Korean state-sponsored actors with ties to PLUTONIUM (DarkSeoul/Andariel), which has compromised small-to-mid-sized businesses—including manufacturers, banks, schools and event planners—across multiple countries since September 2021 by deploying custom SiennaPurple (C++ BTLC_C.exe) and SiennaBlue (Go-based HolyRS.exe, HolyLock.exe, BLTC.exe) families that encrypt Windows files with a .h0lyenc extension, use string obfuscation and public-key management, and enforce persistence via a scheduled task called “lockertask”; victims receive a ransom note delivered over a .onion portal demanding Bitcoin payment under double-extortion threats to publish stolen data if unpaid; between October 2021 and May 2022 MSTIC observed iterative Go-based SiennaBlue variants sharing core encryption and network/intranet connectivity functions, and in April 2022 the group rolled out its latest BTLC.exe, which hard-codes ServerBaseURL fallback credentials for network shares, uploads victim public keys to a C2 server, and encrypts all drive files—underscoring the need for defenders to monitor anomalous scheduled tasks, default-credential share connections, .onion traffic, and the appearance of .h0lyenc files to detect and disrupt this evolving threat.
hits.title: Emerging H0lyGh0st Ransomware Tied to North Korea | Threatpost

hits.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.

retrieved_context.text: Since mid-2016, a cyber espionage operation dubbed Magic Hound, attributed to Iranian government–linked actors including COBALT GYPSY and showing overlaps with Rocket Kitten (Operation Saffron Rose/Ajax Security Team/Operation Woolen-Goldfish) and Newscasters (Charming Kitten/NewsBeef), has targeted energy, government and technology organizations in and tied to Saudi Arabia by distributing Word and Excel documents embedding malicious macros that launch PowerShell downloaders and droppers to deploy a custom toolkit—comprising executable and document loaders, IRC bots and the multi-platform Python-based PupyRAT—for full system access and data exfiltration; analysis by Palo Alto Networks and SecureWorks revealed domain and tool reuse with the Shamoon 2 wiper campaign, and bait lures mimicking holiday greetings, job offers and official Ministry of Health and Commerce communications, underscoring the need for enhanced macro-enablement policies, network segmentation and proactive IOC monitoring of associated domains and IRC traffic.

retrieved_context.text: Between late 2022 and early 2023, the Chinese-affiliated APT15 (aka Flea/Nickel) executed a targeted espionage campaign against foreign ministries in the Americas—alongside a finance department, a regional products firm, and an outlier European victim—deploying a novel Backdoor.Graphican that abuses the Microsoft Graph API and OneDrive for dynamic C2, an evolution of its Ketrican/BS2005 malware. Graphican disables Internet Explorer 10’s first-run wizard, leverages a global IWebBrowser2 COM object to authenticate via Graph API, enumerates the “Person” OneDrive folder, decrypts its first subfolder name into the C2 address, generates a Bot ID from host attributes, registers with the server, and polls for commands to spawn shells, upload/download files, launch hidden processes, or run PowerShell with exfiltration. Concurrently, Flea rolled out updated and legacy Ketrican variants, living-off-the-land binaries, and open-source tools—EWSTEW for Exchange mail harvesting; Mimikatz, Pypykatz, Safetykatz; LaZagne; Quarks PwDump; SharpSecDump; K8Tools; EHole; and web shells such as AntSword, Behinder, China Chopper, Godzilla—while exploiting CVE-2020-1472 for privilege escalation. This persistent-access operation highlights Flea’s sustained evolution of custom tools for geopolitical intelligence gathering and introduces a C2 technique poised for adoption by other threat actors.
retrieved_context.title: Graphican: Flea Uses New Backdoor in Attacks Targeting Foreign Ministries | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
retrieved_context.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
retrieved_context.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

retrieved_context.text: Researchers at NCC Group have identified SnapMC as a new rapid-strike extortion group that eschews file encryption in favor of pure data theft, leveraging the Acunetix vulnerability scanner to pinpoint and exploit unpatched PrintNightmare LPE, Telerik UI for ASPX.NET RCE and SQL-injection flaws in VPN and web-server applications, then running SQL export scripts, compressing stolen CSVs with 7zip and exfiltrating them via the MinIO client—all within 30 minutes—before delivering standard extortion emails. By making data theft the primary leverage, SnapMC renders backup-based recovery moot and heightens the risk that victims who pay ransoms will face repeated extortion or public data sale, as seen with Sodinokibi, Netwalker, Mespinoza and Conti, and echoed by Coveware’s advice never to pay. Effective defenses include prompt patching of known CVEs, deploying well-configured web application firewalls around vulnerable services like Telerik and maintaining rigorous vulnerability management to thwart this growing threat.
retrieved_context.title: SnapMC hackers skip file encryption and just steal your files

hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: NCC Group’s RIFT team has tracked a previously unknown extortion actor, SnapMC, which conducts sub-30-minute data breach attacks—eschewing ransomware to steal and threaten to publicly leak data unless victims pay—by scanning for and exploiting public-facing vulnerabilities (notably CVE-2019-18935 in Telerik UI and SQL injection) to deploy a reverse shell, executing reconnaissance via PowerShell (whoami, wmic, net users), occasionally leveraging privilege-escalation scripts such as Invoke-Nightmare and JuicyPotato, then collecting data with 7zip and Invoke-SQLcmd before exfiltrating compressed CSVs to cloud storage via the MinIO client (mc.exe) configured through config.json in C:\Windows\Temp; extortion emails grant a 24-hour contact window and 72-hour negotiation period, with SnapMC raising pressure early and notifying customers and media upon non-response, illustrating a low-skill, high-impact modus operandi poised to grow as data-only extortion demands less time and expertise than ransomware—mitigations include prompt patching, rigorous vulnerability scanning (including third-party components), properly configured WAFs, and robust detection and incident response processes to counter T1190, T1560.001 and T1567.002 techniques.
hits.title: SnapMC skips ransomware, steals data | NCC Group

hits.text: Karakurt, active since June 2021 and also known as Karakurt Team/Lair, has extorted over 40 small and midsize companies in North America and Europe by skipping encryption to steal data via brokered or stolen VPN credentials (often from unpatched devices without MFA), establishing persistence through service creation, AnyDesk or Cobalt Strike C2 beacons, and harvesting credentials with Mimikatz and PowerShell dumps of ntds.dit. They compress data with WinZip/7zip and exfiltrate via Rclone or SFTP to Mega.io, then threaten public leaks—backed by 11.6 BTC moved into Conti wallets and shared file-tree.txt artifacts—highlighting ties to Conti’s rebranding post–May 19, 2022 “shutdown.” The group’s pure data-extortion model renders backups ineffective, demanding that defenders deploy intrusion prevention systems, enforce VPN MFA, continuously monitor for unauthorized remote-management tools, and strengthen credential hygiene to foil initial access, lateral movement, and exfiltration.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at the Data Extortion Group, Karakurt

hits.text: FARGO ransomware (aka Mallox/TargetCompany) is actively targeting unpatched Microsoft SQL servers, with threat actors evolving from deploying Cobalt Strike beacons in February 2022 to hijacking vulnerable instances for proxy bandwidth by July 2022 and now encrypting databases and extorting owners. The infection chain begins with cmd.exe and PowerShell scripts to download a malicious .NET loader, followed by retrieval of additional malware, execution of a batch script to terminate critical services, disable recovery features, and kill related processes before encrypting files with a “.Fargo3” extension and dropping a “RECOVERY FILES.txt” ransom note demanding Bitcoin payment. These attacks leverage brute‐force login attempts against weak credentials or exploit known SQL vulnerabilities, threatening non‐payers with public data exposure via Telegram. To mitigate this risk, organizations should enforce robust password policies, apply the latest SQL patches, monitor login anomalies, and deploy threat detection for IOCs such as specific MD5, SHA‐1, SHA‐256, vhash, and imphash signatures to prevent severe disruption to business‐critical services.
hits.title: Flash Notice: FARGO Ransomware Attacking Microsoft SQL Servers

canonical_entities: RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022
Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
hits.text: Trend Micro’s analysis of RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022 reveals a predominantly human-operated ransomware campaign that hit the manufacturing sector hardest (followed by education and banking) with the highest attack attempts observed in the U.S., France, and Brazil—driven in part by a high-profile 2021 breach of a Taiwanese hardware manufacturer. Initial access is achieved via malspam delivering multi-stage payloads that leverage IcedID and TrickBot for footholds, deploy Cobalt Strike beacons and PyXie RAT for code execution and data exfiltration, use SMB to propagate a VATET loader for lateral movement, and employ Mimikatz and LaZagne for credential harvesting. Upon execution, RansomEXX evades defense by disabling tools (T1562.001), skipping encryption of critical Windows paths, file names, and extensions, and terminating hundreds of business and security processes to maximize impact (T1486, T1490), then encrypts data and demands ransom. Recommended mitigations include strict audit and asset inventory, hardened configurations and least-privilege access, macro and email sandboxing to block malspam entry, regular patching and virtual patching, multifactor authentication, advanced behavior-based detection (e.g., Trend Micro Vision One™), and continuous employee training and red-team testing to disrupt the ransomware kill chain and protect against future RansomEXX intrusions.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: RansomEXX | Trend Micro (US)

They compress data with WinZip/7zip and exfiltrate via Rclone or SFTP to Mega.io, then threaten public leaks—backed by 11.6 BTC moved into Conti wallets and shared file-tree.txt artifacts—highlighting ties to Conti’s rebranding post–May 19, 2022 “shutdown.” The group’s pure data-extortion model renders backups ineffective, demanding that defenders deploy intrusion prevention systems, enforce VPN MFA, continuously monitor for unauthorized remote-management tools, and strengthen credential hygiene to foil initial access, lateral movement, and exfiltration.
retrieved_context.title: An In-Depth Look at the Data Extortion Group, Karakurt

retrieved_context.text: FARGO ransomware (aka Mallox/TargetCompany) is actively targeting unpatched Microsoft SQL servers, with threat actors evolving from deploying Cobalt Strike beacons in February 2022 to hijacking vulnerable instances for proxy bandwidth by July 2022 and now encrypting databases and extorting owners. The infection chain begins with cmd.exe and PowerShell scripts to download a malicious .NET loader, followed by retrieval of additional malware, execution of a batch script to terminate critical services, disable recovery features, and kill related processes before encrypting files with a “.Fargo3” extension and dropping a “RECOVERY FILES.txt” ransom note demanding Bitcoin payment. These attacks leverage brute‐force login attempts against weak credentials or exploit known SQL vulnerabilities, threatening non‐payers with public data exposure via Telegram. To mitigate this risk, organizations should enforce robust password policies, apply the latest SQL patches, monitor login anomalies, and deploy threat detection for IOCs such as specific MD5, SHA‐1, SHA‐256, vhash, and imphash signatures to prevent severe disruption to business‐critical services.
retrieved_context.title: Flash Notice: FARGO Ransomware Attacking Microsoft SQL Servers

canonical_entities: RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022
Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
retrieved_context.text: Trend Micro’s analysis of RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022 reveals a predominantly human-operated ransomware campaign that hit the manufacturing sector hardest (followed by education and banking) with the highest attack attempts observed in the U.S., France, and Brazil—driven in part by a high-profile 2021 breach of a Taiwanese hardware manufacturer. Initial access is achieved via malspam delivering multi-stage payloads that leverage IcedID and TrickBot for footholds, deploy Cobalt Strike beacons and PyXie RAT for code execution and data exfiltration, use SMB to propagate a VATET loader for lateral movement, and employ Mimikatz and LaZagne for credential harvesting. Upon execution, RansomEXX evades defense by disabling tools (T1562.001), skipping encryption of critical Windows paths, file names, and extensions, and terminating hundreds of business and security processes to maximize impact (T1486, T1490), then encrypts data and demands ransom. Recommended mitigations include strict audit and asset inventory, hardened configurations and least-privilege access, macro and email sandboxing to block malspam entry, regular patching and virtual patching, multifactor authentication, advanced behavior-based detection (e.g., Trend Micro Vision One™), and continuous employee training and red-team testing to disrupt the ransomware kill chain and protect against future RansomEXX intrusions.
retrieved_context.title: Ransomware Spotlight: RansomEXX | Trend Micro (US)

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since at least May 2023, BlackBerry researchers have identified a technically sophisticated Chinese-speaking threat actor—dubbed Silent Skimmer—that after over a year skimming card data from Asia/Pacific e-commerce and point-of-sale sites has expanded its campaign to North and Latin America, compromising organizations across multiple sectors by exploiting known web application vulnerabilities—most notably CVE-2019-18935 in Progress Software’s Telerik UI previously used by China’s Hafnium and Vietnam’s XE Group—on IIS servers to upload a malicious DLL and achieve remote code execution; using a multi-stage toolkit comprising privilege escalation exploits, a remote access tool, stagers/downloaders, and post-exploit utilities along with open-source binaries and scripts to inject card-skimming code into payment pages; and dynamically rotating short-lived, regionally co-located Microsoft Azure VPS-based C2 servers (each active less than a week) to blend exfiltration traffic with normal operations, mirroring Magecart tactics that have impacted hundreds of thousands of sites (e.g., British Airways, Ticketmaster, Newegg), and highlighting the imperative for prompt patching of third-party components, comprehensive web-app security audits, and vigilant monitoring of anomalous C2 infrastructure to thwart credential and payment data theft.
hits.title: Payment Card-Skimming Campaign Now Targeting Websites in North America

canonical_entities: online payment and PoS web applications
hits.text: BlackBerry’s Research and Intelligence Team has uncovered “Silent Skimmer,” a year-long, financially motivated campaign by a Chinese-fluent actor exploiting Internet Information Services (IIS) vulnerabilities to breach online payment and PoS web applications across Asia-Pacific, North America and Latin America, achieving initial foothold before leveraging open-source and living-off-the-land tools for privilege escalation and executing a PowerShell-based RAT (server.ps1); this malware connects to geolocated VPS C2 servers to download additional utilities, deploy web shells and inject scrapers into checkout pages, stealthily harvesting payment data via reverse proxies and Cobalt Strike beacons. In parallel, Sophos detailed a “pig butchering” crypto scam using dating-app social engineering and liquidity-mining lures—no malware required—to trick victims into connecting wallets to malicious Ethereum contracts, netting actors millions; these findings highlight the urgent need for patching IIS, monitoring PowerShell and Cobalt Strike activity, enforcing least-privilege controls, detecting web shells, and training users against DeFi phishing.
hits.title: Silent Skimmer: A Year-Long Web Skimming Campaign Targeting Online Payment Businesses

hits.text: The SnapMC group, newly identified by NCC Group, uses its mc.exe exfiltration tool to rapidly compromise unpatched VPNs and webserver apps—exploiting CVE-2019-18935 in Telerik UI for ASPX.NET and SQL injection flaws—to steal sensitive data and demand extortion within a 24-hour contact window and 72-hour negotiation deadline, often escalating pressure before expiration. Without deploying ransomware, SnapMC publishes a list of exfiltrated records and threatens breach disclosures to customers and media if victims fail to comply, exemplifying a streamlined “smash-and-grab” model that requires minimal technical effort. Observations of related exploits—such as CVE-2019-7418 against SonicWall and CVE-2021-1609 on Cisco VPN routers—underscore the critical need for timely patching, zero-trust network access (ZTNA) policies, cloud access security broker (CASB) controls, and a ready incident response plan to detect and mitigate these accelerated data-extortion attacks.
hits.title: 30 Mins or Less: Rapid Attacks Extort Orgs Without Ransomware

hits.text: Russia’s APT29 (aka Cozy Bear/Nobelium) has been exploiting a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in JetBrains TeamCity (CVE-2023-42793, CVSS 9.8) since September—shortly after JetBrains issued a patch and Rapid7 published a proof-of-concept—to gain initial access to SDLC management servers, escalate privileges, move laterally, deploy stealthy backdoors that persist through updates, and potentially manipulate build pipelines or insert malicious updates in SolarWinds-style supply-chain attacks; CISA, FBI, NSA and international partners warn that around 800 internet-exposed instances remain vulnerable (with uncounted internally reachable servers also at risk), and that North Korea’s Lazarus and Andariel groups have similarly weaponized the same flaw, prompting Fortinet to report multi-actor post-exploit techniques in live incidents; mitigation guidance urges immediate upgrading to TeamCity 2023.05.4, removal of public exposure, comprehensive IoC-based threat hunting across servers and build agents, and full compromise assessments to eradicate entrenched backdoors.
hits.title: Global TeamCity Exploitation Opens Door to SolarWinds-Style Nightmare

hits.text: Researchers at NCC Group have identified SnapMC as a new rapid-strike extortion group that eschews file encryption in favor of pure data theft, leveraging the Acunetix vulnerability scanner to pinpoint and exploit unpatched PrintNightmare LPE, Telerik UI for ASPX.NET RCE and SQL-injection flaws in VPN and web-server applications, then running SQL export scripts, compressing stolen CSVs with 7zip and exfiltrating them via the MinIO client—all within 30 minutes—before delivering standard extortion emails. By making data theft the primary leverage, SnapMC renders backup-based recovery moot and heightens the risk that victims who pay ransoms will face repeated extortion or public data sale, as seen with Sodinokibi, Netwalker, Mespinoza and Conti, and echoed by Coveware’s advice never to pay. Effective defenses include prompt patching of known CVEs, deploying well-configured web application firewalls around vulnerable services like Telerik and maintaining rigorous vulnerability management to thwart this growing threat.
hits.title: SnapMC hackers skip file encryption and just steal your files

hits.text: NCC Group’s RIFT team has tracked a previously unknown extortion actor, SnapMC, which conducts sub-30-minute data breach attacks—eschewing ransomware to steal and threaten to publicly leak data unless victims pay—by scanning for and exploiting public-facing vulnerabilities (notably CVE-2019-18935 in Telerik UI and SQL injection) to deploy a reverse shell, executing reconnaissance via PowerShell (whoami, wmic, net users), occasionally leveraging privilege-escalation scripts such as Invoke-Nightmare and JuicyPotato, then collecting data with 7zip and Invoke-SQLcmd before exfiltrating compressed CSVs to cloud storage via the MinIO client (mc.exe) configured through config.json in C:\Windows\Temp; extortion emails grant a 24-hour contact window and 72-hour negotiation period, with SnapMC raising pressure early and notifying customers and media upon non-response, illustrating a low-skill, high-impact modus operandi poised to grow as data-only extortion demands less time and expertise than ransomware—mitigations include prompt patching, rigorous vulnerability scanning (including third-party components), properly configured WAFs, and robust detection and incident response processes to counter T1190, T1560.001 and T1567.002 techniques.
hits.title: SnapMC skips ransomware, steals data | NCC Group

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
hits.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

canonical_entities: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
hits.text: In late 2023, researchers uncovered a sophisticated Taiwan-focused espionage operation in which a China-linked APT actor (likely APT27) hijacked an abandoned Sogou Zhuyin Windows update server—vacated when Sogou ceased Zhuyin support in mid-2022—and weaponized it to distribute a trojanized updater (SHA-256: 3f5c…) that deployed a custom backdoor and Cobalt Strike beacon via HTTP(S) (MITRE T1195.002, T1071.001). Initial access was achieved by swapping the legitimate SogouZhuyinUpdater.exe with the malicious variant, which installed a loader employing code-injection and obfuscation to evade AV detection; post-deployment techniques included Mimikatz for credential harvesting (T1003.001) and encrypted exfiltration of 2 GB of sensitive defense and policy documents from at least five Taiwanese government and research organizations (T1041). This incident underscores the risk of unmaintained update infrastructure in software supply-chain compromises and highlights the need for regular decommissioning audits, code signing validation, and network segmentation to mitigate such persistent threats.
hits.title: Abandoned Sogou Zhuyin Update Server Hijacked, Weaponized in Taiwan Espionage Campaign

hits.text: Cuba ransomware, first observed in late 2019 but only drawing widespread attention in November 2021 after infiltrating at least 49 organizations across government, healthcare, IT, manufacturing and finance, has since expanded its scope to compromise 101 victims globally (65 in the U.S., 36 abroad), demanded over $145 million in ransoms and collected more than $60 million. Operators gain initial access via Hancitor‐delivered loaders, phishing emails spoofing entities like Ukraine’s armed forces press service, unpatched Microsoft Exchange SSRF vulnerabilities (CVE-2022-41080/41040), compromised credentials and legitimate RDP, then deploy Cobalt Strike beacons via PowerShell and PsExec to execute memory‐injected payloads (“pones.exe,” “krots.exe”/KPOT), use Mimikatz for credential theft, and abuse Windows services to encrypt files with a “.cuba” extension. From 2022, affiliates such as “Tropical Scorpius” have employed the RomCom RAT (rmtpak.dll) for data exfiltration, industrial Spy ransomware tie-ins, and a kernel‐mode dropper (ApcHelper.sys, signed with a LAPSUS-stolen NVIDIA certificate) to terminate security tools, while adopting double-extortion by threatening public release of stolen data. High-impact incidents include attacks on Chilean government VMware and Microsoft ESXi servers, unpatched Microsoft Exchange environments, and The Philadelphia Inquirer in May 2023, which disrupted newspaper distribution and business operations. To counter this evolving threat, organizations should promptly apply Exchange and software patches, enforce multifactor authentication on RDP, restrict PowerShell/PsExec use, deploy EDR to detect Cobalt Strike and memory injection, monitor for malicious driver loads, and implement FBI/CISA mitigation guidelines.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at Cuba Ransomware

In parallel, Sophos detailed a “pig butchering” crypto scam using dating-app social engineering and liquidity-mining lures—no malware required—to trick victims into connecting wallets to malicious Ethereum contracts, netting actors millions; these findings highlight the urgent need for patching IIS, monitoring PowerShell and Cobalt Strike activity, enforcing least-privilege controls, detecting web shells, and training users against DeFi phishing.
hits.title: Silent Skimmer: A Year-Long Web Skimming Campaign Targeting Online Payment Businesses

hits.text: The SnapMC group, newly identified by NCC Group, uses its mc.exe exfiltration tool to rapidly compromise unpatched VPNs and webserver apps—exploiting CVE-2019-18935 in Telerik UI for ASPX.NET and SQL injection flaws—to steal sensitive data and demand extortion within a 24-hour contact window and 72-hour negotiation deadline, often escalating pressure before expiration. Without deploying ransomware, SnapMC publishes a list of exfiltrated records and threatens breach disclosures to customers and media if victims fail to comply, exemplifying a streamlined “smash-and-grab” model that requires minimal technical effort. Observations of related exploits—such as CVE-2019-7418 against SonicWall and CVE-2021-1609 on Cisco VPN routers—underscore the critical need for timely patching, zero-trust network access (ZTNA) policies, cloud access security broker (CASB) controls, and a ready incident response plan to detect and mitigate these accelerated data-extortion attacks.
hits.title: 30 Mins or Less: Rapid Attacks Extort Orgs Without Ransomware

hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
hits.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Microsoft has identified a China-based nation-state threat actor tracked as Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda) conducting espionage against dozens of Taiwanese organizations since mid-2021 by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java and SQL servers to deploy the China Chopper web shell, escalate privileges with Juicy Potato and BadPotato, and establish persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN bridge over HTTPS on port 443 for stealthy command-and-control. Once inside, the actor leverages WinRM and WMIC for lateral movement and deploys Mimikatz to dump LSASS and SAM for pass-the-hash attacks, yet conducts minimal post-persistence activity, suggesting long-term credential harvesting rather than immediate data exfiltration. To mitigate, organizations must enforce rigorous patch management, monitor registry changes and RDP configurations, deploy file integrity and behavioral monitoring on public-facing servers, isolate and forensically examine compromised systems, and rotate or disable exposed credentials.

hits.text: Researchers at NCC Group have identified SnapMC as a new rapid-strike extortion group that eschews file encryption in favor of pure data theft, leveraging the Acunetix vulnerability scanner to pinpoint and exploit unpatched PrintNightmare LPE, Telerik UI for ASPX.NET RCE and SQL-injection flaws in VPN and web-server applications, then running SQL export scripts, compressing stolen CSVs with 7zip and exfiltrating them via the MinIO client—all within 30 minutes—before delivering standard extortion emails. By making data theft the primary leverage, SnapMC renders backup-based recovery moot and heightens the risk that victims who pay ransoms will face repeated extortion or public data sale, as seen with Sodinokibi, Netwalker, Mespinoza and Conti, and echoed by Coveware’s advice never to pay. Effective defenses include prompt patching of known CVEs, deploying well-configured web application firewalls around vulnerable services like Telerik and maintaining rigorous vulnerability management to thwart this growing threat.
hits.title: SnapMC hackers skip file encryption and just steal your files

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
hits.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

canonical_entities: dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora
hits.text: Since at least September 2023, the China-aligned Evasive Panda APT (aka BRONZE HIGHLAND/Daggerfly) has conducted a dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora by compromising both the Kagyu International Monlam Trust’s website and the official Monlam translation-software supply chain—first implanting obfuscated JavaScript into jquery.js on the festival site that verifies victims’ first three IP octets via an MD5 hash salted with “1qaz0okm!@#,” serves a faux “Aw, Snap!” error page to users in India, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Australia and the U.S., and lures them to download a malicious “certificate.exe” or “.pkg” downloader; that loader side-loads memmgrset.dll (http_dy.dll) to fetch a JSON config from update.devicebug[.]com and ultimately deploys the undocumented Nightdoor backdoor alongside the group’s modular MgBot implant, while a trojanized Monlam software installer (Windows autorun.exe abusing MonlamUpdate.exe for DLL side-loading of RPHost.dll, and macOS Mach-O downloaders) has delivered further downloaders and payloads—retrieved from tibetpost[.]net and a direct IP—to %TEMP%\default_ico.exe for additional Nightdoor and MgBot installation.
hits.title: Evasive Panda leverages Monlam Festival to target Tibetans

hits.text: Cuba ransomware, first observed in late 2019 but only drawing widespread attention in November 2021 after infiltrating at least 49 organizations across government, healthcare, IT, manufacturing and finance, has since expanded its scope to compromise 101 victims globally (65 in the U.S., 36 abroad), demanded over $145 million in ransoms and collected more than $60 million. Operators gain initial access via Hancitor‐delivered loaders, phishing emails spoofing entities like Ukraine’s armed forces press service, unpatched Microsoft Exchange SSRF vulnerabilities (CVE-2022-41080/41040), compromised credentials and legitimate RDP, then deploy Cobalt Strike beacons via PowerShell and PsExec to execute memory‐injected payloads (“pones.exe,” “krots.exe”/KPOT), use Mimikatz for credential theft, and abuse Windows services to encrypt files with a “.cuba” extension. From 2022, affiliates such as “Tropical Scorpius” have employed the RomCom RAT (rmtpak.dll) for data exfiltration, industrial Spy ransomware tie-ins, and a kernel‐mode dropper (ApcHelper.sys, signed with a LAPSUS-stolen NVIDIA certificate) to terminate security tools, while adopting double-extortion by threatening public release of stolen data. High-impact incidents include attacks on Chilean government VMware and Microsoft ESXi servers, unpatched Microsoft Exchange environments, and The Philadelphia Inquirer in May 2023, which disrupted newspaper distribution and business operations. To counter this evolving threat, organizations should promptly apply Exchange and software patches, enforce multifactor authentication on RDP, restrict PowerShell/PsExec use, deploy EDR to detect Cobalt Strike and memory injection, monitor for malicious driver loads, and implement FBI/CISA mitigation guidelines.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at Cuba Ransomware

retrieved_context.text: Since at least May 2023, BlackBerry researchers have identified a technically sophisticated Chinese-speaking threat actor—dubbed Silent Skimmer—that after over a year skimming card data from Asia/Pacific e-commerce and point-of-sale sites has expanded its campaign to North and Latin America, compromising organizations across multiple sectors by exploiting known web application vulnerabilities—most notably CVE-2019-18935 in Progress Software’s Telerik UI previously used by China’s Hafnium and Vietnam’s XE Group—on IIS servers to upload a malicious DLL and achieve remote code execution; using a multi-stage toolkit comprising privilege escalation exploits, a remote access tool, stagers/downloaders, and post-exploit utilities along with open-source binaries and scripts to inject card-skimming code into payment pages; and dynamically rotating short-lived, regionally co-located Microsoft Azure VPS-based C2 servers (each active less than a week) to blend exfiltration traffic with normal operations, mirroring Magecart tactics that have impacted hundreds of thousands of sites (e.g., British Airways, Ticketmaster, Newegg), and highlighting the imperative for prompt patching of third-party components, comprehensive web-app security audits, and vigilant monitoring of anomalous C2 infrastructure to thwart credential and payment data theft.

hits.text: Since October 2024, the Chinese-speaking TAOTH operation has repurposed the abandoned “sogouzhuyin[.]com” update server for the discontinued Sogou Zhuyin IME—luring users, including high-value targets across Taiwan, Eastern Asia and the global Taiwanese diaspora, via modified Wikipedia links—to download a malicious “ZhuyinUp.exe” installer that, hours after deployment, delivers up to four malware families: TOSHIS, a stealthy loader/stager injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows binaries to fetch Cobalt Strike and Merlin backdoors on zh-TW/CN and ja-JP systems; DESFY, a file-enumeration spyware profiling victims and exfiltrating metadata; GTELAM, which AES-encrypts document filenames and uploads them to attacker-controlled Google Drive accounts; and C6DOOR, a Go-based backdoor exposing OS commands, screenshots, file transfers and network scans. In parallel, spear-phishing campaigns leveraged tainted decoys and OAuth-based credential-harvesting pages against journalists, dissidents, researchers and business leaders in China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Japan and South Korea. Post-infection telemetry shows extensive reconnaissance—system surveys, VS Code CLI tunneling and third-party cloud storage obfuscation—underscoring persistent tunnels. Overlapping infrastructure, shared C2 domains and consistent TTPs link TAOTH to prior Chinese supply-chain and email intrusion operations. Trend Micro and other vendors now detect these IOCs (e.g., SHA256 f8845b49…18fc for TOSHIS, 90a9be7c…1106 for DESFY), and organizations are advised to sunset unsupported software, enforce strict cloud-app permission monitoring, and scrutinize update-server domains to mitigate similar supply-chain compromises.
hits.title: Hackers Leverage Obsolete Software in Latest TAOTH Operation to Steal Data

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
hits.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

hits.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.

hits.text: North Korean state-sponsored APT Slow Pisces (aka Jade Sleet, TraderTraitor, PUKCHONG) is executing a sophisticated three-stage campaign against cryptocurrency developers by posing as recruiters on LinkedIn, distributing benign PDF job descriptions with embedded coding challenges, and redirecting targets to malicious GitHub repositories containing Python and JavaScript code laced with YAML deserialization and EJS escapeFunction backdoors; once activated under specific conditions, these backdoors deploy in-memory RN Loader and RN Stealer payloads to collect system information, establish C2 communications, and exfiltrate SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations with minimal forensic footprint—building on past successes that netted over $1 billion in 2023 and $1.5 billion in 2024—and highlighting the urgent need for enhanced vetting on professional platforms, proactive detection of unsafe deserialization and templating flaws, and memory-based threat monitoring to defend the cryptocurrency sector.
hits.title: Slow Pisces Group Targets Developers Using Coding Challenges Laced with Python Malware

hits.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
hits.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
hits.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

hits.text: In late August 2021, TAG uncovered a sophisticated, state-backed watering-hole campaign targeting Hong Kong media and pro-democracy sites that leveraged dual iframes to deliver encrypted iOS exploits (partial chain using CVE-2019-8506 in Safari) and a full macOS exploit chain against Catalina (10.15), combining an n-day WebKit RCE (CVE-2021-1789) with a 0-day XNU local privilege escalation (CVE-2021-30869) to load a patched, embedded Mach-O via Capstone.js, escape the Safari sandbox, elevate to root through a port-type confusion variant of CVE-2020-27932, and deploy a highly modular “MACMA” backdoor over DDS for fingerprinting, file transfer, keylogging, screen/audio capture and remote command execution; with rid counters in the 200s confirming scale, researchers disclosed IOCs (e.g. 103[.]255[.]44[.]56, appleid-server[.]com) to enable blocking and urged immediate application of Apple’s Jan 5 and Sept 23 patches.

retrieved_context.text: Since October 2024, the Chinese-speaking TAOTH operation has repurposed the abandoned “sogouzhuyin[.]com” update server for the discontinued Sogou Zhuyin IME—luring users, including high-value targets across Taiwan, Eastern Asia and the global Taiwanese diaspora, via modified Wikipedia links—to download a malicious “ZhuyinUp.exe” installer that, hours after deployment, delivers up to four malware families: TOSHIS, a stealthy loader/stager injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows binaries to fetch Cobalt Strike and Merlin backdoors on zh-TW/CN and ja-JP systems; DESFY, a file-enumeration spyware profiling victims and exfiltrating metadata; GTELAM, which AES-encrypts document filenames and uploads them to attacker-controlled Google Drive accounts; and C6DOOR, a Go-based backdoor exposing OS commands, screenshots, file transfers and network scans. In parallel, spear-phishing campaigns leveraged tainted decoys and OAuth-based credential-harvesting pages against journalists, dissidents, researchers and business leaders in China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Japan and South Korea. Post-infection telemetry shows extensive reconnaissance—system surveys, VS Code CLI tunneling and third-party cloud storage obfuscation—underscoring persistent tunnels. Overlapping infrastructure, shared C2 domains and consistent TTPs link TAOTH to prior Chinese supply-chain and email intrusion operations. Trend Micro and other vendors now detect these IOCs (e.g., SHA256 f8845b49…18fc for TOSHIS, 90a9be7c…1106 for DESFY), and organizations are advised to sunset unsupported software, enforce strict cloud-app permission monitoring, and scrutinize update-server domains to mitigate similar supply-chain compromises.
retrieved_context.title: Hackers Leverage Obsolete Software in Latest TAOTH Operation to Steal Data

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora
retrieved_context.text: Since at least September 2023, the China-aligned Evasive Panda APT (aka BRONZE HIGHLAND/Daggerfly) has conducted a dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora by compromising both the Kagyu International Monlam Trust’s website and the official Monlam translation-software supply chain—first implanting obfuscated JavaScript into jquery.js on the festival site that verifies victims’ first three IP octets via an MD5 hash salted with “1qaz0okm!@#,” serves a faux “Aw, Snap!” error page to users in India, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Australia and the U.S., and lures them to download a malicious “certificate.exe” or “.pkg” downloader; that loader side-loads memmgrset.dll (http_dy.dll) to fetch a JSON config from update.devicebug[.]com and ultimately deploys the undocumented Nightdoor backdoor alongside the group’s modular MgBot implant, while a trojanized Monlam software installer (Windows autorun.exe abusing MonlamUpdate.exe for DLL side-loading of RPHost.dll, and macOS Mach-O downloaders) has delivered further downloaders and payloads—retrieved from tibetpost[.]net and a direct IP—to %TEMP%\default_ico.exe for additional Nightdoor and MgBot installation.
retrieved_context.title: Evasive Panda leverages Monlam Festival to target Tibetans

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
retrieved_context.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
retrieved_context.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia
retrieved_context.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.
