canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022
Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
hits.text: Trend Micro’s analysis of RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022 reveals a predominantly human-operated ransomware campaign that hit the manufacturing sector hardest (followed by education and banking) with the highest attack attempts observed in the U.S., France, and Brazil—driven in part by a high-profile 2021 breach of a Taiwanese hardware manufacturer. Initial access is achieved via malspam delivering multi-stage payloads that leverage IcedID and TrickBot for footholds, deploy Cobalt Strike beacons and PyXie RAT for code execution and data exfiltration, use SMB to propagate a VATET loader for lateral movement, and employ Mimikatz and LaZagne for credential harvesting. Upon execution, RansomEXX evades defense by disabling tools (T1562.001), skipping encryption of critical Windows paths, file names, and extensions, and terminating hundreds of business and security processes to maximize impact (T1486, T1490), then encrypts data and demands ransom. Recommended mitigations include strict audit and asset inventory, hardened configurations and least-privilege access, macro and email sandboxing to block malspam entry, regular patching and virtual patching, multifactor authentication, advanced behavior-based detection (e.g., Trend Micro Vision One™), and continuous employee training and red-team testing to disrupt the ransomware kill chain and protect against future RansomEXX intrusions.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: RansomEXX | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: In May 2023, after U.S. authorities secured convictions against three high-level operators and declared the Russia-based cybercrime enterprise Fin7 “no more,” security experts began spotting first signs of its resurrection in April 2024 when Blackberry reported a typosquatting-based malware intrusion against a major automotive firm; since January 2024, Silent Push analyst Zach Edwards has mapped over 4,000 Fin7-linked hosts—rented largely on the pro-Russia Stark Industries Solutions platform—employing typosquatting, booby-trapped ads, malicious browser extensions and spear-phishing domains to mimic hundreds of brands from American Express and Microsoft 365 to CNN and Zoom, as well as popular free software tools such as 7-zip, PuTTY and Python, all “aged” on innocuous templates for six to nine months before weaponization; eSentire and Malwarebytes also observed sponsored Google ads pushing phony extensions in May and April 2024, and Fin7 has even deployed domains targeting Louvre and Olympic tourists, building on its 2013–present campaign that has extorted some $3 billion from victim organizations, underscoring the urgent need for renewed law enforcement focus and proactive domain-monitoring defenses.
hits.title: The Stark Truth Behind the Resurgence of Russia’s Fin7 – Krebs on Security

hits.text: Since mid-September, unknown cybercriminals have been conducting large-scale brute-force attacks against internet-exposed instances of Foundation Accounting Software—widely used by construction sub-industries such as plumbing, HVAC and concrete—by targeting the default “sa” administrator and a second high-privilege account within the MSSQL database accessible via TCP port 4243 (opened for Foundation’s mobile app). After an observed peak of roughly 35,000 rapid login attempts to obtain valid credentials, the attackers enable an extended stored procedure (e.g., xp_cmdshell) to execute OS-level commands and scripts, automating lateral movement and data theft across multiple unrelated victims. Huntress has identified just 33 hosts left with unchanged default passwords, alerted all impacted and at-risk customers, and urges organizations to rotate all Foundation credentials, remove direct internet exposure, and disable the exploited stored procedure to mitigate further compromise.
hits.title: Threat Actors Target Accounting Software Used by Construction Contractors - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Trend Micro first detected Trigona ransomware in July 2023—attacks peaked in August and ceased after its October leak-site shutdown—targeting Turkey (23.5%), the Philippines (19.6%), Brazil (13.7%), Germany and Thailand, with government entities accounting for 21.4% of SPN detections and technology, retail, FMCG and banking also hit; leak-site data revealed 33 victims (45.5% North America—50% US, 27.3% Europe—9.1% UK, 6.1% AU), over half SMBs and 18.2% finance firms. Operators exploited CVE-2021-40539 and brokered credentials for initial access, evaded defenses by dropping turnoff.bat and defoff.bat to kill AV, performed discovery with network/port scanners, harvested credentials via Mimikatz, moved laterally using Splashtop, LogMeIn, ScreenConnect, AnyDesk, TeamViewer and Cobalt Strike–dropped MHYPROTINST, and escalated privileges on MSSQL via CLR shell to deploy nt.exe. The payload encrypts files with AES and TDCP_rijndael—defaulting to the first 0x80000 bytes with ._locked appended unless /full is used—and supports numerous CLI flags (e.g., /r,/erase,/shdwn) on Windows and Linux. Effective defenses include vulnerability management, least-privilege administration, MFA, allowlisting, secure backups and AI-driven detection across email, endpoint, web and network using solutions like Trend Micro Vision One, Deep Discovery Email Inspector, Cloud One Workload Security and Apex One.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Trigona | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: CISA has added CVE-2022-22047—a high-severity (CVSS 7.8) elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Client Server Runtime Subsystem used since Windows 7 through Windows 11 and Server 2008–2022—to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and is urging federal agencies to install Microsoft’s July 5 Patch Tuesday update by August 2 after evidence emerged of in-the-wild exploitation; initially disclosed as a zero-day by Microsoft’s security team, the CSRSS bug enables adversaries who already hold local or physical access—or who gain remote code execution via malware or specially crafted Office/Adobe documents and macros—to escalate to SYSTEM privileges for lateral movement, although FortiGuard Labs rates the overall business threat as “medium” given the prerequisite foothold and available patch, while Trend Micro’s ZDI notes such elevation flaws are typically paired with a separate RCE vector and Microsoft has signaled future default blocking of VBA macros to mitigate this attack chain.
hits.title: CISA Urges Patch of Exploited Windows 11 Bug by Aug. 2 | Threatpost

canonical_entities: RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022
Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
retrieved_context.text: Trend Micro’s analysis of RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022 reveals a predominantly human-operated ransomware campaign that hit the manufacturing sector hardest (followed by education and banking) with the highest attack attempts observed in the U.S., France, and Brazil—driven in part by a high-profile 2021 breach of a Taiwanese hardware manufacturer. Initial access is achieved via malspam delivering multi-stage payloads that leverage IcedID and TrickBot for footholds, deploy Cobalt Strike beacons and PyXie RAT for code execution and data exfiltration, use SMB to propagate a VATET loader for lateral movement, and employ Mimikatz and LaZagne for credential harvesting. Upon execution, RansomEXX evades defense by disabling tools (T1562.001), skipping encryption of critical Windows paths, file names, and extensions, and terminating hundreds of business and security processes to maximize impact (T1486, T1490), then encrypts data and demands ransom. Recommended mitigations include strict audit and asset inventory, hardened configurations and least-privilege access, macro and email sandboxing to block malspam entry, regular patching and virtual patching, multifactor authentication, advanced behavior-based detection (e.g., Trend Micro Vision One™), and continuous employee training and red-team testing to disrupt the ransomware kill chain and protect against future RansomEXX intrusions.
retrieved_context.title: Ransomware Spotlight: RansomEXX | Trend Micro (US)

canonical_entities: dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora
retrieved_context.text: Since at least September 2023, the China-aligned Evasive Panda APT (aka BRONZE HIGHLAND/Daggerfly) has conducted a dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora by compromising both the Kagyu International Monlam Trust’s website and the official Monlam translation-software supply chain—first implanting obfuscated JavaScript into jquery.js on the festival site that verifies victims’ first three IP octets via an MD5 hash salted with “1qaz0okm!@#,” serves a faux “Aw, Snap!” error page to users in India, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Australia and the U.S., and lures them to download a malicious “certificate.exe” or “.pkg” downloader; that loader side-loads memmgrset.dll (http_dy.dll) to fetch a JSON config from update.devicebug[.]com and ultimately deploys the undocumented Nightdoor backdoor alongside the group’s modular MgBot implant, while a trojanized Monlam software installer (Windows autorun.exe abusing MonlamUpdate.exe for DLL side-loading of RPHost.dll, and macOS Mach-O downloaders) has delivered further downloaders and payloads—retrieved from tibetpost[.]net and a direct IP—to %TEMP%\default_ico.exe for additional Nightdoor and MgBot installation.
retrieved_context.title: Evasive Panda leverages Monlam Festival to target Tibetans

retrieved_context.text: In May 2023, after U.S. authorities secured convictions against three high-level operators and declared the Russia-based cybercrime enterprise Fin7 “no more,” security experts began spotting first signs of its resurrection in April 2024 when Blackberry reported a typosquatting-based malware intrusion against a major automotive firm; since January 2024, Silent Push analyst Zach Edwards has mapped over 4,000 Fin7-linked hosts—rented largely on the pro-Russia Stark Industries Solutions platform—employing typosquatting, booby-trapped ads, malicious browser extensions and spear-phishing domains to mimic hundreds of brands from American Express and Microsoft 365 to CNN and Zoom, as well as popular free software tools such as 7-zip, PuTTY and Python, all “aged” on innocuous templates for six to nine months before weaponization; eSentire and Malwarebytes also observed sponsored Google ads pushing phony extensions in May and April 2024, and Fin7 has even deployed domains targeting Louvre and Olympic tourists, building on its 2013–present campaign that has extorted some $3 billion from victim organizations, underscoring the urgent need for renewed law enforcement focus and proactive domain-monitoring defenses.
retrieved_context.title: The Stark Truth Behind the Resurgence of Russia’s Fin7 – Krebs on Security

retrieved_context.text: Since mid-September, unknown cybercriminals have been conducting large-scale brute-force attacks against internet-exposed instances of Foundation Accounting Software—widely used by construction sub-industries such as plumbing, HVAC and concrete—by targeting the default “sa” administrator and a second high-privilege account within the MSSQL database accessible via TCP port 4243 (opened for Foundation’s mobile app). After an observed peak of roughly 35,000 rapid login attempts to obtain valid credentials, the attackers enable an extended stored procedure (e.g., xp_cmdshell) to execute OS-level commands and scripts, automating lateral movement and data theft across multiple unrelated victims. Huntress has identified just 33 hosts left with unchanged default passwords, alerted all impacted and at-risk customers, and urges organizations to rotate all Foundation credentials, remove direct internet exposure, and disable the exploited stored procedure to mitigate further compromise.
retrieved_context.title: Threat Actors Target Accounting Software Used by Construction Contractors - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Trend Micro first detected Trigona ransomware in July 2023—attacks peaked in August and ceased after its October leak-site shutdown—targeting Turkey (23.5%), the Philippines (19.6%), Brazil (13.7%), Germany and Thailand, with government entities accounting for 21.4% of SPN detections and technology, retail, FMCG and banking also hit; leak-site data revealed 33 victims (45.5% North America—50% US, 27.3% Europe—9.1% UK, 6.1% AU), over half SMBs and 18.2% finance firms. Operators exploited CVE-2021-40539 and brokered credentials for initial access, evaded defenses by dropping turnoff.bat and defoff.bat to kill AV, performed discovery with network/port scanners, harvested credentials via Mimikatz, moved laterally using Splashtop, LogMeIn, ScreenConnect, AnyDesk, TeamViewer and Cobalt Strike–dropped MHYPROTINST, and escalated privileges on MSSQL via CLR shell to deploy nt.exe. The payload encrypts files with AES and TDCP_rijndael—defaulting to the first 0x80000 bytes with ._locked appended unless /full is used—and supports numerous CLI flags (e.g., /r,/erase,/shdwn) on Windows and Linux. Effective defenses include vulnerability management, least-privilege administration, MFA, allowlisting, secure backups and AI-driven detection across email, endpoint, web and network using solutions like Trend Micro Vision One, Deep Discovery Email Inspector, Cloud One Workload Security and Apex One.
retrieved_context.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Trigona | Trend Micro (US)

retrieved_context.text: CISA has added CVE-2022-22047—a high-severity (CVSS 7.8) elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Client Server Runtime Subsystem used since Windows 7 through Windows 11 and Server 2008–2022—to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and is urging federal agencies to install Microsoft’s July 5 Patch Tuesday update by August 2 after evidence emerged of in-the-wild exploitation; initially disclosed as a zero-day by Microsoft’s security team, the CSRSS bug enables adversaries who already hold local or physical access—or who gain remote code execution via malware or specially crafted Office/Adobe documents and macros—to escalate to SYSTEM privileges for lateral movement, although FortiGuard Labs rates the overall business threat as “medium” given the prerequisite foothold and available patch, while Trend Micro’s ZDI notes such elevation flaws are typically paired with a separate RCE vector and Microsoft has signaled future default blocking of VBA macros to mitigate this attack chain.
retrieved_context.title: CISA Urges Patch of Exploited Windows 11 Bug by Aug. 2 | Threatpost

retrieved_context.text: In late August 2021, TAG uncovered a sophisticated, state-backed watering-hole campaign targeting Hong Kong media and pro-democracy sites that leveraged dual iframes to deliver encrypted iOS exploits (partial chain using CVE-2019-8506 in Safari) and a full macOS exploit chain against Catalina (10.15), combining an n-day WebKit RCE (CVE-2021-1789) with a 0-day XNU local privilege escalation (CVE-2021-30869) to load a patched, embedded Mach-O via Capstone.js, escape the Safari sandbox, elevate to root through a port-type confusion variant of CVE-2020-27932, and deploy a highly modular “MACMA” backdoor over DDS for fingerprinting, file transfer, keylogging, screen/audio capture and remote command execution; with rid counters in the 200s confirming scale, researchers disclosed IOCs (e.g. 103[.]255[.]44[.]56, appleid-server[.]com) to enable blocking and urged immediate application of Apple’s Jan 5 and Sept 23 patches.
retrieved_context.title: Analyzing a watering hole campaign using macOS exploits

hits.text: Since October 2024, the Chinese-speaking TAOTH operation has repurposed the abandoned “sogouzhuyin[.]com” update server for the discontinued Sogou Zhuyin IME—luring users, including high-value targets across Taiwan, Eastern Asia and the global Taiwanese diaspora, via modified Wikipedia links—to download a malicious “ZhuyinUp.exe” installer that, hours after deployment, delivers up to four malware families: TOSHIS, a stealthy loader/stager injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows binaries to fetch Cobalt Strike and Merlin backdoors on zh-TW/CN and ja-JP systems; DESFY, a file-enumeration spyware profiling victims and exfiltrating metadata; GTELAM, which AES-encrypts document filenames and uploads them to attacker-controlled Google Drive accounts; and C6DOOR, a Go-based backdoor exposing OS commands, screenshots, file transfers and network scans. In parallel, spear-phishing campaigns leveraged tainted decoys and OAuth-based credential-harvesting pages against journalists, dissidents, researchers and business leaders in China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Japan and South Korea. Post-infection telemetry shows extensive reconnaissance—system surveys, VS Code CLI tunneling and third-party cloud storage obfuscation—underscoring persistent tunnels. Overlapping infrastructure, shared C2 domains and consistent TTPs link TAOTH to prior Chinese supply-chain and email intrusion operations. Trend Micro and other vendors now detect these IOCs (e.g., SHA256 f8845b49…18fc for TOSHIS, 90a9be7c…1106 for DESFY), and organizations are advised to sunset unsupported software, enforce strict cloud-app permission monitoring, and scrutinize update-server domains to mitigate similar supply-chain compromises.
hits.title: Hackers Leverage Obsolete Software in Latest TAOTH Operation to Steal Data

hits.text: HC3’s November 2022 alert warns of human-operated Lorenz ransomware, first observed in February 2021 and linked to earlier sZ40 and ThunderCrypt activity, which specifically targets large healthcare organizations by customizing its executable code and following a kill chain of initial access, extended reconnaissance, lateral movement to Windows domain controllers for administrator credential theft, then encryption and extortion. Operators demand $500,000–$700,000 and employ a non-typical leak site where stolen data is first offered for sale to other threat actors, then distributed in password-protected archives or, if sales fail, released publicly. With relatively limited public intelligence on Lorenz, HC3 emphasizes that victims should address common ransomware vectors—phishing, exploitation of known vulnerabilities, remote-access compromise and distributed attacks—by reinforcing patch management, intrusion detection, access controls and incident-response planning, especially in light of concurrent Hive ransomware warnings issued by HHS, FBI and CISA.
hits.title: Lorenz Ransomware Targets Large Healthcare Orgs, HC3 Warns | TechTarget

canonical_entities: harvest subscriber location, billing and communications metadata
hits.text: On Sept. 25, 2024, the Wall Street Journal disclosed that the Chinese state-sponsored APT Salt Typhoon has stealthily infiltrated multiple U.S. cable and broadband ISPs—likely via firmware and supply-chain compromises in core networking gear—to establish long-term persistence, harvest subscriber location, billing and communications metadata for espionage, and pre-position disruptive capabilities against federal, military and Fortune 100 users; this campaign, echoing Volt Typhoon’s telecom backdoors, Flax Typhoon’s 200,000-device IoT botnet, Brass Typhoon’s cross-domain implants and Mustang Panda’s telco intrusions, signals a shift from surveillance to offensive “blink-the-lights” or infrastructure-crippling attacks in a Taiwan contingency, driving urgent recommendations for carriers to enforce threat-intelligence sharing, secure firmware, tighten supply-chain controls and bolster routing security.
hits.title: China's 'Salt Typhoon' Cooks Up Cyberattacks on US ISPs

canonical_entities: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
hits.text: In late 2023, researchers uncovered a sophisticated Taiwan-focused espionage operation in which a China-linked APT actor (likely APT27) hijacked an abandoned Sogou Zhuyin Windows update server—vacated when Sogou ceased Zhuyin support in mid-2022—and weaponized it to distribute a trojanized updater (SHA-256: 3f5c…) that deployed a custom backdoor and Cobalt Strike beacon via HTTP(S) (MITRE T1195.002, T1071.001). Initial access was achieved by swapping the legitimate SogouZhuyinUpdater.exe with the malicious variant, which installed a loader employing code-injection and obfuscation to evade AV detection; post-deployment techniques included Mimikatz for credential harvesting (T1003.001) and encrypted exfiltration of 2 GB of sensitive defense and policy documents from at least five Taiwanese government and research organizations (T1041). This incident underscores the risk of unmaintained update infrastructure in software supply-chain compromises and highlights the need for regular decommissioning audits, code signing validation, and network segmentation to mitigate such persistent threats.
hits.title: Abandoned Sogou Zhuyin Update Server Hijacked, Weaponized in Taiwan Espionage Campaign

hits.text: On March 4 JetBrains released patches for two critical TeamCity authentication-bypass flaws (CVE-2024-27198 and CVE-2024-27199) that allow unauthenticated remote attackers to create admin accounts or tokens, but misaligned disclosure with Rapid7—whose researchers publicly detailed the bugs hours after the fixes—triggered mass exploitation: by March 6 LeakIX recorded rogue user creation on approximately 1,400 servers and GuidePoint Security linked the BianLian ransomware group to CVE-2024-27198–driven initial access. Despite JetBrains’ efforts to obfuscate patches and limit reverse engineering time, unpatched customers reported at least two file-encryption incidents and one DDoS-prep compromise. This chain of events underscores the necessity of coordinated vendor–researcher disclosure, accelerated patch deployment, and enhanced patch hardening to mitigate rapid exploit development and reduce organizational exposure.

canonical_entities: U.S. energy, oil and gas utilities
U.S. law firm Hunter Taubman Fischer & Li
Indicator Removal on Host: Clear Windows Event Logs
hits.text: Lynx ransomware, emerging in July 2024 as the INC ransomware successor under a Ransomware-as-a-Service model, employs a sophisticated double-extortion strategy—exfiltrating data prior to encryption and threatening publication on a leak site—and reuses significant INC source code. Between July and November 2024, it disrupted U.S. energy, oil and gas utilities, then in January–February 2025 breached Italy’s CONAD retail chain, U.S. law firm Hunter Taubman Fischer & Li, and Idaho retailer Zamzows, Inc., compromising internal documents and sensitive client and customer data. Initial access leverages phishing (T1566.001), drive-by compromises (T1195) and zero-day exploits; execution via user execution (T1204.002) and scripting interpreters (T1059.001); persistence through autostart mechanisms (T1070.001); exfiltration over C2 channels (T1041); and impact via file encryption (T1486) appending “.LYNX.” Operators use CLI flags (--file, --dir, --mode, --stop-processes, --encrypt-network, --hide-cmd, --no-print, --kill, --safe-mode) to granularly control encryption, terminate SQL, Veeam, Backup, Exchange, Java and Notepad processes/services, delete shadow copies, empty recycle bins, change wallpapers and print ransom notes directing victims to a Tor-based chat. Detection and prevention hinge on hardening email gateways, patching public-facing systems, monitoring anomalous process/service terminations, restricting unauthorized command-line encryption tools, and blocking known SHA256 hashes to disrupt this high-impact, automated RaaS operation.
hits.title: Lynx Ransomware: INC Ransomware Reincarnated - Threat Actors

hits.text: Kaspersky researchers have uncovered a new variant of the multi-stage Necro Trojan—first observed in 2019’s CamScanner compromise—that over recent weeks infected two Google Play apps (Wuta Camera, 10 M+ downloads; Max Browser, 1 M+ downloads) and unofficial mods for Spotify, WhatsApp and popular games by exploiting an untrusted advertising-integration SDK; in the Spotify mod the SDK exfiltrated device/app data to a known Necro C&C server and fetched a payload hidden in an image, while in the WhatsApp mod a loader abused Firebase Remote Config for C&C before deploying identical Necro payloads sharing code, structure and C&C infrastructure. Once installed, Necro’s latest variant downloads modules to display and click invisible ads, execute JavaScript in hidden WebViews, download executables and third-party apps, redirect traffic through compromised devices as proxies and subscribe victims to premium services. Between August 26 and September 15, tens of thousands of devices in Russia, Brazil, Vietnam, Ecuador and Mexico were targeted before Google removed the infected apps. Organizations should rigorously vet third-party SDKs, monitor remote-config channels and anomalous network traffic for image-based payload retrieval and invisible ad click-fraud behaviors to mitigate this evolving mobile threat.
hits.title: Necro Trojan Infects Google Play Apps With Millions of Downloads - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia
hits.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.
hits.title: Operation Lotus Blossom: A New Nation-State Cyberthreat?

canonical_entities: government bodies in Taiwan and Thailand
hits.text: On March 5, 2025, the US Department of Justice unsealed an indictment implicating Chinese contractor I-SOON’s FishMonger APT team in Operation FishMedley, a 2022 global espionage campaign that compromised seven high-value targets—government bodies in Taiwan and Thailand, a Hungarian Catholic organization, a Turkish entity, a US-based Catholic charity and NGO, and a French think tank—using privileged domain credentials to deploy implants such as the ScatterBee-packed ShadowPad backdoor (configured with campaign code 2203 and C2 at api.googleauthenticatoronline[.]com:443), the Spyder loader (delivered via malicious .doc, AES-CBC-decoded with hardcoded key F4E4C69EDEE09E820000000000000000, injected into task.exe with C2 at 61.238.103[.]165), and SodaMaster loaders side-loaded via legitimate DLLs decrypting payloads from debug.png or libvlc.dll, supported by Impacket-enabled lateral movement, LSASS and registry hive dumps via comsvcs.dll, and Cobalt Strike, SprySOCKS and BIOPASS RAT, underscoring the need for vigilant monitoring of living-off-the-land binaries, anomalous HTTP downloads, DLL side-loading and high-privilege account usage.
hits.title: Operation FishMedley targeting governments, NGOs, and think tanks

retrieved_context.text: Kaspersky researchers have uncovered a new variant of the multi-stage Necro Trojan—first observed in 2019’s CamScanner compromise—that over recent weeks infected two Google Play apps (Wuta Camera, 10 M+ downloads; Max Browser, 1 M+ downloads) and unofficial mods for Spotify, WhatsApp and popular games by exploiting an untrusted advertising-integration SDK; in the Spotify mod the SDK exfiltrated device/app data to a known Necro C&C server and fetched a payload hidden in an image, while in the WhatsApp mod a loader abused Firebase Remote Config for C&C before deploying identical Necro payloads sharing code, structure and C&C infrastructure. Once installed, Necro’s latest variant downloads modules to display and click invisible ads, execute JavaScript in hidden WebViews, download executables and third-party apps, redirect traffic through compromised devices as proxies and subscribe victims to premium services. Between August 26 and September 15, tens of thousands of devices in Russia, Brazil, Vietnam, Ecuador and Mexico were targeted before Google removed the infected apps. Organizations should rigorously vet third-party SDKs, monitor remote-config channels and anomalous network traffic for image-based payload retrieval and invisible ad click-fraud behaviors to mitigate this evolving mobile threat.
retrieved_context.title: Necro Trojan Infects Google Play Apps With Millions of Downloads - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia
retrieved_context.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.
retrieved_context.title: Operation Lotus Blossom: A New Nation-State Cyberthreat?

canonical_entities: government bodies in Taiwan and Thailand
retrieved_context.text: On March 5, 2025, the US Department of Justice unsealed an indictment implicating Chinese contractor I-SOON’s FishMonger APT team in Operation FishMedley, a 2022 global espionage campaign that compromised seven high-value targets—government bodies in Taiwan and Thailand, a Hungarian Catholic organization, a Turkish entity, a US-based Catholic charity and NGO, and a French think tank—using privileged domain credentials to deploy implants such as the ScatterBee-packed ShadowPad backdoor (configured with campaign code 2203 and C2 at api.googleauthenticatoronline[.]com:443), the Spyder loader (delivered via malicious .doc, AES-CBC-decoded with hardcoded key F4E4C69EDEE09E820000000000000000, injected into task.exe with C2 at 61.238.103[.]165), and SodaMaster loaders side-loaded via legitimate DLLs decrypting payloads from debug.png or libvlc.dll, supported by Impacket-enabled lateral movement, LSASS and registry hive dumps via comsvcs.dll, and Cobalt Strike, SprySOCKS and BIOPASS RAT, underscoring the need for vigilant monitoring of living-off-the-land binaries, anomalous HTTP downloads, DLL side-loading and high-privilege account usage.
retrieved_context.title: Operation FishMedley targeting governments, NGOs, and think tanks

hits.text: Since October 2024, the Chinese-speaking TAOTH operation has repurposed the abandoned “sogouzhuyin[.]com” update server for the discontinued Sogou Zhuyin IME—luring users, including high-value targets across Taiwan, Eastern Asia and the global Taiwanese diaspora, via modified Wikipedia links—to download a malicious “ZhuyinUp.exe” installer that, hours after deployment, delivers up to four malware families: TOSHIS, a stealthy loader/stager injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows binaries to fetch Cobalt Strike and Merlin backdoors on zh-TW/CN and ja-JP systems; DESFY, a file-enumeration spyware profiling victims and exfiltrating metadata; GTELAM, which AES-encrypts document filenames and uploads them to attacker-controlled Google Drive accounts; and C6DOOR, a Go-based backdoor exposing OS commands, screenshots, file transfers and network scans. In parallel, spear-phishing campaigns leveraged tainted decoys and OAuth-based credential-harvesting pages against journalists, dissidents, researchers and business leaders in China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Japan and South Korea. Post-infection telemetry shows extensive reconnaissance—system surveys, VS Code CLI tunneling and third-party cloud storage obfuscation—underscoring persistent tunnels. Overlapping infrastructure, shared C2 domains and consistent TTPs link TAOTH to prior Chinese supply-chain and email intrusion operations. Trend Micro and other vendors now detect these IOCs (e.g., SHA256 f8845b49…18fc for TOSHIS, 90a9be7c…1106 for DESFY), and organizations are advised to sunset unsupported software, enforce strict cloud-app permission monitoring, and scrutinize update-server domains to mitigate similar supply-chain compromises.
hits.title: Hackers Leverage Obsolete Software in Latest TAOTH Operation to Steal Data

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

hits.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
hits.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

hits.text: CISA has added CVE-2022-22047—a high-severity (CVSS 7.8) elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Client Server Runtime Subsystem used since Windows 7 through Windows 11 and Server 2008–2022—to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and is urging federal agencies to install Microsoft’s July 5 Patch Tuesday update by August 2 after evidence emerged of in-the-wild exploitation; initially disclosed as a zero-day by Microsoft’s security team, the CSRSS bug enables adversaries who already hold local or physical access—or who gain remote code execution via malware or specially crafted Office/Adobe documents and macros—to escalate to SYSTEM privileges for lateral movement, although FortiGuard Labs rates the overall business threat as “medium” given the prerequisite foothold and available patch, while Trend Micro’s ZDI notes such elevation flaws are typically paired with a separate RCE vector and Microsoft has signaled future default blocking of VBA macros to mitigate this attack chain.
hits.title: CISA Urges Patch of Exploited Windows 11 Bug by Aug. 2 | Threatpost

hits.text: CISA has added CVE-2024-7593, a critical (CVSS 9.8) authentication-bypass flaw in Ivanti Virtual Traffic Manager (vTM) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog amid evidence of active exploitation and a public proof-of-concept, enabling remote attackers to bypass the admin panel and create rogue administrative users; Ivanti released patches in August 2024 for vTM versions 22.2R1, 22.3R3, 22.5R2, 22.6R2 and 22.7R2, and Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies must remediate by October 15, 2024. This alert follows active exploitation of CVE-2024-8190 and CVE-2024-8963 against a limited number of customers, while Censys data reveals 2,017 exposed Ivanti Cloud Service Appliance instances (predominantly U.S.), underscoring the need for immediate patch deployment, asset inventory and monitoring for unauthorized admin activity to prevent network compromise.
hits.title: CISA Flags Critical Ivanti vTM Vulnerability Amid Active Exploitation Concerns

hits.text: CISA and the FBI have warned that since its discovery by Lacework Labs in 2022—when FortiGuard Labs observed it controlling over 40,000 devices—threat actors deploying the Python-scripted Androxgh0st malware have been building a botnet to steal AWS, Microsoft Office 365, SendGrid and Twilio credentials by scanning for RCE vulnerabilities CVE-2017-9841 (PHPUnit), CVE-2021-41773 (Apache HTTP Server) and CVE-2018-15133 (Laravel) and harvesting .env files; once inside, operators abuse SMTP, API and web shell functions to test email-sending limits for spam campaigns, create fake pages as backdoors, deploy further tools, and spin up new AWS instances and user policies to expand scans for vulnerable targets. FBI/CISA mitigation guidance urges patching all systems (notably Apache 2.4.49/2.4.50), denying unnecessary URI access, disabling Laravel debug mode, removing and revoking .env credentials, auditing for unauthorized access, scanning for unrecognized PHP (especially under /vendor/phpunit), monitoring outgoing cURL GETs to file hosts, and reporting sightings; CISA has added CVE-2018-15133 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog (joining the earlier additions of CVE-2021-41773 and CVE-2017-9841) and ordered federal agencies to harden systems by February 6.
hits.title: FBI: Androxgh0st malware botnet steals AWS, Microsoft credentials

hits.text: Operation RoundPress, attributed with medium confidence to Russian state-sponsored APT28 (Fancy Bear), has since 2023 exploited stored and reflected XSS flaws in widely used webmail platforms—initially leveraging Roundcube CVE-2020-35730 to inject malicious JavaScript into email bodies, then CVE-2023-43770 and additional n-day vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra in early 2024—to execute upon email open without clicks or redirects. Through spear-phishing emails crafted with timely political or news excerpts, the hidden script auto-fills victim credentials via invisible input fields, scrapes DOM content—including emails, contacts, webmail settings, login history, 2FA tokens and passwords—and exfiltrates data via HTTP POST to hardcoded C2 servers. Targets span high-value government entities in Greece, Ukraine, Serbia and Cameroon, military units in Ukraine and Ecuador, defense contractors in Ukraine, Bulgaria and Romania, and critical infrastructure in Ukraine and Bulgaria. The lack of persistence mechanisms confines execution to session scope but underscores the necessity for timely patching of XSS vulnerabilities, disabling HTML rendering in webmail clients, enforcing strict input sanitization and multifactor authentication, and monitoring anomalous outbound traffic to mitigate credential theft and data exfiltration.
hits.title: Government webmail hacked via XSS bugs in global spy campaign

hits.text: On Oct. 10, 2023, Citrix released patches for Netscaler ADC and Gateway to address Citrix Bleed (CVE-2023-4966, CVSS 9.4), a memory-leak vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to exfiltrate session tokens via crafted requests and hijack sessions; public proof-of-concept code from Assetnote and Python exploit scripts rapidly empowered ransomware affiliates and other threat actors to gain footholds, with Unit 42 Incident Response and Managed Threat Hunting teams observing exploitation-linked remote PowerShell sessions spawning cmd.exe, reconnaissance commands (whoami, WMIC, tasklist, net user), deployment of XScan (s.exe), Python HTTP servers, and mRemoteNG on VDI hosts—though no lateral movement beyond VDI was detected. Cortex Xpanse identified nearly 8,000 exposed Netscaler Gateway and 6,000 ADC IPs worldwide (3,100 US, 800 Germany, 450 China, 400 UK), prompting addition to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog. Palo Alto Networks advises immediate patching (including CVE-2023-4967), engagement of Unit 42 for incident response and continuous hunting, deployment of Next-Generation Firewalls with Advanced Threat Prevention signature 94483, updated Advanced WildFire ML models, Cortex Xpanse Threat Response Event, and Cortex XDR/XSIAM behavioral, anti-webshell, and credential-gathering protections to detect and block post-exploitation activity.
hits.title: Threat Brief: Citrix Bleed CVE-2023-4966

hits.text: McAfee Mobile Research Team uncovered Xamalicious, a new Android backdoor built with Xamarin that abuses accessibility permissions to harvest device metadata, query a C2 server for a second-stage payload, and dynamically inject an assembly DLL to perform unauthorized ad-clicking, app installs and other financially motivated actions; this threat has been embedded in 25 apps—ranging from horoscope and gaming to utility tools—on Google Play since mid-2020, amassing over 327,000 installations across Brazil, Argentina, the UK, Australia, the US, Mexico and Europe. To evade detection, Xamalicious encrypts all C2 traffic as JWE tokens (RSA-OAEP/128CBC-HS256), self-updates its APK to transform into spyware or a banking trojan, and links back to the Cash Magnet ad-fraud campaign; its use of non-Java frameworks like Xamarin underscores heightened obfuscation. Google Play Protect now blocks or auto-removes infected apps. Separately, a malicious WhatsApp-based phishing campaign in India distributes fake SBI APKs invoking SMS permissions to capture credentials, banking and identity data, then exfiltrates them for unauthorized transactions.
hits.title: New Sneaky Xamalicious Android Malware Hits Over 327,000 Devices

hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Between March and July 2025, DPRK-linked APT43 “Kimsuky” launched a multi-stage espionage operation against foreign embassies in South Korea by sending at least 19 spear-phishing emails impersonating diplomatic contacts with password-protected ZIPs (hosted on Dropbox and Daum) containing malicious Windows shortcuts disguised as PDFs; on execution, obfuscated PowerShell scripts downloaded base64-encoded XenoRAT payloads from private GitHub repositories (accounts “blairity” and “landjhon”) over HTTPS to evade detection, installed persistence via scheduled tasks, and conducted system reconnaissance (OS version, IP, running processes) before exfiltrating data via GitHub API uploads. The Confuser Core 1.6.0-obfuscated XenoRAT, reflectively loaded after GZIP header manipulation for diskless execution, granted full system control—keystroke logging, screenshots, file transfers—and leveraged GitHub as a C2 hub while using authoritative lures (EU meetings, U.S. Independence Day celebrations, military luncheons) timed to real diplomatic events. Infrastructure analysis linked C2 IPs (158.247.230.196; 141.164.40.239:443) and Monday-Friday operations in the +08:00 timezone—with pauses during Chinese holidays—suggesting China-based support for DPRK actors. The campaign maps to MITRE ATT&CK T1566.001, T1059.001, T1567.002, with Trellix detections for LNK/Downloader.ZRD and XenoRAT/Packed.A and IoCs such as SHA256 1e10203174fb1fcfb47bb00cac2fe6ffe660660839b7a2f53d8c0892845b0029 and cf2cba1859b2df4e927b8d52c630ce7ab6700babf9c7b4030f8243981b1a04fa. This active, state-sponsored threat underscores the urgent need for robust email filtering, continuous GitHub repository monitoring, and network anomaly detection within diplomatic environments.

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: ESET researchers disclosed MoustachedBouncer, a Belarus-aligned cyberespionage group active since at least 2014 targeting foreign embassies in Belarus, employing two parallel malware frameworks: the email-based NightClub (SMTP/IMAP C2) and its 2020-onward successor Disco (Go/.NET) delivered via adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) at ISP level—likely leveraging Belarus’s SORM lawful interception—to redirect Windows captive portal checks to a fake Windows Update page. This page loads jdrop.js to prompt a malicious installer, which schedules SMB-delivered OfficeBroker payloads from attacker-injected Google Cloud IPs. Both frameworks support plugins for screenshots, audio recording and file theft. ESET observed compromises of embassies from four continents and assesses medium confidence in state alignment and low confidence in cooperation with Winter Vivern. Recommendations include out-of-band encrypted VPNs to thwart ISP-level interception.
hits.title: MoustachedBouncer: Espionage against foreign diplomats in Belarus

hits.text: Microsoft’s latest joint report with Dutch intelligence exposes a year-long espionage campaign by the Russia-linked APT “Void Blizzard,” which has systematically purchased stolen credentials from infostealer markets to fuel password-spraying attacks against European and North American government and defense contractors—particularly NATO states and Ukraine—before pivoting in recent weeks to adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) spear-phishing via a typo-squatted Microsoft Entra login page and malicious QR code for a sham European defense summit. Leveraging the open-source Evilginx framework, the group captures usernames, passwords and session cookies, then abuses legitimate cloud APIs such as Exchange Online and Microsoft Graph to enumerate mailboxes (including shared folders), automate bulk exfiltration of emails, files and, in some cases, Microsoft Teams chats, and uses AzureHound to harvest Entra ID tenant configurations. Since mid-2024, Void Blizzard’s straightforward playbook—steal credentials, infiltrate Exchange or SharePoint Online, and automate data downloads—has compromised telcos, defense suppliers, digital services providers, healthcare and IT firms, posing an elevated risk of wartime intelligence siphoning for Kremlin military and diplomatic operations.
hits.title: Russian Government Hackers Caught Buying Passwords from Cybercriminals - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Since at least 2019, the North Korea–affiliated APT group Kimsuky has conducted spear-phishing campaigns using malicious lure documents to deploy a potent mix of backdoors and RATs—most notably the Windows/Android DLL AppleSeed (aka JamBog), its Golang-based AlphaSeed variant (leveraging the chromedp library for DevTools-driven C2), Meterpreter, TightVNC and TinyNuke (Nuclear Bot)—to establish C2 via HTTP, SMTP or headless‐Chrome, drop additional payloads and exfiltrate files, keystrokes and screenshots; evidence shows some intrusions since October 2022 delivered both AppleSeed and AlphaSeed via a JavaScript dropper. Active for over a decade—initially targeting South Korean entities before expanding globally in 2017—and recently sanctioned by the U.S. for intelligence gathering to further North Korea’s strategic objectives, Kimsuky has also created fraudulent LinkedIn and GitHub personas to secure remote tech contracts, generating revenue and facilitating multi-pronged blockchain and cryptocurrency theft to evade sanctions and support regime priorities.
hits.title: Kimsuky Hackers Deploying AppleSeed, Meterpreter, and TinyNuke in Latest Attacks

hits.text: On March 2, 2025, CyberMaterial’s report on Void Manticore (aka Storm-0842, linked to the cybercriminal Storm-1811 cluster) details a coordinated espionage campaign that began in late 2024 against aerospace, defense and government organizations in Europe and North America: operators initiated intrusions via spear-phishing emails embedding weaponized RTFs exploiting CVE-2024-4113 to drop a custom loader (“VoidLoader”), which in turn deployed the “ManticoreShell” backdoor; post-compromise activities included credential harvesting (Mimikatz), lateral movement via PSExec and WMI, privilege escalation through a signed kernel-mode driver exploit, and persistence using registry Run keys and scheduled tasks; C2 communications leveraged HTTPS with a domain generation algorithm (DGA) and fallback to TOR. Over a three-month window they compromised at least 15 organizations, exfiltrated more than 20 GB of intellectual property, and triggered system outages exceeding 48 hours in critical environments. Key mitigation measures include immediate patching of CVE-2024-4113, deployment of EDR solutions to detect anomalous IOCTL and PowerShell activity, network segmentation to contain lateral movement, strict monitoring of DGA-style DNS queries, and implementation of multi-factor authentication to thwart credential abuse.
hits.title: Void Manticore (Storm-0842) – Threat Actor - CyberMaterial

hits.text: Since mid-September, unknown cybercriminals have been conducting large-scale brute-force attacks against internet-exposed instances of Foundation Accounting Software—widely used by construction sub-industries such as plumbing, HVAC and concrete—by targeting the default “sa” administrator and a second high-privilege account within the MSSQL database accessible via TCP port 4243 (opened for Foundation’s mobile app). After an observed peak of roughly 35,000 rapid login attempts to obtain valid credentials, the attackers enable an extended stored procedure (e.g., xp_cmdshell) to execute OS-level commands and scripts, automating lateral movement and data theft across multiple unrelated victims. Huntress has identified just 33 hosts left with unchanged default passwords, alerted all impacted and at-risk customers, and urges organizations to rotate all Foundation credentials, remove direct internet exposure, and disable the exploited stored procedure to mitigate further compromise.
hits.title: Threat Actors Target Accounting Software Used by Construction Contractors - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Since at least April 2024 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a Russia-affiliated cyberespionage actor dubbed Void Blizzard (aka LAUNDRY BEAR) conducting high-volume, targeted operations against government, defense, transportation, media, NGO and healthcare organizations—particularly in NATO member states and Ukraine—by leveraging stolen credentials procured via commodity infostealer ecosystems for password spray attacks and Exchange/SharePoint Online access, then automating bulk email and file collection (and in some cases Teams messages) via cloud APIs and tools like AzureHound; in April 2025 the actor evolved to adversary-in-the-middle spear phishing using a typosquatted domain and the open-source Evilginx framework with a malicious QR-coded PDF to harvest Entra authentication data; this widespread success underscores that even unsophisticated TTPs pose major intelligence risks to critical sectors, so organizations should enforce sign-in risk policies and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO/passkeys), centralize identity management with Conditional Access, monitor risky sign-ins and mailbox auditing, apply least-privilege credential hygiene, and promptly rotate credentials after infostealer detections to disrupt Void Blizzard’s operations.
hits.title: New Russia-affiliated actor Void Blizzard targets critical sectors for espionage | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Between late 2022 and early 2023, the Chinese-affiliated APT15 (aka Flea/Nickel) executed a targeted espionage campaign against foreign ministries in the Americas—alongside a finance department, a regional products firm, and an outlier European victim—deploying a novel Backdoor.Graphican that abuses the Microsoft Graph API and OneDrive for dynamic C2, an evolution of its Ketrican/BS2005 malware. Graphican disables Internet Explorer 10’s first-run wizard, leverages a global IWebBrowser2 COM object to authenticate via Graph API, enumerates the “Person” OneDrive folder, decrypts its first subfolder name into the C2 address, generates a Bot ID from host attributes, registers with the server, and polls for commands to spawn shells, upload/download files, launch hidden processes, or run PowerShell with exfiltration. Concurrently, Flea rolled out updated and legacy Ketrican variants, living-off-the-land binaries, and open-source tools—EWSTEW for Exchange mail harvesting; Mimikatz, Pypykatz, Safetykatz; LaZagne; Quarks PwDump; SharpSecDump; K8Tools; EHole; and web shells such as AntSword, Behinder, China Chopper, Godzilla—while exploiting CVE-2020-1472 for privilege escalation. This persistent-access operation highlights Flea’s sustained evolution of custom tools for geopolitical intelligence gathering and introduces a C2 technique poised for adoption by other threat actors.
hits.title: Graphican: Flea Uses New Backdoor in Attacks Targeting Foreign Ministries | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.

hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Between late 2022 and early 2023, the Chinese-affiliated APT15 (aka Flea/Nickel) executed a targeted espionage campaign against foreign ministries in the Americas—alongside a finance department, a regional products firm, and an outlier European victim—deploying a novel Backdoor.Graphican that abuses the Microsoft Graph API and OneDrive for dynamic C2, an evolution of its Ketrican/BS2005 malware. Graphican disables Internet Explorer 10’s first-run wizard, leverages a global IWebBrowser2 COM object to authenticate via Graph API, enumerates the “Person” OneDrive folder, decrypts its first subfolder name into the C2 address, generates a Bot ID from host attributes, registers with the server, and polls for commands to spawn shells, upload/download files, launch hidden processes, or run PowerShell with exfiltration. Concurrently, Flea rolled out updated and legacy Ketrican variants, living-off-the-land binaries, and open-source tools—EWSTEW for Exchange mail harvesting; Mimikatz, Pypykatz, Safetykatz; LaZagne; Quarks PwDump; SharpSecDump; K8Tools; EHole; and web shells such as AntSword, Behinder, China Chopper, Godzilla—while exploiting CVE-2020-1472 for privilege escalation. This persistent-access operation highlights Flea’s sustained evolution of custom tools for geopolitical intelligence gathering and introduces a C2 technique poised for adoption by other threat actors.
hits.title: Graphican: Flea Uses New Backdoor in Attacks Targeting Foreign Ministries | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: registered variables in the Windows Registry
hits.text: In June 2024, HP’s Threat Research team led by Patrick Schlapfer intercepted a low-grade phishing campaign leveraging HTML smuggling via an AES-encrypted HTML attachment containing JavaScript-embedded decryption logic—a novel twist on typical encrypted archives—which, when decrypted, mimicked a legitimate website but dropped a fully commented, French-language VBScript that registered variables in the Windows Registry, staged a JavaScript payload as a scheduled task, and invoked a PowerShell script to deploy the freely available AsyncRAT infostealer. Schlapfer and co-lead Alex Holland’s analysis, including comparison with generative-AI–produced code, concluded the well-structured, human-readable script was likely authored by gen-AI by a low-skill newcomer benefitting from reduced entry barriers, with no obfuscation or complex infrastructure beyond a single C2 server. This first definitive proof of AI-generated malware in the wild underscores the need for defenders to adapt detection strategies to AI-crafted droppers, monitor anomalous AES-in-JavaScript decryption patterns, and anticipate more sophisticated AI-generated payloads poised to emerge within the next two years, thereby heightening the risk to network and endpoint security.
hits.title: AI-Generated Malware Found in the Wild - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Since at least April 2024 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a Russia-affiliated cyberespionage actor dubbed Void Blizzard (aka LAUNDRY BEAR) conducting high-volume, targeted operations against government, defense, transportation, media, NGO and healthcare organizations—particularly in NATO member states and Ukraine—by leveraging stolen credentials procured via commodity infostealer ecosystems for password spray attacks and Exchange/SharePoint Online access, then automating bulk email and file collection (and in some cases Teams messages) via cloud APIs and tools like AzureHound; in April 2025 the actor evolved to adversary-in-the-middle spear phishing using a typosquatted domain and the open-source Evilginx framework with a malicious QR-coded PDF to harvest Entra authentication data; this widespread success underscores that even unsophisticated TTPs pose major intelligence risks to critical sectors, so organizations should enforce sign-in risk policies and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO/passkeys), centralize identity management with Conditional Access, monitor risky sign-ins and mailbox auditing, apply least-privilege credential hygiene, and promptly rotate credentials after infostealer detections to disrupt Void Blizzard’s operations.
hits.title: New Russia-affiliated actor Void Blizzard targets critical sectors for espionage | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: Western nation’s military mission in Ukraine
hits.text: In February–March 2025, Russia-linked espionage group Shuckworm (aka Gamaredon/Armageddon) targeted a Western nation’s military mission in Ukraine using a multi-stage PowerShell-centric campaign initiated via an infected removable drive and malicious .lnk file. Obfuscated VBScript (~.drv) deployed through mshta.exe and wscript.exe created registry-named payloads: one performing WMI ping checks to mil.gov.ua before resolving dynamic C2 addresses via Teletype, Telegra.ph, t.me, check-host.net and Cloudflare tunnels (e.g., 107.189.19.218), and another altering Explorer registry keys to hide system files and propagate shortcuts across USB and network shares. The attackers then delivered an updated PowerShell infostealer (GammaSteel) alongside reconnaissance scripts that captured screenshots, systeminfo, process lists and host metadata, exfiltrating sensitive documents (*.docx, *.pptx, *.pdf) using PowerShell web requests with certutil-computed MD5 hashes and fallback cURL over Tor to mask origin. This campaign underscores Shuckworm’s shift from VBS to PowerShell, leveraging in-registry script storage and heavy obfuscation to evade detection, with indicators including anomalous UserAssist entries, unusual mshta/wscript invocations and atypical C2 resolution patterns.
hits.title: Shuckworm Targets Foreign Military Mission Based in Ukraine | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: From March to July 2025, North Korea’s state-sponsored Kimsuky group conducted at least 19 spear-phishing attacks against European embassy personnel in Seoul, using 54 multilingual PDF decoys—impersonating diplomatic correspondence and conference invitations—embedded in password-protected ZIPs containing LNK files disguised with double extensions that, when activated, executed obfuscated PowerShell to establish a foothold, overwrite GZIP headers (0x1F8B08) for payload decompression, and load a Confuser Core-obfuscated XenoRAT entirely in memory via .NET reflection. Trellix researchers mapped two GitHub accounts (“blairity” and “landjhon”) hosting private repositories (“europa,” “gulthe,” “themorning”) as covert C2 infrastructure for scripts, decoys, and exfiltration staging. XenoRAT achieved persistence through scheduled tasks, offered keystroke logging, screenshot capture, and remote shell, and exfiltrated base64-encoded intelligence using hardcoded GitHub API tokens—highlighting the urgent need to monitor repository activity, double-extension files, anomalous GZIP manipulations, and scheduled-task creation for early detection.
retrieved_context.title: North Korean Kimsuky Hackers Leveraged GitHub to Attack Foreign Embassies with XenoRAT Malware

canonical_entities: multi-stage espionage operation against foreign embassies in South Korea
retrieved_context.text: Between March and July 2025, DPRK-linked APT43 “Kimsuky” launched a multi-stage espionage operation against foreign embassies in South Korea by sending at least 19 spear-phishing emails impersonating diplomatic contacts with password-protected ZIPs (hosted on Dropbox and Daum) containing malicious Windows shortcuts disguised as PDFs; on execution, obfuscated PowerShell scripts downloaded base64-encoded XenoRAT payloads from private GitHub repositories (accounts “blairity” and “landjhon”) over HTTPS to evade detection, installed persistence via scheduled tasks, and conducted system reconnaissance (OS version, IP, running processes) before exfiltrating data via GitHub API uploads. The Confuser Core 1.6.0-obfuscated XenoRAT, reflectively loaded after GZIP header manipulation for diskless execution, granted full system control—keystroke logging, screenshots, file transfers—and leveraged GitHub as a C2 hub while using authoritative lures (EU meetings, U.S. Independence Day celebrations, military luncheons) timed to real diplomatic events. Infrastructure analysis linked C2 IPs (158.247.230.196; 141.164.40.239:443) and Monday-Friday operations in the +08:00 timezone—with pauses during Chinese holidays—suggesting China-based support for DPRK actors. The campaign maps to MITRE ATT&CK T1566.001, T1059.001, T1567.002, with Trellix detections for LNK/Downloader.ZRD and XenoRAT/Packed.A and IoCs such as SHA256 1e10203174fb1fcfb47bb00cac2fe6ffe660660839b7a2f53d8c0892845b0029 and cf2cba1859b2df4e927b8d52c630ce7ab6700babf9c7b4030f8243981b1a04fa. This active, state-sponsored threat underscores the urgent need for robust email filtering, continuous GitHub repository monitoring, and network anomaly detection within diplomatic environments.
retrieved_context.title: North Korean Kimsuky Hackers Use GitHub to Target Foreign Embassies with XenoRAT Malware

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s latest joint report with Dutch intelligence exposes a year-long espionage campaign by the Russia-linked APT “Void Blizzard,” which has systematically purchased stolen credentials from infostealer markets to fuel password-spraying attacks against European and North American government and defense contractors—particularly NATO states and Ukraine—before pivoting in recent weeks to adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) spear-phishing via a typo-squatted Microsoft Entra login page and malicious QR code for a sham European defense summit. Leveraging the open-source Evilginx framework, the group captures usernames, passwords and session cookies, then abuses legitimate cloud APIs such as Exchange Online and Microsoft Graph to enumerate mailboxes (including shared folders), automate bulk exfiltration of emails, files and, in some cases, Microsoft Teams chats, and uses AzureHound to harvest Entra ID tenant configurations. Since mid-2024, Void Blizzard’s straightforward playbook—steal credentials, infiltrate Exchange or SharePoint Online, and automate data downloads—has compromised telcos, defense suppliers, digital services providers, healthcare and IT firms, posing an elevated risk of wartime intelligence siphoning for Kremlin military and diplomatic operations.
retrieved_context.title: Russian Government Hackers Caught Buying Passwords from Cybercriminals - SecurityWeek

retrieved_context.text: ESET researchers disclosed MoustachedBouncer, a Belarus-aligned cyberespionage group active since at least 2014 targeting foreign embassies in Belarus, employing two parallel malware frameworks: the email-based NightClub (SMTP/IMAP C2) and its 2020-onward successor Disco (Go/.NET) delivered via adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) at ISP level—likely leveraging Belarus’s SORM lawful interception—to redirect Windows captive portal checks to a fake Windows Update page. This page loads jdrop.js to prompt a malicious installer, which schedules SMB-delivered OfficeBroker payloads from attacker-injected Google Cloud IPs. Both frameworks support plugins for screenshots, audio recording and file theft. ESET observed compromises of embassies from four continents and assesses medium confidence in state alignment and low confidence in cooperation with Winter Vivern. Recommendations include out-of-band encrypted VPNs to thwart ISP-level interception.
retrieved_context.title: MoustachedBouncer: Espionage against foreign diplomats in Belarus

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
hits.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

retrieved_context.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
