hits.text: Operation RoundPress, attributed with medium confidence to Russian state-sponsored APT28 (Fancy Bear), has since 2023 exploited stored and reflected XSS flaws in widely used webmail platforms—initially leveraging Roundcube CVE-2020-35730 to inject malicious JavaScript into email bodies, then CVE-2023-43770 and additional n-day vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra in early 2024—to execute upon email open without clicks or redirects. Through spear-phishing emails crafted with timely political or news excerpts, the hidden script auto-fills victim credentials via invisible input fields, scrapes DOM content—including emails, contacts, webmail settings, login history, 2FA tokens and passwords—and exfiltrates data via HTTP POST to hardcoded C2 servers. Targets span high-value government entities in Greece, Ukraine, Serbia and Cameroon, military units in Ukraine and Ecuador, defense contractors in Ukraine, Bulgaria and Romania, and critical infrastructure in Ukraine and Bulgaria. The lack of persistence mechanisms confines execution to session scope but underscores the necessity for timely patching of XSS vulnerabilities, disabling HTML rendering in webmail clients, enforcing strict input sanitization and multifactor authentication, and monitoring anomalous outbound traffic to mitigate credential theft and data exfiltration.

hits.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.

hits.text: In June 2024, HP’s Threat Research team led by Patrick Schlapfer intercepted a low-grade phishing campaign leveraging HTML smuggling via an AES-encrypted HTML attachment containing JavaScript-embedded decryption logic—a novel twist on typical encrypted archives—which, when decrypted, mimicked a legitimate website but dropped a fully commented, French-language VBScript that registered variables in the Windows Registry, staged a JavaScript payload as a scheduled task, and invoked a PowerShell script to deploy the freely available AsyncRAT infostealer. Schlapfer and co-lead Alex Holland’s analysis, including comparison with generative-AI–produced code, concluded the well-structured, human-readable script was likely authored by gen-AI by a low-skill newcomer benefitting from reduced entry barriers, with no obfuscation or complex infrastructure beyond a single C2 server. This first definitive proof of AI-generated malware in the wild underscores the need for defenders to adapt detection strategies to AI-crafted droppers, monitor anomalous AES-in-JavaScript decryption patterns, and anticipate more sophisticated AI-generated payloads poised to emerge within the next two years, thereby heightening the risk to network and endpoint security.
hits.title: AI-Generated Malware Found in the Wild - SecurityWeek

hits.text: CISA has added CVE-2024-7593, a critical (CVSS 9.8) authentication-bypass flaw in Ivanti Virtual Traffic Manager (vTM) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog amid evidence of active exploitation and a public proof-of-concept, enabling remote attackers to bypass the admin panel and create rogue administrative users; Ivanti released patches in August 2024 for vTM versions 22.2R1, 22.3R3, 22.5R2, 22.6R2 and 22.7R2, and Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies must remediate by October 15, 2024. This alert follows active exploitation of CVE-2024-8190 and CVE-2024-8963 against a limited number of customers, while Censys data reveals 2,017 exposed Ivanti Cloud Service Appliance instances (predominantly U.S.), underscoring the need for immediate patch deployment, asset inventory and monitoring for unauthorized admin activity to prevent network compromise.

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s latest joint report with Dutch intelligence exposes a year-long espionage campaign by the Russia-linked APT “Void Blizzard,” which has systematically purchased stolen credentials from infostealer markets to fuel password-spraying attacks against European and North American government and defense contractors—particularly NATO states and Ukraine—before pivoting in recent weeks to adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) spear-phishing via a typo-squatted Microsoft Entra login page and malicious QR code for a sham European defense summit. Leveraging the open-source Evilginx framework, the group captures usernames, passwords and session cookies, then abuses legitimate cloud APIs such as Exchange Online and Microsoft Graph to enumerate mailboxes (including shared folders), automate bulk exfiltration of emails, files and, in some cases, Microsoft Teams chats, and uses AzureHound to harvest Entra ID tenant configurations. Since mid-2024, Void Blizzard’s straightforward playbook—steal credentials, infiltrate Exchange or SharePoint Online, and automate data downloads—has compromised telcos, defense suppliers, digital services providers, healthcare and IT firms, posing an elevated risk of wartime intelligence siphoning for Kremlin military and diplomatic operations.
retrieved_context.title: Russian Government Hackers Caught Buying Passwords from Cybercriminals - SecurityWeek

retrieved_context.text: Operation RoundPress, attributed with medium confidence to Russian state-sponsored APT28 (Fancy Bear), has since 2023 exploited stored and reflected XSS flaws in widely used webmail platforms—initially leveraging Roundcube CVE-2020-35730 to inject malicious JavaScript into email bodies, then CVE-2023-43770 and additional n-day vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra in early 2024—to execute upon email open without clicks or redirects. Through spear-phishing emails crafted with timely political or news excerpts, the hidden script auto-fills victim credentials via invisible input fields, scrapes DOM content—including emails, contacts, webmail settings, login history, 2FA tokens and passwords—and exfiltrates data via HTTP POST to hardcoded C2 servers. Targets span high-value government entities in Greece, Ukraine, Serbia and Cameroon, military units in Ukraine and Ecuador, defense contractors in Ukraine, Bulgaria and Romania, and critical infrastructure in Ukraine and Bulgaria. The lack of persistence mechanisms confines execution to session scope but underscores the necessity for timely patching of XSS vulnerabilities, disabling HTML rendering in webmail clients, enforcing strict input sanitization and multifactor authentication, and monitoring anomalous outbound traffic to mitigate credential theft and data exfiltration.
retrieved_context.title: Government webmail hacked via XSS bugs in global spy campaign

retrieved_context.text: ESET researchers disclosed MoustachedBouncer, a Belarus-aligned cyberespionage group active since at least 2014 targeting foreign embassies in Belarus, employing two parallel malware frameworks: the email-based NightClub (SMTP/IMAP C2) and its 2020-onward successor Disco (Go/.NET) delivered via adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) at ISP level—likely leveraging Belarus’s SORM lawful interception—to redirect Windows captive portal checks to a fake Windows Update page. This page loads jdrop.js to prompt a malicious installer, which schedules SMB-delivered OfficeBroker payloads from attacker-injected Google Cloud IPs. Both frameworks support plugins for screenshots, audio recording and file theft. ESET observed compromises of embassies from four continents and assesses medium confidence in state alignment and low confidence in cooperation with Winter Vivern. Recommendations include out-of-band encrypted VPNs to thwart ISP-level interception.
retrieved_context.title: MoustachedBouncer: Espionage against foreign diplomats in Belarus

retrieved_context.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
retrieved_context.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

retrieved_context.text: Between late 2022 and early 2023, the Chinese-affiliated APT15 (aka Flea/Nickel) executed a targeted espionage campaign against foreign ministries in the Americas—alongside a finance department, a regional products firm, and an outlier European victim—deploying a novel Backdoor.Graphican that abuses the Microsoft Graph API and OneDrive for dynamic C2, an evolution of its Ketrican/BS2005 malware. Graphican disables Internet Explorer 10’s first-run wizard, leverages a global IWebBrowser2 COM object to authenticate via Graph API, enumerates the “Person” OneDrive folder, decrypts its first subfolder name into the C2 address, generates a Bot ID from host attributes, registers with the server, and polls for commands to spawn shells, upload/download files, launch hidden processes, or run PowerShell with exfiltration. Concurrently, Flea rolled out updated and legacy Ketrican variants, living-off-the-land binaries, and open-source tools—EWSTEW for Exchange mail harvesting; Mimikatz, Pypykatz, Safetykatz; LaZagne; Quarks PwDump; SharpSecDump; K8Tools; EHole; and web shells such as AntSword, Behinder, China Chopper, Godzilla—while exploiting CVE-2020-1472 for privilege escalation. This persistent-access operation highlights Flea’s sustained evolution of custom tools for geopolitical intelligence gathering and introduces a C2 technique poised for adoption by other threat actors.
retrieved_context.title: Graphican: Flea Uses New Backdoor in Attacks Targeting Foreign Ministries | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: registered variables in the Windows Registry
retrieved_context.text: In June 2024, HP’s Threat Research team led by Patrick Schlapfer intercepted a low-grade phishing campaign leveraging HTML smuggling via an AES-encrypted HTML attachment containing JavaScript-embedded decryption logic—a novel twist on typical encrypted archives—which, when decrypted, mimicked a legitimate website but dropped a fully commented, French-language VBScript that registered variables in the Windows Registry, staged a JavaScript payload as a scheduled task, and invoked a PowerShell script to deploy the freely available AsyncRAT infostealer. Schlapfer and co-lead Alex Holland’s analysis, including comparison with generative-AI–produced code, concluded the well-structured, human-readable script was likely authored by gen-AI by a low-skill newcomer benefitting from reduced entry barriers, with no obfuscation or complex infrastructure beyond a single C2 server. This first definitive proof of AI-generated malware in the wild underscores the need for defenders to adapt detection strategies to AI-crafted droppers, monitor anomalous AES-in-JavaScript decryption patterns, and anticipate more sophisticated AI-generated payloads poised to emerge within the next two years, thereby heightening the risk to network and endpoint security.
retrieved_context.title: AI-Generated Malware Found in the Wild - SecurityWeek

retrieved_context.text: CISA has added CVE-2024-7593, a critical (CVSS 9.8) authentication-bypass flaw in Ivanti Virtual Traffic Manager (vTM) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog amid evidence of active exploitation and a public proof-of-concept, enabling remote attackers to bypass the admin panel and create rogue administrative users; Ivanti released patches in August 2024 for vTM versions 22.2R1, 22.3R3, 22.5R2, 22.6R2 and 22.7R2, and Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies must remediate by October 15, 2024. This alert follows active exploitation of CVE-2024-8190 and CVE-2024-8963 against a limited number of customers, while Censys data reveals 2,017 exposed Ivanti Cloud Service Appliance instances (predominantly U.S.), underscoring the need for immediate patch deployment, asset inventory and monitoring for unauthorized admin activity to prevent network compromise.
retrieved_context.title: CISA Flags Critical Ivanti vTM Vulnerability Amid Active Exploitation Concerns

hits.text: In mid-March 2025, Kaspersky uncovered Operation ForumTroll, a state-sponsored APT espionage campaign targeting Russian media outlets, educational institutions and government organizations via personalized, short-lived phishing links opened in Google Chrome that automatically triggered a zero-day sandbox-escape exploit (CVE-2025-2783) exploiting a logical error at the Windows–Chrome boundary and chained to an unrecovered RCE payload to install sophisticated malware (Trojan.Win64.Agent, Trojan.Win64.Convagent.gen). Kaspersky’s exploit detection technologies rapidly identified and reverse-engineered the sandbox escape, enabling immediate reporting to Google and the release of Chrome 134.0.6998.177/.178 on March 25, 2025, effectively neutralizing the exploit. Key IoCs include primakovreadings[.]info and detections under Exploit.Win32.Generic, PDM:Exploit.Win32.Generic, PDM:Trojan.Win32.Generic and UDS:DangerousObject.Multi.Generic; defenders should apply the Chrome update, monitor for these indicators and maintain heightened vigilance against targeted phishing lures.
hits.title: Operation ForumTroll: APT attack with Google Chrome zero-day exploit chain

hits.text: In mid-March 2025, state-sponsored APT operators launched “Operation ForumTroll” against Russian media outlets and educational institutions by sending personalized phishing links to a spoofed “Primakov Readings” forum that silently deployed a two-stage malware chain exploiting a critical Chrome zero-day (CVE-2025-2783) logic flaw at the Chrome-Windows interface to bypass sandbox protections and achieve system-level remote code execution; once inside, the malware modifies registry keys and scheduled tasks for persistence, establishes encrypted custom-obfuscated C2 channels, and exfiltrates sensitive documents, browser credentials, and email correspondence, with security products flagging components as Exploit.Win32.Generic, Trojan.Win64.Agent, and Trojan.Win64.Convagent.gen—Google patched the vulnerability on March 25 in Chrome 134.0.6998.177/.178 after concurrent identification by K7 Security Labs and other researchers—organizations should immediately update Chrome, deploy advanced email-filtering solutions, and monitor network traffic for connections to suspicious domains (e.g., primakovreadings[.]info) to mitigate further espionage risks.
hits.title: Operation ForumTroll - APT Hackers Exploit Google Chrome Zero-Day To Bypass Sandbox Protections

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: In May 2023, after U.S. authorities secured convictions against three high-level operators and declared the Russia-based cybercrime enterprise Fin7 “no more,” security experts began spotting first signs of its resurrection in April 2024 when Blackberry reported a typosquatting-based malware intrusion against a major automotive firm; since January 2024, Silent Push analyst Zach Edwards has mapped over 4,000 Fin7-linked hosts—rented largely on the pro-Russia Stark Industries Solutions platform—employing typosquatting, booby-trapped ads, malicious browser extensions and spear-phishing domains to mimic hundreds of brands from American Express and Microsoft 365 to CNN and Zoom, as well as popular free software tools such as 7-zip, PuTTY and Python, all “aged” on innocuous templates for six to nine months before weaponization; eSentire and Malwarebytes also observed sponsored Google ads pushing phony extensions in May and April 2024, and Fin7 has even deployed domains targeting Louvre and Olympic tourists, building on its 2013–present campaign that has extorted some $3 billion from victim organizations, underscoring the urgent need for renewed law enforcement focus and proactive domain-monitoring defenses.
hits.title: The Stark Truth Behind the Resurgence of Russia’s Fin7 – Krebs on Security

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Since mid-September, unknown cybercriminals have been conducting large-scale brute-force attacks against internet-exposed instances of Foundation Accounting Software—widely used by construction sub-industries such as plumbing, HVAC and concrete—by targeting the default “sa” administrator and a second high-privilege account within the MSSQL database accessible via TCP port 4243 (opened for Foundation’s mobile app). After an observed peak of roughly 35,000 rapid login attempts to obtain valid credentials, the attackers enable an extended stored procedure (e.g., xp_cmdshell) to execute OS-level commands and scripts, automating lateral movement and data theft across multiple unrelated victims. Huntress has identified just 33 hosts left with unchanged default passwords, alerted all impacted and at-risk customers, and urges organizations to rotate all Foundation credentials, remove direct internet exposure, and disable the exploited stored procedure to mitigate further compromise.
hits.title: Threat Actors Target Accounting Software Used by Construction Contractors - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: Abuse of previously compromised corporate mailboxes
Phishing emails with ISO or 7z archives
hits.text: In the second half of 2023, ESET telemetry recorded a dramatic uptick in AceCryptor CaaS operations — detections tripled from ~13,000 to over 42,000 endpoints and unique AceCryptor-packed Rescoms RAT incidents soared from under 100 to more than 32,000 — marking Rescoms’ debut as a primary payload. Unlike H1’s focus on Peru, Mexico and Egypt, H2 campaigns heavily targeted European companies, with Poland alone accounting for 26K+ attacks, followed by Ukraine, Spain, Serbia, Bulgaria and Slovakia. Adversaries employed typosquatted domains and abused previously compromised corporate mailboxes to send multi-language, B2B-styled emails containing ISO or 7z archives named “offer/inquiry,” which unpacked AceCryptor to deploy Rescoms for browser and email credential harvesting. Repeated use of identical binaries reduced unique sample counts (23K→17K) despite higher encounter rates, and embedded Rescoms license IDs linked the waves to a single actor. While the overall use of Danabot and RedLine Stealer with AceCryptor decreased by over 60%, other families like SmokeLoader, STOP ransomware and Vidar remained active. The operations aimed at initial access for further ransomware or data exfiltration, underscoring the critical need for strict email hygiene and advanced endpoint security.
hits.title: Rescoms rides waves of AceCryptor spam

hits.text: In Q1 2023, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) found that over 60 percent of Russian state-backed phishing campaigns were aimed at Ukraine, led by FROZENBARENTS (aka Sandworm, GRU Unit 74455), which abused globally compromised EXIM mail servers, SMS-delivered phishing links and fake Windows update payloads deploying the Rhadamanthys stealer, then maintained persistence via webshells and Adminer to exfiltrate data to the CyberArmyofRussia_Reborn Telegram channel across government, defense, energy (notably the Caspian Pipeline Consortium), transport, education and humanitarian sectors while conducting information operations. Simultaneously, FROZENLAKE (APT28) leveraged reflected XSS on Ukrainian government sites to redirect users to phishing domains hosted on free services, with harvested credentials sent to compromised Ubiquiti devices; Belarusian PUSHCHA continued targeted low-volume campaigns against regional webmail providers; and IRA-linked actors deployed coordinated YouTube Shorts and Blogger posts to amplify pro-Wagner, anti-Ukrainian narratives. Financially motivated Cuba ransomware affiliates pivoted to intelligence collection using RomCom malware via ChatGPT/OpenAI-spoofed domains against conference attendees. TAG’s takedowns and Safe Browsing protections, coupled with targeted Gmail alerts, underscore the need for organizations to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, patch mail servers, monitor for unauthorized EXIM access, and guard against reflected XSS and SMS phishing.
hits.title: Ukraine remains Russia’s biggest cyber focus in 2023

canonical_entities: phishing emails with malicious attachments or links
hits.text: Ryuk, first observed in August 2018 and now responsible for one-third of ransomware attacks in 2020, leverages initial access via TrickBot or Emotet infections and, since early 2020, BazarLoader (aka BazarBackdoor) droppers delivered through phishing emails with malicious attachments or links to free file-hosting sites; once inside, attackers use C&C servers to deploy backdoors and exploit vulnerabilities such as EternalBlue and Zerologon to move laterally and encrypt entire domains within hours, demanding average ransoms of US$1.3 million in Q1 2020. After a lull from May to September, Ryuk resurfaced with notable incidents—February’s US government contractor breach and late October attacks on three New York hospitals—underscoring the need to patch domain controllers, disable or firewall administrative shares, restrict PowerShell, enforce 3-2-1 backups and least-privilege file permissions, and enable behavior-based ransomware protection and agent self-protection on security platforms.
hits.title: Ryuk 2020: Distributing Ransomware via TrickBot and BazarLoader | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: In mid-March 2025, state-sponsored APT operators launched “Operation ForumTroll” against Russian media outlets and educational institutions by sending personalized phishing links to a spoofed “Primakov Readings” forum that silently deployed a two-stage malware chain exploiting a critical Chrome zero-day (CVE-2025-2783) logic flaw at the Chrome-Windows interface to bypass sandbox protections and achieve system-level remote code execution; once inside, the malware modifies registry keys and scheduled tasks for persistence, establishes encrypted custom-obfuscated C2 channels, and exfiltrates sensitive documents, browser credentials, and email correspondence, with security products flagging components as Exploit.Win32.Generic, Trojan.Win64.Agent, and Trojan.Win64.Convagent.gen—Google patched the vulnerability on March 25 in Chrome 134.0.6998.177/.178 after concurrent identification by K7 Security Labs and other researchers—organizations should immediately update Chrome, deploy advanced email-filtering solutions, and monitor network traffic for connections to suspicious domains (e.g., primakovreadings[.]info) to mitigate further espionage risks.

hits.text: Symantec has warned that extortion actors, notably the Clop ransomware operation (aka Snakefly/TA505/FIN11), have been exploiting a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability in the MOVEit Transfer web application (CVE-2023-34362) since May 27, 2023, enabling supply-chain attacks across multiple organizations; although first patched on May 31, additional vulnerabilities (CVEs pending) were disclosed on June 9. Attackers deploy a bespoke web shell, Lemurloot (detected as JS.Malscript!g1, Trojan.Gen.2, WS.Malware), to authenticate via hard-coded credentials, execute SQL statements to alter or delete database elements, exfiltrate records and Azure settings, and manipulate user accounts. With proof-of-concept code now public, secondary threat actors face elevated risk of exploitation and data theft. Clop has since threatened data leaks unless ransoms are paid, reflecting its shift from encryption to extortion. Symantec mitigations include file-based and ML detections, network-based attack signatures, and Data Center Security policy controls that harden MS SQL, IIS and sandbox environments to prevent web-shell deployment and unauthorized software execution.

hits.text: Sea Turtle, also known as Cosmic Wolf, Marbled Dust, Teal Kurma and UNC1326, has been conducting a stealthy, Türkiye-linked cyber espionage campaign since at least January 2017, recently targeting Dutch ISPs, telecom, IT-service and media providers as well as Kurdish websites via supply-chain and island-hopping attacks to harvest politically sensitive personal data and potential dissident communications. First detailed by Cisco Talos in April 2019 for state-sponsored DNS hijacking to redirect legitimate domain queries to attacker-controlled servers, the group elevated its upstream foothold tactics in late 2021 by exploiting known telecom and IT vulnerabilities across Armenia, Cyprus, Greece, Iraq and Syria, per Microsoft. Between 2021 and 2023 PwC observed deployment of “SnappyTCP,” a simple Linux/Unix reverse-TCP web shell (with and without OpenSSL/TLS) for persistence and C2, and Hunt & Hackett’s 2023 incident revealed credential-theft via a compromised cPanel account used to deploy SnappyTCP, tar and expose email archives publicly for direct exfiltration. Organizations should enforce strong password policies, 2FA, login-rate limiting, SSH monitoring and timely patching to mitigate this ongoing espionage threat.

ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.

canonical_entities: month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment
hits.text: In November 2023, Russian state-sponsored group Nobelium (aka Midnight Blizzard/APT29) executed a month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment by conducting a password-spray brute-force attack against a legacy non-production test tenant lacking multi-factor authentication, enabling pivoting to a small subset of high-value accounts—including leadership, cybersecurity and legal team mailboxes—from which they exfiltrated emails and attachments; discovered on January 12, 2024, the campaign underscores the risk of poorly secured account configurations rather than software vulnerabilities, prompting Microsoft to notify impacted employees, reaffirm its MFA mandate, and reinforce zero-trust controls. This incident, following Nobelium’s SolarWinds and 2021 support-tool intrusions, highlights the necessity of enforcing MFA, minimizing default permissions, and hardening non-prod assets to mitigate advanced persistent threats.
hits.title: Russian hackers stole Microsoft corporate emails in month-long breach

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
hits.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

canonical_entities: Abuse of previously compromised corporate mailboxes
Phishing emails with ISO or 7z archives
hits.text: In the second half of 2023, ESET telemetry recorded a dramatic uptick in AceCryptor CaaS operations — detections tripled from ~13,000 to over 42,000 endpoints and unique AceCryptor-packed Rescoms RAT incidents soared from under 100 to more than 32,000 — marking Rescoms’ debut as a primary payload. Unlike H1’s focus on Peru, Mexico and Egypt, H2 campaigns heavily targeted European companies, with Poland alone accounting for 26K+ attacks, followed by Ukraine, Spain, Serbia, Bulgaria and Slovakia. Adversaries employed typosquatted domains and abused previously compromised corporate mailboxes to send multi-language, B2B-styled emails containing ISO or 7z archives named “offer/inquiry,” which unpacked AceCryptor to deploy Rescoms for browser and email credential harvesting. Repeated use of identical binaries reduced unique sample counts (23K→17K) despite higher encounter rates, and embedded Rescoms license IDs linked the waves to a single actor. While the overall use of Danabot and RedLine Stealer with AceCryptor decreased by over 60%, other families like SmokeLoader, STOP ransomware and Vidar remained active. The operations aimed at initial access for further ransomware or data exfiltration, underscoring the critical need for strict email hygiene and advanced endpoint security.
hits.title: Rescoms rides waves of AceCryptor spam

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
hits.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has documented how over 30 commercial spyware vendors are selling 0-day and n-day exploits to government-backed actors, enabling targeted campaigns against dissidents, journalists and human rights workers on Android, iOS and Samsung Internet Browser; in November 2022, TAG observed a smishing campaign using bit.ly links to deliver two parallel exploit chains—on iOS (CVE-2022-42856 WebKit RCE with a PAC bypass technique also seen in Cytrox’s Predator, and CVE-2021-30900 AGXAccelerator sandbox escape) that installed a GPS-pinging IPA stager, and on Android (CVE-2022-3723 Chrome type confusion, CVE-2022-4135 GPU sandbox bypass analyzed by Sergei Glazunov, and CVE-2022-38181 ARM privilege escalation) with Intent redirection to Chrome—both remaining effective until patched in Chrome 107/108 and Pixel January 2023 updates; in December 2022, TAG uncovered a one-time SMS link campaign targeting UAE users via a Heliconia-style landing page delivering a C++-based Android spyware suite after chaining four faults—CVE-2022-4262 Chrome type confusion, CVE-2022-3038 Chrome sandbox escape, CVE-2022-22706 Mali GPU kernel exploit and CVE-2023-0266 Linux kernel race (with auxiliary info-leak 0-days)—against unpatched Samsung Internet Browser (Chromium 102), underscoring that smaller surveillance vendors now stockpile and share advanced exploits historically limited to nation-state developers, highlighting the critical need for immediate patch deployment, comprehensive mitigations (PAC, V8 sandbox, MiraclePTR) and continuous IOC monitoring to disrupt these highly targeted intrusion operations.
hits.title: Spyware vendors use 0-days and n-days against popular platforms

canonical_entities: diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine
hits.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.
hits.title: Hackers with Russian Blizzard Steal Data from Rival Networks

hits.text: McAfee Mobile Research Team uncovered Xamalicious, a new Android backdoor built with Xamarin that abuses accessibility permissions to harvest device metadata, query a C2 server for a second-stage payload, and dynamically inject an assembly DLL to perform unauthorized ad-clicking, app installs and other financially motivated actions; this threat has been embedded in 25 apps—ranging from horoscope and gaming to utility tools—on Google Play since mid-2020, amassing over 327,000 installations across Brazil, Argentina, the UK, Australia, the US, Mexico and Europe. To evade detection, Xamalicious encrypts all C2 traffic as JWE tokens (RSA-OAEP/128CBC-HS256), self-updates its APK to transform into spyware or a banking trojan, and links back to the Cash Magnet ad-fraud campaign; its use of non-Java frameworks like Xamarin underscores heightened obfuscation. Google Play Protect now blocks or auto-removes infected apps. Separately, a malicious WhatsApp-based phishing campaign in India distributes fake SBI APKs invoking SMS permissions to capture credentials, banking and identity data, then exfiltrates them for unauthorized transactions.

retrieved_context.text: In mid-March 2025, Kaspersky uncovered Operation ForumTroll, a state-sponsored APT espionage campaign targeting Russian media outlets, educational institutions and government organizations via personalized, short-lived phishing links opened in Google Chrome that automatically triggered a zero-day sandbox-escape exploit (CVE-2025-2783) exploiting a logical error at the Windows–Chrome boundary and chained to an unrecovered RCE payload to install sophisticated malware (Trojan.Win64.Agent, Trojan.Win64.Convagent.gen). Kaspersky’s exploit detection technologies rapidly identified and reverse-engineered the sandbox escape, enabling immediate reporting to Google and the release of Chrome 134.0.6998.177/.178 on March 25, 2025, effectively neutralizing the exploit. Key IoCs include primakovreadings[.]info and detections under Exploit.Win32.Generic, PDM:Exploit.Win32.Generic, PDM:Trojan.Win32.Generic and UDS:DangerousObject.Multi.Generic; defenders should apply the Chrome update, monitor for these indicators and maintain heightened vigilance against targeted phishing lures.

retrieved_context.text: In mid-March 2025, state-sponsored APT operators launched “Operation ForumTroll” against Russian media outlets and educational institutions by sending personalized phishing links to a spoofed “Primakov Readings” forum that silently deployed a two-stage malware chain exploiting a critical Chrome zero-day (CVE-2025-2783) logic flaw at the Chrome-Windows interface to bypass sandbox protections and achieve system-level remote code execution; once inside, the malware modifies registry keys and scheduled tasks for persistence, establishes encrypted custom-obfuscated C2 channels, and exfiltrates sensitive documents, browser credentials, and email correspondence, with security products flagging components as Exploit.Win32.Generic, Trojan.Win64.Agent, and Trojan.Win64.Convagent.gen—Google patched the vulnerability on March 25 in Chrome 134.0.6998.177/.178 after concurrent identification by K7 Security Labs and other researchers—organizations should immediately update Chrome, deploy advanced email-filtering solutions, and monitor network traffic for connections to suspicious domains (e.g., primakovreadings[.]info) to mitigate further espionage risks.

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

retrieved_context.text: Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has documented how over 30 commercial spyware vendors are selling 0-day and n-day exploits to government-backed actors, enabling targeted campaigns against dissidents, journalists and human rights workers on Android, iOS and Samsung Internet Browser; in November 2022, TAG observed a smishing campaign using bit.ly links to deliver two parallel exploit chains—on iOS (CVE-2022-42856 WebKit RCE with a PAC bypass technique also seen in Cytrox’s Predator, and CVE-2021-30900 AGXAccelerator sandbox escape) that installed a GPS-pinging IPA stager, and on Android (CVE-2022-3723 Chrome type confusion, CVE-2022-4135 GPU sandbox bypass analyzed by Sergei Glazunov, and CVE-2022-38181 ARM privilege escalation) with Intent redirection to Chrome—both remaining effective until patched in Chrome 107/108 and Pixel January 2023 updates; in December 2022, TAG uncovered a one-time SMS link campaign targeting UAE users via a Heliconia-style landing page delivering a C++-based Android spyware suite after chaining four faults—CVE-2022-4262 Chrome type confusion, CVE-2022-3038 Chrome sandbox escape, CVE-2022-22706 Mali GPU kernel exploit and CVE-2023-0266 Linux kernel race (with auxiliary info-leak 0-days)—against unpatched Samsung Internet Browser (Chromium 102), underscoring that smaller surveillance vendors now stockpile and share advanced exploits historically limited to nation-state developers, highlighting the critical need for immediate patch deployment, comprehensive mitigations (PAC, V8 sandbox, MiraclePTR) and continuous IOC monitoring to disrupt these highly targeted intrusion operations.
retrieved_context.title: Spyware vendors use 0-days and n-days against popular platforms

retrieved_context.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.

retrieved_context.text: McAfee Mobile Research Team uncovered Xamalicious, a new Android backdoor built with Xamarin that abuses accessibility permissions to harvest device metadata, query a C2 server for a second-stage payload, and dynamically inject an assembly DLL to perform unauthorized ad-clicking, app installs and other financially motivated actions; this threat has been embedded in 25 apps—ranging from horoscope and gaming to utility tools—on Google Play since mid-2020, amassing over 327,000 installations across Brazil, Argentina, the UK, Australia, the US, Mexico and Europe. To evade detection, Xamalicious encrypts all C2 traffic as JWE tokens (RSA-OAEP/128CBC-HS256), self-updates its APK to transform into spyware or a banking trojan, and links back to the Cash Magnet ad-fraud campaign; its use of non-Java frameworks like Xamarin underscores heightened obfuscation. Google Play Protect now blocks or auto-removes infected apps. Separately, a malicious WhatsApp-based phishing campaign in India distributes fake SBI APKs invoking SMS permissions to capture credentials, banking and identity data, then exfiltrates them for unauthorized transactions.

hits.text: In May 2023, after U.S. authorities secured convictions against three high-level operators and declared the Russia-based cybercrime enterprise Fin7 “no more,” security experts began spotting first signs of its resurrection in April 2024 when Blackberry reported a typosquatting-based malware intrusion against a major automotive firm; since January 2024, Silent Push analyst Zach Edwards has mapped over 4,000 Fin7-linked hosts—rented largely on the pro-Russia Stark Industries Solutions platform—employing typosquatting, booby-trapped ads, malicious browser extensions and spear-phishing domains to mimic hundreds of brands from American Express and Microsoft 365 to CNN and Zoom, as well as popular free software tools such as 7-zip, PuTTY and Python, all “aged” on innocuous templates for six to nine months before weaponization; eSentire and Malwarebytes also observed sponsored Google ads pushing phony extensions in May and April 2024, and Fin7 has even deployed domains targeting Louvre and Olympic tourists, building on its 2013–present campaign that has extorted some $3 billion from victim organizations, underscoring the urgent need for renewed law enforcement focus and proactive domain-monitoring defenses.
hits.title: The Stark Truth Behind the Resurgence of Russia’s Fin7 – Krebs on Security

canonical_entities: phishing emails with malicious attachments or links
hits.text: Ryuk, first observed in August 2018 and now responsible for one-third of ransomware attacks in 2020, leverages initial access via TrickBot or Emotet infections and, since early 2020, BazarLoader (aka BazarBackdoor) droppers delivered through phishing emails with malicious attachments or links to free file-hosting sites; once inside, attackers use C&C servers to deploy backdoors and exploit vulnerabilities such as EternalBlue and Zerologon to move laterally and encrypt entire domains within hours, demanding average ransoms of US$1.3 million in Q1 2020. After a lull from May to September, Ryuk resurfaced with notable incidents—February’s US government contractor breach and late October attacks on three New York hospitals—underscoring the need to patch domain controllers, disable or firewall administrative shares, restrict PowerShell, enforce 3-2-1 backups and least-privilege file permissions, and enable behavior-based ransomware protection and agent self-protection on security platforms.
hits.title: Ryuk 2020: Distributing Ransomware via TrickBot and BazarLoader | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
hits.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Operation Triangulation, an advanced persistent threat zero-click iMessage campaign active since 2019 and targeting Russian diplomats, Kaspersky employees and other high-value assets, exploits a previously undocumented Apple SoC feature (ADJUST TrueType font instruction) and four zero-day flaws—CVE-2023-41990 (iMessage RCE), CVE-2023-32434 (XNU integer overflow), CVE-2023-38606 (hardware PPL bypass via MMIO registers) and CVE-2023-32435 (Safari shellcode)—in a multistage chain. Attackers initiate a malicious iMessage attachment to trigger RCE, then use return-oriented programming, NSExpression/NSPredicate payloads and an 11,000-line obfuscated JavaScriptCore exploit leveraging the $vm debugging feature to execute native APIs. Next, they map physical memory for read/write access, bypass hardware memory protections, launch the IMAgent process to clear traces, and spin up an invisible Safari instance for victim verification and shellcode delivery. A Mach-object kernel exploit reuses CVE-2023-32434 and CVE-2023-38606 for root privileges, culminating in deployment of the TriangleDB spyware implant. Kaspersky GReAT deems this the most sophisticated iOS attack chain observed, underscoring the difficulty of detecting hardware-level exploits on closed systems and recommending prompt iOS patching, disabling iMessage/FaceTime, EDR deployment, and network/forensic backup analysis.
hits.title: 'Operation Triangulation' Spyware Attackers Bypass iPhone Memory Protections

hits.text: In Q1 2023, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) found that over 60 percent of Russian state-backed phishing campaigns were aimed at Ukraine, led by FROZENBARENTS (aka Sandworm, GRU Unit 74455), which abused globally compromised EXIM mail servers, SMS-delivered phishing links and fake Windows update payloads deploying the Rhadamanthys stealer, then maintained persistence via webshells and Adminer to exfiltrate data to the CyberArmyofRussia_Reborn Telegram channel across government, defense, energy (notably the Caspian Pipeline Consortium), transport, education and humanitarian sectors while conducting information operations. Simultaneously, FROZENLAKE (APT28) leveraged reflected XSS on Ukrainian government sites to redirect users to phishing domains hosted on free services, with harvested credentials sent to compromised Ubiquiti devices; Belarusian PUSHCHA continued targeted low-volume campaigns against regional webmail providers; and IRA-linked actors deployed coordinated YouTube Shorts and Blogger posts to amplify pro-Wagner, anti-Ukrainian narratives. Financially motivated Cuba ransomware affiliates pivoted to intelligence collection using RomCom malware via ChatGPT/OpenAI-spoofed domains against conference attendees. TAG’s takedowns and Safe Browsing protections, coupled with targeted Gmail alerts, underscore the need for organizations to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, patch mail servers, monitor for unauthorized EXIM access, and guard against reflected XSS and SMS phishing.
hits.title: Ukraine remains Russia’s biggest cyber focus in 2023

retrieved_context.text: In mid-March 2025, state-sponsored APT operators launched “Operation ForumTroll” against Russian media outlets and educational institutions by sending personalized phishing links to a spoofed “Primakov Readings” forum that silently deployed a two-stage malware chain exploiting a critical Chrome zero-day (CVE-2025-2783) logic flaw at the Chrome-Windows interface to bypass sandbox protections and achieve system-level remote code execution; once inside, the malware modifies registry keys and scheduled tasks for persistence, establishes encrypted custom-obfuscated C2 channels, and exfiltrates sensitive documents, browser credentials, and email correspondence, with security products flagging components as Exploit.Win32.Generic, Trojan.Win64.Agent, and Trojan.Win64.Convagent.gen—Google patched the vulnerability on March 25 in Chrome 134.0.6998.177/.178 after concurrent identification by K7 Security Labs and other researchers—organizations should immediately update Chrome, deploy advanced email-filtering solutions, and monitor network traffic for connections to suspicious domains (e.g., primakovreadings[.]info) to mitigate further espionage risks.
retrieved_context.title: Operation ForumTroll - APT Hackers Exploit Google Chrome Zero-Day To Bypass Sandbox Protections

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.

retrieved_context.text: McAfee Mobile Research Team uncovered Xamalicious, a new Android backdoor built with Xamarin that abuses accessibility permissions to harvest device metadata, query a C2 server for a second-stage payload, and dynamically inject an assembly DLL to perform unauthorized ad-clicking, app installs and other financially motivated actions; this threat has been embedded in 25 apps—ranging from horoscope and gaming to utility tools—on Google Play since mid-2020, amassing over 327,000 installations across Brazil, Argentina, the UK, Australia, the US, Mexico and Europe. To evade detection, Xamalicious encrypts all C2 traffic as JWE tokens (RSA-OAEP/128CBC-HS256), self-updates its APK to transform into spyware or a banking trojan, and links back to the Cash Magnet ad-fraud campaign; its use of non-Java frameworks like Xamarin underscores heightened obfuscation. Google Play Protect now blocks or auto-removes infected apps. Separately, a malicious WhatsApp-based phishing campaign in India distributes fake SBI APKs invoking SMS permissions to capture credentials, banking and identity data, then exfiltrates them for unauthorized transactions.
retrieved_context.title: New Sneaky Xamalicious Android Malware Hits Over 327,000 Devices

retrieved_context.text: In May 2023, after U.S. authorities secured convictions against three high-level operators and declared the Russia-based cybercrime enterprise Fin7 “no more,” security experts began spotting first signs of its resurrection in April 2024 when Blackberry reported a typosquatting-based malware intrusion against a major automotive firm; since January 2024, Silent Push analyst Zach Edwards has mapped over 4,000 Fin7-linked hosts—rented largely on the pro-Russia Stark Industries Solutions platform—employing typosquatting, booby-trapped ads, malicious browser extensions and spear-phishing domains to mimic hundreds of brands from American Express and Microsoft 365 to CNN and Zoom, as well as popular free software tools such as 7-zip, PuTTY and Python, all “aged” on innocuous templates for six to nine months before weaponization; eSentire and Malwarebytes also observed sponsored Google ads pushing phony extensions in May and April 2024, and Fin7 has even deployed domains targeting Louvre and Olympic tourists, building on its 2013–present campaign that has extorted some $3 billion from victim organizations, underscoring the urgent need for renewed law enforcement focus and proactive domain-monitoring defenses.
retrieved_context.title: The Stark Truth Behind the Resurgence of Russia’s Fin7 – Krebs on Security

canonical_entities: phishing emails with malicious attachments or links
retrieved_context.text: Ryuk, first observed in August 2018 and now responsible for one-third of ransomware attacks in 2020, leverages initial access via TrickBot or Emotet infections and, since early 2020, BazarLoader (aka BazarBackdoor) droppers delivered through phishing emails with malicious attachments or links to free file-hosting sites; once inside, attackers use C&C servers to deploy backdoors and exploit vulnerabilities such as EternalBlue and Zerologon to move laterally and encrypt entire domains within hours, demanding average ransoms of US$1.3 million in Q1 2020. After a lull from May to September, Ryuk resurfaced with notable incidents—February’s US government contractor breach and late October attacks on three New York hospitals—underscoring the need to patch domain controllers, disable or firewall administrative shares, restrict PowerShell, enforce 3-2-1 backups and least-privilege file permissions, and enable behavior-based ransomware protection and agent self-protection on security platforms.
retrieved_context.title: Ryuk 2020: Distributing Ransomware via TrickBot and BazarLoader | Trend Micro (US)

retrieved_context.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
retrieved_context.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Operation Triangulation, an advanced persistent threat zero-click iMessage campaign active since 2019 and targeting Russian diplomats, Kaspersky employees and other high-value assets, exploits a previously undocumented Apple SoC feature (ADJUST TrueType font instruction) and four zero-day flaws—CVE-2023-41990 (iMessage RCE), CVE-2023-32434 (XNU integer overflow), CVE-2023-38606 (hardware PPL bypass via MMIO registers) and CVE-2023-32435 (Safari shellcode)—in a multistage chain. Attackers initiate a malicious iMessage attachment to trigger RCE, then use return-oriented programming, NSExpression/NSPredicate payloads and an 11,000-line obfuscated JavaScriptCore exploit leveraging the $vm debugging feature to execute native APIs. Next, they map physical memory for read/write access, bypass hardware memory protections, launch the IMAgent process to clear traces, and spin up an invisible Safari instance for victim verification and shellcode delivery. A Mach-object kernel exploit reuses CVE-2023-32434 and CVE-2023-38606 for root privileges, culminating in deployment of the TriangleDB spyware implant. Kaspersky GReAT deems this the most sophisticated iOS attack chain observed, underscoring the difficulty of detecting hardware-level exploits on closed systems and recommending prompt iOS patching, disabling iMessage/FaceTime, EDR deployment, and network/forensic backup analysis.
retrieved_context.title: 'Operation Triangulation' Spyware Attackers Bypass iPhone Memory Protections

retrieved_context.text: In Q1 2023, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) found that over 60 percent of Russian state-backed phishing campaigns were aimed at Ukraine, led by FROZENBARENTS (aka Sandworm, GRU Unit 74455), which abused globally compromised EXIM mail servers, SMS-delivered phishing links and fake Windows update payloads deploying the Rhadamanthys stealer, then maintained persistence via webshells and Adminer to exfiltrate data to the CyberArmyofRussia_Reborn Telegram channel across government, defense, energy (notably the Caspian Pipeline Consortium), transport, education and humanitarian sectors while conducting information operations. Simultaneously, FROZENLAKE (APT28) leveraged reflected XSS on Ukrainian government sites to redirect users to phishing domains hosted on free services, with harvested credentials sent to compromised Ubiquiti devices; Belarusian PUSHCHA continued targeted low-volume campaigns against regional webmail providers; and IRA-linked actors deployed coordinated YouTube Shorts and Blogger posts to amplify pro-Wagner, anti-Ukrainian narratives. Financially motivated Cuba ransomware affiliates pivoted to intelligence collection using RomCom malware via ChatGPT/OpenAI-spoofed domains against conference attendees. TAG’s takedowns and Safe Browsing protections, coupled with targeted Gmail alerts, underscore the need for organizations to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, patch mail servers, monitor for unauthorized EXIM access, and guard against reflected XSS and SMS phishing.
retrieved_context.title: Ukraine remains Russia’s biggest cyber focus in 2023

hits.text: ESET Research uncovered Operation AkaiRyū, a spearphishing-driven cyberespionage campaign conducted by the China-aligned MirrorFace APT (now assessed as a subgroup under the APT10 umbrella) against a Central European diplomatic institute between June and September 2024, using Expo 2025-themed lures referencing prior NGO communications to deliver password-protected Word documents and malicious links; this marks MirrorFace’s first known European targeting. Analysis revealed a significant TTP refresh: the revival of the ANEL (UPPERCUT) backdoor—previously exclusive to APT10—for file manipulation, payload execution and screenshots; a heavily customized AsyncRAT variant stealthily run inside Windows Sandbox via a complex execution chain; continued deployment of the HiddenFace backdoor; and abuse of Visual Studio Code’s remote tunnels for covert access and arbitrary code execution. Attackers abused legitimate McAfee and JustSystems applications to load ANEL, evading detection, while data exfiltration methods remain unclear. ESET’s forensic collaboration with the victim and JSAC presentation in January 2025 provide actionable insights to monitor for ANEL indicators, sandboxed RAT executions, VS Code tunnel anomalies and Expo-themed spearphishing.
hits.title: ESET Research uncovers Operation AkaiRyū: China-aligned MirrorFace targets European diplomats using Expo 2025 as a lure | | ESET

canonical_entities: spear-phishing attacks against European embassies in Seoul (March–July 2025)
exfiltrated ... over HTTPS to the attackers’ private GitHub repo via the Contents API
hits.text: Between March and July 2025, DPRK-linked Kimsuky operators executed at least 19 highly tailored spear-phishing attacks against Western, Central, Eastern and Southern European embassies in Seoul, spoofing real diplomats and embedding password-protected ZIPs delivered via Dropbox, Daum or Google Drive. Victims unwittingly launched malicious .LNK shortcuts that triggered obfuscated PowerShell scripts to decode and in-memory execute a Confuser-Core-obfuscated XenoRAT (MoonPeak) payload—identified by GUID 12DE1212-167D-45BA-1284-780DA98CF901 and mutex “Dansweit_Hk65-PSAccerdle”—leveraging scheduled tasks for persistence. Reconnaissance data (OS build, IP, process list) was exfiltrated as base64-encoded text files over HTTPS to the attackers’ private GitHub repo via the Contents API, while C2 instructions (e.g., onf.txt) directed dynamic payload rotations hosted on Dropbox with rapid header-fix GZIP routines. This ongoing campaign provided full system control—including keystroke logging, screenshots and remote shells—and underscores the need to monitor abnormal GitHub API usage, cloud-based archive downloads and anomalous PowerShell invocations.
hits.title: The Coordinated Embassy Hunt: Unmasking the DPRK-linked GitHub C2 Espionage Campaign

canonical_entities: Western nation’s military mission in Ukraine
hits.text: In February–March 2025, Russia-linked espionage group Shuckworm (aka Gamaredon/Armageddon) targeted a Western nation’s military mission in Ukraine using a multi-stage PowerShell-centric campaign initiated via an infected removable drive and malicious .lnk file. Obfuscated VBScript (~.drv) deployed through mshta.exe and wscript.exe created registry-named payloads: one performing WMI ping checks to mil.gov.ua before resolving dynamic C2 addresses via Teletype, Telegra.ph, t.me, check-host.net and Cloudflare tunnels (e.g., 107.189.19.218), and another altering Explorer registry keys to hide system files and propagate shortcuts across USB and network shares. The attackers then delivered an updated PowerShell infostealer (GammaSteel) alongside reconnaissance scripts that captured screenshots, systeminfo, process lists and host metadata, exfiltrating sensitive documents (*.docx, *.pptx, *.pdf) using PowerShell web requests with certutil-computed MD5 hashes and fallback cURL over Tor to mask origin. This campaign underscores Shuckworm’s shift from VBS to PowerShell, leveraging in-registry script storage and heavy obfuscation to evade detection, with indicators including anomalous UserAssist entries, unusual mshta/wscript invocations and atypical C2 resolution patterns.
hits.title: Shuckworm Targets Foreign Military Mission Based in Ukraine | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: New research reveals that over 80,000 Hikvision cameras worldwide remain unpatched against the critical CVE-2021-36260 command-injection flaw (NIST score 9.8/10) disclosed last fall, allowing remote code execution and potential espionage by state-linked groups such as MISSION2025/APT41, APT10 and unknown Russian actors trading stolen credentials on dark-web forums; systemic deficiencies—default or hardcoded passwords, no auto-update mechanism, poor forensics and lack of security-by-design—have left devices in 100+ countries (including the U.S., despite an FCC “unacceptable risk” designation) continuously discoverable via Shodan or Censys and ripe for exploitation, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to inventory IoT assets, change default credentials, deploy available patches and improve visibility and update processes to mitigate geopolitical and operational impact.
hits.title: Cybercriminals Are Selling Access to Chinese Surveillance Cameras | Threatpost

hits.text: In February 2022, CISA, the FBI, US Cyber Command CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA issued a joint advisory on Iranian Ministry of Intelligence–linked APT MuddyWater (aka MERCURY, Earth Vetala, Static Kitten, Seedworm, TEMP.Zagros), active since 2018 and focused on cyber espionage, intellectual property theft and ransomware against defense, oil & gas, government and telecom sectors across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America. Exploiting publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and open-source tools, MuddyWater delivers malicious PDFs with embedded links that display error messages prompting users to download Excel maldocs or Windows executables; these files host VBA macros that drop WSF scripts to execute PowerShell and VB payloads, leverage LoLBins, and stage RATs and malware families including PowGoop, Canopy, Small Sieve, POWERSTATS and Mori while communicating with C2 over HTTP and DNS and persisting via Registry Run keys. Cisco Talos observed regional campaigns in Turkey (Nov 2021), Pakistan (Aug 2021) and Armenia (Jun 2021) using decoy documents, signaling tokens and a consistent TTP set, suggesting a conglomerate of subgroups migrating techniques across regions. The resultant network access and data exfiltration underscore the imperative for proactive DFIR readiness, deployment of XDR/MDR platforms, rigorous vulnerability management, macro execution restrictions, PowerShell/LoLBin monitoring and ongoing user awareness training reinforced by incident response tabletop exercises.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at Iranian APT "MuddyWater"

canonical_entities: registered variables in the Windows Registry
hits.text: In June 2024, HP’s Threat Research team led by Patrick Schlapfer intercepted a low-grade phishing campaign leveraging HTML smuggling via an AES-encrypted HTML attachment containing JavaScript-embedded decryption logic—a novel twist on typical encrypted archives—which, when decrypted, mimicked a legitimate website but dropped a fully commented, French-language VBScript that registered variables in the Windows Registry, staged a JavaScript payload as a scheduled task, and invoked a PowerShell script to deploy the freely available AsyncRAT infostealer. Schlapfer and co-lead Alex Holland’s analysis, including comparison with generative-AI–produced code, concluded the well-structured, human-readable script was likely authored by gen-AI by a low-skill newcomer benefitting from reduced entry barriers, with no obfuscation or complex infrastructure beyond a single C2 server. This first definitive proof of AI-generated malware in the wild underscores the need for defenders to adapt detection strategies to AI-crafted droppers, monitor anomalous AES-in-JavaScript decryption patterns, and anticipate more sophisticated AI-generated payloads poised to emerge within the next two years, thereby heightening the risk to network and endpoint security.
hits.title: AI-Generated Malware Found in the Wild - SecurityWeek
