Victims unwittingly launched malicious .LNK shortcuts that triggered obfuscated PowerShell scripts to decode and in-memory execute a Confuser-Core-obfuscated XenoRAT (MoonPeak) payload—identified by GUID 12DE1212-167D-45BA-1284-780DA98CF901 and mutex “Dansweit_Hk65-PSAccerdle”—leveraging scheduled tasks for persistence. Reconnaissance data (OS build, IP, process list) was exfiltrated as base64-encoded text files over HTTPS to the attackers’ private GitHub repo via the Contents API, while C2 instructions (e.g., onf.txt) directed dynamic payload rotations hosted on Dropbox with rapid header-fix GZIP routines. This ongoing campaign provided full system control—including keystroke logging, screenshots and remote shells—and underscores the need to monitor abnormal GitHub API usage, cloud-based archive downloads and anomalous PowerShell invocations.
retrieved_context.title: The Coordinated Embassy Hunt: Unmasking the DPRK-linked GitHub C2 Espionage Campaign

canonical_entities: Western nation’s military mission in Ukraine
retrieved_context.text: In February–March 2025, Russia-linked espionage group Shuckworm (aka Gamaredon/Armageddon) targeted a Western nation’s military mission in Ukraine using a multi-stage PowerShell-centric campaign initiated via an infected removable drive and malicious .lnk file. Obfuscated VBScript (~.drv) deployed through mshta.exe and wscript.exe created registry-named payloads: one performing WMI ping checks to mil.gov.ua before resolving dynamic C2 addresses via Teletype, Telegra.ph, t.me, check-host.net and Cloudflare tunnels (e.g., 107.189.19.218), and another altering Explorer registry keys to hide system files and propagate shortcuts across USB and network shares. The attackers then delivered an updated PowerShell infostealer (GammaSteel) alongside reconnaissance scripts that captured screenshots, systeminfo, process lists and host metadata, exfiltrating sensitive documents (*.docx, *.pptx, *.pdf) using PowerShell web requests with certutil-computed MD5 hashes and fallback cURL over Tor to mask origin. This campaign underscores Shuckworm’s shift from VBS to PowerShell, leveraging in-registry script storage and heavy obfuscation to evade detection, with indicators including anomalous UserAssist entries, unusual mshta/wscript invocations and atypical C2 resolution patterns.
retrieved_context.title: Shuckworm Targets Foreign Military Mission Based in Ukraine | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: New research reveals that over 80,000 Hikvision cameras worldwide remain unpatched against the critical CVE-2021-36260 command-injection flaw (NIST score 9.8/10) disclosed last fall, allowing remote code execution and potential espionage by state-linked groups such as MISSION2025/APT41, APT10 and unknown Russian actors trading stolen credentials on dark-web forums; systemic deficiencies—default or hardcoded passwords, no auto-update mechanism, poor forensics and lack of security-by-design—have left devices in 100+ countries (including the U.S., despite an FCC “unacceptable risk” designation) continuously discoverable via Shodan or Censys and ripe for exploitation, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to inventory IoT assets, change default credentials, deploy available patches and improve visibility and update processes to mitigate geopolitical and operational impact.
retrieved_context.title: Cybercriminals Are Selling Access to Chinese Surveillance Cameras | Threatpost

retrieved_context.text: In February 2022, CISA, the FBI, US Cyber Command CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA issued a joint advisory on Iranian Ministry of Intelligence–linked APT MuddyWater (aka MERCURY, Earth Vetala, Static Kitten, Seedworm, TEMP.Zagros), active since 2018 and focused on cyber espionage, intellectual property theft and ransomware against defense, oil & gas, government and telecom sectors across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America. Exploiting publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and open-source tools, MuddyWater delivers malicious PDFs with embedded links that display error messages prompting users to download Excel maldocs or Windows executables; these files host VBA macros that drop WSF scripts to execute PowerShell and VB payloads, leverage LoLBins, and stage RATs and malware families including PowGoop, Canopy, Small Sieve, POWERSTATS and Mori while communicating with C2 over HTTP and DNS and persisting via Registry Run keys. Cisco Talos observed regional campaigns in Turkey (Nov 2021), Pakistan (Aug 2021) and Armenia (Jun 2021) using decoy documents, signaling tokens and a consistent TTP set, suggesting a conglomerate of subgroups migrating techniques across regions. The resultant network access and data exfiltration underscore the imperative for proactive DFIR readiness, deployment of XDR/MDR platforms, rigorous vulnerability management, macro execution restrictions, PowerShell/LoLBin monitoring and ongoing user awareness training reinforced by incident response tabletop exercises.
retrieved_context.title: An In-Depth Look at Iranian APT "MuddyWater"

canonical_entities: registered variables in the Windows Registry
retrieved_context.text: In June 2024, HP’s Threat Research team led by Patrick Schlapfer intercepted a low-grade phishing campaign leveraging HTML smuggling via an AES-encrypted HTML attachment containing JavaScript-embedded decryption logic—a novel twist on typical encrypted archives—which, when decrypted, mimicked a legitimate website but dropped a fully commented, French-language VBScript that registered variables in the Windows Registry, staged a JavaScript payload as a scheduled task, and invoked a PowerShell script to deploy the freely available AsyncRAT infostealer. Schlapfer and co-lead Alex Holland’s analysis, including comparison with generative-AI–produced code, concluded the well-structured, human-readable script was likely authored by gen-AI by a low-skill newcomer benefitting from reduced entry barriers, with no obfuscation or complex infrastructure beyond a single C2 server. This first definitive proof of AI-generated malware in the wild underscores the need for defenders to adapt detection strategies to AI-crafted droppers, monitor anomalous AES-in-JavaScript decryption patterns, and anticipate more sophisticated AI-generated payloads poised to emerge within the next two years, thereby heightening the risk to network and endpoint security.
retrieved_context.title: AI-Generated Malware Found in the Wild - SecurityWeek

hits.text: ESET Research uncovered Operation AkaiRyū, a spearphishing-driven cyberespionage campaign conducted by the China-aligned MirrorFace APT (now assessed as a subgroup under the APT10 umbrella) against a Central European diplomatic institute between June and September 2024, using Expo 2025-themed lures referencing prior NGO communications to deliver password-protected Word documents and malicious links; this marks MirrorFace’s first known European targeting. Analysis revealed a significant TTP refresh: the revival of the ANEL (UPPERCUT) backdoor—previously exclusive to APT10—for file manipulation, payload execution and screenshots; a heavily customized AsyncRAT variant stealthily run inside Windows Sandbox via a complex execution chain; continued deployment of the HiddenFace backdoor; and abuse of Visual Studio Code’s remote tunnels for covert access and arbitrary code execution. Attackers abused legitimate McAfee and JustSystems applications to load ANEL, evading detection, while data exfiltration methods remain unclear. ESET’s forensic collaboration with the victim and JSAC presentation in January 2025 provide actionable insights to monitor for ANEL indicators, sandboxed RAT executions, VS Code tunnel anomalies and Expo-themed spearphishing.
hits.title: ESET Research uncovers Operation AkaiRyū: China-aligned MirrorFace targets European diplomats using Expo 2025 as a lure | | ESET

hits.text: Symantec has warned that extortion actors, notably the Clop ransomware operation (aka Snakefly/TA505/FIN11), have been exploiting a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability in the MOVEit Transfer web application (CVE-2023-34362) since May 27, 2023, enabling supply-chain attacks across multiple organizations; although first patched on May 31, additional vulnerabilities (CVEs pending) were disclosed on June 9. Attackers deploy a bespoke web shell, Lemurloot (detected as JS.Malscript!g1, Trojan.Gen.2, WS.Malware), to authenticate via hard-coded credentials, execute SQL statements to alter or delete database elements, exfiltrate records and Azure settings, and manipulate user accounts. With proof-of-concept code now public, secondary threat actors face elevated risk of exploitation and data theft. Clop has since threatened data leaks unless ransoms are paid, reflecting its shift from encryption to extortion. Symantec mitigations include file-based and ML detections, network-based attack signatures, and Data Center Security policy controls that harden MS SQL, IIS and sandbox environments to prevent web-shell deployment and unauthorized software execution.
hits.title: MOVEit Vulnerabilities: What You Need to Know | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
hits.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Sea Turtle, also known as Cosmic Wolf, Marbled Dust, Teal Kurma and UNC1326, has been conducting a stealthy, Türkiye-linked cyber espionage campaign since at least January 2017, recently targeting Dutch ISPs, telecom, IT-service and media providers as well as Kurdish websites via supply-chain and island-hopping attacks to harvest politically sensitive personal data and potential dissident communications. First detailed by Cisco Talos in April 2019 for state-sponsored DNS hijacking to redirect legitimate domain queries to attacker-controlled servers, the group elevated its upstream foothold tactics in late 2021 by exploiting known telecom and IT vulnerabilities across Armenia, Cyprus, Greece, Iraq and Syria, per Microsoft. Between 2021 and 2023 PwC observed deployment of “SnappyTCP,” a simple Linux/Unix reverse-TCP web shell (with and without OpenSSL/TLS) for persistence and C2, and Hunt & Hackett’s 2023 incident revealed credential-theft via a compromised cPanel account used to deploy SnappyTCP, tar and expose email archives publicly for direct exfiltration. Organizations should enforce strong password policies, 2FA, login-rate limiting, SSH monitoring and timely patching to mitigate this ongoing espionage threat.
hits.title: Sea Turtle Cyber Espionage Campaign Targets Dutch IT and Telecom Companies

canonical_entities: month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment
hits.text: In November 2023, Russian state-sponsored group Nobelium (aka Midnight Blizzard/APT29) executed a month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment by conducting a password-spray brute-force attack against a legacy non-production test tenant lacking multi-factor authentication, enabling pivoting to a small subset of high-value accounts—including leadership, cybersecurity and legal team mailboxes—from which they exfiltrated emails and attachments; discovered on January 12, 2024, the campaign underscores the risk of poorly secured account configurations rather than software vulnerabilities, prompting Microsoft to notify impacted employees, reaffirm its MFA mandate, and reinforce zero-trust controls. This incident, following Nobelium’s SolarWinds and 2021 support-tool intrusions, highlights the necessity of enforcing MFA, minimizing default permissions, and hardening non-prod assets to mitigate advanced persistent threats.
hits.title: Russian hackers stole Microsoft corporate emails in month-long breach

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.

hits.text: Russia’s APT29 (aka Cozy Bear/Nobelium) has been exploiting a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in JetBrains TeamCity (CVE-2023-42793, CVSS 9.8) since September—shortly after JetBrains issued a patch and Rapid7 published a proof-of-concept—to gain initial access to SDLC management servers, escalate privileges, move laterally, deploy stealthy backdoors that persist through updates, and potentially manipulate build pipelines or insert malicious updates in SolarWinds-style supply-chain attacks; CISA, FBI, NSA and international partners warn that around 800 internet-exposed instances remain vulnerable (with uncounted internally reachable servers also at risk), and that North Korea’s Lazarus and Andariel groups have similarly weaponized the same flaw, prompting Fortinet to report multi-actor post-exploit techniques in live incidents; mitigation guidance urges immediate upgrading to TeamCity 2023.05.4, removal of public exposure, comprehensive IoC-based threat hunting across servers and build agents, and full compromise assessments to eradicate entrenched backdoors.
hits.title: Global TeamCity Exploitation Opens Door to SolarWinds-Style Nightmare

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
hits.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

hits.text: HC3’s November 2022 alert warns of human-operated Lorenz ransomware, first observed in February 2021 and linked to earlier sZ40 and ThunderCrypt activity, which specifically targets large healthcare organizations by customizing its executable code and following a kill chain of initial access, extended reconnaissance, lateral movement to Windows domain controllers for administrator credential theft, then encryption and extortion. Operators demand $500,000–$700,000 and employ a non-typical leak site where stolen data is first offered for sale to other threat actors, then distributed in password-protected archives or, if sales fail, released publicly. With relatively limited public intelligence on Lorenz, HC3 emphasizes that victims should address common ransomware vectors—phishing, exploitation of known vulnerabilities, remote-access compromise and distributed attacks—by reinforcing patch management, intrusion detection, access controls and incident-response planning, especially in light of concurrent Hive ransomware warnings issued by HHS, FBI and CISA.
hits.title: Lorenz Ransomware Targets Large Healthcare Orgs, HC3 Warns | TechTarget

canonical_entities: harvest subscriber location, billing and communications metadata
hits.text: On Sept. 25, 2024, the Wall Street Journal disclosed that the Chinese state-sponsored APT Salt Typhoon has stealthily infiltrated multiple U.S. cable and broadband ISPs—likely via firmware and supply-chain compromises in core networking gear—to establish long-term persistence, harvest subscriber location, billing and communications metadata for espionage, and pre-position disruptive capabilities against federal, military and Fortune 100 users; this campaign, echoing Volt Typhoon’s telecom backdoors, Flax Typhoon’s 200,000-device IoT botnet, Brass Typhoon’s cross-domain implants and Mustang Panda’s telco intrusions, signals a shift from surveillance to offensive “blink-the-lights” or infrastructure-crippling attacks in a Taiwan contingency, driving urgent recommendations for carriers to enforce threat-intelligence sharing, secure firmware, tighten supply-chain controls and bolster routing security.

hits.text: On March 4 JetBrains released patches for two critical TeamCity authentication-bypass flaws (CVE-2024-27198 and CVE-2024-27199) that allow unauthenticated remote attackers to create admin accounts or tokens, but misaligned disclosure with Rapid7—whose researchers publicly detailed the bugs hours after the fixes—triggered mass exploitation: by March 6 LeakIX recorded rogue user creation on approximately 1,400 servers and GuidePoint Security linked the BianLian ransomware group to CVE-2024-27198–driven initial access. Despite JetBrains’ efforts to obfuscate patches and limit reverse engineering time, unpatched customers reported at least two file-encryption incidents and one DDoS-prep compromise. This chain of events underscores the necessity of coordinated vendor–researcher disclosure, accelerated patch deployment, and enhanced patch hardening to mitigate rapid exploit development and reduce organizational exposure.

hits.text: Lynx ransomware, emerging in July 2024 as the INC ransomware successor under a Ransomware-as-a-Service model, employs a sophisticated double-extortion strategy—exfiltrating data prior to encryption and threatening publication on a leak site—and reuses significant INC source code. Between July and November 2024, it disrupted U.S. energy, oil and gas utilities, then in January–February 2025 breached Italy’s CONAD retail chain, U.S. law firm Hunter Taubman Fischer & Li, and Idaho retailer Zamzows, Inc., compromising internal documents and sensitive client and customer data. Initial access leverages phishing (T1566.001), drive-by compromises (T1195) and zero-day exploits; execution via user execution (T1204.002) and scripting interpreters (T1059.001); persistence through autostart mechanisms (T1070.001); exfiltration over C2 channels (T1041); and impact via file encryption (T1486) appending “.LYNX.” Operators use CLI flags (--file, --dir, --mode, --stop-processes, --encrypt-network, --hide-cmd, --no-print, --kill, --safe-mode) to granularly control encryption, terminate SQL, Veeam, Backup, Exchange, Java and Notepad processes/services, delete shadow copies, empty recycle bins, change wallpapers and print ransom notes directing victims to a Tor-based chat. Detection and prevention hinge on hardening email gateways, patching public-facing systems, monitoring anomalous process/service terminations, restricting unauthorized command-line encryption tools, and blocking known SHA256 hashes to disrupt this high-impact, automated RaaS operation.

hits.text: In late 2023, researchers uncovered a sophisticated Taiwan-focused espionage operation in which a China-linked APT actor (likely APT27) hijacked an abandoned Sogou Zhuyin Windows update server—vacated when Sogou ceased Zhuyin support in mid-2022—and weaponized it to distribute a trojanized updater (SHA-256: 3f5c…) that deployed a custom backdoor and Cobalt Strike beacon via HTTP(S) (MITRE T1195.002, T1071.001). Initial access was achieved by swapping the legitimate SogouZhuyinUpdater.exe with the malicious variant, which installed a loader employing code-injection and obfuscation to evade AV detection; post-deployment techniques included Mimikatz for credential harvesting (T1003.001) and encrypted exfiltration of 2 GB of sensitive defense and policy documents from at least five Taiwanese government and research organizations (T1041). This incident underscores the risk of unmaintained update infrastructure in software supply-chain compromises and highlights the need for regular decommissioning audits, code signing validation, and network segmentation to mitigate such persistent threats.

hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.

hits.text: Kaspersky researchers have uncovered a new variant of the multi-stage Necro Trojan—first observed in 2019’s CamScanner compromise—that over recent weeks infected two Google Play apps (Wuta Camera, 10 M+ downloads; Max Browser, 1 M+ downloads) and unofficial mods for Spotify, WhatsApp and popular games by exploiting an untrusted advertising-integration SDK; in the Spotify mod the SDK exfiltrated device/app data to a known Necro C&C server and fetched a payload hidden in an image, while in the WhatsApp mod a loader abused Firebase Remote Config for C&C before deploying identical Necro payloads sharing code, structure and C&C infrastructure. Once installed, Necro’s latest variant downloads modules to display and click invisible ads, execute JavaScript in hidden WebViews, download executables and third-party apps, redirect traffic through compromised devices as proxies and subscribe victims to premium services. Between August 26 and September 15, tens of thousands of devices in Russia, Brazil, Vietnam, Ecuador and Mexico were targeted before Google removed the infected apps. Organizations should rigorously vet third-party SDKs, monitor remote-config channels and anomalous network traffic for image-based payload retrieval and invisible ad click-fraud behaviors to mitigate this evolving mobile threat.

hits.text: US and UK agencies (CISA, FBI, CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA) issued a joint advisory detailing how the Iranian-backed MuddyWater group—active since at least 2017 and linked to Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security in January 2022—has expanded its arsenal beyond PowGoop, Canopy/Starwhale, Mori and POWERSTATS to include a new Python backdoor dubbed “Small Sieve” and a PowerShell backdoor that encrypts C2 channels; these tools target telecom, defense, local government and oil and gas organizations across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America, maintain persistence via custom string and traffic obfuscation (hex byte-swapping plus an obfuscated Base64 routine) over the Telegram Bot API via HTTPS, and facilitate lateral movement and data exfiltration, underscoring the need for defenders to monitor anomalous Telegram API calls, obfuscated Base64 traffic and encrypted PowerShell sessions.

hits.text: On March 5, 2025, the US Department of Justice unsealed an indictment implicating Chinese contractor I-SOON’s FishMonger APT team in Operation FishMedley, a 2022 global espionage campaign that compromised seven high-value targets—government bodies in Taiwan and Thailand, a Hungarian Catholic organization, a Turkish entity, a US-based Catholic charity and NGO, and a French think tank—using privileged domain credentials to deploy implants such as the ScatterBee-packed ShadowPad backdoor (configured with campaign code 2203 and C2 at api.googleauthenticatoronline[.]com:443), the Spyder loader (delivered via malicious .doc, AES-CBC-decoded with hardcoded key F4E4C69EDEE09E820000000000000000, injected into task.exe with C2 at 61.238.103[.]165), and SodaMaster loaders side-loaded via legitimate DLLs decrypting payloads from debug.png or libvlc.dll, supported by Impacket-enabled lateral movement, LSASS and registry hive dumps via comsvcs.dll, and Cobalt Strike, SprySOCKS and BIOPASS RAT, underscoring the need for vigilant monitoring of living-off-the-land binaries, anomalous HTTP downloads, DLL side-loading and high-privilege account usage.

retrieved_context.text: ESET Research uncovered Operation AkaiRyū, a spearphishing-driven cyberespionage campaign conducted by the China-aligned MirrorFace APT (now assessed as a subgroup under the APT10 umbrella) against a Central European diplomatic institute between June and September 2024, using Expo 2025-themed lures referencing prior NGO communications to deliver password-protected Word documents and malicious links; this marks MirrorFace’s first known European targeting. Analysis revealed a significant TTP refresh: the revival of the ANEL (UPPERCUT) backdoor—previously exclusive to APT10—for file manipulation, payload execution and screenshots; a heavily customized AsyncRAT variant stealthily run inside Windows Sandbox via a complex execution chain; continued deployment of the HiddenFace backdoor; and abuse of Visual Studio Code’s remote tunnels for covert access and arbitrary code execution. Attackers abused legitimate McAfee and JustSystems applications to load ANEL, evading detection, while data exfiltration methods remain unclear. ESET’s forensic collaboration with the victim and JSAC presentation in January 2025 provide actionable insights to monitor for ANEL indicators, sandboxed RAT executions, VS Code tunnel anomalies and Expo-themed spearphishing.
retrieved_context.title: ESET Research uncovers Operation AkaiRyū: China-aligned MirrorFace targets European diplomats using Expo 2025 as a lure | | ESET

retrieved_context.text: HC3’s November 2022 alert warns of human-operated Lorenz ransomware, first observed in February 2021 and linked to earlier sZ40 and ThunderCrypt activity, which specifically targets large healthcare organizations by customizing its executable code and following a kill chain of initial access, extended reconnaissance, lateral movement to Windows domain controllers for administrator credential theft, then encryption and extortion. Operators demand $500,000–$700,000 and employ a non-typical leak site where stolen data is first offered for sale to other threat actors, then distributed in password-protected archives or, if sales fail, released publicly. With relatively limited public intelligence on Lorenz, HC3 emphasizes that victims should address common ransomware vectors—phishing, exploitation of known vulnerabilities, remote-access compromise and distributed attacks—by reinforcing patch management, intrusion detection, access controls and incident-response planning, especially in light of concurrent Hive ransomware warnings issued by HHS, FBI and CISA.

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

hits.text: New research reveals that over 80,000 Hikvision cameras worldwide remain unpatched against the critical CVE-2021-36260 command-injection flaw (NIST score 9.8/10) disclosed last fall, allowing remote code execution and potential espionage by state-linked groups such as MISSION2025/APT41, APT10 and unknown Russian actors trading stolen credentials on dark-web forums; systemic deficiencies—default or hardcoded passwords, no auto-update mechanism, poor forensics and lack of security-by-design—have left devices in 100+ countries (including the U.S., despite an FCC “unacceptable risk” designation) continuously discoverable via Shodan or Censys and ripe for exploitation, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to inventory IoT assets, change default credentials, deploy available patches and improve visibility and update processes to mitigate geopolitical and operational impact.
hits.title: Cybercriminals Are Selling Access to Chinese Surveillance Cameras | Threatpost

canonical_entities: Exfiltration of SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations
hits.text: North Korean state-sponsored APT Slow Pisces (aka Jade Sleet, TraderTraitor, PUKCHONG) is executing a sophisticated three-stage campaign against cryptocurrency developers by posing as recruiters on LinkedIn, distributing benign PDF job descriptions with embedded coding challenges, and redirecting targets to malicious GitHub repositories containing Python and JavaScript code laced with YAML deserialization and EJS escapeFunction backdoors; once activated under specific conditions, these backdoors deploy in-memory RN Loader and RN Stealer payloads to collect system information, establish C2 communications, and exfiltrate SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations with minimal forensic footprint—building on past successes that netted over $1 billion in 2023 and $1.5 billion in 2024—and highlighting the urgent need for enhanced vetting on professional platforms, proactive detection of unsafe deserialization and templating flaws, and memory-based threat monitoring to defend the cryptocurrency sector.
hits.title: Slow Pisces Group Targets Developers Using Coding Challenges Laced with Python Malware

hits.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
hits.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
hits.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

canonical_entities: deployed a webshell on the router’s web server
Credentials from Password Stores: Security Account Manager
hits.text: Dragos researchers, in collaboration with Ukraine’s CSSC, unearthed FrostyGoop—an ICS-specific malware first spotted in April and used in January to disrupt central heating in over 600 Lviv apartment buildings—marking the first known malware to leverage Modbus TCP for read/write operations on operational technology. Attackers gained initial access in April 2023 by exploiting a MikroTik router vulnerability, deployed a webshell on the router’s web server, and maintained persistence via Tor and L2TP tunnels to Moscow-based IPs. After spending months conducting reconnaissance, they extracted credentials by dumping the SAM registry hive in December, then directly issued scripted Modbus commands—read from a JSON configuration file—to publicly exposed ENCO heating controllers, even downgrading firmware to disable monitoring and force inaccurate measurements that halted heating services for nearly two days amid subzero temperatures. This incident underscores the threat posed by internet-exposed ICS devices—over 46,000 globally using Modbus—and highlights poor network segmentation, unpatched ICS CVEs, and the ease with which FrostyGoop’s protocol-agnostic payload can be repurposed against diverse industrial controllers, necessitating immediate network segmentation, firmware monitoring, and patch management in OT environments.
hits.title: ICS malware FrostyGoop disrupted heating in Ukraine, remains threat to OT worldwide

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.

retrieved_context.text: ESET Research uncovered Operation AkaiRyū, a spearphishing-driven cyberespionage campaign conducted by the China-aligned MirrorFace APT (now assessed as a subgroup under the APT10 umbrella) against a Central European diplomatic institute between June and September 2024, using Expo 2025-themed lures referencing prior NGO communications to deliver password-protected Word documents and malicious links; this marks MirrorFace’s first known European targeting. Analysis revealed a significant TTP refresh: the revival of the ANEL (UPPERCUT) backdoor—previously exclusive to APT10—for file manipulation, payload execution and screenshots; a heavily customized AsyncRAT variant stealthily run inside Windows Sandbox via a complex execution chain; continued deployment of the HiddenFace backdoor; and abuse of Visual Studio Code’s remote tunnels for covert access and arbitrary code execution. Attackers abused legitimate McAfee and JustSystems applications to load ANEL, evading detection, while data exfiltration methods remain unclear. ESET’s forensic collaboration with the victim and JSAC presentation in January 2025 provide actionable insights to monitor for ANEL indicators, sandboxed RAT executions, VS Code tunnel anomalies and Expo-themed spearphishing.

retrieved_context.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. retrieved_context.text: Dragos researchers, in collaboration with Ukraine’s CSSC, unearthed FrostyGoop—an ICS-specific malware first spotted in April and used in January to disrupt central heating in over 600 Lviv apartment buildings—marking the first known malware to leverage Modbus TCP for read/write operations on operational technology. Attackers gained initial access in April 2023 by exploiting a MikroTik router vulnerability, deployed a webshell on the router’s web server, and maintained persistence via Tor and L2TP tunnels to Moscow-based IPs. hits.text: Symantec has warned that extortion actors, notably the Clop ransomware operation (aka Snakefly/TA505/FIN11), have been exploiting a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability in the MOVEit Transfer web application (CVE-2023-34362) since May 27, 2023, enabling supply-chain attacks across multiple organizations; although first patched on May 31, additional vulnerabilities (CVEs pending) were disclosed on June 9. Attackers deploy a bespoke web shell, Lemurloot (detected as JS.Malscript!g1, Trojan.Gen.2, WS.Malware), to authenticate via hard-coded credentials, execute SQL statements to alter or delete database elements, exfiltrate records and Azure settings, and manipulate user accounts. With proof-of-concept code now public, secondary threat actors face elevated risk of exploitation and data theft. Clop has since threatened data leaks unless ransoms are paid, reflecting its shift from encryption to extortion. Symantec mitigations include file-based and ML detections, network-based attack signatures, and Data Center Security policy controls that harden MS SQL, IIS and sandbox environments to prevent web-shell deployment and unauthorized software execution.
hits.title: MOVEit Vulnerabilities: What You Need to Know | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Sea Turtle, also known as Cosmic Wolf, Marbled Dust, Teal Kurma and UNC1326, has been conducting a stealthy, Türkiye-linked cyber espionage campaign since at least January 2017, recently targeting Dutch ISPs, telecom, IT-service and media providers as well as Kurdish websites via supply-chain and island-hopping attacks to harvest politically sensitive personal data and potential dissident communications. First detailed by Cisco Talos in April 2019 for state-sponsored DNS hijacking to redirect legitimate domain queries to attacker-controlled servers, the group elevated its upstream foothold tactics in late 2021 by exploiting known telecom and IT vulnerabilities across Armenia, Cyprus, Greece, Iraq and Syria, per Microsoft. Between 2021 and 2023 PwC observed deployment of “SnappyTCP,” a simple Linux/Unix reverse-TCP web shell (with and without OpenSSL/TLS) for persistence and C2, and Hunt & Hackett’s 2023 incident revealed credential-theft via a compromised cPanel account used to deploy SnappyTCP, tar and expose email archives publicly for direct exfiltration. Organizations should enforce strong password policies, 2FA, login-rate limiting, SSH monitoring and timely patching to mitigate this ongoing espionage threat.
hits.title: Sea Turtle Cyber Espionage Campaign Targets Dutch IT and Telecom Companies

hits.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. More recently, the group shifted to adversary-in-the-middle spear-phishing using a typosquatted “micsrosoftonline[.]com” domain and an Evilginx-based phishing page delivered through malicious QR codes in forged European Defense and Security Summit PDF invitations, automating bulk data collection via Exchange, Microsoft Graph and Teams web client. Overlaps with Forest Blizzard, Midnight Blizzard and Secret Blizzard indicate coordinated Russian strategic espionage, and a September 2024 pass-the-cookie breach of a Dutch police account underscores their evolving cookie-theft capabilities—highlighting urgent needs for phishing-resistant MFA and hardened Entra ID configurations.
hits.title: Russian Hackers Breach 20+ NGOs Using Evilginx Phishing via Fake Microsoft Entra Pages

hits.text: In November 2023, Russian state-sponsored group Nobelium (aka Midnight Blizzard/APT29) executed a month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment by conducting a password-spray brute-force attack against a legacy non-production test tenant lacking multi-factor authentication, enabling pivoting to a small subset of high-value accounts—including leadership, cybersecurity and legal team mailboxes—from which they exfiltrated emails and attachments; discovered on January 12, 2024, the campaign underscores the risk of poorly secured account configurations rather than software vulnerabilities, prompting Microsoft to notify impacted employees, reaffirm its MFA mandate, and reinforce zero-trust controls. This incident, following Nobelium’s SolarWinds and 2021 support-tool intrusions, highlights the necessity of enforcing MFA, minimizing default permissions, and hardening non-prod assets to mitigate advanced persistent threats.

hits.text: Moses Staff, also dubbed Cobalt Sapling, is an Iran-linked APT active since November 2020 and publicly identified in September 2021, originally posting 16 leak events of Israeli corporate data and personal information of IDF intelligence personnel by December 2022 using a toolkit comprising the PyDCrypt custom loader, DCSrv cryptographic wiper, StrifeWater RAT and its DriveGuard monitoring utility; in November 2022, Secureworks attributed a new hacktivist persona, Abraham’s Ax—featuring similar biblical branding, Tor-hosted leak sites on adjacent subnets and recycled “Hollywood-style” hacking videos—to the same operators, who have since shifted toward exfiltrating and leaking data from Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of the Interior (including a purported intercepted ministerial phone conversation) rather than directly attacking Israel, likely in response to Saudi-Israeli rapprochement, while Moses Staff continues operations (claiming a CCTV system hack at an Israeli terror site); these insights highlight the urgency for Saudi and Israeli government entities to strengthen network segmentation, deploy advanced endpoint detection for known Iranian toolsets, monitor darknet leak platforms and prepare incident response plans tailored to politically motivated exfiltration campaigns.
hits.title: Iranian APT Leaks Data From Saudi Arabia Government Under New Persona

hits.text: In August 2025 Microsoft Threat Intelligence revealed that Storm-2460, associated with the Play ransomware group, has resumed exploiting CVE-2025-29824—a zero-day elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Common Log File System patched in April—to gain SYSTEM privileges on unpatched hosts across IT, financial and real estate organizations in the US, Europe, South America and the Middle East. The campaign begins with an in-memory dropper masquerading as the open-source ChatGPT Desktop app that decrypts and launches PipeMagic, a modular backdoor first observed in December 2022 and now updated with persistence and lateral-movement enhancements targeting Saudi Arabian and Brazilian manufacturing entities. PipeMagic communicates with its TCP C2 over a named pipe, self-updates by storing distinct payload modules in memory via doubly linked lists for staging, execution and communication (plus an additional dynamic list), then leverages the CLFS exploit to escalate privileges before deploying Play ransomware. Although the campaign’s footprint remains limited, the combination of a zero-day exploit and a sophisticated modular backdoor underscores a heightened risk; organizations are urged to immediately apply the April patch for CVE-2025-29824, enable tamper and network protection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, run EDR in block mode, enforce full automated investigation and remediation, and leverage cloud-delivered machine-learning protections to block novel variants.
hits.title: PipeMagic Backdoor Resurfaces as Part of Play Ransomware Attack Chain

Overlaps with Forest Blizzard, Midnight Blizzard and Secret Blizzard indicate coordinated Russian strategic espionage, and a September 2024 pass-the-cookie breach of a Dutch police account underscores their evolving cookie-theft capabilities—highlighting urgent needs for phishing-resistant MFA and hardened Entra ID configurations.
retrieved_context.title: Russian Hackers Breach 20+ NGOs Using Evilginx Phishing via Fake Microsoft Entra Pages

canonical_entities: month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment
retrieved_context.text: In November 2023, Russian state-sponsored group Nobelium (aka Midnight Blizzard/APT29) executed a month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment by conducting a password-spray brute-force attack against a legacy non-production test tenant lacking multi-factor authentication, enabling pivoting to a small subset of high-value accounts—including leadership, cybersecurity and legal team mailboxes—from which they exfiltrated emails and attachments; discovered on January 12, 2024, the campaign underscores the risk of poorly secured account configurations rather than software vulnerabilities, prompting Microsoft to notify impacted employees, reaffirm its MFA mandate, and reinforce zero-trust controls. This incident, following Nobelium’s SolarWinds and 2021 support-tool intrusions, highlights the necessity of enforcing MFA, minimizing default permissions, and hardening non-prod assets to mitigate advanced persistent threats.
retrieved_context.title: Russian hackers stole Microsoft corporate emails in month-long breach

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
retrieved_context.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

canonical_entities: Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of the Interior
retrieved_context.text: Moses Staff, also dubbed Cobalt Sapling, is an Iran-linked APT active since November 2020 and publicly identified in September 2021, originally posting 16 leak events of Israeli corporate data and personal information of IDF intelligence personnel by December 2022 using a toolkit comprising the PyDCrypt custom loader, DCSrv cryptographic wiper, StrifeWater RAT and its DriveGuard monitoring utility; in November 2022, Secureworks attributed a new hacktivist persona, Abraham’s Ax—featuring similar biblical branding, Tor-hosted leak sites on adjacent subnets and recycled “Hollywood-style” hacking videos—to the same operators, who have since shifted toward exfiltrating and leaking data from Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of the Interior (including a purported intercepted ministerial phone conversation) rather than directly attacking Israel, likely in response to Saudi-Israeli rapprochement, while Moses Staff continues operations (claiming a CCTV system hack at an Israeli terror site); these insights highlight the urgency for Saudi and Israeli government entities to strengthen network segmentation, deploy advanced endpoint detection for known Iranian toolsets, monitor darknet leak platforms and prepare incident response plans tailored to politically motivated exfiltration campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Iranian APT Leaks Data From Saudi Arabia Government Under New Persona

retrieved_context.text: In August 2025 Microsoft Threat Intelligence revealed that Storm-2460, associated with the Play ransomware group, has resumed exploiting CVE-2025-29824—a zero-day elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Common Log File System patched in April—to gain SYSTEM privileges on unpatched hosts across IT, financial and real estate organizations in the US, Europe, South America and the Middle East. The campaign begins with an in-memory dropper masquerading as the open-source ChatGPT Desktop app that decrypts and launches PipeMagic, a modular backdoor first observed in December 2022 and now updated with persistence and lateral-movement enhancements targeting Saudi Arabian and Brazilian manufacturing entities. PipeMagic communicates with its TCP C2 over a named pipe, self-updates by storing distinct payload modules in memory via doubly linked lists for staging, execution and communication (plus an additional dynamic list), then leverages the CLFS exploit to escalate privileges before deploying Play ransomware. Although the campaign’s footprint remains limited, the combination of a zero-day exploit and a sophisticated modular backdoor underscores a heightened risk; organizations are urged to immediately apply the April patch for CVE-2025-29824, enable tamper and network protection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, run EDR in block mode, enforce full automated investigation and remediation, and leverage cloud-delivered machine-learning protections to block novel variants.
retrieved_context.title: PipeMagic Backdoor Resurfaces as Part of Play Ransomware Attack Chain

hits.text: Since mid-2016, an Iran-linked espionage operation dubbed “Magic Hound” has targeted energy, government and technology organizations in and around Saudi Arabia using macro-enabled Word and Excel documents masquerading as holiday cards, job offers and official Ministry of Health and Commerce files to launch PowerShell-based downloaders and custom droppers, executable and document loaders and IRC bots that ultimately deploy a Python-based Pupy RAT; Palo Alto Networks analysts—citing overlaps in domains and initial breach methods with the recent Shamoon 2 campaign—have linked Magic Hound to the Iran-aligned Rocket Kitten group, while SecureWorks attributes it to COBALT GYPSY and IBM X-Force has observed shared infrastructure, and additional code similarities tie an IRC bot to Charming Kitten/Newscaster activity and to MacDownloader tools used by other Iranian actors, underscoring the need to block malicious macros, monitor PowerShell and IRC traffic for known C2 signatures, and flag Pupy-related domains and custom loader behaviors to disrupt long-running cross-platform intrusion operations.

hits.text: Since mid-2016, a cyber espionage operation dubbed Magic Hound, attributed to Iranian government–linked actors including COBALT GYPSY and showing overlaps with Rocket Kitten (Operation Saffron Rose/Ajax Security Team/Operation Woolen-Goldfish) and Newscasters (Charming Kitten/NewsBeef), has targeted energy, government and technology organizations in and tied to Saudi Arabia by distributing Word and Excel documents embedding malicious macros that launch PowerShell downloaders and droppers to deploy a custom toolkit—comprising executable and document loaders, IRC bots and the multi-platform Python-based PupyRAT—for full system access and data exfiltration; analysis by Palo Alto Networks and SecureWorks revealed domain and tool reuse with the Shamoon 2 wiper campaign, and bait lures mimicking holiday greetings, job offers and official Ministry of Health and Commerce communications, underscoring the need for enhanced macro-enablement policies, network segmentation and proactive IOC monitoring of associated domains and IRC traffic.

hits.text: HC3’s November 2022 alert warns of human-operated Lorenz ransomware, first observed in February 2021 and linked to earlier sZ40 and ThunderCrypt activity, which specifically targets large healthcare organizations by customizing its executable code and following a kill chain of initial access, extended reconnaissance, lateral movement to Windows domain controllers for administrator credential theft, then encryption and extortion. Operators demand $500,000–$700,000 and employ a non-typical leak site where stolen data is first offered for sale to other threat actors, then distributed in password-protected archives or, if sales fail, released publicly. With relatively limited public intelligence on Lorenz, HC3 emphasizes that victims should address common ransomware vectors—phishing, exploitation of known vulnerabilities, remote-access compromise and distributed attacks—by reinforcing patch management, intrusion detection, access controls and incident-response planning, especially in light of concurrent Hive ransomware warnings issued by HHS, FBI and CISA.
hits.title: Lorenz Ransomware Targets Large Healthcare Orgs, HC3 Warns | TechTarget

hits.text: On Sept. 25, 2024, the Wall Street Journal disclosed that the Chinese state-sponsored APT Salt Typhoon has stealthily infiltrated multiple U.S. cable and broadband ISPs—likely via firmware and supply-chain compromises in core networking gear—to establish long-term persistence, harvest subscriber location, billing and communications metadata for espionage, and pre-position disruptive capabilities against federal, military and Fortune 100 users; this campaign, echoing Volt Typhoon’s telecom backdoors, Flax Typhoon’s 200,000-device IoT botnet, Brass Typhoon’s cross-domain implants and Mustang Panda’s telco intrusions, signals a shift from surveillance to offensive “blink-the-lights” or infrastructure-crippling attacks in a Taiwan contingency, driving urgent recommendations for carriers to enforce threat-intelligence sharing, secure firmware, tighten supply-chain controls and bolster routing security.
hits.title: China's 'Salt Typhoon' Cooks Up Cyberattacks on US ISPs

hits.text: Lynx ransomware, a Ransomware-as-a-Service strain first seen in mid-2024 that repurposes INC source code, has targeted finance, architecture and manufacturing organizations—later expanding into energy and APAC retail—via phishing emails that deploy malware to exfiltrate sensitive data for double-extortion (including timed “drip” leaks) before encrypting files with a “.LYNX” extension; Darktrace observed initial lateral movement through SMB enumeration on port 445 and Nmap scans, exploitation of default “admin”/“administrator” credentials via NTLM and Kerberos for privilege escalation, anomalous internal transfers of ~150 GiB over port 3260 and large uploads to wt-prod-euwest1-storm.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com, plus AnyDesk-based remote sessions to aid operator actions, culminating in thousands of encrypted files detected by parallel SMB read/write anomalies and extension appends—Darktrace’s Autonomous Response models, if fully enabled, would automatically block suspicious SMB activity, unusual privileged user behavior and anomalous outbound connections to contain the threat and preserve business continuity.
hits.title: New Threat on the Prowl: Investigating Lynx Ransomware

hits.text: On March 4 JetBrains released patches for two critical TeamCity authentication-bypass flaws (CVE-2024-27198 and CVE-2024-27199) that allow unauthenticated remote attackers to create admin accounts or tokens, but misaligned disclosure with Rapid7—whose researchers publicly detailed the bugs hours after the fixes—triggered mass exploitation: by March 6 LeakIX recorded rogue user creation on approximately 1,400 servers and GuidePoint Security linked the BianLian ransomware group to CVE-2024-27198–driven initial access. Despite JetBrains’ efforts to obfuscate patches and limit reverse engineering time, unpatched customers reported at least two file-encryption incidents and one DDoS-prep compromise. This chain of events underscores the necessity of coordinated vendor–researcher disclosure, accelerated patch deployment, and enhanced patch hardening to mitigate rapid exploit development and reduce organizational exposure.
hits.title: Recent TeamCity Vulnerability Exploited in Ransomware Attacks - SecurityWeek

hits.text: On March 5, 2025, the US Department of Justice unsealed an indictment implicating Chinese contractor I-SOON’s FishMonger APT team in Operation FishMedley, a 2022 global espionage campaign that compromised seven high-value targets—government bodies in Taiwan and Thailand, a Hungarian Catholic organization, a Turkish entity, a US-based Catholic charity and NGO, and a French think tank—using privileged domain credentials to deploy implants such as the ScatterBee-packed ShadowPad backdoor (configured with campaign code 2203 and C2 at api.googleauthenticatoronline[.]com:443), the Spyder loader (delivered via malicious .doc, AES-CBC-decoded with hardcoded key F4E4C69EDEE09E820000000000000000, injected into task.exe with C2 at 61.238.103[.]165), and SodaMaster loaders side-loaded via legitimate DLLs decrypting payloads from debug.png or libvlc.dll, supported by Impacket-enabled lateral movement, LSASS and registry hive dumps via comsvcs.dll, and Cobalt Strike, SprySOCKS and BIOPASS RAT, underscoring the need for vigilant monitoring of living-off-the-land binaries, anomalous HTTP downloads, DLL side-loading and high-privilege account usage.
hits.title: Operation FishMedley targeting governments, NGOs, and think tanks

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: Moses Staff, also dubbed Cobalt Sapling, is an Iran-linked APT active since November 2020 and publicly identified in September 2021, originally posting 16 leak events of Israeli corporate data and personal information of IDF intelligence personnel by December 2022 using a toolkit comprising the PyDCrypt custom loader, DCSrv cryptographic wiper, StrifeWater RAT and its DriveGuard monitoring utility; in November 2022, Secureworks attributed a new hacktivist persona, Abraham’s Ax—featuring similar biblical branding, Tor-hosted leak sites on adjacent subnets and recycled “Hollywood-style” hacking videos—to the same operators, who have since shifted toward exfiltrating and leaking data from Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of the Interior (including a purported intercepted ministerial phone conversation) rather than directly attacking Israel, likely in response to Saudi-Israeli rapprochement, while Moses Staff continues operations (claiming a CCTV system hack at an Israeli terror site); these insights highlight the urgency for Saudi and Israeli government entities to strengthen network segmentation, deploy advanced endpoint detection for known Iranian toolsets, monitor darknet leak platforms and prepare incident response plans tailored to politically motivated exfiltration campaigns.
hits.title: Iranian APT Leaks Data From Saudi Arabia Government Under New Persona

hits.text: In August 2025 Microsoft Threat Intelligence revealed that Storm-2460, associated with the Play ransomware group, has resumed exploiting CVE-2025-29824—a zero-day elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Common Log File System patched in April—to gain SYSTEM privileges on unpatched hosts across IT, financial and real estate organizations in the US, Europe, South America and the Middle East. The campaign begins with an in-memory dropper masquerading as the open-source ChatGPT Desktop app that decrypts and launches PipeMagic, a modular backdoor first observed in December 2022 and now updated with persistence and lateral-movement enhancements targeting Saudi Arabian and Brazilian manufacturing entities. PipeMagic communicates with its TCP C2 over a named pipe, self-updates by storing distinct payload modules in memory via doubly linked lists for staging, execution and communication (plus an additional dynamic list), then leverages the CLFS exploit to escalate privileges before deploying Play ransomware. Although the campaign’s footprint remains limited, the combination of a zero-day exploit and a sophisticated modular backdoor underscores a heightened risk; organizations are urged to immediately apply the April patch for CVE-2025-29824, enable tamper and network protection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, run EDR in block mode, enforce full automated investigation and remediation, and leverage cloud-delivered machine-learning protections to block novel variants.
hits.title: PipeMagic Backdoor Resurfaces as Part of Play Ransomware Attack Chain

hits.text: Unit 42 researchers uncovered a targeted Lampion infostealer campaign in late 2024–early 2025 against Portuguese government, finance and transportation organizations that reuses infrastructure and TTPs dating back to 2019 while introducing ClickFix social-engineering lures—victims receive a phishing email with a malicious ZIP attachment containing an HTML redirect to autoridade-tributaria[.]com, where they are duped into copying a “#Habilitar Visualização de ficheiro” PowerShell command into the Run dialog; this command downloads an obfuscated Visual Basic script (stage 1) that writes a second-stage downloader in %TEMP% and schedules its execution, which in turn fetches a third-stage 30–50 MB VBS stager responsible for reconnaissance (WMI AV checks, VM/sandbox detection, MD5-based victim ID Base64 exfiltration) and constructs a hostname-named .cmd file in the Startup folder to trigger system shutdown and launch a fourth-stage >700 MB DLL loader via rundll32.exe using Portuguese-named exports, although the final Lampion payload download was commented out—this dispersed, highly obfuscated multi-stage chain highlights the need for enhanced PowerShell/VBScript monitoring, advanced detection (Cortex XDR VBS Local Analysis, WildFire, URL Filtering, DNS Security) and ClickFix awareness training to thwart sophisticated banking-credential theft.
hits.title: Lampion Is Back With ClickFix Lures

ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Researchers at ThreatFabric have identified a new Android banking Trojan, Octo2—a direct descendant of Exobot (2016) and its Coper variant (2021)—now distributed across Europe (Italy, Poland, Moldova, Hungary) via trojanized APKs (Europe Enterprise com.xsusb_restore3, Google Chrome com.havirtual06numberresources, NordVPN com.handedfastee5) bound with Zombinder to masquerade as “necessary plugins.” Spawned after the public leak of Octo’s source code earlier this year, Octo2—attributed to the threat actor known as Architect/goodluck—introduces stabilized device takeover (DTO) capabilities for seamless remote actions, a DGA-based C2 framework to evade domain blocklists and takedowns, and enhanced obfuscation and anti-analysis techniques that enable invisible on-device fraud and interception of banking credentials. According to Team Cymru, Octo2 has transitioned to a Malware-as-a-Service model, offered at no extra cost to existing Octo1 customers, signaling imminent global adoption by cybercriminals. With no evidence of Google Play distribution, users are compromised via side-loading or social engineering, highlighting the urgent need for enterprises to enforce strict app-source policies, deploy advanced mobile threat defenses, and monitor anomalous behaviors to prevent unauthorized transactions and account takeovers.
hits.title: New Octo2 Android Banking Trojan Emerges with Device Takeover Capabilities

retrieved_context.text: Since mid-2016, a cyber espionage operation dubbed Magic Hound, attributed to Iranian government–linked actors including COBALT GYPSY and showing overlaps with Rocket Kitten (Operation Saffron Rose/Ajax Security Team/Operation Woolen-Goldfish) and Newscasters (Charming Kitten/NewsBeef), has targeted energy, government and technology organizations in and tied to Saudi Arabia by distributing Word and Excel documents embedding malicious macros that launch PowerShell downloaders and droppers to deploy a custom toolkit—comprising executable and document loaders, IRC bots and the multi-platform Python-based PupyRAT—for full system access and data exfiltration; analysis by Palo Alto Networks and SecureWorks revealed domain and tool reuse with the Shamoon 2 wiper campaign, and bait lures mimicking holiday greetings, job offers and official Ministry of Health and Commerce communications, underscoring the need for enhanced macro-enablement policies, network segmentation and proactive IOC monitoring of associated domains and IRC traffic.

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

retrieved_context.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. More recently, the group shifted to adversary-in-the-middle spear-phishing using a typosquatted “micsrosoftonline[.]com” domain and an Evilginx-based phishing page delivered through malicious QR codes in forged European Defense and Security Summit PDF invitations, automating bulk data collection via Exchange, Microsoft Graph and Teams web client. Overlaps with Forest Blizzard, Midnight Blizzard and Secret Blizzard indicate coordinated Russian strategic espionage, and a September 2024 pass-the-cookie breach of a Dutch police account underscores their evolving cookie-theft capabilities—highlighting urgent needs for phishing-resistant MFA and hardened Entra ID configurations.

hits.text: Lynx ransomware, a Ransomware-as-a-Service strain first seen in mid-2024 that repurposes INC source code, has targeted finance, architecture and manufacturing organizations—later expanding into energy and APAC retail—via phishing emails that deploy malware to exfiltrate sensitive data for double-extortion (including timed “drip” leaks) before encrypting files with a “.LYNX” extension; Darktrace observed initial lateral movement through SMB enumeration on port 445 and Nmap scans, exploitation of default “admin”/“administrator” credentials via NTLM and Kerberos for privilege escalation, anomalous internal transfers of ~150 GiB over port 3260 and large uploads to wt-prod-euwest1-storm.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com, plus AnyDesk-based remote sessions to aid operator actions, culminating in thousands of encrypted files detected by parallel SMB read/write anomalies and extension appends—Darktrace’s Autonomous Response models, if fully enabled, would automatically block suspicious SMB activity, unusual privileged user behavior and anomalous outbound connections to contain the threat and preserve business continuity.
hits.title: New Threat on the Prowl: Investigating Lynx Ransomware
