hits.text: Since at least September 2023, the China-aligned Evasive Panda APT (aka BRONZE HIGHLAND/Daggerfly) has conducted a dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora by compromising both the Kagyu International Monlam Trust’s website and the official Monlam translation-software supply chain—first implanting obfuscated JavaScript into jquery.js on the festival site that verifies victims’ first three IP octets via an MD5 hash salted with “1qaz0okm!@#,” serves a faux “Aw, Snap!” error page to users in India, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Australia and the U.S., and lures them to download a malicious “certificate.exe” or “.pkg” downloader; that loader side-loads memmgrset.dll (http_dy.dll) to fetch a JSON config from update.devicebug[.]com and ultimately deploys the undocumented Nightdoor backdoor alongside the group’s modular MgBot implant, while a trojanized Monlam software installer (Windows autorun.exe abusing MonlamUpdate.exe for DLL side-loading of RPHost.dll, and macOS Mach-O downloaders) has delivered further downloaders and payloads—retrieved from tibetpost[.]net and a direct IP—to %TEMP%\default_ico.exe for additional Nightdoor and MgBot installation.

harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

retrieved_context.text: Since mid-2016, a cyber espionage operation dubbed Magic Hound, attributed to Iranian government–linked actors including COBALT GYPSY and showing overlaps with Rocket Kitten (Operation Saffron Rose/Ajax Security Team/Operation Woolen-Goldfish) and Newscasters (Charming Kitten/NewsBeef), has targeted energy, government and technology organizations in and tied to Saudi Arabia by distributing Word and Excel documents embedding malicious macros that launch PowerShell downloaders and droppers to deploy a custom toolkit—comprising executable and document loaders, IRC bots and the multi-platform Python-based PupyRAT—for full system access and data exfiltration; analysis by Palo Alto Networks and SecureWorks revealed domain and tool reuse with the Shamoon 2 wiper campaign, and bait lures mimicking holiday greetings, job offers and official Ministry of Health and Commerce communications, underscoring the need for enhanced macro-enablement policies, network segmentation and proactive IOC monitoring of associated domains and IRC traffic.
retrieved_context.title: Iranian hackers behind the Magic Hound campaign linked to Shamoon

canonical_entities: Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of the Interior
retrieved_context.text: Moses Staff, also dubbed Cobalt Sapling, is an Iran-linked APT active since November 2020 and publicly identified in September 2021, originally posting 16 leak events of Israeli corporate data and personal information of IDF intelligence personnel by December 2022 using a toolkit comprising the PyDCrypt custom loader, DCSrv cryptographic wiper, StrifeWater RAT and its DriveGuard monitoring utility; in November 2022, Secureworks attributed a new hacktivist persona, Abraham’s Ax—featuring similar biblical branding, Tor-hosted leak sites on adjacent subnets and recycled “Hollywood-style” hacking videos—to the same operators, who have since shifted toward exfiltrating and leaking data from Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of the Interior (including a purported intercepted ministerial phone conversation) rather than directly attacking Israel, likely in response to Saudi-Israeli rapprochement, while Moses Staff continues operations (claiming a CCTV system hack at an Israeli terror site); these insights highlight the urgency for Saudi and Israeli government entities to strengthen network segmentation, deploy advanced endpoint detection for known Iranian toolsets, monitor darknet leak platforms and prepare incident response plans tailored to politically motivated exfiltration campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Iranian APT Leaks Data From Saudi Arabia Government Under New Persona

retrieved_context.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. More recently, the group shifted to adversary-in-the-middle spear-phishing using a typosquatted “micsrosoftonline[.]com” domain and an Evilginx-based phishing page delivered through malicious QR codes in forged European Defense and Security Summit PDF invitations, automating bulk data collection via Exchange, Microsoft Graph and Teams web client. Overlaps with Forest Blizzard, Midnight Blizzard and Secret Blizzard indicate coordinated Russian strategic espionage, and a September 2024 pass-the-cookie breach of a Dutch police account underscores their evolving cookie-theft capabilities—highlighting urgent needs for phishing-resistant MFA and hardened Entra ID configurations.
retrieved_context.title: Russian Hackers Breach 20+ NGOs Using Evilginx Phishing via Fake Microsoft Entra Pages

retrieved_context.text: Lynx ransomware, a Ransomware-as-a-Service strain first seen in mid-2024 that repurposes INC source code, has targeted finance, architecture and manufacturing organizations—later expanding into energy and APAC retail—via phishing emails that deploy malware to exfiltrate sensitive data for double-extortion (including timed “drip” leaks) before encrypting files with a “.LYNX” extension; Darktrace observed initial lateral movement through SMB enumeration on port 445 and Nmap scans, exploitation of default “admin”/“administrator” credentials via NTLM and Kerberos for privilege escalation, anomalous internal transfers of ~150 GiB over port 3260 and large uploads to wt-prod-euwest1-storm.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com, plus AnyDesk-based remote sessions to aid operator actions, culminating in thousands of encrypted files detected by parallel SMB read/write anomalies and extension appends—Darktrace’s Autonomous Response models, if fully enabled, would automatically block suspicious SMB activity, unusual privileged user behavior and anomalous outbound connections to contain the threat and preserve business continuity.
retrieved_context.title: New Threat on the Prowl: Investigating Lynx Ransomware

retrieved_context.text: In August 2025 Microsoft Threat Intelligence revealed that Storm-2460, associated with the Play ransomware group, has resumed exploiting CVE-2025-29824—a zero-day elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Common Log File System patched in April—to gain SYSTEM privileges on unpatched hosts across IT, financial and real estate organizations in the US, Europe, South America and the Middle East. The campaign begins with an in-memory dropper masquerading as the open-source ChatGPT Desktop app that decrypts and launches PipeMagic, a modular backdoor first observed in December 2022 and now updated with persistence and lateral-movement enhancements targeting Saudi Arabian and Brazilian manufacturing entities. PipeMagic communicates with its TCP C2 over a named pipe, self-updates by storing distinct payload modules in memory via doubly linked lists for staging, execution and communication (plus an additional dynamic list), then leverages the CLFS exploit to escalate privileges before deploying Play ransomware. Although the campaign’s footprint remains limited, the combination of a zero-day exploit and a sophisticated modular backdoor underscores a heightened risk; organizations are urged to immediately apply the April patch for CVE-2025-29824, enable tamper and network protection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, run EDR in block mode, enforce full automated investigation and remediation, and leverage cloud-delivered machine-learning protections to block novel variants.
retrieved_context.title: PipeMagic Backdoor Resurfaces as Part of Play Ransomware Attack Chain

canonical_entities: dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora
retrieved_context.text: Since at least September 2023, the China-aligned Evasive Panda APT (aka BRONZE HIGHLAND/Daggerfly) has conducted a dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora by compromising both the Kagyu International Monlam Trust’s website and the official Monlam translation-software supply chain—first implanting obfuscated JavaScript into jquery.js on the festival site that verifies victims’ first three IP octets via an MD5 hash salted with “1qaz0okm!@#,” serves a faux “Aw, Snap!” error page to users in India, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Australia and the U.S., and lures them to download a malicious “certificate.exe” or “.pkg” downloader; that loader side-loads memmgrset.dll (http_dy.dll) to fetch a JSON config from update.devicebug[.]com and ultimately deploys the undocumented Nightdoor backdoor alongside the group’s modular MgBot implant, while a trojanized Monlam software installer (Windows autorun.exe abusing MonlamUpdate.exe for DLL side-loading of RPHost.dll, and macOS Mach-O downloaders) has delivered further downloaders and payloads—retrieved from tibetpost[.]net and a direct IP—to %TEMP%\default_ico.exe for additional Nightdoor and MgBot installation.
retrieved_context.title: Evasive Panda leverages Monlam Festival to target Tibetans

retrieved_context.text: Unit 42 researchers uncovered a targeted Lampion infostealer campaign in late 2024–early 2025 against Portuguese government, finance and transportation organizations that reuses infrastructure and TTPs dating back to 2019 while introducing ClickFix social-engineering lures—victims receive a phishing email with a malicious ZIP attachment containing an HTML redirect to autoridade-tributaria[.]com, where they are duped into copying a “#Habilitar Visualização de ficheiro” PowerShell command into the Run dialog; this command downloads an obfuscated Visual Basic script (stage 1) that writes a second-stage downloader in %TEMP% and schedules its execution, which in turn fetches a third-stage 30–50 MB VBS stager responsible for reconnaissance (WMI AV checks, VM/sandbox detection, MD5-based victim ID Base64 exfiltration) and constructs a hostname-named .cmd file in the Startup folder to trigger system shutdown and launch a fourth-stage >700 MB DLL loader via rundll32.exe using Portuguese-named exports, although the final Lampion payload download was commented out—this dispersed, highly obfuscated multi-stage chain highlights the need for enhanced PowerShell/VBScript monitoring, advanced detection (Cortex XDR VBS Local Analysis, WildFire, URL Filtering, DNS Security) and ClickFix awareness training to thwart sophisticated banking-credential theft.
retrieved_context.title: Lampion Is Back With ClickFix Lures

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since at least 2019, China-linked Winnti APT (aka APT41/BARIUM/Blackfly) has run the stealthy CuckooBees campaign against technology and manufacturing firms in North America, Europe, and Asia to support Beijing’s Made in China 2025 initiative, exploiting ERP platform vulnerabilities for initial access and deploying a “house of cards” kill chain—including an undocumented Deploylog backdoor and updated Winnti malware concealed via rare Windows CLFS abuse—to maintain persistence through a VBScript WebShell (up_win32.jsp variant), modified WinRM HTTP(S) listeners, a signed kernel rootkit, and side-loaded DLLs via IKEEXT and PrintNotify services; after reconnaissance with built-in Windows commands, attackers stole credentials using reg save to dump SYSTEM/SAM/SECURITY hives and a custom MFSDLL.exe loader of mktzx64.dll, leveraged stolen domain admin rights and scheduled tasks for lateral movement, then exfiltrated hundreds of gigabytes of proprietary data in password-protected WinRAR archives renamed as rundll32.exe; Cybereason’s discovery underscores the need to patch ERP systems, monitor unusual CLFS writes and service modifications, detect script-based web shells, scrutinize registry hive exports, review scheduled-task anomalies, and flag renamed archival tools to thwart similar state-sponsored espionage.
hits.title: China-Linked Winnti APT Group Silently Stole Trade Secrets for Years: Report

hits.text: Security researchers at Cybereason uncovered that since at least 2019 a Chinese state-sponsored APT group known as Winnti (also tracked as APT41, Barium, Wicked Panda, Axiom) has been running “Operation CuckooBees,” a multi-year, multi-stage espionage campaign targeting technology and manufacturing firms across Asia, Europe and North America to steal hundreds of gigabytes of trade secrets. The attackers exploited both known and zero-day RCE flaws in a popular ERP platform to deploy JSP web shells, enabled WinRM for persistence, dumped registry-stored credentials to move laterally via scheduled tasks, and used a sophisticated loader chain—Spyder Loader (disguised as SQLite3 DLL), STASHLOG (which hides payloads in Windows’ proprietary CLFS logs), SPARKLOG (which extracts and side-loads PRIVATELOG via DLL hijacking for SYSTEM privileges), and DEPLOYLOG (which abuses Transactional NTFS to overwrite dbghelp.dll and hijack the AMD K8 kernel driver)—to install WINNKIT, a kernel-level rootkit signed with a stolen BenQ certificate that hooks TCP/IP at the NIC to receive commands for shell execution, file enumeration, SOCKS5 proxy, RDP and process control, all while evading detection for years.
hits.title: Chinese APT group Winnti stole trade secrets in years-long undetected campaign

hits.text: Avast researchers uncovered that North Korea’s Lazarus group leveraged a Windows zero-day privilege escalation flaw in Microsoft’s AppLocker “appid.sys” driver (CVE-2024-21338) to execute a truly fileless kernel attack during 2023 intrusions, sending a proof-of-concept exploit to Microsoft in August and prompting a February 2024 patch and subsequent advisory update once active exploitation was confirmed; by abusing a ubiquitous signed driver rather than importing custom code (BYOVD), Lazarus gained kernel read/write primitives, manipulated kernel objects to deploy an enhanced FudModule rootkit—now capable of evading AhnLab V3, Defender, CrowdStrike Falcon and HitmanPro—and bypassed driver allowlisting, then deployed a new remote access trojan for persistent access, underscoring the need for immediate patching, vigilant driver integrity monitoring and behavior-based detection to thwart stealthy, living-off-the-land attacks.
hits.title: Windows Zero-Day Exploited by North Korean Hackers in Rootkit Attack - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Symantec has warned that extortion actors, notably the Clop ransomware operation (aka Snakefly/TA505/FIN11), have been exploiting a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability in the MOVEit Transfer web application (CVE-2023-34362) since May 27, 2023, enabling supply-chain attacks across multiple organizations; although first patched on May 31, additional vulnerabilities (CVEs pending) were disclosed on June 9. Attackers deploy a bespoke web shell, Lemurloot (detected as JS.Malscript!g1, Trojan.Gen.2, WS.Malware), to authenticate via hard-coded credentials, execute SQL statements to alter or delete database elements, exfiltrate records and Azure settings, and manipulate user accounts. With proof-of-concept code now public, secondary threat actors face elevated risk of exploitation and data theft. Clop has since threatened data leaks unless ransoms are paid, reflecting its shift from encryption to extortion. Symantec mitigations include file-based and ML detections, network-based attack signatures, and Data Center Security policy controls that harden MS SQL, IIS and sandbox environments to prevent web-shell deployment and unauthorized software execution.
hits.title: MOVEit Vulnerabilities: What You Need to Know | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: harvest subscriber location, billing and communications metadata
hits.text: On Sept. 25, 2024, the Wall Street Journal disclosed that the Chinese state-sponsored APT Salt Typhoon has stealthily infiltrated multiple U.S. cable and broadband ISPs—likely via firmware and supply-chain compromises in core networking gear—to establish long-term persistence, harvest subscriber location, billing and communications metadata for espionage, and pre-position disruptive capabilities against federal, military and Fortune 100 users; this campaign, echoing Volt Typhoon’s telecom backdoors, Flax Typhoon’s 200,000-device IoT botnet, Brass Typhoon’s cross-domain implants and Mustang Panda’s telco intrusions, signals a shift from surveillance to offensive “blink-the-lights” or infrastructure-crippling attacks in a Taiwan contingency, driving urgent recommendations for carriers to enforce threat-intelligence sharing, secure firmware, tighten supply-chain controls and bolster routing security.
hits.title: China's 'Salt Typhoon' Cooks Up Cyberattacks on US ISPs

hits.text: Sea Turtle, also known as Cosmic Wolf, Marbled Dust, Teal Kurma and UNC1326, has been conducting a stealthy, Türkiye-linked cyber espionage campaign since at least January 2017, recently targeting Dutch ISPs, telecom, IT-service and media providers as well as Kurdish websites via supply-chain and island-hopping attacks to harvest politically sensitive personal data and potential dissident communications. First detailed by Cisco Talos in April 2019 for state-sponsored DNS hijacking to redirect legitimate domain queries to attacker-controlled servers, the group elevated its upstream foothold tactics in late 2021 by exploiting known telecom and IT vulnerabilities across Armenia, Cyprus, Greece, Iraq and Syria, per Microsoft. Between 2021 and 2023 PwC observed deployment of “SnappyTCP,” a simple Linux/Unix reverse-TCP web shell (with and without OpenSSL/TLS) for persistence and C2, and Hunt & Hackett’s 2023 incident revealed credential-theft via a compromised cPanel account used to deploy SnappyTCP, tar and expose email archives publicly for direct exfiltration. Organizations should enforce strong password policies, 2FA, login-rate limiting, SSH monitoring and timely patching to mitigate this ongoing espionage threat.
hits.title: Sea Turtle Cyber Espionage Campaign Targets Dutch IT and Telecom Companies

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
hits.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
hits.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment
hits.text: In November 2023, Russian state-sponsored group Nobelium (aka Midnight Blizzard/APT29) executed a month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment by conducting a password-spray brute-force attack against a legacy non-production test tenant lacking multi-factor authentication, enabling pivoting to a small subset of high-value accounts—including leadership, cybersecurity and legal team mailboxes—from which they exfiltrated emails and attachments; discovered on January 12, 2024, the campaign underscores the risk of poorly secured account configurations rather than software vulnerabilities, prompting Microsoft to notify impacted employees, reaffirm its MFA mandate, and reinforce zero-trust controls. This incident, following Nobelium’s SolarWinds and 2021 support-tool intrusions, highlights the necessity of enforcing MFA, minimizing default permissions, and hardening non-prod assets to mitigate advanced persistent threats.
hits.title: Russian hackers stole Microsoft corporate emails in month-long breach

The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment
retrieved_context.text: In November 2023, Russian state-sponsored group Nobelium (aka Midnight Blizzard/APT29) executed a month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment by conducting a password-spray brute-force attack against a legacy non-production test tenant lacking multi-factor authentication, enabling pivoting to a small subset of high-value accounts—including leadership, cybersecurity and legal team mailboxes—from which they exfiltrated emails and attachments; discovered on January 12, 2024, the campaign underscores the risk of poorly secured account configurations rather than software vulnerabilities, prompting Microsoft to notify impacted employees, reaffirm its MFA mandate, and reinforce zero-trust controls. This incident, following Nobelium’s SolarWinds and 2021 support-tool intrusions, highlights the necessity of enforcing MFA, minimizing default permissions, and hardening non-prod assets to mitigate advanced persistent threats.
retrieved_context.title: Russian hackers stole Microsoft corporate emails in month-long breach

hits.text: Since at least 2019, China-linked Winnti APT (aka APT41/BARIUM/Blackfly) has run the stealthy CuckooBees campaign against technology and manufacturing firms in North America, Europe, and Asia to support Beijing’s Made in China 2025 initiative, exploiting ERP platform vulnerabilities for initial access and deploying a “house of cards” kill chain—including an undocumented Deploylog backdoor and updated Winnti malware concealed via rare Windows CLFS abuse—to maintain persistence through a VBScript WebShell (up_win32.jsp variant), modified WinRM HTTP(S) listeners, a signed kernel rootkit, and side-loaded DLLs via IKEEXT and PrintNotify services; after reconnaissance with built-in Windows commands, attackers stole credentials using reg save to dump SYSTEM/SAM/SECURITY hives and a custom MFSDLL.exe loader of mktzx64.dll, leveraged stolen domain admin rights and scheduled tasks for lateral movement, then exfiltrated hundreds of gigabytes of proprietary data in password-protected WinRAR archives renamed as rundll32.exe; Cybereason’s discovery underscores the need to patch ERP systems, monitor unusual CLFS writes and service modifications, detect script-based web shells, scrutinize registry hive exports, review scheduled-task anomalies, and flag renamed archival tools to thwart similar state-sponsored espionage.

hits.text: Security researchers at Cybereason uncovered that since at least 2019 a Chinese state-sponsored APT group known as Winnti (also tracked as APT41, Barium, Wicked Panda, Axiom) has been running “Operation CuckooBees,” a multi-year, multi-stage espionage campaign targeting technology and manufacturing firms across Asia, Europe and North America to steal hundreds of gigabytes of trade secrets. The attackers exploited both known and zero-day RCE flaws in a popular ERP platform to deploy JSP web shells, enabled WinRM for persistence, dumped registry-stored credentials to move laterally via scheduled tasks, and used a sophisticated loader chain—Spyder Loader (disguised as SQLite3 DLL), STASHLOG (which hides payloads in Windows’ proprietary CLFS logs), SPARKLOG (which extracts and side-loads PRIVATELOG via DLL hijacking for SYSTEM privileges), and DEPLOYLOG (which abuses Transactional NTFS to overwrite dbghelp.dll and hijack the AMD K8 kernel driver)—to install WINNKIT, a kernel-level rootkit signed with a stolen BenQ certificate that hooks TCP/IP at the NIC to receive commands for shell execution, file enumeration, SOCKS5 proxy, RDP and process control, all while evading detection for years.
hits.title: Chinese APT group Winnti stole trade secrets in years-long undetected campaign

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
hits.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

canonical_entities: inject the decoded first-stage shellcode into legitimate processes
hits.text: In September 2024, a Winnti-linked APT began targeting trading and brokerage firms by distributing malicious .scr/.pif screen saver files via Skype that use steganographically embedded shellcode to load GodRAT—a new Gh0st RAT variant evolved from the AwesomePuppet backdoor—into legitimate processes. Two loader types (one with XOR-encoded shellcode bytes, one extracting shellcode from JPG images via an expired Valve.exe/SDL2.dll signed binary) allocate memory, inject the decoded first-stage shellcode, decode configuration data (single-byte XOR key 0x63, “godinfo” header), and fetch a UPX-packed GodRAT DLL from C2. GodRAT launches under a “-Puppet” flag in curl.exe or cmd.exe, collects OS, host, AV, process and user metadata, and communicates over zlib-compressed, triple-XOR TCP channels. It supports in-memory plugin injection—deploying a FileManager plugin for file enumeration, manipulation and 7zip-based extraction—and installs Chrome and Edge password stealers in %ALLUSERSPROFILE%. AsyncRAT serves as a secondary fallback implant. Ongoing detections (12 MD5s across Hong Kong, UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia) through August 12 2025 highlight sustained financial credential theft and long-term C2 persistence.
hits.title: Gh0st RAT-based GodRAT attacks financial organizations

hits.text: New research reveals that over 80,000 Hikvision cameras worldwide remain unpatched against the critical CVE-2021-36260 command-injection flaw (NIST score 9.8/10) disclosed last fall, allowing remote code execution and potential espionage by state-linked groups such as MISSION2025/APT41, APT10 and unknown Russian actors trading stolen credentials on dark-web forums; systemic deficiencies—default or hardcoded passwords, no auto-update mechanism, poor forensics and lack of security-by-design—have left devices in 100+ countries (including the U.S., despite an FCC “unacceptable risk” designation) continuously discoverable via Shodan or Censys and ripe for exploitation, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to inventory IoT assets, change default credentials, deploy available patches and improve visibility and update processes to mitigate geopolitical and operational impact.
hits.title: Cybercriminals Are Selling Access to Chinese Surveillance Cameras | Threatpost

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
hits.text: On March 2, 2025, CyberMaterial’s report on Void Manticore (aka Storm-0842, linked to the cybercriminal Storm-1811 cluster) details a coordinated espionage campaign that began in late 2024 against aerospace, defense and government organizations in Europe and North America: operators initiated intrusions via spear-phishing emails embedding weaponized RTFs exploiting CVE-2024-4113 to drop a custom loader (“VoidLoader”), which in turn deployed the “ManticoreShell” backdoor; post-compromise activities included credential harvesting (Mimikatz), lateral movement via PSExec and WMI, privilege escalation through a signed kernel-mode driver exploit, and persistence using registry Run keys and scheduled tasks; C2 communications leveraged HTTPS with a domain generation algorithm (DGA) and fallback to TOR. Over a three-month window they compromised at least 15 organizations, exfiltrated more than 20 GB of intellectual property, and triggered system outages exceeding 48 hours in critical environments. Key mitigation measures include immediate patching of CVE-2024-4113, deployment of EDR solutions to detect anomalous IOCTL and PowerShell activity, network segmentation to contain lateral movement, strict monitoring of DGA-style DNS queries, and implementation of multi-factor authentication to thwart credential abuse.
hits.title: Void Manticore (Storm-0842) – Threat Actor - CyberMaterial

hits.text: Since mid-September, unknown cybercriminals have been conducting large-scale brute-force attacks against internet-exposed instances of Foundation Accounting Software—widely used by construction sub-industries such as plumbing, HVAC and concrete—by targeting the default “sa” administrator and a second high-privilege account within the MSSQL database accessible via TCP port 4243 (opened for Foundation’s mobile app). After an observed peak of roughly 35,000 rapid login attempts to obtain valid credentials, the attackers enable an extended stored procedure (e.g., xp_cmdshell) to execute OS-level commands and scripts, automating lateral movement and data theft across multiple unrelated victims. Huntress has identified just 33 hosts left with unchanged default passwords, alerted all impacted and at-risk customers, and urges organizations to rotate all Foundation credentials, remove direct internet exposure, and disable the exploited stored procedure to mitigate further compromise.
hits.title: Threat Actors Target Accounting Software Used by Construction Contractors - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Evil Corp–linked operators began by abusing the open-source Responder tool to poison LLMNR and NBT-NS name-resolution queries on Windows hosts, harvesting NTLMv2 hashes and cleartext credentials, then used pass-the-hash techniques alongside PSExec and WMI for rapid lateral movement and privilege escalation to domain admin; once established, they deployed WastedLocker ransomware via scheduled tasks, encrypting over 95% of critical servers and workstations with AES-256, causing 72 hours of operational downtime and a $10 million ransom demand. Cynet’s automated threat detection flagged abnormal name-resolution traffic and excessive SMB authentication failures, enabling immediate host isolation, credential resets, and network segmentation. Key mitigations include disabling LLMNR/NBT-NS, enforcing SMB signing, monitoring NTLM authentication events, and strictly enforcing least-privilege service accounts to prevent similar intrusions.
hits.title: Cynet | Threat Detection Report: Wastedlocker Ransomware

PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.

retrieved_context.text: Since at least 2019, China-linked Winnti APT (aka APT41/BARIUM/Blackfly) has run the stealthy CuckooBees campaign against technology and manufacturing firms in North America, Europe, and Asia to support Beijing’s Made in China 2025 initiative, exploiting ERP platform vulnerabilities for initial access and deploying a “house of cards” kill chain—including an undocumented Deploylog backdoor and updated Winnti malware concealed via rare Windows CLFS abuse—to maintain persistence through a VBScript WebShell (up_win32.jsp variant), modified WinRM HTTP(S) listeners, a signed kernel rootkit, and side-loaded DLLs via IKEEXT and PrintNotify services; after reconnaissance with built-in Windows commands, attackers stole credentials using reg save to dump SYSTEM/SAM/SECURITY hives and a custom MFSDLL.exe loader of mktzx64.dll, leveraged stolen domain admin rights and scheduled tasks for lateral movement, then exfiltrated hundreds of gigabytes of proprietary data in password-protected WinRAR archives renamed as rundll32.exe; Cybereason’s discovery underscores the need to patch ERP systems, monitor unusual CLFS writes and service modifications, detect script-based web shells, scrutinize registry hive exports, review scheduled-task anomalies, and flag renamed archival tools to thwart similar state-sponsored espionage.
retrieved_context.title: China-Linked Winnti APT Group Silently Stole Trade Secrets for Years: Report

retrieved_context.text: Security researchers at Cybereason uncovered that since at least 2019 a Chinese state-sponsored APT group known as Winnti (also tracked as APT41, Barium, Wicked Panda, Axiom) has been running “Operation CuckooBees,” a multi-year, multi-stage espionage campaign targeting technology and manufacturing firms across Asia, Europe and North America to steal hundreds of gigabytes of trade secrets. The attackers exploited both known and zero-day RCE flaws in a popular ERP platform to deploy JSP web shells, enabled WinRM for persistence, dumped registry-stored credentials to move laterally via scheduled tasks, and used a sophisticated loader chain—Spyder Loader (disguised as SQLite3 DLL), STASHLOG (which hides payloads in Windows’ proprietary CLFS logs), SPARKLOG (which extracts and side-loads PRIVATELOG via DLL hijacking for SYSTEM privileges), and DEPLOYLOG (which abuses Transactional NTFS to overwrite dbghelp.dll and hijack the AMD K8 kernel driver)—to install WINNKIT, a kernel-level rootkit signed with a stolen BenQ certificate that hooks TCP/IP at the NIC to receive commands for shell execution, file enumeration, SOCKS5 proxy, RDP and process control, all while evading detection for years.
retrieved_context.title: Chinese APT group Winnti stole trade secrets in years-long undetected campaign

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
retrieved_context.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
retrieved_context.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: inject the decoded first-stage shellcode into legitimate processes
retrieved_context.text: In September 2024, a Winnti-linked APT began targeting trading and brokerage firms by distributing malicious .scr/.pif screen saver files via Skype that use steganographically embedded shellcode to load GodRAT—a new Gh0st RAT variant evolved from the AwesomePuppet backdoor—into legitimate processes. Two loader types (one with XOR-encoded shellcode bytes, one extracting shellcode from JPG images via an expired Valve.exe/SDL2.dll signed binary) allocate memory, inject the decoded first-stage shellcode, decode configuration data (single-byte XOR key 0x63, “godinfo” header), and fetch a UPX-packed GodRAT DLL from C2. GodRAT launches under a “-Puppet” flag in curl.exe or cmd.exe, collects OS, host, AV, process and user metadata, and communicates over zlib-compressed, triple-XOR TCP channels. It supports in-memory plugin injection—deploying a FileManager plugin for file enumeration, manipulation and 7zip-based extraction—and installs Chrome and Edge password stealers in %ALLUSERSPROFILE%. AsyncRAT serves as a secondary fallback implant. Ongoing detections (12 MD5s across Hong Kong, UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia) through August 12 2025 highlight sustained financial credential theft and long-term C2 persistence.
retrieved_context.title: Gh0st RAT-based GodRAT attacks financial organizations

retrieved_context.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
retrieved_context.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

canonical_entities: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
retrieved_context.text: On March 2, 2025, CyberMaterial’s report on Void Manticore (aka Storm-0842, linked to the cybercriminal Storm-1811 cluster) details a coordinated espionage campaign that began in late 2024 against aerospace, defense and government organizations in Europe and North America: operators initiated intrusions via spear-phishing emails embedding weaponized RTFs exploiting CVE-2024-4113 to drop a custom loader (“VoidLoader”), which in turn deployed the “ManticoreShell” backdoor; post-compromise activities included credential harvesting (Mimikatz), lateral movement via PSExec and WMI, privilege escalation through a signed kernel-mode driver exploit, and persistence using registry Run keys and scheduled tasks; C2 communications leveraged HTTPS with a domain generation algorithm (DGA) and fallback to TOR. Over a three-month window they compromised at least 15 organizations, exfiltrated more than 20 GB of intellectual property, and triggered system outages exceeding 48 hours in critical environments. Key mitigation measures include immediate patching of CVE-2024-4113, deployment of EDR solutions to detect anomalous IOCTL and PowerShell activity, network segmentation to contain lateral movement, strict monitoring of DGA-style DNS queries, and implementation of multi-factor authentication to thwart credential abuse.
retrieved_context.title: Void Manticore (Storm-0842) – Threat Actor - CyberMaterial

canonical_entities: registered variables in the Windows Registry
retrieved_context.text: In June 2024, HP’s Threat Research team led by Patrick Schlapfer intercepted a low-grade phishing campaign leveraging HTML smuggling via an AES-encrypted HTML attachment containing JavaScript-embedded decryption logic—a novel twist on typical encrypted archives—which, when decrypted, mimicked a legitimate website but dropped a fully commented, French-language VBScript that registered variables in the Windows Registry, staged a JavaScript payload as a scheduled task, and invoked a PowerShell script to deploy the freely available AsyncRAT infostealer. Schlapfer and co-lead Alex Holland’s analysis, including comparison with generative-AI–produced code, concluded the well-structured, human-readable script was likely authored by gen-AI by a low-skill newcomer benefitting from reduced entry barriers, with no obfuscation or complex infrastructure beyond a single C2 server. This first definitive proof of AI-generated malware in the wild underscores the need for defenders to adapt detection strategies to AI-crafted droppers, monitor anomalous AES-in-JavaScript decryption patterns, and anticipate more sophisticated AI-generated payloads poised to emerge within the next two years, thereby heightening the risk to network and endpoint security.
retrieved_context.title: AI-Generated Malware Found in the Wild - SecurityWeek

retrieved_context.text: New research reveals that over 80,000 Hikvision cameras worldwide remain unpatched against the critical CVE-2021-36260 command-injection flaw (NIST score 9.8/10) disclosed last fall, allowing remote code execution and potential espionage by state-linked groups such as MISSION2025/APT41, APT10 and unknown Russian actors trading stolen credentials on dark-web forums; systemic deficiencies—default or hardcoded passwords, no auto-update mechanism, poor forensics and lack of security-by-design—have left devices in 100+ countries (including the U.S., despite an FCC “unacceptable risk” designation) continuously discoverable via Shodan or Censys and ripe for exploitation, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to inventory IoT assets, change default credentials, deploy available patches and improve visibility and update processes to mitigate geopolitical and operational impact.
retrieved_context.title: Cybercriminals Are Selling Access to Chinese Surveillance Cameras | Threatpost

canonical_entities: regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea
hits.text: In early 2018 McAfee Advanced Threat Research uncovered Operation Honeybee, a North Korean–linked campaign—tracked to the persona snoopykiller@mail.ru and control domains navermail.byethost3.com/nihon.byethost11.com—targeting humanitarian aid groups and regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea with malicious Microsoft Word documents named “Honeybee” that exploited politically themed and generic “not compatible” lures to execute VBA macros embedding a custom‐alphabet Base64 payload. Beginning January 15, these macros dropped CAB archives to %TEMP%, used wusa.exe or expand.exe for UAC bypass, then hijacked cliconfg.exe via a malicious NTWDBLIB.dll to install a persistent COMSysApp service loading ipnet.dll from %SystemRoot%\System32. The implant gathers systeminfo and tasklist outputs, packages them into Base64‐encoded ZIPs, and exfiltrates data to FTP servers (e.g., 1113427185.ifastnet.org), while also supporting remote commands (pull, chip, put, user execution). A related Win32 dropper, MaoCheng—signed with a stolen Adobe certificate—demonstrated a tactical shift with Xero lures and test-phase bugs. This operation’s technical sophistication and evolving decoy tactics underscore a sustained threat to critical NGO networks, resulting in persistent backdoors and unauthorized data extraction.
hits.title: McAfee Uncovers Operation Honeybee, a Malicious Campaign Targeting Humanitarian Aid Groups | McAfee Blog

hits.text: CISA has added CVE-2022-22047—a high-severity (CVSS 7.8) elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Client Server Runtime Subsystem used since Windows 7 through Windows 11 and Server 2008–2022—to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and is urging federal agencies to install Microsoft’s July 5 Patch Tuesday update by August 2 after evidence emerged of in-the-wild exploitation; initially disclosed as a zero-day by Microsoft’s security team, the CSRSS bug enables adversaries who already hold local or physical access—or who gain remote code execution via malware or specially crafted Office/Adobe documents and macros—to escalate to SYSTEM privileges for lateral movement, although FortiGuard Labs rates the overall business threat as “medium” given the prerequisite foothold and available patch, while Trend Micro’s ZDI notes such elevation flaws are typically paired with a separate RCE vector and Microsoft has signaled future default blocking of VBA macros to mitigate this attack chain.
hits.title: CISA Urges Patch of Exploited Windows 11 Bug by Aug. 2 | Threatpost

hits.text: Operation RoundPress, attributed with medium confidence to Russian state-sponsored APT28 (Fancy Bear), has since 2023 exploited stored and reflected XSS flaws in widely used webmail platforms—initially leveraging Roundcube CVE-2020-35730 to inject malicious JavaScript into email bodies, then CVE-2023-43770 and additional n-day vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra in early 2024—to execute upon email open without clicks or redirects. Through spear-phishing emails crafted with timely political or news excerpts, the hidden script auto-fills victim credentials via invisible input fields, scrapes DOM content—including emails, contacts, webmail settings, login history, 2FA tokens and passwords—and exfiltrates data via HTTP POST to hardcoded C2 servers. Targets span high-value government entities in Greece, Ukraine, Serbia and Cameroon, military units in Ukraine and Ecuador, defense contractors in Ukraine, Bulgaria and Romania, and critical infrastructure in Ukraine and Bulgaria. The lack of persistence mechanisms confines execution to session scope but underscores the necessity for timely patching of XSS vulnerabilities, disabling HTML rendering in webmail clients, enforcing strict input sanitization and multifactor authentication, and monitoring anomalous outbound traffic to mitigate credential theft and data exfiltration.
hits.title: Government webmail hacked via XSS bugs in global spy campaign

hits.text: In February 2022, CISA, the FBI, US Cyber Command CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA issued a joint advisory on Iranian Ministry of Intelligence–linked APT MuddyWater (aka MERCURY, Earth Vetala, Static Kitten, Seedworm, TEMP.Zagros), active since 2018 and focused on cyber espionage, intellectual property theft and ransomware against defense, oil & gas, government and telecom sectors across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America. Exploiting publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and open-source tools, MuddyWater delivers malicious PDFs with embedded links that display error messages prompting users to download Excel maldocs or Windows executables; these files host VBA macros that drop WSF scripts to execute PowerShell and VB payloads, leverage LoLBins, and stage RATs and malware families including PowGoop, Canopy, Small Sieve, POWERSTATS and Mori while communicating with C2 over HTTP and DNS and persisting via Registry Run keys. Cisco Talos observed regional campaigns in Turkey (Nov 2021), Pakistan (Aug 2021) and Armenia (Jun 2021) using decoy documents, signaling tokens and a consistent TTP set, suggesting a conglomerate of subgroups migrating techniques across regions. The resultant network access and data exfiltration underscore the imperative for proactive DFIR readiness, deployment of XDR/MDR platforms, rigorous vulnerability management, macro execution restrictions, PowerShell/LoLBin monitoring and ongoing user awareness training reinforced by incident response tabletop exercises.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at Iranian APT "MuddyWater"

hits.text: CISA has added CVE-2024-7593, a critical (CVSS 9.8) authentication-bypass flaw in Ivanti Virtual Traffic Manager (vTM) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog amid evidence of active exploitation and a public proof-of-concept, enabling remote attackers to bypass the admin panel and create rogue administrative users; Ivanti released patches in August 2024 for vTM versions 22.2R1, 22.3R3, 22.5R2, 22.6R2 and 22.7R2, and Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies must remediate by October 15, 2024. This alert follows active exploitation of CVE-2024-8190 and CVE-2024-8963 against a limited number of customers, while Censys data reveals 2,017 exposed Ivanti Cloud Service Appliance instances (predominantly U.S.), underscoring the need for immediate patch deployment, asset inventory and monitoring for unauthorized admin activity to prevent network compromise.
hits.title: CISA Flags Critical Ivanti vTM Vulnerability Amid Active Exploitation Concerns

hits.text: ESET researchers uncovered the Iran-aligned APT35 (aka Ballistic Bobcat, Charming Kitten, TA453/PHOSPHORUS) deploying a novel Sponsor backdoor across at least 34 opportunistic victims—primarily Israeli organizations in sectors from automotive to telecommunications, plus medical targets in Brazil and the UAE—by scanning for and exploiting Exchange CVE-2021-26855 vulnerabilities since September 2021, wrapping up their CISA AA21-321A/PowerLess campaign before dropping Sponsor via innocuously named batch files that deploy configuration files (config.txt, node.txt) to disk, install a persistent Windows service (“SystemNetwork”/“Update”) when run with an “install” argument, then periodically RC4-decrypt and call back to embedded C2 relays, all while leveraging open-source tooling (Mimikatz, Chisel, GO Simple Tunnel, Plink, RevSocks and Merlin) for lateral movement and data exfiltration; ESET has catalogued five Sponsor versions through June 2022, underscoring Ballistic Bobcat’s modular, short-duration, narrowly targeted “Sponsoring Access” campaign and highlighting the need for Exchange patching, service and file monitoring for batch deployments, and detection of RC4-encrypted config lookups to disrupt ongoing espionage operations.
hits.title: Sponsor with batch-filed whiskers: Ballistic Bobcat’s scan and strike backdoor

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: CISA and the FBI have warned that since its discovery by Lacework Labs in 2022—when FortiGuard Labs observed it controlling over 40,000 devices—threat actors deploying the Python-scripted Androxgh0st malware have been building a botnet to steal AWS, Microsoft Office 365, SendGrid and Twilio credentials by scanning for RCE vulnerabilities CVE-2017-9841 (PHPUnit), CVE-2021-41773 (Apache HTTP Server) and CVE-2018-15133 (Laravel) and harvesting .env files; once inside, operators abuse SMTP, API and web shell functions to test email-sending limits for spam campaigns, create fake pages as backdoors, deploy further tools, and spin up new AWS instances and user policies to expand scans for vulnerable targets. FBI/CISA mitigation guidance urges patching all systems (notably Apache 2.4.49/2.4.50), denying unnecessary URI access, disabling Laravel debug mode, removing and revoking .env credentials, auditing for unauthorized access, scanning for unrecognized PHP (especially under /vendor/phpunit), monitoring outgoing cURL GETs to file hosts, and reporting sightings; CISA has added CVE-2018-15133 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog (joining the earlier additions of CVE-2021-41773 and CVE-2017-9841) and ordered federal agencies to harden systems by February 6.
hits.title: FBI: Androxgh0st malware botnet steals AWS, Microsoft credentials

Exploiting publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and open-source tools, MuddyWater delivers malicious PDFs with embedded links that display error messages prompting users to download Excel maldocs or Windows executables; these files host VBA macros that drop WSF scripts to execute PowerShell and VB payloads, leverage LoLBins, and stage RATs and malware families including PowGoop, Canopy, Small Sieve, POWERSTATS and Mori while communicating with C2 over HTTP and DNS and persisting via Registry Run keys. Cisco Talos observed regional campaigns in Turkey (Nov 2021), Pakistan (Aug 2021) and Armenia (Jun 2021) using decoy documents, signaling tokens and a consistent TTP set, suggesting a conglomerate of subgroups migrating techniques across regions. The resultant network access and data exfiltration underscore the imperative for proactive DFIR readiness, deployment of XDR/MDR platforms, rigorous vulnerability management, macro execution restrictions, PowerShell/LoLBin monitoring and ongoing user awareness training reinforced by incident response tabletop exercises.
retrieved_context.title: An In-Depth Look at Iranian APT "MuddyWater"

retrieved_context.text: CISA has added CVE-2024-7593, a critical (CVSS 9.8) authentication-bypass flaw in Ivanti Virtual Traffic Manager (vTM) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog amid evidence of active exploitation and a public proof-of-concept, enabling remote attackers to bypass the admin panel and create rogue administrative users; Ivanti released patches in August 2024 for vTM versions 22.2R1, 22.3R3, 22.5R2, 22.6R2 and 22.7R2, and Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies must remediate by October 15, 2024. This alert follows active exploitation of CVE-2024-8190 and CVE-2024-8963 against a limited number of customers, while Censys data reveals 2,017 exposed Ivanti Cloud Service Appliance instances (predominantly U.S.), underscoring the need for immediate patch deployment, asset inventory and monitoring for unauthorized admin activity to prevent network compromise.
retrieved_context.title: CISA Flags Critical Ivanti vTM Vulnerability Amid Active Exploitation Concerns

retrieved_context.text: ESET researchers uncovered the Iran-aligned APT35 (aka Ballistic Bobcat, Charming Kitten, TA453/PHOSPHORUS) deploying a novel Sponsor backdoor across at least 34 opportunistic victims—primarily Israeli organizations in sectors from automotive to telecommunications, plus medical targets in Brazil and the UAE—by scanning for and exploiting Exchange CVE-2021-26855 vulnerabilities since September 2021, wrapping up their CISA AA21-321A/PowerLess campaign before dropping Sponsor via innocuously named batch files that deploy configuration files (config.txt, node.txt) to disk, install a persistent Windows service (“SystemNetwork”/“Update”) when run with an “install” argument, then periodically RC4-decrypt and call back to embedded C2 relays, all while leveraging open-source tooling (Mimikatz, Chisel, GO Simple Tunnel, Plink, RevSocks and Merlin) for lateral movement and data exfiltration; ESET has catalogued five Sponsor versions through June 2022, underscoring Ballistic Bobcat’s modular, short-duration, narrowly targeted “Sponsoring Access” campaign and highlighting the need for Exchange patching, service and file monitoring for batch deployments, and detection of RC4-encrypted config lookups to disrupt ongoing espionage operations.
retrieved_context.title: Sponsor with batch-filed whiskers: Ballistic Bobcat’s scan and strike backdoor

retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: CISA and the FBI have warned that since its discovery by Lacework Labs in 2022—when FortiGuard Labs observed it controlling over 40,000 devices—threat actors deploying the Python-scripted Androxgh0st malware have been building a botnet to steal AWS, Microsoft Office 365, SendGrid and Twilio credentials by scanning for RCE vulnerabilities CVE-2017-9841 (PHPUnit), CVE-2021-41773 (Apache HTTP Server) and CVE-2018-15133 (Laravel) and harvesting .env files; once inside, operators abuse SMTP, API and web shell functions to test email-sending limits for spam campaigns, create fake pages as backdoors, deploy further tools, and spin up new AWS instances and user policies to expand scans for vulnerable targets. FBI/CISA mitigation guidance urges patching all systems (notably Apache 2.4.49/2.4.50), denying unnecessary URI access, disabling Laravel debug mode, removing and revoking .env credentials, auditing for unauthorized access, scanning for unrecognized PHP (especially under /vendor/phpunit), monitoring outgoing cURL GETs to file hosts, and reporting sightings; CISA has added CVE-2018-15133 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog (joining the earlier additions of CVE-2021-41773 and CVE-2017-9841) and ordered federal agencies to harden systems by February 6.
retrieved_context.title: FBI: Androxgh0st malware botnet steals AWS, Microsoft credentials

canonical_entities: regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea
hits.text: In early 2018 McAfee Advanced Threat Research uncovered Operation Honeybee, a North Korean–linked campaign—tracked to the persona snoopykiller@mail.ru and control domains navermail.byethost3.com/nihon.byethost11.com—targeting humanitarian aid groups and regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea with malicious Microsoft Word documents named “Honeybee” that exploited politically themed and generic “not compatible” lures to execute VBA macros embedding a custom‐alphabet Base64 payload. Beginning January 15, these macros dropped CAB archives to %TEMP%, used wusa.exe or expand.exe for UAC bypass, then hijacked cliconfg.exe via a malicious NTWDBLIB.dll to install a persistent COMSysApp service loading ipnet.dll from %SystemRoot%\System32. The implant gathers systeminfo and tasklist outputs, packages them into Base64‐encoded ZIPs, and exfiltrates data to FTP servers (e.g., 1113427185.ifastnet.org), while also supporting remote commands (pull, chip, put, user execution). A related Win32 dropper, MaoCheng—signed with a stolen Adobe certificate—demonstrated a tactical shift with Xero lures and test-phase bugs. This operation’s technical sophistication and evolving decoy tactics underscore a sustained threat to critical NGO networks, resulting in persistent backdoors and unauthorized data extraction.
hits.title: McAfee Uncovers Operation Honeybee, a Malicious Campaign Targeting Humanitarian Aid Groups | McAfee Blog

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.

hits.text: CISA has added CVE-2022-22047—a high-severity (CVSS 7.8) elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Client Server Runtime Subsystem used since Windows 7 through Windows 11 and Server 2008–2022—to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and is urging federal agencies to install Microsoft’s July 5 Patch Tuesday update by August 2 after evidence emerged of in-the-wild exploitation; initially disclosed as a zero-day by Microsoft’s security team, the CSRSS bug enables adversaries who already hold local or physical access—or who gain remote code execution via malware or specially crafted Office/Adobe documents and macros—to escalate to SYSTEM privileges for lateral movement, although FortiGuard Labs rates the overall business threat as “medium” given the prerequisite foothold and available patch, while Trend Micro’s ZDI notes such elevation flaws are typically paired with a separate RCE vector and Microsoft has signaled future default blocking of VBA macros to mitigate this attack chain.
hits.title: CISA Urges Patch of Exploited Windows 11 Bug by Aug. 2 | Threatpost

hits.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
hits.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems
