hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: McAfee Mobile Research Team uncovered Xamalicious, a new Android backdoor built with Xamarin that abuses accessibility permissions to harvest device metadata, query a C2 server for a second-stage payload, and dynamically inject an assembly DLL to perform unauthorized ad-clicking, app installs and other financially motivated actions; this threat has been embedded in 25 apps—ranging from horoscope and gaming to utility tools—on Google Play since mid-2020, amassing over 327,000 installations across Brazil, Argentina, the UK, Australia, the US, Mexico and Europe. To evade detection, Xamalicious encrypts all C2 traffic as JWE tokens (RSA-OAEP/128CBC-HS256), self-updates its APK to transform into spyware or a banking trojan, and links back to the Cash Magnet ad-fraud campaign; its use of non-Java frameworks like Xamarin underscores heightened obfuscation. Google Play Protect now blocks or auto-removes infected apps. Separately, a malicious WhatsApp-based phishing campaign in India distributes fake SBI APKs invoking SMS permissions to capture credentials, banking and identity data, then exfiltrates them for unauthorized transactions.
hits.title: New Sneaky Xamalicious Android Malware Hits Over 327,000 Devices

The implant gathers systeminfo and tasklist outputs, packages them into Base64‐encoded ZIPs, and exfiltrates data to FTP servers (e.g., 1113427185.ifastnet.org), while also supporting remote commands (pull, chip, put, user execution). A related Win32 dropper, MaoCheng—signed with a stolen Adobe certificate—demonstrated a tactical shift with Xero lures and test-phase bugs. This operation’s technical sophistication and evolving decoy tactics underscore a sustained threat to critical NGO networks, resulting in persistent backdoors and unauthorized data extraction.
hits.title: McAfee Uncovers Operation Honeybee, a Malicious Campaign Targeting Humanitarian Aid Groups | McAfee Blog

hits.text: CISA has added CVE-2022-22047—a high-severity (CVSS 7.8) elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Client Server Runtime Subsystem used since Windows 7 through Windows 11 and Server 2008–2022—to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and is urging federal agencies to install Microsoft’s July 5 Patch Tuesday update by August 2 after evidence emerged of in-the-wild exploitation; initially disclosed as a zero-day by Microsoft’s security team, the CSRSS bug enables adversaries who already hold local or physical access—or who gain remote code execution via malware or specially crafted Office/Adobe documents and macros—to escalate to SYSTEM privileges for lateral movement, although FortiGuard Labs rates the overall business threat as “medium” given the prerequisite foothold and available patch, while Trend Micro’s ZDI notes such elevation flaws are typically paired with a separate RCE vector and Microsoft has signaled future default blocking of VBA macros to mitigate this attack chain.
hits.title: CISA Urges Patch of Exploited Windows 11 Bug by Aug. 2 | Threatpost

hits.text: Symantec has warned that extortion actors, notably the Clop ransomware operation (aka Snakefly/TA505/FIN11), have been exploiting a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability in the MOVEit Transfer web application (CVE-2023-34362) since May 27, 2023, enabling supply-chain attacks across multiple organizations; although first patched on May 31, additional vulnerabilities (CVEs pending) were disclosed on June 9. Attackers deploy a bespoke web shell, Lemurloot (detected as JS.Malscript!g1, Trojan.Gen.2, WS.Malware), to authenticate via hard-coded credentials, execute SQL statements to alter or delete database elements, exfiltrate records and Azure settings, and manipulate user accounts. With proof-of-concept code now public, secondary threat actors face elevated risk of exploitation and data theft. Clop has since threatened data leaks unless ransoms are paid, reflecting its shift from encryption to extortion. Symantec mitigations include file-based and ML detections, network-based attack signatures, and Data Center Security policy controls that harden MS SQL, IIS and sandbox environments to prevent web-shell deployment and unauthorized software execution.
hits.title: MOVEit Vulnerabilities: What You Need to Know | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
hits.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

hits.text: Russia’s APT29 (aka Cozy Bear/Nobelium) has been exploiting a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in JetBrains TeamCity (CVE-2023-42793, CVSS 9.8) since September—shortly after JetBrains issued a patch and Rapid7 published a proof-of-concept—to gain initial access to SDLC management servers, escalate privileges, move laterally, deploy stealthy backdoors that persist through updates, and potentially manipulate build pipelines or insert malicious updates in SolarWinds-style supply-chain attacks; CISA, FBI, NSA and international partners warn that around 800 internet-exposed instances remain vulnerable (with uncounted internally reachable servers also at risk), and that North Korea’s Lazarus and Andariel groups have similarly weaponized the same flaw, prompting Fortinet to report multi-actor post-exploit techniques in live incidents; mitigation guidance urges immediate upgrading to TeamCity 2023.05.4, removal of public exposure, comprehensive IoC-based threat hunting across servers and build agents, and full compromise assessments to eradicate entrenched backdoors.
hits.title: Global TeamCity Exploitation Opens Door to SolarWinds-Style Nightmare

hits.text: Avast researchers uncovered that North Korea’s Lazarus group leveraged a Windows zero-day privilege escalation flaw in Microsoft’s AppLocker “appid.sys” driver (CVE-2024-21338) to execute a truly fileless kernel attack during 2023 intrusions, sending a proof-of-concept exploit to Microsoft in August and prompting a February 2024 patch and subsequent advisory update once active exploitation was confirmed; by abusing a ubiquitous signed driver rather than importing custom code (BYOVD), Lazarus gained kernel read/write primitives, manipulated kernel objects to deploy an enhanced FudModule rootkit—now capable of evading AhnLab V3, Defender, CrowdStrike Falcon and HitmanPro—and bypassed driver allowlisting, then deployed a new remote access trojan for persistent access, underscoring the need for immediate patching, vigilant driver integrity monitoring and behavior-based detection to thwart stealthy, living-off-the-land attacks.
hits.title: Windows Zero-Day Exploited by North Korean Hackers in Rootkit Attack - SecurityWeek

Indicator Removal on Host: Clear Windows Event Logs
hits.text: Lynx ransomware, emerging in July 2024 as the INC ransomware successor under a Ransomware-as-a-Service model, employs a sophisticated double-extortion strategy—exfiltrating data prior to encryption and threatening publication on a leak site—and reuses significant INC source code. Between July and November 2024, it disrupted U.S. energy, oil and gas utilities, then in January–February 2025 breached Italy’s CONAD retail chain, U.S. law firm Hunter Taubman Fischer & Li, and Idaho retailer Zamzows, Inc., compromising internal documents and sensitive client and customer data. Initial access leverages phishing (T1566.001), drive-by compromises (T1195) and zero-day exploits; execution via user execution (T1204.002) and scripting interpreters (T1059.001); persistence through autostart mechanisms (T1070.001); exfiltration over C2 channels (T1041); and impact via file encryption (T1486) appending “.LYNX.” Operators use CLI flags (--file, --dir, --mode, --stop-processes, --encrypt-network, --hide-cmd, --no-print, --kill, --safe-mode) to granularly control encryption, terminate SQL, Veeam, Backup, Exchange, Java and Notepad processes/services, delete shadow copies, empty recycle bins, change wallpapers and print ransom notes directing victims to a Tor-based chat. Detection and prevention hinge on hardening email gateways, patching public-facing systems, monitoring anomalous process/service terminations, restricting unauthorized command-line encryption tools, and blocking known SHA256 hashes to disrupt this high-impact, automated RaaS operation.
hits.title: Lynx Ransomware: INC Ransomware Reincarnated - Threat Actors

hits.text: Sea Turtle, also known as Cosmic Wolf, Marbled Dust, Teal Kurma and UNC1326, has been conducting a stealthy, Türkiye-linked cyber espionage campaign since at least January 2017, recently targeting Dutch ISPs, telecom, IT-service and media providers as well as Kurdish websites via supply-chain and island-hopping attacks to harvest politically sensitive personal data and potential dissident communications. First detailed by Cisco Talos in April 2019 for state-sponsored DNS hijacking to redirect legitimate domain queries to attacker-controlled servers, the group elevated its upstream foothold tactics in late 2021 by exploiting known telecom and IT vulnerabilities across Armenia, Cyprus, Greece, Iraq and Syria, per Microsoft. Between 2021 and 2023 PwC observed deployment of “SnappyTCP,” a simple Linux/Unix reverse-TCP web shell (with and without OpenSSL/TLS) for persistence and C2, and Hunt & Hackett’s 2023 incident revealed credential-theft via a compromised cPanel account used to deploy SnappyTCP, tar and expose email archives publicly for direct exfiltration. Organizations should enforce strong password policies, 2FA, login-rate limiting, SSH monitoring and timely patching to mitigate this ongoing espionage threat.
hits.title: Sea Turtle Cyber Espionage Campaign Targets Dutch IT and Telecom Companies

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: In February 2022, CISA, the FBI, US Cyber Command CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA issued a joint advisory on Iranian Ministry of Intelligence–linked APT MuddyWater (aka MERCURY, Earth Vetala, Static Kitten, Seedworm, TEMP.Zagros), active since 2018 and focused on cyber espionage, intellectual property theft and ransomware against defense, oil & gas, government and telecom sectors across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America. Exploiting publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and open-source tools, MuddyWater delivers malicious PDFs with embedded links that display error messages prompting users to download Excel maldocs or Windows executables; these files host VBA macros that drop WSF scripts to execute PowerShell and VB payloads, leverage LoLBins, and stage RATs and malware families including PowGoop, Canopy, Small Sieve, POWERSTATS and Mori while communicating with C2 over HTTP and DNS and persisting via Registry Run keys. Cisco Talos observed regional campaigns in Turkey (Nov 2021), Pakistan (Aug 2021) and Armenia (Jun 2021) using decoy documents, signaling tokens and a consistent TTP set, suggesting a conglomerate of subgroups migrating techniques across regions. The resultant network access and data exfiltration underscore the imperative for proactive DFIR readiness, deployment of XDR/MDR platforms, rigorous vulnerability management, macro execution restrictions, PowerShell/LoLBin monitoring and ongoing user awareness training reinforced by incident response tabletop exercises.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at Iranian APT "MuddyWater"

hits.text: In Q2–Q3 2024, ESET Research uncovered Operation AkaiRyū, a spearphishing-driven cyberespionage campaign by China-aligned APT10 subgroup MirrorFace targeting a Central European diplomatic institute over Expo 2025—its first known European operation—where carefully crafted emails and OneDrive links triggered LNK-based PowerShell loaders and VBA-macro Word decoys that side-loaded the resurrected ANEL backdoor (versions 5.5.4/5.5.5) via signed McAfee and JustSystems binaries; post-compromise activity included deployment of a heavily customized AsyncRAT within a multi-stage execution chain running inside Windows Sandbox, abuse of Visual Studio Code remote tunnels for stealthy command-and-control, and later-stage HiddenFace backdoor installation for persistent file exfiltration, all revealed through collaborative forensic analysis of disk images—unearthing novel execution proxies (WMI/wlrmdr.exe), decoy documents (tmp.docx/normal_.dotm), and evidence of resumed ANEL development—thereby strengthening the attribution of MirrorFace as an APT10 subgroup and highlighting the critical need to monitor signed-binary side-loading, sandbox evasion techniques, and legitimate-tool abuse; these findings, presented at JSAC January 2025, underscore MirrorFace’s expanded targeting and sophisticated TTPs.
hits.title: Operation AkaiRyū: MirrorFace invites Europe to Expo 2025 and revives ANEL backdoor

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

canonical_entities: Scanning the Internet for IoT devices with open Telnet/SSH ports
Use of default or weak credentials
Encrypted SOCKS5 tunneling to proxy infrastructure
hits.text: Researchers have uncovered that since early 2024 a previously undocumented botnet, dubbed Ngioweb, has been systematically scanning the Internet for IoT devices—primarily DVRs, IP cameras and home routers—with open Telnet/SSH ports and default or weak credentials, exploiting known firmware vulnerabilities to deploy a lightweight Go-based loader that establishes encrypted SOCKS5 tunnels back to a resilient NSOCKS residential proxy network of over 150,000 infected nodes. Once a device is compromised, Ngioweb drops a persistent agent that connects to fast-flux C2 domains via HTTPS, retrieves updated encryption keys and proxy configuration, and registers the node for NSOCKS’ tiered subscription service (starting at $25/month), which reportedly generates upwards of $500K in monthly revenue by fueling large-scale credential-stuffing campaigns, ad fraud and DDoS-for-hire operations. The actors behind Ngioweb continually rotate fallback C2 domains, employ encryption and obfuscation to evade signature-based detection, and monitor infection success rates in real time, enabling rapid retooling and expansion. Defenders are urged to enforce strong, unique credentials on all IoT assets, disable unused management interfaces, apply timely firmware updates, implement network segmentation and deploy behavioral analytics or honeypots to detect anomalous outbound proxy traffic.
hits.title: Ngioweb Botnet Fuels NSOCKS Residential Proxy Network Exploiting IoT Devices

hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.

canonical_entities: regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea
retrieved_context.text: In early 2018 McAfee Advanced Threat Research uncovered Operation Honeybee, a North Korean–linked campaign—tracked to the persona snoopykiller@mail.ru and control domains navermail.byethost3.com/nihon.byethost11.com—targeting humanitarian aid groups and regional organizations in Vietnam and South Korea with malicious Microsoft Word documents named “Honeybee” that exploited politically themed and generic “not compatible” lures to execute VBA macros embedding a custom‐alphabet Base64 payload. Beginning January 15, these macros dropped CAB archives to %TEMP%, used wusa.exe or expand.exe for UAC bypass, then hijacked cliconfg.exe via a malicious NTWDBLIB.dll to install a persistent COMSysApp service loading ipnet.dll from %SystemRoot%\System32. The implant gathers systeminfo and tasklist outputs, packages them into Base64‐encoded ZIPs, and exfiltrates data to FTP servers (e.g., 1113427185.ifastnet.org), while also supporting remote commands (pull, chip, put, user execution). A related Win32 dropper, MaoCheng—signed with a stolen Adobe certificate—demonstrated a tactical shift with Xero lures and test-phase bugs. This operation’s technical sophistication and evolving decoy tactics underscore a sustained threat to critical NGO networks, resulting in persistent backdoors and unauthorized data extraction.
retrieved_context.title: McAfee Uncovers Operation Honeybee, a Malicious Campaign Targeting Humanitarian Aid Groups | McAfee Blog

retrieved_context.text: CISA has added CVE-2022-22047—a high-severity (CVSS 7.8) elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Client Server Runtime Subsystem used since Windows 7 through Windows 11 and Server 2008–2022—to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and is urging federal agencies to install Microsoft’s July 5 Patch Tuesday update by August 2 after evidence emerged of in-the-wild exploitation; initially disclosed as a zero-day by Microsoft’s security team, the CSRSS bug enables adversaries who already hold local or physical access—or who gain remote code execution via malware or specially crafted Office/Adobe documents and macros—to escalate to SYSTEM privileges for lateral movement, although FortiGuard Labs rates the overall business threat as “medium” given the prerequisite foothold and available patch, while Trend Micro’s ZDI notes such elevation flaws are typically paired with a separate RCE vector and Microsoft has signaled future default blocking of VBA macros to mitigate this attack chain.
retrieved_context.title: CISA Urges Patch of Exploited Windows 11 Bug by Aug. 2 | Threatpost

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: In February 2022, CISA, the FBI, US Cyber Command CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA issued a joint advisory on Iranian Ministry of Intelligence–linked APT MuddyWater (aka MERCURY, Earth Vetala, Static Kitten, Seedworm, TEMP.Zagros), active since 2018 and focused on cyber espionage, intellectual property theft and ransomware against defense, oil & gas, government and telecom sectors across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America. Exploiting publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and open-source tools, MuddyWater delivers malicious PDFs with embedded links that display error messages prompting users to download Excel maldocs or Windows executables; these files host VBA macros that drop WSF scripts to execute PowerShell and VB payloads, leverage LoLBins, and stage RATs and malware families including PowGoop, Canopy, Small Sieve, POWERSTATS and Mori while communicating with C2 over HTTP and DNS and persisting via Registry Run keys. Cisco Talos observed regional campaigns in Turkey (Nov 2021), Pakistan (Aug 2021) and Armenia (Jun 2021) using decoy documents, signaling tokens and a consistent TTP set, suggesting a conglomerate of subgroups migrating techniques across regions. The resultant network access and data exfiltration underscore the imperative for proactive DFIR readiness, deployment of XDR/MDR platforms, rigorous vulnerability management, macro execution restrictions, PowerShell/LoLBin monitoring and ongoing user awareness training reinforced by incident response tabletop exercises.
retrieved_context.title: An In-Depth Look at Iranian APT "MuddyWater"

retrieved_context.text: In Q2–Q3 2024, ESET Research uncovered Operation AkaiRyū, a spearphishing-driven cyberespionage campaign by China-aligned APT10 subgroup MirrorFace targeting a Central European diplomatic institute over Expo 2025—its first known European operation—where carefully crafted emails and OneDrive links triggered LNK-based PowerShell loaders and VBA-macro Word decoys that side-loaded the resurrected ANEL backdoor (versions 5.5.4/5.5.5) via signed McAfee and JustSystems binaries; post-compromise activity included deployment of a heavily customized AsyncRAT within a multi-stage execution chain running inside Windows Sandbox, abuse of Visual Studio Code remote tunnels for stealthy command-and-control, and later-stage HiddenFace backdoor installation for persistent file exfiltration, all revealed through collaborative forensic analysis of disk images—unearthing novel execution proxies (WMI/wlrmdr.exe), decoy documents (tmp.docx/normal_.dotm), and evidence of resumed ANEL development—thereby strengthening the attribution of MirrorFace as an APT10 subgroup and highlighting the critical need to monitor signed-binary side-loading, sandbox evasion techniques, and legitimate-tool abuse; these findings, presented at JSAC January 2025, underscore MirrorFace’s expanded targeting and sophisticated TTPs.
retrieved_context.title: Operation AkaiRyū: MirrorFace invites Europe to Expo 2025 and revives ANEL backdoor

hits.text: Security researchers at McAfee first observed Operation Sharpshooter in October–November 2018, a sophisticated phishing campaign targeting 87 critical‐infrastructure organizations—predominantly in the United States—including nuclear, defense, energy and financial firms, via recruitment‐style Microsoft Word attachments containing weaponized macros that load an in‐memory downloader to fetch a second‐stage implant dubbed Rising Sun; this implant, which exfiltrates host data to a command server, incorporates publicly available Lazarus Group source code as a likely false flag rather than evidence of Lazarus involvement. McAfee analysts Ryan Sherstobitoff and Asheer Malhotra note that Rising Sun’s multi‐step execution—weaponized document, in‐memory downloader, intelligence‐gathering implant—highlights the continued efficacy of social‐engineering vectors, while experts from CipherCloud, Positive Technologies and Lucy Security emphasize that defenses must go beyond spam filters to include ongoing user awareness training, holistic people-and-technology security models, robust data protection, network visibility and rapid incident response to detect and halt such advanced, evolving threats.
hits.title: Operation Sharpshooter targets infrastructure around the world | TechTarget

canonical_entities: automated encrypted exfiltration over C2 channels
hits.text: McAfee’s Advanced Threat Research team uncovered “Operation Sharpshooter,” a global cyber-espionage campaign targeting nuclear, defense, energy and financial organizations via weaponized Office documents masquerading as recruitment materials; an initial macro‐enabled loader drops an in‐memory implant that retrieves a second‐stage backdoor dubbed “Rising Sun,” which leverages source code from Lazarus Group’s 2015 Duuzer Trojan to perform account, file/directory, process and system/network discovery, process injection and automated encrypted exfiltration over C2 channels (e.g., 34.214.99.20/view_style.php); from October to November 2018 McAfee telemetry identified at least 87 predominantly English-speaking targets, with key IOCs including hashes such as 8106a30bd35526bded384627d8eebce15da35d17 and document URLs like hxxp://208.117.44.112/Strategic Planning Manager.doc, detectable by McAfee signatures RDN/Generic Downloader.x and Rising-Sun, and mitigated by monitoring macro executions, anomalous process injections and outbound C2 traffic while the broader community assesses attribution and monitors for follow-on exploitation.
hits.title: ‘Operation Sharpshooter’ Targets Global Defense, Critical Infrastructure | McAfee Blog

canonical_entities: Palo Alto Networks Cortex XDR Anti-Ransomware
hits.text: Following the sale of INC ransomware source code in March 2024 and its initial appearance in August 2023, researchers in July 2024 uncovered Lynx ransomware, a Windows-only, C++-based RaaS variant that shares ~48% of INC’s functions (70.8% among common routines) and has been deployed against U.S. and U.K. retail, real estate, architecture, financial and environmental service firms via phishing, malicious downloads and underground forums; employing AES-128-CTR and Curve25519 Donna for encryption with a .lynx extension, it conducts double-extortion by exfiltrating victims’ data (published on lynxblog[.]net under a policy excluding governments, hospitals and non-profits) before encrypting all files by default—killing processes, encrypting network shares and hidden disks, deleting shadow copies and backups, leveraging the Restart Manager API to target in-use files, and printing a OneNote report—then dropping a README.txt ransom note; this evolution of RaaS underscores the need for organizations to adopt robust cybersecurity measures, including anti-phishing training, backup hardening, dynamic and behavioral detections via Palo Alto Networks’ Cortex XDR Anti-Ransomware and Advanced WildFire, and vigilant monitoring of Indicators of Compromise such as published SHA256 hashes to mitigate high-profile, code-reused ransomware campaigns.
hits.title: Lynx Ransomware: A Rebranding of INC Ransomware

hits.text: Moses Staff, an Iran-linked APT active since September 2021, has conducted politically motivated sabotage campaigns—initially against Israeli organizations and later targets in India, Germany, the U.S., Italy, Chile, Turkey and the UAE—by exploiting known public-facing server vulnerabilities (e.g., Microsoft Exchange), moving laterally with PsExec, WMIC and PowerShell, and deploying a two-stage destructive toolkit: a Python-based loader (PyDCrypt) that installs a custom DiskCryptor variant (DCSrv) to encrypt files and disrupt operations without ransom demands, and, as newly documented by Cybereason, the StrifeWater RAT masquerading as calc.exe to establish early footholds, harvest system metadata (machine name, OS version, CPU architecture, user privileges, time zone), execute commands, capture screens, maintain persistence via scheduled tasks, and download auxiliary modules before self-removal—all while communicating with hard-coded C2 IPs, URLs and domain names—to evade detection; organizations should urgently patch exposed servers, monitor anomalous calc.exe and scheduled-task activity, and enhance EDR rules to detect PyDCrypt, DCSrv and StrifeWater behaviors to thwart data exfiltration and infrastructure damage.
hits.title: Iranian APT group uses previously undocumented Trojan for destructive access to organizations

hits.text: ESET researchers have traced the China-aligned hacker group FishMonger, aka Aquatic Panda, and its global espionage campaign “FishMedley” back to the iSoon APT contractor (Axun Information Technology) operating under the Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security and PLA, following the U.S. DOJ’s addition of key members to the FBI’s Most Wanted list; FishMonger’s modus operandi relies on compromising high-privilege user accounts—likely harvested via phishing or credential theft—to gain domain administrator access, then deploying publicly available modular backdoors and loaders (ShadowPad, Spyder loader, SodaMaster) and the RPipeCommander reverse shell rather than zero-day exploits, enabling sustained infiltration of governmental bodies, Catholic charities, NGOs and think tanks across Taiwan, Hungary, Turkey, Thailand, the U.S. and France; while technically unsophisticated, the group’s efficient use of known tools has yielded consistent exfiltration of confidential data, underscoring the need for potential targets to hunt for these specific indicators of compromise and strengthen monitoring of privileged accounts.
hits.title: Chinese Hacker Group Tracked Back to iSoon APT Operation

hits.text: In August, the DPRK–linked APT TA444 (aka APT38, BlueNoroff, BlackAlicanto, Coperenicum, Sapphire Sleet and Stardust Chollima) deployed SpectralBlur, a custom post-exploitation macOS backdoor that leverages command-and-control instructions to upload/download files, spawn a shell, update its configuration, delete files or enter hibernation/sleep mode; Proofpoint researcher Greg Lesnewich identified code overlaps with the KandyKorn macOS data stealer—earlier tied to Lazarus Group phishing campaigns against blockchain engineers—linking both tools through shared strings and infrastructure. This rapid iteration of proprietary macOS malware underscores TA444’s dedicated development capability and signals an intensified DPRK espionage focus on Apple users, particularly within the cryptocurrency sector, demonstrating persistent operational tempo and advanced post-exploitation tactics.
hits.title: North Korea Debuts 'SpectralBlur' Malware Amid macOS Onslaught

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora
hits.text: Since at least September 2023, the China-aligned Evasive Panda APT (aka BRONZE HIGHLAND/Daggerfly) has conducted a dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora by compromising both the Kagyu International Monlam Trust’s website and the official Monlam translation-software supply chain—first implanting obfuscated JavaScript into jquery.js on the festival site that verifies victims’ first three IP octets via an MD5 hash salted with “1qaz0okm!@#,” serves a faux “Aw, Snap!” error page to users in India, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Australia and the U.S., and lures them to download a malicious “certificate.exe” or “.pkg” downloader; that loader side-loads memmgrset.dll (http_dy.dll) to fetch a JSON config from update.devicebug[.]com and ultimately deploys the undocumented Nightdoor backdoor alongside the group’s modular MgBot implant, while a trojanized Monlam software installer (Windows autorun.exe abusing MonlamUpdate.exe for DLL side-loading of RPHost.dll, and macOS Mach-O downloaders) has delivered further downloaders and payloads—retrieved from tibetpost[.]net and a direct IP—to %TEMP%\default_ico.exe for additional Nightdoor and MgBot installation.
hits.title: Evasive Panda leverages Monlam Festival to target Tibetans

hits.text: Since its emergence in 2013, Iran-linked APT35 (aka Charming Kitten/Phosphorus) has executed a series of high-value espionage campaigns—beginning with a 2014 social-media spying operation—and continued in 2019 with spear-phishing against U.S., French and Middle East academic institutions before Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit seized control of 99 APT35 domains; in late 2020 the group targeted oncology, genetics and neurology researchers in Israel and the U.S. via its “BadBlood” PDF-based spear-phishing campaign, while in 2021 it chained Exchange Server flaws (ProxyShell) for network intrusion and demonstrated TTP overlaps with Momento ransomware (CVE-2021-21972 exploiter); in January 2022 it performed mass Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) scans—over 80 percent of attempts originated in the U.S.—and later deployed a stealthy .NET-based PowerShell backdoor (“PowerLess”) that runs in-process to avoid detection, followed by Hyperscrape, a Windows .NET mailbox exfiltration tool for Outlook, Gmail and Yahoo! that quietly harvests emails once the actor possesses valid credentials or session cookies, and a companion Telegram dump utility; APT35 maintains persistence for intelligence collection or monetizes access when systems lack strategic value, underscoring the need for timely patching, multi-factor authentication and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at APT35 aka Charming Kitten

hits.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
hits.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Following the sale of INC ransomware source code in March 2024 and its initial appearance in August 2023, researchers in July 2024 uncovered Lynx ransomware, a Windows-only, C++-based RaaS variant that shares ~48% of INC’s functions (70.8% among common routines) and has been deployed against U.S. and U.K. retail, real estate, architecture, financial and environmental service firms via phishing, malicious downloads and underground forums; employing AES-128-CTR and Curve25519 Donna for encryption with a .lynx extension, it conducts double-extortion by exfiltrating victims’ data (published on lynxblog[.]net under a policy excluding governments, hospitals and non-profits) before encrypting all files by default—killing processes, encrypting network shares and hidden disks, deleting shadow copies and backups, leveraging the Restart Manager API to target in-use files, and printing a OneNote report—then dropping a README.txt ransom note; this evolution of RaaS underscores the need for organizations to adopt robust cybersecurity measures, including anti-phishing training, backup hardening, dynamic and behavioral detections via Palo Alto Networks’ Cortex XDR Anti-Ransomware and Advanced WildFire, and vigilant monitoring of Indicators of Compromise such as published SHA256 hashes to mitigate high-profile, code-reused ransomware campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Lynx Ransomware: A Rebranding of INC Ransomware

retrieved_context.text: Moses Staff, an Iran-linked APT active since September 2021, has conducted politically motivated sabotage campaigns—initially against Israeli organizations and later targets in India, Germany, the U.S., Italy, Chile, Turkey and the UAE—by exploiting known public-facing server vulnerabilities (e.g., Microsoft Exchange), moving laterally with PsExec, WMIC and PowerShell, and deploying a two-stage destructive toolkit: a Python-based loader (PyDCrypt) that installs a custom DiskCryptor variant (DCSrv) to encrypt files and disrupt operations without ransom demands, and, as newly documented by Cybereason, the StrifeWater RAT masquerading as calc.exe to establish early footholds, harvest system metadata (machine name, OS version, CPU architecture, user privileges, time zone), execute commands, capture screens, maintain persistence via scheduled tasks, and download auxiliary modules before self-removal—all while communicating with hard-coded C2 IPs, URLs and domain names—to evade detection; organizations should urgently patch exposed servers, monitor anomalous calc.exe and scheduled-task activity, and enhance EDR rules to detect PyDCrypt, DCSrv and StrifeWater behaviors to thwart data exfiltration and infrastructure damage.

retrieved_context.text: ESET researchers have traced the China-aligned hacker group FishMonger, aka Aquatic Panda, and its global espionage campaign “FishMedley” back to the iSoon APT contractor (Axun Information Technology) operating under the Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security and PLA, following the U.S. DOJ’s addition of key members to the FBI’s Most Wanted list; FishMonger’s modus operandi relies on compromising high-privilege user accounts—likely harvested via phishing or credential theft—to gain domain administrator access, then deploying publicly available modular backdoors and loaders (ShadowPad, Spyder loader, SodaMaster) and the RPipeCommander reverse shell rather than zero-day exploits, enabling sustained infiltration of governmental bodies, Catholic charities, NGOs and think tanks across Taiwan, Hungary, Turkey, Thailand, the U.S. and France; while technically unsophisticated, the group’s efficient use of known tools has yielded consistent exfiltration of confidential data, underscoring the need for potential targets to hunt for these specific indicators of compromise and strengthen monitoring of privileged accounts.
retrieved_context.title: Chinese Hacker Group Tracked Back to iSoon APT Operation

retrieved_context.text: In August, the DPRK–linked APT TA444 (aka APT38, BlueNoroff, BlackAlicanto, Coperenicum, Sapphire Sleet and Stardust Chollima) deployed SpectralBlur, a custom post-exploitation macOS backdoor that leverages command-and-control instructions to upload/download files, spawn a shell, update its configuration, delete files or enter hibernation/sleep mode; Proofpoint researcher Greg Lesnewich identified code overlaps with the KandyKorn macOS data stealer—earlier tied to Lazarus Group phishing campaigns against blockchain engineers—linking both tools through shared strings and infrastructure. This rapid iteration of proprietary macOS malware underscores TA444’s dedicated development capability and signals an intensified DPRK espionage focus on Apple users, particularly within the cryptocurrency sector, demonstrating persistent operational tempo and advanced post-exploitation tactics.
retrieved_context.title: North Korea Debuts 'SpectralBlur' Malware Amid macOS Onslaught

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora
retrieved_context.text: Since at least September 2023, the China-aligned Evasive Panda APT (aka BRONZE HIGHLAND/Daggerfly) has conducted a dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora by compromising both the Kagyu International Monlam Trust’s website and the official Monlam translation-software supply chain—first implanting obfuscated JavaScript into jquery.js on the festival site that verifies victims’ first three IP octets via an MD5 hash salted with “1qaz0okm!@#,” serves a faux “Aw, Snap!” error page to users in India, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Australia and the U.S., and lures them to download a malicious “certificate.exe” or “.pkg” downloader; that loader side-loads memmgrset.dll (http_dy.dll) to fetch a JSON config from update.devicebug[.]com and ultimately deploys the undocumented Nightdoor backdoor alongside the group’s modular MgBot implant, while a trojanized Monlam software installer (Windows autorun.exe abusing MonlamUpdate.exe for DLL side-loading of RPHost.dll, and macOS Mach-O downloaders) has delivered further downloaders and payloads—retrieved from tibetpost[.]net and a direct IP—to %TEMP%\default_ico.exe for additional Nightdoor and MgBot installation.
retrieved_context.title: Evasive Panda leverages Monlam Festival to target Tibetans

retrieved_context.text: Since its emergence in 2013, Iran-linked APT35 (aka Charming Kitten/Phosphorus) has executed a series of high-value espionage campaigns—beginning with a 2014 social-media spying operation—and continued in 2019 with spear-phishing against U.S., French and Middle East academic institutions before Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit seized control of 99 APT35 domains; in late 2020 the group targeted oncology, genetics and neurology researchers in Israel and the U.S. via its “BadBlood” PDF-based spear-phishing campaign, while in 2021 it chained Exchange Server flaws (ProxyShell) for network intrusion and demonstrated TTP overlaps with Momento ransomware (CVE-2021-21972 exploiter); in January 2022 it performed mass Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) scans—over 80 percent of attempts originated in the U.S.—and later deployed a stealthy .NET-based PowerShell backdoor (“PowerLess”) that runs in-process to avoid detection, followed by Hyperscrape, a Windows .NET mailbox exfiltration tool for Outlook, Gmail and Yahoo! that quietly harvests emails once the actor possesses valid credentials or session cookies, and a companion Telegram dump utility; APT35 maintains persistence for intelligence collection or monetizes access when systems lack strategic value, underscoring the need for timely patching, multi-factor authentication and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: An In-Depth Look at APT35 aka Charming Kitten

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
retrieved_context.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Security researchers at McAfee first observed Operation Sharpshooter in October–November 2018, a sophisticated phishing campaign targeting 87 critical‐infrastructure organizations—predominantly in the United States—including nuclear, defense, energy and financial firms, via recruitment‐style Microsoft Word attachments containing weaponized macros that load an in‐memory downloader to fetch a second‐stage implant dubbed Rising Sun; this implant, which exfiltrates host data to a command server, incorporates publicly available Lazarus Group source code as a likely false flag rather than evidence of Lazarus involvement. McAfee analysts Ryan Sherstobitoff and Asheer Malhotra note that Rising Sun’s multi‐step execution—weaponized document, in‐memory downloader, intelligence‐gathering implant—highlights the continued efficacy of social‐engineering vectors, while experts from CipherCloud, Positive Technologies and Lucy Security emphasize that defenses must go beyond spam filters to include ongoing user awareness training, holistic people-and-technology security models, robust data protection, network visibility and rapid incident response to detect and halt such advanced, evolving threats.
hits.title: Operation Sharpshooter targets infrastructure around the world | TechTarget

hits.text: Avast researchers uncovered that North Korea’s Lazarus group leveraged a Windows zero-day privilege escalation flaw in Microsoft’s AppLocker “appid.sys” driver (CVE-2024-21338) to execute a truly fileless kernel attack during 2023 intrusions, sending a proof-of-concept exploit to Microsoft in August and prompting a February 2024 patch and subsequent advisory update once active exploitation was confirmed; by abusing a ubiquitous signed driver rather than importing custom code (BYOVD), Lazarus gained kernel read/write primitives, manipulated kernel objects to deploy an enhanced FudModule rootkit—now capable of evading AhnLab V3, Defender, CrowdStrike Falcon and HitmanPro—and bypassed driver allowlisting, then deployed a new remote access trojan for persistent access, underscoring the need for immediate patching, vigilant driver integrity monitoring and behavior-based detection to thwart stealthy, living-off-the-land attacks.
hits.title: Windows Zero-Day Exploited by North Korean Hackers in Rootkit Attack - SecurityWeek

hits.text: In November 2023, Russian state-sponsored group Nobelium (aka Midnight Blizzard/APT29) executed a month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment by conducting a password-spray brute-force attack against a legacy non-production test tenant lacking multi-factor authentication, enabling pivoting to a small subset of high-value accounts—including leadership, cybersecurity and legal team mailboxes—from which they exfiltrated emails and attachments; discovered on January 12, 2024, the campaign underscores the risk of poorly secured account configurations rather than software vulnerabilities, prompting Microsoft to notify impacted employees, reaffirm its MFA mandate, and reinforce zero-trust controls. This incident, following Nobelium’s SolarWinds and 2021 support-tool intrusions, highlights the necessity of enforcing MFA, minimizing default permissions, and hardening non-prod assets to mitigate advanced persistent threats.
hits.title: Russian hackers stole Microsoft corporate emails in month-long breach

hits.text: Symantec has warned that extortion actors, notably the Clop ransomware operation (aka Snakefly/TA505/FIN11), have been exploiting a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability in the MOVEit Transfer web application (CVE-2023-34362) since May 27, 2023, enabling supply-chain attacks across multiple organizations; although first patched on May 31, additional vulnerabilities (CVEs pending) were disclosed on June 9. Attackers deploy a bespoke web shell, Lemurloot (detected as JS.Malscript!g1, Trojan.Gen.2, WS.Malware), to authenticate via hard-coded credentials, execute SQL statements to alter or delete database elements, exfiltrate records and Azure settings, and manipulate user accounts. With proof-of-concept code now public, secondary threat actors face elevated risk of exploitation and data theft. Clop has since threatened data leaks unless ransoms are paid, reflecting its shift from encryption to extortion. Symantec mitigations include file-based and ML detections, network-based attack signatures, and Data Center Security policy controls that harden MS SQL, IIS and sandbox environments to prevent web-shell deployment and unauthorized software execution.
hits.title: MOVEit Vulnerabilities: What You Need to Know | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Lynx ransomware, emerging in July 2024 as the INC ransomware successor under a Ransomware-as-a-Service model, employs a sophisticated double-extortion strategy—exfiltrating data prior to encryption and threatening publication on a leak site—and reuses significant INC source code. Between July and November 2024, it disrupted U.S. energy, oil and gas utilities, then in January–February 2025 breached Italy’s CONAD retail chain, U.S. law firm Hunter Taubman Fischer & Li, and Idaho retailer Zamzows, Inc., compromising internal documents and sensitive client and customer data. Initial access leverages phishing (T1566.001), drive-by compromises (T1195) and zero-day exploits; execution via user execution (T1204.002) and scripting interpreters (T1059.001); persistence through autostart mechanisms (T1070.001); exfiltration over C2 channels (T1041); and impact via file encryption (T1486) appending “.LYNX.” Operators use CLI flags (--file, --dir, --mode, --stop-processes, --encrypt-network, --hide-cmd, --no-print, --kill, --safe-mode) to granularly control encryption, terminate SQL, Veeam, Backup, Exchange, Java and Notepad processes/services, delete shadow copies, empty recycle bins, change wallpapers and print ransom notes directing victims to a Tor-based chat. Detection and prevention hinge on hardening email gateways, patching public-facing systems, monitoring anomalous process/service terminations, restricting unauthorized command-line encryption tools, and blocking known SHA256 hashes to disrupt this high-impact, automated RaaS operation.
hits.title: Lynx Ransomware: INC Ransomware Reincarnated - Threat Actors

retrieved_context.text: Lynx ransomware, emerging in July 2024 as the INC ransomware successor under a Ransomware-as-a-Service model, employs a sophisticated double-extortion strategy—exfiltrating data prior to encryption and threatening publication on a leak site—and reuses significant INC source code. Between July and November 2024, it disrupted U.S. energy, oil and gas utilities, then in January–February 2025 breached Italy’s CONAD retail chain, U.S. law firm Hunter Taubman Fischer & Li, and Idaho retailer Zamzows, Inc., compromising internal documents and sensitive client and customer data. Initial access leverages phishing (T1566.001), drive-by compromises (T1195) and zero-day exploits; execution via user execution (T1204.002) and scripting interpreters (T1059.001); persistence through autostart mechanisms (T1070.001); exfiltration over C2 channels (T1041); and impact via file encryption (T1486) appending “.LYNX.” Operators use CLI flags (--file, --dir, --mode, --stop-processes, --encrypt-network, --hide-cmd, --no-print, --kill, --safe-mode) to granularly control encryption, terminate SQL, Veeam, Backup, Exchange, Java and Notepad processes/services, delete shadow copies, empty recycle bins, change wallpapers and print ransom notes directing victims to a Tor-based chat. Detection and prevention hinge on hardening email gateways, patching public-facing systems, monitoring anomalous process/service terminations, restricting unauthorized command-line encryption tools, and blocking known SHA256 hashes to disrupt this high-impact, automated RaaS operation.

hits.text: Security researchers at McAfee first observed Operation Sharpshooter in October–November 2018, a sophisticated phishing campaign targeting 87 critical‐infrastructure organizations—predominantly in the United States—including nuclear, defense, energy and financial firms, via recruitment‐style Microsoft Word attachments containing weaponized macros that load an in‐memory downloader to fetch a second‐stage implant dubbed Rising Sun; this implant, which exfiltrates host data to a command server, incorporates publicly available Lazarus Group source code as a likely false flag rather than evidence of Lazarus involvement. McAfee analysts Ryan Sherstobitoff and Asheer Malhotra note that Rising Sun’s multi‐step execution—weaponized document, in‐memory downloader, intelligence‐gathering implant—highlights the continued efficacy of social‐engineering vectors, while experts from CipherCloud, Positive Technologies and Lucy Security emphasize that defenses must go beyond spam filters to include ongoing user awareness training, holistic people-and-technology security models, robust data protection, network visibility and rapid incident response to detect and halt such advanced, evolving threats.
hits.title: Operation Sharpshooter targets infrastructure around the world | TechTarget

canonical_entities: Palo Alto Networks Cortex XDR Anti-Ransomware
hits.text: Following the sale of INC ransomware source code in March 2024 and its initial appearance in August 2023, researchers in July 2024 uncovered Lynx ransomware, a Windows-only, C++-based RaaS variant that shares ~48% of INC’s functions (70.8% among common routines) and has been deployed against U.S. and U.K. retail, real estate, architecture, financial and environmental service firms via phishing, malicious downloads and underground forums; employing AES-128-CTR and Curve25519 Donna for encryption with a .lynx extension, it conducts double-extortion by exfiltrating victims’ data (published on lynxblog[.]net under a policy excluding governments, hospitals and non-profits) before encrypting all files by default—killing processes, encrypting network shares and hidden disks, deleting shadow copies and backups, leveraging the Restart Manager API to target in-use files, and printing a OneNote report—then dropping a README.txt ransom note; this evolution of RaaS underscores the need for organizations to adopt robust cybersecurity measures, including anti-phishing training, backup hardening, dynamic and behavioral detections via Palo Alto Networks’ Cortex XDR Anti-Ransomware and Advanced WildFire, and vigilant monitoring of Indicators of Compromise such as published SHA256 hashes to mitigate high-profile, code-reused ransomware campaigns.
hits.title: Lynx Ransomware: A Rebranding of INC Ransomware

canonical_entities: automated encrypted exfiltration over C2 channels
hits.text: McAfee’s Advanced Threat Research team uncovered “Operation Sharpshooter,” a global cyber-espionage campaign targeting nuclear, defense, energy and financial organizations via weaponized Office documents masquerading as recruitment materials; an initial macro‐enabled loader drops an in‐memory implant that retrieves a second‐stage backdoor dubbed “Rising Sun,” which leverages source code from Lazarus Group’s 2015 Duuzer Trojan to perform account, file/directory, process and system/network discovery, process injection and automated encrypted exfiltration over C2 channels (e.g., 34.214.99.20/view_style.php); from October to November 2018 McAfee telemetry identified at least 87 predominantly English-speaking targets, with key IOCs including hashes such as 8106a30bd35526bded384627d8eebce15da35d17 and document URLs like hxxp://208.117.44.112/Strategic Planning Manager.doc, detectable by McAfee signatures RDN/Generic Downloader.x and Rising-Sun, and mitigated by monitoring macro executions, anomalous process injections and outbound C2 traffic while the broader community assesses attribution and monitors for follow-on exploitation.
hits.title: ‘Operation Sharpshooter’ Targets Global Defense, Critical Infrastructure | McAfee Blog

hits.text: Moses Staff, an Iran-linked APT active since September 2021, has conducted politically motivated sabotage campaigns—initially against Israeli organizations and later targets in India, Germany, the U.S., Italy, Chile, Turkey and the UAE—by exploiting known public-facing server vulnerabilities (e.g., Microsoft Exchange), moving laterally with PsExec, WMIC and PowerShell, and deploying a two-stage destructive toolkit: a Python-based loader (PyDCrypt) that installs a custom DiskCryptor variant (DCSrv) to encrypt files and disrupt operations without ransom demands, and, as newly documented by Cybereason, the StrifeWater RAT masquerading as calc.exe to establish early footholds, harvest system metadata (machine name, OS version, CPU architecture, user privileges, time zone), execute commands, capture screens, maintain persistence via scheduled tasks, and download auxiliary modules before self-removal—all while communicating with hard-coded C2 IPs, URLs and domain names—to evade detection; organizations should urgently patch exposed servers, monitor anomalous calc.exe and scheduled-task activity, and enhance EDR rules to detect PyDCrypt, DCSrv and StrifeWater behaviors to thwart data exfiltration and infrastructure damage.
hits.title: Iranian APT group uses previously undocumented Trojan for destructive access to organizations

hits.text: In August, the DPRK–linked APT TA444 (aka APT38, BlueNoroff, BlackAlicanto, Coperenicum, Sapphire Sleet and Stardust Chollima) deployed SpectralBlur, a custom post-exploitation macOS backdoor that leverages command-and-control instructions to upload/download files, spawn a shell, update its configuration, delete files or enter hibernation/sleep mode; Proofpoint researcher Greg Lesnewich identified code overlaps with the KandyKorn macOS data stealer—earlier tied to Lazarus Group phishing campaigns against blockchain engineers—linking both tools through shared strings and infrastructure. This rapid iteration of proprietary macOS malware underscores TA444’s dedicated development capability and signals an intensified DPRK espionage focus on Apple users, particularly within the cryptocurrency sector, demonstrating persistent operational tempo and advanced post-exploitation tactics.
hits.title: North Korea Debuts 'SpectralBlur' Malware Amid macOS Onslaught

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: Since its emergence in 2013, Iran-linked APT35 (aka Charming Kitten/Phosphorus) has executed a series of high-value espionage campaigns—beginning with a 2014 social-media spying operation—and continued in 2019 with spear-phishing against U.S., French and Middle East academic institutions before Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit seized control of 99 APT35 domains; in late 2020 the group targeted oncology, genetics and neurology researchers in Israel and the U.S. via its “BadBlood” PDF-based spear-phishing campaign, while in 2021 it chained Exchange Server flaws (ProxyShell) for network intrusion and demonstrated TTP overlaps with Momento ransomware (CVE-2021-21972 exploiter); in January 2022 it performed mass Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) scans—over 80 percent of attempts originated in the U.S.—and later deployed a stealthy .NET-based PowerShell backdoor (“PowerLess”) that runs in-process to avoid detection, followed by Hyperscrape, a Windows .NET mailbox exfiltration tool for Outlook, Gmail and Yahoo! that quietly harvests emails once the actor possesses valid credentials or session cookies, and a companion Telegram dump utility; APT35 maintains persistence for intelligence collection or monetizes access when systems lack strategic value, underscoring the need for timely patching, multi-factor authentication and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at APT35 aka Charming Kitten

hits.text: ESET researchers have traced the China-aligned hacker group FishMonger, aka Aquatic Panda, and its global espionage campaign “FishMedley” back to the iSoon APT contractor (Axun Information Technology) operating under the Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security and PLA, following the U.S. DOJ’s addition of key members to the FBI’s Most Wanted list; FishMonger’s modus operandi relies on compromising high-privilege user accounts—likely harvested via phishing or credential theft—to gain domain administrator access, then deploying publicly available modular backdoors and loaders (ShadowPad, Spyder loader, SodaMaster) and the RPipeCommander reverse shell rather than zero-day exploits, enabling sustained infiltration of governmental bodies, Catholic charities, NGOs and think tanks across Taiwan, Hungary, Turkey, Thailand, the U.S. and France; while technically unsophisticated, the group’s efficient use of known tools has yielded consistent exfiltration of confidential data, underscoring the need for potential targets to hunt for these specific indicators of compromise and strengthen monitoring of privileged accounts.
hits.title: Chinese Hacker Group Tracked Back to iSoon APT Operation

canonical_entities: dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora
hits.text: Since at least September 2023, the China-aligned Evasive Panda APT (aka BRONZE HIGHLAND/Daggerfly) has conducted a dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora by compromising both the Kagyu International Monlam Trust’s website and the official Monlam translation-software supply chain—first implanting obfuscated JavaScript into jquery.js on the festival site that verifies victims’ first three IP octets via an MD5 hash salted with “1qaz0okm!@#,” serves a faux “Aw, Snap!” error page to users in India, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Australia and the U.S., and lures them to download a malicious “certificate.exe” or “.pkg” downloader; that loader side-loads memmgrset.dll (http_dy.dll) to fetch a JSON config from update.devicebug[.]com and ultimately deploys the undocumented Nightdoor backdoor alongside the group’s modular MgBot implant, while a trojanized Monlam software installer (Windows autorun.exe abusing MonlamUpdate.exe for DLL side-loading of RPHost.dll, and macOS Mach-O downloaders) has delivered further downloaders and payloads—retrieved from tibetpost[.]net and a direct IP—to %TEMP%\default_ico.exe for additional Nightdoor and MgBot installation.
hits.title: Evasive Panda leverages Monlam Festival to target Tibetans

hits.text: Since mid-2021, Microsoft has tracked Volt Typhoon, a China-linked state-sponsored actor, conducting stealthy living-off-the-land campaigns against U.S. critical infrastructure—spanning communications, utilities, transportation, manufacturing, government and education—aimed at post-compromise credential access, network discovery and long-term espionage with an eye toward potential disruption of Asia-U.S. communications in future crises. Initial access is achieved via internet-exposed Fortinet FortiGuard devices, whose AD credentials are harvested to move laterally; all traffic is proxied through compromised SOHO routers, firewalls and VPN hardware (ASUS, Cisco, D-Link, NETGEAR, Zyxel) to blend with legitimate activity. Post-compromise hands-on-keyboard operations rely almost exclusively on LOLBins and valid credentials to dump LSASS memory and use Ntdsutil.exe to create domain controller installation media for offline hash cracking, enumerate systems via PowerShell, WMIC and ping, collect browser and system data into staged archives, then exfiltrate via password-protected files. In rare cases, Volt Typhoon deploys custom Impacket or FRP-based C2 over portproxy, observable as unusual successful sign-ins and command-line activity from anomalous IPs. Detection is challenging due to use of built-in binaries and normal sign-in channels; Microsoft 365 Defender and cloud-delivered Microsoft Defender Antivirus yield behavioral alerts (e.g., SuspPowershellExec, SuspNtdsUtilUsage), while Defender for Endpoint flags suspicious LSASS dumps, wmic.exe executions and domain-controller media creation. Mitigation hinges on closing or rotating compromised accounts, enforcing strong MFA or passwordless authentication, disabling internet-facing device management interfaces, enabling LSASS Protective Process Light and Credential Guard on Windows 11, applying attack surface reduction rules to block LSASS and PSExec/WMI abuse, and running EDR in block mode to thwart post-compromise artifacts.
hits.title: Volt Typhoon targets US critical infrastructure with living-off-the-land techniques | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.title: Chinese Hacker Group Tracked Back to iSoon APT Operation

canonical_entities: lateral movement to additional cloud resources
hits.text: Attackers exploited an unpatched SQL injection vulnerability in an application to gain elevated permissions on a Microsoft SQL Server instance running in an Azure VM, then enumerated databases, schemas, network settings and enabled xp_cmdshell via “sp_configure” commands to execute OS-level commands, deploy encoded PowerShell scripts, establish persistence via scheduled tasks, dump SAM and SECURITY hives, and exfiltrate data discreetly using webhook[.]site. In a novel twist on known techniques, they attempted lateral movement to additional cloud resources by querying the Azure Instance Metadata Service (169.254.169.254) to obtain the managed identity’s OAuth2 token and abuse its privileges, but the move failed due to an error. Microsoft Defender for SQL triggered alerts for potential SQL injection, abnormal shell spawning, and IMDS calls from SQL Server, while Defender for Cloud and Defender for Endpoint provide further visibility into anomalous cloud-identity and xp_cmdshell activity. Although no breach of downstream cloud services was confirmed, this case underscores the critical need to enforce least privilege on managed identities, disable or tightly control xp_cmdshell, patch applications, monitor metadata endpoint access, and leverage Defender XDR’s detection capabilities to thwart SQL Server–to-cloud lateral movement.
hits.title: Defending new vectors: Threat actors attempt SQL Server to cloud lateral movement | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: harvest subscriber location, billing and communications metadata
hits.text: On Sept. 25, 2024, the Wall Street Journal disclosed that the Chinese state-sponsored APT Salt Typhoon has stealthily infiltrated multiple U.S. cable and broadband ISPs—likely via firmware and supply-chain compromises in core networking gear—to establish long-term persistence, harvest subscriber location, billing and communications metadata for espionage, and pre-position disruptive capabilities against federal, military and Fortune 100 users; this campaign, echoing Volt Typhoon’s telecom backdoors, Flax Typhoon’s 200,000-device IoT botnet, Brass Typhoon’s cross-domain implants and Mustang Panda’s telco intrusions, signals a shift from surveillance to offensive “blink-the-lights” or infrastructure-crippling attacks in a Taiwan contingency, driving urgent recommendations for carriers to enforce threat-intelligence sharing, secure firmware, tighten supply-chain controls and bolster routing security.
