hits.text: Lynx ransomware, emerging in July 2024 as the INC ransomware successor under a Ransomware-as-a-Service model, employs a sophisticated double-extortion strategy—exfiltrating data prior to encryption and threatening publication on a leak site—and reuses significant INC source code. Between July and November 2024, it disrupted U.S. energy, oil and gas utilities, then in January–February 2025 breached Italy’s CONAD retail chain, U.S. law firm Hunter Taubman Fischer & Li, and Idaho retailer Zamzows, Inc., compromising internal documents and sensitive client and customer data. Initial access leverages phishing (T1566.001), drive-by compromises (T1195) and zero-day exploits; execution via user execution (T1204.002) and scripting interpreters (T1059.001); persistence through autostart mechanisms (T1070.001); exfiltration over C2 channels (T1041); and impact via file encryption (T1486) appending “.LYNX.” Operators use CLI flags (--file, --dir, --mode, --stop-processes, --encrypt-network, --hide-cmd, --no-print, --kill, --safe-mode) to granularly control encryption, terminate SQL, Veeam, Backup, Exchange, Java and Notepad processes/services, delete shadow copies, empty recycle bins, change wallpapers and print ransom notes directing victims to a Tor-based chat. Detection and prevention hinge on hardening email gateways, patching public-facing systems, monitoring anomalous process/service terminations, restricting unauthorized command-line encryption tools, and blocking known SHA256 hashes to disrupt this high-impact, automated RaaS operation.
hits.title: Lynx Ransomware: INC Ransomware Reincarnated - Threat Actors

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has uncovered a supply chain attack by the North Korean group Diamond Sleet in which a legitimate CyberLink Corp. multimedia installer was trojanized—tracked as LambLoad (SHA-256 166d1a6ddcde4e859a89c2c825cd3c8c953a86bfa92b343de7e5bfbfb5afb8be) and signed with a valid CyberLink code-signing certificate—and hosted on CyberLink’s own update infrastructure; the loader enforces a narrow execution window, checks for EDR processes (CrowdStrike’s csfalconservice.exe, FireEye’s xagt.exe, Tanium’s taniumclient.exe) to evade detection, then downloads, decrypts, and in-memory loads a second-stage payload masquerading as a PNG file (SHA-256 089573b3a1167f387dcdad5e014a5132e998b2c89bff29bcf8b06dd497d4e63d; decrypted PE 915c2495e03ff7408f11a2a197f23344004c533ff87db4b807cc937f80c217a1) from compromised domains before calling back for commands; observed since October 2023 on over 100 devices across Japan, Taiwan, Canada, and the US and targeting IT, defense, and media organizations for espionage and data theft, Microsoft has alerted CyberLink, notified Defender for Endpoint customers, reported the payload to GitHub for takedown, blacklisted the abused certificate, published detections (Trojan:Win32/LambLoad; Diamond Sleet activity group alerts), provided hunting queries and IOCs, and recommended cloud-delivered protection, network protection, automated remediation, attack surface reduction rules, and immediate isolation and credential resets upon compromise.
hits.title: Diamond Sleet supply chain compromise distributes a modified CyberLink installer | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Moses Staff, an Iran-linked APT active since September 2021, has conducted politically motivated sabotage campaigns—initially against Israeli organizations and later targets in India, Germany, the U.S., Italy, Chile, Turkey and the UAE—by exploiting known public-facing server vulnerabilities (e.g., Microsoft Exchange), moving laterally with PsExec, WMIC and PowerShell, and deploying a two-stage destructive toolkit: a Python-based loader (PyDCrypt) that installs a custom DiskCryptor variant (DCSrv) to encrypt files and disrupt operations without ransom demands, and, as newly documented by Cybereason, the StrifeWater RAT masquerading as calc.exe to establish early footholds, harvest system metadata (machine name, OS version, CPU architecture, user privileges, time zone), execute commands, capture screens, maintain persistence via scheduled tasks, and download auxiliary modules before self-removal—all while communicating with hard-coded C2 IPs, URLs and domain names—to evade detection; organizations should urgently patch exposed servers, monitor anomalous calc.exe and scheduled-task activity, and enhance EDR rules to detect PyDCrypt, DCSrv and StrifeWater behaviors to thwart data exfiltration and infrastructure damage.
hits.title: Iranian APT group uses previously undocumented Trojan for destructive access to organizations

retrieved_context.text: Security researchers at McAfee first observed Operation Sharpshooter in October–November 2018, a sophisticated phishing campaign targeting 87 critical‐infrastructure organizations—predominantly in the United States—including nuclear, defense, energy and financial firms, via recruitment‐style Microsoft Word attachments containing weaponized macros that load an in‐memory downloader to fetch a second‐stage implant dubbed Rising Sun; this implant, which exfiltrates host data to a command server, incorporates publicly available Lazarus Group source code as a likely false flag rather than evidence of Lazarus involvement. McAfee analysts Ryan Sherstobitoff and Asheer Malhotra note that Rising Sun’s multi‐step execution—weaponized document, in‐memory downloader, intelligence‐gathering implant—highlights the continued efficacy of social‐engineering vectors, while experts from CipherCloud, Positive Technologies and Lucy Security emphasize that defenses must go beyond spam filters to include ongoing user awareness training, holistic people-and-technology security models, robust data protection, network visibility and rapid incident response to detect and halt such advanced, evolving threats.
retrieved_context.title: Operation Sharpshooter targets infrastructure around the world | TechTarget

canonical_entities: automated encrypted exfiltration over C2 channels
retrieved_context.text: McAfee’s Advanced Threat Research team uncovered “Operation Sharpshooter,” a global cyber-espionage campaign targeting nuclear, defense, energy and financial organizations via weaponized Office documents masquerading as recruitment materials; an initial macro‐enabled loader drops an in‐memory implant that retrieves a second‐stage backdoor dubbed “Rising Sun,” which leverages source code from Lazarus Group’s 2015 Duuzer Trojan to perform account, file/directory, process and system/network discovery, process injection and automated encrypted exfiltration over C2 channels (e.g., 34.214.99.20/view_style.php); from October to November 2018 McAfee telemetry identified at least 87 predominantly English-speaking targets, with key IOCs including hashes such as 8106a30bd35526bded384627d8eebce15da35d17 and document URLs like hxxp://208.117.44.112/Strategic Planning Manager.doc, detectable by McAfee signatures RDN/Generic Downloader.x and Rising-Sun, and mitigated by monitoring macro executions, anomalous process injections and outbound C2 traffic while the broader community assesses attribution and monitors for follow-on exploitation.
retrieved_context.title: ‘Operation Sharpshooter’ Targets Global Defense, Critical Infrastructure | McAfee Blog

retrieved_context.text: In August, the DPRK–linked APT TA444 (aka APT38, BlueNoroff, BlackAlicanto, Coperenicum, Sapphire Sleet and Stardust Chollima) deployed SpectralBlur, a custom post-exploitation macOS backdoor that leverages command-and-control instructions to upload/download files, spawn a shell, update its configuration, delete files or enter hibernation/sleep mode; Proofpoint researcher Greg Lesnewich identified code overlaps with the KandyKorn macOS data stealer—earlier tied to Lazarus Group phishing campaigns against blockchain engineers—linking both tools through shared strings and infrastructure. This rapid iteration of proprietary macOS malware underscores TA444’s dedicated development capability and signals an intensified DPRK espionage focus on Apple users, particularly within the cryptocurrency sector, demonstrating persistent operational tempo and advanced post-exploitation tactics.
retrieved_context.title: North Korea Debuts 'SpectralBlur' Malware Amid macOS Onslaught

canonical_entities: Palo Alto Networks Cortex XDR Anti-Ransomware
retrieved_context.text: Following the sale of INC ransomware source code in March 2024 and its initial appearance in August 2023, researchers in July 2024 uncovered Lynx ransomware, a Windows-only, C++-based RaaS variant that shares ~48% of INC’s functions (70.8% among common routines) and has been deployed against U.S. and U.K. retail, real estate, architecture, financial and environmental service firms via phishing, malicious downloads and underground forums; employing AES-128-CTR and Curve25519 Donna for encryption with a .lynx extension, it conducts double-extortion by exfiltrating victims’ data (published on lynxblog[.]net under a policy excluding governments, hospitals and non-profits) before encrypting all files by default—killing processes, encrypting network shares and hidden disks, deleting shadow copies and backups, leveraging the Restart Manager API to target in-use files, and printing a OneNote report—then dropping a README.txt ransom note; this evolution of RaaS underscores the need for organizations to adopt robust cybersecurity measures, including anti-phishing training, backup hardening, dynamic and behavioral detections via Palo Alto Networks’ Cortex XDR Anti-Ransomware and Advanced WildFire, and vigilant monitoring of Indicators of Compromise such as published SHA256 hashes to mitigate high-profile, code-reused ransomware campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Lynx Ransomware: A Rebranding of INC Ransomware

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: Kaspersky’s Unified Monitoring and Analysis Platform (KUMA)
hits.text: Operation Triangulation is a sophisticated, zero-click iMessage exploit campaign active since 2019 and observed as recently as June 2023 targeting iOS up to 15.7, in which threat actors deliver an encrypted attachment that automatically triggers a vulnerability, spawns IMTransferAgent to fetch and delete the initial exploit, invokes the deprecated BackupAgent process to download privilege-escalation stages and a final root-level APT payload capable of arbitrary code execution and data exfiltration. Analysts using Kaspersky’s Unified Monitoring and Analysis Platform (KUMA) generated offline iTunes or idevicebackup2 backups and parsed them with the Mobile Verification Toolkit (mvt-ios) to produce “timeline.csv” super-timelines, reliably detecting compromise via BackupAgent data-usage entries, SMS attachment directory modifications, plist changes (com.apple.ImageIO, com.apple.locationd.StatusBarIconManager, com.apple.imservice.ids.FaceTime), anomalous WebKit data flows and failed iOS updates due to tampered com.apple.softwareupdateservicesd.plist. Network indicators include ~242 KB HTTPS downloads from *.icloud-content.com followed by heavy traffic to C2 domains such as addatamarket[.]net, backuprabbit[.]com, cloudsponcer[.]com and others. Since the malware lacks persistence—devices clear on reboot but can be reinfected—defenders should implement full backups, routine mvt-ios scans, DNS/NetFlow monitoring for known C2 domains and map the campaign against MITRE ATT&CK’s newly created Operation Triangulation framework entry.
hits.title: Operation Triangulation: iOS devices targeted with previously unknown malware

hits.text: Operation RoundPress, attributed with medium confidence to Russian state-sponsored APT28 (Fancy Bear), has since 2023 exploited stored and reflected XSS flaws in widely used webmail platforms—initially leveraging Roundcube CVE-2020-35730 to inject malicious JavaScript into email bodies, then CVE-2023-43770 and additional n-day vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra in early 2024—to execute upon email open without clicks or redirects. Through spear-phishing emails crafted with timely political or news excerpts, the hidden script auto-fills victim credentials via invisible input fields, scrapes DOM content—including emails, contacts, webmail settings, login history, 2FA tokens and passwords—and exfiltrates data via HTTP POST to hardcoded C2 servers. Targets span high-value government entities in Greece, Ukraine, Serbia and Cameroon, military units in Ukraine and Ecuador, defense contractors in Ukraine, Bulgaria and Romania, and critical infrastructure in Ukraine and Bulgaria. The lack of persistence mechanisms confines execution to session scope but underscores the necessity for timely patching of XSS vulnerabilities, disabling HTML rendering in webmail clients, enforcing strict input sanitization and multifactor authentication, and monitoring anomalous outbound traffic to mitigate credential theft and data exfiltration.
hits.title: Government webmail hacked via XSS bugs in global spy campaign

canonical_entities: malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails
hits.text: Attackers are leveraging the six-year-old CVE-2017-11882 Microsoft Office RCE vulnerability via malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails to initiate a multi-stage infection chain that delivers the Agent Tesla RAT and advanced keylogger. Once a user opens the Excel file on an unpatched Office build, it connects to a malicious server to retrieve a heavily obfuscated VBS script, which in turn downloads a JPEG containing a Base64-encoded DLL. The VBS launches PowerShell to extract and load the DLL, then abuses RegAsm.exe—disguised as a legitimate registry utility—to inject a thread that fetches and executes the Agent Tesla payload. Deployed Agent Tesla uses clipboard and window hooking for keystroke logging, screen capture and browser, mail and FTP credential theft, exfiltrating data via attacker-controlled Telegram bots. Zscaler’s detailed IoCs—including malicious URLs, file hashes and Telegram endpoints—underscore the critical need for organizations to patch legacy Office versions, deploy email defenses, and monitor for the described artifacts to prevent credential compromise and system takeover.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit 6-Year-Old Microsoft Office Bug to Spread Spyware

hits.text: On Oct. 10, 2023, Citrix released patches for Netscaler ADC and Gateway to address Citrix Bleed (CVE-2023-4966, CVSS 9.4), a memory-leak vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to exfiltrate session tokens via crafted requests and hijack sessions; public proof-of-concept code from Assetnote and Python exploit scripts rapidly empowered ransomware affiliates and other threat actors to gain footholds, with Unit 42 Incident Response and Managed Threat Hunting teams observing exploitation-linked remote PowerShell sessions spawning cmd.exe, reconnaissance commands (whoami, WMIC, tasklist, net user), deployment of XScan (s.exe), Python HTTP servers, and mRemoteNG on VDI hosts—though no lateral movement beyond VDI was detected. Cortex Xpanse identified nearly 8,000 exposed Netscaler Gateway and 6,000 ADC IPs worldwide (3,100 US, 800 Germany, 450 China, 400 UK), prompting addition to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog. Palo Alto Networks advises immediate patching (including CVE-2023-4967), engagement of Unit 42 for incident response and continuous hunting, deployment of Next-Generation Firewalls with Advanced Threat Prevention signature 94483, updated Advanced WildFire ML models, Cortex Xpanse Threat Response Event, and Cortex XDR/XSIAM behavioral, anti-webshell, and credential-gathering protections to detect and block post-exploitation activity.
hits.title: Threat Brief: Citrix Bleed CVE-2023-4966

hits.text: Active since at least 2004 and linked to the Russian GRU, APT28 (Fancy Bear, Forest Blizzard, Sednit, Sofacy) has been exploiting XSS vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra mail servers across Europe, Africa and South America since September 2023 under “Operation RoundPress,” targeting governments tied to the Ukraine conflict—such as Ukraine’s government and defense firms in Bulgaria and Romania—and more broadly French organizations after France’s recent attribution of a dozen government and other entities, including a decade-old TV5Monde attack. Employing CVE-2020-35730 (Roundcube; CISA KEV June 2023), CVE-2023-43770 (Roundcube; KEV February 2024) and zero-day CVE-2024-11182 (MDaemon), APT28 injects malicious JavaScript implants (“SpyPress”) via phishing emails that bypass spam filters and execute in the victim’s browser context to steal webmail credentials through hidden forms or counterfeit login pages, harvest messages and contacts, create forwarding rules, and defeat two-factor authentication. ESET’s findings highlight the convenience of remote-triggered webmail XSS, the prevalence of unpatched servers, and the urgent need for organizations to apply KEV-listed patches, enforce robust email filtering, and monitor for anomalous mailbox behaviors to mitigate email exfiltration and credential compromise.
hits.title: Russian APT Exploiting Mail Servers Against Government, Defense Organizations - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
hits.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: On November 29, 2023, Google’s Threat Analysis Group disclosed and patched CVE-2023-6345, an actively exploited integer-overflow vulnerability in the Skia 2D graphics library that permits sandbox escape via a malicious file on Chrome versions prior to 119.0.6045.199—its seventh zero-day this year and fourth since August—underscoring a broader surge of critical browser flaws such as WebP heap overflow CVE-2023-4863 impacting Chrome, Safari and Firefox; Chromium-fork bug CVE-2023-5217 in Edge, Opera, Brave and Vivaldi; and four Apple WebKit zero-days (CVE-2023-28205, ‑32409, ‑28204, ‑32373) that commercial spyware vendors like Predator and likely state-sponsored actors have exploited to drop malware, steal credentials and exfiltrate data. Experts attribute this trend to browsers’ ubiquitous role in delivering web applications, expanded device-access features (USB, Bluetooth, WebGPU) and Chromium’s cross-platform reach, which amplifies an exploit’s impact across multiple browsers; they recommend organizations prioritize rigorous patch management, real-time version tracking and strict network segmentation to contain infection pathways and mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: Google Patches Another Chrome Zero-Day as Browser Attacks Mount

hits.text: Kaspersky researchers have uncovered a new variant of the multi-stage Necro Trojan—first observed in 2019’s CamScanner compromise—that over recent weeks infected two Google Play apps (Wuta Camera, 10 M+ downloads; Max Browser, 1 M+ downloads) and unofficial mods for Spotify, WhatsApp and popular games by exploiting an untrusted advertising-integration SDK; in the Spotify mod the SDK exfiltrated device/app data to a known Necro C&C server and fetched a payload hidden in an image, while in the WhatsApp mod a loader abused Firebase Remote Config for C&C before deploying identical Necro payloads sharing code, structure and C&C infrastructure. Once installed, Necro’s latest variant downloads modules to display and click invisible ads, execute JavaScript in hidden WebViews, download executables and third-party apps, redirect traffic through compromised devices as proxies and subscribe victims to premium services. Between August 26 and September 15, tens of thousands of devices in Russia, Brazil, Vietnam, Ecuador and Mexico were targeted before Google removed the infected apps. Organizations should rigorously vet third-party SDKs, monitor remote-config channels and anomalous network traffic for image-based payload retrieval and invisible ad click-fraud behaviors to mitigate this evolving mobile threat.
hits.title: Necro Trojan Infects Google Play Apps With Millions of Downloads - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Google has released Chrome 120.0.6099.129/130 updates to patch an actively exploited high-severity zero-day (CVE-2023-7024), a heap-based buffer overflow in the WebRTC framework that enables crashes or arbitrary code execution, discovered by TAG researchers Clément Lecigne and Vlad Stolyarov on December 19, 2023. This marks the eighth Chrome zero-day exploited in the wild this year—following type confusion flaws in V8 (CVE-2023-2033, CVSS 8.8; CVE-2023-2136, CVSS 9.6; CVE-2023-3079, CVSS 8.8; CVE-2023-4762, CVSS 8.8), a heap overflow in WebP (CVE-2023-4863, CVSS 8.8), a heap overflow in libvpx (CVE-2023-5217, CVSS 8.8) and an integer overflow in Skia (CVE-2023-6345, CVSS 9.6)—amid a record 26,447 CVEs disclosed in 2023, 115 of which have been weaponized by threat actors and ransomware groups using remote code execution, security-feature bypass, buffer manipulation, privilege escalation and input-validation flaws. Given WebRTC’s cross-browser support, impacts on Firefox and Safari remain under assessment. Administrators and end users should immediately upgrade Chrome for Windows, macOS and Linux and apply forthcoming patches for Chromium-based browsers (Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi) to mitigate potential compromise.
hits.title: Urgent: New Chrome Zero-Day Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild - Update ASAP

retrieval_events.query: What vulnerabilities (CVEs) were exploited in this campaign?

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: Kaspersky’s Unified Monitoring and Analysis Platform (KUMA)
retrieved_context.text: Operation Triangulation is a sophisticated, zero-click iMessage exploit campaign active since 2019 and observed as recently as June 2023 targeting iOS up to 15.7, in which threat actors deliver an encrypted attachment that automatically triggers a vulnerability, spawns IMTransferAgent to fetch and delete the initial exploit, invokes the deprecated BackupAgent process to download privilege-escalation stages and a final root-level APT payload capable of arbitrary code execution and data exfiltration. Analysts using Kaspersky’s Unified Monitoring and Analysis Platform (KUMA) generated offline iTunes or idevicebackup2 backups and parsed them with the Mobile Verification Toolkit (mvt-ios) to produce “timeline.csv” super-timelines, reliably detecting compromise via BackupAgent data-usage entries, SMS attachment directory modifications, plist changes (com.apple.ImageIO, com.apple.locationd.StatusBarIconManager, com.apple.imservice.ids.FaceTime), anomalous WebKit data flows and failed iOS updates due to tampered com.apple.softwareupdateservicesd.plist. Network indicators include ~242 KB HTTPS downloads from *.icloud-content.com followed by heavy traffic to C2 domains such as addatamarket[.]net, backuprabbit[.]com, cloudsponcer[.]com and others. Since the malware lacks persistence—devices clear on reboot but can be reinfected—defenders should implement full backups, routine mvt-ios scans, DNS/NetFlow monitoring for known C2 domains and map the campaign against MITRE ATT&CK’s newly created Operation Triangulation framework entry.
retrieved_context.title: Operation Triangulation: iOS devices targeted with previously unknown malware

retrieved_context.text: Operation RoundPress, attributed with medium confidence to Russian state-sponsored APT28 (Fancy Bear), has since 2023 exploited stored and reflected XSS flaws in widely used webmail platforms—initially leveraging Roundcube CVE-2020-35730 to inject malicious JavaScript into email bodies, then CVE-2023-43770 and additional n-day vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra in early 2024—to execute upon email open without clicks or redirects. Through spear-phishing emails crafted with timely political or news excerpts, the hidden script auto-fills victim credentials via invisible input fields, scrapes DOM content—including emails, contacts, webmail settings, login history, 2FA tokens and passwords—and exfiltrates data via HTTP POST to hardcoded C2 servers. Targets span high-value government entities in Greece, Ukraine, Serbia and Cameroon, military units in Ukraine and Ecuador, defense contractors in Ukraine, Bulgaria and Romania, and critical infrastructure in Ukraine and Bulgaria. The lack of persistence mechanisms confines execution to session scope but underscores the necessity for timely patching of XSS vulnerabilities, disabling HTML rendering in webmail clients, enforcing strict input sanitization and multifactor authentication, and monitoring anomalous outbound traffic to mitigate credential theft and data exfiltration.
retrieved_context.title: Government webmail hacked via XSS bugs in global spy campaign

canonical_entities: malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails
retrieved_context.text: Attackers are leveraging the six-year-old CVE-2017-11882 Microsoft Office RCE vulnerability via malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails to initiate a multi-stage infection chain that delivers the Agent Tesla RAT and advanced keylogger. Once a user opens the Excel file on an unpatched Office build, it connects to a malicious server to retrieve a heavily obfuscated VBS script, which in turn downloads a JPEG containing a Base64-encoded DLL. The VBS launches PowerShell to extract and load the DLL, then abuses RegAsm.exe—disguised as a legitimate registry utility—to inject a thread that fetches and executes the Agent Tesla payload. Deployed Agent Tesla uses clipboard and window hooking for keystroke logging, screen capture and browser, mail and FTP credential theft, exfiltrating data via attacker-controlled Telegram bots. Zscaler’s detailed IoCs—including malicious URLs, file hashes and Telegram endpoints—underscore the critical need for organizations to patch legacy Office versions, deploy email defenses, and monitor for the described artifacts to prevent credential compromise and system takeover.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit 6-Year-Old Microsoft Office Bug to Spread Spyware

retrieved_context.text: On Oct. 10, 2023, Citrix released patches for Netscaler ADC and Gateway to address Citrix Bleed (CVE-2023-4966, CVSS 9.4), a memory-leak vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to exfiltrate session tokens via crafted requests and hijack sessions; public proof-of-concept code from Assetnote and Python exploit scripts rapidly empowered ransomware affiliates and other threat actors to gain footholds, with Unit 42 Incident Response and Managed Threat Hunting teams observing exploitation-linked remote PowerShell sessions spawning cmd.exe, reconnaissance commands (whoami, WMIC, tasklist, net user), deployment of XScan (s.exe), Python HTTP servers, and mRemoteNG on VDI hosts—though no lateral movement beyond VDI was detected. Cortex Xpanse identified nearly 8,000 exposed Netscaler Gateway and 6,000 ADC IPs worldwide (3,100 US, 800 Germany, 450 China, 400 UK), prompting addition to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog. Palo Alto Networks advises immediate patching (including CVE-2023-4967), engagement of Unit 42 for incident response and continuous hunting, deployment of Next-Generation Firewalls with Advanced Threat Prevention signature 94483, updated Advanced WildFire ML models, Cortex Xpanse Threat Response Event, and Cortex XDR/XSIAM behavioral, anti-webshell, and credential-gathering protections to detect and block post-exploitation activity.
retrieved_context.title: Threat Brief: Citrix Bleed CVE-2023-4966

retrieved_context.text: Active since at least 2004 and linked to the Russian GRU, APT28 (Fancy Bear, Forest Blizzard, Sednit, Sofacy) has been exploiting XSS vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra mail servers across Europe, Africa and South America since September 2023 under “Operation RoundPress,” targeting governments tied to the Ukraine conflict—such as Ukraine’s government and defense firms in Bulgaria and Romania—and more broadly French organizations after France’s recent attribution of a dozen government and other entities, including a decade-old TV5Monde attack. Employing CVE-2020-35730 (Roundcube; CISA KEV June 2023), CVE-2023-43770 (Roundcube; KEV February 2024) and zero-day CVE-2024-11182 (MDaemon), APT28 injects malicious JavaScript implants (“SpyPress”) via phishing emails that bypass spam filters and execute in the victim’s browser context to steal webmail credentials through hidden forms or counterfeit login pages, harvest messages and contacts, create forwarding rules, and defeat two-factor authentication. ESET’s findings highlight the convenience of remote-triggered webmail XSS, the prevalence of unpatched servers, and the urgent need for organizations to apply KEV-listed patches, enforce robust email filtering, and monitor for anomalous mailbox behaviors to mitigate email exfiltration and credential compromise.
retrieved_context.title: Russian APT Exploiting Mail Servers Against Government, Defense Organizations - SecurityWeek

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
retrieved_context.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: On November 29, 2023, Google’s Threat Analysis Group disclosed and patched CVE-2023-6345, an actively exploited integer-overflow vulnerability in the Skia 2D graphics library that permits sandbox escape via a malicious file on Chrome versions prior to 119.0.6045.199—its seventh zero-day this year and fourth since August—underscoring a broader surge of critical browser flaws such as WebP heap overflow CVE-2023-4863 impacting Chrome, Safari and Firefox; Chromium-fork bug CVE-2023-5217 in Edge, Opera, Brave and Vivaldi; and four Apple WebKit zero-days (CVE-2023-28205, ‑32409, ‑28204, ‑32373) that commercial spyware vendors like Predator and likely state-sponsored actors have exploited to drop malware, steal credentials and exfiltrate data. Experts attribute this trend to browsers’ ubiquitous role in delivering web applications, expanded device-access features (USB, Bluetooth, WebGPU) and Chromium’s cross-platform reach, which amplifies an exploit’s impact across multiple browsers; they recommend organizations prioritize rigorous patch management, real-time version tracking and strict network segmentation to contain infection pathways and mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: Google Patches Another Chrome Zero-Day as Browser Attacks Mount

attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
hits.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

hits.text: Citrix on Tuesday issued an urgent advisory to patch customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances against two actively exploited zero-days (CVE-2023-6548 enabling remote code execution with a logged-in low-privilege account via NSIP/CLIP/SNIP management interfaces and CVE-2023-6549 causing denial-of-service on VPN virtual servers or AAA virtual servers), affecting NetScaler ADC/Gateway 14.1 before 14.1-12.35, 13.1 before 13.1-51.15, 13.0 before 13.0-92.21, 13.1-FIPS before 13.1-37.176, and 12.1-FIPS/NDcPP before 12.1-55.302, with Shadowserver reporting over 1,500 exposed management interfaces worldwide; exploits have already been observed, prompting Citrix and the HHS HC3 to urge immediate installation of patched versions or, for those unable to update, logical or physical segregation of management interfaces, network traffic blocking, removal of internet exposure, and upgrade off end-of-life 12.1 releases to thwart potential ransomware and intrusion campaigns—an alert amplified by the October patch of a prior critical Netscaler flaw (CVE-2023-4966 “Citrix Bleed”) that threat actors have leveraged since August against government agencies and high-profile tech firms such as Boeing.
hits.title: Citrix warns of new Netscaler zero-days exploited in attacks

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

hits.text: Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has documented how over 30 commercial spyware vendors are selling 0-day and n-day exploits to government-backed actors, enabling targeted campaigns against dissidents, journalists and human rights workers on Android, iOS and Samsung Internet Browser; in November 2022, TAG observed a smishing campaign using bit.ly links to deliver two parallel exploit chains—on iOS (CVE-2022-42856 WebKit RCE with a PAC bypass technique also seen in Cytrox’s Predator, and CVE-2021-30900 AGXAccelerator sandbox escape) that installed a GPS-pinging IPA stager, and on Android (CVE-2022-3723 Chrome type confusion, CVE-2022-4135 GPU sandbox bypass analyzed by Sergei Glazunov, and CVE-2022-38181 ARM privilege escalation) with Intent redirection to Chrome—both remaining effective until patched in Chrome 107/108 and Pixel January 2023 updates; in December 2022, TAG uncovered a one-time SMS link campaign targeting UAE users via a Heliconia-style landing page delivering a C++-based Android spyware suite after chaining four faults—CVE-2022-4262 Chrome type confusion, CVE-2022-3038 Chrome sandbox escape, CVE-2022-22706 Mali GPU kernel exploit and CVE-2023-0266 Linux kernel race (with auxiliary info-leak 0-days)—against unpatched Samsung Internet Browser (Chromium 102), underscoring that smaller surveillance vendors now stockpile and share advanced exploits historically limited to nation-state developers, highlighting the critical need for immediate patch deployment, comprehensive mitigations (PAC, V8 sandbox, MiraclePTR) and continuous IOC monitoring to disrupt these highly targeted intrusion operations.
hits.title: Spyware vendors use 0-days and n-days against popular platforms

retrieved_context.title: Citrix warns of new Netscaler zero-days exploited in attacks

canonical_entities: malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails
retrieved_context.text: Attackers are leveraging the six-year-old CVE-2017-11882 Microsoft Office RCE vulnerability via malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails to initiate a multi-stage infection chain that delivers the Agent Tesla RAT and advanced keylogger. Once a user opens the Excel file on an unpatched Office build, it connects to a malicious server to retrieve a heavily obfuscated VBS script, which in turn downloads a JPEG containing a Base64-encoded DLL. The VBS launches PowerShell to extract and load the DLL, then abuses RegAsm.exe—disguised as a legitimate registry utility—to inject a thread that fetches and executes the Agent Tesla payload. Deployed Agent Tesla uses clipboard and window hooking for keystroke logging, screen capture and browser, mail and FTP credential theft, exfiltrating data via attacker-controlled Telegram bots. Zscaler’s detailed IoCs—including malicious URLs, file hashes and Telegram endpoints—underscore the critical need for organizations to patch legacy Office versions, deploy email defenses, and monitor for the described artifacts to prevent credential compromise and system takeover.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit 6-Year-Old Microsoft Office Bug to Spread Spyware

retrieved_context.text: On November 29, 2023, Google’s Threat Analysis Group disclosed and patched CVE-2023-6345, an actively exploited integer-overflow vulnerability in the Skia 2D graphics library that permits sandbox escape via a malicious file on Chrome versions prior to 119.0.6045.199—its seventh zero-day this year and fourth since August—underscoring a broader surge of critical browser flaws such as WebP heap overflow CVE-2023-4863 impacting Chrome, Safari and Firefox; Chromium-fork bug CVE-2023-5217 in Edge, Opera, Brave and Vivaldi; and four Apple WebKit zero-days (CVE-2023-28205, ‑32409, ‑28204, ‑32373) that commercial spyware vendors like Predator and likely state-sponsored actors have exploited to drop malware, steal credentials and exfiltrate data. Experts attribute this trend to browsers’ ubiquitous role in delivering web applications, expanded device-access features (USB, Bluetooth, WebGPU) and Chromium’s cross-platform reach, which amplifies an exploit’s impact across multiple browsers; they recommend organizations prioritize rigorous patch management, real-time version tracking and strict network segmentation to contain infection pathways and mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: Google Patches Another Chrome Zero-Day as Browser Attacks Mount

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
retrieved_context.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
retrieved_context.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

retrieved_context.text: Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has documented how over 30 commercial spyware vendors are selling 0-day and n-day exploits to government-backed actors, enabling targeted campaigns against dissidents, journalists and human rights workers on Android, iOS and Samsung Internet Browser; in November 2022, TAG observed a smishing campaign using bit.ly links to deliver two parallel exploit chains—on iOS (CVE-2022-42856 WebKit RCE with a PAC bypass technique also seen in Cytrox’s Predator, and CVE-2021-30900 AGXAccelerator sandbox escape) that installed a GPS-pinging IPA stager, and on Android (CVE-2022-3723 Chrome type confusion, CVE-2022-4135 GPU sandbox bypass analyzed by Sergei Glazunov, and CVE-2022-38181 ARM privilege escalation) with Intent redirection to Chrome—both remaining effective until patched in Chrome 107/108 and Pixel January 2023 updates; in December 2022, TAG uncovered a one-time SMS link campaign targeting UAE users via a Heliconia-style landing page delivering a C++-based Android spyware suite after chaining four faults—CVE-2022-4262 Chrome type confusion, CVE-2022-3038 Chrome sandbox escape, CVE-2022-22706 Mali GPU kernel exploit and CVE-2023-0266 Linux kernel race (with auxiliary info-leak 0-days)—against unpatched Samsung Internet Browser (Chromium 102), underscoring that smaller surveillance vendors now stockpile and share advanced exploits historically limited to nation-state developers, highlighting the critical need for immediate patch deployment, comprehensive mitigations (PAC, V8 sandbox, MiraclePTR) and continuous IOC monitoring to disrupt these highly targeted intrusion operations.
retrieved_context.title: Spyware vendors use 0-days and n-days against popular platforms

retrieved_context.text: Kaspersky researchers have uncovered a new variant of the multi-stage Necro Trojan—first observed in 2019’s CamScanner compromise—that over recent weeks infected two Google Play apps (Wuta Camera, 10 M+ downloads; Max Browser, 1 M+ downloads) and unofficial mods for Spotify, WhatsApp and popular games by exploiting an untrusted advertising-integration SDK; in the Spotify mod the SDK exfiltrated device/app data to a known Necro C&C server and fetched a payload hidden in an image, while in the WhatsApp mod a loader abused Firebase Remote Config for C&C before deploying identical Necro payloads sharing code, structure and C&C infrastructure. Once installed, Necro’s latest variant downloads modules to display and click invisible ads, execute JavaScript in hidden WebViews, download executables and third-party apps, redirect traffic through compromised devices as proxies and subscribe victims to premium services. Between August 26 and September 15, tens of thousands of devices in Russia, Brazil, Vietnam, Ecuador and Mexico were targeted before Google removed the infected apps. Organizations should rigorously vet third-party SDKs, monitor remote-config channels and anomalous network traffic for image-based payload retrieval and invisible ad click-fraud behaviors to mitigate this evolving mobile threat.
retrieved_context.title: Necro Trojan Infects Google Play Apps With Millions of Downloads - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: Kaspersky’s Unified Monitoring and Analysis Platform (KUMA)
hits.text: Operation Triangulation is a sophisticated, zero-click iMessage exploit campaign active since 2019 and observed as recently as June 2023 targeting iOS up to 15.7, in which threat actors deliver an encrypted attachment that automatically triggers a vulnerability, spawns IMTransferAgent to fetch and delete the initial exploit, invokes the deprecated BackupAgent process to download privilege-escalation stages and a final root-level APT payload capable of arbitrary code execution and data exfiltration. Analysts using Kaspersky’s Unified Monitoring and Analysis Platform (KUMA) generated offline iTunes or idevicebackup2 backups and parsed them with the Mobile Verification Toolkit (mvt-ios) to produce “timeline.csv” super-timelines, reliably detecting compromise via BackupAgent data-usage entries, SMS attachment directory modifications, plist changes (com.apple.ImageIO, com.apple.locationd.StatusBarIconManager, com.apple.imservice.ids.FaceTime), anomalous WebKit data flows and failed iOS updates due to tampered com.apple.softwareupdateservicesd.plist. Network indicators include ~242 KB HTTPS downloads from *.icloud-content.com followed by heavy traffic to C2 domains such as addatamarket[.]net, backuprabbit[.]com, cloudsponcer[.]com and others. Since the malware lacks persistence—devices clear on reboot but can be reinfected—defenders should implement full backups, routine mvt-ios scans, DNS/NetFlow monitoring for known C2 domains and map the campaign against MITRE ATT&CK’s newly created Operation Triangulation framework entry.
hits.title: Operation Triangulation: iOS devices targeted with previously unknown malware

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

hits.text: Symantec has warned that extortion actors, notably the Clop ransomware operation (aka Snakefly/TA505/FIN11), have been exploiting a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability in the MOVEit Transfer web application (CVE-2023-34362) since May 27, 2023, enabling supply-chain attacks across multiple organizations; although first patched on May 31, additional vulnerabilities (CVEs pending) were disclosed on June 9. Attackers deploy a bespoke web shell, Lemurloot (detected as JS.Malscript!g1, Trojan.Gen.2, WS.Malware), to authenticate via hard-coded credentials, execute SQL statements to alter or delete database elements, exfiltrate records and Azure settings, and manipulate user accounts. With proof-of-concept code now public, secondary threat actors face elevated risk of exploitation and data theft. Clop has since threatened data leaks unless ransoms are paid, reflecting its shift from encryption to extortion. Symantec mitigations include file-based and ML detections, network-based attack signatures, and Data Center Security policy controls that harden MS SQL, IIS and sandbox environments to prevent web-shell deployment and unauthorized software execution.
hits.title: MOVEit Vulnerabilities: What You Need to Know | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

The actor exploits n-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473, CVE-2022-41352, CVE-2023-32315, CVE-2023-42793, CVE-2023-23397, CVE-2024-1709, CVE-2023-48788), conducts credential theft and supply-chain attacks via regionally managed IT service providers, deploys LocalOlive web shells and uses legitimate management tools (Atera Agent, Splashtop) for initial access and persistence; post-compromise, it harvests credentials with Procdump and registry modifications, exfiltrates data via Rclone, Chisel and Plink over covert Tor-routed tunnels, and performs lateral movement through DNS reconfiguration, new services, scheduled tasks and OpenSSH backdoors. Microsoft warns the subgroup’s near-global reach and horizontal scaling capabilities, and has published hunting queries, IoCs and YARA rules to enable defenders to detect and disrupt its operations.
retrieved_context.title: BadPilot network hacking campaign fuels Russian SandWorm attacks

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
retrieved_context.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: On November 29, 2023, Google’s Threat Analysis Group disclosed and patched CVE-2023-6345, an actively exploited integer-overflow vulnerability in the Skia 2D graphics library that permits sandbox escape via a malicious file on Chrome versions prior to 119.0.6045.199—its seventh zero-day this year and fourth since August—underscoring a broader surge of critical browser flaws such as WebP heap overflow CVE-2023-4863 impacting Chrome, Safari and Firefox; Chromium-fork bug CVE-2023-5217 in Edge, Opera, Brave and Vivaldi; and four Apple WebKit zero-days (CVE-2023-28205, ‑32409, ‑28204, ‑32373) that commercial spyware vendors like Predator and likely state-sponsored actors have exploited to drop malware, steal credentials and exfiltrate data. Experts attribute this trend to browsers’ ubiquitous role in delivering web applications, expanded device-access features (USB, Bluetooth, WebGPU) and Chromium’s cross-platform reach, which amplifies an exploit’s impact across multiple browsers; they recommend organizations prioritize rigorous patch management, real-time version tracking and strict network segmentation to contain infection pathways and mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: Google Patches Another Chrome Zero-Day as Browser Attacks Mount

retrieved_context.text: Kaspersky researchers have uncovered a new variant of the multi-stage Necro Trojan—first observed in 2019’s CamScanner compromise—that over recent weeks infected two Google Play apps (Wuta Camera, 10 M+ downloads; Max Browser, 1 M+ downloads) and unofficial mods for Spotify, WhatsApp and popular games by exploiting an untrusted advertising-integration SDK; in the Spotify mod the SDK exfiltrated device/app data to a known Necro C&C server and fetched a payload hidden in an image, while in the WhatsApp mod a loader abused Firebase Remote Config for C&C before deploying identical Necro payloads sharing code, structure and C&C infrastructure. Once installed, Necro’s latest variant downloads modules to display and click invisible ads, execute JavaScript in hidden WebViews, download executables and third-party apps, redirect traffic through compromised devices as proxies and subscribe victims to premium services. Between August 26 and September 15, tens of thousands of devices in Russia, Brazil, Vietnam, Ecuador and Mexico were targeted before Google removed the infected apps. Organizations should rigorously vet third-party SDKs, monitor remote-config channels and anomalous network traffic for image-based payload retrieval and invisible ad click-fraud behaviors to mitigate this evolving mobile threat.
retrieved_context.title: Necro Trojan Infects Google Play Apps With Millions of Downloads - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: Kaspersky’s Unified Monitoring and Analysis Platform (KUMA)
hits.text: Operation Triangulation is a sophisticated, zero-click iMessage exploit campaign active since 2019 and observed as recently as June 2023 targeting iOS up to 15.7, in which threat actors deliver an encrypted attachment that automatically triggers a vulnerability, spawns IMTransferAgent to fetch and delete the initial exploit, invokes the deprecated BackupAgent process to download privilege-escalation stages and a final root-level APT payload capable of arbitrary code execution and data exfiltration. Analysts using Kaspersky’s Unified Monitoring and Analysis Platform (KUMA) generated offline iTunes or idevicebackup2 backups and parsed them with the Mobile Verification Toolkit (mvt-ios) to produce “timeline.csv” super-timelines, reliably detecting compromise via BackupAgent data-usage entries, SMS attachment directory modifications, plist changes (com.apple.ImageIO, com.apple.locationd.StatusBarIconManager, com.apple.imservice.ids.FaceTime), anomalous WebKit data flows and failed iOS updates due to tampered com.apple.softwareupdateservicesd.plist. Network indicators include ~242 KB HTTPS downloads from *.icloud-content.com followed by heavy traffic to C2 domains such as addatamarket[.]net, backuprabbit[.]com, cloudsponcer[.]com and others. Since the malware lacks persistence—devices clear on reboot but can be reinfected—defenders should implement full backups, routine mvt-ios scans, DNS/NetFlow monitoring for known C2 domains and map the campaign against MITRE ATT&CK’s newly created Operation Triangulation framework entry.
hits.title: Operation Triangulation: iOS devices targeted with previously unknown malware

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.

hits.text: Google has released Chrome 120.0.6099.129/130 updates to patch an actively exploited high-severity zero-day (CVE-2023-7024), a heap-based buffer overflow in the WebRTC framework that enables crashes or arbitrary code execution, discovered by TAG researchers Clément Lecigne and Vlad Stolyarov on December 19, 2023. This marks the eighth Chrome zero-day exploited in the wild this year—following type confusion flaws in V8 (CVE-2023-2033, CVSS 8.8; CVE-2023-2136, CVSS 9.6; CVE-2023-3079, CVSS 8.8; CVE-2023-4762, CVSS 8.8), a heap overflow in WebP (CVE-2023-4863, CVSS 8.8), a heap overflow in libvpx (CVE-2023-5217, CVSS 8.8) and an integer overflow in Skia (CVE-2023-6345, CVSS 9.6)—amid a record 26,447 CVEs disclosed in 2023, 115 of which have been weaponized by threat actors and ransomware groups using remote code execution, security-feature bypass, buffer manipulation, privilege escalation and input-validation flaws. Given WebRTC’s cross-browser support, impacts on Firefox and Safari remain under assessment. Administrators and end users should immediately upgrade Chrome for Windows, macOS and Linux and apply forthcoming patches for Chromium-based browsers (Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi) to mitigate potential compromise.
hits.title: Urgent: New Chrome Zero-Day Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild - Update ASAP

canonical_entities: malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails
hits.text: Attackers are leveraging the six-year-old CVE-2017-11882 Microsoft Office RCE vulnerability via malicious Excel attachments in socially engineered “orders” and “invoices” emails to initiate a multi-stage infection chain that delivers the Agent Tesla RAT and advanced keylogger. Once a user opens the Excel file on an unpatched Office build, it connects to a malicious server to retrieve a heavily obfuscated VBS script, which in turn downloads a JPEG containing a Base64-encoded DLL. The VBS launches PowerShell to extract and load the DLL, then abuses RegAsm.exe—disguised as a legitimate registry utility—to inject a thread that fetches and executes the Agent Tesla payload. Deployed Agent Tesla uses clipboard and window hooking for keystroke logging, screen capture and browser, mail and FTP credential theft, exfiltrating data via attacker-controlled Telegram bots. Zscaler’s detailed IoCs—including malicious URLs, file hashes and Telegram endpoints—underscore the critical need for organizations to patch legacy Office versions, deploy email defenses, and monitor for the described artifacts to prevent credential compromise and system takeover.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit 6-Year-Old Microsoft Office Bug to Spread Spyware

hits.text: Equation, a highly resourced cyber-espionage group identified by Kaspersky Lab and tracked by Symantec, targets global organizations using a multi-stage infection chain that begins with reconnaissance/backdoor Trojans—Infostealer, Micstus (DoubleFantasy) and Tripfant (TripleFantasy)—to fingerprint systems and maintain access, then deploys modular, stealthy payloads such as Grayphish (a bootkit with an encrypted registry-based virtual file system) and its predecessor EquationDrug (Equdrug), plus the earlier Lassrv.B (EquationLaser), each supporting specialized modules including a rare HDD firmware reprogramming implant (detectable as Packed.Generic.483) that survives disk reformatting; the group further employs bespoke tools—Grokey keylogger and the W32.Fanny worm exploiting two zero-days later used by Stuxnet—to infiltrate air-gapped networks via USB and exfiltrate data. Symantec and Norton products currently detect these threats with AV signatures (e.g., Trojan.Grayphish, Trojan.Equdrug, W32.Fanny) and IPS rules, providing actionable defenses against Equation’s advanced stealth techniques, firmware-level persistence and sophisticated data exfiltration capabilities.
hits.title: Equation: Advanced cyberespionage group has all the tricks in the book, and more | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Since 2022, Check Point has observed the financially motivated threat actor Magnet Goblin exploiting one-day vulnerabilities in public-facing services—beginning with Magento (CVE-2022-24086) and later targeting Ivanti VPNs (CVE-2023-46805, CVE-2024-21887, CVE-2024-21888, CVE-2024-21893), Qlik Sense (CVE-2023-41265, CVE-2023-41266, CVE-2023-48365) and potentially Apache ActiveMQ—to deliver its custom Linux backdoors NerbianRAT and a streamlined MiniNerbian variant. In recent Ivanti attacks, Magnet Goblin chained the Warpwire JavaScript credential stealer with NerbianRAT, the open-source tunneling tool Ligolo, and RMM platforms (ScreenConnect, AnyDesk) to establish stealthy AES-encrypted raw socket C2 channels (and HTTP C2 for MiniNerbian), enabling system reconnaissance and arbitrary command execution. This campaign underscores the urgent need for aggressive patch management, edge-device hardening, and monitoring for anomalous RMM and tunneling activities.
hits.title: Magnet Goblin Delivers Linux Malware Using One-Day Vulnerabilities - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. hits.text: Since mid-November 2024, Russian nation-state actor Star Blizzard has significantly escalated its evasion tradecraft following public exposure by Microsoft Threat Intelligence: shifting from a single registrar (NameCheap) to multiple registrars (Hostinger, RealTime Register, GMO Internet) and implementing multi-stage redirection chains—embedding Microsoft 365 Safe Links in PDF lures that pass through Bitly and Cuttly shortened URLs and legitimate open-redirect sites (e.g., mechengsys[.]net) before landing on an Evilginx-equipped VPS (vidmemax[.]com)—to mount AiTM spear-phishing campaigns that harvest email credentials, including MFA tokens. Between July and August 2024 they also experimented with altered OneDrive file-share notifications—using ProtonMail accounts to spoof trusted senders and rewire the “Open” button URL to their Evilginx infrastructure—targeting individuals in politics, diplomacy, NGOs and think tanks. Historically, since 2022 Star Blizzard has iteratively refined detection evasion—employing server-side fingerprinting scripts, HubSpot and MailerLite email platforms to mask domains, DNS obfuscation, password-protected PDFs and randomized DGAs—with each ephemeral TTP swiftly modified, underscoring the need for continuous updates to email security controls, link inspection and behavioral detection.

hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.

hits.text: Since February 2023, Microsoft has tracked an Iranian nation-state threat actor known as Peach Sandstorm (a.k.a. APT33/Elfin/Refined Kitten) conducting high-volume password spray attacks—often via Tor IPs and a “go-http-client” user agent—against thousands of satellite, defense, and pharmaceutical organizations worldwide to gain initial access for state-sponsored intelligence collection; upon successful logins the group employed Go-based AzureHound or Roadtools for Microsoft Entra ID reconnaissance, established persistence through malicious Azure subscriptions and Azure Arc, and in parallel attempted remote exploitation of internet-facing Zoho ManageEngine (CVE-2022-47966) and Confluence (CVE-2022-26134) vulnerabilities. In later stages Peach Sandstorm deployed AnyDesk RMM, executed Golden SAML attacks to mint Microsoft 365 tokens, used DLL search-order hijacking via legitimate VMware binaries, tunneled traffic with custom EagleRelay VMs, leveraged RDP for lateral movement, and in a subset of intrusions exfiltrated sensitive data. Microsoft’s assessment underscores the risk to confidentiality and urges defenders to reset compromised passwords and session cookies, revoke unauthorized MFA changes, implement conditional-access policies, block legacy authentication, patch known CVEs, and apply the Azure Security Benchmark to harden identity infrastructures against evolving Peach Sandstorm tradecraft.

hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: ESET researchers disclosed MoustachedBouncer, a Belarus-aligned cyberespionage group active since at least 2014 targeting foreign embassies in Belarus, employing two parallel malware frameworks: the email-based NightClub (SMTP/IMAP C2) and its 2020-onward successor Disco (Go/.NET) delivered via adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) at ISP level—likely leveraging Belarus’s SORM lawful interception—to redirect Windows captive portal checks to a fake Windows Update page. This page loads jdrop.js to prompt a malicious installer, which schedules SMB-delivered OfficeBroker payloads from attacker-injected Google Cloud IPs. Both frameworks support plugins for screenshots, audio recording and file theft. ESET observed compromises of embassies from four continents and assesses medium confidence in state alignment and low confidence in cooperation with Winter Vivern. Recommendations include out-of-band encrypted VPNs to thwart ISP-level interception.
hits.title: MoustachedBouncer: Espionage against foreign diplomats in Belarus

hits.text: Operation RoundPress, attributed with medium confidence to Russian state-sponsored APT28 (Fancy Bear), has since 2023 exploited stored and reflected XSS flaws in widely used webmail platforms—initially leveraging Roundcube CVE-2020-35730 to inject malicious JavaScript into email bodies, then CVE-2023-43770 and additional n-day vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra in early 2024—to execute upon email open without clicks or redirects. Through spear-phishing emails crafted with timely political or news excerpts, the hidden script auto-fills victim credentials via invisible input fields, scrapes DOM content—including emails, contacts, webmail settings, login history, 2FA tokens and passwords—and exfiltrates data via HTTP POST to hardcoded C2 servers. Targets span high-value government entities in Greece, Ukraine, Serbia and Cameroon, military units in Ukraine and Ecuador, defense contractors in Ukraine, Bulgaria and Romania, and critical infrastructure in Ukraine and Bulgaria. The lack of persistence mechanisms confines execution to session scope but underscores the necessity for timely patching of XSS vulnerabilities, disabling HTML rendering in webmail clients, enforcing strict input sanitization and multifactor authentication, and monitoring anomalous outbound traffic to mitigate credential theft and data exfiltration.
hits.title: Government webmail hacked via XSS bugs in global spy campaign

hits.text: In August 2025 Microsoft Threat Intelligence revealed that Storm-2460, associated with the Play ransomware group, has resumed exploiting CVE-2025-29824—a zero-day elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Common Log File System patched in April—to gain SYSTEM privileges on unpatched hosts across IT, financial and real estate organizations in the US, Europe, South America and the Middle East. The campaign begins with an in-memory dropper masquerading as the open-source ChatGPT Desktop app that decrypts and launches PipeMagic, a modular backdoor first observed in December 2022 and now updated with persistence and lateral-movement enhancements targeting Saudi Arabian and Brazilian manufacturing entities. PipeMagic communicates with its TCP C2 over a named pipe, self-updates by storing distinct payload modules in memory via doubly linked lists for staging, execution and communication (plus an additional dynamic list), then leverages the CLFS exploit to escalate privileges before deploying Play ransomware. Although the campaign’s footprint remains limited, the combination of a zero-day exploit and a sophisticated modular backdoor underscores a heightened risk; organizations are urged to immediately apply the April patch for CVE-2025-29824, enable tamper and network protection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, run EDR in block mode, enforce full automated investigation and remediation, and leverage cloud-delivered machine-learning protections to block novel variants.
hits.title: PipeMagic Backdoor Resurfaces as Part of Play Ransomware Attack Chain

hits.text: In November 2023, Russian state-sponsored group Nobelium (aka Midnight Blizzard/APT29) executed a month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment by conducting a password-spray brute-force attack against a legacy non-production test tenant lacking multi-factor authentication, enabling pivoting to a small subset of high-value accounts—including leadership, cybersecurity and legal team mailboxes—from which they exfiltrated emails and attachments; discovered on January 12, 2024, the campaign underscores the risk of poorly secured account configurations rather than software vulnerabilities, prompting Microsoft to notify impacted employees, reaffirm its MFA mandate, and reinforce zero-trust controls. This incident, following Nobelium’s SolarWinds and 2021 support-tool intrusions, highlights the necessity of enforcing MFA, minimizing default permissions, and hardening non-prod assets to mitigate advanced persistent threats.

hits.text: ESET researchers disclosed MoustachedBouncer, a Belarus-aligned cyberespionage group active since at least 2014 targeting foreign embassies in Belarus, employing two parallel malware frameworks: the email-based NightClub (SMTP/IMAP C2) and its 2020-onward successor Disco (Go/.NET) delivered via adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) at ISP level—likely leveraging Belarus’s SORM lawful interception—to redirect Windows captive portal checks to a fake Windows Update page. This page loads jdrop.js to prompt a malicious installer, which schedules SMB-delivered OfficeBroker payloads from attacker-injected Google Cloud IPs. Both frameworks support plugins for screenshots, audio recording and file theft. ESET observed compromises of embassies from four continents and assesses medium confidence in state alignment and low confidence in cooperation with Winter Vivern. Recommendations include out-of-band encrypted VPNs to thwart ISP-level interception.

hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
