retrieved_context.text: Since at least April 2024 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a Russia-affiliated cyberespionage actor dubbed Void Blizzard (aka LAUNDRY BEAR) conducting high-volume, targeted operations against government, defense, transportation, media, NGO and healthcare organizations—particularly in NATO member states and Ukraine—by leveraging stolen credentials procured via commodity infostealer ecosystems for password spray attacks and Exchange/SharePoint Online access, then automating bulk email and file collection (and in some cases Teams messages) via cloud APIs and tools like AzureHound; in April 2025 the actor evolved to adversary-in-the-middle spear phishing using a typosquatted domain and the open-source Evilginx framework with a malicious QR-coded PDF to harvest Entra authentication data; this widespread success underscores that even unsophisticated TTPs pose major intelligence risks to critical sectors, so organizations should enforce sign-in risk policies and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO/passkeys), centralize identity management with Conditional Access, monitor risky sign-ins and mailbox auditing, apply least-privilege credential hygiene, and promptly rotate credentials after infostealer detections to disrupt Void Blizzard’s operations.

retrieved_context.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. More recently, the group shifted to adversary-in-the-middle spear-phishing using a typosquatted “micsrosoftonline[.]com” domain and an Evilginx-based phishing page delivered through malicious QR codes in forged European Defense and Security Summit PDF invitations, automating bulk data collection via Exchange, Microsoft Graph and Teams web client. Overlaps with Forest Blizzard, Midnight Blizzard and Secret Blizzard indicate coordinated Russian strategic espionage, and a September 2024 pass-the-cookie breach of a Dutch police account underscores their evolving cookie-theft capabilities—highlighting urgent needs for phishing-resistant MFA and hardened Entra ID configurations.
retrieved_context.title: Russian Hackers Breach 20+ NGOs Using Evilginx Phishing via Fake Microsoft Entra Pages

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
retrieved_context.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Since mid-November 2024, Russian nation-state actor Star Blizzard has significantly escalated its evasion tradecraft following public exposure by Microsoft Threat Intelligence: shifting from a single registrar (NameCheap) to multiple registrars (Hostinger, RealTime Register, GMO Internet) and implementing multi-stage redirection chains—embedding Microsoft 365 Safe Links in PDF lures that pass through Bitly and Cuttly shortened URLs and legitimate open-redirect sites (e.g., mechengsys[.]net) before landing on an Evilginx-equipped VPS (vidmemax[.]com)—to mount AiTM spear-phishing campaigns that harvest email credentials, including MFA tokens. Between July and August 2024 they also experimented with altered OneDrive file-share notifications—using ProtonMail accounts to spoof trusted senders and rewire the “Open” button URL to their Evilginx infrastructure—targeting individuals in politics, diplomacy, NGOs and think tanks. In October 2024, Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit disrupted core infrastructure, and ongoing collaboration with UK NCSC, NSA and FBI ensures rapid customer notification and defenses. Historically, since 2022 Star Blizzard has iteratively refined detection evasion—employing server-side fingerprinting scripts, HubSpot and MailerLite email platforms to mask domains, DNS obfuscation, password-protected PDFs and randomized DGAs—with each ephemeral TTP swiftly modified, underscoring the need for continuous updates to email security controls, link inspection and behavioral detection.
retrieved_context.title: Star Blizzard increases sophistication and evasion in ongoing attacks | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

retrieved_context.text: Operation RoundPress, attributed with medium confidence to Russian state-sponsored APT28 (Fancy Bear), has since 2023 exploited stored and reflected XSS flaws in widely used webmail platforms—initially leveraging Roundcube CVE-2020-35730 to inject malicious JavaScript into email bodies, then CVE-2023-43770 and additional n-day vulnerabilities in Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon and Zimbra in early 2024—to execute upon email open without clicks or redirects. Through spear-phishing emails crafted with timely political or news excerpts, the hidden script auto-fills victim credentials via invisible input fields, scrapes DOM content—including emails, contacts, webmail settings, login history, 2FA tokens and passwords—and exfiltrates data via HTTP POST to hardcoded C2 servers. Targets span high-value government entities in Greece, Ukraine, Serbia and Cameroon, military units in Ukraine and Ecuador, defense contractors in Ukraine, Bulgaria and Romania, and critical infrastructure in Ukraine and Bulgaria. The lack of persistence mechanisms confines execution to session scope but underscores the necessity for timely patching of XSS vulnerabilities, disabling HTML rendering in webmail clients, enforcing strict input sanitization and multifactor authentication, and monitoring anomalous outbound traffic to mitigate credential theft and data exfiltration.
retrieved_context.title: Government webmail hacked via XSS bugs in global spy campaign

retrieved_context.text: Since February 2023, Microsoft has tracked an Iranian nation-state threat actor known as Peach Sandstorm (a.k.a. APT33/Elfin/Refined Kitten) conducting high-volume password spray attacks—often via Tor IPs and a “go-http-client” user agent—against thousands of satellite, defense, and pharmaceutical organizations worldwide to gain initial access for state-sponsored intelligence collection; upon successful logins the group employed Go-based AzureHound or Roadtools for Microsoft Entra ID reconnaissance, established persistence through malicious Azure subscriptions and Azure Arc, and in parallel attempted remote exploitation of internet-facing Zoho ManageEngine (CVE-2022-47966) and Confluence (CVE-2022-26134) vulnerabilities. In later stages Peach Sandstorm deployed AnyDesk RMM, executed Golden SAML attacks to mint Microsoft 365 tokens, used DLL search-order hijacking via legitimate VMware binaries, tunneled traffic with custom EagleRelay VMs, leveraged RDP for lateral movement, and in a subset of intrusions exfiltrated sensitive data. Microsoft’s assessment underscores the risk to confidentiality and urges defenders to reset compromised passwords and session cookies, revoke unauthorized MFA changes, implement conditional-access policies, block legacy authentication, patch known CVEs, and apply the Azure Security Benchmark to harden identity infrastructures against evolving Peach Sandstorm tradecraft.

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment
retrieved_context.text: In November 2023, Russian state-sponsored group Nobelium (aka Midnight Blizzard/APT29) executed a month-long breach of Microsoft’s corporate email environment by conducting a password-spray brute-force attack against a legacy non-production test tenant lacking multi-factor authentication, enabling pivoting to a small subset of high-value accounts—including leadership, cybersecurity and legal team mailboxes—from which they exfiltrated emails and attachments; discovered on January 12, 2024, the campaign underscores the risk of poorly secured account configurations rather than software vulnerabilities, prompting Microsoft to notify impacted employees, reaffirm its MFA mandate, and reinforce zero-trust controls. This incident, following Nobelium’s SolarWinds and 2021 support-tool intrusions, highlights the necessity of enforcing MFA, minimizing default permissions, and hardening non-prod assets to mitigate advanced persistent threats.
retrieved_context.title: Russian hackers stole Microsoft corporate emails in month-long breach

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
retrieved_context.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
retrieved_context.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

retrieved_context.text: Since February 2023, Microsoft has tracked an Iranian nation-state threat actor known as Peach Sandstorm (a.k.a. APT33/Elfin/Refined Kitten) conducting high-volume password spray attacks—often via Tor IPs and a “go-http-client” user agent—against thousands of satellite, defense, and pharmaceutical organizations worldwide to gain initial access for state-sponsored intelligence collection; upon successful logins the group employed Go-based AzureHound or Roadtools for Microsoft Entra ID reconnaissance, established persistence through malicious Azure subscriptions and Azure Arc, and in parallel attempted remote exploitation of internet-facing Zoho ManageEngine (CVE-2022-47966) and Confluence (CVE-2022-26134) vulnerabilities. In later stages Peach Sandstorm deployed AnyDesk RMM, executed Golden SAML attacks to mint Microsoft 365 tokens, used DLL search-order hijacking via legitimate VMware binaries, tunneled traffic with custom EagleRelay VMs, leveraged RDP for lateral movement, and in a subset of intrusions exfiltrated sensitive data. Microsoft’s assessment underscores the risk to confidentiality and urges defenders to reset compromised passwords and session cookies, revoke unauthorized MFA changes, implement conditional-access policies, block legacy authentication, patch known CVEs, and apply the Azure Security Benchmark to harden identity infrastructures against evolving Peach Sandstorm tradecraft.
retrieved_context.title: Peach Sandstorm password spray campaigns enable intelligence collection at high-value targets | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Since September 2017, the Iran-aligned BladedFeline subcluster of the OilRig APT has executed persistent cyber espionage against Kurdish and Iraqi government entities, initially compromising KRG systems and a regional Uzbekistan telecom provider via an internet-facing application vulnerability and social engineering to deploy the Flog web shell. ESET’s Q4 2023–Q1 2024 report documents the group’s evolving malware arsenal: the Shahmaran backdoor for remote file manipulation, the C#/.NET Whisper (aka Veaty) email-based implant, the DNS-tunneling Spearal and its optimized variant, Optimizer, the Slippery Snakelet Python implant for command execution and data exfiltration, and tunneling tools Laret and Pinar. BladedFeline leverages a malicious IIS module, PrimeCache—akin to OilRig’s RDAT—and the Hawking Listener early-stage implant to maintain stealthy access, systematically harvesting diplomatic and financial intelligence tied to KRG oil reserves and Western relations to further Iranian strategic objectives.
hits.title: Iran-Linked BladedFeline Hits Iraqi and Kurdish Targets with Whisper and Spearal Malware

hits.text: ESET’s analysis of the Iranian APT “BladedFeline,” assessed with medium confidence as a subgroup of APT34/OilRig, reveals the actor infiltrated Kurdish and Iraqi government networks as early as September 2017 and remained undetected until 2023–2024, maintaining strategic espionage access to high-ranking officials tied to Western diplomatic relations and regional oil reserves. The group deployed a suite of proprietary and modified implants—most notably the simple, uncompressed 64-bit Shahmaran backdoor, the Whisper backdoor, the PrimeCache IIS module, the VideoSRV reverse shell, PowerShell executors and multiple reverse tunnels—via unknown initial vectors and a likely internet-facing web server exploit, using unencrypted C2 channels over normal traffic to execute commands, manipulate files and exfiltrate data. ESET identified code overlaps between PrimeCache and OilRig’s RDAT and common usage of VideoSRV, expects continued implant development, and advises defenders to maintain detailed inventories of VIP-used applications, establish network baselines to detect stealthy exfiltration paths and anomalies, and audit internet-facing servers to thwart initial compromise.
hits.title: Iranian APT 'BladedFeline' Hides in Network for 8 Years

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates
hits.text: Unit 42 has observed a sharp rise in post-intrusion WastedLocker ransomware attacks by the Evil Corp group—already known for Dridex—against large U.S. organizations in sectors from manufacturing to legal services, with initial compromise typically via ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates that deploy a SocGholish JavaScript loader to profile systems and invoke PowerShell-based Cobalt Strike payloads; attackers then leverage WMI and PsExec for lateral movement, identify high-value and backup systems, elevate privileges, disable Windows Defender, delete shadow copies, install WastedLocker as a service, and encrypt files using a “.<victim_name>wasted” extension while appending ransom notes (“.<victim_name>wasted_info”) with contact addresses on ProtonMail, Airmail and others. Palo Alto Networks’ WildFire, Cortex XDR (anti-ransomware and behavioral threat protection), NGFW DNS signatures and AutoFocus tagging detect and prevent WastedLocker activity; organizations are urged to implement robust, off-site backup strategies and hardened cybersecurity controls to mitigate this high-impact targeted ransomware threat.
hits.title: Threat Assessment: WastedLocker Ransomware

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
hits.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Security researcher Marc Newlin of SkySafe disclosed CVE-2023-45866, a critical, decade-old keystroke-injection flaw in the Bluetooth host state-machine that exploits an unauthenticated pairing mechanism in the Bluetooth specification to trick macOS (13.3.3), iOS (16.6, even in Lockdown Mode), Android (from 4.2.2 through 14 on devices including Pixel 7/6/4a, Pixel 2, Nexus 5, BLU DASH), and Linux BlueZ stacks (Ubuntu 18.04–23.10) into pairing with a malicious emulated keyboard, enabling remote attackers within Bluetooth range to run a Python-based script, inject arbitrary keystrokes, install apps, forward emails or texts, and execute commands without user confirmation or biometric/password authentication. After informing Apple, Google, Canonical, and the Bluetooth SIG between August and September, patches have been released for Android 11–14 and BlueZ (via GitHub) but Apple has yet to announce a timeline for CVE-2023-42929, proof-of-concept exploit scripts will be published in January, and no active in-the-wild exploitation has been observed to date.
hits.title: Critical Bluetooth Flaw Exposes Android, Apple & Linux Devices to Takeover

hits.text: In early April, Palo Alto Networks’ Advanced WildFire and Cortex XDR uncovered SnipBot—a new v5.0 iteration of the RomCom RAT family—employing advanced window message–based control-flow obfuscation and anti-sandbox checks (filename hash and HKCU\…\RecentDocs entries) in a multi-stage chain beginning with a PDF-labeled EXE downloader signed using a likely stolen certificate; the downloader contacts xeontime[.]com for config-pdf.dll, which uses registry-based COM hijacking to load keyprov.dll from drvmcprotect[.]com into explorer.exe, decrypts payloads stored in HKCU\Software\AppDataSoft\Software, and opens a TCP listener on port 1342 for commands to update, delete, or execute modules. The main backdoor single.dll (mutex “SnipMutex”) supports 27 encrypted commands for drive and process enumeration, file upload/download, and remote module execution, facilitating network pivoting and targeted file exfiltration. Active since December 2023 (RomCom activity since 2022), SnipBot’s tactics, stolen certificates, unique obfuscation, and sophisticated loader underscore a high-risk threat actor likely focused on intelligence gathering; Palo Alto products classify its samples, URLs, and domains as malicious to prevent compromise.
hits.title: Inside SnipBot: The Latest RomCom Malware Variant

hits.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
hits.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

hits.text: Since at least September 2023, the China-aligned Evasive Panda APT (aka BRONZE HIGHLAND/Daggerfly) has conducted a dual-pronged cyberespionage campaign against the Tibetan diaspora by compromising both the Kagyu International Monlam Trust’s website and the official Monlam translation-software supply chain—first implanting obfuscated JavaScript into jquery.js on the festival site that verifies victims’ first three IP octets via an MD5 hash salted with “1qaz0okm!@#,” serves a faux “Aw, Snap!” error page to users in India, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Australia and the U.S., and lures them to download a malicious “certificate.exe” or “.pkg” downloader; that loader side-loads memmgrset.dll (http_dy.dll) to fetch a JSON config from update.devicebug[.]com and ultimately deploys the undocumented Nightdoor backdoor alongside the group’s modular MgBot implant, while a trojanized Monlam software installer (Windows autorun.exe abusing MonlamUpdate.exe for DLL side-loading of RPHost.dll, and macOS Mach-O downloaders) has delivered further downloaders and payloads—retrieved from tibetpost[.]net and a direct IP—to %TEMP%\default_ico.exe for additional Nightdoor and MgBot installation.
hits.title: Evasive Panda leverages Monlam Festival to target Tibetans

canonical_entities: diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine
hits.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.
hits.title: Hackers with Russian Blizzard Steal Data from Rival Networks

hits.text: Storm-842 (Void Manticore), an Iranian MOIS-linked APT also operating as Homeland Justice in Albania and Karma in Israel, first emerged in July 2022 by crippling Albania’s e-government and border systems ahead of an MEK conference—an attack detailed in a Sept. 2022 FBI/CISA advisory—and by December 2023 had extended its destructive campaigns to Israeli infrastructure; it executes a two-stage kill chain in partnership with Scarred Manticore (OilRig/APT34), which gains initial access via web shells (reGeorge, Karma Shell), RDP and SSH-based SOCKS C2 channels, credential harvesting and environment mapping, then hands off to Void Manticore to deploy custom Windows/Linux wipers (Cl Wiper using ElRawDisk, Partition Wiper, BiBi Wiper with .BiBi extension variants) that delete files, corrupt partitions, disable recovery mechanisms and erase shadow copies, all while concurrent influence operations leak stolen data under various personas to sow distrust—mitigation requires enforcing MFA and role-based access, rigorous patch and vulnerability management, network segmentation with IDS/IPS monitoring, phishing-resistant email/web filtering, offline backups with tested recovery drills and integration of real-time threat intelligence to detect and disrupt this sophisticated blend of destructive malware and psychological warfare.

hits.text: Since mid-2016, an Iran-linked espionage operation dubbed “Magic Hound” has targeted energy, government and technology organizations in and around Saudi Arabia using macro-enabled Word and Excel documents masquerading as holiday cards, job offers and official Ministry of Health and Commerce files to launch PowerShell-based downloaders and custom droppers, executable and document loaders and IRC bots that ultimately deploy a Python-based Pupy RAT; Palo Alto Networks analysts—citing overlaps in domains and initial breach methods with the recent Shamoon 2 campaign—have linked Magic Hound to the Iran-aligned Rocket Kitten group, while SecureWorks attributes it to COBALT GYPSY and IBM X-Force has observed shared infrastructure, and additional code similarities tie an IRC bot to Charming Kitten/Newscaster activity and to MacDownloader tools used by other Iranian actors, underscoring the need to block malicious macros, monitor PowerShell and IRC traffic for known C2 signatures, and flag Pupy-related domains and custom loader behaviors to disrupt long-running cross-platform intrusion operations.

hits.text: Iran-linked APT Hexane (aka Lyceum/SiameseKitten), active since at least 2018 and previously focused on oil & gas and telecommunications in the Middle East and Africa, has shifted in 2021 to target Israeli IT and communications firms via sophisticated supply-chain phishing operations, ClearSky reports. Leveraging a newly expanded infrastructure to impersonate legitimate companies and HR personnel on LinkedIn, Hexane conducted a May 2021 attack on an Israeli IT provider followed by a July wave against additional organizations by luring candidates with fake job offers for roles in France, Israel and the UK. Victims are directed to a phishing site where tailored lure files deploy a dual-stage infection—first the Milan implant to establish C2 connectivity, then the DanBot RAT—to harvest data, perform espionage and move laterally, presumably to breach client networks downstream. This upgrade mirrors North Korea’s “dream job” campaigns and OilRig (APT34) activity, underscoring Hexane’s evolving tactics, renewed toolset and continued focus on supply-chain compromise to facilitate deep network infiltration.
hits.title: Report: Iranian APT Hexane Targets Israeli Companies

hits.text: Since mid-2016, a cyber espionage operation dubbed Magic Hound, attributed to Iranian government–linked actors including COBALT GYPSY and showing overlaps with Rocket Kitten (Operation Saffron Rose/Ajax Security Team/Operation Woolen-Goldfish) and Newscasters (Charming Kitten/NewsBeef), has targeted energy, government and technology organizations in and tied to Saudi Arabia by distributing Word and Excel documents embedding malicious macros that launch PowerShell downloaders and droppers to deploy a custom toolkit—comprising executable and document loaders, IRC bots and the multi-platform Python-based PupyRAT—for full system access and data exfiltration; analysis by Palo Alto Networks and SecureWorks revealed domain and tool reuse with the Shamoon 2 wiper campaign, and bait lures mimicking holiday greetings, job offers and official Ministry of Health and Commerce communications, underscoring the need for enhanced macro-enablement policies, network segmentation and proactive IOC monitoring of associated domains and IRC traffic.
hits.title: Iranian hackers behind the Magic Hound campaign linked to Shamoon

hits.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
hits.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Since September 2017, the Iran-aligned BladedFeline subcluster of the OilRig APT has executed persistent cyber espionage against Kurdish and Iraqi government entities, initially compromising KRG systems and a regional Uzbekistan telecom provider via an internet-facing application vulnerability and social engineering to deploy the Flog web shell. ESET’s Q4 2023–Q1 2024 report documents the group’s evolving malware arsenal: the Shahmaran backdoor for remote file manipulation, the C#/.NET Whisper (aka Veaty) email-based implant, the DNS-tunneling Spearal and its optimized variant, Optimizer, the Slippery Snakelet Python implant for command execution and data exfiltration, and tunneling tools Laret and Pinar. BladedFeline leverages a malicious IIS module, PrimeCache—akin to OilRig’s RDAT—and the Hawking Listener early-stage implant to maintain stealthy access, systematically harvesting diplomatic and financial intelligence tied to KRG oil reserves and Western relations to further Iranian strategic objectives.
retrieved_context.title: Iran-Linked BladedFeline Hits Iraqi and Kurdish Targets with Whisper and Spearal Malware

retrieved_context.text: ESET’s analysis of the Iranian APT “BladedFeline,” assessed with medium confidence as a subgroup of APT34/OilRig, reveals the actor infiltrated Kurdish and Iraqi government networks as early as September 2017 and remained undetected until 2023–2024, maintaining strategic espionage access to high-ranking officials tied to Western diplomatic relations and regional oil reserves. The group deployed a suite of proprietary and modified implants—most notably the simple, uncompressed 64-bit Shahmaran backdoor, the Whisper backdoor, the PrimeCache IIS module, the VideoSRV reverse shell, PowerShell executors and multiple reverse tunnels—via unknown initial vectors and a likely internet-facing web server exploit, using unencrypted C2 channels over normal traffic to execute commands, manipulate files and exfiltrate data. ESET identified code overlaps between PrimeCache and OilRig’s RDAT and common usage of VideoSRV, expects continued implant development, and advises defenders to maintain detailed inventories of VIP-used applications, establish network baselines to detect stealthy exfiltration paths and anomalies, and audit internet-facing servers to thwart initial compromise.
retrieved_context.title: Iranian APT 'BladedFeline' Hides in Network for 8 Years

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

hits.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.
hits.title: Follina Exploited by State-Sponsored Hackers | Threatpost

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
hits.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
hits.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

The group deployed a suite of proprietary and modified implants—most notably the simple, uncompressed 64-bit Shahmaran backdoor, the Whisper backdoor, the PrimeCache IIS module, the VideoSRV reverse shell, PowerShell executors and multiple reverse tunnels—via unknown initial vectors and a likely internet-facing web server exploit, using unencrypted C2 channels over normal traffic to execute commands, manipulate files and exfiltrate data. ESET identified code overlaps between PrimeCache and OilRig’s RDAT and common usage of VideoSRV, expects continued implant development, and advises defenders to maintain detailed inventories of VIP-used applications, establish network baselines to detect stealthy exfiltration paths and anomalies, and audit internet-facing servers to thwart initial compromise.
retrieved_context.title: Iranian APT 'BladedFeline' Hides in Network for 8 Years

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
retrieved_context.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
retrieved_context.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

retrieved_context.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.
retrieved_context.title: Follina Exploited by State-Sponsored Hackers | Threatpost

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
retrieved_context.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
retrieved_context.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
retrieved_context.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

retrieved_context.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
retrieved_context.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

hits.text: Researchers at Mandiant Intelligence have identified UNC2165—the latest evolution of the U.S.-sanctioned Evil Corp—as leveraging the FakeUpdates infection chain to gain initial access, followed by deployment of LockBit ransomware to obscure attribution and monetize extortion efforts. After OFAC sanctions in December 2019 crippled Evil Corp’s ability to profit from Dridex and its WastedLocker strain, the group briefly resurfaced under PayloadBin (likely a WastedLocker rebrand) and used HTML redirectors in malicious Excel files, then adopted Hades ransomware with code overlaps to distance itself further. By aligning with LockBit’s RaaS model—already proven effective against high-profile victims such as Accenture and Bangkok Air—UNC2165 can blend in with legitimate affiliates, reduce development overhead, and bypass sanctions enforcement that deters U.S. entities from negotiating ransoms with known Evil Corp actors. This shift underscores the need for defenders to monitor FakeUpdates chains and LockBit activity for potential Evil Corp–linked intrusions and to enhance detection of rebranded ransomware variants despite attribution obfuscation tactics.
hits.title: Evil Corp Pivots LockBit to Dodge U.S. Sanctions | Threatpost

hits.text: During a recent incident, a LockBit affiliate conducted initial intrusions using gpresult for policy dumping, Cobalt Strike loaders and PsExec for privilege escalation, followed by reconnaissance (whoami, netstat, quser, net view), lateral movement, persistence via a new user account, and data exfiltration over FTP with Wput; when deployment of LockBit (SHA256 079b99f6…) was blocked on the target network, the attacker pivoted to a newly observed Rust-written ransomware family dubbed 3AM (SHA256 307a1217…), which appends “.threeamtime” to encrypted files, stops over 100 security and backup services via net stop and wbadmin/bcdedit/wmic commands, deletes Volume Shadow copies with vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet, and drops a Tor‐accessible ransom note requiring a 32-character “-k” access key and offering decryption/mystical-themed extortion; although 3AM encryption succeeded on only one of three attempted hosts, its Conti-style “-m” (local/net) and “-h” parameters, heavy service-termination payload, and aggressive VSS wipe underscore its potential as a fallback vector—defenders should update Symantec/Broadcom signatures, monitor for the .threeamtime extension, suspicious Rust binaries, command-line flags “-k” and “-m”, and mass service stoppage activity, and block associated IOCs (185.202.0[.]111, 212.18.104[.]6, 85.159.229[.]62) to mitigate future 3AM use.
hits.title: 3AM: New Ransomware Family Used As Fallback in Failed LockBit Attack | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: In early 2023, ransomware postings dropped 41% month-on-month yet LockBit stayed dominant, and despite predictions of waning ROI, Q3 saw a surge—driven by CL0P’s mass exploits of file-transfer flaws—that surpassed the combined victim counts of 2021–22 and hit law firms, government, manufacturing, oil & gas, and logistics hardest. In Q4 two new strains surfaced: CACTUS, first observed by Kroll in March 2023, leverages critical Qlik Sense vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-41266, ‑41265, ‑48365) or VPN appliance flaws for initial access; embeds a decryption key in ntuser.dat via scheduled tasks; uses SoftPerfect Network Scanner, PowerShell, Cobalt Strike, Splashtop, AnyDesk and Chisel for reconnaissance, persistence and lateral movement; exfiltrates data over Tox and Rclone; and encrypts files with AES/OpenSSL (.cts1 extension) accompanied by cAcTuS.readme.txt demands. When a LockBit affiliate’s deployment failed, they defaulted to 3AM, a new Rust-based backup encryptor that halts services, deletes VSS snapshots, appends .threeamtime and a “0x666” marker, exfiltrates via Wput to FTP, and issues Tor-based ransom negotiations. To counter these evolving threats, organizations must patch VPN and Qlik Sense flaws, enforce least-privilege RDP with MFA, restrict unauthorized remote access tools, monitor for anomalous scheduled tasks, scanner and Tox/Rclone traffic, deploy EDR to flag Cobalt Strike and script-based execution, and maintain secure, offline backups.
hits.title: New Ransomware Strains - CACTUS and 3AM

canonical_entities: FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns
hits.text: Clop ransomware, a TA505-sponsored RaaS strain appending the “.ClOP” extension, infects entire networks by compromising Active Directory servers and manipulating Group Policy for persistence, then uses phishing-delivered HTML attachments to drop the Get2 loader, which in turn pulls SDBOT, FlawedAmmyy RATs, Cobalt Strike beacons and TinyMet reverse shells for reconnaissance, lateral movement (via SMB exploits), and exfiltration (often using the DEWMODE web shell). Operators employ double and quadruple extortion—threatening to publish or auction stolen data on their Cl0p^_-Leaks site and targeting executives/customers—to coerce ransoms, driving average payments up 43% to $220,298 (median $78,398) in Q1 2021 after FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns against Kiteworks FTA (CVE-2021-27101/02/03/04) and Fortra GoAnywhere MFT, while in 2023 they exploited PaperCut CVE-2023-27350 to deploy Truebot and LockBit/Clop, then MOVEit CVE-2023-24362/CVE-2023-35036 and an unpatched SQL injection flaw to steal data without payloads. Trend Micro detections reveal a May 2023 surge (245 attempts), with top targets in banking, retail and healthcare across Türkiye, Canada, the US and large enterprises worldwide.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Clop | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: Trend Micro’s investigation into the LockBit ransomware-as-a-service operation, tracked as intrusion set Water Selkie, reveals the group’s marketing of its lightning-fast AES-128 head-only file encryption (first 4 KB) with RSA-wrapped keys, deployed via versatile affiliate-driven campaigns that source initial access through phishing (T1566), CVE-2018-13379 Fortinet VPN exploits (T1190) and compromised RDP/VPN accounts (T1078), then execute payloads via PowerShell Empire, Meterpreter, scheduled tasks or signed binaries (T1059, T1218), evade defenses with Mimikatz, GMER, Process Hacker or disabled Windows Defender (T1562), discover network shares and AD servers (T1083, T1135), laterally propagate via SMB or Cobalt Strike (T1570), exfiltrate data using StealBit or cloud storage (T1567) and encrypt data for impact (T1486), often on weekdays (~78%). Between July 2021 and January 2022 LockBit attempts surged globally—chiefly the US, India and Brazil—targeting healthcare and education yet boasting 41 leak-site victims (Dec 2021–Jan 2022) primarily SMBs (65.9%) across North America, Europe and APAC. With a professional affiliate program fueling continuous innovation and predicted upticks in supply-chain attacks in 2022, organizations should implement comprehensive asset inventory, least-privilege access, regular patching (including Fortinet CVE-2018-13379), RDP/VPN lockdown, application allow-listing, multifactor authentication, offline backups and MITRE TTP monitoring to detect and disrupt LockBit activity.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: LockBit | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: Since its discovery in November 2021, the ALPHV group has operated the BlackCat ransomware-as-a-service platform—recruiting affiliates from BlackMatter, REvil and DarkSide with revenue shares up to 90%—and deployed sophisticated triple-extortion schemes that combine data theft, encryption of Linux and Windows systems, public data leaks on a Tor-hosted site active since December 2021, and DDoS attacks if ransoms ($400K-$3M, negotiable; +15% for Bitcoin) go unpaid; coded in Rust and compiled for multiple OS architectures, BlackCat uses the --access-token flag to thwart sandbox analysis, kills security and backup processes (e.g., sql*, oracle, msaccess, synctime), excludes critical folders and files (e.g., Windows, System Volume Information, AppData, ntuser.dat, thumbs.db), and supports customizable payloads that resist reverse engineering—enabling strikes on over twenty organizations across U.S. critical infrastructure, retail, transport, telecom and pharma, including Colonial Pipeline, German fuel terminals and Belgian energy firms—and signaling a shift toward more secure, high-performance ransomware that demands enhanced backup validation, network segmentation, process monitoring and proactive threat hunting to mitigate.
hits.title: BlackCat Ransomware & Triple Extortion (Analysis & Tactics)

hits.text: BlackCat ransomware operators have introduced “Munchkin,” a new VM-based utility—delivered as an Alpine ISO loaded in VirtualBox—that automates propagation of the Rust-based BlackCat payload to remote machines and SMB/CIFS shares to evade host-level defenses. At boot, Munchkin’s ISO resets the VM root password, spawns a tmux “controller” session to run the /app/controller binary, decrypts strings via single-byte XOR, validates and deserializes a serialized /app/config file containing access tokens, victim credentials, target hosts/shares and block-lists, then mounts a /payloads directory to generate customized BlackCat samples from a template before iterating through configured tasks to encrypt network shares. The VM also houses numerous Python scripts for lateral movement and credential harvesting. This evolution in BlackCat’s RaaS toolkit reflects a broader trend of leveraging embedded VMs to thwart security solutions, expands the group’s global targeting footprint and underscores the need for defenses tuned to detect ISO-based VM deployments and tmux-launched malware.
hits.title: BlackCat Climbs the Summit With a New Tactic

hits.text: Emerging January 2022 and initially attributed to Microsoft’s DEV-0569, the Royal ransomware gang—comprising vetted operators rather than affiliates—has rebranded itself in Tor-hosted README.TXT notes and leaked exfiltrated data via victim-specific negotiation pages, employing malvertising (including Google Ads through the Keitaro TDS), phishing (callback lures impersonating software or food delivery), malicious attachments, and forum/blog links to deliver signed BATLOADER payloads that leverage MSI Custom Actions, Nsudo and PowerShell/batch scripts to disable security controls and install remote-access tools (notably Zoho), then deploy either BlackCat’s encryptor or their own Zeon encryptor with a .Royal extension; since intensifying operations in September 2022, they’ve struck high-profile victims such as Silverstone Circuit and Travis Central Appraisal District, exfiltrating data and demanding $250K–$2M, prompting HC3, CISA and FBI alerts—particularly for healthcare—while continuously innovating defense-evasion and post-compromise techniques; organizations should proactively monitor IOCs, enforce MFA, patch systems, segment networks, restrict macros, audit remote-access deployments and maintain offline backups to mitigate this financially driven threat.
hits.title: Everything You Need to Know About Royal Ransomware

hits.text: Since mid-2022, Unit 42 has attributed over 100 high-value cryptocurrency and BPO incidents to Muddled Libra—a fluid subset of the Scattered Spider collective—initially executing structured smishing and 0ktapus phishing campaigns (leveraging over 200 realistic mobile-auth portals) against large business process outsourcers, then evolving in 2023 into an ALPHV/BlackCat affiliate with multi-million-dollar extortion demands, later resuming high-profile attacks in late 2024 and expanding through May 2025 into software automation, telecom, hospitality, finance and retail verticals; their adaptable tradecraft blends social engineering of IT helpdesks to reset passwords and MFA, inside BPO access, legitimate remote management tools for CRM exfiltration, NSOCKS/TrueSocks anonymizing proxies, custom virtual machines, the open-source “bedevil” rootkit on VMware vCenter, email-forwarding rules to hijack incident response communications, and AI-driven voice spoofing for vishing, with members cycling via Discord and Telegram to refresh niche skills and spawn offshoots such as Scatter Swine and Octo Tempest, while leveraging deep incident response framework knowledge to persist in environments and repeatedly reclaim stolen data before affiliating with DragonForce for ransomware; defenders should deploy interwoven modern security architectures (Cortex XSIAM/XDR, Advanced URL Filtering, DNS Security, App-ID), enforce strict access controls, conduct rigorous awareness training, and maintain vigilant MITRE-mapped monitoring (T1566, T1556, T1215, T1562) to thwart these multifaceted, evolving extortion campaigns.
hits.title: Threat Group Assessment: Muddled Libra (Updated May 16, 2025)
