retrieved_context.text: BlackCat ransomware operators have introduced “Munchkin,” a new VM-based utility—delivered as an Alpine ISO loaded in VirtualBox—that automates propagation of the Rust-based BlackCat payload to remote machines and SMB/CIFS shares to evade host-level defenses. At boot, Munchkin’s ISO resets the VM root password, spawns a tmux “controller” session to run the /app/controller binary, decrypts strings via single-byte XOR, validates and deserializes a serialized /app/config file containing access tokens, victim credentials, target hosts/shares and block-lists, then mounts a /payloads directory to generate customized BlackCat samples from a template before iterating through configured tasks to encrypt network shares. The VM also houses numerous Python scripts for lateral movement and credential harvesting. This evolution in BlackCat’s RaaS toolkit reflects a broader trend of leveraging embedded VMs to thwart security solutions, expands the group’s global targeting footprint and underscores the need for defenses tuned to detect ISO-based VM deployments and tmux-launched malware.
retrieved_context.title: BlackCat Climbs the Summit With a New Tactic

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

retrieved_context.text: Emerging January 2022 and initially attributed to Microsoft’s DEV-0569, the Royal ransomware gang—comprising vetted operators rather than affiliates—has rebranded itself in Tor-hosted README.TXT notes and leaked exfiltrated data via victim-specific negotiation pages, employing malvertising (including Google Ads through the Keitaro TDS), phishing (callback lures impersonating software or food delivery), malicious attachments, and forum/blog links to deliver signed BATLOADER payloads that leverage MSI Custom Actions, Nsudo and PowerShell/batch scripts to disable security controls and install remote-access tools (notably Zoho), then deploy either BlackCat’s encryptor or their own Zeon encryptor with a .Royal extension; since intensifying operations in September 2022, they’ve struck high-profile victims such as Silverstone Circuit and Travis Central Appraisal District, exfiltrating data and demanding $250K–$2M, prompting HC3, CISA and FBI alerts—particularly for healthcare—while continuously innovating defense-evasion and post-compromise techniques; organizations should proactively monitor IOCs, enforce MFA, patch systems, segment networks, restrict macros, audit remote-access deployments and maintain offline backups to mitigate this financially driven threat.
retrieved_context.title: Everything You Need to Know About Royal Ransomware

retrieved_context.text: Since mid-2022, Unit 42 has attributed over 100 high-value cryptocurrency and BPO incidents to Muddled Libra—a fluid subset of the Scattered Spider collective—initially executing structured smishing and 0ktapus phishing campaigns (leveraging over 200 realistic mobile-auth portals) against large business process outsourcers, then evolving in 2023 into an ALPHV/BlackCat affiliate with multi-million-dollar extortion demands, later resuming high-profile attacks in late 2024 and expanding through May 2025 into software automation, telecom, hospitality, finance and retail verticals; their adaptable tradecraft blends social engineering of IT helpdesks to reset passwords and MFA, inside BPO access, legitimate remote management tools for CRM exfiltration, NSOCKS/TrueSocks anonymizing proxies, custom virtual machines, the open-source “bedevil” rootkit on VMware vCenter, email-forwarding rules to hijack incident response communications, and AI-driven voice spoofing for vishing, with members cycling via Discord and Telegram to refresh niche skills and spawn offshoots such as Scatter Swine and Octo Tempest, while leveraging deep incident response framework knowledge to persist in environments and repeatedly reclaim stolen data before affiliating with DragonForce for ransomware; defenders should deploy interwoven modern security architectures (Cortex XSIAM/XDR, Advanced URL Filtering, DNS Security, App-ID), enforce strict access controls, conduct rigorous awareness training, and maintain vigilant MITRE-mapped monitoring (T1566, T1556, T1215, T1562) to thwart these multifaceted, evolving extortion campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Threat Group Assessment: Muddled Libra (Updated May 16, 2025)

hits.text: Researchers at Mandiant Intelligence have identified UNC2165—the latest evolution of the U.S.-sanctioned Evil Corp—as leveraging the FakeUpdates infection chain to gain initial access, followed by deployment of LockBit ransomware to obscure attribution and monetize extortion efforts. After OFAC sanctions in December 2019 crippled Evil Corp’s ability to profit from Dridex and its WastedLocker strain, the group briefly resurfaced under PayloadBin (likely a WastedLocker rebrand) and used HTML redirectors in malicious Excel files, then adopted Hades ransomware with code overlaps to distance itself further. By aligning with LockBit’s RaaS model—already proven effective against high-profile victims such as Accenture and Bangkok Air—UNC2165 can blend in with legitimate affiliates, reduce development overhead, and bypass sanctions enforcement that deters U.S. entities from negotiating ransoms with known Evil Corp actors. This shift underscores the need for defenders to monitor FakeUpdates chains and LockBit activity for potential Evil Corp–linked intrusions and to enhance detection of rebranded ransomware variants despite attribution obfuscation tactics.
hits.title: Evil Corp Pivots LockBit to Dodge U.S. Sanctions | Threatpost

hits.text: During a recent incident, a LockBit affiliate conducted initial intrusions using gpresult for policy dumping, Cobalt Strike loaders and PsExec for privilege escalation, followed by reconnaissance (whoami, netstat, quser, net view), lateral movement, persistence via a new user account, and data exfiltration over FTP with Wput; when deployment of LockBit (SHA256 079b99f6…) was blocked on the target network, the attacker pivoted to a newly observed Rust-written ransomware family dubbed 3AM (SHA256 307a1217…), which appends “.threeamtime” to encrypted files, stops over 100 security and backup services via net stop and wbadmin/bcdedit/wmic commands, deletes Volume Shadow copies with vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet, and drops a Tor‐accessible ransom note requiring a 32-character “-k” access key and offering decryption/mystical-themed extortion; although 3AM encryption succeeded on only one of three attempted hosts, its Conti-style “-m” (local/net) and “-h” parameters, heavy service-termination payload, and aggressive VSS wipe underscore its potential as a fallback vector—defenders should update Symantec/Broadcom signatures, monitor for the .threeamtime extension, suspicious Rust binaries, command-line flags “-k” and “-m”, and mass service stoppage activity, and block associated IOCs (185.202.0[.]111, 212.18.104[.]6, 85.159.229[.]62) to mitigate future 3AM use.
hits.title: 3AM: New Ransomware Family Used As Fallback in Failed LockBit Attack | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: In early 2023, ransomware postings dropped 41% month-on-month yet LockBit stayed dominant, and despite predictions of waning ROI, Q3 saw a surge—driven by CL0P’s mass exploits of file-transfer flaws—that surpassed the combined victim counts of 2021–22 and hit law firms, government, manufacturing, oil & gas, and logistics hardest. In Q4 two new strains surfaced: CACTUS, first observed by Kroll in March 2023, leverages critical Qlik Sense vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-41266, ‑41265, ‑48365) or VPN appliance flaws for initial access; embeds a decryption key in ntuser.dat via scheduled tasks; uses SoftPerfect Network Scanner, PowerShell, Cobalt Strike, Splashtop, AnyDesk and Chisel for reconnaissance, persistence and lateral movement; exfiltrates data over Tox and Rclone; and encrypts files with AES/OpenSSL (.cts1 extension) accompanied by cAcTuS.readme.txt demands. When a LockBit affiliate’s deployment failed, they defaulted to 3AM, a new Rust-based backup encryptor that halts services, deletes VSS snapshots, appends .threeamtime and a “0x666” marker, exfiltrates via Wput to FTP, and issues Tor-based ransom negotiations. To counter these evolving threats, organizations must patch VPN and Qlik Sense flaws, enforce least-privilege RDP with MFA, restrict unauthorized remote access tools, monitor for anomalous scheduled tasks, scanner and Tox/Rclone traffic, deploy EDR to flag Cobalt Strike and script-based execution, and maintain secure, offline backups.
hits.title: New Ransomware Strains - CACTUS and 3AM

canonical_entities: FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns
hits.text: Clop ransomware, a TA505-sponsored RaaS strain appending the “.ClOP” extension, infects entire networks by compromising Active Directory servers and manipulating Group Policy for persistence, then uses phishing-delivered HTML attachments to drop the Get2 loader, which in turn pulls SDBOT, FlawedAmmyy RATs, Cobalt Strike beacons and TinyMet reverse shells for reconnaissance, lateral movement (via SMB exploits), and exfiltration (often using the DEWMODE web shell). Operators employ double and quadruple extortion—threatening to publish or auction stolen data on their Cl0p^_-Leaks site and targeting executives/customers—to coerce ransoms, driving average payments up 43% to $220,298 (median $78,398) in Q1 2021 after FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns against Kiteworks FTA (CVE-2021-27101/02/03/04) and Fortra GoAnywhere MFT, while in 2023 they exploited PaperCut CVE-2023-27350 to deploy Truebot and LockBit/Clop, then MOVEit CVE-2023-24362/CVE-2023-35036 and an unpatched SQL injection flaw to steal data without payloads. Trend Micro detections reveal a May 2023 surge (245 attempts), with top targets in banking, retail and healthcare across Türkiye, Canada, the US and large enterprises worldwide.

Between July 2021 and January 2022 LockBit attempts surged globally—chiefly the US, India and Brazil—targeting healthcare and education yet boasting 41 leak-site victims (Dec 2021–Jan 2022) primarily SMBs (65.9%) across North America, Europe and APAC. With a professional affiliate program fueling continuous innovation and predicted upticks in supply-chain attacks in 2022, organizations should implement comprehensive asset inventory, least-privilege access, regular patching (including Fortinet CVE-2018-13379), RDP/VPN lockdown, application allow-listing, multifactor authentication, offline backups and MITRE TTP monitoring to detect and disrupt LockBit activity.

retrieved_context.text: Since mid-2022, Unit 42 has attributed over 100 high-value cryptocurrency and BPO incidents to Muddled Libra—a fluid subset of the Scattered Spider collective—initially executing structured smishing and 0ktapus phishing campaigns (leveraging over 200 realistic mobile-auth portals) against large business process outsourcers, then evolving in 2023 into an ALPHV/BlackCat affiliate with multi-million-dollar extortion demands, later resuming high-profile attacks in late 2024 and expanding through May 2025 into software automation, telecom, hospitality, finance and retail verticals; their adaptable tradecraft blends social engineering of IT helpdesks to reset passwords and MFA, inside BPO access, legitimate remote management tools for CRM exfiltration, NSOCKS/TrueSocks anonymizing proxies, custom virtual machines, the open-source “bedevil” rootkit on VMware vCenter, email-forwarding rules to hijack incident response communications, and AI-driven voice spoofing for vishing, with members cycling via Discord and Telegram to refresh niche skills and spawn offshoots such as Scatter Swine and Octo Tempest, while leveraging deep incident response framework knowledge to persist in environments and repeatedly reclaim stolen data before affiliating with DragonForce for ransomware; defenders should deploy interwoven modern security architectures (Cortex XSIAM/XDR, Advanced URL Filtering, DNS Security, App-ID), enforce strict access controls, conduct rigorous awareness training, and maintain vigilant MITRE-mapped monitoring (T1566, T1556, T1215, T1562) to thwart these multifaceted, evolving extortion campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Threat Group Assessment: Muddled Libra (Updated May 16, 2025)

hits.text: Researchers at Mandiant Intelligence have identified UNC2165—the latest evolution of the U.S.-sanctioned Evil Corp—as leveraging the FakeUpdates infection chain to gain initial access, followed by deployment of LockBit ransomware to obscure attribution and monetize extortion efforts. After OFAC sanctions in December 2019 crippled Evil Corp’s ability to profit from Dridex and its WastedLocker strain, the group briefly resurfaced under PayloadBin (likely a WastedLocker rebrand) and used HTML redirectors in malicious Excel files, then adopted Hades ransomware with code overlaps to distance itself further. By aligning with LockBit’s RaaS model—already proven effective against high-profile victims such as Accenture and Bangkok Air—UNC2165 can blend in with legitimate affiliates, reduce development overhead, and bypass sanctions enforcement that deters U.S. entities from negotiating ransoms with known Evil Corp actors. This shift underscores the need for defenders to monitor FakeUpdates chains and LockBit activity for potential Evil Corp–linked intrusions and to enhance detection of rebranded ransomware variants despite attribution obfuscation tactics.
hits.title: Evil Corp Pivots LockBit to Dodge U.S. Sanctions | Threatpost

hits.text: During a recent incident, a LockBit affiliate conducted initial intrusions using gpresult for policy dumping, Cobalt Strike loaders and PsExec for privilege escalation, followed by reconnaissance (whoami, netstat, quser, net view), lateral movement, persistence via a new user account, and data exfiltration over FTP with Wput; when deployment of LockBit (SHA256 079b99f6…) was blocked on the target network, the attacker pivoted to a newly observed Rust-written ransomware family dubbed 3AM (SHA256 307a1217…), which appends “.threeamtime” to encrypted files, stops over 100 security and backup services via net stop and wbadmin/bcdedit/wmic commands, deletes Volume Shadow copies with vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet, and drops a Tor‐accessible ransom note requiring a 32-character “-k” access key and offering decryption/mystical-themed extortion; although 3AM encryption succeeded on only one of three attempted hosts, its Conti-style “-m” (local/net) and “-h” parameters, heavy service-termination payload, and aggressive VSS wipe underscore its potential as a fallback vector—defenders should update Symantec/Broadcom signatures, monitor for the .threeamtime extension, suspicious Rust binaries, command-line flags “-k” and “-m”, and mass service stoppage activity, and block associated IOCs (185.202.0[.]111, 212.18.104[.]6, 85.159.229[.]62) to mitigate future 3AM use.
hits.title: 3AM: New Ransomware Family Used As Fallback in Failed LockBit Attack | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: In early 2023, ransomware postings dropped 41% month-on-month yet LockBit stayed dominant, and despite predictions of waning ROI, Q3 saw a surge—driven by CL0P’s mass exploits of file-transfer flaws—that surpassed the combined victim counts of 2021–22 and hit law firms, government, manufacturing, oil & gas, and logistics hardest. In Q4 two new strains surfaced: CACTUS, first observed by Kroll in March 2023, leverages critical Qlik Sense vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-41266, ‑41265, ‑48365) or VPN appliance flaws for initial access; embeds a decryption key in ntuser.dat via scheduled tasks; uses SoftPerfect Network Scanner, PowerShell, Cobalt Strike, Splashtop, AnyDesk and Chisel for reconnaissance, persistence and lateral movement; exfiltrates data over Tox and Rclone; and encrypts files with AES/OpenSSL (.cts1 extension) accompanied by cAcTuS.readme.txt demands. When a LockBit affiliate’s deployment failed, they defaulted to 3AM, a new Rust-based backup encryptor that halts services, deletes VSS snapshots, appends .threeamtime and a “0x666” marker, exfiltrates via Wput to FTP, and issues Tor-based ransom negotiations. To counter these evolving threats, organizations must patch VPN and Qlik Sense flaws, enforce least-privilege RDP with MFA, restrict unauthorized remote access tools, monitor for anomalous scheduled tasks, scanner and Tox/Rclone traffic, deploy EDR to flag Cobalt Strike and script-based execution, and maintain secure, offline backups.
hits.title: New Ransomware Strains - CACTUS and 3AM

hits.text: Trend Micro’s investigation into the LockBit ransomware-as-a-service operation, tracked as intrusion set Water Selkie, reveals the group’s marketing of its lightning-fast AES-128 head-only file encryption (first 4 KB) with RSA-wrapped keys, deployed via versatile affiliate-driven campaigns that source initial access through phishing (T1566), CVE-2018-13379 Fortinet VPN exploits (T1190) and compromised RDP/VPN accounts (T1078), then execute payloads via PowerShell Empire, Meterpreter, scheduled tasks or signed binaries (T1059, T1218), evade defenses with Mimikatz, GMER, Process Hacker or disabled Windows Defender (T1562), discover network shares and AD servers (T1083, T1135), laterally propagate via SMB or Cobalt Strike (T1570), exfiltrate data using StealBit or cloud storage (T1567) and encrypt data for impact (T1486), often on weekdays (~78%). Between July 2021 and January 2022 LockBit attempts surged globally—chiefly the US, India and Brazil—targeting healthcare and education yet boasting 41 leak-site victims (Dec 2021–Jan 2022) primarily SMBs (65.9%) across North America, Europe and APAC. With a professional affiliate program fueling continuous innovation and predicted upticks in supply-chain attacks in 2022, organizations should implement comprehensive asset inventory, least-privilege access, regular patching (including Fortinet CVE-2018-13379), RDP/VPN lockdown, application allow-listing, multifactor authentication, offline backups and MITRE TTP monitoring to detect and disrupt LockBit activity.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: LockBit | Trend Micro (US)

canonical_entities: FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns
hits.text: Clop ransomware, a TA505-sponsored RaaS strain appending the “.ClOP” extension, infects entire networks by compromising Active Directory servers and manipulating Group Policy for persistence, then uses phishing-delivered HTML attachments to drop the Get2 loader, which in turn pulls SDBOT, FlawedAmmyy RATs, Cobalt Strike beacons and TinyMet reverse shells for reconnaissance, lateral movement (via SMB exploits), and exfiltration (often using the DEWMODE web shell). Operators employ double and quadruple extortion—threatening to publish or auction stolen data on their Cl0p^_-Leaks site and targeting executives/customers—to coerce ransoms, driving average payments up 43% to $220,298 (median $78,398) in Q1 2021 after FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns against Kiteworks FTA (CVE-2021-27101/02/03/04) and Fortra GoAnywhere MFT, while in 2023 they exploited PaperCut CVE-2023-27350 to deploy Truebot and LockBit/Clop, then MOVEit CVE-2023-24362/CVE-2023-35036 and an unpatched SQL injection flaw to steal data without payloads. Trend Micro detections reveal a May 2023 surge (245 attempts), with top targets in banking, retail and healthcare across Türkiye, Canada, the US and large enterprises worldwide.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Clop | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: Since its discovery in November 2021, the ALPHV group has operated the BlackCat ransomware-as-a-service platform—recruiting affiliates from BlackMatter, REvil and DarkSide with revenue shares up to 90%—and deployed sophisticated triple-extortion schemes that combine data theft, encryption of Linux and Windows systems, public data leaks on a Tor-hosted site active since December 2021, and DDoS attacks if ransoms ($400K-$3M, negotiable; +15% for Bitcoin) go unpaid; coded in Rust and compiled for multiple OS architectures, BlackCat uses the --access-token flag to thwart sandbox analysis, kills security and backup processes (e.g., sql*, oracle, msaccess, synctime), excludes critical folders and files (e.g., Windows, System Volume Information, AppData, ntuser.dat, thumbs.db), and supports customizable payloads that resist reverse engineering—enabling strikes on over twenty organizations across U.S. critical infrastructure, retail, transport, telecom and pharma, including Colonial Pipeline, German fuel terminals and Belgian energy firms—and signaling a shift toward more secure, high-performance ransomware that demands enhanced backup validation, network segmentation, process monitoring and proactive threat hunting to mitigate.
hits.title: BlackCat Ransomware & Triple Extortion (Analysis & Tactics)

hits.text: BlackCat ransomware operators have introduced “Munchkin,” a new VM-based utility—delivered as an Alpine ISO loaded in VirtualBox—that automates propagation of the Rust-based BlackCat payload to remote machines and SMB/CIFS shares to evade host-level defenses. At boot, Munchkin’s ISO resets the VM root password, spawns a tmux “controller” session to run the /app/controller binary, decrypts strings via single-byte XOR, validates and deserializes a serialized /app/config file containing access tokens, victim credentials, target hosts/shares and block-lists, then mounts a /payloads directory to generate customized BlackCat samples from a template before iterating through configured tasks to encrypt network shares. The VM also houses numerous Python scripts for lateral movement and credential harvesting. This evolution in BlackCat’s RaaS toolkit reflects a broader trend of leveraging embedded VMs to thwart security solutions, expands the group’s global targeting footprint and underscores the need for defenses tuned to detect ISO-based VM deployments and tmux-launched malware.
hits.title: BlackCat Climbs the Summit With a New Tactic

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

hits.text: Security researcher Marc Newlin of SkySafe disclosed CVE-2023-45866, a critical, decade-old keystroke-injection flaw in the Bluetooth host state-machine that exploits an unauthenticated pairing mechanism in the Bluetooth specification to trick macOS (13.3.3), iOS (16.6, even in Lockdown Mode), Android (from 4.2.2 through 14 on devices including Pixel 7/6/4a, Pixel 2, Nexus 5, BLU DASH), and Linux BlueZ stacks (Ubuntu 18.04–23.10) into pairing with a malicious emulated keyboard, enabling remote attackers within Bluetooth range to run a Python-based script, inject arbitrary keystrokes, install apps, forward emails or texts, and execute commands without user confirmation or biometric/password authentication. hits.text: Since at least August 2021, the Yanluowang ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) operation has targeted U.S. financial firms and other sectors—including manufacturing, IT services, consultancy, and engineering—using a toolkit and playbook that mirror veteran groups Thieflock and Fivehands and suggesting possible affiliate ties; Symantec’s Threat Hunter Team first observed an underdeveloped October 2021 deployment in which attackers used AdFind for Active Directory reconnaissance, then refined their approach with PowerShell-driven BazarLoader implants, registry-based RDP enablement, ConnectWise for persistent access, and SoftPerfect Network Scanner for lateral movement, followed by credential theft via KeeThief, custom secretdump.exe, and deployment of Cobalt Strike Beacon, culminating in file encryption and double-extortion ransom notes threatening DDoS, employee calls, repeated attacks, and data deletion if law enforcement or negotiation firms are engaged; this operation contributes to the $590 million in ransomware payments recorded in 2021 and 314 global double-extortion incidents in October alone, underscoring the need for hardened Active Directory security, RDP restrictions, EDR with credential-dump detection, network monitoring for AdFind and BazarLoader activity, and adherence to FBI/CISA incident response recommendations.

hits.text: Since its emergence in 2018, the Ngioweb threat cluster has maintained continuous operations by systematically exploiting high-severity web application flaws—initially leveraging Apache Struts CVE-2017-5638 before pivoting in 2019 to Citrix ADC CVE-2019-19781 and F5 BIG-IP CVE-2020-5902, then targeting Log4Shell CVE-2021-44228 in 2021—while deploying fileless PowerShell loaders, Mimikatz credential theft, and Cobalt Strike beacons for persistent C2 over Tor. hits.text: Trend Micro observed over one million Conti ransomware attack attempts in the U.S. (Jan–Nov 2021), with the retail, insurance, manufacturing, telecommunications and healthcare sectors most targeted; operators—tied to Trickbot—gain initial access via BazarLoader phishing emails (Google Drive links) and exploitation of FortiGate flaws (CVE-2018-13379/13374) or Exchange ProxyShell, deploy Cobalt Strike, then perform reconnaissance (Whoami, Nltest, Net, ShareFinder), escalate privileges by harvesting domain-admin credentials or exploiting Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) and PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-1675), and dump credentials using ProcDump and Mimikatz (mass-mimikatz, Rubeus, kerberoasting), “reg save,” Get-GPPPassword, SharpChrome and SeatBelt; they move laterally via EternalBlue, PSExec, scheduled tasks and remote-access tools (Atera, AnyDesk), evade defenses with automated batch scripts (GMER, PC Hunter, PowerShell) to disable security services, then execute ransomware via scheduled jobs or DontSleep.exe, exfiltrate data using Rclone (to Mega) or WinSCP, and encrypt files with ChaCha20/RSA-4096 while deleting shadow copies for double extortion; organizations should inventory assets, enforce least privilege, virtual-patch public-facing apps, monitor for Cobalt Strike and anomalous scheduled tasks or credential-dumping activities, deploy multilayered endpoint and network defenses, and maintain reliable backups.

hits.text: Conti ransomware, a profit-driven RaaS syndicate linked by the FBI to over 400 global attacks (75% in the U.S.) with demands up to $25 million, has spent more than a year targeting high-stakes environments—hospitals, 911 dispatch centers, EMS and law enforcement—where IT outages can be life-threatening, exemplified by Ireland’s mid-May healthcare system shutdown that halted X-ray services and COVID testing; it gains initial access through Spearphishing Attachment (T1566.001), Exploit Public-Facing Application (T1190) and lacking MFA, then uses Cobalt Strike and PowerShell for discovery (T1083, T1135), lateral movement (SMB Shares T1021.002), privilege escalation (DLL Injection T1055.001) and defense evasion (Obfuscated Files T1027, Deobfuscate/Decode T1140), before executing “double extortion” (Data Encrypted for Impact T1486, Inhibit System Recovery T1490) and often reneging on decryption promises; actionable defenses include enforcing MFA, applying NGFW Threat Prevention with secure Vulnerability Protection Profiles, WildFire file analysis, Cortex XDR’s anti-malware/exploit modules, regular WildFire updates, Cortex XSOAR playbooks, and tracking IoCs via Unit 42’s GitHub and TAXII feeds.
hits.title: Conti Ransomware Gang: An Overview

hits.text: In August 2025 the FBI issued a public service announcement that FSB-linked Berserk Bear (aka Blue Kraken, Crouching Yeti, Dragonfly, Koala Team) has been exploiting the seven-year-old Cisco IOS/IOS XE Smart Install remote code execution/DoS vulnerability (CVE-2018-0171) to compromise critical infrastructure worldwide. Since Cisco first detected opportunistic attacks in November 2021, the group has collected configuration files from thousands of unpatched devices associated with U.S. critical infrastructure sectors, covertly modified those configs to maintain persistent unauthorized access, and conducted network reconnaissance targeting ICS-related protocols and applications. Cisco Talos reports that the campaign, referred to as Static Tundra, has aggressively hit telecommunications, higher education, and manufacturing networks across North America, Asia, Africa, and Europe, deploying custom SNMP tools and the SYNful Knock firmware implant—originally identified by FireEye in 2015—to evade detection and embed for years. The FBI’s warning underscores the urgent need for organizations to patch CVE-2018-0171, disable Smart Install, and implement comprehensive hardening, as other state-sponsored actors are likely conducting similar network device compromise campaigns.
hits.title: FBI warns of Russian hackers exploiting 7-year-old Cisco flaw

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.

canonical_entities: RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022
Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
hits.text: Trend Micro’s analysis of RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022 reveals a predominantly human-operated ransomware campaign that hit the manufacturing sector hardest (followed by education and banking) with the highest attack attempts observed in the U.S., France, and Brazil—driven in part by a high-profile 2021 breach of a Taiwanese hardware manufacturer. Initial access is achieved via malspam delivering multi-stage payloads that leverage IcedID and TrickBot for footholds, deploy Cobalt Strike beacons and PyXie RAT for code execution and data exfiltration, use SMB to propagate a VATET loader for lateral movement, and employ Mimikatz and LaZagne for credential harvesting. Upon execution, RansomEXX evades defense by disabling tools (T1562.001), skipping encryption of critical Windows paths, file names, and extensions, and terminating hundreds of business and security processes to maximize impact (T1486, T1490), then encrypts data and demands ransom. Recommended mitigations include strict audit and asset inventory, hardened configurations and least-privilege access, macro and email sandboxing to block malspam entry, regular patching and virtual patching, multifactor authentication, advanced behavior-based detection (e.g., Trend Micro Vision One™), and continuous employee training and red-team testing to disrupt the ransomware kill chain and protect against future RansomEXX intrusions.

hits.text: Trend Micro first detected Trigona ransomware in July 2023—attacks peaked in August and ceased after its October leak-site shutdown—targeting Turkey (23.5%), the Philippines (19.6%), Brazil (13.7%), Germany and Thailand, with government entities accounting for 21.4% of SPN detections and technology, retail, FMCG and banking also hit; leak-site data revealed 33 victims (45.5% North America—50% US, 27.3% Europe—9.1% UK, 6.1% AU), over half SMBs and 18.2% finance firms. Operators exploited CVE-2021-40539 and brokered credentials for initial access, evaded defenses by dropping turnoff.bat and defoff.bat to kill AV, performed discovery with network/port scanners, harvested credentials via Mimikatz, moved laterally using Splashtop, LogMeIn, ScreenConnect, AnyDesk, TeamViewer and Cobalt Strike–dropped MHYPROTINST, and escalated privileges on MSSQL via CLR shell to deploy nt.exe. The payload encrypts files with AES and TDCP_rijndael—defaulting to the first 0x80000 bytes with ._locked appended unless /full is used—and supports numerous CLI flags (e.g., /r,/erase,/shdwn) on Windows and Linux. Effective defenses include vulnerability management, least-privilege administration, MFA, allowlisting, secure backups and AI-driven detection across email, endpoint, web and network using solutions like Trend Micro Vision One, Deep Discovery Email Inspector, Cloud One Workload Security and Apex One.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Trigona | Trend Micro (US)

retrieved_context.text: Researchers at Accenture Security exposed Q3 2021 proliferation of Karakurt, a financially motivated data‐extortion group first identified in June 2021 upon registering two domains and launching a Twitter handle, which compromised over 40 primarily North American (95 percent) organizations across random sectors between September and November by sourcing or phishing VPN credentials for initial access, establishing persistence with Cobalt Strike beacons or AnyDesk, then harvesting administrator privileges via Mimikatz to evade EDR solutions; they compress stolen data with 7zip or WinZip and exfiltrate it to Mega.io using Rclone or FileZilla, foregoing ransomware encryption in favor of public leak threats, a low-overhead approach that can still cripple victims—underscoring the need for robust VPN credential management, continuous monitoring for living-off-the-land tools, and preventative controls to detect and disrupt such intrusions before data exfiltration.
retrieved_context.title: New 'Karakurt' hacking group focuses on data theft and extortion

retrieved_context.text: Trend Micro observed over one million Conti ransomware attack attempts in the U.S. (Jan–Nov 2021), with the retail, insurance, manufacturing, telecommunications and healthcare sectors most targeted; operators—tied to Trickbot—gain initial access via BazarLoader phishing emails (Google Drive links) and exploitation of FortiGate flaws (CVE-2018-13379/13374) or Exchange ProxyShell, deploy Cobalt Strike, then perform reconnaissance (Whoami, Nltest, Net, ShareFinder), escalate privileges by harvesting domain-admin credentials or exploiting Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) and PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-1675), and dump credentials using ProcDump and Mimikatz (mass-mimikatz, Rubeus, kerberoasting), “reg save,” Get-GPPPassword, SharpChrome and SeatBelt; they move laterally via EternalBlue, PSExec, scheduled tasks and remote-access tools (Atera, AnyDesk), evade defenses with automated batch scripts (GMER, PC Hunter, PowerShell) to disable security services, then execute ransomware via scheduled jobs or DontSleep.exe, exfiltrate data using Rclone (to Mega) or WinSCP, and encrypt files with ChaCha20/RSA-4096 while deleting shadow copies for double extortion; organizations should inventory assets, enforce least privilege, virtual-patch public-facing apps, monitor for Cobalt Strike and anomalous scheduled tasks or credential-dumping activities, deploy multilayered endpoint and network defenses, and maintain reliable backups.
retrieved_context.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Conti | Trend Micro (US)

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

retrieved_context.text: NCC Group’s CIRT has tracked Karakurt as an extortion-focused threat actor exploiting single-factor FortiGate VPNs via legitimate Active Directory credentials to achieve initial access, with an average dwell time of just over one month due to living-off-the-land techniques and lack of malware. Although the exact privilege escalation method remains unclear, Karakurt has attempted CVE-2020-1472 (Zerologon) and attained domain-admin rights, then used PsExec and RDP for lateral movement to the primary domain controller. Early in the breach they execute an encoded PowerShell DNS zone export—generating Microsoft-Windows-DNS-Server-Service Event ID 3150—and extract NTDS.dit via Volume Shadow Copy for further credential harvesting. After a brief exit, they re-enter to deploy AnyDesk for persistence, archive sensitive files with 7-Zip, and likely exfiltrate data via Rclone to cloud hosts. NCC Group recommends immediate FortiGate VPN MFA implementation, critical patching of domain controllers, and monitoring for Event ID 3150, unauthorized AnyDesk or PsExec usage, and VPN pool host authentications (e.g., DESKTOP-XXXXXX) to detect potential Karakurt intrusions.
retrieved_context.title: Detecting Karakurt – an extortion focused threat actor

retrieved_context.text: Conti ransomware, a profit-driven RaaS syndicate linked by the FBI to over 400 global attacks (75% in the U.S.) with demands up to $25 million, has spent more than a year targeting high-stakes environments—hospitals, 911 dispatch centers, EMS and law enforcement—where IT outages can be life-threatening, exemplified by Ireland’s mid-May healthcare system shutdown that halted X-ray services and COVID testing; it gains initial access through Spearphishing Attachment (T1566.001), Exploit Public-Facing Application (T1190) and lacking MFA, then uses Cobalt Strike and PowerShell for discovery (T1083, T1135), lateral movement (SMB Shares T1021.002), privilege escalation (DLL Injection T1055.001) and defense evasion (Obfuscated Files T1027, Deobfuscate/Decode T1140), before executing “double extortion” (Data Encrypted for Impact T1486, Inhibit System Recovery T1490) and often reneging on decryption promises; actionable defenses include enforcing MFA, applying NGFW Threat Prevention with secure Vulnerability Protection Profiles, WildFire file analysis, Cortex XDR’s anti-malware/exploit modules, regular WildFire updates, Cortex XSOAR playbooks, and tracking IoCs via Unit 42’s GitHub and TAXII feeds.
retrieved_context.title: Conti Ransomware Gang: An Overview

retrieved_context.text: In August 2025 the FBI issued a public service announcement that FSB-linked Berserk Bear (aka Blue Kraken, Crouching Yeti, Dragonfly, Koala Team) has been exploiting the seven-year-old Cisco IOS/IOS XE Smart Install remote code execution/DoS vulnerability (CVE-2018-0171) to compromise critical infrastructure worldwide. Since Cisco first detected opportunistic attacks in November 2021, the group has collected configuration files from thousands of unpatched devices associated with U.S. critical infrastructure sectors, covertly modified those configs to maintain persistent unauthorized access, and conducted network reconnaissance targeting ICS-related protocols and applications. Cisco Talos reports that the campaign, referred to as Static Tundra, has aggressively hit telecommunications, higher education, and manufacturing networks across North America, Asia, Africa, and Europe, deploying custom SNMP tools and the SYNful Knock firmware implant—originally identified by FireEye in 2015—to evade detection and embed for years. The FBI’s warning underscores the urgent need for organizations to patch CVE-2018-0171, disable Smart Install, and implement comprehensive hardening, as other state-sponsored actors are likely conducting similar network device compromise campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: FBI warns of Russian hackers exploiting 7-year-old Cisco flaw

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022
Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
retrieved_context.text: Trend Micro’s analysis of RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022 reveals a predominantly human-operated ransomware campaign that hit the manufacturing sector hardest (followed by education and banking) with the highest attack attempts observed in the U.S., France, and Brazil—driven in part by a high-profile 2021 breach of a Taiwanese hardware manufacturer. Initial access is achieved via malspam delivering multi-stage payloads that leverage IcedID and TrickBot for footholds, deploy Cobalt Strike beacons and PyXie RAT for code execution and data exfiltration, use SMB to propagate a VATET loader for lateral movement, and employ Mimikatz and LaZagne for credential harvesting. Upon execution, RansomEXX evades defense by disabling tools (T1562.001), skipping encryption of critical Windows paths, file names, and extensions, and terminating hundreds of business and security processes to maximize impact (T1486, T1490), then encrypts data and demands ransom. Recommended mitigations include strict audit and asset inventory, hardened configurations and least-privilege access, macro and email sandboxing to block malspam entry, regular patching and virtual patching, multifactor authentication, advanced behavior-based detection (e.g., Trend Micro Vision One™), and continuous employee training and red-team testing to disrupt the ransomware kill chain and protect against future RansomEXX intrusions.
retrieved_context.title: Ransomware Spotlight: RansomEXX | Trend Micro (US)

retrieved_context.text: Symantec’s Threat Hunter Team has linked the newly discovered Sidewalk loader backdoor—an evolution of the Crosswalk/Backdoor.Motnug family—to Grayfly (aka GREF/Wicked Panda), a China-linked espionage group active since March 2017 that employs custom backdoors, Trojan.Chattak, Cobalt Strike, web shells and credential-dumpers against telecom, IT, media and finance targets in Taiwan, Vietnam, the US and Mexico; in a recent campaign they exploited public-facing Microsoft Exchange and MySQL servers via commodity and zero-day flaws to execute Base64-encoded PowerShell commands through certutil, install an ASPX web shell in the ClientAccess\ecp directory, deploy Sidewalk via installutil.exe, create persistence with WMIC-launched scheduled tasks, then run a custom Mimikatz variant (SHA256 b3eb783b017da32e33d19670b39eae0b11de8e983891dd4feb873d6e9333608d) to harvest credentials—all within about an hour before ceasing observable activity; three Chengdu 404 executives were indicted in 2020 for attacks on over 100 organizations, highlighting Grayfly’s persistence and underscoring the need to promptly patch Exchange and MySQL servers, monitor anomalous PowerShell and scheduled-task activity, and deploy IOC-based detection to block Sidewalk and related tools.
retrieved_context.title: Grayfly: Chinese Threat Actor Uses Newly-discovered Sidewalk Malware | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: exfiltrating sensitive diplomatic and policy-related data
hits.text: Since at least 2021, the Chinese state-linked APT group FishMonger—operating under the I-SOON umbrella—has waged sophisticated espionage against government institutions and NGOs in Southeast Asia and Europe, initiating attacks via spear-phishing emails that deliver template-injected Microsoft Office documents to exploit vulnerabilities or employ social engineering and deploy a Spyder loader, then install the custom “SilentBreeze” backdoor. SilentBreeze establishes persistence through a scheduled PowerShell task using a Mozilla-style User-Agent header to download additional payloads from hxxps://cdn-storage.cloud-service.site/updates.php, communicates with command-and-control servers over encrypted channels via compromised third-party proxies, and remains undetected for months while harvesting credentials and exfiltrating sensitive diplomatic and policy-related data aligned with Chinese strategic interests in the South China Sea and human rights monitoring. ESET researchers note FishMonger’s continual toolset modifications and counter-detection tactics, distinctive network traffic patterns, and reliance on third-party proxies to mask true C2 infrastructure, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to harden phishing defenses, monitor for template injection in Office files, audit scheduled PowerShell tasks, and scrutinize outbound connections to anomalous cloud-service URLs to disrupt this persistent threat.
hits.title: Chinese FishMonger APT Operated by I‑SOON Attacking Government Entities & NGOs

canonical_entities: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
hits.text: In late 2023, researchers uncovered a sophisticated Taiwan-focused espionage operation in which a China-linked APT actor (likely APT27) hijacked an abandoned Sogou Zhuyin Windows update server—vacated when Sogou ceased Zhuyin support in mid-2022—and weaponized it to distribute a trojanized updater (SHA-256: 3f5c…) that deployed a custom backdoor and Cobalt Strike beacon via HTTP(S) (MITRE T1195.002, T1071.001). Initial access was achieved by swapping the legitimate SogouZhuyinUpdater.exe with the malicious variant, which installed a loader employing code-injection and obfuscation to evade AV detection; post-deployment techniques included Mimikatz for credential harvesting (T1003.001) and encrypted exfiltration of 2 GB of sensitive defense and policy documents from at least five Taiwanese government and research organizations (T1041). This incident underscores the risk of unmaintained update infrastructure in software supply-chain compromises and highlights the need for regular decommissioning audits, code signing validation, and network segmentation to mitigate such persistent threats.
hits.title: Abandoned Sogou Zhuyin Update Server Hijacked, Weaponized in Taiwan Espionage Campaign

canonical_entities: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
hits.text: Since its emergence in 2021 and first detection on Trend Micro telemetry in March 2022, the TargetCompany ransomware group has launched 269 attempted attacks against 250 disclosed Trend customers—predominantly in Asia (notably India and Saudi Arabia)—while avoiding Kazakhstan, Russia, Qatar, and Ukraine, and focusing on manufacturing, retail, and telecommunications; their November 2022–May 2023 leak site lists 20 confirmed victims (mostly small businesses) across the Asia-Pacific, Europe, and Middle East in IT, manufacturing, apparel, and automotive sectors. Initial access vectors include exploitation of CVE-2019-1069 and CVE-2020-0618 RCE flaws, SQL Server xp_cmdshell abuse, and OneNote-based spam campaigns. Execution relies on WMIC-invoked PowerShell scripts to retrieve various payloads (TargetComp ransomware, Remcos backdoor, Negasteal, Snake Keylogger) and, since January 2022, reflective loading of a .NET downloader that decrypts and runs payloads in memory via XOR or inversion. For defense evasion, operators deploy GMER, PCHunter64 (YDArk.exe), Advance Process Termination, KILLAV, and killer.bat to disable AV and security services; discovery is achieved through network scans and Mimikatz credential dumping; lateral movement via RDP-based RCE; C2 evolved from an open Mallox directory to an Nginx-protected server. Impact involves ChaCha20 file encryption with keys generated by Curve25519 and AES-128, file extensions such as .mallox/.exploit/.avast and ransom notes titled “HOW TO RECOVER!!.TXT,” and potential data exfiltration. Their tactics span MITRE techniques T1190, T1059.001, T1047, T1562.001, T1003.001, T1071.001, T1486, and more. The group’s maturation—evidenced by reflective loading and possible RaaS adoption—underscores the urgency for organizations to enforce asset inventories, least-privilege access, prompt patching (or virtual patching), multifactor authentication, sandboxed email defenses, AI/ML-driven detection, regular backups, and continuous red-team testing to thwart this active threat.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: TargetCompany | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: A state-sponsored APT42 (formerly UNC788), attributed to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, conducted over 30 confirmed espionage attacks since 2015 targeting activists, dissidents, and strategic organizations across non-profits, education, governments, healthcare, legal, manufacturing, media, and pharmaceuticals in 14+ countries including Australia, Europe, Middle East, and U.S. The group shares partial overlaps with APT35 (Charming Kitten, Cobalt Illusion, ITG18, Phosphorus, TA453, Yellow Garuda) and uses highly targeted spear-phishing and social engineering to build trust, distributing Android malware VINETHORN and PINEFLOWER via text messages capable of recording audio, extracting multimedia/SMS, and tracking geolocation, with a SaferVPN masqueraded payload observed April-October 2021. Windows malware includes TAMECAT (PowerShell backdoor), TABBYCAT (VBA macro dropper), and VBREVSHELL (reverse shell macro). APT42's link to UNC2448/DEV-0270/Cobalt Mirage (ransomware operators using BitLocker) operates through front company Najee Technology Hooshmand with aliases Secnerd and Lifeweb, though missions differ—APT42 focuses on domestic politics and regime stability while APT35 targets long-term resource-intensive operations, with pharmaceutical intrusions commencing March 2020 during COVID-19 pandemic onset.
hits.title: Iranian APT42 Launched Over 30 Espionage Attacks Against Activists and Dissidents

hits.text: In February 2022, CISA, the FBI, US Cyber Command CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA issued a joint advisory on Iranian Ministry of Intelligence–linked APT MuddyWater (aka MERCURY, Earth Vetala, Static Kitten, Seedworm, TEMP.Zagros), active since 2018 and focused on cyber espionage, intellectual property theft and ransomware against defense, oil & gas, government and telecom sectors across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America. Exploiting publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and open-source tools, MuddyWater delivers malicious PDFs with embedded links that display error messages prompting users to download Excel maldocs or Windows executables; these files host VBA macros that drop WSF scripts to execute PowerShell and VB payloads, leverage LoLBins, and stage RATs and malware families including PowGoop, Canopy, Small Sieve, POWERSTATS and Mori while communicating with C2 over HTTP and DNS and persisting via Registry Run keys. Cisco Talos observed regional campaigns in Turkey (Nov 2021), Pakistan (Aug 2021) and Armenia (Jun 2021) using decoy documents, signaling tokens and a consistent TTP set, suggesting a conglomerate of subgroups migrating techniques across regions. The resultant network access and data exfiltration underscore the imperative for proactive DFIR readiness, deployment of XDR/MDR platforms, rigorous vulnerability management, macro execution restrictions, PowerShell/LoLBin monitoring and ongoing user awareness training reinforced by incident response tabletop exercises.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at Iranian APT "MuddyWater"

hits.text: Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has observed a 33% year-over-year increase in government-backed phishing warnings—over 50,000 sent to users so far in 2021—driven in part by a large APT28 (Fancy Bear) campaign and sustained by ongoing operations from Iran-aligned APT35. Since early 2021, APT35 has compromised a UK university website to host a phishing kit targeting Gmail, Yahoo and Hotmail credentials—including second-factor codes—and continues its credential harvesting campaigns against government, academia, journalism and NGOs using hijacked sites and link-shortening redirects. In May 2020 it attempted to distribute spyware disguised as a VPN on Google Play Store (blocked before installation) and has pursued similar Android C2 apps on other platforms. The group also impersonates conference officials (e.g., Munich Security, T20 Italy) to initiate phishing, embedding JavaScript to relay visitor IP, user-agent and locale via Telegram bots—a tactic TAG disrupted by reporting the bots. TAG’s layered defenses include batch-sent warnings, Workspace admin alerts, Safe Browsing domain blocks and urging high-risk users to enable two-factor authentication or enroll in Advanced Protection.
hits.title: Countering threats from Iran

canonical_entities: deployed a webshell on the router’s web server
Credentials from Password Stores: Security Account Manager
hits.text: Dragos researchers, in collaboration with Ukraine’s CSSC, unearthed FrostyGoop—an ICS-specific malware first spotted in April and used in January to disrupt central heating in over 600 Lviv apartment buildings—marking the first known malware to leverage Modbus TCP for read/write operations on operational technology. Attackers gained initial access in April 2023 by exploiting a MikroTik router vulnerability, deployed a webshell on the router’s web server, and maintained persistence via Tor and L2TP tunnels to Moscow-based IPs. After spending months conducting reconnaissance, they extracted credentials by dumping the SAM registry hive in December, then directly issued scripted Modbus commands—read from a JSON configuration file—to publicly exposed ENCO heating controllers, even downgrading firmware to disable monitoring and force inaccurate measurements that halted heating services for nearly two days amid subzero temperatures. This incident underscores the threat posed by internet-exposed ICS devices—over 46,000 globally using Modbus—and highlights poor network segmentation, unpatched ICS CVEs, and the ease with which FrostyGoop’s protocol-agnostic payload can be repurposed against diverse industrial controllers, necessitating immediate network segmentation, firmware monitoring, and patch management in OT environments.
hits.title: ICS malware FrostyGoop disrupted heating in Ukraine, remains threat to OT worldwide

hits.text: Since at least 2015, Mandiant has identified APT42—an IRGC-linked Iranian state-sponsored threat actor also known as APT35—conducting over 30 spear-phishing operations across 14 countries against government officials, policymakers, journalists, academics and dissidents, evolving tactics from 2020 Oxford vaccinologist-themed pharmaceutical lures to 2021 fake interview requests using compromised U.S. media accounts for 37-day MFA-intercepting credential harvesting, and February 2022 phishes posing as a British news agency targeting political science professors; beyond credential theft via shortened URLs and PDF attachments directing victims to spoofed login portals, APT42 deploys custom Android spyware—spread via SMS links to messaging/VPN apps—to exfiltrate calls, SMS, audio recordings, images and GPS data in real time, while on Windows it employs lightweight custom malware for initial access, privilege escalation, reconnaissance, lateral movement through follow-on phishing, and persistence via scheduled tasks and registry keys; Mandiant further correlates APT42’s TTPs with November 2021 PHOSPHORUS BitLocker ransomware attempts against Fortinet FortiOS SSL VPN and unpatched Exchange servers, highlighting the group’s multi-platform espionage-to-ransom capabilities and real-world threat to high-value targets.
hits.title: New Iranian hacking group APT42 deploys custom Android spyware

canonical_entities: installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry
hits.text: The Lotus Blossom APT (aka Lotus Panda, Billbug, Spring Dragon) has stepped up cyberespionage against APAC government targets by deploying new Sagerunex backdoor variants and abusing Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) for stealthy post-exploitation and lateral movement, enabling remote command execution without additional malware. Initial access methods include spear-phishing, watering-hole attacks and exploiting public-facing application flaws; once inside, operators run reconnaissance commands (tasklist, ipconfig, netstat), harvest credentials with Chrome cookie stealers, compress data via RAR and relay traffic through custom Venom proxies or proxy configurations when direct internet access is blocked. Persistence is achieved by installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry under hijacked service names (tapisrv, swprv) to auto-launch at startup, while command-and-control blends encrypted traffic into legitimate platforms—stolen data uploaded as .rar on Dropbox, commands hidden in Twitter status updates and Zimbra draft emails—evading detection. Organizations are advised to deploy behavior-based EDR for registry and encrypted cloud-service anomalies, implement zero-trust network segmentation, validate defenses with breach-and-attack simulation and maintain robust, regularly tested incident response plans.
hits.title: Lotus Blossom APT Exploits WMI for Post-Exploitation Activities

Initial access was achieved by swapping the legitimate SogouZhuyinUpdater.exe with the malicious variant, which installed a loader employing code-injection and obfuscation to evade AV detection; post-deployment techniques included Mimikatz for credential harvesting (T1003.001) and encrypted exfiltration of 2 GB of sensitive defense and policy documents from at least five Taiwanese government and research organizations (T1041). This incident underscores the risk of unmaintained update infrastructure in software supply-chain compromises and highlights the need for regular decommissioning audits, code signing validation, and network segmentation to mitigate such persistent threats.
retrieved_context.title: Abandoned Sogou Zhuyin Update Server Hijacked, Weaponized in Taiwan Espionage Campaign

canonical_entities: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
retrieved_context.text: Since its emergence in 2021 and first detection on Trend Micro telemetry in March 2022, the TargetCompany ransomware group has launched 269 attempted attacks against 250 disclosed Trend customers—predominantly in Asia (notably India and Saudi Arabia)—while avoiding Kazakhstan, Russia, Qatar, and Ukraine, and focusing on manufacturing, retail, and telecommunications; their November 2022–May 2023 leak site lists 20 confirmed victims (mostly small businesses) across the Asia-Pacific, Europe, and Middle East in IT, manufacturing, apparel, and automotive sectors. Initial access vectors include exploitation of CVE-2019-1069 and CVE-2020-0618 RCE flaws, SQL Server xp_cmdshell abuse, and OneNote-based spam campaigns. Execution relies on WMIC-invoked PowerShell scripts to retrieve various payloads (TargetComp ransomware, Remcos backdoor, Negasteal, Snake Keylogger) and, since January 2022, reflective loading of a .NET downloader that decrypts and runs payloads in memory via XOR or inversion. For defense evasion, operators deploy GMER, PCHunter64 (YDArk.exe), Advance Process Termination, KILLAV, and killer.bat to disable AV and security services; discovery is achieved through network scans and Mimikatz credential dumping; lateral movement via RDP-based RCE; C2 evolved from an open Mallox directory to an Nginx-protected server. Impact involves ChaCha20 file encryption with keys generated by Curve25519 and AES-128, file extensions such as .mallox/.exploit/.avast and ransom notes titled “HOW TO RECOVER!!.TXT,” and potential data exfiltration. Their tactics span MITRE techniques T1190, T1059.001, T1047, T1562.001, T1003.001, T1071.001, T1486, and more. The group’s maturation—evidenced by reflective loading and possible RaaS adoption—underscores the urgency for organizations to enforce asset inventories, least-privilege access, prompt patching (or virtual patching), multifactor authentication, sandboxed email defenses, AI/ML-driven detection, regular backups, and continuous red-team testing to thwart this active threat.
retrieved_context.title: Ransomware Spotlight: TargetCompany | Trend Micro (US)

retrieved_context.text: A state-sponsored APT42 (formerly UNC788), attributed to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, conducted over 30 confirmed espionage attacks since 2015 targeting activists, dissidents, and strategic organizations across non-profits, education, governments, healthcare, legal, manufacturing, media, and pharmaceuticals in 14+ countries including Australia, Europe, Middle East, and U.S. The group shares partial overlaps with APT35 (Charming Kitten, Cobalt Illusion, ITG18, Phosphorus, TA453, Yellow Garuda) and uses highly targeted spear-phishing and social engineering to build trust, distributing Android malware VINETHORN and PINEFLOWER via text messages capable of recording audio, extracting multimedia/SMS, and tracking geolocation, with a SaferVPN masqueraded payload observed April-October 2021. Windows malware includes TAMECAT (PowerShell backdoor), TABBYCAT (VBA macro dropper), and VBREVSHELL (reverse shell macro). APT42's link to UNC2448/DEV-0270/Cobalt Mirage (ransomware operators using BitLocker) operates through front company Najee Technology Hooshmand with aliases Secnerd and Lifeweb, though missions differ—APT42 focuses on domestic politics and regime stability while APT35 targets long-term resource-intensive operations, with pharmaceutical intrusions commencing March 2020 during COVID-19 pandemic onset.
retrieved_context.title: Iranian APT42 Launched Over 30 Espionage Attacks Against Activists and Dissidents

retrieved_context.text: In February 2022, CISA, the FBI, US Cyber Command CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA issued a joint advisory on Iranian Ministry of Intelligence–linked APT MuddyWater (aka MERCURY, Earth Vetala, Static Kitten, Seedworm, TEMP.Zagros), active since 2018 and focused on cyber espionage, intellectual property theft and ransomware against defense, oil & gas, government and telecom sectors across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America. Exploiting publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and open-source tools, MuddyWater delivers malicious PDFs with embedded links that display error messages prompting users to download Excel maldocs or Windows executables; these files host VBA macros that drop WSF scripts to execute PowerShell and VB payloads, leverage LoLBins, and stage RATs and malware families including PowGoop, Canopy, Small Sieve, POWERSTATS and Mori while communicating with C2 over HTTP and DNS and persisting via Registry Run keys. Cisco Talos observed regional campaigns in Turkey (Nov 2021), Pakistan (Aug 2021) and Armenia (Jun 2021) using decoy documents, signaling tokens and a consistent TTP set, suggesting a conglomerate of subgroups migrating techniques across regions. The resultant network access and data exfiltration underscore the imperative for proactive DFIR readiness, deployment of XDR/MDR platforms, rigorous vulnerability management, macro execution restrictions, PowerShell/LoLBin monitoring and ongoing user awareness training reinforced by incident response tabletop exercises.
retrieved_context.title: An In-Depth Look at Iranian APT "MuddyWater"

retrieved_context.text: Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has observed a 33% year-over-year increase in government-backed phishing warnings—over 50,000 sent to users so far in 2021—driven in part by a large APT28 (Fancy Bear) campaign and sustained by ongoing operations from Iran-aligned APT35. Since early 2021, APT35 has compromised a UK university website to host a phishing kit targeting Gmail, Yahoo and Hotmail credentials—including second-factor codes—and continues its credential harvesting campaigns against government, academia, journalism and NGOs using hijacked sites and link-shortening redirects. In May 2020 it attempted to distribute spyware disguised as a VPN on Google Play Store (blocked before installation) and has pursued similar Android C2 apps on other platforms. The group also impersonates conference officials (e.g., Munich Security, T20 Italy) to initiate phishing, embedding JavaScript to relay visitor IP, user-agent and locale via Telegram bots—a tactic TAG disrupted by reporting the bots. TAG’s layered defenses include batch-sent warnings, Workspace admin alerts, Safe Browsing domain blocks and urging high-risk users to enable two-factor authentication or enroll in Advanced Protection.
retrieved_context.title: Countering threats from Iran

retrieved_context.text: Dragos researchers, in collaboration with Ukraine’s CSSC, unearthed FrostyGoop—an ICS-specific malware first spotted in April and used in January to disrupt central heating in over 600 Lviv apartment buildings—marking the first known malware to leverage Modbus TCP for read/write operations on operational technology. Attackers gained initial access in April 2023 by exploiting a MikroTik router vulnerability, deployed a webshell on the router’s web server, and maintained persistence via Tor and L2TP tunnels to Moscow-based IPs. After spending months conducting reconnaissance, they extracted credentials by dumping the SAM registry hive in December, then directly issued scripted Modbus commands—read from a JSON configuration file—to publicly exposed ENCO heating controllers, even downgrading firmware to disable monitoring and force inaccurate measurements that halted heating services for nearly two days amid subzero temperatures. This incident underscores the threat posed by internet-exposed ICS devices—over 46,000 globally using Modbus—and highlights poor network segmentation, unpatched ICS CVEs, and the ease with which FrostyGoop’s protocol-agnostic payload can be repurposed against diverse industrial controllers, necessitating immediate network segmentation, firmware monitoring, and patch management in OT environments.
retrieved_context.title: ICS malware FrostyGoop disrupted heating in Ukraine, remains threat to OT worldwide

retrieved_context.text: Since at least 2015, Mandiant has identified APT42—an IRGC-linked Iranian state-sponsored threat actor also known as APT35—conducting over 30 spear-phishing operations across 14 countries against government officials, policymakers, journalists, academics and dissidents, evolving tactics from 2020 Oxford vaccinologist-themed pharmaceutical lures to 2021 fake interview requests using compromised U.S. media accounts for 37-day MFA-intercepting credential harvesting, and February 2022 phishes posing as a British news agency targeting political science professors; beyond credential theft via shortened URLs and PDF attachments directing victims to spoofed login portals, APT42 deploys custom Android spyware—spread via SMS links to messaging/VPN apps—to exfiltrate calls, SMS, audio recordings, images and GPS data in real time, while on Windows it employs lightweight custom malware for initial access, privilege escalation, reconnaissance, lateral movement through follow-on phishing, and persistence via scheduled tasks and registry keys; Mandiant further correlates APT42’s TTPs with November 2021 PHOSPHORUS BitLocker ransomware attempts against Fortinet FortiOS SSL VPN and unpatched Exchange servers, highlighting the group’s multi-platform espionage-to-ransom capabilities and real-world threat to high-value targets.

retrieved_context.text: The Lotus Blossom APT (aka Lotus Panda, Billbug, Spring Dragon) has stepped up cyberespionage against APAC government targets by deploying new Sagerunex backdoor variants and abusing Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) for stealthy post-exploitation and lateral movement, enabling remote command execution without additional malware. Initial access methods include spear-phishing, watering-hole attacks and exploiting public-facing application flaws; once inside, operators run reconnaissance commands (tasklist, ipconfig, netstat), harvest credentials with Chrome cookie stealers, compress data via RAR and relay traffic through custom Venom proxies or proxy configurations when direct internet access is blocked. Persistence is achieved by installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry under hijacked service names (tapisrv, swprv) to auto-launch at startup, while command-and-control blends encrypted traffic into legitimate platforms—stolen data uploaded as .rar on Dropbox, commands hidden in Twitter status updates and Zimbra draft emails—evading detection. Organizations are advised to deploy behavior-based EDR for registry and encrypted cloud-service anomalies, implement zero-trust network segmentation, validate defenses with breach-and-attack simulation and maintain robust, regularly tested incident response plans.
retrieved_context.title: Lotus Blossom APT Exploits WMI for Post-Exploitation Activities

hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.

hits.text: Water Ouroboros is a Ransomware-as-a-Service operation that exploits public-facing Oracle WebLogic vulnerabilities (CVE-2019-2725, CVE-2017-10271, CVE-2019-2729) or drive-by installers for initial access (T1190, T1189), then executes remote Windows commands (wmic.exe, bcdedit.exe, wbadmin.exe, vssadmin.exe) to delete backups and disable recovery (T1490, T1562.001) before encrypting fixed, removable and network drives via a Go-based custom routine that uses RTLGenRandom to generate a symmetric key, protects it with embedded RSA public keys (App_ExportKey), appends “.locked” (unless suppressed with –E), excludes over 60 file extensions, and accepts credentials (c {user}:{pass}), logging (–a), non-aggressive (–A) and size filters (–m). Victims find Contact Us.txt ransom notes pointing to a TOR payment site and Hive Leaks data-dump threat. Post-infection, actors maintain access via compromised admin accounts (T1078), disable security tools (PCHunter, ProcessHacker), dump credentials from registry hives (T1003.002), move laterally over RDP/SMB (T1021.001/002), discover assets via AdFind (T1595.002) and exfiltrate data over C&C (SharpRhino RAT/T1071.001, T1041). With 136 incidents in the US and notable impacts on construction, IT, manufacturing and healthcare SMBs, the campaign underscores the need for timely patching, hardened public-facing apps, least-privilege access, MFA, robust backups and advanced threat detection.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Water Ouroboros | Trend Micro (US)

Post-infection, actors maintain access via compromised admin accounts (T1078), disable security tools (PCHunter, ProcessHacker), dump credentials from registry hives (T1003.002), move laterally over RDP/SMB (T1021.001/002), discover assets via AdFind (T1595.002) and exfiltrate data over C&C (SharpRhino RAT/T1071.001, T1041).
