canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

hits.text: In a multi-year espionage campaign uncovered by Mandiant, the Chinese UNC3886 group exploited a critical VMware vCenter Server zero-day (CVE-2023-34048) from late 2021 until its October 2023 patch, triggering vmdird service crashes and removing core dumps to stealthily gain privileged access, then delivering VirtualPita and VirtualPie backdoors via malicious vSphere Installation Bundles on ESXi hosts; they subsequently chained the VMware Tools authentication bypass flaw (CVE-2023-20867) to escalate privileges, harvest and exfiltrate files from guest VMs. UNC3886—targeting defense, government, telecom and technology sectors in the US and APJ—also abused a Fortinet firewall zero-day (CVE-2022-41328) to deploy Castletap and Thincrust implants, demonstrating advanced reverse-engineering of FortiOS. This campaign highlights the urgent need for rapid patching of virtualization and firewall platforms, deployment of EDR solutions and preservation of forensic artifacts to detect and thwart such sophisticated attacks.
hits.title: Chinese hackers exploit VMware bug as zero-day for two years

hits.text: Since its emergence in 2013, Iran-linked APT35 (aka Charming Kitten/Phosphorus) has executed a series of high-value espionage campaigns—beginning with a 2014 social-media spying operation—and continued in 2019 with spear-phishing against U.S., French and Middle East academic institutions before Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit seized control of 99 APT35 domains; in late 2020 the group targeted oncology, genetics and neurology researchers in Israel and the U.S. via its “BadBlood” PDF-based spear-phishing campaign, while in 2021 it chained Exchange Server flaws (ProxyShell) for network intrusion and demonstrated TTP overlaps with Momento ransomware (CVE-2021-21972 exploiter); in January 2022 it performed mass Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) scans—over 80 percent of attempts originated in the U.S.—and later deployed a stealthy .NET-based PowerShell backdoor (“PowerLess”) that runs in-process to avoid detection, followed by Hyperscrape, a Windows .NET mailbox exfiltration tool for Outlook, Gmail and Yahoo! that quietly harvests emails once the actor possesses valid credentials or session cookies, and a companion Telegram dump utility; APT35 maintains persistence for intelligence collection or monetizes access when systems lack strategic value, underscoring the need for timely patching, multi-factor authentication and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at APT35 aka Charming Kitten

retrieved_context.text: In a multi-year espionage campaign uncovered by Mandiant, the Chinese UNC3886 group exploited a critical VMware vCenter Server zero-day (CVE-2023-34048) from late 2021 until its October 2023 patch, triggering vmdird service crashes and removing core dumps to stealthily gain privileged access, then delivering VirtualPita and VirtualPie backdoors via malicious vSphere Installation Bundles on ESXi hosts; they subsequently chained the VMware Tools authentication bypass flaw (CVE-2023-20867) to escalate privileges, harvest and exfiltrate files from guest VMs. UNC3886—targeting defense, government, telecom and technology sectors in the US and APJ—also abused a Fortinet firewall zero-day (CVE-2022-41328) to deploy Castletap and Thincrust implants, demonstrating advanced reverse-engineering of FortiOS. This campaign highlights the urgent need for rapid patching of virtualization and firewall platforms, deployment of EDR solutions and preservation of forensic artifacts to detect and thwart such sophisticated attacks.
retrieved_context.title: Chinese hackers exploit VMware bug as zero-day for two years

retrieved_context.text: In February 2022, CISA, the FBI, US Cyber Command CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA issued a joint advisory on Iranian Ministry of Intelligence–linked APT MuddyWater (aka MERCURY, Earth Vetala, Static Kitten, Seedworm, TEMP.Zagros), active since 2018 and focused on cyber espionage, intellectual property theft and ransomware against defense, oil & gas, government and telecom sectors across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America. Exploiting publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and open-source tools, MuddyWater delivers malicious PDFs with embedded links that display error messages prompting users to download Excel maldocs or Windows executables; these files host VBA macros that drop WSF scripts to execute PowerShell and VB payloads, leverage LoLBins, and stage RATs and malware families including PowGoop, Canopy, Small Sieve, POWERSTATS and Mori while communicating with C2 over HTTP and DNS and persisting via Registry Run keys. Cisco Talos observed regional campaigns in Turkey (Nov 2021), Pakistan (Aug 2021) and Armenia (Jun 2021) using decoy documents, signaling tokens and a consistent TTP set, suggesting a conglomerate of subgroups migrating techniques across regions. The resultant network access and data exfiltration underscore the imperative for proactive DFIR readiness, deployment of XDR/MDR platforms, rigorous vulnerability management, macro execution restrictions, PowerShell/LoLBin monitoring and ongoing user awareness training reinforced by incident response tabletop exercises.
retrieved_context.title: An In-Depth Look at Iranian APT "MuddyWater"

retrieved_context.text: Since 2021, BadPilot—a subgroup of Russia’s state-sponsored APT44 (also known as Seashell Blizzard/Sandworm)—has executed a multi-year campaign to compromise critical energy, oil & gas, telecom, shipping, arms manufacturing, government, military, transportation and logistics networks across Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East, intensifying after Russia’s 2022 invasion with intelligence gathering, operational disruption and at least three wiper-style destructive attacks in Ukraine; by 2023 its scope expanded to large-scale compromises across Europe, the United States and the Middle East, and in 2024 it added the UK, Canada and Australia. The actor exploits n-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473, CVE-2022-41352, CVE-2023-32315, CVE-2023-42793, CVE-2023-23397, CVE-2024-1709, CVE-2023-48788), conducts credential theft and supply-chain attacks via regionally managed IT service providers, deploys LocalOlive web shells and uses legitimate management tools (Atera Agent, Splashtop) for initial access and persistence; post-compromise, it harvests credentials with Procdump and registry modifications, exfiltrates data via Rclone, Chisel and Plink over covert Tor-routed tunnels, and performs lateral movement through DNS reconfiguration, new services, scheduled tasks and OpenSSH backdoors. Microsoft warns the subgroup’s near-global reach and horizontal scaling capabilities, and has published hunting queries, IoCs and YARA rules to enable defenders to detect and disrupt its operations.
retrieved_context.title: BadPilot network hacking campaign fuels Russian SandWorm attacks

retrieved_context.text: Since its emergence in 2013, Iran-linked APT35 (aka Charming Kitten/Phosphorus) has executed a series of high-value espionage campaigns—beginning with a 2014 social-media spying operation—and continued in 2019 with spear-phishing against U.S., French and Middle East academic institutions before Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit seized control of 99 APT35 domains; in late 2020 the group targeted oncology, genetics and neurology researchers in Israel and the U.S. via its “BadBlood” PDF-based spear-phishing campaign, while in 2021 it chained Exchange Server flaws (ProxyShell) for network intrusion and demonstrated TTP overlaps with Momento ransomware (CVE-2021-21972 exploiter); in January 2022 it performed mass Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) scans—over 80 percent of attempts originated in the U.S.—and later deployed a stealthy .NET-based PowerShell backdoor (“PowerLess”) that runs in-process to avoid detection, followed by Hyperscrape, a Windows .NET mailbox exfiltration tool for Outlook, Gmail and Yahoo! that quietly harvests emails once the actor possesses valid credentials or session cookies, and a companion Telegram dump utility; APT35 maintains persistence for intelligence collection or monetizes access when systems lack strategic value, underscoring the need for timely patching, multi-factor authentication and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: An In-Depth Look at APT35 aka Charming Kitten

retrieved_context.text: ESET researchers uncovered the Iran-aligned APT35 (aka Ballistic Bobcat, Charming Kitten, TA453/PHOSPHORUS) deploying a novel Sponsor backdoor across at least 34 opportunistic victims—primarily Israeli organizations in sectors from automotive to telecommunications, plus medical targets in Brazil and the UAE—by scanning for and exploiting Exchange CVE-2021-26855 vulnerabilities since September 2021, wrapping up their CISA AA21-321A/PowerLess campaign before dropping Sponsor via innocuously named batch files that deploy configuration files (config.txt, node.txt) to disk, install a persistent Windows service (“SystemNetwork”/“Update”) when run with an “install” argument, then periodically RC4-decrypt and call back to embedded C2 relays, all while leveraging open-source tooling (Mimikatz, Chisel, GO Simple Tunnel, Plink, RevSocks and Merlin) for lateral movement and data exfiltration; ESET has catalogued five Sponsor versions through June 2022, underscoring Ballistic Bobcat’s modular, short-duration, narrowly targeted “Sponsoring Access” campaign and highlighting the need for Exchange patching, service and file monitoring for batch deployments, and detection of RC4-encrypted config lookups to disrupt ongoing espionage operations.
retrieved_context.title: Sponsor with batch-filed whiskers: Ballistic Bobcat’s scan and strike backdoor

hits.text: ESET’s updated analysis consolidates OilRig APT (aka APT34) under a parent-subgroup structure and attributes two exclusive Israeli-targeted campaigns—Outer Space (2021) and Juicy Mix (2022)—to its Lyceum subgroup, revealing a repeatable playbook in which spear-phishing VBS droppers employing arithmetic and base64 obfuscation deliver C#/.NET first-stage backdoors (Solar then its enhanced successor Mango) as scheduled Earth/Venus-style tasks that communicate via compromised Israeli websites using HTTP(S) URIs with “rt=d”/“rt=u” flags, XOR-based JupiterX encryption and Base64, and leverage the SC5k downloader (via Microsoft Exchange Web Services API) to fetch additional payloads. Post-compromise, Lyceum deployed MKG Chrome/Edge credential dumpers, Windows Credential Manager stealers and OilRig’s DanBot, Shark, Milan and Marlin backdoors to exfiltrate browser data and credentials. Code overlaps with Out to Sea, DNSpionage and HardPass campaigns—namely the MKG dumper, upload/download URI conventions, obfuscation techniques and downloader structures—solidify attribution to the Iran-linked group. Defenders should hunt for VBS scripts with obfuscation patterns, anomalous scheduled task creation (30/40-second or 14-minute intervals), EWS-based C&C traffic to non-public domains, Solar.exe/Mango.exe binaries and SC5k indicators to disrupt these data exfiltration pipelines.
hits.title: OilRig’s Outer Space and Juicy Mix: Same ol’ rig, new drill pipes

hits.title: Iranian Spies Target Saudi Arabia in "Magic Hound" Attacks

hits.text: Storm-842 (Void Manticore), an Iranian MOIS-linked APT also operating as Homeland Justice in Albania and Karma in Israel, first emerged in July 2022 by crippling Albania’s e-government and border systems ahead of an MEK conference—an attack detailed in a Sept. 2022 FBI/CISA advisory—and by December 2023 had extended its destructive campaigns to Israeli infrastructure; it executes a two-stage kill chain in partnership with Scarred Manticore (OilRig/APT34), which gains initial access via web shells (reGeorge, Karma Shell), RDP and SSH-based SOCKS C2 channels, credential harvesting and environment mapping, then hands off to Void Manticore to deploy custom Windows/Linux wipers (Cl Wiper using ElRawDisk, Partition Wiper, BiBi Wiper with .BiBi extension variants) that delete files, corrupt partitions, disable recovery mechanisms and erase shadow copies, all while concurrent influence operations leak stolen data under various personas to sow distrust—mitigation requires enforcing MFA and role-based access, rigorous patch and vulnerability management, network segmentation with IDS/IPS monitoring, phishing-resistant email/web filtering, offline backups with tested recovery drills and integration of real-time threat intelligence to detect and disrupt this sophisticated blend of destructive malware and psychological warfare.

hits.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
hits.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Researchers have identified SpectralBlur, a new Mach-O backdoor targeting macOS and attributed to North Korean group TA444 (aka BlueNoroff), which shares core functionality with the KANDYKORN/SockRacket implant—file upload/download, remote shell execution via grantpt-driven pseudo-terminal, configuration updates, file deletion, hibernation and sleep—and exhibits advanced evasion techniques; in recent months, TA444 has increasingly fused RustBucket droppers and late-stage ObjCShellz payloads from Lazarus campaigns to deploy KANDYKORN variants, underscoring a strategic shift toward macOS infiltration of high-value cryptocurrency and blockchain targets. The initial SpectralBlur sample, uploaded to VirusTotal from Colombia in August 2023, highlights possible multi-developer reuse of requirements, and follows a surge from 13 to 21 newly discovered macOS malware families in 2023—a trend likely to accelerate in 2024—prompting defenders to monitor anomalous pseudo-terminal invocations, atypical grantpt calls and cross-chain dropper activity for early detection.
hits.title: SpectralBlur: New macOS Backdoor Threat from North Korean Hackers

hits.text: Since mid-2016, a cyber espionage operation dubbed Magic Hound, attributed to Iranian government–linked actors including COBALT GYPSY and showing overlaps with Rocket Kitten (Operation Saffron Rose/Ajax Security Team/Operation Woolen-Goldfish) and Newscasters (Charming Kitten/NewsBeef), has targeted energy, government and technology organizations in and tied to Saudi Arabia by distributing Word and Excel documents embedding malicious macros that launch PowerShell downloaders and droppers to deploy a custom toolkit—comprising executable and document loaders, IRC bots and the multi-platform Python-based PupyRAT—for full system access and data exfiltration; analysis by Palo Alto Networks and SecureWorks revealed domain and tool reuse with the Shamoon 2 wiper campaign, and bait lures mimicking holiday greetings, job offers and official Ministry of Health and Commerce communications, underscoring the need for enhanced macro-enablement policies, network segmentation and proactive IOC monitoring of associated domains and IRC traffic.
hits.title: Iranian hackers behind the Magic Hound campaign linked to Shamoon

hits.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.
hits.title: Hackers with Russian Blizzard Steal Data from Rival Networks

hits.text: In 2024, ESET researchers uncovered a sustained cyberespionage campaign by the Iran-aligned APT group BladedFeline—active since at least 2017 against Kurdish Regional Government (KRG) and Iraqi government officials—that leverages an evolving toolset including the Shahmaran 64-bit backdoor, two reverse tunnels (Laret and Pinar), Whisper (an Exchange-based backdoor communicating via email attachments), a malicious IIS module dubbed PrimeCache bearing code similarities to OilRig’s RDAT backdoor, and supplementary implants such as the Flog webshell and Hawking Listener. Forensic analysis revealed early indicators on KRG systems—VideoSRV reverse shell (Sept 2017) and RDAT (Jan 2018)—consistent with OilRig’s operational patterns, leading to a medium-confidence assessment that BladedFeline operates as a subgroup of OilRig alongside Lyceum. The timeline spans initial KRG compromises in 2017–2018, Shahmaran deployment against diplomatic officials in early 2023, expansion to a telecommunications provider in Uzbekistan in March 2023, and the 2024 discovery of Whisper, Laret, Pinar, and PrimeCache across KRG, GOI, and Uzbek networks. BladedFeline’s tactics—native IIS module implantation, email-based C&C, reverse tunnels, and webshell exploitation—underscore the need to monitor Exchange mailbox activity for anomalous attachments, IIS module registrations (e.g., HttpModule.pdb), port listeners, and VirusTotal submitter IDs to detect and disrupt this persistent threat targeting strategic communications, oil-related infrastructure, and diplomatic data in the Middle East.
hits.title: BladedFeline: Whispering in the dark

hits.text: Symantec’s Threat Hunter Team has linked the newly discovered Sidewalk loader backdoor—an evolution of the Crosswalk/Backdoor.Motnug family—to Grayfly (aka GREF/Wicked Panda), a China-linked espionage group active since March 2017 that employs custom backdoors, Trojan.Chattak, Cobalt Strike, web shells and credential-dumpers against telecom, IT, media and finance targets in Taiwan, Vietnam, the US and Mexico; in a recent campaign they exploited public-facing Microsoft Exchange and MySQL servers via commodity and zero-day flaws to execute Base64-encoded PowerShell commands through certutil, install an ASPX web shell in the ClientAccess\ecp directory, deploy Sidewalk via installutil.exe, create persistence with WMIC-launched scheduled tasks, then run a custom Mimikatz variant (SHA256 b3eb783b017da32e33d19670b39eae0b11de8e983891dd4feb873d6e9333608d) to harvest credentials—all within about an hour before ceasing observable activity; three Chengdu 404 executives were indicted in 2020 for attacks on over 100 organizations, highlighting Grayfly’s persistence and underscoring the need to promptly patch Exchange and MySQL servers, monitor anomalous PowerShell and scheduled-task activity, and deploy IOC-based detection to block Sidewalk and related tools.
hits.title: Grayfly: Chinese Threat Actor Uses Newly-discovered Sidewalk Malware | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: US and UK agencies (CISA, FBI, CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA) issued a joint advisory detailing how the Iranian-backed MuddyWater group—active since at least 2017 and linked to Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security in January 2022—has expanded its arsenal beyond PowGoop, Canopy/Starwhale, Mori and POWERSTATS to include a new Python backdoor dubbed “Small Sieve” and a PowerShell backdoor that encrypts C2 channels; these tools target telecom, defense, local government and oil and gas organizations across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America, maintain persistence via custom string and traffic obfuscation (hex byte-swapping plus an obfuscated Base64 routine) over the Telegram Bot API via HTTPS, and facilitate lateral movement and data exfiltration, underscoring the need for defenders to monitor anomalous Telegram API calls, obfuscated Base64 traffic and encrypted PowerShell sessions.

hits.text: ESET’s updated analysis consolidates OilRig APT (aka APT34) under a parent-subgroup structure and attributes two exclusive Israeli-targeted campaigns—Outer Space (2021) and Juicy Mix (2022)—to its Lyceum subgroup, revealing a repeatable playbook in which spear-phishing VBS droppers employing arithmetic and base64 obfuscation deliver C#/.NET first-stage backdoors (Solar then its enhanced successor Mango) as scheduled Earth/Venus-style tasks that communicate via compromised Israeli websites using HTTP(S) URIs with “rt=d”/“rt=u” flags, XOR-based JupiterX encryption and Base64, and leverage the SC5k downloader (via Microsoft Exchange Web Services API) to fetch additional payloads. Post-compromise, Lyceum deployed MKG Chrome/Edge credential dumpers, Windows Credential Manager stealers and OilRig’s DanBot, Shark, Milan and Marlin backdoors to exfiltrate browser data and credentials. Code overlaps with Out to Sea, DNSpionage and HardPass campaigns—namely the MKG dumper, upload/download URI conventions, obfuscation techniques and downloader structures—solidify attribution to the Iran-linked group. Defenders should hunt for VBS scripts with obfuscation patterns, anomalous scheduled task creation (30/40-second or 14-minute intervals), EWS-based C&C traffic to non-public domains, Solar.exe/Mango.exe binaries and SC5k indicators to disrupt these data exfiltration pipelines.
hits.title: OilRig’s Outer Space and Juicy Mix: Same ol’ rig, new drill pipes

hits.text: Storm-842 (Void Manticore), an Iranian MOIS-linked APT also operating as Homeland Justice in Albania and Karma in Israel, first emerged in July 2022 by crippling Albania’s e-government and border systems ahead of an MEK conference—an attack detailed in a Sept. 2022 FBI/CISA advisory—and by December 2023 had extended its destructive campaigns to Israeli infrastructure; it executes a two-stage kill chain in partnership with Scarred Manticore (OilRig/APT34), which gains initial access via web shells (reGeorge, Karma Shell), RDP and SSH-based SOCKS C2 channels, credential harvesting and environment mapping, then hands off to Void Manticore to deploy custom Windows/Linux wipers (Cl Wiper using ElRawDisk, Partition Wiper, BiBi Wiper with .BiBi extension variants) that delete files, corrupt partitions, disable recovery mechanisms and erase shadow copies, all while concurrent influence operations leak stolen data under various personas to sow distrust—mitigation requires enforcing MFA and role-based access, rigorous patch and vulnerability management, network segmentation with IDS/IPS monitoring, phishing-resistant email/web filtering, offline backups with tested recovery drills and integration of real-time threat intelligence to detect and disrupt this sophisticated blend of destructive malware and psychological warfare.
hits.title: Dark Web Profile: Storm-842 (Void Manticore) - SOCRadar® Cyber Intelligence Inc.

hits.text: In 2024, ESET researchers uncovered a sustained cyberespionage campaign by the Iran-aligned APT group BladedFeline—active since at least 2017 against Kurdish Regional Government (KRG) and Iraqi government officials—that leverages an evolving toolset including the Shahmaran 64-bit backdoor, two reverse tunnels (Laret and Pinar), Whisper (an Exchange-based backdoor communicating via email attachments), a malicious IIS module dubbed PrimeCache bearing code similarities to OilRig’s RDAT backdoor, and supplementary implants such as the Flog webshell and Hawking Listener. Forensic analysis revealed early indicators on KRG systems—VideoSRV reverse shell (Sept 2017) and RDAT (Jan 2018)—consistent with OilRig’s operational patterns, leading to a medium-confidence assessment that BladedFeline operates as a subgroup of OilRig alongside Lyceum. The timeline spans initial KRG compromises in 2017–2018, Shahmaran deployment against diplomatic officials in early 2023, expansion to a telecommunications provider in Uzbekistan in March 2023, and the 2024 discovery of Whisper, Laret, Pinar, and PrimeCache across KRG, GOI, and Uzbek networks. BladedFeline’s tactics—native IIS module implantation, email-based C&C, reverse tunnels, and webshell exploitation—underscore the need to monitor Exchange mailbox activity for anomalous attachments, IIS module registrations (e.g., HttpModule.pdb), port listeners, and VirusTotal submitter IDs to detect and disrupt this persistent threat targeting strategic communications, oil-related infrastructure, and diplomatic data in the Middle East.

hits.text: ESET’s analysis of the Iranian APT “BladedFeline,” assessed with medium confidence as a subgroup of APT34/OilRig, reveals the actor infiltrated Kurdish and Iraqi government networks as early as September 2017 and remained undetected until 2023–2024, maintaining strategic espionage access to high-ranking officials tied to Western diplomatic relations and regional oil reserves. The group deployed a suite of proprietary and modified implants—most notably the simple, uncompressed 64-bit Shahmaran backdoor, the Whisper backdoor, the PrimeCache IIS module, the VideoSRV reverse shell, PowerShell executors and multiple reverse tunnels—via unknown initial vectors and a likely internet-facing web server exploit, using unencrypted C2 channels over normal traffic to execute commands, manipulate files and exfiltrate data. ESET identified code overlaps between PrimeCache and OilRig’s RDAT and common usage of VideoSRV, expects continued implant development, and advises defenders to maintain detailed inventories of VIP-used applications, establish network baselines to detect stealthy exfiltration paths and anomalies, and audit internet-facing servers to thwart initial compromise.
hits.title: Iranian APT 'BladedFeline' Hides in Network for 8 Years

hits.text: Since mid-2016, a cyber espionage operation dubbed Magic Hound, attributed to Iranian government–linked actors including COBALT GYPSY and showing overlaps with Rocket Kitten (Operation Saffron Rose/Ajax Security Team/Operation Woolen-Goldfish) and Newscasters (Charming Kitten/NewsBeef), has targeted energy, government and technology organizations in and tied to Saudi Arabia by distributing Word and Excel documents embedding malicious macros that launch PowerShell downloaders and droppers to deploy a custom toolkit—comprising executable and document loaders, IRC bots and the multi-platform Python-based PupyRAT—for full system access and data exfiltration; analysis by Palo Alto Networks and SecureWorks revealed domain and tool reuse with the Shamoon 2 wiper campaign, and bait lures mimicking holiday greetings, job offers and official Ministry of Health and Commerce communications, underscoring the need for enhanced macro-enablement policies, network segmentation and proactive IOC monitoring of associated domains and IRC traffic.
hits.title: Iranian hackers behind the Magic Hound campaign linked to Shamoon

hits.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
hits.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.

hits.text: Since September 2017, the Iran-aligned BladedFeline subcluster of the OilRig APT has executed persistent cyber espionage against Kurdish and Iraqi government entities, initially compromising KRG systems and a regional Uzbekistan telecom provider via an internet-facing application vulnerability and social engineering to deploy the Flog web shell. ESET’s Q4 2023–Q1 2024 report documents the group’s evolving malware arsenal: the Shahmaran backdoor for remote file manipulation, the C#/.NET Whisper (aka Veaty) email-based implant, the DNS-tunneling Spearal and its optimized variant, Optimizer, the Slippery Snakelet Python implant for command execution and data exfiltration, and tunneling tools Laret and Pinar. BladedFeline leverages a malicious IIS module, PrimeCache—akin to OilRig’s RDAT—and the Hawking Listener early-stage implant to maintain stealthy access, systematically harvesting diplomatic and financial intelligence tied to KRG oil reserves and Western relations to further Iranian strategic objectives.
hits.title: Iran-Linked BladedFeline Hits Iraqi and Kurdish Targets with Whisper and Spearal Malware

hits.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.

hits.text: Moses Staff, an Iran-linked APT active since September 2021, has conducted politically motivated sabotage campaigns—initially against Israeli organizations and later targets in India, Germany, the U.S., Italy, Chile, Turkey and the UAE—by exploiting known public-facing server vulnerabilities (e.g., Microsoft Exchange), moving laterally with PsExec, WMIC and PowerShell, and deploying a two-stage destructive toolkit: a Python-based loader (PyDCrypt) that installs a custom DiskCryptor variant (DCSrv) to encrypt files and disrupt operations without ransom demands, and, as newly documented by Cybereason, the StrifeWater RAT masquerading as calc.exe to establish early footholds, harvest system metadata (machine name, OS version, CPU architecture, user privileges, time zone), execute commands, capture screens, maintain persistence via scheduled tasks, and download auxiliary modules before self-removal—all while communicating with hard-coded C2 IPs, URLs and domain names—to evade detection; organizations should urgently patch exposed servers, monitor anomalous calc.exe and scheduled-task activity, and enhance EDR rules to detect PyDCrypt, DCSrv and StrifeWater behaviors to thwart data exfiltration and infrastructure damage.
hits.title: Iranian APT group uses previously undocumented Trojan for destructive access to organizations

hits.text: In August 2025 Microsoft Threat Intelligence revealed that Storm-2460, associated with the Play ransomware group, has resumed exploiting CVE-2025-29824—a zero-day elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Common Log File System patched in April—to gain SYSTEM privileges on unpatched hosts across IT, financial and real estate organizations in the US, Europe, South America and the Middle East. The campaign begins with an in-memory dropper masquerading as the open-source ChatGPT Desktop app that decrypts and launches PipeMagic, a modular backdoor first observed in December 2022 and now updated with persistence and lateral-movement enhancements targeting Saudi Arabian and Brazilian manufacturing entities. PipeMagic communicates with its TCP C2 over a named pipe, self-updates by storing distinct payload modules in memory via doubly linked lists for staging, execution and communication (plus an additional dynamic list), then leverages the CLFS exploit to escalate privileges before deploying Play ransomware. Although the campaign’s footprint remains limited, the combination of a zero-day exploit and a sophisticated modular backdoor underscores a heightened risk; organizations are urged to immediately apply the April patch for CVE-2025-29824, enable tamper and network protection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, run EDR in block mode, enforce full automated investigation and remediation, and leverage cloud-delivered machine-learning protections to block novel variants.
hits.title: PipeMagic Backdoor Resurfaces as Part of Play Ransomware Attack Chain

hits.text: Since September 2021 the politically motivated Moses Staff group has launched ransomless encryptions against Israeli organizations, exploiting unpatched public-facing infrastructure—most notably vulnerable Microsoft Exchange servers—and leveraging off-the-shelf exploits to breach networks, then moving laterally via PsExec, WMIC, and PowerShell without deploying custom backdoors. Upon infiltration, the group deploys PyDCrypt, a custom variant built atop the open-source DiskCryptor tool, which generates unique symmetric keys per hostname using an MD5 hash and salt; however, Check Point researchers note that failed self-deletion of PyDCrypt payloads allows key recovery and decryption under certain conditions. Rather than seeking financial gain, Moses Staff focuses on maximum operational disruption by exfiltrating corporate secrets and posting stolen data across a Tor leak site, Twitter, and Telegram channels—tactics reminiscent of Pay2Key and BlackShadow—and may originate from Palestine based on VirusTotal submissions. The attacks have caused widespread system downtime and data exposure, prompting Check Point to advise immediate patching of known vulnerabilities on public-facing servers, enhanced monitoring for lateral-movement utilities, and rapid retrieval of PyDCrypt samples to facilitate decryption.
hits.title: Moses Staff hackers wreak havoc on Israeli orgs with ransomless encryptions

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
hits.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

retrieved_context.text: Moses Staff, an Iran-linked APT active since September 2021, has conducted politically motivated sabotage campaigns—initially against Israeli organizations and later targets in India, Germany, the U.S., Italy, Chile, Turkey and the UAE—by exploiting known public-facing server vulnerabilities (e.g., Microsoft Exchange), moving laterally with PsExec, WMIC and PowerShell, and deploying a two-stage destructive toolkit: a Python-based loader (PyDCrypt) that installs a custom DiskCryptor variant (DCSrv) to encrypt files and disrupt operations without ransom demands, and, as newly documented by Cybereason, the StrifeWater RAT masquerading as calc.exe to establish early footholds, harvest system metadata (machine name, OS version, CPU architecture, user privileges, time zone), execute commands, capture screens, maintain persistence via scheduled tasks, and download auxiliary modules before self-removal—all while communicating with hard-coded C2 IPs, URLs and domain names—to evade detection; organizations should urgently patch exposed servers, monitor anomalous calc.exe and scheduled-task activity, and enhance EDR rules to detect PyDCrypt, DCSrv and StrifeWater behaviors to thwart data exfiltration and infrastructure damage.
retrieved_context.title: Iranian APT group uses previously undocumented Trojan for destructive access to organizations

retrieved_context.text: In August 2025 Microsoft Threat Intelligence revealed that Storm-2460, associated with the Play ransomware group, has resumed exploiting CVE-2025-29824—a zero-day elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Common Log File System patched in April—to gain SYSTEM privileges on unpatched hosts across IT, financial and real estate organizations in the US, Europe, South America and the Middle East. The campaign begins with an in-memory dropper masquerading as the open-source ChatGPT Desktop app that decrypts and launches PipeMagic, a modular backdoor first observed in December 2022 and now updated with persistence and lateral-movement enhancements targeting Saudi Arabian and Brazilian manufacturing entities. PipeMagic communicates with its TCP C2 over a named pipe, self-updates by storing distinct payload modules in memory via doubly linked lists for staging, execution and communication (plus an additional dynamic list), then leverages the CLFS exploit to escalate privileges before deploying Play ransomware. Although the campaign’s footprint remains limited, the combination of a zero-day exploit and a sophisticated modular backdoor underscores a heightened risk; organizations are urged to immediately apply the April patch for CVE-2025-29824, enable tamper and network protection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, run EDR in block mode, enforce full automated investigation and remediation, and leverage cloud-delivered machine-learning protections to block novel variants.
retrieved_context.title: PipeMagic Backdoor Resurfaces as Part of Play Ransomware Attack Chain

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

retrieved_context.text: Since September 2021 the politically motivated Moses Staff group has launched ransomless encryptions against Israeli organizations, exploiting unpatched public-facing infrastructure—most notably vulnerable Microsoft Exchange servers—and leveraging off-the-shelf exploits to breach networks, then moving laterally via PsExec, WMIC, and PowerShell without deploying custom backdoors. Upon infiltration, the group deploys PyDCrypt, a custom variant built atop the open-source DiskCryptor tool, which generates unique symmetric keys per hostname using an MD5 hash and salt; however, Check Point researchers note that failed self-deletion of PyDCrypt payloads allows key recovery and decryption under certain conditions. Rather than seeking financial gain, Moses Staff focuses on maximum operational disruption by exfiltrating corporate secrets and posting stolen data across a Tor leak site, Twitter, and Telegram channels—tactics reminiscent of Pay2Key and BlackShadow—and may originate from Palestine based on VirusTotal submissions. The attacks have caused widespread system downtime and data exposure, prompting Check Point to advise immediate patching of known vulnerabilities on public-facing servers, enhanced monitoring for lateral-movement utilities, and rapid retrieval of PyDCrypt samples to facilitate decryption.
retrieved_context.title: Moses Staff hackers wreak havoc on Israeli orgs with ransomless encryptions

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
retrieved_context.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

hits.text: Check Point Research has revealed that Void Manticore, an Iranian MOIS–affiliated threat actor operating under personas “Homeland Justice” for its 2022 Albania campaign and “Karma” for 2023–2024 Israel attacks, conducts coordinated espionage and destructive wiping operations by collaborating with Scarred Manticore (Storm-0861), which exploits CVE-2019-0604 via Foxshell and Liontail to dwell for over a year and exfiltrate emails (using LionHead), before handing victims to Void Manticore (Storm-0842) to deploy custom Windows and Linux wipers—CI Wiper, CL Wiper, partition-table LowEraser and the BiBi Wiper—thereby corrupting files and obliterating partition tables; the repetition of tactics across regions underscores a systematic, state-sponsored influence and destruction playbook and highlights the need for defenders to patch legacy SharePoint flaws, monitor for public-tool usage, implement immutable backups and share threat intelligence.
hits.title: Unveiling Void Manticore: Structured Collaboration Between Espionage and Destruction in MOIS - Check Point Blog

hits.text: Since mid-2016, a persistent espionage campaign dubbed Magic Hound has targeted Saudi energy, government and technology organizations using spear-phishing emails linking to weaponized Word and Excel documents with malicious macros that invoke PowerShell to download shellcode-based payloads via open-source modules like Magic Unicorn and deliver Metasploit’s Meterpreter, Pupy RAT and custom IRC bots. Infrastructure pivoting around “gerry knight” metadata and chrome-up[.]date domains revealed over fifty samples—including MagicHound.Rollover (document loader), Fetch (executable loader that writes c:\temp\rr.exe and creates autorun registry keys using an AES-encrypted “agkrhfpdbvhdhrkj” key), DropIt (base64 blob dropper/binder), Retriever (downloader) and Leash (IRC backdoor)—hosted on diverse VPS providers and overlapping with Rocket Kitten’s MPK bot IP. The campaign’s evolving multi-stage toolset, domain spoofing (ntg-sa[.]com, mol.com-ho[.]me) and obfs3-obfuscated communications underscore its sophistication and persistent intelligence impact.
hits.title: Magic Hound Campaign Attacks Saudi Targets

hits.text: ESET researchers have traced the China-aligned hacker group FishMonger, aka Aquatic Panda, and its global espionage campaign “FishMedley” back to the iSoon APT contractor (Axun Information Technology) operating under the Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security and PLA, following the U.S. DOJ’s addition of key members to the FBI’s Most Wanted list; FishMonger’s modus operandi relies on compromising high-privilege user accounts—likely harvested via phishing or credential theft—to gain domain administrator access, then deploying publicly available modular backdoors and loaders (ShadowPad, Spyder loader, SodaMaster) and the RPipeCommander reverse shell rather than zero-day exploits, enabling sustained infiltration of governmental bodies, Catholic charities, NGOs and think tanks across Taiwan, Hungary, Turkey, Thailand, the U.S. and France; while technically unsophisticated, the group’s efficient use of known tools has yielded consistent exfiltration of confidential data, underscoring the need for potential targets to hunt for these specific indicators of compromise and strengthen monitoring of privileged accounts.
hits.title: Chinese Hacker Group Tracked Back to iSoon APT Operation

retrieved_context.text: Storm-842 (Void Manticore), an Iranian MOIS-linked APT also operating as Homeland Justice in Albania and Karma in Israel, first emerged in July 2022 by crippling Albania’s e-government and border systems ahead of an MEK conference—an attack detailed in a Sept. 2022 FBI/CISA advisory—and by December 2023 had extended its destructive campaigns to Israeli infrastructure; it executes a two-stage kill chain in partnership with Scarred Manticore (OilRig/APT34), which gains initial access via web shells (reGeorge, Karma Shell), RDP and SSH-based SOCKS C2 channels, credential harvesting and environment mapping, then hands off to Void Manticore to deploy custom Windows/Linux wipers (Cl Wiper using ElRawDisk, Partition Wiper, BiBi Wiper with .BiBi extension variants) that delete files, corrupt partitions, disable recovery mechanisms and erase shadow copies, all while concurrent influence operations leak stolen data under various personas to sow distrust—mitigation requires enforcing MFA and role-based access, rigorous patch and vulnerability management, network segmentation with IDS/IPS monitoring, phishing-resistant email/web filtering, offline backups with tested recovery drills and integration of real-time threat intelligence to detect and disrupt this sophisticated blend of destructive malware and psychological warfare.
retrieved_context.title: Dark Web Profile: Storm-842 (Void Manticore) - SOCRadar® Cyber Intelligence Inc.

retrieved_context.text: Check Point Research has revealed that Void Manticore, an Iranian MOIS–affiliated threat actor operating under personas “Homeland Justice” for its 2022 Albania campaign and “Karma” for 2023–2024 Israel attacks, conducts coordinated espionage and destructive wiping operations by collaborating with Scarred Manticore (Storm-0861), which exploits CVE-2019-0604 via Foxshell and Liontail to dwell for over a year and exfiltrate emails (using LionHead), before handing victims to Void Manticore (Storm-0842) to deploy custom Windows and Linux wipers—CI Wiper, CL Wiper, partition-table LowEraser and the BiBi Wiper—thereby corrupting files and obliterating partition tables; the repetition of tactics across regions underscores a systematic, state-sponsored influence and destruction playbook and highlights the need for defenders to patch legacy SharePoint flaws, monitor for public-tool usage, implement immutable backups and share threat intelligence.

retrieved_context.text: Since mid-2016, a persistent espionage campaign dubbed Magic Hound has targeted Saudi energy, government and technology organizations using spear-phishing emails linking to weaponized Word and Excel documents with malicious macros that invoke PowerShell to download shellcode-based payloads via open-source modules like Magic Unicorn and deliver Metasploit’s Meterpreter, Pupy RAT and custom IRC bots. Infrastructure pivoting around “gerry knight” metadata and chrome-up[.]date domains revealed over fifty samples—including MagicHound.Rollover (document loader), Fetch (executable loader that writes c:\temp\rr.exe and creates autorun registry keys using an AES-encrypted “agkrhfpdbvhdhrkj” key), DropIt (base64 blob dropper/binder), Retriever (downloader) and Leash (IRC backdoor)—hosted on diverse VPS providers and overlapping with Rocket Kitten’s MPK bot IP. The campaign’s evolving multi-stage toolset, domain spoofing (ntg-sa[.]com, mol.com-ho[.]me) and obfs3-obfuscated communications underscore its sophistication and persistent intelligence impact.
retrieved_context.title: Magic Hound Campaign Attacks Saudi Targets

retrieved_context.text: ESET researchers have traced the China-aligned hacker group FishMonger, aka Aquatic Panda, and its global espionage campaign “FishMedley” back to the iSoon APT contractor (Axun Information Technology) operating under the Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security and PLA, following the U.S. DOJ’s addition of key members to the FBI’s Most Wanted list; FishMonger’s modus operandi relies on compromising high-privilege user accounts—likely harvested via phishing or credential theft—to gain domain administrator access, then deploying publicly available modular backdoors and loaders (ShadowPad, Spyder loader, SodaMaster) and the RPipeCommander reverse shell rather than zero-day exploits, enabling sustained infiltration of governmental bodies, Catholic charities, NGOs and think tanks across Taiwan, Hungary, Turkey, Thailand, the U.S. and France; while technically unsophisticated, the group’s efficient use of known tools has yielded consistent exfiltration of confidential data, underscoring the need for potential targets to hunt for these specific indicators of compromise and strengthen monitoring of privileged accounts.
retrieved_context.title: Chinese Hacker Group Tracked Back to iSoon APT Operation

hits.text: Moses Staff, an Iran-linked APT active since September 2021, has conducted politically motivated sabotage campaigns—initially against Israeli organizations and later targets in India, Germany, the U.S., Italy, Chile, Turkey and the UAE—by exploiting known public-facing server vulnerabilities (e.g., Microsoft Exchange), moving laterally with PsExec, WMIC and PowerShell, and deploying a two-stage destructive toolkit: a Python-based loader (PyDCrypt) that installs a custom DiskCryptor variant (DCSrv) to encrypt files and disrupt operations without ransom demands, and, as newly documented by Cybereason, the StrifeWater RAT masquerading as calc.exe to establish early footholds, harvest system metadata (machine name, OS version, CPU architecture, user privileges, time zone), execute commands, capture screens, maintain persistence via scheduled tasks, and download auxiliary modules before self-removal—all while communicating with hard-coded C2 IPs, URLs and domain names—to evade detection; organizations should urgently patch exposed servers, monitor anomalous calc.exe and scheduled-task activity, and enhance EDR rules to detect PyDCrypt, DCSrv and StrifeWater behaviors to thwart data exfiltration and infrastructure damage.
hits.title: Iranian APT group uses previously undocumented Trojan for destructive access to organizations

hits.text: Since September 2021 the politically motivated Moses Staff group has launched ransomless encryptions against Israeli organizations, exploiting unpatched public-facing infrastructure—most notably vulnerable Microsoft Exchange servers—and leveraging off-the-shelf exploits to breach networks, then moving laterally via PsExec, WMIC, and PowerShell without deploying custom backdoors. Upon infiltration, the group deploys PyDCrypt, a custom variant built atop the open-source DiskCryptor tool, which generates unique symmetric keys per hostname using an MD5 hash and salt; however, Check Point researchers note that failed self-deletion of PyDCrypt payloads allows key recovery and decryption under certain conditions. Rather than seeking financial gain, Moses Staff focuses on maximum operational disruption by exfiltrating corporate secrets and posting stolen data across a Tor leak site, Twitter, and Telegram channels—tactics reminiscent of Pay2Key and BlackShadow—and may originate from Palestine based on VirusTotal submissions. The attacks have caused widespread system downtime and data exposure, prompting Check Point to advise immediate patching of known vulnerabilities on public-facing servers, enhanced monitoring for lateral-movement utilities, and rapid retrieval of PyDCrypt samples to facilitate decryption.
hits.title: Moses Staff hackers wreak havoc on Israeli orgs with ransomless encryptions

PipeMagic communicates with its TCP C2 over a named pipe, self-updates by storing distinct payload modules in memory via doubly linked lists for staging, execution and communication (plus an additional dynamic list), then leverages the CLFS exploit to escalate privileges before deploying Play ransomware. Although the campaign’s footprint remains limited, the combination of a zero-day exploit and a sophisticated modular backdoor underscores a heightened risk; organizations are urged to immediately apply the April patch for CVE-2025-29824, enable tamper and network protection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, run EDR in block mode, enforce full automated investigation and remediation, and leverage cloud-delivered machine-learning protections to block novel variants.

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

hits.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.
hits.title: Follina Exploited by State-Sponsored Hackers | Threatpost

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
hits.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

hits.text: Since at least 2021, the Chinese state-linked APT group Salt Typhoon—supported by Sichuan Juxinhe Network Technology Co. Ltd., Beijing Huanyu Tianqiong Information Technology Co., and Sichuan Zhixin Ruijie Network Technology Co. Ltd., which supply cyber products and services to China’s Ministry of State Security and PLA—has conducted global cyber-espionage against government, telecommunications, transportation, lodging and military networks, notably breaching U.S. carriers (AT&T, Verizon, Lumen) to exfiltrate text messages, voicemails and law-enforcement wiretaps, infiltrating U.S. and Canadian telcos via unpatched Cisco IOS XE vulnerabilities to establish GRE tunnels and steal configurations, and executing a nine-month 2024 compromise of a U.S. Army National Guard network to harvest admin credentials and config files. Their primary tactic exploits widely known, fixed edge-device flaws—CVE-2024-21887 (Ivanti Connect Secure command injection), CVE-2024-3400 (Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect RCE), CVE-2023-20273 & CVE-2023-20198 (Cisco IOS XE auth bypass/privilege escalation) and CVE-2018-0171 (Cisco Smart Install RCE)—to gain router access, modify ACLs, enable SSH on nonstandard ports, deploy GRE/IPsec tunnels, abuse Cisco Guest Shell for persistence, capture TACACS+ traffic, and deploy custom Golang SFTP tools (“cmd1,” “cmd3,” “new2,” “sft”). A 13-nation advisory warns that compromised edge devices and trusted provider interconnects facilitate lateral movement into core targets. Recommended mitigations include urgent patching, device hardening, configuration monitoring, disabling unused services (Cisco Smart Install/Guest Shell), restricting management interfaces to secure networks, enforcing SSHv2/SNMPv3 and proactively hunting for known-vulnerability exploitation to thwart further espionage.
hits.title: Global Salt Typhoon hacking campaigns linked to Chinese tech firms

hits.text: Symantec’s Threat Hunter Team has linked the newly discovered Sidewalk loader backdoor—an evolution of the Crosswalk/Backdoor.Motnug family—to Grayfly (aka GREF/Wicked Panda), a China-linked espionage group active since March 2017 that employs custom backdoors, Trojan.Chattak, Cobalt Strike, web shells and credential-dumpers against telecom, IT, media and finance targets in Taiwan, Vietnam, the US and Mexico; in a recent campaign they exploited public-facing Microsoft Exchange and MySQL servers via commodity and zero-day flaws to execute Base64-encoded PowerShell commands through certutil, install an ASPX web shell in the ClientAccess\ecp directory, deploy Sidewalk via installutil.exe, create persistence with WMIC-launched scheduled tasks, then run a custom Mimikatz variant (SHA256 b3eb783b017da32e33d19670b39eae0b11de8e983891dd4feb873d6e9333608d) to harvest credentials—all within about an hour before ceasing observable activity; three Chengdu 404 executives were indicted in 2020 for attacks on over 100 organizations, highlighting Grayfly’s persistence and underscoring the need to promptly patch Exchange and MySQL servers, monitor anomalous PowerShell and scheduled-task activity, and deploy IOC-based detection to block Sidewalk and related tools.
hits.title: Grayfly: Chinese Threat Actor Uses Newly-discovered Sidewalk Malware | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
hits.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates
hits.text: Unit 42 has observed a sharp rise in post-intrusion WastedLocker ransomware attacks by the Evil Corp group—already known for Dridex—against large U.S. organizations in sectors from manufacturing to legal services, with initial compromise typically via ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates that deploy a SocGholish JavaScript loader to profile systems and invoke PowerShell-based Cobalt Strike payloads; attackers then leverage WMI and PsExec for lateral movement, identify high-value and backup systems, elevate privileges, disable Windows Defender, delete shadow copies, install WastedLocker as a service, and encrypt files using a “.<victim_name>wasted” extension while appending ransom notes (“.<victim_name>wasted_info”) with contact addresses on ProtonMail, Airmail and others. Palo Alto Networks’ WildFire, Cortex XDR (anti-ransomware and behavioral threat protection), NGFW DNS signatures and AutoFocus tagging detect and prevent WastedLocker activity; organizations are urged to implement robust, off-site backup strategies and hardened cybersecurity controls to mitigate this high-impact targeted ransomware threat.
hits.title: Threat Assessment: WastedLocker Ransomware

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia
hits.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.

hits.text: In early April, Palo Alto Networks’ Advanced WildFire and Cortex XDR uncovered SnipBot—a new v5.0 iteration of the RomCom RAT family—employing advanced window message–based control-flow obfuscation and anti-sandbox checks (filename hash and HKCU\…\RecentDocs entries) in a multi-stage chain beginning with a PDF-labeled EXE downloader signed using a likely stolen certificate; the downloader contacts xeontime[.]com for config-pdf.dll, which uses registry-based COM hijacking to load keyprov.dll from drvmcprotect[.]com into explorer.exe, decrypts payloads stored in HKCU\Software\AppDataSoft\Software, and opens a TCP listener on port 1342 for commands to update, delete, or execute modules. The main backdoor single.dll (mutex “SnipMutex”) supports 27 encrypted commands for drive and process enumeration, file upload/download, and remote module execution, facilitating network pivoting and targeted file exfiltration. Active since December 2023 (RomCom activity since 2022), SnipBot’s tactics, stolen certificates, unique obfuscation, and sophisticated loader underscore a high-risk threat actor likely focused on intelligence gathering; Palo Alto products classify its samples, URLs, and domains as malicious to prevent compromise.
hits.title: Inside SnipBot: The Latest RomCom Malware Variant

hits.text: Security researcher Marc Newlin of SkySafe disclosed CVE-2023-45866, a critical, decade-old keystroke-injection flaw in the Bluetooth host state-machine that exploits an unauthenticated pairing mechanism in the Bluetooth specification to trick macOS (13.3.3), iOS (16.6, even in Lockdown Mode), Android (from 4.2.2 through 14 on devices including Pixel 7/6/4a, Pixel 2, Nexus 5, BLU DASH), and Linux BlueZ stacks (Ubuntu 18.04–23.10) into pairing with a malicious emulated keyboard, enabling remote attackers within Bluetooth range to run a Python-based script, inject arbitrary keystrokes, install apps, forward emails or texts, and execute commands without user confirmation or biometric/password authentication. After informing Apple, Google, Canonical, and the Bluetooth SIG between August and September, patches have been released for Android 11–14 and BlueZ (via GitHub) but Apple has yet to announce a timeline for CVE-2023-42929, proof-of-concept exploit scripts will be published in January, and no active in-the-wild exploitation has been observed to date.
hits.title: Critical Bluetooth Flaw Exposes Android, Apple & Linux Devices to Takeover

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs
