canonical_entities: Sichuan Juxinhe Network Technology Co. Ltd.
Beijing Huanyu Tianqiong Information Technology Co.
Sichuan Zhixin Ruijie Network Technology Co. Ltd.
retrieved_context.text: Since at least 2021, the Chinese state-linked APT group Salt Typhoon—supported by Sichuan Juxinhe Network Technology Co. Ltd., Beijing Huanyu Tianqiong Information Technology Co., and Sichuan Zhixin Ruijie Network Technology Co. Ltd., which supply cyber products and services to China’s Ministry of State Security and PLA—has conducted global cyber-espionage against government, telecommunications, transportation, lodging and military networks, notably breaching U.S. carriers (AT&T, Verizon, Lumen) to exfiltrate text messages, voicemails and law-enforcement wiretaps, infiltrating U.S. and Canadian telcos via unpatched Cisco IOS XE vulnerabilities to establish GRE tunnels and steal configurations, and executing a nine-month 2024 compromise of a U.S. Army National Guard network to harvest admin credentials and config files. Their primary tactic exploits widely known, fixed edge-device flaws—CVE-2024-21887 (Ivanti Connect Secure command injection), CVE-2024-3400 (Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect RCE), CVE-2023-20273 & CVE-2023-20198 (Cisco IOS XE auth bypass/privilege escalation) and CVE-2018-0171 (Cisco Smart Install RCE)—to gain router access, modify ACLs, enable SSH on nonstandard ports, deploy GRE/IPsec tunnels, abuse Cisco Guest Shell for persistence, capture TACACS+ traffic, and deploy custom Golang SFTP tools (“cmd1,” “cmd3,” “new2,” “sft”). A 13-nation advisory warns that compromised edge devices and trusted provider interconnects facilitate lateral movement into core targets. Recommended mitigations include urgent patching, device hardening, configuration monitoring, disabling unused services (Cisco Smart Install/Guest Shell), restricting management interfaces to secure networks, enforcing SSHv2/SNMPv3 and proactively hunting for known-vulnerability exploitation to thwart further espionage.
retrieved_context.title: Global Salt Typhoon hacking campaigns linked to Chinese tech firms

retrieved_context.text: Symantec’s Threat Hunter Team has linked the newly discovered Sidewalk loader backdoor—an evolution of the Crosswalk/Backdoor.Motnug family—to Grayfly (aka GREF/Wicked Panda), a China-linked espionage group active since March 2017 that employs custom backdoors, Trojan.Chattak, Cobalt Strike, web shells and credential-dumpers against telecom, IT, media and finance targets in Taiwan, Vietnam, the US and Mexico; in a recent campaign they exploited public-facing Microsoft Exchange and MySQL servers via commodity and zero-day flaws to execute Base64-encoded PowerShell commands through certutil, install an ASPX web shell in the ClientAccess\ecp directory, deploy Sidewalk via installutil.exe, create persistence with WMIC-launched scheduled tasks, then run a custom Mimikatz variant (SHA256 b3eb783b017da32e33d19670b39eae0b11de8e983891dd4feb873d6e9333608d) to harvest credentials—all within about an hour before ceasing observable activity; three Chengdu 404 executives were indicted in 2020 for attacks on over 100 organizations, highlighting Grayfly’s persistence and underscoring the need to promptly patch Exchange and MySQL servers, monitor anomalous PowerShell and scheduled-task activity, and deploy IOC-based detection to block Sidewalk and related tools.
retrieved_context.title: Grayfly: Chinese Threat Actor Uses Newly-discovered Sidewalk Malware | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: harvest subscriber location, billing and communications metadata
hits.text: On Sept. 25, 2024, the Wall Street Journal disclosed that the Chinese state-sponsored APT Salt Typhoon has stealthily infiltrated multiple U.S. cable and broadband ISPs—likely via firmware and supply-chain compromises in core networking gear—to establish long-term persistence, harvest subscriber location, billing and communications metadata for espionage, and pre-position disruptive capabilities against federal, military and Fortune 100 users; this campaign, echoing Volt Typhoon’s telecom backdoors, Flax Typhoon’s 200,000-device IoT botnet, Brass Typhoon’s cross-domain implants and Mustang Panda’s telco intrusions, signals a shift from surveillance to offensive “blink-the-lights” or infrastructure-crippling attacks in a Taiwan contingency, driving urgent recommendations for carriers to enforce threat-intelligence sharing, secure firmware, tighten supply-chain controls and bolster routing security.
hits.title: China's 'Salt Typhoon' Cooks Up Cyberattacks on US ISPs

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

hits.text: Microsoft has identified a China-based nation-state threat actor tracked as Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda) conducting espionage against dozens of Taiwanese organizations since mid-2021 by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java and SQL servers to deploy the China Chopper web shell, escalate privileges with Juicy Potato and BadPotato, and establish persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN bridge over HTTPS on port 443 for stealthy command-and-control. Once inside, the actor leverages WinRM and WMIC for lateral movement and deploys Mimikatz to dump LSASS and SAM for pass-the-hash attacks, yet conducts minimal post-persistence activity, suggesting long-term credential harvesting rather than immediate data exfiltration. To mitigate, organizations must enforce rigorous patch management, monitor registry changes and RDP configurations, deploy file integrity and behavioral monitoring on public-facing servers, isolate and forensically examine compromised systems, and rotate or disable exposed credentials.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
hits.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

canonical_entities: multi-year espionage campaign uncovered by Mandiant
hits.text: In a multi-year espionage campaign uncovered by Mandiant, the Chinese UNC3886 group exploited a critical VMware vCenter Server zero-day (CVE-2023-34048) from late 2021 until its October 2023 patch, triggering vmdird service crashes and removing core dumps to stealthily gain privileged access, then delivering VirtualPita and VirtualPie backdoors via malicious vSphere Installation Bundles on ESXi hosts; they subsequently chained the VMware Tools authentication bypass flaw (CVE-2023-20867) to escalate privileges, harvest and exfiltrate files from guest VMs. UNC3886—targeting defense, government, telecom and technology sectors in the US and APJ—also abused a Fortinet firewall zero-day (CVE-2022-41328) to deploy Castletap and Thincrust implants, demonstrating advanced reverse-engineering of FortiOS. retrieved_context.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has identified a China-based nation-state threat actor tracked as Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda) conducting espionage against dozens of Taiwanese organizations since mid-2021 by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java and SQL servers to deploy the China Chopper web shell, escalate privileges with Juicy Potato and BadPotato, and establish persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN bridge over HTTPS on port 443 for stealthy command-and-control. Once inside, the actor leverages WinRM and WMIC for lateral movement and deploys Mimikatz to dump LSASS and SAM for pass-the-hash attacks, yet conducts minimal post-persistence activity, suggesting long-term credential harvesting rather than immediate data exfiltration. To mitigate, organizations must enforce rigorous patch management, monitor registry changes and RDP configurations, deploy file integrity and behavioral monitoring on public-facing servers, isolate and forensically examine compromised systems, and rotate or disable exposed credentials.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
retrieved_context.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
retrieved_context.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

retrieved_context.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.

hits.text: Water Ouroboros is a Ransomware-as-a-Service operation that exploits public-facing Oracle WebLogic vulnerabilities (CVE-2019-2725, CVE-2017-10271, CVE-2019-2729) or drive-by installers for initial access (T1190, T1189), then executes remote Windows commands (wmic.exe, bcdedit.exe, wbadmin.exe, vssadmin.exe) to delete backups and disable recovery (T1490, T1562.001) before encrypting fixed, removable and network drives via a Go-based custom routine that uses RTLGenRandom to generate a symmetric key, protects it with embedded RSA public keys (App_ExportKey), appends “.locked” (unless suppressed with –E), excludes over 60 file extensions, and accepts credentials (c {user}:{pass}), logging (–a), non-aggressive (–A) and size filters (–m). Victims find Contact Us.txt ransom notes pointing to a TOR payment site and Hive Leaks data-dump threat. Post-infection, actors maintain access via compromised admin accounts (T1078), disable security tools (PCHunter, ProcessHacker), dump credentials from registry hives (T1003.002), move laterally over RDP/SMB (T1021.001/002), discover assets via AdFind (T1595.002) and exfiltrate data over C&C (SharpRhino RAT/T1071.001, T1041). With 136 incidents in the US and notable impacts on construction, IT, manufacturing and healthcare SMBs, the campaign underscores the need for timely patching, hardened public-facing apps, least-privilege access, MFA, robust backups and advanced threat detection.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Water Ouroboros | Trend Micro (US)

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.

retrieved_context.text: In early April, Palo Alto Networks’ Advanced WildFire and Cortex XDR uncovered SnipBot—a new v5.0 iteration of the RomCom RAT family—employing advanced window message–based control-flow obfuscation and anti-sandbox checks (filename hash and HKCU\…\RecentDocs entries) in a multi-stage chain beginning with a PDF-labeled EXE downloader signed using a likely stolen certificate; the downloader contacts xeontime[.]com for config-pdf.dll, which uses registry-based COM hijacking to load keyprov.dll from drvmcprotect[.]com into explorer.exe, decrypts payloads stored in HKCU\Software\AppDataSoft\Software, and opens a TCP listener on port 1342 for commands to update, delete, or execute modules. The main backdoor single.dll (mutex “SnipMutex”) supports 27 encrypted commands for drive and process enumeration, file upload/download, and remote module execution, facilitating network pivoting and targeted file exfiltration. Active since December 2023 (RomCom activity since 2022), SnipBot’s tactics, stolen certificates, unique obfuscation, and sophisticated loader underscore a high-risk threat actor likely focused on intelligence gathering; Palo Alto products classify its samples, URLs, and domains as malicious to prevent compromise.
retrieved_context.title: Inside SnipBot: The Latest RomCom Malware Variant

canonical_entities: multi-year espionage campaign uncovered by Mandiant
retrieved_context.text: In a multi-year espionage campaign uncovered by Mandiant, the Chinese UNC3886 group exploited a critical VMware vCenter Server zero-day (CVE-2023-34048) from late 2021 until its October 2023 patch, triggering vmdird service crashes and removing core dumps to stealthily gain privileged access, then delivering VirtualPita and VirtualPie backdoors via malicious vSphere Installation Bundles on ESXi hosts; they subsequently chained the VMware Tools authentication bypass flaw (CVE-2023-20867) to escalate privileges, harvest and exfiltrate files from guest VMs. UNC3886—targeting defense, government, telecom and technology sectors in the US and APJ—also abused a Fortinet firewall zero-day (CVE-2022-41328) to deploy Castletap and Thincrust implants, demonstrating advanced reverse-engineering of FortiOS. This campaign highlights the urgent need for rapid patching of virtualization and firewall platforms, deployment of EDR solutions and preservation of forensic artifacts to detect and thwart such sophisticated attacks.
retrieved_context.title: Chinese hackers exploit VMware bug as zero-day for two years

canonical_entities: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager
retrieved_context.text: Water Ouroboros is a Ransomware-as-a-Service operation that exploits public-facing Oracle WebLogic vulnerabilities (CVE-2019-2725, CVE-2017-10271, CVE-2019-2729) or drive-by installers for initial access (T1190, T1189), then executes remote Windows commands (wmic.exe, bcdedit.exe, wbadmin.exe, vssadmin.exe) to delete backups and disable recovery (T1490, T1562.001) before encrypting fixed, removable and network drives via a Go-based custom routine that uses RTLGenRandom to generate a symmetric key, protects it with embedded RSA public keys (App_ExportKey), appends “.locked” (unless suppressed with –E), excludes over 60 file extensions, and accepts credentials (c {user}:{pass}), logging (–a), non-aggressive (–A) and size filters (–m). Victims find Contact Us.txt ransom notes pointing to a TOR payment site and Hive Leaks data-dump threat. Post-infection, actors maintain access via compromised admin accounts (T1078), disable security tools (PCHunter, ProcessHacker), dump credentials from registry hives (T1003.002), move laterally over RDP/SMB (T1021.001/002), discover assets via AdFind (T1595.002) and exfiltrate data over C&C (SharpRhino RAT/T1071.001, T1041). With 136 incidents in the US and notable impacts on construction, IT, manufacturing and healthcare SMBs, the campaign underscores the need for timely patching, hardened public-facing apps, least-privilege access, MFA, robust backups and advanced threat detection.
retrieved_context.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Water Ouroboros | Trend Micro (US)

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Between July and October 2021, Iranian state-sponsored group Lyceum (aka Hexane, Spirlin) conducted targeted intrusions against ISPs and telecom operators in Israel, Morocco, Tunisia, and Saudi Arabia, plus an African ministry of foreign affairs, using credential stuffing and brute-force attacks for initial access before deploying malware implants Shark and Milan to execute arbitrary commands and exfiltrate data; researchers from Accenture Cyber Threat Intelligence and Prevailion's Adversarial Counterintelligence Team identified over 20 web-based infrastructure components enabling victim identification, with at least two compromises assessed as ongoing despite prior public disclosure of indicators of compromise, and beaconing from reconfigured or new Lyceum backdoors detected in late October 2021 from Tunisian telecom and African MFA victims indicating active modifications to evade security detection.
hits.title: Iran's Lyceum Hackers Target Telecoms, ISPs in Israel, Saudi Arabia, and Africa

hits.text: The North Korea-linked threat actor Slow Pisces (also tracked as Jade Sleet, PUKCHONG, TraderTraitor, and UNC4899) has been conducting a multi-stage malware campaign targeting cryptocurrency developers via LinkedIn job opportunity lures since at least June 2024, leveraging trojanized Python and JavaScript projects hosted on GitHub that employ YAML deserialization and EJS templating to execute gated payloads only to validated targets meeting specific criteria (IP address, geolocation, time, HTTP headers); the campaign delivers RN Loader and RN Stealer malware on macOS systems capable of harvesting system metadata, installed applications, SSH keys, AWS/Kubernetes/Google Cloud configuration files, and iCloud Keychain data, with payloads remaining memory-resident and deployed selectively to prevent analysis; Slow Pisces is assessed to be responsible for the February 2025 Bybit cryptocurrency exchange breach and operates alongside other North Korean clusters including Operation Dream Job, Contagious Interview, Alluring Pisces, and Moonstone Sleet, though with notably superior operational security practices involving heavily guarded payload delivery across infection stages.
hits.title: Crypto Developers Targeted by Python Malware Disguised as Coding Challenges

hits.text: In August 2025 Microsoft Threat Intelligence revealed that Storm-2460, associated with the Play ransomware group, has resumed exploiting CVE-2025-29824—a zero-day elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Common Log File System patched in April—to gain SYSTEM privileges on unpatched hosts across IT, financial and real estate organizations in the US, Europe, South America and the Middle East. The campaign begins with an in-memory dropper masquerading as the open-source ChatGPT Desktop app that decrypts and launches PipeMagic, a modular backdoor first observed in December 2022 and now updated with persistence and lateral-movement enhancements targeting Saudi Arabian and Brazilian manufacturing entities. PipeMagic communicates with its TCP C2 over a named pipe, self-updates by storing distinct payload modules in memory via doubly linked lists for staging, execution and communication (plus an additional dynamic list), then leverages the CLFS exploit to escalate privileges before deploying Play ransomware. Although the campaign’s footprint remains limited, the combination of a zero-day exploit and a sophisticated modular backdoor underscores a heightened risk; organizations are urged to immediately apply the April patch for CVE-2025-29824, enable tamper and network protection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, run EDR in block mode, enforce full automated investigation and remediation, and leverage cloud-delivered machine-learning protections to block novel variants.
hits.title: PipeMagic Backdoor Resurfaces as Part of Play Ransomware Attack Chain

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: Since January 2021, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has tracked a government-backed North Korean campaign that leverages social engineering via X (formerly Twitter) and encrypted messaging apps to befriend security researchers and deliver malicious files containing at least one unpatched 0-day in a popular software package; upon exploitation the custom shellcode performs anti-virtual-machine checks, captures system data and screenshots, and exfiltrates them to C2 infrastructure (e.g., 23.106.215[.]105, www.blgbeach[.]com), with the latest vulnerability reported and patched on September 12, 2023 (see TAG’s published RCA). In parallel, the actors published a seemingly benign Windows tool called GetSymbol on GitHub (https://github.com/dbgsymbol/) that quietly downloads debugging symbols—and arbitrary code—from attacker domains, requiring full OS reinstalls for compromised hosts. TAG has added malicious sites to Safe Browsing, issued government-backed attacker alerts to targeted Gmail and Workspace users, and urges researchers to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, keep software up to date, and verify system integrity after using third-party tools.
hits.title: Active North Korean campaign targeting security researchers

hits.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
hits.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

hits.text: Unit 42’s investigation reveals that North Korean state‐sponsored group Jumpy Pisces (aka Andariel/Onyx Sleet) gained initial access to a corporate network in May 2024 via a compromised user account, deployed a customized Sliver C2 beaconing to 172.96.137[.]224/americajobmail[.]site and their bespoke DTrack infostealer across hosts via SMB, and leveraged Impacket’s secretsdump.py, Mimikatz dumps (KB0722.log), a custom RDP account tool and a trojanized browser‐data stealer for credential harvesting, lateral movement and persistence; this activity continued until early September when the same account and toolset were abused—using TokenPlayer for Windows token abuse, PsExec for privilege escalation and EDR sensor removal—to facilitate Play ransomware (Fiddling Scorpius) deployment, marking the first observed collaboration (affiliate or initial access brokerage) between Jumpy Pisces and Play ransomware and signaling a shift from espionage to broader ransomware operations that could target victims globally, underscoring the imperative for defenders to treat Jumpy Pisces activity as a precursory ransomware threat and to deploy mitigations such as Cortex XDR, Advanced WildFire, Advanced URL Filtering and Advanced DNS Security.
hits.title: Jumpy Pisces Engages in Play Ransomware

hits.text: North Korean APT Lazarus has launched “Operation In(ter)ception,” a macOS-focused cyberespionage campaign that lures engineering professionals with a fake Coinbase job posting and deploys a signed universal macOS executable (Intel and Apple Silicon) that drops three components—a decoy PDF (Coinbase_online_careers_2022_07.pdf), a FinderFontsUpdater.app bundle and a downloader named safarifontagent—before phoning home to a new, currently nonresponsive C2 at concrecapital[.]com/%user%.jpg. Identified by ESET in late July and using a February-2022 developer certificate for “Shankey Nohria” revoked by Apple on August 12, the malware mirrors a May sample but introduces fresh C2 infrastructure and was first uploaded from Brazil. A companion Windows variant, spotted by Malwarebytes on August 4, follows the same decoy routine. This marks another evolution in Lazarus’s longstanding impersonation tactics—previously targeting engineers via spear-phishing and defense-sector ruses—while the group simultaneously diversifies into cryptocurrency heists (prompting Tornado Cash sanctions) and VHD ransomware operations to fund the North Korean regime.
hits.title: APT Lazarus Targets Engineers with macOS Malware | Threatpost

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates
hits.text: Unit 42 has observed a sharp rise in post-intrusion WastedLocker ransomware attacks by the Evil Corp group—already known for Dridex—against large U.S. organizations in sectors from manufacturing to legal services, with initial compromise typically via ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates that deploy a SocGholish JavaScript loader to profile systems and invoke PowerShell-based Cobalt Strike payloads; attackers then leverage WMI and PsExec for lateral movement, identify high-value and backup systems, elevate privileges, disable Windows Defender, delete shadow copies, install WastedLocker as a service, and encrypt files using a “.<victim_name>wasted” extension while appending ransom notes (“.<victim_name>wasted_info”) with contact addresses on ProtonMail, Airmail and others. Palo Alto Networks’ WildFire, Cortex XDR (anti-ransomware and behavioral threat protection), NGFW DNS signatures and AutoFocus tagging detect and prevent WastedLocker activity; organizations are urged to implement robust, off-site backup strategies and hardened cybersecurity controls to mitigate this high-impact targeted ransomware threat.
hits.title: Threat Assessment: WastedLocker Ransomware

hits.text: In August 2025 the FBI issued a public service announcement that FSB-linked Berserk Bear (aka Blue Kraken, Crouching Yeti, Dragonfly, Koala Team) has been exploiting the seven-year-old Cisco IOS/IOS XE Smart Install remote code execution/DoS vulnerability (CVE-2018-0171) to compromise critical infrastructure worldwide. Since Cisco first detected opportunistic attacks in November 2021, the group has collected configuration files from thousands of unpatched devices associated with U.S. critical infrastructure sectors, covertly modified those configs to maintain persistent unauthorized access, and conducted network reconnaissance targeting ICS-related protocols and applications. Cisco Talos reports that the campaign, referred to as Static Tundra, has aggressively hit telecommunications, higher education, and manufacturing networks across North America, Asia, Africa, and Europe, deploying custom SNMP tools and the SYNful Knock firmware implant—originally identified by FireEye in 2015—to evade detection and embed for years. The FBI’s warning underscores the urgent need for organizations to patch CVE-2018-0171, disable Smart Install, and implement comprehensive hardening, as other state-sponsored actors are likely conducting similar network device compromise campaigns.

retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.

retrieved_context.text: In August 2025 Microsoft Threat Intelligence revealed that Storm-2460, associated with the Play ransomware group, has resumed exploiting CVE-2025-29824—a zero-day elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Common Log File System patched in April—to gain SYSTEM privileges on unpatched hosts across IT, financial and real estate organizations in the US, Europe, South America and the Middle East. hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

hits.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.
hits.title: Follina Exploited by State-Sponsored Hackers | Threatpost

hits.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
hits.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

PipeMagic communicates with its TCP C2 over a named pipe, self-updates by storing distinct payload modules in memory via doubly linked lists for staging, execution and communication (plus an additional dynamic list), then leverages the CLFS exploit to escalate privileges before deploying Play ransomware. Although the campaign’s footprint remains limited, the combination of a zero-day exploit and a sophisticated modular backdoor underscores a heightened risk; organizations are urged to immediately apply the April patch for CVE-2025-29824, enable tamper and network protection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, run EDR in block mode, enforce full automated investigation and remediation, and leverage cloud-delivered machine-learning protections to block novel variants.
retrieved_context.title: PipeMagic Backdoor Resurfaces as Part of Play Ransomware Attack Chain

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

retrieved_context.text: Since January 2021, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has tracked a government-backed North Korean campaign that leverages social engineering via X (formerly Twitter) and encrypted messaging apps to befriend security researchers and deliver malicious files containing at least one unpatched 0-day in a popular software package; upon exploitation the custom shellcode performs anti-virtual-machine checks, captures system data and screenshots, and exfiltrates them to C2 infrastructure (e.g., 23.106.215[.]105, www.blgbeach[.]com), with the latest vulnerability reported and patched on September 12, 2023 (see TAG’s published RCA). In parallel, the actors published a seemingly benign Windows tool called GetSymbol on GitHub (https://github.com/dbgsymbol/) that quietly downloads debugging symbols—and arbitrary code—from attacker domains, requiring full OS reinstalls for compromised hosts. TAG has added malicious sites to Safe Browsing, issued government-backed attacker alerts to targeted Gmail and Workspace users, and urges researchers to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, keep software up to date, and verify system integrity after using third-party tools.
retrieved_context.title: Active North Korean campaign targeting security researchers

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
retrieved_context.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
retrieved_context.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

retrieved_context.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.
retrieved_context.title: Follina Exploited by State-Sponsored Hackers | Threatpost

retrieved_context.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

retrieved_context.text: Unit 42’s investigation reveals that North Korean state‐sponsored group Jumpy Pisces (aka Andariel/Onyx Sleet) gained initial access to a corporate network in May 2024 via a compromised user account, deployed a customized Sliver C2 beaconing to 172.96.137[.]224/americajobmail[.]site and their bespoke DTrack infostealer across hosts via SMB, and leveraged Impacket’s secretsdump.py, Mimikatz dumps (KB0722.log), a custom RDP account tool and a trojanized browser‐data stealer for credential harvesting, lateral movement and persistence; this activity continued until early September when the same account and toolset were abused—using TokenPlayer for Windows token abuse, PsExec for privilege escalation and EDR sensor removal—to facilitate Play ransomware (Fiddling Scorpius) deployment, marking the first observed collaboration (affiliate or initial access brokerage) between Jumpy Pisces and Play ransomware and signaling a shift from espionage to broader ransomware operations that could target victims globally, underscoring the imperative for defenders to treat Jumpy Pisces activity as a precursory ransomware threat and to deploy mitigations such as Cortex XDR, Advanced WildFire, Advanced URL Filtering and Advanced DNS Security.
retrieved_context.title: Jumpy Pisces Engages in Play Ransomware

hits.text: Between July and October 2021, Iranian state-sponsored group Lyceum (aka Hexane, Spirlin) conducted targeted intrusions against ISPs and telecom operators in Israel, Morocco, Tunisia, and Saudi Arabia, plus an African ministry of foreign affairs, using credential stuffing and brute-force attacks for initial access before deploying malware implants Shark and Milan to execute arbitrary commands and exfiltrate data; researchers from Accenture Cyber Threat Intelligence and Prevailion's Adversarial Counterintelligence Team identified over 20 web-based infrastructure components enabling victim identification, with at least two compromises assessed as ongoing despite prior public disclosure of indicators of compromise, and beaconing from reconfigured or new Lyceum backdoors detected in late October 2021 from Tunisian telecom and African MFA victims indicating active modifications to evade security detection.
hits.title: Iran's Lyceum Hackers Target Telecoms, ISPs in Israel, Saudi Arabia, and Africa

hits.text: Between May and September 2024, threat actors tracked as "Jumpy Pisces" (also known as Andariel, APT45, DarkSeoul, Nickel Hyatt, Onyx Sleet, Operation Troy, Silent Chollima, Stonefly)—affiliated with North Korea's Reconnaissance General Bureau and active since 2009—collaborated with the Play ransomware group (also called Balloonfly, Fiddling Scorpius, PlayCrypt) in what Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 described as "the first recorded collaboration between the Jumpy Pisces North Korean state-sponsored group and an underground ransomware network"; initial access came via compromised user account in May 2024, followed by lateral movement and persistence using Sliver C2 framework and Dtrack backdoor (aka Valefor, Preft), with communication to C2 server 172.96.137[.]224 continuing until early September before Play ransomware deployment; pre-ransomware activities included credential harvesting, privilege escalation, EDR sensor uninstallation, and trojanized binary harvesting web browser history and credit card details from Chrome, Edge, and Brave; Andariel previously deployed SHATTEREDGLASS and Maui ransomware strains and targeted three U.S. organizations in August 2024 in financially-motivated attacks without ransomware deployment; the collaboration suggests North Korean actors may conduct widespread ransomware operations to evade sanctions and generate revenue.
hits.title: North Korean Group Collaborates with Play Ransomware in Significant Cyber Attack

hits.text: Security researcher Marc Newlin of SkySafe disclosed CVE-2023-45866, a critical, decade-old keystroke-injection flaw in the Bluetooth host state-machine that exploits an unauthenticated pairing mechanism in the Bluetooth specification to trick macOS (13.3.3), iOS (16.6, even in Lockdown Mode), Android (from 4.2.2 through 14 on devices including Pixel 7/6/4a, Pixel 2, Nexus 5, BLU DASH), and Linux BlueZ stacks (Ubuntu 18.04–23.10) into pairing with a malicious emulated keyboard, enabling remote attackers within Bluetooth range to run a Python-based script, inject arbitrary keystrokes, install apps, forward emails or texts, and execute commands without user confirmation or biometric/password authentication. After informing Apple, Google, Canonical, and the Bluetooth SIG between August and September, patches have been released for Android 11–14 and BlueZ (via GitHub) but Apple has yet to announce a timeline for CVE-2023-42929, proof-of-concept exploit scripts will be published in January, and no active in-the-wild exploitation has been observed to date.
hits.title: Critical Bluetooth Flaw Exposes Android, Apple & Linux Devices to Takeover

hits.text: On Oct. 10, 2023, Citrix released patches for Netscaler ADC and Gateway to address Citrix Bleed (CVE-2023-4966, CVSS 9.4), a memory-leak vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to exfiltrate session tokens via crafted requests and hijack sessions; public proof-of-concept code from Assetnote and Python exploit scripts rapidly empowered ransomware affiliates and other threat actors to gain footholds, with Unit 42 Incident Response and Managed Threat Hunting teams observing exploitation-linked remote PowerShell sessions spawning cmd.exe, reconnaissance commands (whoami, WMIC, tasklist, net user), deployment of XScan (s.exe), Python HTTP servers, and mRemoteNG on VDI hosts—though no lateral movement beyond VDI was detected. Cortex Xpanse identified nearly 8,000 exposed Netscaler Gateway and 6,000 ADC IPs worldwide (3,100 US, 800 Germany, 450 China, 400 UK), prompting addition to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog. Palo Alto Networks advises immediate patching (including CVE-2023-4967), engagement of Unit 42 for incident response and continuous hunting, deployment of Next-Generation Firewalls with Advanced Threat Prevention signature 94483, updated Advanced WildFire ML models, Cortex Xpanse Threat Response Event, and Cortex XDR/XSIAM behavioral, anti-webshell, and credential-gathering protections to detect and block post-exploitation activity.
hits.title: Threat Brief: Citrix Bleed CVE-2023-4966

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates
hits.text: Unit 42 has observed a sharp rise in post-intrusion WastedLocker ransomware attacks by the Evil Corp group—already known for Dridex—against large U.S. organizations in sectors from manufacturing to legal services, with initial compromise typically via ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates that deploy a SocGholish JavaScript loader to profile systems and invoke PowerShell-based Cobalt Strike payloads; attackers then leverage WMI and PsExec for lateral movement, identify high-value and backup systems, elevate privileges, disable Windows Defender, delete shadow copies, install WastedLocker as a service, and encrypt files using a “.<victim_name>wasted” extension while appending ransom notes (“.<victim_name>wasted_info”) with contact addresses on ProtonMail, Airmail and others. Palo Alto Networks’ WildFire, Cortex XDR (anti-ransomware and behavioral threat protection), NGFW DNS signatures and AutoFocus tagging detect and prevent WastedLocker activity; organizations are urged to implement robust, off-site backup strategies and hardened cybersecurity controls to mitigate this high-impact targeted ransomware threat.
hits.title: Threat Assessment: WastedLocker Ransomware

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Operation Triangulation, a sophisticated iOS-targeting advanced persistent threat (APT) platform documented by Kaspersky researchers Georgy Kucherin, Leonid Bezvershenko, and Valentin Pashkov, exploited zero-day kernel vulnerabilities CVE-2023-32434 and CVE-2023-32435 via iMessage to deliver the TriangleDB backdoor implant; the attack chain utilized JavaScript Validator and Binary Validator stages performing canvas fingerprinting and device reconnaissance before deployment, with the validators collecting fingerprint data to identify research environments and subsequently exfiltrating crash logs, iMessage evidence, process lists, jailbreak status, device identifiers (username, phone number, IMEI, Apple ID), and installed applications via C2 servers; TriangleDB comprised microphone-recording, iCloud Keychain extraction, SQLite database theft, and location-triangulation modules using GSM data (MCC, MNC, LAC) when GPS unavailable, with recording suspended during screen-on states and below 10% battery; the backdoor employed private undocumented APIs and periodically exfiltrated data from /private/var/tmp while establishing heartbeat C2 communication and receiving commands to delete forensic artifacts; Kaspersky became a target in early 2023, prompting investigation; Apple patched CVE-2023-32434 in iOS 15.8 and iPadOS 15.8 as of October 25, 2023.
hits.title: iOS Zero-Day Attacks: Experts Uncover Deeper Insights into Operation Triangulation

canonical_entities: Exfiltration of SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations
hits.text: North Korean state-sponsored APT Slow Pisces (aka Jade Sleet, TraderTraitor, PUKCHONG) is executing a sophisticated three-stage campaign against cryptocurrency developers by posing as recruiters on LinkedIn, distributing benign PDF job descriptions with embedded coding challenges, and redirecting targets to malicious GitHub repositories containing Python and JavaScript code laced with YAML deserialization and EJS escapeFunction backdoors; once activated under specific conditions, these backdoors deploy in-memory RN Loader and RN Stealer payloads to collect system information, establish C2 communications, and exfiltrate SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations with minimal forensic footprint—building on past successes that netted over $1 billion in 2023 and $1.5 billion in 2024—and highlighting the urgent need for enhanced vetting on professional platforms, proactive detection of unsafe deserialization and templating flaws, and memory-based threat monitoring to defend the cryptocurrency sector.
hits.title: Slow Pisces Group Targets Developers Using Coding Challenges Laced with Python Malware

hits.text: Between May and September 2024, threat actors tracked as "Jumpy Pisces" (also known as Andariel, APT45, DarkSeoul, Nickel Hyatt, Onyx Sleet, Operation Troy, Silent Chollima, Stonefly)—affiliated with North Korea's Reconnaissance General Bureau and active since 2009—collaborated with the Play ransomware group (also called Balloonfly, Fiddling Scorpius, PlayCrypt) in what Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 described as "the first recorded collaboration between the Jumpy Pisces North Korean state-sponsored group and an underground ransomware network"; initial access came via compromised user account in May 2024, followed by lateral movement and persistence using Sliver C2 framework and Dtrack backdoor (aka Valefor, Preft), with communication to C2 server 172.96.137[.]224 continuing until early September before Play ransomware deployment; pre-ransomware activities included credential harvesting, privilege escalation, EDR sensor uninstallation, and trojanized binary harvesting web browser history and credit card details from Chrome, Edge, and Brave; Andariel previously deployed SHATTEREDGLASS and Maui ransomware strains and targeted three U.S. organizations in August 2024 in financially-motivated attacks without ransomware deployment; the collaboration suggests North Korean actors may conduct widespread ransomware operations to evade sanctions and generate revenue.
hits.title: North Korean Group Collaborates with Play Ransomware in Significant Cyber Attack

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: Operation Triangulation, a sophisticated iOS-targeting advanced persistent threat (APT) platform documented by Kaspersky researchers Georgy Kucherin, Leonid Bezvershenko, and Valentin Pashkov, exploited zero-day kernel vulnerabilities CVE-2023-32434 and CVE-2023-32435 via iMessage to deliver the TriangleDB backdoor implant; the attack chain utilized JavaScript Validator and Binary Validator stages performing canvas fingerprinting and device reconnaissance before deployment, with the validators collecting fingerprint data to identify research environments and subsequently exfiltrating crash logs, iMessage evidence, process lists, jailbreak status, device identifiers (username, phone number, IMEI, Apple ID), and installed applications via C2 servers; TriangleDB comprised microphone-recording, iCloud Keychain extraction, SQLite database theft, and location-triangulation modules using GSM data (MCC, MNC, LAC) when GPS unavailable, with recording suspended during screen-on states and below 10% battery; the backdoor employed private undocumented APIs and periodically exfiltrated data from /private/var/tmp while establishing heartbeat C2 communication and receiving commands to delete forensic artifacts; Kaspersky became a target in early 2023, prompting investigation; Apple patched CVE-2023-32434 in iOS 15.8 and iPadOS 15.8 as of October 25, 2023.
hits.title: iOS Zero-Day Attacks: Experts Uncover Deeper Insights into Operation Triangulation

canonical_entities: Exfiltration of SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations
hits.text: North Korean state-sponsored APT Slow Pisces (aka Jade Sleet, TraderTraitor, PUKCHONG) is executing a sophisticated three-stage campaign against cryptocurrency developers by posing as recruiters on LinkedIn, distributing benign PDF job descriptions with embedded coding challenges, and redirecting targets to malicious GitHub repositories containing Python and JavaScript code laced with YAML deserialization and EJS escapeFunction backdoors; once activated under specific conditions, these backdoors deploy in-memory RN Loader and RN Stealer payloads to collect system information, establish C2 communications, and exfiltrate SSH keys, saved credentials, and cloud configurations with minimal forensic footprint—building on past successes that netted over $1 billion in 2023 and $1.5 billion in 2024—and highlighting the urgent need for enhanced vetting on professional platforms, proactive detection of unsafe deserialization and templating flaws, and memory-based threat monitoring to defend the cryptocurrency sector.
hits.title: Slow Pisces Group Targets Developers Using Coding Challenges Laced with Python Malware

hits.text: ChromeLoader, a resurging cross-platform browser hijacker detailed by Malwarebytes Labs and Red Canary, infects Windows via ISO files masquerading as cracked games or pirated media and macOS via DMG files containing installer scripts; once executed, it leverages PowerShell-encoded commands (including the shortened –e flag) to inject a malicious Chrome (or Safari) extension fetched via cURL and ZIP, and employs a .NET wrapper for Windows Task Scheduler (or shell scripts on macOS) to maintain persistence before deleting its own scheduled task to evade detection. After installation, victims experience untrusted, ad-laden search results and potential credential harvesting or spyware deployment, since this rare PowerShell-driven injection technique can be repurposed for higher-impact payloads. Researchers recommend users avoid pirated software, inspect Chrome’s “More Tools → Extensions” menu for suspicious add-ons, and administrators hunt for PowerShell processes invoking encodedCommand or spawning chrome.exe with appdata\local flags on Windows, as well as encoded sh/bash/zsh commands or installer scripts on macOS, to detect and mitigate infections before escalation.
hits.title: ChromeLoader Browser Hijacker Provides Gateway to Bigger Threats | Threatpost

hits.text: After a year-long investigation researchers at Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs dissected the Ngioweb botnet—first observed in 2017—which uses a loader network and roughly 15 n-day exploits to deploy malware that contacts C2 domains generated via a domain generation algorithm (augmented by DNS TXT records to resist sinkholing), evaluates device traffic capacity, and links compromised Zyxel, Reolink, Alpha Technologies and, increasingly, Netgear routers (now 10 % of bots) to over 180 “backconnect” C2 nodes that provide at least 80 % of the 35,000 residential proxies in the NSOCKS[.]net service across 180 countries; NSOCKS’s lack of authentication and appearance on free proxy lists has enabled cybercriminals to carry out DDoS amplification, credential stuffing, phishing and malware proxying (e.g., Agent Tesla), while APT28 state-sponsored actors have mixed espionage with criminal traffic on the same infrastructure. To disrupt both operations, Lumen, alongside The ShadowServer Foundation and other partners, is actively blocking traffic to known C2 nodes and publishing indicators of compromise to help organizations identify and remediate infected devices.
hits.title: Botnet fueling residential proxies disrupted in cybercrime crackdown

hits.text: Maintainers of the Python Package Index (PyPI) were forced this week to suspend new project creation and user registrations after Checkmarx researchers discovered a multi-stage malware upload campaign leveraging typo-squatting to push multiple malicious Python packages created via automation tools. Each package’s setup.py script automatically executed on installation and dynamically constructed a command-and-control URL—by appending the package name as a query parameter—to fetch an additional payload. That payload operated as an advanced info-stealer, harvesting crypto wallets, browser cookies, extensions data and credentials, and deployed a persistence mechanism to survive reboots. Although PyPI has since resolved the incident, the attack underscores the ongoing risk of supply-chain compromises in software ecosystems and highlights the need for stringent package provenance verification, automated code review, two-factor authentication for maintainers and continuous monitoring of repository uploads to prevent similar threats and minimize impact.
hits.title: Malware Upload Attack Hits PyPI Repository - SecurityWeek

hits.text: On Oct. 10, 2023, Citrix released patches for Netscaler ADC and Gateway to address Citrix Bleed (CVE-2023-4966, CVSS 9.4), a memory-leak vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to exfiltrate session tokens via crafted requests and hijack sessions; public proof-of-concept code from Assetnote and Python exploit scripts rapidly empowered ransomware affiliates and other threat actors to gain footholds, with Unit 42 Incident Response and Managed Threat Hunting teams observing exploitation-linked remote PowerShell sessions spawning cmd.exe, reconnaissance commands (whoami, WMIC, tasklist, net user), deployment of XScan (s.exe), Python HTTP servers, and mRemoteNG on VDI hosts—though no lateral movement beyond VDI was detected. Cortex Xpanse identified nearly 8,000 exposed Netscaler Gateway and 6,000 ADC IPs worldwide (3,100 US, 800 Germany, 450 China, 400 UK), prompting addition to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog. Palo Alto Networks advises immediate patching (including CVE-2023-4967), engagement of Unit 42 for incident response and continuous hunting, deployment of Next-Generation Firewalls with Advanced Threat Prevention signature 94483, updated Advanced WildFire ML models, Cortex Xpanse Threat Response Event, and Cortex XDR/XSIAM behavioral, anti-webshell, and credential-gathering protections to detect and block post-exploitation activity.
hits.title: Threat Brief: Citrix Bleed CVE-2023-4966

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

hits.text: Our GReAT team uncovered Operation ForumTroll—a state-sponsored APT campaign targeting Russian media, academic and government personnel—delivering previously unknown malware via phishing emails masquerading as Primakov Readings invitations containing two malicious links; clicking either on a Windows PC using Chrome or any Chromium-based browser silently triggers a zero-day exploit (CVE-2025-2783), exploiting a logic flaw at the Chrome-Windows interface to bypass the browser’s sandbox and deploy the payload without further user interaction. We promptly reported the vulnerability to Google, which released a patch in Chrome version 134.0.6998.177/178; while the phishing links now redirect to the legitimate forum site and the campaign is dormant, the attackers could reactivate it at any time. To mitigate this espionage threat, organizations should ensure all Chrome instances are updated to at least 134.0.6998.177/.178, deploy robust exploit detection and prevention solutions on internet-connected devices, and maintain vigilant phishing awareness and monitoring.
hits.title: CVE-2025-2783 in Operation ForumTroll APT
