retrieved_context.text: Between July and October 2021, Iranian state-sponsored group Lyceum (aka Hexane, Spirlin) conducted targeted intrusions against ISPs and telecom operators in Israel, Morocco, Tunisia, and Saudi Arabia, plus an African ministry of foreign affairs, using credential stuffing and brute-force attacks for initial access before deploying malware implants Shark and Milan to execute arbitrary commands and exfiltrate data; researchers from Accenture Cyber Threat Intelligence and Prevailion's Adversarial Counterintelligence Team identified over 20 web-based infrastructure components enabling victim identification, with at least two compromises assessed as ongoing despite prior public disclosure of indicators of compromise, and beaconing from reconfigured or new Lyceum backdoors detected in late October 2021 from Tunisian telecom and African MFA victims indicating active modifications to evade security detection.
retrieved_context.title: Iran's Lyceum Hackers Target Telecoms, ISPs in Israel, Saudi Arabia, and Africa

retrieved_context.text: Between May and September 2024, threat actors tracked as "Jumpy Pisces" (also known as Andariel, APT45, DarkSeoul, Nickel Hyatt, Onyx Sleet, Operation Troy, Silent Chollima, Stonefly)—affiliated with North Korea's Reconnaissance General Bureau and active since 2009—collaborated with the Play ransomware group (also called Balloonfly, Fiddling Scorpius, PlayCrypt) in what Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 described as "the first recorded collaboration between the Jumpy Pisces North Korean state-sponsored group and an underground ransomware network"; initial access came via compromised user account in May 2024, followed by lateral movement and persistence using Sliver C2 framework and Dtrack backdoor (aka Valefor, Preft), with communication to C2 server 172.96.137[.]224 continuing until early September before Play ransomware deployment; pre-ransomware activities included credential harvesting, privilege escalation, EDR sensor uninstallation, and trojanized binary harvesting web browser history and credit card details from Chrome, Edge, and Brave; Andariel previously deployed SHATTEREDGLASS and Maui ransomware strains and targeted three U.S. organizations in August 2024 in financially-motivated attacks without ransomware deployment; the collaboration suggests North Korean actors may conduct widespread ransomware operations to evade sanctions and generate revenue.
retrieved_context.title: North Korean Group Collaborates with Play Ransomware in Significant Cyber Attack

retrieved_context.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.
retrieved_context.title: Follina Exploited by State-Sponsored Hackers | Threatpost

retrieved_context.text: After a year-long investigation researchers at Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs dissected the Ngioweb botnet—first observed in 2017—which uses a loader network and roughly 15 n-day exploits to deploy malware that contacts C2 domains generated via a domain generation algorithm (augmented by DNS TXT records to resist sinkholing), evaluates device traffic capacity, and links compromised Zyxel, Reolink, Alpha Technologies and, increasingly, Netgear routers (now 10 % of bots) to over 180 “backconnect” C2 nodes that provide at least 80 % of the 35,000 residential proxies in the NSOCKS[.]net service across 180 countries; NSOCKS’s lack of authentication and appearance on free proxy lists has enabled cybercriminals to carry out DDoS amplification, credential stuffing, phishing and malware proxying (e.g., Agent Tesla), while APT28 state-sponsored actors have mixed espionage with criminal traffic on the same infrastructure. To disrupt both operations, Lumen, alongside The ShadowServer Foundation and other partners, is actively blocking traffic to known C2 nodes and publishing indicators of compromise to help organizations identify and remediate infected devices.
retrieved_context.title: Botnet fueling residential proxies disrupted in cybercrime crackdown

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
retrieved_context.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
retrieved_context.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

retrieved_context.text: Our GReAT team uncovered Operation ForumTroll—a state-sponsored APT campaign targeting Russian media, academic and government personnel—delivering previously unknown malware via phishing emails masquerading as Primakov Readings invitations containing two malicious links; clicking either on a Windows PC using Chrome or any Chromium-based browser silently triggers a zero-day exploit (CVE-2025-2783), exploiting a logic flaw at the Chrome-Windows interface to bypass the browser’s sandbox and deploy the payload without further user interaction. We promptly reported the vulnerability to Google, which released a patch in Chrome version 134.0.6998.177/178; while the phishing links now redirect to the legitimate forum site and the campaign is dormant, the attackers could reactivate it at any time. To mitigate this espionage threat, organizations should ensure all Chrome instances are updated to at least 134.0.6998.177/.178, deploy robust exploit detection and prevention solutions on internet-connected devices, and maintain vigilant phishing awareness and monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CVE-2025-2783 in Operation ForumTroll APT

retrieved_context.text: On Oct. 10, 2023, Citrix released patches for Netscaler ADC and Gateway to address Citrix Bleed (CVE-2023-4966, CVSS 9.4), a memory-leak vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to exfiltrate session tokens via crafted requests and hijack sessions; public proof-of-concept code from Assetnote and Python exploit scripts rapidly empowered ransomware affiliates and other threat actors to gain footholds, with Unit 42 Incident Response and Managed Threat Hunting teams observing exploitation-linked remote PowerShell sessions spawning cmd.exe, reconnaissance commands (whoami, WMIC, tasklist, net user), deployment of XScan (s.exe), Python HTTP servers, and mRemoteNG on VDI hosts—though no lateral movement beyond VDI was detected. Cortex Xpanse identified nearly 8,000 exposed Netscaler Gateway and 6,000 ADC IPs worldwide (3,100 US, 800 Germany, 450 China, 400 UK), prompting addition to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog. Palo Alto Networks advises immediate patching (including CVE-2023-4967), engagement of Unit 42 for incident response and continuous hunting, deployment of Next-Generation Firewalls with Advanced Threat Prevention signature 94483, updated Advanced WildFire ML models, Cortex Xpanse Threat Response Event, and Cortex XDR/XSIAM behavioral, anti-webshell, and credential-gathering protections to detect and block post-exploitation activity.

hits.text: Researchers at NCC Group have identified SnapMC as a new rapid-strike extortion group that eschews file encryption in favor of pure data theft, leveraging the Acunetix vulnerability scanner to pinpoint and exploit unpatched PrintNightmare LPE, Telerik UI for ASPX.NET RCE and SQL-injection flaws in VPN and web-server applications, then running SQL export scripts, compressing stolen CSVs with 7zip and exfiltrating them via the MinIO client—all within 30 minutes—before delivering standard extortion emails. By making data theft the primary leverage, SnapMC renders backup-based recovery moot and heightens the risk that victims who pay ransoms will face repeated extortion or public data sale, as seen with Sodinokibi, Netwalker, Mespinoza and Conti, and echoed by Coveware’s advice never to pay. Effective defenses include prompt patching of known CVEs, deploying well-configured web application firewalls around vulnerable services like Telerik and maintaining rigorous vulnerability management to thwart this growing threat.
hits.title: SnapMC hackers skip file encryption and just steal your files

hits.text: NCC Group’s RIFT team has tracked a previously unknown extortion actor, SnapMC, which conducts sub-30-minute data breach attacks—eschewing ransomware to steal and threaten to publicly leak data unless victims pay—by scanning for and exploiting public-facing vulnerabilities (notably CVE-2019-18935 in Telerik UI and SQL injection) to deploy a reverse shell, executing reconnaissance via PowerShell (whoami, wmic, net users), occasionally leveraging privilege-escalation scripts such as Invoke-Nightmare and JuicyPotato, then collecting data with 7zip and Invoke-SQLcmd before exfiltrating compressed CSVs to cloud storage via the MinIO client (mc.exe) configured through config.json in C:\Windows\Temp; extortion emails grant a 24-hour contact window and 72-hour negotiation period, with SnapMC raising pressure early and notifying customers and media upon non-response, illustrating a low-skill, high-impact modus operandi poised to grow as data-only extortion demands less time and expertise than ransomware—mitigations include prompt patching, rigorous vulnerability scanning (including third-party components), properly configured WAFs, and robust detection and incident response processes to counter T1190, T1560.001 and T1567.002 techniques.
hits.title: SnapMC skips ransomware, steals data | NCC Group

canonical_entities: Progress Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX
hits.text: BlackBerry researchers have identified “Silent Skimming,” a year-long, financially motivated campaign by a Chinese-language proficient threat actor that exploits a .NET deserialization flaw (CVE-2019-18935) in Progress Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX to remotely deploy malicious DLLs on internet-facing payment and POS servers across APAC, North America and Latin America. Following initial access, the actor leverages a suite of post-exploitation tools—BadPotato, Godzilla Webshell, Juicy Potato, SweetPotato, PowerShell RATs (server.ps1), HTML HTA downloaders and Cobalt Strike beacons—hosted on attacker-controlled HTTP file servers to escalate privileges, execute code, establish C2 via Cloudflare and exfiltrate billing and credit-card data. Attribution is supported by Simplified Chinese code, C2 infrastructure in Japan and region-specific VPS deployments, while intelligence links similar tactics to BlackSuit and Zeon groups. To mitigate risk, organizations should urgently patch Telerik components, monitor for anomalous DLL or webshell activity, enforce PCI DSS Requirement 6.5 for third-party applications, implement rigorous Governance, Risk and Compliance frameworks, and continuously assess payment-processing systems for insecure deserialization and unauthorized data flows.
hits.title: Everything You Need to Know About Silent Skimming

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates
hits.text: Unit 42 has observed a sharp rise in post-intrusion WastedLocker ransomware attacks by the Evil Corp group—already known for Dridex—against large U.S. organizations in sectors from manufacturing to legal services, with initial compromise typically via ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates that deploy a SocGholish JavaScript loader to profile systems and invoke PowerShell-based Cobalt Strike payloads; attackers then leverage WMI and PsExec for lateral movement, identify high-value and backup systems, elevate privileges, disable Windows Defender, delete shadow copies, install WastedLocker as a service, and encrypt files using a “.<victim_name>wasted” extension while appending ransom notes (“.<victim_name>wasted_info”) with contact addresses on ProtonMail, Airmail and others. Palo Alto Networks’ WildFire, Cortex XDR (anti-ransomware and behavioral threat protection), NGFW DNS signatures and AutoFocus tagging detect and prevent WastedLocker activity; organizations are urged to implement robust, off-site backup strategies and hardened cybersecurity controls to mitigate this high-impact targeted ransomware threat.

hits.text: Since at least May 2023, BlackBerry researchers have identified a technically sophisticated Chinese-speaking threat actor—dubbed Silent Skimmer—that after over a year skimming card data from Asia/Pacific e-commerce and point-of-sale sites has expanded its campaign to North and Latin America, compromising organizations across multiple sectors by exploiting known web application vulnerabilities—most notably CVE-2019-18935 in Progress Software’s Telerik UI previously used by China’s Hafnium and Vietnam’s XE Group—on IIS servers to upload a malicious DLL and achieve remote code execution; using a multi-stage toolkit comprising privilege escalation exploits, a remote access tool, stagers/downloaders, and post-exploit utilities along with open-source binaries and scripts to inject card-skimming code into payment pages; and dynamically rotating short-lived, regionally co-located Microsoft Azure VPS-based C2 servers (each active less than a week) to blend exfiltration traffic with normal operations, mirroring Magecart tactics that have impacted hundreds of thousands of sites (e.g., British Airways, Ticketmaster, Newegg), and highlighting the imperative for prompt patching of third-party components, comprehensive web-app security audits, and vigilant monitoring of anomalous C2 infrastructure to thwart credential and payment data theft.
hits.title: Payment Card-Skimming Campaign Now Targeting Websites in North America

canonical_entities: FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns
hits.text: Clop ransomware, a TA505-sponsored RaaS strain appending the “.ClOP” extension, infects entire networks by compromising Active Directory servers and manipulating Group Policy for persistence, then uses phishing-delivered HTML attachments to drop the Get2 loader, which in turn pulls SDBOT, FlawedAmmyy RATs, Cobalt Strike beacons and TinyMet reverse shells for reconnaissance, lateral movement (via SMB exploits), and exfiltration (often using the DEWMODE web shell). Operators employ double and quadruple extortion—threatening to publish or auction stolen data on their Cl0p^_-Leaks site and targeting executives/customers—to coerce ransoms, driving average payments up 43% to $220,298 (median $78,398) in Q1 2021 after FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns against Kiteworks FTA (CVE-2021-27101/02/03/04) and Fortra GoAnywhere MFT, while in 2023 they exploited PaperCut CVE-2023-27350 to deploy Truebot and LockBit/Clop, then MOVEit CVE-2023-24362/CVE-2023-35036 and an unpatched SQL injection flaw to steal data without payloads. Trend Micro detections reveal a May 2023 surge (245 attempts), with top targets in banking, retail and healthcare across Türkiye, Canada, the US and large enterprises worldwide.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Clop | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: Security researcher Marc Newlin of SkySafe disclosed CVE-2023-45866, a critical, decade-old keystroke-injection flaw in the Bluetooth host state-machine that exploits an unauthenticated pairing mechanism in the Bluetooth specification to trick macOS (13.3.3), iOS (16.6, even in Lockdown Mode), Android (from 4.2.2 through 14 on devices including Pixel 7/6/4a, Pixel 2, Nexus 5, BLU DASH), and Linux BlueZ stacks (Ubuntu 18.04–23.10) into pairing with a malicious emulated keyboard, enabling remote attackers within Bluetooth range to run a Python-based script, inject arbitrary keystrokes, install apps, forward emails or texts, and execute commands without user confirmation or biometric/password authentication. After informing Apple, Google, Canonical, and the Bluetooth SIG between August and September, patches have been released for Android 11–14 and BlueZ (via GitHub) but Apple has yet to announce a timeline for CVE-2023-42929, proof-of-concept exploit scripts will be published in January, and no active in-the-wild exploitation has been observed to date.
hits.title: Critical Bluetooth Flaw Exposes Android, Apple & Linux Devices to Takeover

retrieved_context.text: Since at least May 2023, BlackBerry researchers have identified a technically sophisticated Chinese-speaking threat actor—dubbed Silent Skimmer—that after over a year skimming card data from Asia/Pacific e-commerce and point-of-sale sites has expanded its campaign to North and Latin America, compromising organizations across multiple sectors by exploiting known web application vulnerabilities—most notably CVE-2019-18935 in Progress Software’s Telerik UI previously used by China’s Hafnium and Vietnam’s XE Group—on IIS servers to upload a malicious DLL and achieve remote code execution; using a multi-stage toolkit comprising privilege escalation exploits, a remote access tool, stagers/downloaders, and post-exploit utilities along with open-source binaries and scripts to inject card-skimming code into payment pages; and dynamically rotating short-lived, regionally co-located Microsoft Azure VPS-based C2 servers (each active less than a week) to blend exfiltration traffic with normal operations, mirroring Magecart tactics that have impacted hundreds of thousands of sites (e.g., British Airways, Ticketmaster, Newegg), and highlighting the imperative for prompt patching of third-party components, comprehensive web-app security audits, and vigilant monitoring of anomalous C2 infrastructure to thwart credential and payment data theft.

canonical_entities: FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns

retrieved_context.text: Security researcher Marc Newlin of SkySafe disclosed CVE-2023-45866, a critical, decade-old keystroke-injection flaw in the Bluetooth host state-machine that exploits an unauthenticated pairing mechanism in the Bluetooth specification to trick macOS (13.3.3), iOS (16.6, even in Lockdown Mode), Android (from 4.2.2 through 14 on devices including Pixel 7/6/4a, Pixel 2, Nexus 5, BLU DASH), and Linux BlueZ stacks (Ubuntu 18.04–23.10) into pairing with a malicious emulated keyboard, enabling remote attackers within Bluetooth range to run a Python-based script, inject arbitrary keystrokes, install apps, forward emails or texts, and execute commands without user confirmation or biometric/password authentication. After informing Apple, Google, Canonical, and the Bluetooth SIG between August and September, patches have been released for Android 11–14 and BlueZ (via GitHub) but Apple has yet to announce a timeline for CVE-2023-42929, proof-of-concept exploit scripts will be published in January, and no active in-the-wild exploitation has been observed to date.
retrieved_context.title: Critical Bluetooth Flaw Exposes Android, Apple & Linux Devices to Takeover

hits.text: Researchers at NCC Group have identified SnapMC as a new rapid-strike extortion group that eschews file encryption in favor of pure data theft, leveraging the Acunetix vulnerability scanner to pinpoint and exploit unpatched PrintNightmare LPE, Telerik UI for ASPX.NET RCE and SQL-injection flaws in VPN and web-server applications, then running SQL export scripts, compressing stolen CSVs with 7zip and exfiltrating them via the MinIO client—all within 30 minutes—before delivering standard extortion emails. By making data theft the primary leverage, SnapMC renders backup-based recovery moot and heightens the risk that victims who pay ransoms will face repeated extortion or public data sale, as seen with Sodinokibi, Netwalker, Mespinoza and Conti, and echoed by Coveware’s advice never to pay. Effective defenses include prompt patching of known CVEs, deploying well-configured web application firewalls around vulnerable services like Telerik and maintaining rigorous vulnerability management to thwart this growing threat.

hits.text: NCC Group’s RIFT team has tracked a previously unknown extortion actor, SnapMC, which conducts sub-30-minute data breach attacks—eschewing ransomware to steal and threaten to publicly leak data unless victims pay—by scanning for and exploiting public-facing vulnerabilities (notably CVE-2019-18935 in Telerik UI and SQL injection) to deploy a reverse shell, executing reconnaissance via PowerShell (whoami, wmic, net users), occasionally leveraging privilege-escalation scripts such as Invoke-Nightmare and JuicyPotato, then collecting data with 7zip and Invoke-SQLcmd before exfiltrating compressed CSVs to cloud storage via the MinIO client (mc.exe) configured through config.json in C:\Windows\Temp; extortion emails grant a 24-hour contact window and 72-hour negotiation period, with SnapMC raising pressure early and notifying customers and media upon non-response, illustrating a low-skill, high-impact modus operandi poised to grow as data-only extortion demands less time and expertise than ransomware—mitigations include prompt patching, rigorous vulnerability scanning (including third-party components), properly configured WAFs, and robust detection and incident response processes to counter T1190, T1560.001 and T1567.002 techniques.

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.

hits.text: BlackBerry researchers have identified “Silent Skimming,” a year-long, financially motivated campaign by a Chinese-language proficient threat actor that exploits a .NET deserialization flaw (CVE-2019-18935) in Progress Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX to remotely deploy malicious DLLs on internet-facing payment and POS servers across APAC, North America and Latin America. hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.

hits.text: Water Ouroboros is a Ransomware-as-a-Service operation that exploits public-facing Oracle WebLogic vulnerabilities (CVE-2019-2725, CVE-2017-10271, CVE-2019-2729) or drive-by installers for initial access (T1190, T1189), then executes remote Windows commands (wmic.exe, bcdedit.exe, wbadmin.exe, vssadmin.exe) to delete backups and disable recovery (T1490, T1562.001) before encrypting fixed, removable and network drives via a Go-based custom routine that uses RTLGenRandom to generate a symmetric key, protects it with embedded RSA public keys (App_ExportKey), appends “.locked” (unless suppressed with –E), excludes over 60 file extensions, and accepts credentials (c {user}:{pass}), logging (–a), non-aggressive (–A) and size filters (–m). Victims find Contact Us.txt ransom notes pointing to a TOR payment site and Hive Leaks data-dump threat. Post-infection, actors maintain access via compromised admin accounts (T1078), disable security tools (PCHunter, ProcessHacker), dump credentials from registry hives (T1003.002), move laterally over RDP/SMB (T1021.001/002), discover assets via AdFind (T1595.002) and exfiltrate data over C&C (SharpRhino RAT/T1071.001, T1041). With 136 incidents in the US and notable impacts on construction, IT, manufacturing and healthcare SMBs, the campaign underscores the need for timely patching, hardened public-facing apps, least-privilege access, MFA, robust backups and advanced threat detection.

hits.text: Trend Micro observed over one million Conti ransomware attack attempts in the U.S. (Jan–Nov 2021), with the retail, insurance, manufacturing, telecommunications and healthcare sectors most targeted; operators—tied to Trickbot—gain initial access via BazarLoader phishing emails (Google Drive links) and exploitation of FortiGate flaws (CVE-2018-13379/13374) or Exchange ProxyShell, deploy Cobalt Strike, then perform reconnaissance (Whoami, Nltest, Net, ShareFinder), escalate privileges by harvesting domain-admin credentials or exploiting Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) and PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-1675), and dump credentials using ProcDump and Mimikatz (mass-mimikatz, Rubeus, kerberoasting), “reg save,” Get-GPPPassword, SharpChrome and SeatBelt; they move laterally via EternalBlue, PSExec, scheduled tasks and remote-access tools (Atera, AnyDesk), evade defenses with automated batch scripts (GMER, PC Hunter, PowerShell) to disable security services, then execute ransomware via scheduled jobs or DontSleep.exe, exfiltrate data using Rclone (to Mega) or WinSCP, and encrypt files with ChaCha20/RSA-4096 while deleting shadow copies for double extortion; organizations should inventory assets, enforce least privilege, virtual-patch public-facing apps, monitor for Cobalt Strike and anomalous scheduled tasks or credential-dumping activities, deploy multilayered endpoint and network defenses, and maintain reliable backups.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Conti | Trend Micro (US)

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services

hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Russian state-linked cyberespionage group “Static Tundra” (aka Energetic Bear/Berserk Bear/Dragonfly) has spent the past year exploiting a seven-year-old Cisco IOS/IOS XE Smart Install vulnerability (CVE-2018-0171, CVSS 9.8) in end-of-life devices to breach thousands of enterprise and critical-infrastructure networks worldwide, harvesting configuration files, manipulating settings to create backdoor accounts, and leveraging stolen SNMP v1/v2 credentials and a SYNful Knock IOS firmware implant for long-term, stealthy access. After Cisco patched the flaw in March 2018, the FSB Center 16 unit automated mass scans of unpatched switches, pivoted into industrial control protocols, and established secondary footholds for potential OT disruption. The FBI and Cisco Talos warn that manufacturing, telecommunications, and higher-education sectors remain at high risk and urge immediate patching or Smart Install disablement, inventory of end-of-life gear, and rigorous configuration management to mitigate further compromise.

hits.text: In August 2025 the FBI issued a public service announcement that FSB-linked Berserk Bear (aka Blue Kraken, Crouching Yeti, Dragonfly, Koala Team) has been exploiting the seven-year-old Cisco IOS/IOS XE Smart Install remote code execution/DoS vulnerability (CVE-2018-0171) to compromise critical infrastructure worldwide. Since Cisco first detected opportunistic attacks in November 2021, the group has collected configuration files from thousands of unpatched devices associated with U.S. critical infrastructure sectors, covertly modified those configs to maintain persistent unauthorized access, and conducted network reconnaissance targeting ICS-related protocols and applications. Cisco Talos reports that the campaign, referred to as Static Tundra, has aggressively hit telecommunications, higher education, and manufacturing networks across North America, Asia, Africa, and Europe, deploying custom SNMP tools and the SYNful Knock firmware implant—originally identified by FireEye in 2015—to evade detection and embed for years. The FBI’s warning underscores the urgent need for organizations to patch CVE-2018-0171, disable Smart Install, and implement comprehensive hardening, as other state-sponsored actors are likely conducting similar network device compromise campaigns.
hits.title: FBI warns of Russian hackers exploiting 7-year-old Cisco flaw

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
hits.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates
hits.text: Unit 42 has observed a sharp rise in post-intrusion WastedLocker ransomware attacks by the Evil Corp group—already known for Dridex—against large U.S. organizations in sectors from manufacturing to legal services, with initial compromise typically via ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates that deploy a SocGholish JavaScript loader to profile systems and invoke PowerShell-based Cobalt Strike payloads; attackers then leverage WMI and PsExec for lateral movement, identify high-value and backup systems, elevate privileges, disable Windows Defender, delete shadow copies, install WastedLocker as a service, and encrypt files using a “.<victim_name>wasted” extension while appending ransom notes (“.<victim_name>wasted_info”) with contact addresses on ProtonMail, Airmail and others. Palo Alto Networks’ WildFire, Cortex XDR (anti-ransomware and behavioral threat protection), NGFW DNS signatures and AutoFocus tagging detect and prevent WastedLocker activity; organizations are urged to implement robust, off-site backup strategies and hardened cybersecurity controls to mitigate this high-impact targeted ransomware threat.
hits.title: Threat Assessment: WastedLocker Ransomware

hits.text: In early April, Palo Alto Networks’ Advanced WildFire and Cortex XDR uncovered SnipBot—a new v5.0 iteration of the RomCom RAT family—employing advanced window message–based control-flow obfuscation and anti-sandbox checks (filename hash and HKCU\…\RecentDocs entries) in a multi-stage chain beginning with a PDF-labeled EXE downloader signed using a likely stolen certificate; the downloader contacts xeontime[.]com for config-pdf.dll, which uses registry-based COM hijacking to load keyprov.dll from drvmcprotect[.]com into explorer.exe, decrypts payloads stored in HKCU\Software\AppDataSoft\Software, and opens a TCP listener on port 1342 for commands to update, delete, or execute modules. The main backdoor single.dll (mutex “SnipMutex”) supports 27 encrypted commands for drive and process enumeration, file upload/download, and remote module execution, facilitating network pivoting and targeted file exfiltration. Active since December 2023 (RomCom activity since 2022), SnipBot’s tactics, stolen certificates, unique obfuscation, and sophisticated loader underscore a high-risk threat actor likely focused on intelligence gathering; Palo Alto products classify its samples, URLs, and domains as malicious to prevent compromise.
hits.title: Inside SnipBot: The Latest RomCom Malware Variant

canonical_entities: diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine
hits.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.
hits.title: Hackers with Russian Blizzard Steal Data from Rival Networks

hits.text: Security researcher Marc Newlin of SkySafe disclosed CVE-2023-45866, a critical, decade-old keystroke-injection flaw in the Bluetooth host state-machine that exploits an unauthenticated pairing mechanism in the Bluetooth specification to trick macOS (13.3.3), iOS (16.6, even in Lockdown Mode), Android (from 4.2.2 through 14 on devices including Pixel 7/6/4a, Pixel 2, Nexus 5, BLU DASH), and Linux BlueZ stacks (Ubuntu 18.04–23.10) into pairing with a malicious emulated keyboard, enabling remote attackers within Bluetooth range to run a Python-based script, inject arbitrary keystrokes, install apps, forward emails or texts, and execute commands without user confirmation or biometric/password authentication. After informing Apple, Google, Canonical, and the Bluetooth SIG between August and September, patches have been released for Android 11–14 and BlueZ (via GitHub) but Apple has yet to announce a timeline for CVE-2023-42929, proof-of-concept exploit scripts will be published in January, and no active in-the-wild exploitation has been observed to date.
hits.title: Critical Bluetooth Flaw Exposes Android, Apple & Linux Devices to Takeover

canonical_entities: installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry
hits.text: The Lotus Blossom APT (aka Lotus Panda, Billbug, Spring Dragon) has stepped up cyberespionage against APAC government targets by deploying new Sagerunex backdoor variants and abusing Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) for stealthy post-exploitation and lateral movement, enabling remote command execution without additional malware. Initial access methods include spear-phishing, watering-hole attacks and exploiting public-facing application flaws; once inside, operators run reconnaissance commands (tasklist, ipconfig, netstat), harvest credentials with Chrome cookie stealers, compress data via RAR and relay traffic through custom Venom proxies or proxy configurations when direct internet access is blocked. Persistence is achieved by installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry under hijacked service names (tapisrv, swprv) to auto-launch at startup, while command-and-control blends encrypted traffic into legitimate platforms—stolen data uploaded as .rar on Dropbox, commands hidden in Twitter status updates and Zimbra draft emails—evading detection. Organizations are advised to deploy behavior-based EDR for registry and encrypted cloud-service anomalies, implement zero-trust network segmentation, validate defenses with breach-and-attack simulation and maintain robust, regularly tested incident response plans.
hits.title: Lotus Blossom APT Exploits WMI for Post-Exploitation Activities

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since its emergence in 2008, Russian GRU-linked APT Fancy Bear (aka APT28, Sofacy, Swallowtail) has advanced from low-key credential harvesting via spear-phishing emails and spoofed domains to high-impact operations, notably the 2016 DNC and WADA breaches—in which fake webmail domains tricked victims into password resets, enabling network infiltration, malware deployment and public data leaks. After a covert phase (2017–early 2022) targeting energy, government, media, aerospace and defense sectors, Fancy Bear reemerged in July 2022 exploiting Microsoft Office zero-day CVE-2022-30190 (“Follina”) via malicious RTF template injection, remote HTML retrieval and ms-msdt URI calls to execute PowerShell and load a .NET credential stealer that exfiltrates usernames, passwords and URLs from Edge and Chrome browsers in Ukrainian targets. The group maintains persistence with reconnaissance Trojans (Sofacy/Seduploader), X-Agent backdoors, .NET Shunnael encrypted tunnels and a Lojax UEFI rootkit for firmware-level access, typically delivered through visually deceptive domains. These activities underscore the urgent need for proactive Web Application Firewalls, real-time inbound/outbound traffic monitoring, rigorous patch management (including zero-day workarounds), and well-rehearsed incident response plans to detect and mitigate APT28’s evolving espionage and disruptive tactics.
hits.title: Everything You Need to Know About the APT, Fancy Bear

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y

retrieved_context.text: In August 2025 the FBI issued a public service announcement that FSB-linked Berserk Bear (aka Blue Kraken, Crouching Yeti, Dragonfly, Koala Team) has been exploiting the seven-year-old Cisco IOS/IOS XE Smart Install remote code execution/DoS vulnerability (CVE-2018-0171) to compromise critical infrastructure worldwide. Since Cisco first detected opportunistic attacks in November 2021, the group has collected configuration files from thousands of unpatched devices associated with U.S. critical infrastructure sectors, covertly modified those configs to maintain persistent unauthorized access, and conducted network reconnaissance targeting ICS-related protocols and applications. Cisco Talos reports that the campaign, referred to as Static Tundra, has aggressively hit telecommunications, higher education, and manufacturing networks across North America, Asia, Africa, and Europe, deploying custom SNMP tools and the SYNful Knock firmware implant—originally identified by FireEye in 2015—to evade detection and embed for years. The FBI’s warning underscores the urgent need for organizations to patch CVE-2018-0171, disable Smart Install, and implement comprehensive hardening, as other state-sponsored actors are likely conducting similar network device compromise campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: FBI warns of Russian hackers exploiting 7-year-old Cisco flaw

retrieved_context.text: Russian state-linked cyberespionage group “Static Tundra” (aka Energetic Bear/Berserk Bear/Dragonfly) has spent the past year exploiting a seven-year-old Cisco IOS/IOS XE Smart Install vulnerability (CVE-2018-0171, CVSS 9.8) in end-of-life devices to breach thousands of enterprise and critical-infrastructure networks worldwide, harvesting configuration files, manipulating settings to create backdoor accounts, and leveraging stolen SNMP v1/v2 credentials and a SYNful Knock IOS firmware implant for long-term, stealthy access. After Cisco patched the flaw in March 2018, the FSB Center 16 unit automated mass scans of unpatched switches, pivoted into industrial control protocols, and established secondary footholds for potential OT disruption. The FBI and Cisco Talos warn that manufacturing, telecommunications, and higher-education sectors remain at high risk and urge immediate patching or Smart Install disablement, inventory of end-of-life gear, and rigorous configuration management to mitigate further compromise.
retrieved_context.title: FBI, Cisco Warn of Russian Attacks on 7-Year Flaw

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine
retrieved_context.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.
retrieved_context.title: Hackers with Russian Blizzard Steal Data from Rival Networks

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry
retrieved_context.text: The Lotus Blossom APT (aka Lotus Panda, Billbug, Spring Dragon) has stepped up cyberespionage against APAC government targets by deploying new Sagerunex backdoor variants and abusing Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) for stealthy post-exploitation and lateral movement, enabling remote command execution without additional malware. Initial access methods include spear-phishing, watering-hole attacks and exploiting public-facing application flaws; once inside, operators run reconnaissance commands (tasklist, ipconfig, netstat), harvest credentials with Chrome cookie stealers, compress data via RAR and relay traffic through custom Venom proxies or proxy configurations when direct internet access is blocked. Persistence is achieved by installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry under hijacked service names (tapisrv, swprv) to auto-launch at startup, while command-and-control blends encrypted traffic into legitimate platforms—stolen data uploaded as .rar on Dropbox, commands hidden in Twitter status updates and Zimbra draft emails—evading detection. Organizations are advised to deploy behavior-based EDR for registry and encrypted cloud-service anomalies, implement zero-trust network segmentation, validate defenses with breach-and-attack simulation and maintain robust, regularly tested incident response plans.
retrieved_context.title: Lotus Blossom APT Exploits WMI for Post-Exploitation Activities

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Since its emergence in 2008, Russian GRU-linked APT Fancy Bear (aka APT28, Sofacy, Swallowtail) has advanced from low-key credential harvesting via spear-phishing emails and spoofed domains to high-impact operations, notably the 2016 DNC and WADA breaches—in which fake webmail domains tricked victims into password resets, enabling network infiltration, malware deployment and public data leaks. After a covert phase (2017–early 2022) targeting energy, government, media, aerospace and defense sectors, Fancy Bear reemerged in July 2022 exploiting Microsoft Office zero-day CVE-2022-30190 (“Follina”) via malicious RTF template injection, remote HTML retrieval and ms-msdt URI calls to execute PowerShell and load a .NET credential stealer that exfiltrates usernames, passwords and URLs from Edge and Chrome browsers in Ukrainian targets. The group maintains persistence with reconnaissance Trojans (Sofacy/Seduploader), X-Agent backdoors, .NET Shunnael encrypted tunnels and a Lojax UEFI rootkit for firmware-level access, typically delivered through visually deceptive domains. These activities underscore the urgent need for proactive Web Application Firewalls, real-time inbound/outbound traffic monitoring, rigorous patch management (including zero-day workarounds), and well-rehearsed incident response plans to detect and mitigate APT28’s evolving espionage and disruptive tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Everything You Need to Know About the APT, Fancy Bear

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
retrieved_context.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
hits.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.
hits.title: Follina Exploited by State-Sponsored Hackers | Threatpost

hits.text: After a year-long investigation researchers at Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs dissected the Ngioweb botnet—first observed in 2017—which uses a loader network and roughly 15 n-day exploits to deploy malware that contacts C2 domains generated via a domain generation algorithm (augmented by DNS TXT records to resist sinkholing), evaluates device traffic capacity, and links compromised Zyxel, Reolink, Alpha Technologies and, increasingly, Netgear routers (now 10 % of bots) to over 180 “backconnect” C2 nodes that provide at least 80 % of the 35,000 residential proxies in the NSOCKS[.]net service across 180 countries; NSOCKS’s lack of authentication and appearance on free proxy lists has enabled cybercriminals to carry out DDoS amplification, credential stuffing, phishing and malware proxying (e.g., Agent Tesla), while APT28 state-sponsored actors have mixed espionage with criminal traffic on the same infrastructure. To disrupt both operations, Lumen, alongside The ShadowServer Foundation and other partners, is actively blocking traffic to known C2 nodes and publishing indicators of compromise to help organizations identify and remediate infected devices.
hits.title: Botnet fueling residential proxies disrupted in cybercrime crackdown

The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows.
