retrieved_context.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.
retrieved_context.title: Follina Exploited by State-Sponsored Hackers | Threatpost

retrieved_context.text: After a year-long investigation researchers at Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs dissected the Ngioweb botnet—first observed in 2017—which uses a loader network and roughly 15 n-day exploits to deploy malware that contacts C2 domains generated via a domain generation algorithm (augmented by DNS TXT records to resist sinkholing), evaluates device traffic capacity, and links compromised Zyxel, Reolink, Alpha Technologies and, increasingly, Netgear routers (now 10 % of bots) to over 180 “backconnect” C2 nodes that provide at least 80 % of the 35,000 residential proxies in the NSOCKS[.]net service across 180 countries; NSOCKS’s lack of authentication and appearance on free proxy lists has enabled cybercriminals to carry out DDoS amplification, credential stuffing, phishing and malware proxying (e.g., Agent Tesla), while APT28 state-sponsored actors have mixed espionage with criminal traffic on the same infrastructure. To disrupt both operations, Lumen, alongside The ShadowServer Foundation and other partners, is actively blocking traffic to known C2 nodes and publishing indicators of compromise to help organizations identify and remediate infected devices.
retrieved_context.title: Botnet fueling residential proxies disrupted in cybercrime crackdown

hits.text: Secret Blizzard, attributed to Russia’s FSB and active for over seven years, has escalated state-level espionage by hijacking the infrastructure and tools of at least six threat actors—most notably Pakistan’s Storm-0156 (aka SideCopy/APT36)—to target Windows environments in ministries of foreign affairs, embassies and defense departments worldwide. Since November 2022, it has abused Storm-0156’s CrimsonRAT and Arsenal toolsets via DLL-sideloading to deploy its own backdoors TwoDash, MiniPocket, TinyTurla variant and Statuezy clipboard monitor, redirecting C2 traffic to its infrastructure. In October 2023 it added the Golang-based Wainscot backdoor alongside a Linux variant, enabling command execution, file transfer, screenshots and keylogging. The campaign has successfully exfiltrated politically sensitive data from Afghan and Indian government networks, highlighting the need for vigilant C2 traffic analysis, DLL integrity checks and behavioral detection of novel payloads.
hits.title: Secret Blizzard Hackers Attack Windows Infrastructure Using Multiple Hacking Tools

canonical_entities: Palo Alto Networks NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention
hits.text: Since its debut in 2017 as an advanced .NET second-stage backdoor, Kazuar—attributed to Russian FSB–linked Pensive Ursa (Turla)—reemerged in July 2023 targeting Ukraine’s defense sector alongside a new Capibar first-stage loader, marking its first wild appearance since late 2020. This upgraded variant features extensive stealth and anti-analysis countermeasures—fake 2008 compilation timestamps, custom multi-layer string encryption, assembly-location checks and GUID-based pseudorandom directory and mutex generation—and boasts 45 C2-driven commands for comprehensive system profiling, data collection and credential theft from cloud platforms, source control and Signal. It supports six injection modes (inject, zombify, combined, remote, single and non-interactive), a multithreaded architecture for asynchronous task execution, and a hybrid AES–RSA encryption scheme for task/result files, complicating forensic recovery. Organizations can detect and block Kazuar with Palo Alto Networks NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention, Cortex XDR/XSIAM and WildFire, and engage Unit 42 Incident Response teams for targeted hunting and mitigation guidance.
hits.title: Over the Kazuar’s Nest: Cracking Down on a Freshly Hatched Backdoor Used by Pensive Ursa (Aka Turla)

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates
hits.text: Unit 42 has observed a sharp rise in post-intrusion WastedLocker ransomware attacks by the Evil Corp group—already known for Dridex—against large U.S. organizations in sectors from manufacturing to legal services, with initial compromise typically via ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates that deploy a SocGholish JavaScript loader to profile systems and invoke PowerShell-based Cobalt Strike payloads; attackers then leverage WMI and PsExec for lateral movement, identify high-value and backup systems, elevate privileges, disable Windows Defender, delete shadow copies, install WastedLocker as a service, and encrypt files using a “.<victim_name>wasted” extension while appending ransom notes (“.<victim_name>wasted_info”) with contact addresses on ProtonMail, Airmail and others. Palo Alto Networks’ WildFire, Cortex XDR (anti-ransomware and behavioral threat protection), NGFW DNS signatures and AutoFocus tagging detect and prevent WastedLocker activity; organizations are urged to implement robust, off-site backup strategies and hardened cybersecurity controls to mitigate this high-impact targeted ransomware threat.
hits.title: Threat Assessment: WastedLocker Ransomware

hits.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. More recently, the group shifted to adversary-in-the-middle spear-phishing using a typosquatted “micsrosoftonline[.]com” domain and an Evilginx-based phishing page delivered through malicious QR codes in forged European Defense and Security Summit PDF invitations, automating bulk data collection via Exchange, Microsoft Graph and Teams web client. Overlaps with Forest Blizzard, Midnight Blizzard and Secret Blizzard indicate coordinated Russian strategic espionage, and a September 2024 pass-the-cookie breach of a Dutch police account underscores their evolving cookie-theft capabilities—highlighting urgent needs for phishing-resistant MFA and hardened Entra ID configurations.
hits.title: Russian Hackers Breach 20+ NGOs Using Evilginx Phishing via Fake Microsoft Entra Pages

hits.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
hits.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

hits.text: Since at least 2004, Russian FSB-linked threat group Turla (aka Pensive Ursa, Snake, Uroburos) has orchestrated stealthy, globally distributed espionage campaigns against government, military, research and critical infrastructure victims in over 45 countries—most recently targeting Ukraine’s defense sector—using an evolving arsenal assessed in the 2023 MITRE ATT&CK evaluation that ranges from the legacy Snake backdoor (2003) with P2P C2, kernel-level stealth and VM driver privilege escalation; ComRAT/Agent.btz (2007); the Crutch backdoor (2015) leveraging DLL hijacking and Dropbox for C2; the Kopiluwak JavaScript downloader (2016) deployed via multilayered droppers and scheduled tasks for reconnaissance; modular .NET backdoors Kazuar (2017) and QUIETCANARY/Tunnus (2017) with remote plugin loading and RC4-encrypted C2; to the recent Capibar/GAMEDAY MOF-based backdoor (2022) on Exchange servers—and their techniques for persistence, reconnaissance and data exfiltration are effectively detected and blocked by Palo Alto Networks’ Cortex XDR, Advanced URL Filtering, DNS Security and WildFire through behavioral and exploit protection across all stages of the attack lifecycle.
hits.title: Threat Group Assessment: Turla (aka Pensive Ursa)

canonical_entities: Palo Alto Networks NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention
hits.text: Unit 42 researchers have uncovered a new, substantially upgraded variant of the Kazuar .NET backdoor—previously observed in 2017 as a second-stage payload by Russian Federal Security Service–linked Pensive Ursa (Turla/Uroburos)—that re-emerged in July 2023 targeting Ukrainian defense organizations via a multi-stage Capibar loader to steal Signal messages, cloud and source-control credentials and other high-value data. This variant adds robust anti-analysis checks (Assembly.Location byte-array loader validation, faked 2008 compilation timestamps), extensive string encryption (multiple custom and ConfuserEx ciphers), hybrid AES payload encryption with RSA-encrypted IV/key plus HMAC-MD5 integrity, and obfuscation of IOCs. It supports 45 discrete commands for system profiling, credential theft and automated task workflows in a multithreaded solver component that writes AES- and RSA-protected result files. Kazuar also implements multiple injection modes (inject, browser- and svchost.exe-centric zombify, combined fallback, remote proxy, single and headless) and uses GUID-derived pseudorandom directories and mutexes to evade detection, while hard-coded agent and build identifiers enable variant tracking. Code overlap with Sunburst underscores its sophistication. Unit 42 has released detailed IOCs, artifacts and a GitHub appendix, and recommends Palo Alto Networks NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention, Cortex XDR, XSIAM, Advanced WildFire and Unit 42 incident response engagement to detect, hunt and mitigate this persistent threat.
hits.title: Over the Kazuar’s Nest: Cracking Down on a Freshly Hatched Backdoor Used by Pensive Ursa (Aka Turla)

retrieved_context.text: Since its debut in 2017 as an advanced .NET second-stage backdoor, Kazuar—attributed to Russian FSB–linked Pensive Ursa (Turla)—reemerged in July 2023 targeting Ukraine’s defense sector alongside a new Capibar first-stage loader, marking its first wild appearance since late 2020. hits.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.
hits.title: Follina Exploited by State-Sponsored Hackers | Threatpost

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: After a year-long investigation researchers at Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs dissected the Ngioweb botnet—first observed in 2017—which uses a loader network and roughly 15 n-day exploits to deploy malware that contacts C2 domains generated via a domain generation algorithm (augmented by DNS TXT records to resist sinkholing), evaluates device traffic capacity, and links compromised Zyxel, Reolink, Alpha Technologies and, increasingly, Netgear routers (now 10 % of bots) to over 180 “backconnect” C2 nodes that provide at least 80 % of the 35,000 residential proxies in the NSOCKS[.]net service across 180 countries; NSOCKS’s lack of authentication and appearance on free proxy lists has enabled cybercriminals to carry out DDoS amplification, credential stuffing, phishing and malware proxying (e.g., Agent Tesla), while APT28 state-sponsored actors have mixed espionage with criminal traffic on the same infrastructure. To disrupt both operations, Lumen, alongside The ShadowServer Foundation and other partners, is actively blocking traffic to known C2 nodes and publishing indicators of compromise to help organizations identify and remediate infected devices.

retrieved_context.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
retrieved_context.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.
retrieved_context.title: Follina Exploited by State-Sponsored Hackers | Threatpost

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
retrieved_context.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: After a year-long investigation researchers at Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs dissected the Ngioweb botnet—first observed in 2017—which uses a loader network and roughly 15 n-day exploits to deploy malware that contacts C2 domains generated via a domain generation algorithm (augmented by DNS TXT records to resist sinkholing), evaluates device traffic capacity, and links compromised Zyxel, Reolink, Alpha Technologies and, increasingly, Netgear routers (now 10 % of bots) to over 180 “backconnect” C2 nodes that provide at least 80 % of the 35,000 residential proxies in the NSOCKS[.]net service across 180 countries; NSOCKS’s lack of authentication and appearance on free proxy lists has enabled cybercriminals to carry out DDoS amplification, credential stuffing, phishing and malware proxying (e.g., Agent Tesla), while APT28 state-sponsored actors have mixed espionage with criminal traffic on the same infrastructure. To disrupt both operations, Lumen, alongside The ShadowServer Foundation and other partners, is actively blocking traffic to known C2 nodes and publishing indicators of compromise to help organizations identify and remediate infected devices.
retrieved_context.title: Botnet fueling residential proxies disrupted in cybercrime crackdown

retrieved_context.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. More recently, the group shifted to adversary-in-the-middle spear-phishing using a typosquatted “micsrosoftonline[.]com” domain and an Evilginx-based phishing page delivered through malicious QR codes in forged European Defense and Security Summit PDF invitations, automating bulk data collection via Exchange, Microsoft Graph and Teams web client. Overlaps with Forest Blizzard, Midnight Blizzard and Secret Blizzard indicate coordinated Russian strategic espionage, and a September 2024 pass-the-cookie breach of a Dutch police account underscores their evolving cookie-theft capabilities—highlighting urgent needs for phishing-resistant MFA and hardened Entra ID configurations.
retrieved_context.title: Russian Hackers Breach 20+ NGOs Using Evilginx Phishing via Fake Microsoft Entra Pages

canonical_entities: government bodies in Taiwan and Thailand
hits.text: On March 5, 2025, the US Department of Justice unsealed an indictment implicating Chinese contractor I-SOON’s FishMonger APT team in Operation FishMedley, a 2022 global espionage campaign that compromised seven high-value targets—government bodies in Taiwan and Thailand, a Hungarian Catholic organization, a Turkish entity, a US-based Catholic charity and NGO, and a French think tank—using privileged domain credentials to deploy implants such as the ScatterBee-packed ShadowPad backdoor (configured with campaign code 2203 and C2 at api.googleauthenticatoronline[.]com:443), the Spyder loader (delivered via malicious .doc, AES-CBC-decoded with hardcoded key F4E4C69EDEE09E820000000000000000, injected into task.exe with C2 at 61.238.103[.]165), and SodaMaster loaders side-loaded via legitimate DLLs decrypting payloads from debug.png or libvlc.dll, supported by Impacket-enabled lateral movement, LSASS and registry hive dumps via comsvcs.dll, and Cobalt Strike, SprySOCKS and BIOPASS RAT, underscoring the need for vigilant monitoring of living-off-the-land binaries, anomalous HTTP downloads, DLL side-loading and high-privilege account usage.
hits.title: Operation FishMedley targeting governments, NGOs, and think tanks

canonical_entities: Sichuan Juxinhe Network Technology Co. Ltd.
Beijing Huanyu Tianqiong Information Technology Co.
Sichuan Zhixin Ruijie Network Technology Co. Ltd.
hits.text: Since at least 2021, the Chinese state-linked APT group Salt Typhoon—supported by Sichuan Juxinhe Network Technology Co. Ltd., Beijing Huanyu Tianqiong Information Technology Co., and Sichuan Zhixin Ruijie Network Technology Co. Ltd., which supply cyber products and services to China’s Ministry of State Security and PLA—has conducted global cyber-espionage against government, telecommunications, transportation, lodging and military networks, notably breaching U.S. carriers (AT&T, Verizon, Lumen) to exfiltrate text messages, voicemails and law-enforcement wiretaps, infiltrating U.S. and Canadian telcos via unpatched Cisco IOS XE vulnerabilities to establish GRE tunnels and steal configurations, and executing a nine-month 2024 compromise of a U.S. Army National Guard network to harvest admin credentials and config files. Their primary tactic exploits widely known, fixed edge-device flaws—CVE-2024-21887 (Ivanti Connect Secure command injection), CVE-2024-3400 (Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect RCE), CVE-2023-20273 & CVE-2023-20198 (Cisco IOS XE auth bypass/privilege escalation) and CVE-2018-0171 (Cisco Smart Install RCE)—to gain router access, modify ACLs, enable SSH on nonstandard ports, deploy GRE/IPsec tunnels, abuse Cisco Guest Shell for persistence, capture TACACS+ traffic, and deploy custom Golang SFTP tools (“cmd1,” “cmd3,” “new2,” “sft”). A 13-nation advisory warns that compromised edge devices and trusted provider interconnects facilitate lateral movement into core targets. Recommended mitigations include urgent patching, device hardening, configuration monitoring, disabling unused services (Cisco Smart Install/Guest Shell), restricting management interfaces to secure networks, enforcing SSHv2/SNMPv3 and proactively hunting for known-vulnerability exploitation to thwart further espionage.

canonical_entities: exfiltrating sensitive diplomatic and policy-related data
hits.text: Since at least 2021, the Chinese state-linked APT group FishMonger—operating under the I-SOON umbrella—has waged sophisticated espionage against government institutions and NGOs in Southeast Asia and Europe, initiating attacks via spear-phishing emails that deliver template-injected Microsoft Office documents to exploit vulnerabilities or employ social engineering and deploy a Spyder loader, then install the custom “SilentBreeze” backdoor. SilentBreeze establishes persistence through a scheduled PowerShell task using a Mozilla-style User-Agent header to download additional payloads from hxxps://cdn-storage.cloud-service.site/updates.php, communicates with command-and-control servers over encrypted channels via compromised third-party proxies, and remains undetected for months while harvesting credentials and exfiltrating sensitive diplomatic and policy-related data aligned with Chinese strategic interests in the South China Sea and human rights monitoring. ESET researchers note FishMonger’s continual toolset modifications and counter-detection tactics, distinctive network traffic patterns, and reliance on third-party proxies to mask true C2 infrastructure, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to harden phishing defenses, monitor for template injection in Office files, audit scheduled PowerShell tasks, and scrutinize outbound connections to anomalous cloud-service URLs to disrupt this persistent threat.
hits.title: Chinese FishMonger APT Operated by I‑SOON Attacking Government Entities & NGOs

hits.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
hits.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

hits.text: Since mid-November 2024, Russian nation-state actor Star Blizzard has significantly escalated its evasion tradecraft following public exposure by Microsoft Threat Intelligence: shifting from a single registrar (NameCheap) to multiple registrars (Hostinger, RealTime Register, GMO Internet) and implementing multi-stage redirection chains—embedding Microsoft 365 Safe Links in PDF lures that pass through Bitly and Cuttly shortened URLs and legitimate open-redirect sites (e.g., mechengsys[.]net) before landing on an Evilginx-equipped VPS (vidmemax[.]com)—to mount AiTM spear-phishing campaigns that harvest email credentials, including MFA tokens. Between July and August 2024 they also experimented with altered OneDrive file-share notifications—using ProtonMail accounts to spoof trusted senders and rewire the “Open” button URL to their Evilginx infrastructure—targeting individuals in politics, diplomacy, NGOs and think tanks. In October 2024, Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit disrupted core infrastructure, and ongoing collaboration with UK NCSC, NSA and FBI ensures rapid customer notification and defenses. Historically, since 2022 Star Blizzard has iteratively refined detection evasion—employing server-side fingerprinting scripts, HubSpot and MailerLite email platforms to mask domains, DNS obfuscation, password-protected PDFs and randomized DGAs—with each ephemeral TTP swiftly modified, underscoring the need for continuous updates to email security controls, link inspection and behavioral detection.
hits.title: Star Blizzard increases sophistication and evasion in ongoing attacks | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security
hits.text: US and UK agencies (CISA, FBI, CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA) issued a joint advisory detailing how the Iranian-backed MuddyWater group—active since at least 2017 and linked to Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security in January 2022—has expanded its arsenal beyond PowGoop, Canopy/Starwhale, Mori and POWERSTATS to include a new Python backdoor dubbed “Small Sieve” and a PowerShell backdoor that encrypts C2 channels; these tools target telecom, defense, local government and oil and gas organizations across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America, maintain persistence via custom string and traffic obfuscation (hex byte-swapping plus an obfuscated Base64 routine) over the Telegram Bot API via HTTPS, and facilitate lateral movement and data exfiltration, underscoring the need for defenders to monitor anomalous Telegram API calls, obfuscated Base64 traffic and encrypted PowerShell sessions.
hits.title: US and UK expose new malware used by MuddyWater hackers

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
hits.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

hits.text: McAfee researchers at RSA Conference 2019 revealed that Operation Sharpshooter—a previously disclosed December 2018 espionage campaign first observed via October 25 weaponized macro-laden Dropbox documents—actually began as early as September 2017, using embedded shellcode in Microsoft Word to deploy a modular, in-memory second-stage implant dubbed “Rising Sun.” Rising Sun, which reuses source code from the Lazarus Group’s Duuzer backdoor, performs reconnaissance, encrypts and exfiltrates system data (computer names, IP addresses, native OS details) and communicates with multiple newly identified command-and-control servers. Initially detected in 87 global organizations—50 percent in U.S. defense, nuclear, energy and financial sectors—the ongoing campaign has expanded to target financial services, government and critical infrastructure in Germany, Turkey, the U.K. and the U.S., exhibiting TTP overlaps and code reuse linking it to Lazarus operations. These findings underscore the need for strengthened macro and memory-resident malware defenses, proactive C2 infrastructure takedown efforts and enhanced attribution methodologies.
hits.title: RSAC 2019: New Operation Sharpshooter Data Reveals Higher Complexity, Scope | Threatpost

These findings underscore the need for strengthened macro and memory-resident malware defenses, proactive C2 infrastructure takedown efforts and enhanced attribution methodologies.

hits.text: On March 5, 2025, the US Department of Justice unsealed an indictment implicating Chinese contractor I-SOON’s FishMonger APT team in Operation FishMedley, a 2022 global espionage campaign that compromised seven high-value targets—government bodies in Taiwan and Thailand, a Hungarian Catholic organization, a Turkish entity, a US-based Catholic charity and NGO, and a French think tank—using privileged domain credentials to deploy implants such as the ScatterBee-packed ShadowPad backdoor (configured with campaign code 2203 and C2 at api.googleauthenticatoronline[.]com:443), the Spyder loader (delivered via malicious .doc, AES-CBC-decoded with hardcoded key F4E4C69EDEE09E820000000000000000, injected into task.exe with C2 at 61.238.103[.]165), and SodaMaster loaders side-loaded via legitimate DLLs decrypting payloads from debug.png or libvlc.dll, supported by Impacket-enabled lateral movement, LSASS and registry hive dumps via comsvcs.dll, and Cobalt Strike, SprySOCKS and BIOPASS RAT, underscoring the need for vigilant monitoring of living-off-the-land binaries, anomalous HTTP downloads, DLL side-loading and high-privilege account usage.

hits.text: Since at least 2021, the Chinese state-linked APT group Salt Typhoon—supported by Sichuan Juxinhe Network Technology Co. Ltd., Beijing Huanyu Tianqiong Information Technology Co., and Sichuan Zhixin Ruijie Network Technology Co. Ltd., which supply cyber products and services to China’s Ministry of State Security and PLA—has conducted global cyber-espionage against government, telecommunications, transportation, lodging and military networks, notably breaching U.S. carriers (AT&T, Verizon, Lumen) to exfiltrate text messages, voicemails and law-enforcement wiretaps, infiltrating U.S. and Canadian telcos via unpatched Cisco IOS XE vulnerabilities to establish GRE tunnels and steal configurations, and executing a nine-month 2024 compromise of a U.S. Army National Guard network to harvest admin credentials and config files. Their primary tactic exploits widely known, fixed edge-device flaws—CVE-2024-21887 (Ivanti Connect Secure command injection), CVE-2024-3400 (Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect RCE), CVE-2023-20273 & CVE-2023-20198 (Cisco IOS XE auth bypass/privilege escalation) and CVE-2018-0171 (Cisco Smart Install RCE)—to gain router access, modify ACLs, enable SSH on nonstandard ports, deploy GRE/IPsec tunnels, abuse Cisco Guest Shell for persistence, capture TACACS+ traffic, and deploy custom Golang SFTP tools (“cmd1,” “cmd3,” “new2,” “sft”). A 13-nation advisory warns that compromised edge devices and trusted provider interconnects facilitate lateral movement into core targets. Recommended mitigations include urgent patching, device hardening, configuration monitoring, disabling unused services (Cisco Smart Install/Guest Shell), restricting management interfaces to secure networks, enforcing SSHv2/SNMPv3 and proactively hunting for known-vulnerability exploitation to thwart further espionage.

canonical_entities: exfiltrating sensitive diplomatic and policy-related data
hits.text: Since at least 2021, the Chinese state-linked APT group FishMonger—operating under the I-SOON umbrella—has waged sophisticated espionage against government institutions and NGOs in Southeast Asia and Europe, initiating attacks via spear-phishing emails that deliver template-injected Microsoft Office documents to exploit vulnerabilities or employ social engineering and deploy a Spyder loader, then install the custom “SilentBreeze” backdoor. SilentBreeze establishes persistence through a scheduled PowerShell task using a Mozilla-style User-Agent header to download additional payloads from hxxps://cdn-storage.cloud-service.site/updates.php, communicates with command-and-control servers over encrypted channels via compromised third-party proxies, and remains undetected for months while harvesting credentials and exfiltrating sensitive diplomatic and policy-related data aligned with Chinese strategic interests in the South China Sea and human rights monitoring. ESET researchers note FishMonger’s continual toolset modifications and counter-detection tactics, distinctive network traffic patterns, and reliance on third-party proxies to mask true C2 infrastructure, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to harden phishing defenses, monitor for template injection in Office files, audit scheduled PowerShell tasks, and scrutinize outbound connections to anomalous cloud-service URLs to disrupt this persistent threat.

hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
hits.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

canonical_entities: Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security
hits.text: US and UK agencies (CISA, FBI, CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA) issued a joint advisory detailing how the Iranian-backed MuddyWater group—active since at least 2017 and linked to Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security in January 2022—has expanded its arsenal beyond PowGoop, Canopy/Starwhale, Mori and POWERSTATS to include a new Python backdoor dubbed “Small Sieve” and a PowerShell backdoor that encrypts C2 channels; these tools target telecom, defense, local government and oil and gas organizations across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America, maintain persistence via custom string and traffic obfuscation (hex byte-swapping plus an obfuscated Base64 routine) over the Telegram Bot API via HTTPS, and facilitate lateral movement and data exfiltration, underscoring the need for defenders to monitor anomalous Telegram API calls, obfuscated Base64 traffic and encrypted PowerShell sessions.
hits.title: US and UK expose new malware used by MuddyWater hackers

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since mid-2016, a cyber espionage operation dubbed Magic Hound, attributed to Iranian government–linked actors including COBALT GYPSY and showing overlaps with Rocket Kitten (Operation Saffron Rose/Ajax Security Team/Operation Woolen-Goldfish) and Newscasters (Charming Kitten/NewsBeef), has targeted energy, government and technology organizations in and tied to Saudi Arabia by distributing Word and Excel documents embedding malicious macros that launch PowerShell downloaders and droppers to deploy a custom toolkit—comprising executable and document loaders, IRC bots and the multi-platform Python-based PupyRAT—for full system access and data exfiltration; analysis by Palo Alto Networks and SecureWorks revealed domain and tool reuse with the Shamoon 2 wiper campaign, and bait lures mimicking holiday greetings, job offers and official Ministry of Health and Commerce communications, underscoring the need for enhanced macro-enablement policies, network segmentation and proactive IOC monitoring of associated domains and IRC traffic.
hits.title: Iranian hackers behind the Magic Hound campaign linked to Shamoon

hits.text: Lynx ransomware, a Ransomware-as-a-Service strain first seen in mid-2024 that repurposes INC source code, has targeted finance, architecture and manufacturing organizations—later expanding into energy and APAC retail—via phishing emails that deploy malware to exfiltrate sensitive data for double-extortion (including timed “drip” leaks) before encrypting files with a “.LYNX” extension; Darktrace observed initial lateral movement through SMB enumeration on port 445 and Nmap scans, exploitation of default “admin”/“administrator” credentials via NTLM and Kerberos for privilege escalation, anomalous internal transfers of ~150 GiB over port 3260 and large uploads to wt-prod-euwest1-storm.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com, plus AnyDesk-based remote sessions to aid operator actions, culminating in thousands of encrypted files detected by parallel SMB read/write anomalies and extension appends—Darktrace’s Autonomous Response models, if fully enabled, would automatically block suspicious SMB activity, unusual privileged user behavior and anomalous outbound connections to contain the threat and preserve business continuity.
hits.title: New Threat on the Prowl: Investigating Lynx Ransomware

hits.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.
hits.title: Follina Exploited by State-Sponsored Hackers | Threatpost

hits.text: After a year-long investigation researchers at Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs dissected the Ngioweb botnet—first observed in 2017—which uses a loader network and roughly 15 n-day exploits to deploy malware that contacts C2 domains generated via a domain generation algorithm (augmented by DNS TXT records to resist sinkholing), evaluates device traffic capacity, and links compromised Zyxel, Reolink, Alpha Technologies and, increasingly, Netgear routers (now 10 % of bots) to over 180 “backconnect” C2 nodes that provide at least 80 % of the 35,000 residential proxies in the NSOCKS[.]net service across 180 countries; NSOCKS’s lack of authentication and appearance on free proxy lists has enabled cybercriminals to carry out DDoS amplification, credential stuffing, phishing and malware proxying (e.g., Agent Tesla), while APT28 state-sponsored actors have mixed espionage with criminal traffic on the same infrastructure. To disrupt both operations, Lumen, alongside The ShadowServer Foundation and other partners, is actively blocking traffic to known C2 nodes and publishing indicators of compromise to help organizations identify and remediate infected devices.

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

hits.text: McAfee researchers at RSA Conference 2019 revealed that Operation Sharpshooter—a previously disclosed December 2018 espionage campaign first observed via October 25 weaponized macro-laden Dropbox documents—actually began as early as September 2017, using embedded shellcode in Microsoft Word to deploy a modular, in-memory second-stage implant dubbed “Rising Sun.” Rising Sun, which reuses source code from the Lazarus Group’s Duuzer backdoor, performs reconnaissance, encrypts and exfiltrates system data (computer names, IP addresses, native OS details) and communicates with multiple newly identified command-and-control servers. Initially detected in 87 global organizations—50 percent in U.S. defense, nuclear, energy and financial sectors—the ongoing campaign has expanded to target financial services, government and critical infrastructure in Germany, Turkey, the U.K. and the U.S., exhibiting TTP overlaps and code reuse linking it to Lazarus operations. These findings underscore the need for strengthened macro and memory-resident malware defenses, proactive C2 infrastructure takedown efforts and enhanced attribution methodologies.
hits.title: RSAC 2019: New Operation Sharpshooter Data Reveals Higher Complexity, Scope | Threatpost

canonical_entities: exfiltrating sensitive diplomatic and policy-related data
hits.text: Since at least 2021, the Chinese state-linked APT group FishMonger—operating under the I-SOON umbrella—has waged sophisticated espionage against government institutions and NGOs in Southeast Asia and Europe, initiating attacks via spear-phishing emails that deliver template-injected Microsoft Office documents to exploit vulnerabilities or employ social engineering and deploy a Spyder loader, then install the custom “SilentBreeze” backdoor. SilentBreeze establishes persistence through a scheduled PowerShell task using a Mozilla-style User-Agent header to download additional payloads from hxxps://cdn-storage.cloud-service.site/updates.php, communicates with command-and-control servers over encrypted channels via compromised third-party proxies, and remains undetected for months while harvesting credentials and exfiltrating sensitive diplomatic and policy-related data aligned with Chinese strategic interests in the South China Sea and human rights monitoring. ESET researchers note FishMonger’s continual toolset modifications and counter-detection tactics, distinctive network traffic patterns, and reliance on third-party proxies to mask true C2 infrastructure, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to harden phishing defenses, monitor for template injection in Office files, audit scheduled PowerShell tasks, and scrutinize outbound connections to anomalous cloud-service URLs to disrupt this persistent threat.
hits.title: Chinese FishMonger APT Operated by I‑SOON Attacking Government Entities & NGOs

canonical_entities: government bodies in Taiwan and Thailand
retrieved_context.text: On March 5, 2025, the US Department of Justice unsealed an indictment implicating Chinese contractor I-SOON’s FishMonger APT team in Operation FishMedley, a 2022 global espionage campaign that compromised seven high-value targets—government bodies in Taiwan and Thailand, a Hungarian Catholic organization, a Turkish entity, a US-based Catholic charity and NGO, and a French think tank—using privileged domain credentials to deploy implants such as the ScatterBee-packed ShadowPad backdoor (configured with campaign code 2203 and C2 at api.googleauthenticatoronline[.]com:443), the Spyder loader (delivered via malicious .doc, AES-CBC-decoded with hardcoded key F4E4C69EDEE09E820000000000000000, injected into task.exe with C2 at 61.238.103[.]165), and SodaMaster loaders side-loaded via legitimate DLLs decrypting payloads from debug.png or libvlc.dll, supported by Impacket-enabled lateral movement, LSASS and registry hive dumps via comsvcs.dll, and Cobalt Strike, SprySOCKS and BIOPASS RAT, underscoring the need for vigilant monitoring of living-off-the-land binaries, anomalous HTTP downloads, DLL side-loading and high-privilege account usage.
retrieved_context.title: Operation FishMedley targeting governments, NGOs, and think tanks

canonical_entities: Sichuan Juxinhe Network Technology Co. Ltd.
Beijing Huanyu Tianqiong Information Technology Co.
Sichuan Zhixin Ruijie Network Technology Co. Ltd.
retrieved_context.text: Since at least 2021, the Chinese state-linked APT group Salt Typhoon—supported by Sichuan Juxinhe Network Technology Co. Ltd., Beijing Huanyu Tianqiong Information Technology Co., and Sichuan Zhixin Ruijie Network Technology Co. Ltd., which supply cyber products and services to China’s Ministry of State Security and PLA—has conducted global cyber-espionage against government, telecommunications, transportation, lodging and military networks, notably breaching U.S. carriers (AT&T, Verizon, Lumen) to exfiltrate text messages, voicemails and law-enforcement wiretaps, infiltrating U.S. and Canadian telcos via unpatched Cisco IOS XE vulnerabilities to establish GRE tunnels and steal configurations, and executing a nine-month 2024 compromise of a U.S. Army National Guard network to harvest admin credentials and config files. Their primary tactic exploits widely known, fixed edge-device flaws—CVE-2024-21887 (Ivanti Connect Secure command injection), CVE-2024-3400 (Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect RCE), CVE-2023-20273 & CVE-2023-20198 (Cisco IOS XE auth bypass/privilege escalation) and CVE-2018-0171 (Cisco Smart Install RCE)—to gain router access, modify ACLs, enable SSH on nonstandard ports, deploy GRE/IPsec tunnels, abuse Cisco Guest Shell for persistence, capture TACACS+ traffic, and deploy custom Golang SFTP tools (“cmd1,” “cmd3,” “new2,” “sft”). A 13-nation advisory warns that compromised edge devices and trusted provider interconnects facilitate lateral movement into core targets. Recommended mitigations include urgent patching, device hardening, configuration monitoring, disabling unused services (Cisco Smart Install/Guest Shell), restricting management interfaces to secure networks, enforcing SSHv2/SNMPv3 and proactively hunting for known-vulnerability exploitation to thwart further espionage.
retrieved_context.title: Global Salt Typhoon hacking campaigns linked to Chinese tech firms

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
retrieved_context.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

retrieved_context.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.
retrieved_context.title: Follina Exploited by State-Sponsored Hackers | Threatpost

retrieved_context.text: After a year-long investigation researchers at Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs dissected the Ngioweb botnet—first observed in 2017—which uses a loader network and roughly 15 n-day exploits to deploy malware that contacts C2 domains generated via a domain generation algorithm (augmented by DNS TXT records to resist sinkholing), evaluates device traffic capacity, and links compromised Zyxel, Reolink, Alpha Technologies and, increasingly, Netgear routers (now 10 % of bots) to over 180 “backconnect” C2 nodes that provide at least 80 % of the 35,000 residential proxies in the NSOCKS[.]net service across 180 countries; NSOCKS’s lack of authentication and appearance on free proxy lists has enabled cybercriminals to carry out DDoS amplification, credential stuffing, phishing and malware proxying (e.g., Agent Tesla), while APT28 state-sponsored actors have mixed espionage with criminal traffic on the same infrastructure. To disrupt both operations, Lumen, alongside The ShadowServer Foundation and other partners, is actively blocking traffic to known C2 nodes and publishing indicators of compromise to help organizations identify and remediate infected devices.
retrieved_context.title: Botnet fueling residential proxies disrupted in cybercrime crackdown

canonical_entities: installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry
hits.text: The Lotus Blossom APT (aka Lotus Panda, Billbug, Spring Dragon) has stepped up cyberespionage against APAC government targets by deploying new Sagerunex backdoor variants and abusing Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) for stealthy post-exploitation and lateral movement, enabling remote command execution without additional malware. Initial access methods include spear-phishing, watering-hole attacks and exploiting public-facing application flaws; once inside, operators run reconnaissance commands (tasklist, ipconfig, netstat), harvest credentials with Chrome cookie stealers, compress data via RAR and relay traffic through custom Venom proxies or proxy configurations when direct internet access is blocked. Persistence is achieved by installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry under hijacked service names (tapisrv, swprv) to auto-launch at startup, while command-and-control blends encrypted traffic into legitimate platforms—stolen data uploaded as .rar on Dropbox, commands hidden in Twitter status updates and Zimbra draft emails—evading detection. Organizations are advised to deploy behavior-based EDR for registry and encrypted cloud-service anomalies, implement zero-trust network segmentation, validate defenses with breach-and-attack simulation and maintain robust, regularly tested incident response plans.
hits.title: Lotus Blossom APT Exploits WMI for Post-Exploitation Activities

canonical_entities: military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia
hits.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.

canonical_entities: ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates
hits.text: Unit 42 has observed a sharp rise in post-intrusion WastedLocker ransomware attacks by the Evil Corp group—already known for Dridex—against large U.S. organizations in sectors from manufacturing to legal services, with initial compromise typically via ZIP files masquerading as legitimate updates that deploy a SocGholish JavaScript loader to profile systems and invoke PowerShell-based Cobalt Strike payloads; attackers then leverage WMI and PsExec for lateral movement, identify high-value and backup systems, elevate privileges, disable Windows Defender, delete shadow copies, install WastedLocker as a service, and encrypt files using a “.<victim_name>wasted” extension while appending ransom notes (“.<victim_name>wasted_info”) with contact addresses on ProtonMail, Airmail and others. Palo Alto Networks’ WildFire, Cortex XDR (anti-ransomware and behavioral threat protection), NGFW DNS signatures and AutoFocus tagging detect and prevent WastedLocker activity; organizations are urged to implement robust, off-site backup strategies and hardened cybersecurity controls to mitigate this high-impact targeted ransomware threat.

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: enumerated and deleted Volume Shadow Copies
encrypted recovery folders and user data
hits.text: On May 6, 2021, CISA disclosed that FiveHands ransomware actors exploited a zero-day VPN vulnerability for initial access, then used SoftPerfect Network Scanner for host discovery and PsExec to deploy ServeManager.exe (the NTRUEncrypt-based FiveHands payload) alongside SombRAT RAT, leveraging publicly available tools (RouterScan, grabff, rclone, s3browser) and PowerSploit modules for credential access, persistence, token manipulation, Kerberoasting, and exfiltration; once in place, FiveHands enumerated and deleted Volume Shadow Copies via WMI (T1490, T1047), encrypted recovery folders and user data (T1486), and dropped ransom notes across directories. The campaign caused direct financial losses (ransoms, legal fees, incident response, downtime, reputational harm) and exposed third-party partners. Mitigation hinges on patching/decommissioning unused VPN servers, enforcing MFA on remote and privileged accounts, maintaining up-to-date AV/OS, implementing robust backup and recovery routines, hunting for IoCs, and reinforcing employee training against phishing and malicious attachments.
hits.title: FiveHands Ransomware Overview

hits.text: Security researcher Marc Newlin of SkySafe disclosed CVE-2023-45866, a critical, decade-old keystroke-injection flaw in the Bluetooth host state-machine that exploits an unauthenticated pairing mechanism in the Bluetooth specification to trick macOS (13.3.3), iOS (16.6, even in Lockdown Mode), Android (from 4.2.2 through 14 on devices including Pixel 7/6/4a, Pixel 2, Nexus 5, BLU DASH), and Linux BlueZ stacks (Ubuntu 18.04–23.10) into pairing with a malicious emulated keyboard, enabling remote attackers within Bluetooth range to run a Python-based script, inject arbitrary keystrokes, install apps, forward emails or texts, and execute commands without user confirmation or biometric/password authentication. After informing Apple, Google, Canonical, and the Bluetooth SIG between August and September, patches have been released for Android 11–14 and BlueZ (via GitHub) but Apple has yet to announce a timeline for CVE-2023-42929, proof-of-concept exploit scripts will be published in January, and no active in-the-wild exploitation has been observed to date.
hits.title: Critical Bluetooth Flaw Exposes Android, Apple & Linux Devices to Takeover

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
hits.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek
