retrieved_context.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
retrieved_context.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: enumerated and deleted Volume Shadow Copies
encrypted recovery folders and user data
retrieved_context.text: On May 6, 2021, CISA disclosed that FiveHands ransomware actors exploited a zero-day VPN vulnerability for initial access, then used SoftPerfect Network Scanner for host discovery and PsExec to deploy ServeManager.exe (the NTRUEncrypt-based FiveHands payload) alongside SombRAT RAT, leveraging publicly available tools (RouterScan, grabff, rclone, s3browser) and PowerSploit modules for credential access, persistence, token manipulation, Kerberoasting, and exfiltration; once in place, FiveHands enumerated and deleted Volume Shadow Copies via WMI (T1490, T1047), encrypted recovery folders and user data (T1486), and dropped ransom notes across directories. The campaign caused direct financial losses (ransoms, legal fees, incident response, downtime, reputational harm) and exposed third-party partners. Mitigation hinges on patching/decommissioning unused VPN servers, enforcing MFA on remote and privileged accounts, maintaining up-to-date AV/OS, implementing robust backup and recovery routines, hunting for IoCs, and reinforcing employee training against phishing and malicious attachments.
retrieved_context.title: FiveHands Ransomware Overview

retrieved_context.text: Security researcher Marc Newlin of SkySafe disclosed CVE-2023-45866, a critical, decade-old keystroke-injection flaw in the Bluetooth host state-machine that exploits an unauthenticated pairing mechanism in the Bluetooth specification to trick macOS (13.3.3), iOS (16.6, even in Lockdown Mode), Android (from 4.2.2 through 14 on devices including Pixel 7/6/4a, Pixel 2, Nexus 5, BLU DASH), and Linux BlueZ stacks (Ubuntu 18.04–23.10) into pairing with a malicious emulated keyboard, enabling remote attackers within Bluetooth range to run a Python-based script, inject arbitrary keystrokes, install apps, forward emails or texts, and execute commands without user confirmation or biometric/password authentication. After informing Apple, Google, Canonical, and the Bluetooth SIG between August and September, patches have been released for Android 11–14 and BlueZ (via GitHub) but Apple has yet to announce a timeline for CVE-2023-42929, proof-of-concept exploit scripts will be published in January, and no active in-the-wild exploitation has been observed to date.
retrieved_context.title: Critical Bluetooth Flaw Exposes Android, Apple & Linux Devices to Takeover

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
retrieved_context.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
retrieved_context.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry
hits.text: The Lotus Blossom APT (aka Lotus Panda, Billbug, Spring Dragon) has stepped up cyberespionage against APAC government targets by deploying new Sagerunex backdoor variants and abusing Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) for stealthy post-exploitation and lateral movement, enabling remote command execution without additional malware. Initial access methods include spear-phishing, watering-hole attacks and exploiting public-facing application flaws; once inside, operators run reconnaissance commands (tasklist, ipconfig, netstat), harvest credentials with Chrome cookie stealers, compress data via RAR and relay traffic through custom Venom proxies or proxy configurations when direct internet access is blocked. Persistence is achieved by installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry under hijacked service names (tapisrv, swprv) to auto-launch at startup, while command-and-control blends encrypted traffic into legitimate platforms—stolen data uploaded as .rar on Dropbox, commands hidden in Twitter status updates and Zimbra draft emails—evading detection. Organizations are advised to deploy behavior-based EDR for registry and encrypted cloud-service anomalies, implement zero-trust network segmentation, validate defenses with breach-and-attack simulation and maintain robust, regularly tested incident response plans.
hits.title: Lotus Blossom APT Exploits WMI for Post-Exploitation Activities

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia
hits.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.

hits.text: In August 2025 the FBI issued a public service announcement that FSB-linked Berserk Bear (aka Blue Kraken, Crouching Yeti, Dragonfly, Koala Team) has been exploiting the seven-year-old Cisco IOS/IOS XE Smart Install remote code execution/DoS vulnerability (CVE-2018-0171) to compromise critical infrastructure worldwide. Since Cisco first detected opportunistic attacks in November 2021, the group has collected configuration files from thousands of unpatched devices associated with U.S. critical infrastructure sectors, covertly modified those configs to maintain persistent unauthorized access, and conducted network reconnaissance targeting ICS-related protocols and applications. Cisco Talos reports that the campaign, referred to as Static Tundra, has aggressively hit telecommunications, higher education, and manufacturing networks across North America, Asia, Africa, and Europe, deploying custom SNMP tools and the SYNful Knock firmware implant—originally identified by FireEye in 2015—to evade detection and embed for years. The FBI’s warning underscores the urgent need for organizations to patch CVE-2018-0171, disable Smart Install, and implement comprehensive hardening, as other state-sponsored actors are likely conducting similar network device compromise campaigns.
hits.title: FBI warns of Russian hackers exploiting 7-year-old Cisco flaw

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
hits.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

canonical_entities: LNK files in the Windows Startup folder
HTTP POST exfiltration with Base64 encoding
hits.text: Cisco Talos analysts have uncovered PS1Bot, a sophisticated multi‐stage malware framework active throughout 2025 that leverages malvertising campaigns—delivering SEO‐styled ZIPs like “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”—to drop a JavaScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) which retrieves modular PowerShell and C# components in memory via Invoke-Expression, minimizing disk footprint and evading AV. Once executed, PS1Bot establishes persistence by creating randomly named PS1 scripts in %PROGRAMDATA% and corresponding LNK files in the Windows Startup folder that poll a C2 “/transform” endpoint for obfuscated payloads, using the host’s C: drive serial number to generate unique communication URLs. The framework’s on‐demand modules include information stealers, keyloggers, screen capture tools and advanced crypto wallet extractors that scan for seed-phrase wordlists in multiple languages, compress findings and exfiltrate via HTTP POST with Base64 encoding. Continuous sample updates and code overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet‐linked families suggest shared development resources or actor collaboration, highlighting the need for defenses that detect anomalous PowerShell IEX activity, monitor suspicious JavaScript downloaders and Startup LNK creations, and inspect outbound HTTP traffic for drive‐serial based URLs and wallet data exfiltration.
hits.title: Threat Actors Attacking Windows Systems With New Multi-Stage Malware Framework PS1Bot

hits.text: A zero-day VPN vulnerability provided initial access for a sophisticated threat actor who employed publicly available penetration‐testing and exploitation tools—SoftPerfect Network Scanner for network discovery, PsExec to deploy ServeManager.exe (the FiveHands ransomware variant using lattice-based NTRUEncrypt public key cryptography), and SombRAT for remote information theft—alongside RouterScan, grabff.exe, rclone.exe, and s3browser-9-5-3.exe to harvest credentials and exfiltrate data. Once inside, the attacker leveraged Windows Management Instrumentation (T1047) to enumerate and delete Volume Shadow Copies (Inhibit System Recovery, T1490), encrypted files (including those in recovery folders) for impact (T1486), and dropped ransom notes across directories, demanding payment to restore access. Post-encryption activities align with MITRE techniques such as Access Token Manipulation, Boot or Logon Autostart, PowerShell command and scripting interpreter, Domain Trust Discovery, Process Discovery, Screen Capture, and Kerberoasting. The combined use of FiveHands ransomware and SombRAT RAT resulted in both data theft and destruction of backup artifacts, underscoring the need for proactive patch management, network segmentation, strict credential hygiene, and rapid incident response to mitigate novel lattice-based encryption threats.
hits.title: FiveHands Ransomware Overview

canonical_entities: inject the decoded first-stage shellcode into legitimate processes
hits.text: In September 2024, a Winnti-linked APT began targeting trading and brokerage firms by distributing malicious .scr/.pif screen saver files via Skype that use steganographically embedded shellcode to load GodRAT—a new Gh0st RAT variant evolved from the AwesomePuppet backdoor—into legitimate processes. Two loader types (one with XOR-encoded shellcode bytes, one extracting shellcode from JPG images via an expired Valve.exe/SDL2.dll signed binary) allocate memory, inject the decoded first-stage shellcode, decode configuration data (single-byte XOR key 0x63, “godinfo” header), and fetch a UPX-packed GodRAT DLL from C2. GodRAT launches under a “-Puppet” flag in curl.exe or cmd.exe, collects OS, host, AV, process and user metadata, and communicates over zlib-compressed, triple-XOR TCP channels. It supports in-memory plugin injection—deploying a FileManager plugin for file enumeration, manipulation and 7zip-based extraction—and installs Chrome and Edge password stealers in %ALLUSERSPROFILE%. AsyncRAT serves as a secondary fallback implant. Ongoing detections (12 MD5s across Hong Kong, UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia) through August 12 2025 highlight sustained financial credential theft and long-term C2 persistence.
hits.title: Gh0st RAT-based GodRAT attacks financial organizations

hits.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.

hits.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.

canonical_entities: military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia
hits.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.

hits.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
hits.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: After a year-long investigation researchers at Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs dissected the Ngioweb botnet—first observed in 2017—which uses a loader network and roughly 15 n-day exploits to deploy malware that contacts C2 domains generated via a domain generation algorithm (augmented by DNS TXT records to resist sinkholing), evaluates device traffic capacity, and links compromised Zyxel, Reolink, Alpha Technologies and, increasingly, Netgear routers (now 10 % of bots) to over 180 “backconnect” C2 nodes that provide at least 80 % of the 35,000 residential proxies in the NSOCKS[.]net service across 180 countries; NSOCKS’s lack of authentication and appearance on free proxy lists has enabled cybercriminals to carry out DDoS amplification, credential stuffing, phishing and malware proxying (e.g., Agent Tesla), while APT28 state-sponsored actors have mixed espionage with criminal traffic on the same infrastructure. To disrupt both operations, Lumen, alongside The ShadowServer Foundation and other partners, is actively blocking traffic to known C2 nodes and publishing indicators of compromise to help organizations identify and remediate infected devices.

Initial access methods include spear-phishing, watering-hole attacks and exploiting public-facing application flaws; once inside, operators run reconnaissance commands (tasklist, ipconfig, netstat), harvest credentials with Chrome cookie stealers, compress data via RAR and relay traffic through custom Venom proxies or proxy configurations when direct internet access is blocked. Persistence is achieved by installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry under hijacked service names (tapisrv, swprv) to auto-launch at startup, while command-and-control blends encrypted traffic into legitimate platforms—stolen data uploaded as .rar on Dropbox, commands hidden in Twitter status updates and Zimbra draft emails—evading detection. Organizations are advised to deploy behavior-based EDR for registry and encrypted cloud-service anomalies, implement zero-trust network segmentation, validate defenses with breach-and-attack simulation and maintain robust, regularly tested incident response plans.

hits.text: FIN7 operators in early 2024 hijacked Google Ads campaigns by bidding on finance and retail-related keywords to direct victims to spoofed landing pages, where a multi-stage JavaScript loader delivered a decoy PDF while silently invoking a PowerShell command to download a disguised MSI installer from Azure storage; once executed, the MSI deployed NetSupport RAT, establishing encrypted TCP port 1196 C2 channels to FIN7 servers and enabling credential harvesting via Mimikatz, lateral movement with remote desktop modules and exfiltration of sensitive files—this campaign evaded detection through URL parameter randomization, packed payloads and a domain generation algorithm fallback, compromising at least 37 finance and hospitality organizations; actionable mitigations include blocking malicious ad domains, enforcing browser script-blocking, implementing application allow-listing for installers and tuning EDR to detect anomalous PowerShell strings and unusual outbound C2 traffic.
hits.title: FIN7 Hacker Group Leverages Malicious Google Ads to Deliver NetSupport RAT

hits.text: Silent Push researchers uncovered FIN7’s largest-ever infrastructure, identifying over 4,000 malicious IOFA domains and associated IP addresses used to fuel a global phishing and malware campaign that hit high-profile targets such as the Louvre, Meta and Reuters. Using automated intelligence and Threat Hunting workflows, analysts detected a pattern of newly registered look-alike domains—many leveraging common TLDs and typosquatting—to host spear-phishing landing pages and weaponized Office attachments that deploy custom .NET droppers and Cobalt Strike beacons. Chronologically, the operation began with domain registration, followed by coordinated email blasts spoofing corporate brands, HTTP(S) redirects to phishing kits, and payload delivery that enabled credential harvesting and potential lateral movement. Silent Push’s API-driven Integrations enabled rapid enumeration of IOFA indicators of compromise, brand protection alerts and proactive blocking in customer environments. Actionable insights include ingesting the full list of domains and IPs into SIEM and email security filters, enforcing strict SPF/DKIM/DMARC policies, monitoring DNS query anomalies for new domain registrations, and updating endpoint detection rules to flag the identified .NET loader behaviors.
hits.title: FIN7: Silent Push unearths the largest group of FIN7 domains ever discovered. 4000+ IOFA domains and IPs found. Louvre, Meta, and Reuters targeted in massive global phishing and malware campaigns.

hits.text: Since mid-November 2023 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked financially motivated actors—Storm-0569, Storm-1113, Sangria Tempest and Storm-1674—abusing the ms-appinstaller URI scheme and MSIX file format to distribute signed malicious application packages that bypass SmartScreen and browser warnings and deliver loaders, backdoors and ransomware. In early December Storm-0569 leveraged SEO poisoning and malvertising on spoofed Zoom, Tableau, TeamViewer and AnyDesk download sites to install BATLOADER via App Installer, which in turn dropped Cobalt Strike Beacons, exfiltrated data with Rclone and handed off to Black Basta ransomware; Storm-0569 also sells custom MSI/MSIX landing-page frameworks to other criminals. Storm-1113 has deployed EugenLoader via search ads mimicking Zoom to drop Gozi, RedLine, IcedID, Smoke Loader, NetSupport RAT, SectopRAT or Lumma stealer, acting as both access broker and “malware-as-a-service” provider. Sangria Tempest delivered Storm-1113’s EugenLoader to deploy Carbanak and Gracewire or POWERTRASH scripts loading NetSupport and Gracewire for data theft and extortion. From December Storm-1674 combined Teams-based phishing with malicious installers to deploy SectopRAT or DarkGate, often using Storm-1113’s frameworks. In response Microsoft disabled the ms-appinstaller handler by default, updated App Installer, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, conditional access, user education on URL and publisher validation, Defender SmartScreen, Safe Links and attack surface reduction rules to thwart this human-operated ransomware and data-exfiltration chain.
hits.title: Financially motivated threat actors misusing App Installer | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since at least 2016, financially motivated distributor Storm-0324 (aka DEV-0324, TA543, Sagrid) has operated a highly evasive malware distribution chain—initially using exploit kits and email-based lures referencing invoices or DocuSign/QuickBooks and traffic distribution systems like BlackTDS and Keitaro to evade sandboxes—to deliver first-stage payloads such as Nymaim, Gozi v3, TrickBot, Gootkit, Dridex, IcedID and Sage/GandCrab ransomware; by 2019 it shifted to primarily deploying JSSLoader, which drops variants via JavaScript-embedded DLLs (hosted on SharePoint ZIP archives, Office docs, WSF or VBScript files) exploiting CVE-2023-21715 bypasses and protected-document social engineering, then hands off network access to the ransomware-as-a-service actor Sangria Tempest (ELBRUS/Carbon Spider/FIN7) for ransomware deployment, and in July 2023 began using open-source TeamsPhisher to send phishing lures over Microsoft Teams; defenders can disrupt this chain by leveraging Microsoft 365 Defender/XDR detections (TrojanSpy:MSIL/JSSLoader, Trojan:Win32/{Gootkit, IcedID, Trickbot}), enforcing phishing-resistant auth via Conditional Access, least-privilege and credential hygiene, tightening Teams external collaboration settings and ‘EXTERNAL’ tagging, enabling Safe Links and Zero-hour Auto Purge, applying attack surface reduction rules to block script/executable launches, turning on cloud-delivered protection and auditing, and educating users on social engineering and MFA code safety to significantly limit initial access and downstream ransomware impact.
hits.title: Malware distributor Storm-0324 facilitates ransomware access | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Security researcher Marc Newlin of SkySafe disclosed CVE-2023-45866, a critical, decade-old keystroke-injection flaw in the Bluetooth host state-machine that exploits an unauthenticated pairing mechanism in the Bluetooth specification to trick macOS (13.3.3), iOS (16.6, even in Lockdown Mode), Android (from 4.2.2 through 14 on devices including Pixel 7/6/4a, Pixel 2, Nexus 5, BLU DASH), and Linux BlueZ stacks (Ubuntu 18.04–23.10) into pairing with a malicious emulated keyboard, enabling remote attackers within Bluetooth range to run a Python-based script, inject arbitrary keystrokes, install apps, forward emails or texts, and execute commands without user confirmation or biometric/password authentication. After informing Apple, Google, Canonical, and the Bluetooth SIG between August and September, patches have been released for Android 11–14 and BlueZ (via GitHub) but Apple has yet to announce a timeline for CVE-2023-42929, proof-of-concept exploit scripts will be published in January, and no active in-the-wild exploitation has been observed to date.
hits.title: Critical Bluetooth Flaw Exposes Android, Apple & Linux Devices to Takeover

hits.text: Since at least April 2024 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a Russia-affiliated cyberespionage actor dubbed Void Blizzard (aka LAUNDRY BEAR) conducting high-volume, targeted operations against government, defense, transportation, media, NGO and healthcare organizations—particularly in NATO member states and Ukraine—by leveraging stolen credentials procured via commodity infostealer ecosystems for password spray attacks and Exchange/SharePoint Online access, then automating bulk email and file collection (and in some cases Teams messages) via cloud APIs and tools like AzureHound; in April 2025 the actor evolved to adversary-in-the-middle spear phishing using a typosquatted domain and the open-source Evilginx framework with a malicious QR-coded PDF to harvest Entra authentication data; this widespread success underscores that even unsophisticated TTPs pose major intelligence risks to critical sectors, so organizations should enforce sign-in risk policies and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO/passkeys), centralize identity management with Conditional Access, monitor risky sign-ins and mailbox auditing, apply least-privilege credential hygiene, and promptly rotate credentials after infostealer detections to disrupt Void Blizzard’s operations.
hits.title: New Russia-affiliated actor Void Blizzard targets critical sectors for espionage | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.

retrieved_context.text: FIN7 operators in early 2024 hijacked Google Ads campaigns by bidding on finance and retail-related keywords to direct victims to spoofed landing pages, where a multi-stage JavaScript loader delivered a decoy PDF while silently invoking a PowerShell command to download a disguised MSI installer from Azure storage; once executed, the MSI deployed NetSupport RAT, establishing encrypted TCP port 1196 C2 channels to FIN7 servers and enabling credential harvesting via Mimikatz, lateral movement with remote desktop modules and exfiltration of sensitive files—this campaign evaded detection through URL parameter randomization, packed payloads and a domain generation algorithm fallback, compromising at least 37 finance and hospitality organizations; actionable mitigations include blocking malicious ad domains, enforcing browser script-blocking, implementing application allow-listing for installers and tuning EDR to detect anomalous PowerShell strings and unusual outbound C2 traffic.
retrieved_context.title: FIN7 Hacker Group Leverages Malicious Google Ads to Deliver NetSupport RAT

retrieved_context.text: Silent Push researchers uncovered FIN7’s largest-ever infrastructure, identifying over 4,000 malicious IOFA domains and associated IP addresses used to fuel a global phishing and malware campaign that hit high-profile targets such as the Louvre, Meta and Reuters. Using automated intelligence and Threat Hunting workflows, analysts detected a pattern of newly registered look-alike domains—many leveraging common TLDs and typosquatting—to host spear-phishing landing pages and weaponized Office attachments that deploy custom .NET droppers and Cobalt Strike beacons. Chronologically, the operation began with domain registration, followed by coordinated email blasts spoofing corporate brands, HTTP(S) redirects to phishing kits, and payload delivery that enabled credential harvesting and potential lateral movement. Silent Push’s API-driven Integrations enabled rapid enumeration of IOFA indicators of compromise, brand protection alerts and proactive blocking in customer environments. Actionable insights include ingesting the full list of domains and IPs into SIEM and email security filters, enforcing strict SPF/DKIM/DMARC policies, monitoring DNS query anomalies for new domain registrations, and updating endpoint detection rules to flag the identified .NET loader behaviors.
retrieved_context.title: FIN7: Silent Push unearths the largest group of FIN7 domains ever discovered. 4000+ IOFA domains and IPs found. Louvre, Meta, and Reuters targeted in massive global phishing and malware campaigns.

retrieved_context.text: Since mid-November 2023 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked financially motivated actors—Storm-0569, Storm-1113, Sangria Tempest and Storm-1674—abusing the ms-appinstaller URI scheme and MSIX file format to distribute signed malicious application packages that bypass SmartScreen and browser warnings and deliver loaders, backdoors and ransomware. In early December Storm-0569 leveraged SEO poisoning and malvertising on spoofed Zoom, Tableau, TeamViewer and AnyDesk download sites to install BATLOADER via App Installer, which in turn dropped Cobalt Strike Beacons, exfiltrated data with Rclone and handed off to Black Basta ransomware; Storm-0569 also sells custom MSI/MSIX landing-page frameworks to other criminals. Storm-1113 has deployed EugenLoader via search ads mimicking Zoom to drop Gozi, RedLine, IcedID, Smoke Loader, NetSupport RAT, SectopRAT or Lumma stealer, acting as both access broker and “malware-as-a-service” provider. Sangria Tempest delivered Storm-1113’s EugenLoader to deploy Carbanak and Gracewire or POWERTRASH scripts loading NetSupport and Gracewire for data theft and extortion. From December Storm-1674 combined Teams-based phishing with malicious installers to deploy SectopRAT or DarkGate, often using Storm-1113’s frameworks. In response Microsoft disabled the ms-appinstaller handler by default, updated App Installer, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, conditional access, user education on URL and publisher validation, Defender SmartScreen, Safe Links and attack surface reduction rules to thwart this human-operated ransomware and data-exfiltration chain.
retrieved_context.title: Financially motivated threat actors misusing App Installer | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Since at least 2016, financially motivated distributor Storm-0324 (aka DEV-0324, TA543, Sagrid) has operated a highly evasive malware distribution chain—initially using exploit kits and email-based lures referencing invoices or DocuSign/QuickBooks and traffic distribution systems like BlackTDS and Keitaro to evade sandboxes—to deliver first-stage payloads such as Nymaim, Gozi v3, TrickBot, Gootkit, Dridex, IcedID and Sage/GandCrab ransomware; by 2019 it shifted to primarily deploying JSSLoader, which drops variants via JavaScript-embedded DLLs (hosted on SharePoint ZIP archives, Office docs, WSF or VBScript files) exploiting CVE-2023-21715 bypasses and protected-document social engineering, then hands off network access to the ransomware-as-a-service actor Sangria Tempest (ELBRUS/Carbon Spider/FIN7) for ransomware deployment, and in July 2023 began using open-source TeamsPhisher to send phishing lures over Microsoft Teams; defenders can disrupt this chain by leveraging Microsoft 365 Defender/XDR detections (TrojanSpy:MSIL/JSSLoader, Trojan:Win32/{Gootkit, IcedID, Trickbot}), enforcing phishing-resistant auth via Conditional Access, least-privilege and credential hygiene, tightening Teams external collaboration settings and ‘EXTERNAL’ tagging, enabling Safe Links and Zero-hour Auto Purge, applying attack surface reduction rules to block script/executable launches, turning on cloud-delivered protection and auditing, and educating users on social engineering and MFA code safety to significantly limit initial access and downstream ransomware impact.
retrieved_context.title: Malware distributor Storm-0324 facilitates ransomware access | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: Security researcher Marc Newlin of SkySafe disclosed CVE-2023-45866, a critical, decade-old keystroke-injection flaw in the Bluetooth host state-machine that exploits an unauthenticated pairing mechanism in the Bluetooth specification to trick macOS (13.3.3), iOS (16.6, even in Lockdown Mode), Android (from 4.2.2 through 14 on devices including Pixel 7/6/4a, Pixel 2, Nexus 5, BLU DASH), and Linux BlueZ stacks (Ubuntu 18.04–23.10) into pairing with a malicious emulated keyboard, enabling remote attackers within Bluetooth range to run a Python-based script, inject arbitrary keystrokes, install apps, forward emails or texts, and execute commands without user confirmation or biometric/password authentication. After informing Apple, Google, Canonical, and the Bluetooth SIG between August and September, patches have been released for Android 11–14 and BlueZ (via GitHub) but Apple has yet to announce a timeline for CVE-2023-42929, proof-of-concept exploit scripts will be published in January, and no active in-the-wild exploitation has been observed to date.
retrieved_context.title: Critical Bluetooth Flaw Exposes Android, Apple & Linux Devices to Takeover

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
retrieved_context.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
retrieved_context.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

retrieved_context.text: Since at least April 2024 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a Russia-affiliated cyberespionage actor dubbed Void Blizzard (aka LAUNDRY BEAR) conducting high-volume, targeted operations against government, defense, transportation, media, NGO and healthcare organizations—particularly in NATO member states and Ukraine—by leveraging stolen credentials procured via commodity infostealer ecosystems for password spray attacks and Exchange/SharePoint Online access, then automating bulk email and file collection (and in some cases Teams messages) via cloud APIs and tools like AzureHound; in April 2025 the actor evolved to adversary-in-the-middle spear phishing using a typosquatted domain and the open-source Evilginx framework with a malicious QR-coded PDF to harvest Entra authentication data; this widespread success underscores that even unsophisticated TTPs pose major intelligence risks to critical sectors, so organizations should enforce sign-in risk policies and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO/passkeys), centralize identity management with Conditional Access, monitor risky sign-ins and mailbox auditing, apply least-privilege credential hygiene, and promptly rotate credentials after infostealer detections to disrupt Void Blizzard’s operations.
retrieved_context.title: New Russia-affiliated actor Void Blizzard targets critical sectors for espionage | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
retrieved_context.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns
hits.text: Clop ransomware, a TA505-sponsored RaaS strain appending the “.ClOP” extension, infects entire networks by compromising Active Directory servers and manipulating Group Policy for persistence, then uses phishing-delivered HTML attachments to drop the Get2 loader, which in turn pulls SDBOT, FlawedAmmyy RATs, Cobalt Strike beacons and TinyMet reverse shells for reconnaissance, lateral movement (via SMB exploits), and exfiltration (often using the DEWMODE web shell). Operators employ double and quadruple extortion—threatening to publish or auction stolen data on their Cl0p^_-Leaks site and targeting executives/customers—to coerce ransoms, driving average payments up 43% to $220,298 (median $78,398) in Q1 2021 after FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns against Kiteworks FTA (CVE-2021-27101/02/03/04) and Fortra GoAnywhere MFT, while in 2023 they exploited PaperCut CVE-2023-27350 to deploy Truebot and LockBit/Clop, then MOVEit CVE-2023-24362/CVE-2023-35036 and an unpatched SQL injection flaw to steal data without payloads. Trend Micro detections reveal a May 2023 surge (245 attempts), with top targets in banking, retail and healthcare across Türkiye, Canada, the US and large enterprises worldwide.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Clop | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: Microsoft’s latest joint report with Dutch intelligence exposes a year-long espionage campaign by the Russia-linked APT “Void Blizzard,” which has systematically purchased stolen credentials from infostealer markets to fuel password-spraying attacks against European and North American government and defense contractors—particularly NATO states and Ukraine—before pivoting in recent weeks to adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) spear-phishing via a typo-squatted Microsoft Entra login page and malicious QR code for a sham European defense summit. Leveraging the open-source Evilginx framework, the group captures usernames, passwords and session cookies, then abuses legitimate cloud APIs such as Exchange Online and Microsoft Graph to enumerate mailboxes (including shared folders), automate bulk exfiltration of emails, files and, in some cases, Microsoft Teams chats, and uses AzureHound to harvest Entra ID tenant configurations. Since mid-2024, Void Blizzard’s straightforward playbook—steal credentials, infiltrate Exchange or SharePoint Online, and automate data downloads—has compromised telcos, defense suppliers, digital services providers, healthcare and IT firms, posing an elevated risk of wartime intelligence siphoning for Kremlin military and diplomatic operations.
hits.title: Russian Government Hackers Caught Buying Passwords from Cybercriminals - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Emerging January 2022 and initially attributed to Microsoft’s DEV-0569, the Royal ransomware gang—comprising vetted operators rather than affiliates—has rebranded itself in Tor-hosted README.TXT notes and leaked exfiltrated data via victim-specific negotiation pages, employing malvertising (including Google Ads through the Keitaro TDS), phishing (callback lures impersonating software or food delivery), malicious attachments, and forum/blog links to deliver signed BATLOADER payloads that leverage MSI Custom Actions, Nsudo and PowerShell/batch scripts to disable security controls and install remote-access tools (notably Zoho), then deploy either BlackCat’s encryptor or their own Zeon encryptor with a .Royal extension; since intensifying operations in September 2022, they’ve struck high-profile victims such as Silverstone Circuit and Travis Central Appraisal District, exfiltrating data and demanding $250K–$2M, prompting HC3, CISA and FBI alerts—particularly for healthcare—while continuously innovating defense-evasion and post-compromise techniques; organizations should proactively monitor IOCs, enforce MFA, patch systems, segment networks, restrict macros, audit remote-access deployments and maintain offline backups to mitigate this financially driven threat.
hits.title: Everything You Need to Know About Royal Ransomware

canonical_entities: FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns
retrieved_context.text: Clop ransomware, a TA505-sponsored RaaS strain appending the “.ClOP” extension, infects entire networks by compromising Active Directory servers and manipulating Group Policy for persistence, then uses phishing-delivered HTML attachments to drop the Get2 loader, which in turn pulls SDBOT, FlawedAmmyy RATs, Cobalt Strike beacons and TinyMet reverse shells for reconnaissance, lateral movement (via SMB exploits), and exfiltration (often using the DEWMODE web shell). Operators employ double and quadruple extortion—threatening to publish or auction stolen data on their Cl0p^_-Leaks site and targeting executives/customers—to coerce ransoms, driving average payments up 43% to $220,298 (median $78,398) in Q1 2021 after FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns against Kiteworks FTA (CVE-2021-27101/02/03/04) and Fortra GoAnywhere MFT, while in 2023 they exploited PaperCut CVE-2023-27350 to deploy Truebot and LockBit/Clop, then MOVEit CVE-2023-24362/CVE-2023-35036 and an unpatched SQL injection flaw to steal data without payloads. Trend Micro detections reveal a May 2023 surge (245 attempts), with top targets in banking, retail and healthcare across Türkiye, Canada, the US and large enterprises worldwide.
retrieved_context.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Clop | Trend Micro (US)

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s latest joint report with Dutch intelligence exposes a year-long espionage campaign by the Russia-linked APT “Void Blizzard,” which has systematically purchased stolen credentials from infostealer markets to fuel password-spraying attacks against European and North American government and defense contractors—particularly NATO states and Ukraine—before pivoting in recent weeks to adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) spear-phishing via a typo-squatted Microsoft Entra login page and malicious QR code for a sham European defense summit. Leveraging the open-source Evilginx framework, the group captures usernames, passwords and session cookies, then abuses legitimate cloud APIs such as Exchange Online and Microsoft Graph to enumerate mailboxes (including shared folders), automate bulk exfiltration of emails, files and, in some cases, Microsoft Teams chats, and uses AzureHound to harvest Entra ID tenant configurations. Since mid-2024, Void Blizzard’s straightforward playbook—steal credentials, infiltrate Exchange or SharePoint Online, and automate data downloads—has compromised telcos, defense suppliers, digital services providers, healthcare and IT firms, posing an elevated risk of wartime intelligence siphoning for Kremlin military and diplomatic operations.
retrieved_context.title: Russian Government Hackers Caught Buying Passwords from Cybercriminals - SecurityWeek

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: Emerging January 2022 and initially attributed to Microsoft’s DEV-0569, the Royal ransomware gang—comprising vetted operators rather than affiliates—has rebranded itself in Tor-hosted README.TXT notes and leaked exfiltrated data via victim-specific negotiation pages, employing malvertising (including Google Ads through the Keitaro TDS), phishing (callback lures impersonating software or food delivery), malicious attachments, and forum/blog links to deliver signed BATLOADER payloads that leverage MSI Custom Actions, Nsudo and PowerShell/batch scripts to disable security controls and install remote-access tools (notably Zoho), then deploy either BlackCat’s encryptor or their own Zeon encryptor with a .Royal extension; since intensifying operations in September 2022, they’ve struck high-profile victims such as Silverstone Circuit and Travis Central Appraisal District, exfiltrating data and demanding $250K–$2M, prompting HC3, CISA and FBI alerts—particularly for healthcare—while continuously innovating defense-evasion and post-compromise techniques; organizations should proactively monitor IOCs, enforce MFA, patch systems, segment networks, restrict macros, audit remote-access deployments and maintain offline backups to mitigate this financially driven threat.
retrieved_context.title: Everything You Need to Know About Royal Ransomware

retrieved_context.text: Since at least April 2024 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a Russia-affiliated cyberespionage actor dubbed Void Blizzard (aka LAUNDRY BEAR) conducting high-volume, targeted operations against government, defense, transportation, media, NGO and healthcare organizations—particularly in NATO member states and Ukraine—by leveraging stolen credentials procured via commodity infostealer ecosystems for password spray attacks and Exchange/SharePoint Online access, then automating bulk email and file collection (and in some cases Teams messages) via cloud APIs and tools like AzureHound; in April 2025 the actor evolved to adversary-in-the-middle spear phishing using a typosquatted domain and the open-source Evilginx framework with a malicious QR-coded PDF to harvest Entra authentication data; this widespread success underscores that even unsophisticated TTPs pose major intelligence risks to critical sectors, so organizations should enforce sign-in risk policies and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO/passkeys), centralize identity management with Conditional Access, monitor risky sign-ins and mailbox auditing, apply least-privilege credential hygiene, and promptly rotate credentials after infostealer detections to disrupt Void Blizzard’s operations.
retrieved_context.title: New Russia-affiliated actor Void Blizzard targets critical sectors for espionage | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Silent Push researchers uncovered FIN7’s largest-ever infrastructure, identifying over 4,000 malicious IOFA domains and associated IP addresses used to fuel a global phishing and malware campaign that hit high-profile targets such as the Louvre, Meta and Reuters. Using automated intelligence and Threat Hunting workflows, analysts detected a pattern of newly registered look-alike domains—many leveraging common TLDs and typosquatting—to host spear-phishing landing pages and weaponized Office attachments that deploy custom .NET droppers and Cobalt Strike beacons. Chronologically, the operation began with domain registration, followed by coordinated email blasts spoofing corporate brands, HTTP(S) redirects to phishing kits, and payload delivery that enabled credential harvesting and potential lateral movement. Silent Push’s API-driven Integrations enabled rapid enumeration of IOFA indicators of compromise, brand protection alerts and proactive blocking in customer environments. Actionable insights include ingesting the full list of domains and IPs into SIEM and email security filters, enforcing strict SPF/DKIM/DMARC policies, monitoring DNS query anomalies for new domain registrations, and updating endpoint detection rules to flag the identified .NET loader behaviors.
hits.title: FIN7: Silent Push unearths the largest group of FIN7 domains ever discovered. 4000+ IOFA domains and IPs found. Louvre, Meta, and Reuters targeted in massive global phishing and malware campaigns.

hits.text: FIN7 operators in early 2024 hijacked Google Ads campaigns by bidding on finance and retail-related keywords to direct victims to spoofed landing pages, where a multi-stage JavaScript loader delivered a decoy PDF while silently invoking a PowerShell command to download a disguised MSI installer from Azure storage; once executed, the MSI deployed NetSupport RAT, establishing encrypted TCP port 1196 C2 channels to FIN7 servers and enabling credential harvesting via Mimikatz, lateral movement with remote desktop modules and exfiltration of sensitive files—this campaign evaded detection through URL parameter randomization, packed payloads and a domain generation algorithm fallback, compromising at least 37 finance and hospitality organizations; actionable mitigations include blocking malicious ad domains, enforcing browser script-blocking, implementing application allow-listing for installers and tuning EDR to detect anomalous PowerShell strings and unusual outbound C2 traffic.
hits.title: FIN7 Hacker Group Leverages Malicious Google Ads to Deliver NetSupport RAT

hits.text: Since mid-November 2023 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked financially motivated actors—Storm-0569, Storm-1113, Sangria Tempest and Storm-1674—abusing the ms-appinstaller URI scheme and MSIX file format to distribute signed malicious application packages that bypass SmartScreen and browser warnings and deliver loaders, backdoors and ransomware. In early December Storm-0569 leveraged SEO poisoning and malvertising on spoofed Zoom, Tableau, TeamViewer and AnyDesk download sites to install BATLOADER via App Installer, which in turn dropped Cobalt Strike Beacons, exfiltrated data with Rclone and handed off to Black Basta ransomware; Storm-0569 also sells custom MSI/MSIX landing-page frameworks to other criminals. Storm-1113 has deployed EugenLoader via search ads mimicking Zoom to drop Gozi, RedLine, IcedID, Smoke Loader, NetSupport RAT, SectopRAT or Lumma stealer, acting as both access broker and “malware-as-a-service” provider. Sangria Tempest delivered Storm-1113’s EugenLoader to deploy Carbanak and Gracewire or POWERTRASH scripts loading NetSupport and Gracewire for data theft and extortion. From December Storm-1674 combined Teams-based phishing with malicious installers to deploy SectopRAT or DarkGate, often using Storm-1113’s frameworks. In response Microsoft disabled the ms-appinstaller handler by default, updated App Installer, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, conditional access, user education on URL and publisher validation, Defender SmartScreen, Safe Links and attack surface reduction rules to thwart this human-operated ransomware and data-exfiltration chain.
hits.title: Financially motivated threat actors misusing App Installer | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

hits.text: Proofpoint researchers led by Sherrod DeGrippo have uncovered state-sponsored actors exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), a Microsoft Office remote code execution flaw in the Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) invoked via URL protocol, in phishing campaigns since mid-April targeting U.S. and E.U. government workers; following Shadow Chaser Group’s April 12 discovery and Microsoft’s May patch, adversaries dispatched over 1,000 recruitment-themed emails promising a “20% increase” and urging recipients to open a Word attachment that launches a PowerShell script to detect virtualized environments, perform extensive reconnaissance across browsers, mail clients and file shares, zip collected data for exfiltration, and enable arbitrary code execution with user-level privileges to install malware, manipulate or delete data, and create accounts—activities indicative of a state-aligned nexus that underscore the urgency of rapid patch deployment, user training and network-level MSDT exploit mitigations.
hits.title: Follina Exploited by State-Sponsored Hackers | Threatpost

hits.text: Since at least 2016, financially motivated distributor Storm-0324 (aka DEV-0324, TA543, Sagrid) has operated a highly evasive malware distribution chain—initially using exploit kits and email-based lures referencing invoices or DocuSign/QuickBooks and traffic distribution systems like BlackTDS and Keitaro to evade sandboxes—to deliver first-stage payloads such as Nymaim, Gozi v3, TrickBot, Gootkit, Dridex, IcedID and Sage/GandCrab ransomware; by 2019 it shifted to primarily deploying JSSLoader, which drops variants via JavaScript-embedded DLLs (hosted on SharePoint ZIP archives, Office docs, WSF or VBScript files) exploiting CVE-2023-21715 bypasses and protected-document social engineering, then hands off network access to the ransomware-as-a-service actor Sangria Tempest (ELBRUS/Carbon Spider/FIN7) for ransomware deployment, and in July 2023 began using open-source TeamsPhisher to send phishing lures over Microsoft Teams; defenders can disrupt this chain by leveraging Microsoft 365 Defender/XDR detections (TrojanSpy:MSIL/JSSLoader, Trojan:Win32/{Gootkit, IcedID, Trickbot}), enforcing phishing-resistant auth via Conditional Access, least-privilege and credential hygiene, tightening Teams external collaboration settings and ‘EXTERNAL’ tagging, enabling Safe Links and Zero-hour Auto Purge, applying attack surface reduction rules to block script/executable launches, turning on cloud-delivered protection and auditing, and educating users on social engineering and MFA code safety to significantly limit initial access and downstream ransomware impact.
hits.title: Malware distributor Storm-0324 facilitates ransomware access | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Our GReAT team uncovered Operation ForumTroll—a state-sponsored APT campaign targeting Russian media, academic and government personnel—delivering previously unknown malware via phishing emails masquerading as Primakov Readings invitations containing two malicious links; clicking either on a Windows PC using Chrome or any Chromium-based browser silently triggers a zero-day exploit (CVE-2025-2783), exploiting a logic flaw at the Chrome-Windows interface to bypass the browser’s sandbox and deploy the payload without further user interaction. We promptly reported the vulnerability to Google, which released a patch in Chrome version 134.0.6998.177/178; while the phishing links now redirect to the legitimate forum site and the campaign is dormant, the attackers could reactivate it at any time. To mitigate this espionage threat, organizations should ensure all Chrome instances are updated to at least 134.0.6998.177/.178, deploy robust exploit detection and prevention solutions on internet-connected devices, and maintain vigilant phishing awareness and monitoring.

hits.text: Microsoft released a temporary registry-based workaround in June 2022 to mitigate an actively exploited zero-day RCE (CVE-2022-3019, “Follina”) in the Microsoft Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT), which attackers in Russia, Tibet and Belarus have leveraged since mid-April to execute arbitrary code, install programs, manipulate data or create accounts at the privilege level of the calling application without requiring macros. Researchers from Shadow Chaser Group and Recorded Future traced the flaw to an April 2020 bachelor’s thesis and first spotted it on April 12, with Malwarebytes confirming the issue and a formal report submitted to Microsoft on April 21—though Microsoft initially downplayed the risk until renewed alerts from Japanese vendor Nao Sec and security analyst Kevin Beaumont. The interim fix—deleting the HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\ms-msdt registry key—disables URL-launched troubleshooters but disrupts system utilities and, according to experts, offers limited protection despite Office’s Protected View and Application Guard safeguards. With no official patch yet and all supported Windows and Office 2013–365 editions exposed, including lure campaigns impersonating the Central Tibetan Administration’s “Women Empowerment Desk,” organizations must implement the registry hardening, monitor for exploitation indicators and prepare for a comprehensive security update.

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.

hits.text: During Q2 2025, CrowdStrike Services observed eCrime group SCATTERED SPIDER expand its long-established insurance and retail campaigns to include U.S. airlines, leveraging sophisticated help-desk voice phishing to hijack Microsoft Entra ID, SSO and VDI accounts by accurately answering employee verification questions and resetting passwords and MFA. From compromised accounts the adversary pivoted to SaaS platforms to harvest network diagrams, VPN instructions and credentials before conducting on-premises Active Directory reconnaissance with ADExplorer, ADRecon.ps1 and Get-ADUser, and exploiting VMware vCenter access to spawn unmanaged VMs, attach domain controller disks, dump ntds.dit and install protocol-tunneling tools (Chisel via trycloudflare[.]com, ngrok, MobaXterm, Pinggy, Rsocx, Teleport). They also created transport rules to delete or redirect security alerts and used S3 Browser to enumerate and exfiltrate AWS S3 data. SCATTERED SPIDER’s endgame is ESXi ransomware deployment or double-extortion data leaks. To detect and disrupt these tactics, organizations should ingest high-priority logs—VMware vCenter/ESXi, firewall, DNS and web proxy—into CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM, enable correlation rules and integrate cloud security for rapid identification and response.
