canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
hits.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
hits.text: Since its emergence in 2021 and first detection on Trend Micro telemetry in March 2022, the TargetCompany ransomware group has launched 269 attempted attacks against 250 disclosed Trend customers—predominantly in Asia (notably India and Saudi Arabia)—while avoiding Kazakhstan, Russia, Qatar, and Ukraine, and focusing on manufacturing, retail, and telecommunications; their November 2022–May 2023 leak site lists 20 confirmed victims (mostly small businesses) across the Asia-Pacific, Europe, and Middle East in IT, manufacturing, apparel, and automotive sectors. Initial access vectors include exploitation of CVE-2019-1069 and CVE-2020-0618 RCE flaws, SQL Server xp_cmdshell abuse, and OneNote-based spam campaigns. Execution relies on WMIC-invoked PowerShell scripts to retrieve various payloads (TargetComp ransomware, Remcos backdoor, Negasteal, Snake Keylogger) and, since January 2022, reflective loading of a .NET downloader that decrypts and runs payloads in memory via XOR or inversion. For defense evasion, operators deploy GMER, PCHunter64 (YDArk.exe), Advance Process Termination, KILLAV, and killer.bat to disable AV and security services; discovery is achieved through network scans and Mimikatz credential dumping; lateral movement via RDP-based RCE; C2 evolved from an open Mallox directory to an Nginx-protected server. Impact involves ChaCha20 file encryption with keys generated by Curve25519 and AES-128, file extensions such as .mallox/.exploit/.avast and ransom notes titled “HOW TO RECOVER!!.TXT,” and potential data exfiltration. Their tactics span MITRE techniques T1190, T1059.001, T1047, T1562.001, T1003.001, T1071.001, T1486, and more. The group’s maturation—evidenced by reflective loading and possible RaaS adoption—underscores the urgency for organizations to enforce asset inventories, least-privilege access, prompt patching (or virtual patching), multifactor authentication, sandboxed email defenses, AI/ML-driven detection, regular backups, and continuous red-team testing to thwart this active threat.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: TargetCompany | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: registered variables in the Windows Registry
hits.text: In June 2024, HP’s Threat Research team led by Patrick Schlapfer intercepted a low-grade phishing campaign leveraging HTML smuggling via an AES-encrypted HTML attachment containing JavaScript-embedded decryption logic—a novel twist on typical encrypted archives—which, when decrypted, mimicked a legitimate website but dropped a fully commented, French-language VBScript that registered variables in the Windows Registry, staged a JavaScript payload as a scheduled task, and invoked a PowerShell script to deploy the freely available AsyncRAT infostealer. Schlapfer and co-lead Alex Holland’s analysis, including comparison with generative-AI–produced code, concluded the well-structured, human-readable script was likely authored by gen-AI by a low-skill newcomer benefitting from reduced entry barriers, with no obfuscation or complex infrastructure beyond a single C2 server. This first definitive proof of AI-generated malware in the wild underscores the need for defenders to adapt detection strategies to AI-crafted droppers, monitor anomalous AES-in-JavaScript decryption patterns, and anticipate more sophisticated AI-generated payloads poised to emerge within the next two years, thereby heightening the risk to network and endpoint security.
hits.title: AI-Generated Malware Found in the Wild - SecurityWeek

retrieval_events.query: How has the operational approach of the RansomHub threat actor evolved over time according to the reports?

retrieved_context.text: RansomHub, first reported in February 2024 and linked to the Knight ransomware family, gains initial access through spear-phishing voice scams with convincing American-accent callers and compromised VPN credentials, then leverages PsExec, PowerShell and Python scripts to harvest credentials (Mimikatz, LaZagne, SecretServerSecretStealer), discover remote systems, establish SSH sessions and exploit CVE-2023-27532 in Veeam Backup & Replication to dump database credentials. Operators maintain persistence by creating local administrative accounts and registry run keys, evade defenses with disableAV.bat (BAT.KAPROCHANDLER.A), the STONESTOP binary using the signed POORTRY driver, batch scripts that disable Windows Defender and purge AV registry entries, TDSSKiller, EDR Kill Shifter via BYOVD and IOBit Unlocker, then transfer encryptors via SFTP or an Impacket-based SMB spreader. They also automate vCenter interactions to enable and exploit ESXi SSH, reset host passwords and move laterally, while command and control is managed through Atera, Splashtop, AnyDesk, Ngrok, Screen Connect and Remmina, and data exfiltration is conducted using RClone. The ransomware employs ECDH and AES to encrypt files—appending a 32-byte master public key and requiring a 32-byte passphrase to decrypt its embedded configuration that specifies targeted file types, exclusions and service terminations. Since April 2024, Trend Micro observed at least 338 RansomHub victims across 58 countries—predominantly small educational enterprises in the U.S. and Malaysia—underscoring the need for hardened email defenses, credential monitoring, timely Veeam patching, isolated backups and robust EDR solutions.
retrieved_context.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Ransomhub | Trend Micro (US)

retrieved_context.text: Trend Micro analysts uncovered in December 2023 a new ransomware strain dubbed Kasseika—likely developed by former BlackMatter affiliates or buyers of its source code—that employs a Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) attack by abusing TG Soft’s Martini driver (Martini.sys/viragt64.sys) to disable antivirus and security tools before encryption. Kasseika’s chain begins with credential-harvesting phishing emails for initial access, followed by PsExec-driven execution of malicious .bat scripts that terminate any running Martini.exe, deploy the vulnerable Martini.sys driver (without which the attack halts), and leverage its flaws to kill 991 hard-coded processes. The threat then runs Martini.exe to neutralize defenses, launches its main ransomware binary (smartscreen_protected.exe), encrypts files with ChaCha20 and RSA—appending pseudo-random strings to filenames—drops ransom notes and wallpaper warnings, and erases event logs via wevutil.exe. Victims face a 72-hour deadline to pay 50 BTC (~$2 million) with $500,000 added every 24 hours of delay and must post proof to a private Telegram group within five days; Trend Micro has separately published related IoCs.
retrieved_context.title: Kasseika ransomware uses antivirus driver to kill other antiviruses

canonical_entities: Scanning the Internet for IoT devices with open Telnet/SSH ports
Use of default or weak credentials
Encrypted SOCKS5 tunneling to proxy infrastructure
retrieved_context.text: Researchers have uncovered that since early 2024 a previously undocumented botnet, dubbed Ngioweb, has been systematically scanning the Internet for IoT devices—primarily DVRs, IP cameras and home routers—with open Telnet/SSH ports and default or weak credentials, exploiting known firmware vulnerabilities to deploy a lightweight Go-based loader that establishes encrypted SOCKS5 tunnels back to a resilient NSOCKS residential proxy network of over 150,000 infected nodes. Once a device is compromised, Ngioweb drops a persistent agent that connects to fast-flux C2 domains via HTTPS, retrieves updated encryption keys and proxy configuration, and registers the node for NSOCKS’ tiered subscription service (starting at $25/month), which reportedly generates upwards of $500K in monthly revenue by fueling large-scale credential-stuffing campaigns, ad fraud and DDoS-for-hire operations. The actors behind Ngioweb continually rotate fallback C2 domains, employ encryption and obfuscation to evade signature-based detection, and monitor infection success rates in real time, enabling rapid retooling and expansion. Defenders are urged to enforce strong, unique credentials on all IoT assets, disable unused management interfaces, apply timely firmware updates, implement network segmentation and deploy behavioral analytics or honeypots to detect anomalous outbound proxy traffic.
retrieved_context.title: Ngioweb Botnet Fuels NSOCKS Residential Proxy Network Exploiting IoT Devices

retrieved_context.text: Avast researchers uncovered that North Korea’s Lazarus group leveraged a Windows zero-day privilege escalation flaw in Microsoft’s AppLocker “appid.sys” driver (CVE-2024-21338) to execute a truly fileless kernel attack during 2023 intrusions, sending a proof-of-concept exploit to Microsoft in August and prompting a February 2024 patch and subsequent advisory update once active exploitation was confirmed; by abusing a ubiquitous signed driver rather than importing custom code (BYOVD), Lazarus gained kernel read/write primitives, manipulated kernel objects to deploy an enhanced FudModule rootkit—now capable of evading AhnLab V3, Defender, CrowdStrike Falcon and HitmanPro—and bypassed driver allowlisting, then deployed a new remote access trojan for persistent access, underscoring the need for immediate patching, vigilant driver integrity monitoring and behavior-based detection to thwart stealthy, living-off-the-land attacks.
retrieved_context.title: Windows Zero-Day Exploited by North Korean Hackers in Rootkit Attack - SecurityWeek

attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
retrieved_context.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
retrieved_context.text: Since its emergence in 2021 and first detection on Trend Micro telemetry in March 2022, the TargetCompany ransomware group has launched 269 attempted attacks against 250 disclosed Trend customers—predominantly in Asia (notably India and Saudi Arabia)—while avoiding Kazakhstan, Russia, Qatar, and Ukraine, and focusing on manufacturing, retail, and telecommunications; their November 2022–May 2023 leak site lists 20 confirmed victims (mostly small businesses) across the Asia-Pacific, Europe, and Middle East in IT, manufacturing, apparel, and automotive sectors. Initial access vectors include exploitation of CVE-2019-1069 and CVE-2020-0618 RCE flaws, SQL Server xp_cmdshell abuse, and OneNote-based spam campaigns. Execution relies on WMIC-invoked PowerShell scripts to retrieve various payloads (TargetComp ransomware, Remcos backdoor, Negasteal, Snake Keylogger) and, since January 2022, reflective loading of a .NET downloader that decrypts and runs payloads in memory via XOR or inversion. For defense evasion, operators deploy GMER, PCHunter64 (YDArk.exe), Advance Process Termination, KILLAV, and killer.bat to disable AV and security services; discovery is achieved through network scans and Mimikatz credential dumping; lateral movement via RDP-based RCE; C2 evolved from an open Mallox directory to an Nginx-protected server. Impact involves ChaCha20 file encryption with keys generated by Curve25519 and AES-128, file extensions such as .mallox/.exploit/.avast and ransom notes titled “HOW TO RECOVER!!.TXT,” and potential data exfiltration. Their tactics span MITRE techniques T1190, T1059.001, T1047, T1562.001, T1003.001, T1071.001, T1486, and more. The group’s maturation—evidenced by reflective loading and possible RaaS adoption—underscores the urgency for organizations to enforce asset inventories, least-privilege access, prompt patching (or virtual patching), multifactor authentication, sandboxed email defenses, AI/ML-driven detection, regular backups, and continuous red-team testing to thwart this active threat.
retrieved_context.title: Ransomware Spotlight: TargetCompany | Trend Micro (US)

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
retrieved_context.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
hits.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

hits.text: ESET’s 2024 analysis shows that in the wake of law-enforcement-led Operation Cronos and the collapse of LockBit and BlackCat, RansomHub emerged in February as the dominant RaaS operator—driving a 15 percent rise in leak-site victims even as overall ransomware payments fell 35 percent—and by November had eclipsed LockBit in cumulative victim postings. By tracing unique victim IDs and builder tool fingerprints, researchers linked RansomHub to established gangs Play, Medusa and BianLian and revealed that its multiplatform encryptor (Windows, Linux, ESXi) repurposes Knight source code and is protected by a unique 64-character password per sample. In May, operators added “EDRKillShifter,” a custom EDR killer that abuses at least two publicly known vulnerable drivers and uses password-encrypted shellcode to disable security products, all delivered via RansomHub’s web panel under the same affiliate-specific password model. Affiliates—who keep 90 percent of ransoms and enroll via recommendation, reputation proof or a refundable US $5 000 deposit—negotiate exclusively over Tor, post detailed ransom notes to victims, and benefit from free trial decryptions. Key mitigations include strict driver allow-listing, monitoring for anomalous driver loads, hardening EDR self-protection, blocking known Tor endpoints, and correlating builder requests and password probes to detect emerging RansomHub activity.
hits.title: Shifting the sands of RansomHub’s EDRKillShifter

hits.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.
hits.title: Operation Lotus Blossom: A New Nation-State Cyberthreat?

hits.text: Symantec’s Threat Hunter Team has linked the newly discovered Sidewalk loader backdoor—an evolution of the Crosswalk/Backdoor.Motnug family—to Grayfly (aka GREF/Wicked Panda), a China-linked espionage group active since March 2017 that employs custom backdoors, Trojan.Chattak, Cobalt Strike, web shells and credential-dumpers against telecom, IT, media and finance targets in Taiwan, Vietnam, the US and Mexico; in a recent campaign they exploited public-facing Microsoft Exchange and MySQL servers via commodity and zero-day flaws to execute Base64-encoded PowerShell commands through certutil, install an ASPX web shell in the ClientAccess\ecp directory, deploy Sidewalk via installutil.exe, create persistence with WMIC-launched scheduled tasks, then run a custom Mimikatz variant (SHA256 b3eb783b017da32e33d19670b39eae0b11de8e983891dd4feb873d6e9333608d) to harvest credentials—all within about an hour before ceasing observable activity; three Chengdu 404 executives were indicted in 2020 for attacks on over 100 organizations, highlighting Grayfly’s persistence and underscoring the need to promptly patch Exchange and MySQL servers, monitor anomalous PowerShell and scheduled-task activity, and deploy IOC-based detection to block Sidewalk and related tools.
hits.title: Grayfly: Chinese Threat Actor Uses Newly-discovered Sidewalk Malware | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: Avast researchers uncovered that North Korea’s Lazarus group leveraged a Windows zero-day privilege escalation flaw in Microsoft’s AppLocker “appid.sys” driver (CVE-2024-21338) to execute a truly fileless kernel attack during 2023 intrusions, sending a proof-of-concept exploit to Microsoft in August and prompting a February 2024 patch and subsequent advisory update once active exploitation was confirmed; by abusing a ubiquitous signed driver rather than importing custom code (BYOVD), Lazarus gained kernel read/write primitives, manipulated kernel objects to deploy an enhanced FudModule rootkit—now capable of evading AhnLab V3, Defender, CrowdStrike Falcon and HitmanPro—and bypassed driver allowlisting, then deployed a new remote access trojan for persistent access, underscoring the need for immediate patching, vigilant driver integrity monitoring and behavior-based detection to thwart stealthy, living-off-the-land attacks.
retrieved_context.title: Windows Zero-Day Exploited by North Korean Hackers in Rootkit Attack - SecurityWeek

retrieved_context.text: ESET’s 2024 analysis shows that in the wake of law-enforcement-led Operation Cronos and the collapse of LockBit and BlackCat, RansomHub emerged in February as the dominant RaaS operator—driving a 15 percent rise in leak-site victims even as overall ransomware payments fell 35 percent—and by November had eclipsed LockBit in cumulative victim postings. By tracing unique victim IDs and builder tool fingerprints, researchers linked RansomHub to established gangs Play, Medusa and BianLian and revealed that its multiplatform encryptor (Windows, Linux, ESXi) repurposes Knight source code and is protected by a unique 64-character password per sample. In May, operators added “EDRKillShifter,” a custom EDR killer that abuses at least two publicly known vulnerable drivers and uses password-encrypted shellcode to disable security products, all delivered via RansomHub’s web panel under the same affiliate-specific password model. Affiliates—who keep 90 percent of ransoms and enroll via recommendation, reputation proof or a refundable US $5 000 deposit—negotiate exclusively over Tor, post detailed ransom notes to victims, and benefit from free trial decryptions. Key mitigations include strict driver allow-listing, monitoring for anomalous driver loads, hardening EDR self-protection, blocking known Tor endpoints, and correlating builder requests and password probes to detect emerging RansomHub activity.
retrieved_context.title: Shifting the sands of RansomHub’s EDRKillShifter

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
retrieved_context.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia
retrieved_context.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.
retrieved_context.title: Operation Lotus Blossom: A New Nation-State Cyberthreat?

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
retrieved_context.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

retrieved_context.text: Symantec’s Threat Hunter Team has linked the newly discovered Sidewalk loader backdoor—an evolution of the Crosswalk/Backdoor.Motnug family—to Grayfly (aka GREF/Wicked Panda), a China-linked espionage group active since March 2017 that employs custom backdoors, Trojan.Chattak, Cobalt Strike, web shells and credential-dumpers against telecom, IT, media and finance targets in Taiwan, Vietnam, the US and Mexico; in a recent campaign they exploited public-facing Microsoft Exchange and MySQL servers via commodity and zero-day flaws to execute Base64-encoded PowerShell commands through certutil, install an ASPX web shell in the ClientAccess\ecp directory, deploy Sidewalk via installutil.exe, create persistence with WMIC-launched scheduled tasks, then run a custom Mimikatz variant (SHA256 b3eb783b017da32e33d19670b39eae0b11de8e983891dd4feb873d6e9333608d) to harvest credentials—all within about an hour before ceasing observable activity; three Chengdu 404 executives were indicted in 2020 for attacks on over 100 organizations, highlighting Grayfly’s persistence and underscoring the need to promptly patch Exchange and MySQL servers, monitor anomalous PowerShell and scheduled-task activity, and deploy IOC-based detection to block Sidewalk and related tools.
retrieved_context.title: Grayfly: Chinese Threat Actor Uses Newly-discovered Sidewalk Malware | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Since at least 2017, the Kremlin-sponsored APT group Star Blizzard (aka Seaborgium, BlueCharlie, Callisto Group, Coldriver) has conducted credential-theft and influence campaigns against NATO-aligned NGOs, think tanks, journalists, academic institutions and Ukraine supporters, and despite a Microsoft disruption in August 2022 and ongoing Recorded Future monitoring, its December 2023 upgrade unveiled five new evasion tricks: weaponizing MailerLite and HubSpot email-marketing platforms to provision dedicated subdomains and sender addresses that redirect via URLs into actor-controlled Evilginx infrastructure; embedding links in password-protected PDFs or cloud-hosted files whose passwords are sent alongside to bypass filters; using a DNS provider as a reverse proxy to obscure VPS IPs; deploying server-side JavaScript to thwart automated scans; and employing a more randomized domain generation algorithm—though Namecheap registrations and Let’s Encrypt TLS certificates remain persistent hallmarks. Recent operations have targeted U.S. grants-management portals, UK officials including former MI6 chief Richard Dearlove and MP Stewart McDonald, and employees at U.S. nuclear labs, demonstrating successful credential harvesting and hack-and-leak influence tactics; defenders should monitor for sudden spikes in password-protected document deliveries, anomalies in marketing-platform subdomains and redirect chains, DGA-style naming patterns, and reverse-proxy DNS usage to detect and disrupt future intrusions.
hits.title: Russia's 'Star Blizzard' APT Upgrades Its Stealth, Only to Be Unmasked Again

hits.text: Since January 2021, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has tracked a government-backed North Korean campaign that leverages social engineering via X (formerly Twitter) and encrypted messaging apps to befriend security researchers and deliver malicious files containing at least one unpatched 0-day in a popular software package; upon exploitation the custom shellcode performs anti-virtual-machine checks, captures system data and screenshots, and exfiltrates them to C2 infrastructure (e.g., 23.106.215[.]105, www.blgbeach[.]com), with the latest vulnerability reported and patched on September 12, 2023 (see TAG’s published RCA). In parallel, the actors published a seemingly benign Windows tool called GetSymbol on GitHub (https://github.com/dbgsymbol/) that quietly downloads debugging symbols—and arbitrary code—from attacker domains, requiring full OS reinstalls for compromised hosts. TAG has added malicious sites to Safe Browsing, issued government-backed attacker alerts to targeted Gmail and Workspace users, and urges researchers to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, keep software up to date, and verify system integrity after using third-party tools.
hits.title: Active North Korean campaign targeting security researchers

hits.text: Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has observed a 33% year-over-year increase in government-backed phishing warnings—over 50,000 sent to users so far in 2021—driven in part by a large APT28 (Fancy Bear) campaign and sustained by ongoing operations from Iran-aligned APT35. Since early 2021, APT35 has compromised a UK university website to host a phishing kit targeting Gmail, Yahoo and Hotmail credentials—including second-factor codes—and continues its credential harvesting campaigns against government, academia, journalism and NGOs using hijacked sites and link-shortening redirects. In May 2020 it attempted to distribute spyware disguised as a VPN on Google Play Store (blocked before installation) and has pursued similar Android C2 apps on other platforms. The group also impersonates conference officials (e.g., Munich Security, T20 Italy) to initiate phishing, embedding JavaScript to relay visitor IP, user-agent and locale via Telegram bots—a tactic TAG disrupted by reporting the bots. TAG’s layered defenses include batch-sent warnings, Workspace admin alerts, Safe Browsing domain blocks and urging high-risk users to enable two-factor authentication or enroll in Advanced Protection.
hits.title: Countering threats from Iran

hits.text: Since late 2019, a hack-for-hire group recruited via Russian-language forums has conducted coordinated phishing campaigns against YouTube creators by posing as legitimate companies (e.g., VPNs, antivirus, photo editors, “Covid19 news” software) to deliver non-persistent cookie-theft malware (RedLine, Vidar, Predator The Thief, Nexus Stealer, Azorult, Raccoon, Grand Stealer, Vikro Stealer, Masad, Kantal, Sorano, AdamantiumThief) via fake landing pages on over 1,011 domains and forged social-media pages; upon infection they exfiltrate session cookies for channel hijack and resale ($3–$4,000 USD) or crypto-scam livestreams. In partnership with YouTube, Gmail, Trust & Safety, Cybercrime Investigation and Safe Browsing teams, Google’s Threat Analysis Group reduced related Gmail phishing by 99.6% since May 2021—blocking 1.6 M messages, warning 62 K users, blocking 2.4 K files and restoring ~4 K accounts—while observing a shift to email.cz, seznam.cz, post.cz and aol.com and messaging apps. Protections include heuristic email filters, Safe Browsing blocks, hardened authentication and channel recovery workflows; users are urged to heed Safe Browsing warnings, scan files via antivirus or VirusTotal, enable Enhanced Safe Browsing and enforce 2-Step Verification.
hits.title: Phishing campaign targets YouTube creators with cookie theft malware

hits.text: Google’s TAG disclosed that Charming Kitten (Iranian APT35) has been using a custom .NET Windows tool called HYPERSCRAPE—active since 2020—to siphon inbox data from fewer than two dozen Gmail, Yahoo! and Outlook accounts in Iran by leveraging hijacked or pre-obtained credentials; the tool validates connectivity via hardcoded/Base64-obfuscated C2s (e.g. 136.243.108.14, 173.209.51.54), spoofs an outdated browser UA to force basic HTML view, switches the account language to English, iteratively downloads emails as .eml files while preserving unread status, reverts language settings, deletes Google security alerts, and reports system metadata via HTTP POST without exfiltrating content, with early builds also offering an automated Google Takeout option using pipe communication; TAG re-secured compromised accounts, issued Government-Backed Attacker Warnings and published detection data—including numerous SHA-256 hashes for HYPERSCRAPE binaries and a related Live DLL—to aid defenders, and urges high-risk users to enroll in Google’s Advanced Protection Program and enable Enhanced Safe Browsing.
hits.title: New Iranian APT data extraction tool

hits.text: In Q1 2023, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) found that over 60 percent of Russian state-backed phishing campaigns were aimed at Ukraine, led by FROZENBARENTS (aka Sandworm, GRU Unit 74455), which abused globally compromised EXIM mail servers, SMS-delivered phishing links and fake Windows update payloads deploying the Rhadamanthys stealer, then maintained persistence via webshells and Adminer to exfiltrate data to the CyberArmyofRussia_Reborn Telegram channel across government, defense, energy (notably the Caspian Pipeline Consortium), transport, education and humanitarian sectors while conducting information operations. Simultaneously, FROZENLAKE (APT28) leveraged reflected XSS on Ukrainian government sites to redirect users to phishing domains hosted on free services, with harvested credentials sent to compromised Ubiquiti devices; Belarusian PUSHCHA continued targeted low-volume campaigns against regional webmail providers; and IRA-linked actors deployed coordinated YouTube Shorts and Blogger posts to amplify pro-Wagner, anti-Ukrainian narratives. Financially motivated Cuba ransomware affiliates pivoted to intelligence collection using RomCom malware via ChatGPT/OpenAI-spoofed domains against conference attendees. TAG’s takedowns and Safe Browsing protections, coupled with targeted Gmail alerts, underscore the need for organizations to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, patch mail servers, monitor for unauthorized EXIM access, and guard against reflected XSS and SMS phishing.
hits.title: Ukraine remains Russia’s biggest cyber focus in 2023

hits.text: Since mid-November 2024, Russian nation-state actor Star Blizzard has significantly escalated its evasion tradecraft following public exposure by Microsoft Threat Intelligence: shifting from a single registrar (NameCheap) to multiple registrars (Hostinger, RealTime Register, GMO Internet) and implementing multi-stage redirection chains—embedding Microsoft 365 Safe Links in PDF lures that pass through Bitly and Cuttly shortened URLs and legitimate open-redirect sites (e.g., mechengsys[.]net) before landing on an Evilginx-equipped VPS (vidmemax[.]com)—to mount AiTM spear-phishing campaigns that harvest email credentials, including MFA tokens. Between July and August 2024 they also experimented with altered OneDrive file-share notifications—using ProtonMail accounts to spoof trusted senders and rewire the “Open” button URL to their Evilginx infrastructure—targeting individuals in politics, diplomacy, NGOs and think tanks. In October 2024, Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit disrupted core infrastructure, and ongoing collaboration with UK NCSC, NSA and FBI ensures rapid customer notification and defenses. Historically, since 2022 Star Blizzard has iteratively refined detection evasion—employing server-side fingerprinting scripts, HubSpot and MailerLite email platforms to mask domains, DNS obfuscation, password-protected PDFs and randomized DGAs—with each ephemeral TTP swiftly modified, underscoring the need for continuous updates to email security controls, link inspection and behavioral detection.
hits.title: Star Blizzard increases sophistication and evasion in ongoing attacks | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. More recently, the group shifted to adversary-in-the-middle spear-phishing using a typosquatted “micsrosoftonline[.]com” domain and an Evilginx-based phishing page delivered through malicious QR codes in forged European Defense and Security Summit PDF invitations, automating bulk data collection via Exchange, Microsoft Graph and Teams web client. Overlaps with Forest Blizzard, Midnight Blizzard and Secret Blizzard indicate coordinated Russian strategic espionage, and a September 2024 pass-the-cookie breach of a Dutch police account underscores their evolving cookie-theft capabilities—highlighting urgent needs for phishing-resistant MFA and hardened Entra ID configurations.
hits.title: Russian Hackers Breach 20+ NGOs Using Evilginx Phishing via Fake Microsoft Entra Pages

hits.text: Since at least April 2024 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a Russia-affiliated cyberespionage actor dubbed Void Blizzard (aka LAUNDRY BEAR) conducting high-volume, targeted operations against government, defense, transportation, media, NGO and healthcare organizations—particularly in NATO member states and Ukraine—by leveraging stolen credentials procured via commodity infostealer ecosystems for password spray attacks and Exchange/SharePoint Online access, then automating bulk email and file collection (and in some cases Teams messages) via cloud APIs and tools like AzureHound; in April 2025 the actor evolved to adversary-in-the-middle spear phishing using a typosquatted domain and the open-source Evilginx framework with a malicious QR-coded PDF to harvest Entra authentication data; this widespread success underscores that even unsophisticated TTPs pose major intelligence risks to critical sectors, so organizations should enforce sign-in risk policies and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO/passkeys), centralize identity management with Conditional Access, monitor risky sign-ins and mailbox auditing, apply least-privilege credential hygiene, and promptly rotate credentials after infostealer detections to disrupt Void Blizzard’s operations.
hits.title: New Russia-affiliated actor Void Blizzard targets critical sectors for espionage | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Government-backed actors have rapidly weaponized CVE-2023-38831, a logic flaw in WinRAR versions prior to 6.23 that abuses Windows ShellExecute’s handling of filenames with embedded spaces to trigger default extension resolution and execute unintended “.cmd” or “.bat” payloads; although RARLabs patched the bug in August 2023, public proof-of-concepts surfaced within hours, enabling multiple APTs and financially motivated groups to launch spear-phishing and drive-by campaigns. TAG observed Russian GRU-linked FROZENBARENTS (aka SANDWORM) in September luring energy sector and financial targets with a faux Ukrainian drone-training PDF that dropped a packed Rhadamanthys infostealer, FROZENLAKE (aka APT28) using a free hosting redirect chain and a decoy Razumkov Centre invite to deploy a BAT-delivered reverse SSH shell and IRONJAW PowerShell stealer, and Chinese-linked ISLANDDREAMS (aka APT40) targeting Papua New Guinea via Dropbox-hosted archives that sideload an XOR-encoded DLL to load a Donut-generated BOXRAT backdoor in-memory. These operations underscore the urgency of immediate patch deployment, throttled n-day mitigation, Google Safe Browsing/Gmail defenses, and ongoing monitoring for exploit indicators to prevent credential theft, unauthorized code execution, and persistent C2 channels.
hits.title: Government-backed actors exploiting WinRAR vulnerability

retrieved_context.title: New Russia-affiliated actor Void Blizzard targets critical sectors for espionage | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Government-backed actors have rapidly weaponized CVE-2023-38831, a logic flaw in WinRAR versions prior to 6.23 that abuses Windows ShellExecute’s handling of filenames with embedded spaces to trigger default extension resolution and execute unintended “.cmd” or “.bat” payloads; although RARLabs patched the bug in August 2023, public proof-of-concepts surfaced within hours, enabling multiple APTs and financially motivated groups to launch spear-phishing and drive-by campaigns. TAG observed Russian GRU-linked FROZENBARENTS (aka SANDWORM) in September luring energy sector and financial targets with a faux Ukrainian drone-training PDF that dropped a packed Rhadamanthys infostealer, FROZENLAKE (aka APT28) using a free hosting redirect chain and a decoy Razumkov Centre invite to deploy a BAT-delivered reverse SSH shell and IRONJAW PowerShell stealer, and Chinese-linked ISLANDDREAMS (aka APT40) targeting Papua New Guinea via Dropbox-hosted archives that sideload an XOR-encoded DLL to load a Donut-generated BOXRAT backdoor in-memory. These operations underscore the urgency of immediate patch deployment, throttled n-day mitigation, Google Safe Browsing/Gmail defenses, and ongoing monitoring for exploit indicators to prevent credential theft, unauthorized code execution, and persistent C2 channels.
retrieved_context.title: Government-backed actors exploiting WinRAR vulnerability

hits.text: Since at least 2017, the Kremlin-sponsored APT group Star Blizzard (aka Seaborgium, BlueCharlie, Callisto Group, Coldriver) has conducted credential-theft and influence campaigns against NATO-aligned NGOs, think tanks, journalists, academic institutions and Ukraine supporters, and despite a Microsoft disruption in August 2022 and ongoing Recorded Future monitoring, its December 2023 upgrade unveiled five new evasion tricks: weaponizing MailerLite and HubSpot email-marketing platforms to provision dedicated subdomains and sender addresses that redirect via URLs into actor-controlled Evilginx infrastructure; embedding links in password-protected PDFs or cloud-hosted files whose passwords are sent alongside to bypass filters; using a DNS provider as a reverse proxy to obscure VPS IPs; deploying server-side JavaScript to thwart automated scans; and employing a more randomized domain generation algorithm—though Namecheap registrations and Let’s Encrypt TLS certificates remain persistent hallmarks. Recent operations have targeted U.S. grants-management portals, UK officials including former MI6 chief Richard Dearlove and MP Stewart McDonald, and employees at U.S. nuclear labs, demonstrating successful credential harvesting and hack-and-leak influence tactics; defenders should monitor for sudden spikes in password-protected document deliveries, anomalies in marketing-platform subdomains and redirect chains, DGA-style naming patterns, and reverse-proxy DNS usage to detect and disrupt future intrusions.
hits.title: Russia's 'Star Blizzard' APT Upgrades Its Stealth, Only to Be Unmasked Again

hits.text: Since January 2021, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has tracked a government-backed North Korean campaign that leverages social engineering via X (formerly Twitter) and encrypted messaging apps to befriend security researchers and deliver malicious files containing at least one unpatched 0-day in a popular software package; upon exploitation the custom shellcode performs anti-virtual-machine checks, captures system data and screenshots, and exfiltrates them to C2 infrastructure (e.g., 23.106.215[.]105, www.blgbeach[.]com), with the latest vulnerability reported and patched on September 12, 2023 (see TAG’s published RCA). In parallel, the actors published a seemingly benign Windows tool called GetSymbol on GitHub (https://github.com/dbgsymbol/) that quietly downloads debugging symbols—and arbitrary code—from attacker domains, requiring full OS reinstalls for compromised hosts. TAG has added malicious sites to Safe Browsing, issued government-backed attacker alerts to targeted Gmail and Workspace users, and urges researchers to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, keep software up to date, and verify system integrity after using third-party tools.
hits.title: Active North Korean campaign targeting security researchers

hits.text: Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has observed a 33% year-over-year increase in government-backed phishing warnings—over 50,000 sent to users so far in 2021—driven in part by a large APT28 (Fancy Bear) campaign and sustained by ongoing operations from Iran-aligned APT35. Since early 2021, APT35 has compromised a UK university website to host a phishing kit targeting Gmail, Yahoo and Hotmail credentials—including second-factor codes—and continues its credential harvesting campaigns against government, academia, journalism and NGOs using hijacked sites and link-shortening redirects. In May 2020 it attempted to distribute spyware disguised as a VPN on Google Play Store (blocked before installation) and has pursued similar Android C2 apps on other platforms. The group also impersonates conference officials (e.g., Munich Security, T20 Italy) to initiate phishing, embedding JavaScript to relay visitor IP, user-agent and locale via Telegram bots—a tactic TAG disrupted by reporting the bots. TAG’s layered defenses include batch-sent warnings, Workspace admin alerts, Safe Browsing domain blocks and urging high-risk users to enable two-factor authentication or enroll in Advanced Protection.
hits.title: Countering threats from Iran

hits.text: Since late 2019, a hack-for-hire group recruited via Russian-language forums has conducted coordinated phishing campaigns against YouTube creators by posing as legitimate companies (e.g., VPNs, antivirus, photo editors, “Covid19 news” software) to deliver non-persistent cookie-theft malware (RedLine, Vidar, Predator The Thief, Nexus Stealer, Azorult, Raccoon, Grand Stealer, Vikro Stealer, Masad, Kantal, Sorano, AdamantiumThief) via fake landing pages on over 1,011 domains and forged social-media pages; upon infection they exfiltrate session cookies for channel hijack and resale ($3–$4,000 USD) or crypto-scam livestreams. In partnership with YouTube, Gmail, Trust & Safety, Cybercrime Investigation and Safe Browsing teams, Google’s Threat Analysis Group reduced related Gmail phishing by 99.6% since May 2021—blocking 1.6 M messages, warning 62 K users, blocking 2.4 K files and restoring ~4 K accounts—while observing a shift to email.cz, seznam.cz, post.cz and aol.com and messaging apps. Protections include heuristic email filters, Safe Browsing blocks, hardened authentication and channel recovery workflows; users are urged to heed Safe Browsing warnings, scan files via antivirus or VirusTotal, enable Enhanced Safe Browsing and enforce 2-Step Verification.
hits.title: Phishing campaign targets YouTube creators with cookie theft malware

hits.text: Google’s TAG disclosed that Charming Kitten (Iranian APT35) has been using a custom .NET Windows tool called HYPERSCRAPE—active since 2020—to siphon inbox data from fewer than two dozen Gmail, Yahoo! and Outlook accounts in Iran by leveraging hijacked or pre-obtained credentials; the tool validates connectivity via hardcoded/Base64-obfuscated C2s (e.g. 136.243.108.14, 173.209.51.54), spoofs an outdated browser UA to force basic HTML view, switches the account language to English, iteratively downloads emails as .eml files while preserving unread status, reverts language settings, deletes Google security alerts, and reports system metadata via HTTP POST without exfiltrating content, with early builds also offering an automated Google Takeout option using pipe communication; TAG re-secured compromised accounts, issued Government-Backed Attacker Warnings and published detection data—including numerous SHA-256 hashes for HYPERSCRAPE binaries and a related Live DLL—to aid defenders, and urges high-risk users to enroll in Google’s Advanced Protection Program and enable Enhanced Safe Browsing.
hits.title: New Iranian APT data extraction tool

hits.text: In Q1 2023, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) found that over 60 percent of Russian state-backed phishing campaigns were aimed at Ukraine, led by FROZENBARENTS (aka Sandworm, GRU Unit 74455), which abused globally compromised EXIM mail servers, SMS-delivered phishing links and fake Windows update payloads deploying the Rhadamanthys stealer, then maintained persistence via webshells and Adminer to exfiltrate data to the CyberArmyofRussia_Reborn Telegram channel across government, defense, energy (notably the Caspian Pipeline Consortium), transport, education and humanitarian sectors while conducting information operations. Simultaneously, FROZENLAKE (APT28) leveraged reflected XSS on Ukrainian government sites to redirect users to phishing domains hosted on free services, with harvested credentials sent to compromised Ubiquiti devices; Belarusian PUSHCHA continued targeted low-volume campaigns against regional webmail providers; and IRA-linked actors deployed coordinated YouTube Shorts and Blogger posts to amplify pro-Wagner, anti-Ukrainian narratives. Financially motivated Cuba ransomware affiliates pivoted to intelligence collection using RomCom malware via ChatGPT/OpenAI-spoofed domains against conference attendees. TAG’s takedowns and Safe Browsing protections, coupled with targeted Gmail alerts, underscore the need for organizations to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, patch mail servers, monitor for unauthorized EXIM access, and guard against reflected XSS and SMS phishing.
hits.title: Ukraine remains Russia’s biggest cyber focus in 2023

hits.text: Since mid-November 2024, Russian nation-state actor Star Blizzard has significantly escalated its evasion tradecraft following public exposure by Microsoft Threat Intelligence: shifting from a single registrar (NameCheap) to multiple registrars (Hostinger, RealTime Register, GMO Internet) and implementing multi-stage redirection chains—embedding Microsoft 365 Safe Links in PDF lures that pass through Bitly and Cuttly shortened URLs and legitimate open-redirect sites (e.g., mechengsys[.]net) before landing on an Evilginx-equipped VPS (vidmemax[.]com)—to mount AiTM spear-phishing campaigns that harvest email credentials, including MFA tokens. Between July and August 2024 they also experimented with altered OneDrive file-share notifications—using ProtonMail accounts to spoof trusted senders and rewire the “Open” button URL to their Evilginx infrastructure—targeting individuals in politics, diplomacy, NGOs and think tanks. In October 2024, Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit disrupted core infrastructure, and ongoing collaboration with UK NCSC, NSA and FBI ensures rapid customer notification and defenses. Historically, since 2022 Star Blizzard has iteratively refined detection evasion—employing server-side fingerprinting scripts, HubSpot and MailerLite email platforms to mask domains, DNS obfuscation, password-protected PDFs and randomized DGAs—with each ephemeral TTP swiftly modified, underscoring the need for continuous updates to email security controls, link inspection and behavioral detection.
hits.title: Star Blizzard increases sophistication and evasion in ongoing attacks | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access.
