canonical_entities: FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns
hits.text: Clop ransomware, a TA505-sponsored RaaS strain appending the “.ClOP” extension, infects entire networks by compromising Active Directory servers and manipulating Group Policy for persistence, then uses phishing-delivered HTML attachments to drop the Get2 loader, which in turn pulls SDBOT, FlawedAmmyy RATs, Cobalt Strike beacons and TinyMet reverse shells for reconnaissance, lateral movement (via SMB exploits), and exfiltration (often using the DEWMODE web shell). Operators employ double and quadruple extortion—threatening to publish or auction stolen data on their Cl0p^_-Leaks site and targeting executives/customers—to coerce ransoms, driving average payments up 43% to $220,298 (median $78,398) in Q1 2021 after FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns against Kiteworks FTA (CVE-2021-27101/02/03/04) and Fortra GoAnywhere MFT, while in 2023 they exploited PaperCut CVE-2023-27350 to deploy Truebot and LockBit/Clop, then MOVEit CVE-2023-24362/CVE-2023-35036 and an unpatched SQL injection flaw to steal data without payloads. Trend Micro detections reveal a May 2023 surge (245 attempts), with top targets in banking, retail and healthcare across Türkiye, Canada, the US and large enterprises worldwide.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Clop | Trend Micro (US)

canonical_entities: RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022
Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
hits.text: Trend Micro’s analysis of RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022 reveals a predominantly human-operated ransomware campaign that hit the manufacturing sector hardest (followed by education and banking) with the highest attack attempts observed in the U.S., France, and Brazil—driven in part by a high-profile 2021 breach of a Taiwanese hardware manufacturer. Initial access is achieved via malspam delivering multi-stage payloads that leverage IcedID and TrickBot for footholds, deploy Cobalt Strike beacons and PyXie RAT for code execution and data exfiltration, use SMB to propagate a VATET loader for lateral movement, and employ Mimikatz and LaZagne for credential harvesting. Upon execution, RansomEXX evades defense by disabling tools (T1562.001), skipping encryption of critical Windows paths, file names, and extensions, and terminating hundreds of business and security processes to maximize impact (T1486, T1490), then encrypts data and demands ransom. Recommended mitigations include strict audit and asset inventory, hardened configurations and least-privilege access, macro and email sandboxing to block malspam entry, regular patching and virtual patching, multifactor authentication, advanced behavior-based detection (e.g., Trend Micro Vision One™), and continuous employee training and red-team testing to disrupt the ransomware kill chain and protect against future RansomEXX intrusions.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: RansomEXX | Trend Micro (US)

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

canonical_entities: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager
hits.text: Water Ouroboros is a Ransomware-as-a-Service operation that exploits public-facing Oracle WebLogic vulnerabilities (CVE-2019-2725, CVE-2017-10271, CVE-2019-2729) or drive-by installers for initial access (T1190, T1189), then executes remote Windows commands (wmic.exe, bcdedit.exe, wbadmin.exe, vssadmin.exe) to delete backups and disable recovery (T1490, T1562.001) before encrypting fixed, removable and network drives via a Go-based custom routine that uses RTLGenRandom to generate a symmetric key, protects it with embedded RSA public keys (App_ExportKey), appends “.locked” (unless suppressed with –E), excludes over 60 file extensions, and accepts credentials (c {user}:{pass}), logging (–a), non-aggressive (–A) and size filters (–m). Victims find Contact Us.txt ransom notes pointing to a TOR payment site and Hive Leaks data-dump threat. Post-infection, actors maintain access via compromised admin accounts (T1078), disable security tools (PCHunter, ProcessHacker), dump credentials from registry hives (T1003.002), move laterally over RDP/SMB (T1021.001/002), discover assets via AdFind (T1595.002) and exfiltrate data over C&C (SharpRhino RAT/T1071.001, T1041). With 136 incidents in the US and notable impacts on construction, IT, manufacturing and healthcare SMBs, the campaign underscores the need for timely patching, hardened public-facing apps, least-privilege access, MFA, robust backups and advanced threat detection.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Water Ouroboros | Trend Micro (US)

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.

retrieved_context.text: Since at least 2016, financially motivated distributor Storm-0324 (aka DEV-0324, TA543, Sagrid) has operated a highly evasive malware distribution chain—initially using exploit kits and email-based lures referencing invoices or DocuSign/QuickBooks and traffic distribution systems like BlackTDS and Keitaro to evade sandboxes—to deliver first-stage payloads such as Nymaim, Gozi v3, TrickBot, Gootkit, Dridex, IcedID and Sage/GandCrab ransomware; by 2019 it shifted to primarily deploying JSSLoader, which drops variants via JavaScript-embedded DLLs (hosted on SharePoint ZIP archives, Office docs, WSF or VBScript files) exploiting CVE-2023-21715 bypasses and protected-document social engineering, then hands off network access to the ransomware-as-a-service actor Sangria Tempest (ELBRUS/Carbon Spider/FIN7) for ransomware deployment, and in July 2023 began using open-source TeamsPhisher to send phishing lures over Microsoft Teams; defenders can disrupt this chain by leveraging Microsoft 365 Defender/XDR detections (TrojanSpy:MSIL/JSSLoader, Trojan:Win32/{Gootkit, IcedID, Trickbot}), enforcing phishing-resistant auth via Conditional Access, least-privilege and credential hygiene, tightening Teams external collaboration settings and ‘EXTERNAL’ tagging, enabling Safe Links and Zero-hour Auto Purge, applying attack surface reduction rules to block script/executable launches, turning on cloud-delivered protection and auditing, and educating users on social engineering and MFA code safety to significantly limit initial access and downstream ransomware impact.
retrieved_context.title: Malware distributor Storm-0324 facilitates ransomware access | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns
retrieved_context.text: Clop ransomware, a TA505-sponsored RaaS strain appending the “.ClOP” extension, infects entire networks by compromising Active Directory servers and manipulating Group Policy for persistence, then uses phishing-delivered HTML attachments to drop the Get2 loader, which in turn pulls SDBOT, FlawedAmmyy RATs, Cobalt Strike beacons and TinyMet reverse shells for reconnaissance, lateral movement (via SMB exploits), and exfiltration (often using the DEWMODE web shell). Operators employ double and quadruple extortion—threatening to publish or auction stolen data on their Cl0p^_-Leaks site and targeting executives/customers—to coerce ransoms, driving average payments up 43% to $220,298 (median $78,398) in Q1 2021 after FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns against Kiteworks FTA (CVE-2021-27101/02/03/04) and Fortra GoAnywhere MFT, while in 2023 they exploited PaperCut CVE-2023-27350 to deploy Truebot and LockBit/Clop, then MOVEit CVE-2023-24362/CVE-2023-35036 and an unpatched SQL injection flaw to steal data without payloads. Trend Micro detections reveal a May 2023 surge (245 attempts), with top targets in banking, retail and healthcare across Türkiye, Canada, the US and large enterprises worldwide.
retrieved_context.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Clop | Trend Micro (US)

canonical_entities: RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022
Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
retrieved_context.text: Trend Micro’s analysis of RansomEXX activity from March 31, 2021 to March 31, 2022 reveals a predominantly human-operated ransomware campaign that hit the manufacturing sector hardest (followed by education and banking) with the highest attack attempts observed in the U.S., France, and Brazil—driven in part by a high-profile 2021 breach of a Taiwanese hardware manufacturer. Initial access is achieved via malspam delivering multi-stage payloads that leverage IcedID and TrickBot for footholds, deploy Cobalt Strike beacons and PyXie RAT for code execution and data exfiltration, use SMB to propagate a VATET loader for lateral movement, and employ Mimikatz and LaZagne for credential harvesting. Upon execution, RansomEXX evades defense by disabling tools (T1562.001), skipping encryption of critical Windows paths, file names, and extensions, and terminating hundreds of business and security processes to maximize impact (T1486, T1490), then encrypts data and demands ransom. Recommended mitigations include strict audit and asset inventory, hardened configurations and least-privilege access, macro and email sandboxing to block malspam entry, regular patching and virtual patching, multifactor authentication, advanced behavior-based detection (e.g., Trend Micro Vision One™), and continuous employee training and red-team testing to disrupt the ransomware kill chain and protect against future RansomEXX intrusions.
retrieved_context.title: Ransomware Spotlight: RansomEXX | Trend Micro (US)

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
retrieved_context.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
retrieved_context.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

canonical_entities: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager
retrieved_context.text: Water Ouroboros is a Ransomware-as-a-Service operation that exploits public-facing Oracle WebLogic vulnerabilities (CVE-2019-2725, CVE-2017-10271, CVE-2019-2729) or drive-by installers for initial access (T1190, T1189), then executes remote Windows commands (wmic.exe, bcdedit.exe, wbadmin.exe, vssadmin.exe) to delete backups and disable recovery (T1490, T1562.001) before encrypting fixed, removable and network drives via a Go-based custom routine that uses RTLGenRandom to generate a symmetric key, protects it with embedded RSA public keys (App_ExportKey), appends “.locked” (unless suppressed with –E), excludes over 60 file extensions, and accepts credentials (c {user}:{pass}), logging (–a), non-aggressive (–A) and size filters (–m). Victims find Contact Us.txt ransom notes pointing to a TOR payment site and Hive Leaks data-dump threat. Post-infection, actors maintain access via compromised admin accounts (T1078), disable security tools (PCHunter, ProcessHacker), dump credentials from registry hives (T1003.002), move laterally over RDP/SMB (T1021.001/002), discover assets via AdFind (T1595.002) and exfiltrate data over C&C (SharpRhino RAT/T1071.001, T1041). With 136 incidents in the US and notable impacts on construction, IT, manufacturing and healthcare SMBs, the campaign underscores the need for timely patching, hardened public-facing apps, least-privilege access, MFA, robust backups and advanced threat detection.

hits.text: In early April, Palo Alto Networks’ Advanced WildFire and Cortex XDR uncovered SnipBot—a new v5.0 iteration of the RomCom RAT family—employing advanced window message–based control-flow obfuscation and anti-sandbox checks (filename hash and HKCU\…\RecentDocs entries) in a multi-stage chain beginning with a PDF-labeled EXE downloader signed using a likely stolen certificate; the downloader contacts xeontime[.]com for config-pdf.dll, which uses registry-based COM hijacking to load keyprov.dll from drvmcprotect[.]com into explorer.exe, decrypts payloads stored in HKCU\Software\AppDataSoft\Software, and opens a TCP listener on port 1342 for commands to update, delete, or execute modules. The main backdoor single.dll (mutex “SnipMutex”) supports 27 encrypted commands for drive and process enumeration, file upload/download, and remote module execution, facilitating network pivoting and targeted file exfiltration. Active since December 2023 (RomCom activity since 2022), SnipBot’s tactics, stolen certificates, unique obfuscation, and sophisticated loader underscore a high-risk threat actor likely focused on intelligence gathering; Palo Alto products classify its samples, URLs, and domains as malicious to prevent compromise.
hits.title: Inside SnipBot: The Latest RomCom Malware Variant

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: ESET researchers uncovered a novel crimeware campaign, active in Czechia since November 2023 and paused only by the arrest of a suspect in March 2024, in which attackers combined social engineering, phishing and Android malware to target clients of three Czech banks via deceptive SMS links to malicious progressive web apps (PWAs) and WebAPKs; after harvesting credentials, the attackers lured victims into installing NGate, a custom Android malware named for its incorporation of the open-source NFCGate tool, which relays NFC data from victims’ unrooted smartphones to an attacker’s rooted device, enabling the emulation of cloned payment cards and unauthorized ATM withdrawals (over 160,000 CZK recovered from just three recent victims, with likely higher overall losses), with a fallback tactic of illicit bank-to-bank transfers when the relay method fails.
hits.title: NGate Android malware relays NFC traffic to steal cash

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

retrieved_context.text: Since at least 2016, financially motivated distributor Storm-0324 (aka DEV-0324, TA543, Sagrid) has operated a highly evasive malware distribution chain—initially using exploit kits and email-based lures referencing invoices or DocuSign/QuickBooks and traffic distribution systems like BlackTDS and Keitaro to evade sandboxes—to deliver first-stage payloads such as Nymaim, Gozi v3, TrickBot, Gootkit, Dridex, IcedID and Sage/GandCrab ransomware; by 2019 it shifted to primarily deploying JSSLoader, which drops variants via JavaScript-embedded DLLs (hosted on SharePoint ZIP archives, Office docs, WSF or VBScript files) exploiting CVE-2023-21715 bypasses and protected-document social engineering, then hands off network access to the ransomware-as-a-service actor Sangria Tempest (ELBRUS/Carbon Spider/FIN7) for ransomware deployment, and in July 2023 began using open-source TeamsPhisher to send phishing lures over Microsoft Teams; defenders can disrupt this chain by leveraging Microsoft 365 Defender/XDR detections (TrojanSpy:MSIL/JSSLoader, Trojan:Win32/{Gootkit, IcedID, Trickbot}), enforcing phishing-resistant auth via Conditional Access, least-privilege and credential hygiene, tightening Teams external collaboration settings and ‘EXTERNAL’ tagging, enabling Safe Links and Zero-hour Auto Purge, applying attack surface reduction rules to block script/executable launches, turning on cloud-delivered protection and auditing, and educating users on social engineering and MFA code safety to significantly limit initial access and downstream ransomware impact.
retrieved_context.title: Malware distributor Storm-0324 facilitates ransomware access | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns
retrieved_context.text: Clop ransomware, a TA505-sponsored RaaS strain appending the “.ClOP” extension, infects entire networks by compromising Active Directory servers and manipulating Group Policy for persistence, then uses phishing-delivered HTML attachments to drop the Get2 loader, which in turn pulls SDBOT, FlawedAmmyy RATs, Cobalt Strike beacons and TinyMet reverse shells for reconnaissance, lateral movement (via SMB exploits), and exfiltration (often using the DEWMODE web shell). Operators employ double and quadruple extortion—threatening to publish or auction stolen data on their Cl0p^_-Leaks site and targeting executives/customers—to coerce ransoms, driving average payments up 43% to $220,298 (median $78,398) in Q1 2021 after FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns against Kiteworks FTA (CVE-2021-27101/02/03/04) and Fortra GoAnywhere MFT, while in 2023 they exploited PaperCut CVE-2023-27350 to deploy Truebot and LockBit/Clop, then MOVEit CVE-2023-24362/CVE-2023-35036 and an unpatched SQL injection flaw to steal data without payloads. Trend Micro detections reveal a May 2023 surge (245 attempts), with top targets in banking, retail and healthcare across Türkiye, Canada, the US and large enterprises worldwide.
retrieved_context.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Clop | Trend Micro (US)

retrieved_context.text: In early April, Palo Alto Networks’ Advanced WildFire and Cortex XDR uncovered SnipBot—a new v5.0 iteration of the RomCom RAT family—employing advanced window message–based control-flow obfuscation and anti-sandbox checks (filename hash and HKCU\…\RecentDocs entries) in a multi-stage chain beginning with a PDF-labeled EXE downloader signed using a likely stolen certificate; the downloader contacts xeontime[.]com for config-pdf.dll, which uses registry-based COM hijacking to load keyprov.dll from drvmcprotect[.]com into explorer.exe, decrypts payloads stored in HKCU\Software\AppDataSoft\Software, and opens a TCP listener on port 1342 for commands to update, delete, or execute modules. The main backdoor single.dll (mutex “SnipMutex”) supports 27 encrypted commands for drive and process enumeration, file upload/download, and remote module execution, facilitating network pivoting and targeted file exfiltration. Active since December 2023 (RomCom activity since 2022), SnipBot’s tactics, stolen certificates, unique obfuscation, and sophisticated loader underscore a high-risk threat actor likely focused on intelligence gathering; Palo Alto products classify its samples, URLs, and domains as malicious to prevent compromise.
retrieved_context.title: Inside SnipBot: The Latest RomCom Malware Variant

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
retrieved_context.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: ESET researchers uncovered a novel crimeware campaign, active in Czechia since November 2023 and paused only by the arrest of a suspect in March 2024, in which attackers combined social engineering, phishing and Android malware to target clients of three Czech banks via deceptive SMS links to malicious progressive web apps (PWAs) and WebAPKs; after harvesting credentials, the attackers lured victims into installing NGate, a custom Android malware named for its incorporation of the open-source NFCGate tool, which relays NFC data from victims’ unrooted smartphones to an attacker’s rooted device, enabling the emulation of cloned payment cards and unauthorized ATM withdrawals (over 160,000 CZK recovered from just three recent victims, with likely higher overall losses), with a fallback tactic of illicit bank-to-bank transfers when the relay method fails.
retrieved_context.title: NGate Android malware relays NFC traffic to steal cash

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
retrieved_context.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: In May 2023, after U.S. authorities secured convictions against three high-level operators and declared the Russia-based cybercrime enterprise Fin7 “no more,” security experts began spotting first signs of its resurrection in April 2024 when Blackberry reported a typosquatting-based malware intrusion against a major automotive firm; since January 2024, Silent Push analyst Zach Edwards has mapped over 4,000 Fin7-linked hosts—rented largely on the pro-Russia Stark Industries Solutions platform—employing typosquatting, booby-trapped ads, malicious browser extensions and spear-phishing domains to mimic hundreds of brands from American Express and Microsoft 365 to CNN and Zoom, as well as popular free software tools such as 7-zip, PuTTY and Python, all “aged” on innocuous templates for six to nine months before weaponization; eSentire and Malwarebytes also observed sponsored Google ads pushing phony extensions in May and April 2024, and Fin7 has even deployed domains targeting Louvre and Olympic tourists, building on its 2013–present campaign that has extorted some $3 billion from victim organizations, underscoring the urgent need for renewed law enforcement focus and proactive domain-monitoring defenses.
hits.title: The Stark Truth Behind the Resurgence of Russia’s Fin7 – Krebs on Security

hits.text: Since mid-November 2023 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked financially motivated actors—Storm-0569, Storm-1113, Sangria Tempest and Storm-1674—abusing the ms-appinstaller URI scheme and MSIX file format to distribute signed malicious application packages that bypass SmartScreen and browser warnings and deliver loaders, backdoors and ransomware. In early December Storm-0569 leveraged SEO poisoning and malvertising on spoofed Zoom, Tableau, TeamViewer and AnyDesk download sites to install BATLOADER via App Installer, which in turn dropped Cobalt Strike Beacons, exfiltrated data with Rclone and handed off to Black Basta ransomware; Storm-0569 also sells custom MSI/MSIX landing-page frameworks to other criminals. Storm-1113 has deployed EugenLoader via search ads mimicking Zoom to drop Gozi, RedLine, IcedID, Smoke Loader, NetSupport RAT, SectopRAT or Lumma stealer, acting as both access broker and “malware-as-a-service” provider. Sangria Tempest delivered Storm-1113’s EugenLoader to deploy Carbanak and Gracewire or POWERTRASH scripts loading NetSupport and Gracewire for data theft and extortion. From December Storm-1674 combined Teams-based phishing with malicious installers to deploy SectopRAT or DarkGate, often using Storm-1113’s frameworks. In response Microsoft disabled the ms-appinstaller handler by default, updated App Installer, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, conditional access, user education on URL and publisher validation, Defender SmartScreen, Safe Links and attack surface reduction rules to thwart this human-operated ransomware and data-exfiltration chain.
hits.title: Financially motivated threat actors misusing App Installer | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Silent Push researchers uncovered FIN7’s largest-ever infrastructure, identifying over 4,000 malicious IOFA domains and associated IP addresses used to fuel a global phishing and malware campaign that hit high-profile targets such as the Louvre, Meta and Reuters. Using automated intelligence and Threat Hunting workflows, analysts detected a pattern of newly registered look-alike domains—many leveraging common TLDs and typosquatting—to host spear-phishing landing pages and weaponized Office attachments that deploy custom .NET droppers and Cobalt Strike beacons. Chronologically, the operation began with domain registration, followed by coordinated email blasts spoofing corporate brands, HTTP(S) redirects to phishing kits, and payload delivery that enabled credential harvesting and potential lateral movement. Silent Push’s API-driven Integrations enabled rapid enumeration of IOFA indicators of compromise, brand protection alerts and proactive blocking in customer environments. Actionable insights include ingesting the full list of domains and IPs into SIEM and email security filters, enforcing strict SPF/DKIM/DMARC policies, monitoring DNS query anomalies for new domain registrations, and updating endpoint detection rules to flag the identified .NET loader behaviors.
hits.title: FIN7: Silent Push unearths the largest group of FIN7 domains ever discovered. 4000+ IOFA domains and IPs found. Louvre, Meta, and Reuters targeted in massive global phishing and malware campaigns.

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Lynx ransomware, a Ransomware-as-a-Service strain first seen in mid-2024 that repurposes INC source code, has targeted finance, architecture and manufacturing organizations—later expanding into energy and APAC retail—via phishing emails that deploy malware to exfiltrate sensitive data for double-extortion (including timed “drip” leaks) before encrypting files with a “.LYNX” extension; Darktrace observed initial lateral movement through SMB enumeration on port 445 and Nmap scans, exploitation of default “admin”/“administrator” credentials via NTLM and Kerberos for privilege escalation, anomalous internal transfers of ~150 GiB over port 3260 and large uploads to wt-prod-euwest1-storm.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com, plus AnyDesk-based remote sessions to aid operator actions, culminating in thousands of encrypted files detected by parallel SMB read/write anomalies and extension appends—Darktrace’s Autonomous Response models, if fully enabled, would automatically block suspicious SMB activity, unusual privileged user behavior and anomalous outbound connections to contain the threat and preserve business continuity.
hits.title: New Threat on the Prowl: Investigating Lynx Ransomware

canonical_entities: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
hits.text: On Monday Qantas detected unusual activity on a third-party call-centre customer-service platform used by six million customers and immediately contained the system, confirming that a “significant” volume of data—names, email addresses, phone numbers, birth dates and frequent flyer numbers—was likely stolen while credit card and personal financial data, as well as passwords, PINs and login details, remained secure; the airline, which operates globally across six continents, has notified the Australian Cyber Security Centre, the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner and the Australian Federal Police and reports all Qantas systems are currently secure. Although attribution remains unconfirmed, the breach shares hallmarks of the Scattered Spider threat group (aka 0ktapus, UNC3944, Scatter Swine, Starfraud, Muddled Libra), known for social-engineering and identity-based attacks—including phishing, SIM swapping, MFA bombing and help-desk phone calls—and recent pivots to aviation targets such as Hawaiian Airlines and WestJet (which was breached via a self-service password reset exploit). To defend against these tactics, organizations should gain complete visibility across infrastructure and identity systems and harden self-service password reset portals, help desks and third-party identity vendors, leveraging hardening guides published by Google Threat Intelligence Group and Palo Alto Networks.
hits.title: Qantas discloses cyberattack amid Scattered Spider aviation breaches

hits.text: Microsoft has identified a China-based nation-state threat actor tracked as Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda) conducting espionage against dozens of Taiwanese organizations since mid-2021 by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java and SQL servers to deploy the China Chopper web shell, escalate privileges with Juicy Potato and BadPotato, and establish persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN bridge over HTTPS on port 443 for stealthy command-and-control. Once inside, the actor leverages WinRM and WMIC for lateral movement and deploys Mimikatz to dump LSASS and SAM for pass-the-hash attacks, yet conducts minimal post-persistence activity, suggesting long-term credential harvesting rather than immediate data exfiltration. To mitigate, organizations must enforce rigorous patch management, monitor registry changes and RDP configurations, deploy file integrity and behavioral monitoring on public-facing servers, isolate and forensically examine compromised systems, and rotate or disable exposed credentials.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Lynx ransomware, a Ransomware-as-a-Service strain first seen in mid-2024 that repurposes INC source code, has targeted finance, architecture and manufacturing organizations—later expanding into energy and APAC retail—via phishing emails that deploy malware to exfiltrate sensitive data for double-extortion (including timed “drip” leaks) before encrypting files with a “.LYNX” extension; Darktrace observed initial lateral movement through SMB enumeration on port 445 and Nmap scans, exploitation of default “admin”/“administrator” credentials via NTLM and Kerberos for privilege escalation, anomalous internal transfers of ~150 GiB over port 3260 and large uploads to wt-prod-euwest1-storm.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com, plus AnyDesk-based remote sessions to aid operator actions, culminating in thousands of encrypted files detected by parallel SMB read/write anomalies and extension appends—Darktrace’s Autonomous Response models, if fully enabled, would automatically block suspicious SMB activity, unusual privileged user behavior and anomalous outbound connections to contain the threat and preserve business continuity.
retrieved_context.title: New Threat on the Prowl: Investigating Lynx Ransomware

canonical_entities: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
retrieved_context.text: On Monday Qantas detected unusual activity on a third-party call-centre customer-service platform used by six million customers and immediately contained the system, confirming that a “significant” volume of data—names, email addresses, phone numbers, birth dates and frequent flyer numbers—was likely stolen while credit card and personal financial data, as well as passwords, PINs and login details, remained secure; the airline, which operates globally across six continents, has notified the Australian Cyber Security Centre, the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner and the Australian Federal Police and reports all Qantas systems are currently secure. Although attribution remains unconfirmed, the breach shares hallmarks of the Scattered Spider threat group (aka 0ktapus, UNC3944, Scatter Swine, Starfraud, Muddled Libra), known for social-engineering and identity-based attacks—including phishing, SIM swapping, MFA bombing and help-desk phone calls—and recent pivots to aviation targets such as Hawaiian Airlines and WestJet (which was breached via a self-service password reset exploit). To defend against these tactics, organizations should gain complete visibility across infrastructure and identity systems and harden self-service password reset portals, help desks and third-party identity vendors, leveraging hardening guides published by Google Threat Intelligence Group and Palo Alto Networks.
retrieved_context.title: Qantas discloses cyberattack amid Scattered Spider aviation breaches

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has identified a China-based nation-state threat actor tracked as Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda) conducting espionage against dozens of Taiwanese organizations since mid-2021 by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java and SQL servers to deploy the China Chopper web shell, escalate privileges with Juicy Potato and BadPotato, and establish persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN bridge over HTTPS on port 443 for stealthy command-and-control. Once inside, the actor leverages WinRM and WMIC for lateral movement and deploys Mimikatz to dump LSASS and SAM for pass-the-hash attacks, yet conducts minimal post-persistence activity, suggesting long-term credential harvesting rather than immediate data exfiltration. To mitigate, organizations must enforce rigorous patch management, monitor registry changes and RDP configurations, deploy file integrity and behavioral monitoring on public-facing servers, isolate and forensically examine compromised systems, and rotate or disable exposed credentials.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: In May 2023, after U.S. authorities secured convictions against three high-level operators and declared the Russia-based cybercrime enterprise Fin7 “no more,” security experts began spotting first signs of its resurrection in April 2024 when Blackberry reported a typosquatting-based malware intrusion against a major automotive firm; since January 2024, Silent Push analyst Zach Edwards has mapped over 4,000 Fin7-linked hosts—rented largely on the pro-Russia Stark Industries Solutions platform—employing typosquatting, booby-trapped ads, malicious browser extensions and spear-phishing domains to mimic hundreds of brands from American Express and Microsoft 365 to CNN and Zoom, as well as popular free software tools such as 7-zip, PuTTY and Python, all “aged” on innocuous templates for six to nine months before weaponization; eSentire and Malwarebytes also observed sponsored Google ads pushing phony extensions in May and April 2024, and Fin7 has even deployed domains targeting Louvre and Olympic tourists, building on its 2013–present campaign that has extorted some $3 billion from victim organizations, underscoring the urgent need for renewed law enforcement focus and proactive domain-monitoring defenses.
hits.title: The Stark Truth Behind the Resurgence of Russia’s Fin7 – Krebs on Security

hits.text: Silent Push researchers uncovered FIN7’s largest-ever infrastructure, identifying over 4,000 malicious IOFA domains and associated IP addresses used to fuel a global phishing and malware campaign that hit high-profile targets such as the Louvre, Meta and Reuters. Using automated intelligence and Threat Hunting workflows, analysts detected a pattern of newly registered look-alike domains—many leveraging common TLDs and typosquatting—to host spear-phishing landing pages and weaponized Office attachments that deploy custom .NET droppers and Cobalt Strike beacons. Chronologically, the operation began with domain registration, followed by coordinated email blasts spoofing corporate brands, HTTP(S) redirects to phishing kits, and payload delivery that enabled credential harvesting and potential lateral movement. Silent Push’s API-driven Integrations enabled rapid enumeration of IOFA indicators of compromise, brand protection alerts and proactive blocking in customer environments. Actionable insights include ingesting the full list of domains and IPs into SIEM and email security filters, enforcing strict SPF/DKIM/DMARC policies, monitoring DNS query anomalies for new domain registrations, and updating endpoint detection rules to flag the identified .NET loader behaviors.
hits.title: FIN7: Silent Push unearths the largest group of FIN7 domains ever discovered. 4000+ IOFA domains and IPs found. Louvre, Meta, and Reuters targeted in massive global phishing and malware campaigns.

hits.text: Since mid-November 2023 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked financially motivated actors—Storm-0569, Storm-1113, Sangria Tempest and Storm-1674—abusing the ms-appinstaller URI scheme and MSIX file format to distribute signed malicious application packages that bypass SmartScreen and browser warnings and deliver loaders, backdoors and ransomware. In early December Storm-0569 leveraged SEO poisoning and malvertising on spoofed Zoom, Tableau, TeamViewer and AnyDesk download sites to install BATLOADER via App Installer, which in turn dropped Cobalt Strike Beacons, exfiltrated data with Rclone and handed off to Black Basta ransomware; Storm-0569 also sells custom MSI/MSIX landing-page frameworks to other criminals. Storm-1113 has deployed EugenLoader via search ads mimicking Zoom to drop Gozi, RedLine, IcedID, Smoke Loader, NetSupport RAT, SectopRAT or Lumma stealer, acting as both access broker and “malware-as-a-service” provider. Sangria Tempest delivered Storm-1113’s EugenLoader to deploy Carbanak and Gracewire or POWERTRASH scripts loading NetSupport and Gracewire for data theft and extortion. From December Storm-1674 combined Teams-based phishing with malicious installers to deploy SectopRAT or DarkGate, often using Storm-1113’s frameworks. In response Microsoft disabled the ms-appinstaller handler by default, updated App Installer, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, conditional access, user education on URL and publisher validation, Defender SmartScreen, Safe Links and attack surface reduction rules to thwart this human-operated ransomware and data-exfiltration chain.
hits.title: Financially motivated threat actors misusing App Installer | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
hits.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

canonical_entities: FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns
hits.text: Clop ransomware, a TA505-sponsored RaaS strain appending the “.ClOP” extension, infects entire networks by compromising Active Directory servers and manipulating Group Policy for persistence, then uses phishing-delivered HTML attachments to drop the Get2 loader, which in turn pulls SDBOT, FlawedAmmyy RATs, Cobalt Strike beacons and TinyMet reverse shells for reconnaissance, lateral movement (via SMB exploits), and exfiltration (often using the DEWMODE web shell). Operators employ double and quadruple extortion—threatening to publish or auction stolen data on their Cl0p^_-Leaks site and targeting executives/customers—to coerce ransoms, driving average payments up 43% to $220,298 (median $78,398) in Q1 2021 after FIN11’s and FIN7’s twin zero-day campaigns against Kiteworks FTA (CVE-2021-27101/02/03/04) and Fortra GoAnywhere MFT, while in 2023 they exploited PaperCut CVE-2023-27350 to deploy Truebot and LockBit/Clop, then MOVEit CVE-2023-24362/CVE-2023-35036 and an unpatched SQL injection flaw to steal data without payloads. Trend Micro detections reveal a May 2023 surge (245 attempts), with top targets in banking, retail and healthcare across Türkiye, Canada, the US and large enterprises worldwide.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Clop | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: Since at least 2016, financially motivated distributor Storm-0324 (aka DEV-0324, TA543, Sagrid) has operated a highly evasive malware distribution chain—initially using exploit kits and email-based lures referencing invoices or DocuSign/QuickBooks and traffic distribution systems like BlackTDS and Keitaro to evade sandboxes—to deliver first-stage payloads such as Nymaim, Gozi v3, TrickBot, Gootkit, Dridex, IcedID and Sage/GandCrab ransomware; by 2019 it shifted to primarily deploying JSSLoader, which drops variants via JavaScript-embedded DLLs (hosted on SharePoint ZIP archives, Office docs, WSF or VBScript files) exploiting CVE-2023-21715 bypasses and protected-document social engineering, then hands off network access to the ransomware-as-a-service actor Sangria Tempest (ELBRUS/Carbon Spider/FIN7) for ransomware deployment, and in July 2023 began using open-source TeamsPhisher to send phishing lures over Microsoft Teams; defenders can disrupt this chain by leveraging Microsoft 365 Defender/XDR detections (TrojanSpy:MSIL/JSSLoader, Trojan:Win32/{Gootkit, IcedID, Trickbot}), enforcing phishing-resistant auth via Conditional Access, least-privilege and credential hygiene, tightening Teams external collaboration settings and ‘EXTERNAL’ tagging, enabling Safe Links and Zero-hour Auto Purge, applying attack surface reduction rules to block script/executable launches, turning on cloud-delivered protection and auditing, and educating users on social engineering and MFA code safety to significantly limit initial access and downstream ransomware impact.
hits.title: Malware distributor Storm-0324 facilitates ransomware access | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

hits.text: Since January 2021, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has tracked a government-backed North Korean campaign that leverages social engineering via X (formerly Twitter) and encrypted messaging apps to befriend security researchers and deliver malicious files containing at least one unpatched 0-day in a popular software package; upon exploitation the custom shellcode performs anti-virtual-machine checks, captures system data and screenshots, and exfiltrates them to C2 infrastructure (e.g., 23.106.215[.]105, www.blgbeach[.]com), with the latest vulnerability reported and patched on September 12, 2023 (see TAG’s published RCA). In parallel, the actors published a seemingly benign Windows tool called GetSymbol on GitHub (https://github.com/dbgsymbol/) that quietly downloads debugging symbols—and arbitrary code—from attacker domains, requiring full OS reinstalls for compromised hosts. TAG has added malicious sites to Safe Browsing, issued government-backed attacker alerts to targeted Gmail and Workspace users, and urges researchers to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, keep software up to date, and verify system integrity after using third-party tools.
hits.title: Active North Korean campaign targeting security researchers

hits.text: Between July and October 2021, Iranian state-sponsored group Lyceum (aka Hexane, Spirlin) conducted targeted intrusions against ISPs and telecom operators in Israel, Morocco, Tunisia, and Saudi Arabia, plus an African ministry of foreign affairs, using credential stuffing and brute-force attacks for initial access before deploying malware implants Shark and Milan to execute arbitrary commands and exfiltrate data; researchers from Accenture Cyber Threat Intelligence and Prevailion's Adversarial Counterintelligence Team identified over 20 web-based infrastructure components enabling victim identification, with at least two compromises assessed as ongoing despite prior public disclosure of indicators of compromise, and beaconing from reconfigured or new Lyceum backdoors detected in late October 2021 from Tunisian telecom and African MFA victims indicating active modifications to evade security detection.
hits.title: Iran's Lyceum Hackers Target Telecoms, ISPs in Israel, Saudi Arabia, and Africa

hits.text: Since January 2021, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has tracked a government-backed North Korean campaign that leverages social engineering via X (formerly Twitter) and encrypted messaging apps to befriend security researchers and deliver malicious files containing at least one unpatched 0-day in a popular software package; upon exploitation the custom shellcode performs anti-virtual-machine checks, captures system data and screenshots, and exfiltrates them to C2 infrastructure (e.g., 23.106.215[.]105, www.blgbeach[.]com), with the latest vulnerability reported and patched on September 12, 2023 (see TAG’s published RCA). In parallel, the actors published a seemingly benign Windows tool called GetSymbol on GitHub (https://github.com/dbgsymbol/) that quietly downloads debugging symbols—and arbitrary code—from attacker domains, requiring full OS reinstalls for compromised hosts. TAG has added malicious sites to Safe Browsing, issued government-backed attacker alerts to targeted Gmail and Workspace users, and urges researchers to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, keep software up to date, and verify system integrity after using third-party tools.
hits.title: Active North Korean campaign targeting security researchers

hits.text: The North Korea-linked threat actor Slow Pisces (also tracked as Jade Sleet, PUKCHONG, TraderTraitor, and UNC4899) has been conducting a multi-stage malware campaign targeting cryptocurrency developers via LinkedIn job opportunity lures since at least June 2024, leveraging trojanized Python and JavaScript projects hosted on GitHub that employ YAML deserialization and EJS templating to execute gated payloads only to validated targets meeting specific criteria (IP address, geolocation, time, HTTP headers); the campaign delivers RN Loader and RN Stealer malware on macOS systems capable of harvesting system metadata, installed applications, SSH keys, AWS/Kubernetes/Google Cloud configuration files, and iCloud Keychain data, with payloads remaining memory-resident and deployed selectively to prevent analysis; Slow Pisces is assessed to be responsible for the February 2025 Bybit cryptocurrency exchange breach and operates alongside other North Korean clusters including Operation Dream Job, Contagious Interview, Alluring Pisces, and Moonstone Sleet, though with notably superior operational security practices involving heavily guarded payload delivery across infection stages.
hits.title: Crypto Developers Targeted by Python Malware Disguised as Coding Challenges

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

hits.text: In August 2025 Microsoft Threat Intelligence revealed that Storm-2460, associated with the Play ransomware group, has resumed exploiting CVE-2025-29824—a zero-day elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Common Log File System patched in April—to gain SYSTEM privileges on unpatched hosts across IT, financial and real estate organizations in the US, Europe, South America and the Middle East. The campaign begins with an in-memory dropper masquerading as the open-source ChatGPT Desktop app that decrypts and launches PipeMagic, a modular backdoor first observed in December 2022 and now updated with persistence and lateral-movement enhancements targeting Saudi Arabian and Brazilian manufacturing entities. PipeMagic communicates with its TCP C2 over a named pipe, self-updates by storing distinct payload modules in memory via doubly linked lists for staging, execution and communication (plus an additional dynamic list), then leverages the CLFS exploit to escalate privileges before deploying Play ransomware. Although the campaign’s footprint remains limited, the combination of a zero-day exploit and a sophisticated modular backdoor underscores a heightened risk; organizations are urged to immediately apply the April patch for CVE-2025-29824, enable tamper and network protection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, run EDR in block mode, enforce full automated investigation and remediation, and leverage cloud-delivered machine-learning protections to block novel variants.
hits.title: PipeMagic Backdoor Resurfaces as Part of Play Ransomware Attack Chain

canonical_entities: trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia
hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
hits.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

hits.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
hits.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

hits.text: Unit 42’s investigation reveals that North Korean state‐sponsored group Jumpy Pisces (aka Andariel/Onyx Sleet) gained initial access to a corporate network in May 2024 via a compromised user account, deployed a customized Sliver C2 beaconing to 172.96.137[.]224/americajobmail[.]site and their bespoke DTrack infostealer across hosts via SMB, and leveraged Impacket’s secretsdump.py, Mimikatz dumps (KB0722.log), a custom RDP account tool and a trojanized browser‐data stealer for credential harvesting, lateral movement and persistence; this activity continued until early September when the same account and toolset were abused—using TokenPlayer for Windows token abuse, PsExec for privilege escalation and EDR sensor removal—to facilitate Play ransomware (Fiddling Scorpius) deployment, marking the first observed collaboration (affiliate or initial access brokerage) between Jumpy Pisces and Play ransomware and signaling a shift from espionage to broader ransomware operations that could target victims globally, underscoring the imperative for defenders to treat Jumpy Pisces activity as a precursory ransomware threat and to deploy mitigations such as Cortex XDR, Advanced WildFire, Advanced URL Filtering and Advanced DNS Security.
hits.title: Jumpy Pisces Engages in Play Ransomware

hits.text: North Korean APT Lazarus has launched “Operation In(ter)ception,” a macOS-focused cyberespionage campaign that lures engineering professionals with a fake Coinbase job posting and deploys a signed universal macOS executable (Intel and Apple Silicon) that drops three components—a decoy PDF (Coinbase_online_careers_2022_07.pdf), a FinderFontsUpdater.app bundle and a downloader named safarifontagent—before phoning home to a new, currently nonresponsive C2 at concrecapital[.]com/%user%.jpg. Identified by ESET in late July and using a February-2022 developer certificate for “Shankey Nohria” revoked by Apple on August 12, the malware mirrors a May sample but introduces fresh C2 infrastructure and was first uploaded from Brazil. A companion Windows variant, spotted by Malwarebytes on August 4, follows the same decoy routine. This marks another evolution in Lazarus’s longstanding impersonation tactics—previously targeting engineers via spear-phishing and defense-sector ruses—while the group simultaneously diversifies into cryptocurrency heists (prompting Tornado Cash sanctions) and VHD ransomware operations to fund the North Korean regime.
hits.title: APT Lazarus Targets Engineers with macOS Malware | Threatpost

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
hits.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: In August 2025 the FBI issued a public service announcement that FSB-linked Berserk Bear (aka Blue Kraken, Crouching Yeti, Dragonfly, Koala Team) has been exploiting the seven-year-old Cisco IOS/IOS XE Smart Install remote code execution/DoS vulnerability (CVE-2018-0171) to compromise critical infrastructure worldwide. Since Cisco first detected opportunistic attacks in November 2021, the group has collected configuration files from thousands of unpatched devices associated with U.S. critical infrastructure sectors, covertly modified those configs to maintain persistent unauthorized access, and conducted network reconnaissance targeting ICS-related protocols and applications. Cisco Talos reports that the campaign, referred to as Static Tundra, has aggressively hit telecommunications, higher education, and manufacturing networks across North America, Asia, Africa, and Europe, deploying custom SNMP tools and the SYNful Knock firmware implant—originally identified by FireEye in 2015—to evade detection and embed for years. The FBI’s warning underscores the urgent need for organizations to patch CVE-2018-0171, disable Smart Install, and implement comprehensive hardening, as other state-sponsored actors are likely conducting similar network device compromise campaigns.
hits.title: FBI warns of Russian hackers exploiting 7-year-old Cisco flaw

canonical_entities: Bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters with requirePasswordChange=Y
hits.text: A critical zero-day flaw (CVE-2023-51467) has been identified in Apache OfBiz’s login functionality—stemming from an incomplete patch for a prior high-severity RCE vulnerability (CVE-2023-49070, CVSS 9.8) tied to a deprecated XML-RPC component—that allows attackers to bypass authentication by sending empty or invalid USERNAME and PASSWORD parameters alongside “requirePasswordChange=Y,” effectively granting unauthorized access and enabling simple SSRF attacks against internal resources; discovered by SonicWall Capture Labs, the bug follows observations by The Shadowserver Foundation of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2023-49070, and SonicWall reports exploit traffic for CVE-2023-51467 spiking from 235 attempts on December 27, 2023, to 26,928 on December 29 and 3,129 on January 1, 2024, underscoring urgent need for organizations using OfBiz versions prior to 18.12.11 to upgrade immediately to mitigate further data exfiltration and system takeover risks.
hits.title: Critical Zero-Day in Apache OfBiz ERP System Exposes Businesses to Attack

canonical_entities: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager
hits.text: Water Ouroboros is a Ransomware-as-a-Service operation that exploits public-facing Oracle WebLogic vulnerabilities (CVE-2019-2725, CVE-2017-10271, CVE-2019-2729) or drive-by installers for initial access (T1190, T1189), then executes remote Windows commands (wmic.exe, bcdedit.exe, wbadmin.exe, vssadmin.exe) to delete backups and disable recovery (T1490, T1562.001) before encrypting fixed, removable and network drives via a Go-based custom routine that uses RTLGenRandom to generate a symmetric key, protects it with embedded RSA public keys (App_ExportKey), appends “.locked” (unless suppressed with –E), excludes over 60 file extensions, and accepts credentials (c {user}:{pass}), logging (–a), non-aggressive (–A) and size filters (–m). Victims find Contact Us.txt ransom notes pointing to a TOR payment site and Hive Leaks data-dump threat. Post-infection, actors maintain access via compromised admin accounts (T1078), disable security tools (PCHunter, ProcessHacker), dump credentials from registry hives (T1003.002), move laterally over RDP/SMB (T1021.001/002), discover assets via AdFind (T1595.002) and exfiltrate data over C&C (SharpRhino RAT/T1071.001, T1041). With 136 incidents in the US and notable impacts on construction, IT, manufacturing and healthcare SMBs, the campaign underscores the need for timely patching, hardened public-facing apps, least-privilege access, MFA, robust backups and advanced threat detection.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: Water Ouroboros | Trend Micro (US)
