canonical_entities: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
hits.text: Since its emergence in 2021 and first detection on Trend Micro telemetry in March 2022, the TargetCompany ransomware group has launched 269 attempted attacks against 250 disclosed Trend customers—predominantly in Asia (notably India and Saudi Arabia)—while avoiding Kazakhstan, Russia, Qatar, and Ukraine, and focusing on manufacturing, retail, and telecommunications; their November 2022–May 2023 leak site lists 20 confirmed victims (mostly small businesses) across the Asia-Pacific, Europe, and Middle East in IT, manufacturing, apparel, and automotive sectors. Initial access vectors include exploitation of CVE-2019-1069 and CVE-2020-0618 RCE flaws, SQL Server xp_cmdshell abuse, and OneNote-based spam campaigns. Execution relies on WMIC-invoked PowerShell scripts to retrieve various payloads (TargetComp ransomware, Remcos backdoor, Negasteal, Snake Keylogger) and, since January 2022, reflective loading of a .NET downloader that decrypts and runs payloads in memory via XOR or inversion. For defense evasion, operators deploy GMER, PCHunter64 (YDArk.exe), Advance Process Termination, KILLAV, and killer.bat to disable AV and security services; discovery is achieved through network scans and Mimikatz credential dumping; lateral movement via RDP-based RCE; C2 evolved from an open Mallox directory to an Nginx-protected server. Impact involves ChaCha20 file encryption with keys generated by Curve25519 and AES-128, file extensions such as .mallox/.exploit/.avast and ransom notes titled “HOW TO RECOVER!!.TXT,” and potential data exfiltration. Their tactics span MITRE techniques T1190, T1059.001, T1047, T1562.001, T1003.001, T1071.001, T1486, and more. The group’s maturation—evidenced by reflective loading and possible RaaS adoption—underscores the urgency for organizations to enforce asset inventories, least-privilege access, prompt patching (or virtual patching), multifactor authentication, sandboxed email defenses, AI/ML-driven detection, regular backups, and continuous red-team testing to thwart this active threat.
hits.title: Ransomware Spotlight: TargetCompany | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: Since at least 2015, Mandiant has identified APT42—an IRGC-linked Iranian state-sponsored threat actor also known as APT35—conducting over 30 spear-phishing operations across 14 countries against government officials, policymakers, journalists, academics and dissidents, evolving tactics from 2020 Oxford vaccinologist-themed pharmaceutical lures to 2021 fake interview requests using compromised U.S. media accounts for 37-day MFA-intercepting credential harvesting, and February 2022 phishes posing as a British news agency targeting political science professors; beyond credential theft via shortened URLs and PDF attachments directing victims to spoofed login portals, APT42 deploys custom Android spyware—spread via SMS links to messaging/VPN apps—to exfiltrate calls, SMS, audio recordings, images and GPS data in real time, while on Windows it employs lightweight custom malware for initial access, privilege escalation, reconnaissance, lateral movement through follow-on phishing, and persistence via scheduled tasks and registry keys; Mandiant further correlates APT42’s TTPs with November 2021 PHOSPHORUS BitLocker ransomware attempts against Fortinet FortiOS SSL VPN and unpatched Exchange servers, highlighting the group’s multi-platform espionage-to-ransom capabilities and real-world threat to high-value targets.
hits.title: New Iranian hacking group APT42 deploys custom Android spyware

canonical_entities: exfiltrating sensitive diplomatic and policy-related data
hits.text: Since at least 2021, the Chinese state-linked APT group FishMonger—operating under the I-SOON umbrella—has waged sophisticated espionage against government institutions and NGOs in Southeast Asia and Europe, initiating attacks via spear-phishing emails that deliver template-injected Microsoft Office documents to exploit vulnerabilities or employ social engineering and deploy a Spyder loader, then install the custom “SilentBreeze” backdoor. SilentBreeze establishes persistence through a scheduled PowerShell task using a Mozilla-style User-Agent header to download additional payloads from hxxps://cdn-storage.cloud-service.site/updates.php, communicates with command-and-control servers over encrypted channels via compromised third-party proxies, and remains undetected for months while harvesting credentials and exfiltrating sensitive diplomatic and policy-related data aligned with Chinese strategic interests in the South China Sea and human rights monitoring. ESET researchers note FishMonger’s continual toolset modifications and counter-detection tactics, distinctive network traffic patterns, and reliance on third-party proxies to mask true C2 infrastructure, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to harden phishing defenses, monitor for template injection in Office files, audit scheduled PowerShell tasks, and scrutinize outbound connections to anomalous cloud-service URLs to disrupt this persistent threat.
hits.title: Chinese FishMonger APT Operated by I‑SOON Attacking Government Entities & NGOs

canonical_entities: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
hits.text: In late 2023, researchers uncovered a sophisticated Taiwan-focused espionage operation in which a China-linked APT actor (likely APT27) hijacked an abandoned Sogou Zhuyin Windows update server—vacated when Sogou ceased Zhuyin support in mid-2022—and weaponized it to distribute a trojanized updater (SHA-256: 3f5c…) that deployed a custom backdoor and Cobalt Strike beacon via HTTP(S) (MITRE T1195.002, T1071.001). Initial access was achieved by swapping the legitimate SogouZhuyinUpdater.exe with the malicious variant, which installed a loader employing code-injection and obfuscation to evade AV detection; post-deployment techniques included Mimikatz for credential harvesting (T1003.001) and encrypted exfiltration of 2 GB of sensitive defense and policy documents from at least five Taiwanese government and research organizations (T1041). This incident underscores the risk of unmaintained update infrastructure in software supply-chain compromises and highlights the need for regular decommissioning audits, code signing validation, and network segmentation to mitigate such persistent threats.
hits.title: Abandoned Sogou Zhuyin Update Server Hijacked, Weaponized in Taiwan Espionage Campaign

canonical_entities: Scanning the Internet for IoT devices with open Telnet/SSH ports
Use of default or weak credentials
Encrypted SOCKS5 tunneling to proxy infrastructure
hits.text: Researchers have uncovered that since early 2024 a previously undocumented botnet, dubbed Ngioweb, has been systematically scanning the Internet for IoT devices—primarily DVRs, IP cameras and home routers—with open Telnet/SSH ports and default or weak credentials, exploiting known firmware vulnerabilities to deploy a lightweight Go-based loader that establishes encrypted SOCKS5 tunnels back to a resilient NSOCKS residential proxy network of over 150,000 infected nodes. Once a device is compromised, Ngioweb drops a persistent agent that connects to fast-flux C2 domains via HTTPS, retrieves updated encryption keys and proxy configuration, and registers the node for NSOCKS’ tiered subscription service (starting at $25/month), which reportedly generates upwards of $500K in monthly revenue by fueling large-scale credential-stuffing campaigns, ad fraud and DDoS-for-hire operations. The actors behind Ngioweb continually rotate fallback C2 domains, employ encryption and obfuscation to evade signature-based detection, and monitor infection success rates in real time, enabling rapid retooling and expansion. Defenders are urged to enforce strong, unique credentials on all IoT assets, disable unused management interfaces, apply timely firmware updates, implement network segmentation and deploy behavioral analytics or honeypots to detect anomalous outbound proxy traffic.
hits.title: Ngioweb Botnet Fuels NSOCKS Residential Proxy Network Exploiting IoT Devices

hits.text: A state-sponsored APT42 (formerly UNC788), attributed to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, conducted over 30 confirmed espionage attacks since 2015 targeting activists, dissidents, and strategic organizations across non-profits, education, governments, healthcare, legal, manufacturing, media, and pharmaceuticals in 14+ countries including Australia, Europe, Middle East, and U.S. The group shares partial overlaps with APT35 (Charming Kitten, Cobalt Illusion, ITG18, Phosphorus, TA453, Yellow Garuda) and uses highly targeted spear-phishing and social engineering to build trust, distributing Android malware VINETHORN and PINEFLOWER via text messages capable of recording audio, extracting multimedia/SMS, and tracking geolocation, with a SaferVPN masqueraded payload observed April-October 2021. Windows malware includes TAMECAT (PowerShell backdoor), TABBYCAT (VBA macro dropper), and VBREVSHELL (reverse shell macro). APT42's link to UNC2448/DEV-0270/Cobalt Mirage (ransomware operators using BitLocker) operates through front company Najee Technology Hooshmand with aliases Secnerd and Lifeweb, though missions differ—APT42 focuses on domestic politics and regime stability while APT35 targets long-term resource-intensive operations, with pharmaceutical intrusions commencing March 2020 during COVID-19 pandemic onset.
hits.title: Iranian APT42 Launched Over 30 Espionage Attacks Against Activists and Dissidents

hits.text: In February 2022, CISA, the FBI, US Cyber Command CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA issued a joint advisory on Iranian Ministry of Intelligence–linked APT MuddyWater (aka MERCURY, Earth Vetala, Static Kitten, Seedworm, TEMP.Zagros), active since 2018 and focused on cyber espionage, intellectual property theft and ransomware against defense, oil & gas, government and telecom sectors across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America. Exploiting publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and open-source tools, MuddyWater delivers malicious PDFs with embedded links that display error messages prompting users to download Excel maldocs or Windows executables; these files host VBA macros that drop WSF scripts to execute PowerShell and VB payloads, leverage LoLBins, and stage RATs and malware families including PowGoop, Canopy, Small Sieve, POWERSTATS and Mori while communicating with C2 over HTTP and DNS and persisting via Registry Run keys. Cisco Talos observed regional campaigns in Turkey (Nov 2021), Pakistan (Aug 2021) and Armenia (Jun 2021) using decoy documents, signaling tokens and a consistent TTP set, suggesting a conglomerate of subgroups migrating techniques across regions. The resultant network access and data exfiltration underscore the imperative for proactive DFIR readiness, deployment of XDR/MDR platforms, rigorous vulnerability management, macro execution restrictions, PowerShell/LoLBin monitoring and ongoing user awareness training reinforced by incident response tabletop exercises.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at Iranian APT "MuddyWater"

hits.text: Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has observed a 33% year-over-year increase in government-backed phishing warnings—over 50,000 sent to users so far in 2021—driven in part by a large APT28 (Fancy Bear) campaign and sustained by ongoing operations from Iran-aligned APT35. Since early 2021, APT35 has compromised a UK university website to host a phishing kit targeting Gmail, Yahoo and Hotmail credentials—including second-factor codes—and continues its credential harvesting campaigns against government, academia, journalism and NGOs using hijacked sites and link-shortening redirects. In May 2020 it attempted to distribute spyware disguised as a VPN on Google Play Store (blocked before installation) and has pursued similar Android C2 apps on other platforms. The group also impersonates conference officials (e.g., Munich Security, T20 Italy) to initiate phishing, embedding JavaScript to relay visitor IP, user-agent and locale via Telegram bots—a tactic TAG disrupted by reporting the bots. TAG’s layered defenses include batch-sent warnings, Workspace admin alerts, Safe Browsing domain blocks and urging high-risk users to enable two-factor authentication or enroll in Advanced Protection.
hits.title: Countering threats from Iran

hits.text: The Lotus Blossom APT (aka Lotus Panda, Billbug, Spring Dragon) has stepped up cyberespionage against APAC government targets by deploying new Sagerunex backdoor variants and abusing Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) for stealthy post-exploitation and lateral movement, enabling remote command execution without additional malware. Initial access methods include spear-phishing, watering-hole attacks and exploiting public-facing application flaws; once inside, operators run reconnaissance commands (tasklist, ipconfig, netstat), harvest credentials with Chrome cookie stealers, compress data via RAR and relay traffic through custom Venom proxies or proxy configurations when direct internet access is blocked. Persistence is achieved by installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry under hijacked service names (tapisrv, swprv) to auto-launch at startup, while command-and-control blends encrypted traffic into legitimate platforms—stolen data uploaded as .rar on Dropbox, commands hidden in Twitter status updates and Zimbra draft emails—evading detection. Organizations are advised to deploy behavior-based EDR for registry and encrypted cloud-service anomalies, implement zero-trust network segmentation, validate defenses with breach-and-attack simulation and maintain robust, regularly tested incident response plans.
hits.title: Lotus Blossom APT Exploits WMI for Post-Exploitation Activities

canonical_entities: lateral movement to additional cloud resources

hits.text: Dragos researchers, in collaboration with Ukraine’s CSSC, unearthed FrostyGoop—an ICS-specific malware first spotted in April and used in January to disrupt central heating in over 600 Lviv apartment buildings—marking the first known malware to leverage Modbus TCP for read/write operations on operational technology. retrieved_context.text: In late 2023, researchers uncovered a sophisticated Taiwan-focused espionage operation in which a China-linked APT actor (likely APT27) hijacked an abandoned Sogou Zhuyin Windows update server—vacated when Sogou ceased Zhuyin support in mid-2022—and weaponized it to distribute a trojanized updater (SHA-256: 3f5c…) that deployed a custom backdoor and Cobalt Strike beacon via HTTP(S) (MITRE T1195.002, T1071.001). retrieved_context.text: Since its emergence in 2021 and first detection on Trend Micro telemetry in March 2022, the TargetCompany ransomware group has launched 269 attempted attacks against 250 disclosed Trend customers—predominantly in Asia (notably India and Saudi Arabia)—while avoiding Kazakhstan, Russia, Qatar, and Ukraine, and focusing on manufacturing, retail, and telecommunications; their November 2022–May 2023 leak site lists 20 confirmed victims (mostly small businesses) across the Asia-Pacific, Europe, and Middle East in IT, manufacturing, apparel, and automotive sectors. Initial access vectors include exploitation of CVE-2019-1069 and CVE-2020-0618 RCE flaws, SQL Server xp_cmdshell abuse, and OneNote-based spam campaigns. Execution relies on WMIC-invoked PowerShell scripts to retrieve various payloads (TargetComp ransomware, Remcos backdoor, Negasteal, Snake Keylogger) and, since January 2022, reflective loading of a .NET downloader that decrypts and runs payloads in memory via XOR or inversion. For defense evasion, operators deploy GMER, PCHunter64 (YDArk.exe), Advance Process Termination, KILLAV, and killer.bat to disable AV and security services; discovery is achieved through network scans and Mimikatz credential dumping; lateral movement via RDP-based RCE; C2 evolved from an open Mallox directory to an Nginx-protected server. The group’s maturation—evidenced by reflective loading and possible RaaS adoption—underscores the urgency for organizations to enforce asset inventories, least-privilege access, prompt patching (or virtual patching), multifactor authentication, sandboxed email defenses, AI/ML-driven detection, regular backups, and continuous red-team testing to thwart this active threat.

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.

Initial access vectors include exploitation of CVE-2019-1069 and CVE-2020-0618 RCE flaws, SQL Server xp_cmdshell abuse, and OneNote-based spam campaigns. Execution relies on WMIC-invoked PowerShell scripts to retrieve various payloads (TargetComp ransomware, Remcos backdoor, Negasteal, Snake Keylogger) and, since January 2022, reflective loading of a .NET downloader that decrypts and runs payloads in memory via XOR or inversion. For defense evasion, operators deploy GMER, PCHunter64 (YDArk.exe), Advance Process Termination, KILLAV, and killer.bat to disable AV and security services; discovery is achieved through network scans and Mimikatz credential dumping; lateral movement via RDP-based RCE; C2 evolved from an open Mallox directory to an Nginx-protected server. Impact involves ChaCha20 file encryption with keys generated by Curve25519 and AES-128, file extensions such as .mallox/.exploit/.avast and ransom notes titled “HOW TO RECOVER!!.TXT,” and potential data exfiltration. Their tactics span MITRE techniques T1190, T1059.001, T1047, T1562.001, T1003.001, T1071.001, T1486, and more. The group’s maturation—evidenced by reflective loading and possible RaaS adoption—underscores the urgency for organizations to enforce asset inventories, least-privilege access, prompt patching (or virtual patching), multifactor authentication, sandboxed email defenses, AI/ML-driven detection, regular backups, and continuous red-team testing to thwart this active threat.

canonical_entities: installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry
retrieved_context.text: The Lotus Blossom APT (aka Lotus Panda, Billbug, Spring Dragon) has stepped up cyberespionage against APAC government targets by deploying new Sagerunex backdoor variants and abusing Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) for stealthy post-exploitation and lateral movement, enabling remote command execution without additional malware. Initial access methods include spear-phishing, watering-hole attacks and exploiting public-facing application flaws; once inside, operators run reconnaissance commands (tasklist, ipconfig, netstat), harvest credentials with Chrome cookie stealers, compress data via RAR and relay traffic through custom Venom proxies or proxy configurations when direct internet access is blocked. Persistence is achieved by installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry under hijacked service names (tapisrv, swprv) to auto-launch at startup, while command-and-control blends encrypted traffic into legitimate platforms—stolen data uploaded as .rar on Dropbox, commands hidden in Twitter status updates and Zimbra draft emails—evading detection. Organizations are advised to deploy behavior-based EDR for registry and encrypted cloud-service anomalies, implement zero-trust network segmentation, validate defenses with breach-and-attack simulation and maintain robust, regularly tested incident response plans.

canonical_entities: exfiltrating sensitive diplomatic and policy-related data
retrieved_context.text: Since at least 2021, the Chinese state-linked APT group FishMonger—operating under the I-SOON umbrella—has waged sophisticated espionage against government institutions and NGOs in Southeast Asia and Europe, initiating attacks via spear-phishing emails that deliver template-injected Microsoft Office documents to exploit vulnerabilities or employ social engineering and deploy a Spyder loader, then install the custom “SilentBreeze” backdoor. retrieved_context.text: Dragos researchers, in collaboration with Ukraine’s CSSC, unearthed FrostyGoop—an ICS-specific malware first spotted in April and used in January to disrupt central heating in over 600 Lviv apartment buildings—marking the first known malware to leverage Modbus TCP for read/write operations on operational technology. Attackers gained initial access in April 2023 by exploiting a MikroTik router vulnerability, deployed a webshell on the router’s web server, and maintained persistence via Tor and L2TP tunnels to Moscow-based IPs. After spending months conducting reconnaissance, they extracted credentials by dumping the SAM registry hive in December, then directly issued scripted Modbus commands—read from a JSON configuration file—to publicly exposed ENCO heating controllers, even downgrading firmware to disable monitoring and force inaccurate measurements that halted heating services for nearly two days amid subzero temperatures. hits.text: Check Point Research has revealed that Void Manticore, an Iranian MOIS–affiliated threat actor operating under personas “Homeland Justice” for its 2022 Albania campaign and “Karma” for 2023–2024 Israel attacks, conducts coordinated espionage and destructive wiping operations by collaborating with Scarred Manticore (Storm-0861), which exploits CVE-2019-0604 via Foxshell and Liontail to dwell for over a year and exfiltrate emails (using LionHead), before handing victims to Void Manticore (Storm-0842) to deploy custom Windows and Linux wipers—CI Wiper, CL Wiper, partition-table LowEraser and the BiBi Wiper—thereby corrupting files and obliterating partition tables; the repetition of tactics across regions underscores a systematic, state-sponsored influence and destruction playbook and highlights the need for defenders to patch legacy SharePoint flaws, monitor for public-tool usage, implement immutable backups and share threat intelligence.

hits.text: First observed in September 2024 and active through at least August 12, 2025, the GodRAT campaign—attributed to an APT likely linked to Winnti—targets financial institutions, particularly trading and brokerage firms in Hong Kong, the UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia, by distributing malicious .scr and .pif files via Skype messenger disguised as legitimate financial documents. Evolving from the AwesomePuppet RAT on a Gh0st RAT codebase, GodRAT employs a two-stage loader architecture: an initial stub invokes SDL2.dll to allocate memory and extract XOR-decoded (key 0x63) shellcode hidden via steganography in image files named to mimic authentic financial reports, then searches for the “godinfo” marker and uses the authentication string “GETGOD” to contact C2 servers, download UPX-packed GodRAT DLL modules and launch browser credential-stealing and remote-access payloads. This advanced steganographic delivery evades signature-based defenses and underscores the need to inspect .scr/.pif attachments, monitor Skype channels, and deploy detection rules for “godinfo,” “GETGOD” and related shellcode patterns.
hits.title: New GodRAT Weaponizing Screen Saver and Program Files to Attack Organizations

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

hits.text: Since mid-2016, a cyber espionage operation dubbed Magic Hound, attributed to Iranian government–linked actors including COBALT GYPSY and showing overlaps with Rocket Kitten (Operation Saffron Rose/Ajax Security Team/Operation Woolen-Goldfish) and Newscasters (Charming Kitten/NewsBeef), has targeted energy, government and technology organizations in and tied to Saudi Arabia by distributing Word and Excel documents embedding malicious macros that launch PowerShell downloaders and droppers to deploy a custom toolkit—comprising executable and document loaders, IRC bots and the multi-platform Python-based PupyRAT—for full system access and data exfiltration; analysis by Palo Alto Networks and SecureWorks revealed domain and tool reuse with the Shamoon 2 wiper campaign, and bait lures mimicking holiday greetings, job offers and official Ministry of Health and Commerce communications, underscoring the need for enhanced macro-enablement policies, network segmentation and proactive IOC monitoring of associated domains and IRC traffic.

hits.text: Since mid-2016, an Iran-linked espionage operation dubbed “Magic Hound” has targeted energy, government and technology organizations in and around Saudi Arabia using macro-enabled Word and Excel documents masquerading as holiday cards, job offers and official Ministry of Health and Commerce files to launch PowerShell-based downloaders and custom droppers, executable and document loaders and IRC bots that ultimately deploy a Python-based Pupy RAT; Palo Alto Networks analysts—citing overlaps in domains and initial breach methods with the recent Shamoon 2 campaign—have linked Magic Hound to the Iran-aligned Rocket Kitten group, while SecureWorks attributes it to COBALT GYPSY and IBM X-Force has observed shared infrastructure, and additional code similarities tie an IRC bot to Charming Kitten/Newscaster activity and to MacDownloader tools used by other Iranian actors, underscoring the need to block malicious macros, monitor PowerShell and IRC traffic for known C2 signatures, and flag Pupy-related domains and custom loader behaviors to disrupt long-running cross-platform intrusion operations.

hits.text: Iran-linked APT Hexane (aka Lyceum/SiameseKitten), active since at least 2018 and previously focused on oil & gas and telecommunications in the Middle East and Africa, has shifted in 2021 to target Israeli IT and communications firms via sophisticated supply-chain phishing operations, ClearSky reports. Leveraging a newly expanded infrastructure to impersonate legitimate companies and HR personnel on LinkedIn, Hexane conducted a May 2021 attack on an Israeli IT provider followed by a July wave against additional organizations by luring candidates with fake job offers for roles in France, Israel and the UK. Victims are directed to a phishing site where tailored lure files deploy a dual-stage infection—first the Milan implant to establish C2 connectivity, then the DanBot RAT—to harvest data, perform espionage and move laterally, presumably to breach client networks downstream. This upgrade mirrors North Korea’s “dream job” campaigns and OilRig (APT34) activity, underscoring Hexane’s evolving tactics, renewed toolset and continued focus on supply-chain compromise to facilitate deep network infiltration.
hits.title: Report: Iranian APT Hexane Targets Israeli Companies

hits.text: Since September 2017, the Iran-aligned BladedFeline subcluster of the OilRig APT has executed persistent cyber espionage against Kurdish and Iraqi government entities, initially compromising KRG systems and a regional Uzbekistan telecom provider via an internet-facing application vulnerability and social engineering to deploy the Flog web shell. ESET’s Q4 2023–Q1 2024 report documents the group’s evolving malware arsenal: the Shahmaran backdoor for remote file manipulation, the C#/.NET Whisper (aka Veaty) email-based implant, the DNS-tunneling Spearal and its optimized variant, Optimizer, the Slippery Snakelet Python implant for command execution and data exfiltration, and tunneling tools Laret and Pinar. BladedFeline leverages a malicious IIS module, PrimeCache—akin to OilRig’s RDAT—and the Hawking Listener early-stage implant to maintain stealthy access, systematically harvesting diplomatic and financial intelligence tied to KRG oil reserves and Western relations to further Iranian strategic objectives.
hits.title: Iran-Linked BladedFeline Hits Iraqi and Kurdish Targets with Whisper and Spearal Malware

hits.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.
hits.title: Hackers with Russian Blizzard Steal Data from Rival Networks

hits.text: ESET’s updated analysis consolidates OilRig APT (aka APT34) under a parent-subgroup structure and attributes two exclusive Israeli-targeted campaigns—Outer Space (2021) and Juicy Mix (2022)—to its Lyceum subgroup, revealing a repeatable playbook in which spear-phishing VBS droppers employing arithmetic and base64 obfuscation deliver C#/.NET first-stage backdoors (Solar then its enhanced successor Mango) as scheduled Earth/Venus-style tasks that communicate via compromised Israeli websites using HTTP(S) URIs with “rt=d”/“rt=u” flags, XOR-based JupiterX encryption and Base64, and leverage the SC5k downloader (via Microsoft Exchange Web Services API) to fetch additional payloads. Post-compromise, Lyceum deployed MKG Chrome/Edge credential dumpers, Windows Credential Manager stealers and OilRig’s DanBot, Shark, Milan and Marlin backdoors to exfiltrate browser data and credentials. Code overlaps with Out to Sea, DNSpionage and HardPass campaigns—namely the MKG dumper, upload/download URI conventions, obfuscation techniques and downloader structures—solidify attribution to the Iran-linked group. Defenders should hunt for VBS scripts with obfuscation patterns, anomalous scheduled task creation (30/40-second or 14-minute intervals), EWS-based C&C traffic to non-public domains, Solar.exe/Mango.exe binaries and SC5k indicators to disrupt these data exfiltration pipelines.
hits.title: OilRig’s Outer Space and Juicy Mix: Same ol’ rig, new drill pipes

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.

retrieved_context.text: Iran-linked APT Hexane (aka Lyceum/SiameseKitten), active since at least 2018 and previously focused on oil & gas and telecommunications in the Middle East and Africa, has shifted in 2021 to target Israeli IT and communications firms via sophisticated supply-chain phishing operations, ClearSky reports. Leveraging a newly expanded infrastructure to impersonate legitimate companies and HR personnel on LinkedIn, Hexane conducted a May 2021 attack on an Israeli IT provider followed by a July wave against additional organizations by luring candidates with fake job offers for roles in France, Israel and the UK. Victims are directed to a phishing site where tailored lure files deploy a dual-stage infection—first the Milan implant to establish C2 connectivity, then the DanBot RAT—to harvest data, perform espionage and move laterally, presumably to breach client networks downstream. This upgrade mirrors North Korea’s “dream job” campaigns and OilRig (APT34) activity, underscoring Hexane’s evolving tactics, renewed toolset and continued focus on supply-chain compromise to facilitate deep network infiltration.
retrieved_context.title: Report: Iranian APT Hexane Targets Israeli Companies

retrieved_context.text: Since September 2017, the Iran-aligned BladedFeline subcluster of the OilRig APT has executed persistent cyber espionage against Kurdish and Iraqi government entities, initially compromising KRG systems and a regional Uzbekistan telecom provider via an internet-facing application vulnerability and social engineering to deploy the Flog web shell. ESET’s Q4 2023–Q1 2024 report documents the group’s evolving malware arsenal: the Shahmaran backdoor for remote file manipulation, the C#/.NET Whisper (aka Veaty) email-based implant, the DNS-tunneling Spearal and its optimized variant, Optimizer, the Slippery Snakelet Python implant for command execution and data exfiltration, and tunneling tools Laret and Pinar. BladedFeline leverages a malicious IIS module, PrimeCache—akin to OilRig’s RDAT—and the Hawking Listener early-stage implant to maintain stealthy access, systematically harvesting diplomatic and financial intelligence tied to KRG oil reserves and Western relations to further Iranian strategic objectives.
retrieved_context.title: Iran-Linked BladedFeline Hits Iraqi and Kurdish Targets with Whisper and Spearal Malware

canonical_entities: diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine
retrieved_context.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.
retrieved_context.title: Hackers with Russian Blizzard Steal Data from Rival Networks

retrieved_context.text: ESET’s updated analysis consolidates OilRig APT (aka APT34) under a parent-subgroup structure and attributes two exclusive Israeli-targeted campaigns—Outer Space (2021) and Juicy Mix (2022)—to its Lyceum subgroup, revealing a repeatable playbook in which spear-phishing VBS droppers employing arithmetic and base64 obfuscation deliver C#/.NET first-stage backdoors (Solar then its enhanced successor Mango) as scheduled Earth/Venus-style tasks that communicate via compromised Israeli websites using HTTP(S) URIs with “rt=d”/“rt=u” flags, XOR-based JupiterX encryption and Base64, and leverage the SC5k downloader (via Microsoft Exchange Web Services API) to fetch additional payloads. Post-compromise, Lyceum deployed MKG Chrome/Edge credential dumpers, Windows Credential Manager stealers and OilRig’s DanBot, Shark, Milan and Marlin backdoors to exfiltrate browser data and credentials. Code overlaps with Out to Sea, DNSpionage and HardPass campaigns—namely the MKG dumper, upload/download URI conventions, obfuscation techniques and downloader structures—solidify attribution to the Iran-linked group. Defenders should hunt for VBS scripts with obfuscation patterns, anomalous scheduled task creation (30/40-second or 14-minute intervals), EWS-based C&C traffic to non-public domains, Solar.exe/Mango.exe binaries and SC5k indicators to disrupt these data exfiltration pipelines.
retrieved_context.title: OilRig’s Outer Space and Juicy Mix: Same ol’ rig, new drill pipes

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
retrieved_context.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Check Point Research has revealed that Void Manticore, an Iranian MOIS–affiliated threat actor operating under personas “Homeland Justice” for its 2022 Albania campaign and “Karma” for 2023–2024 Israel attacks, conducts coordinated espionage and destructive wiping operations by collaborating with Scarred Manticore (Storm-0861), which exploits CVE-2019-0604 via Foxshell and Liontail to dwell for over a year and exfiltrate emails (using LionHead), before handing victims to Void Manticore (Storm-0842) to deploy custom Windows and Linux wipers—CI Wiper, CL Wiper, partition-table LowEraser and the BiBi Wiper—thereby corrupting files and obliterating partition tables; the repetition of tactics across regions underscores a systematic, state-sponsored influence and destruction playbook and highlights the need for defenders to patch legacy SharePoint flaws, monitor for public-tool usage, implement immutable backups and share threat intelligence.
hits.title: Unveiling Void Manticore: Structured Collaboration Between Espionage and Destruction in MOIS - Check Point Blog

hits.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.
hits.title: Operation Lotus Blossom: A New Nation-State Cyberthreat?

hits.text: At least four distinct campaigns exploited CVE-2023-37580, a reflected XSS zero-day in Zimbra Collaboration Suite, to siphon emails, attachments, user credentials and authentication tokens from government organizations worldwide before the July 5 hotfix and July 25 official patch; in chronological order, unidentified actors targeted Greece on June 29 via malicious URLs that, when clicked during active Zimbra sessions, deployed a data-theft framework and auto-forward rules, Winter Vivern’s APT leveraged unique exploit links to hit Moldova and Tunisia between July 11 and 25, another group used a phishing-style XSS link in Vietnam to harvest webmail credentials and exfiltrate them to a compromised government domain, and on August 25 unknown attackers employed an N-day variant to steal tokens from Pakistan’s mail servers; Google’s Threat Analysis Group warns these campaigns underscore the urgency of promptly applying open-source fixes, hardening mail-server code to prevent XSS, and maintaining vigilant patch management as attackers continuously monitor public repositories for unpatched vulnerabilities.
hits.title: APTs Swarm Zimbra Zero-Day to Steal Government Info Worldwide

hits.text: Since January 2021, Google’s Threat Analysis Group (TAG) has tracked a government-backed North Korean campaign that leverages social engineering via X (formerly Twitter) and encrypted messaging apps to befriend security researchers and deliver malicious files containing at least one unpatched 0-day in a popular software package; upon exploitation the custom shellcode performs anti-virtual-machine checks, captures system data and screenshots, and exfiltrates them to C2 infrastructure (e.g., 23.106.215[.]105, www.blgbeach[.]com), with the latest vulnerability reported and patched on September 12, 2023 (see TAG’s published RCA). In parallel, the actors published a seemingly benign Windows tool called GetSymbol on GitHub (https://github.com/dbgsymbol/) that quietly downloads debugging symbols—and arbitrary code—from attacker domains, requiring full OS reinstalls for compromised hosts. TAG has added malicious sites to Safe Browsing, issued government-backed attacker alerts to targeted Gmail and Workspace users, and urges researchers to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing, keep software up to date, and verify system integrity after using third-party tools.
hits.title: Active North Korean campaign targeting security researchers

hits.text: ESET researchers uncovered a novel crimeware campaign, active in Czechia since November 2023 and paused only by the arrest of a suspect in March 2024, in which attackers combined social engineering, phishing and Android malware to target clients of three Czech banks via deceptive SMS links to malicious progressive web apps (PWAs) and WebAPKs; after harvesting credentials, the attackers lured victims into installing NGate, a custom Android malware named for its incorporation of the open-source NFCGate tool, which relays NFC data from victims’ unrooted smartphones to an attacker’s rooted device, enabling the emulation of cloned payment cards and unauthorized ATM withdrawals (over 160,000 CZK recovered from just three recent victims, with likely higher overall losses), with a fallback tactic of illicit bank-to-bank transfers when the relay method fails.
hits.title: NGate Android malware relays NFC traffic to steal cash

hits.text: Since mid-November 2024, Russian nation-state actor Star Blizzard has significantly escalated its evasion tradecraft following public exposure by Microsoft Threat Intelligence: shifting from a single registrar (NameCheap) to multiple registrars (Hostinger, RealTime Register, GMO Internet) and implementing multi-stage redirection chains—embedding Microsoft 365 Safe Links in PDF lures that pass through Bitly and Cuttly shortened URLs and legitimate open-redirect sites (e.g., mechengsys[.]net) before landing on an Evilginx-equipped VPS (vidmemax[.]com)—to mount AiTM spear-phishing campaigns that harvest email credentials, including MFA tokens. Between July and August 2024 they also experimented with altered OneDrive file-share notifications—using ProtonMail accounts to spoof trusted senders and rewire the “Open” button URL to their Evilginx infrastructure—targeting individuals in politics, diplomacy, NGOs and think tanks. In October 2024, Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit disrupted core infrastructure, and ongoing collaboration with UK NCSC, NSA and FBI ensures rapid customer notification and defenses. Historically, since 2022 Star Blizzard has iteratively refined detection evasion—employing server-side fingerprinting scripts, HubSpot and MailerLite email platforms to mask domains, DNS obfuscation, password-protected PDFs and randomized DGAs—with each ephemeral TTP swiftly modified, underscoring the need for continuous updates to email security controls, link inspection and behavioral detection.
hits.title: Star Blizzard increases sophistication and evasion in ongoing attacks | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

hits.text: Since at least April 2024 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a Russia-affiliated cyberespionage actor dubbed Void Blizzard (aka LAUNDRY BEAR) conducting high-volume, targeted operations against government, defense, transportation, media, NGO and healthcare organizations—particularly in NATO member states and Ukraine—by leveraging stolen credentials procured via commodity infostealer ecosystems for password spray attacks and Exchange/SharePoint Online access, then automating bulk email and file collection (and in some cases Teams messages) via cloud APIs and tools like AzureHound; in April 2025 the actor evolved to adversary-in-the-middle spear phishing using a typosquatted domain and the open-source Evilginx framework with a malicious QR-coded PDF to harvest Entra authentication data; this widespread success underscores that even unsophisticated TTPs pose major intelligence risks to critical sectors, so organizations should enforce sign-in risk policies and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO/passkeys), centralize identity management with Conditional Access, monitor risky sign-ins and mailbox auditing, apply least-privilege credential hygiene, and promptly rotate credentials after infostealer detections to disrupt Void Blizzard’s operations.

hits.text: On March 2, 2025, CyberMaterial’s report on Void Manticore (aka Storm-0842, linked to the cybercriminal Storm-1811 cluster) details a coordinated espionage campaign that began in late 2024 against aerospace, defense and government organizations in Europe and North America: operators initiated intrusions via spear-phishing emails embedding weaponized RTFs exploiting CVE-2024-4113 to drop a custom loader (“VoidLoader”), which in turn deployed the “ManticoreShell” backdoor; post-compromise activities included credential harvesting (Mimikatz), lateral movement via PSExec and WMI, privilege escalation through a signed kernel-mode driver exploit, and persistence using registry Run keys and scheduled tasks; C2 communications leveraged HTTPS with a domain generation algorithm (DGA) and fallback to TOR. Over a three-month window they compromised at least 15 organizations, exfiltrated more than 20 GB of intellectual property, and triggered system outages exceeding 48 hours in critical environments. Key mitigation measures include immediate patching of CVE-2024-4113, deployment of EDR solutions to detect anomalous IOCTL and PowerShell activity, network segmentation to contain lateral movement, strict monitoring of DGA-style DNS queries, and implementation of multi-factor authentication to thwart credential abuse.
hits.title: Void Manticore (Storm-0842) – Threat Actor - CyberMaterial

canonical_entities: diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine
hits.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.
hits.title: Hackers with Russian Blizzard Steal Data from Rival Networks

hits.text: Originally released by the Chinese C.Rufus Security Team in March 2008, the open-source Gh0st RAT has reemerged in late August 2023 as SugarGh0st RAT, deployed by a China-linked actor against South Korean targets and Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs via phishing-delivered archives containing Windows .LNK shortcuts that execute embedded JavaScript, display customized decoy documents, and install the 32-bit C++ DLL. The backdoor collects system data, grants full remote control—including process and file manipulation, log removal, keylogging, screenshot and camera access, and arbitrary command execution—and now evades legacy detection by altering its C2 protocol packet header from 5 to 8 magic bytes. Cisco Talos highlights these cosmetic yet effective modifications as a blind spot in signature-based defenses, underscoring the urgent need for updated heuristics and layered monitoring.
hits.title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
hits.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia
hits.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.
hits.title: Operation Lotus Blossom: A New Nation-State Cyberthreat?

hits.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.

canonical_entities: Scanning the Internet for IoT devices with open Telnet/SSH ports
Use of default or weak credentials
Encrypted SOCKS5 tunneling to proxy infrastructure
hits.text: Researchers have uncovered that since early 2024 a previously undocumented botnet, dubbed Ngioweb, has been systematically scanning the Internet for IoT devices—primarily DVRs, IP cameras and home routers—with open Telnet/SSH ports and default or weak credentials, exploiting known firmware vulnerabilities to deploy a lightweight Go-based loader that establishes encrypted SOCKS5 tunnels back to a resilient NSOCKS residential proxy network of over 150,000 infected nodes. Once a device is compromised, Ngioweb drops a persistent agent that connects to fast-flux C2 domains via HTTPS, retrieves updated encryption keys and proxy configuration, and registers the node for NSOCKS’ tiered subscription service (starting at $25/month), which reportedly generates upwards of $500K in monthly revenue by fueling large-scale credential-stuffing campaigns, ad fraud and DDoS-for-hire operations. The actors behind Ngioweb continually rotate fallback C2 domains, employ encryption and obfuscation to evade signature-based detection, and monitor infection success rates in real time, enabling rapid retooling and expansion. Defenders are urged to enforce strong, unique credentials on all IoT assets, disable unused management interfaces, apply timely firmware updates, implement network segmentation and deploy behavioral analytics or honeypots to detect anomalous outbound proxy traffic.
hits.title: Ngioweb Botnet Fuels NSOCKS Residential Proxy Network Exploiting IoT Devices

retrieval_events.query: How has the operational approach of the threat actor evolved according to the reports BLOG-267, BLOG-242, and BLOG-235?

retrieved_context.text: Check Point Research has revealed that Void Manticore, an Iranian MOIS–affiliated threat actor operating under personas “Homeland Justice” for its 2022 Albania campaign and “Karma” for 2023–2024 Israel attacks, conducts coordinated espionage and destructive wiping operations by collaborating with Scarred Manticore (Storm-0861), which exploits CVE-2019-0604 via Foxshell and Liontail to dwell for over a year and exfiltrate emails (using LionHead), before handing victims to Void Manticore (Storm-0842) to deploy custom Windows and Linux wipers—CI Wiper, CL Wiper, partition-table LowEraser and the BiBi Wiper—thereby corrupting files and obliterating partition tables; the repetition of tactics across regions underscores a systematic, state-sponsored influence and destruction playbook and highlights the need for defenders to patch legacy SharePoint flaws, monitor for public-tool usage, implement immutable backups and share threat intelligence.
retrieved_context.title: Unveiling Void Manticore: Structured Collaboration Between Espionage and Destruction in MOIS - Check Point Blog

canonical_entities: diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine
retrieved_context.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.
retrieved_context.title: Hackers with Russian Blizzard Steal Data from Rival Networks

canonical_entities: Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of the Interior
retrieved_context.text: Moses Staff, also dubbed Cobalt Sapling, is an Iran-linked APT active since November 2020 and publicly identified in September 2021, originally posting 16 leak events of Israeli corporate data and personal information of IDF intelligence personnel by December 2022 using a toolkit comprising the PyDCrypt custom loader, DCSrv cryptographic wiper, StrifeWater RAT and its DriveGuard monitoring utility; in November 2022, Secureworks attributed a new hacktivist persona, Abraham’s Ax—featuring similar biblical branding, Tor-hosted leak sites on adjacent subnets and recycled “Hollywood-style” hacking videos—to the same operators, who have since shifted toward exfiltrating and leaking data from Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of the Interior (including a purported intercepted ministerial phone conversation) rather than directly attacking Israel, likely in response to Saudi-Israeli rapprochement, while Moses Staff continues operations (claiming a CCTV system hack at an Israeli terror site); these insights highlight the urgency for Saudi and Israeli government entities to strengthen network segmentation, deploy advanced endpoint detection for known Iranian toolsets, monitor darknet leak platforms and prepare incident response plans tailored to politically motivated exfiltration campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Iranian APT Leaks Data From Saudi Arabia Government Under New Persona

retrieved_context.text: Since mid-2016, a cyber espionage operation dubbed Magic Hound, attributed to Iranian government–linked actors including COBALT GYPSY and showing overlaps with Rocket Kitten (Operation Saffron Rose/Ajax Security Team/Operation Woolen-Goldfish) and Newscasters (Charming Kitten/NewsBeef), has targeted energy, government and technology organizations in and tied to Saudi Arabia by distributing Word and Excel documents embedding malicious macros that launch PowerShell downloaders and droppers to deploy a custom toolkit—comprising executable and document loaders, IRC bots and the multi-platform Python-based PupyRAT—for full system access and data exfiltration; analysis by Palo Alto Networks and SecureWorks revealed domain and tool reuse with the Shamoon 2 wiper campaign, and bait lures mimicking holiday greetings, job offers and official Ministry of Health and Commerce communications, underscoring the need for enhanced macro-enablement policies, network segmentation and proactive IOC monitoring of associated domains and IRC traffic.
retrieved_context.title: Iranian hackers behind the Magic Hound campaign linked to Shamoon

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
retrieved_context.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
retrieved_context.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia
retrieved_context.text: In their June 16, 2015 report, Unit 42 unveiled Operation Lotus Blossom, a three-year, state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign against military and government organizations in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia, in which over 50 spearphishing attacks exploited enticing subject lines and decoy personnel-roster documents to deploy the custom “Elise” Trojan backdoor in three variants capable of evading virtual-machine analysis, contacting C2 servers for instructions and exfiltrating data; Unit 42’s use of Palo Alto Networks’ AutoFocus and WildFire platforms enabled the rapid correlation of samples and the deployment of IPS signature 14358 to block Elise, and they recommend that defenders review the published indicators of compromise in the full report and GitHub repo, bolster email security controls and ensure WildFire and Threat Prevention signatures are properly implemented to thwart future Lotus Blossom intrusions.
retrieved_context.title: Operation Lotus Blossom: A New Nation-State Cyberthreat?

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed the Russia-based SVR actor Midnight Blizzard (aka NOBELIUM, APT29/UNC2452/Cozy Bear) launch a highly targeted social-engineering campaign since at least late May 2023 by leveraging previously compromised small-business Microsoft 365 tenants to create security-themed onmicrosoft.com domains and Teams accounts that masquerade as technical-support entities; attackers then initiate Microsoft Teams chat requests to elicit approval of MFA prompts or codes via Microsoft Authenticator, enabling credential theft, access to fewer than 40 global organizations across government, NGOs, IT services, technology, manufacturing and media sectors, and subsequent post-compromise activities including data exfiltration and attempts to add managed devices via Microsoft Entra ID to bypass conditional access. Microsoft has mitigated the malicious domains, directly notified affected customers, and recommends phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, Microsoft Teams best practices, auditing, and user education to detect and prevent unsolicited MFA requests.
retrieved_context.title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

retrieved_context.text: Since at least April 2024 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a Russia-affiliated cyberespionage actor dubbed Void Blizzard (aka LAUNDRY BEAR) conducting high-volume, targeted operations against government, defense, transportation, media, NGO and healthcare organizations—particularly in NATO member states and Ukraine—by leveraging stolen credentials procured via commodity infostealer ecosystems for password spray attacks and Exchange/SharePoint Online access, then automating bulk email and file collection (and in some cases Teams messages) via cloud APIs and tools like AzureHound; in April 2025 the actor evolved to adversary-in-the-middle spear phishing using a typosquatted domain and the open-source Evilginx framework with a malicious QR-coded PDF to harvest Entra authentication data; this widespread success underscores that even unsophisticated TTPs pose major intelligence risks to critical sectors, so organizations should enforce sign-in risk policies and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO/passkeys), centralize identity management with Conditional Access, monitor risky sign-ins and mailbox auditing, apply least-privilege credential hygiene, and promptly rotate credentials after infostealer detections to disrupt Void Blizzard’s operations.
retrieved_context.title: New Russia-affiliated actor Void Blizzard targets critical sectors for espionage | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: Scanning the Internet for IoT devices with open Telnet/SSH ports
Use of default or weak credentials
Encrypted SOCKS5 tunneling to proxy infrastructure
retrieved_context.text: Researchers have uncovered that since early 2024 a previously undocumented botnet, dubbed Ngioweb, has been systematically scanning the Internet for IoT devices—primarily DVRs, IP cameras and home routers—with open Telnet/SSH ports and default or weak credentials, exploiting known firmware vulnerabilities to deploy a lightweight Go-based loader that establishes encrypted SOCKS5 tunnels back to a resilient NSOCKS residential proxy network of over 150,000 infected nodes. Once a device is compromised, Ngioweb drops a persistent agent that connects to fast-flux C2 domains via HTTPS, retrieves updated encryption keys and proxy configuration, and registers the node for NSOCKS’ tiered subscription service (starting at $25/month), which reportedly generates upwards of $500K in monthly revenue by fueling large-scale credential-stuffing campaigns, ad fraud and DDoS-for-hire operations. The actors behind Ngioweb continually rotate fallback C2 domains, employ encryption and obfuscation to evade signature-based detection, and monitor infection success rates in real time, enabling rapid retooling and expansion. Defenders are urged to enforce strong, unique credentials on all IoT assets, disable unused management interfaces, apply timely firmware updates, implement network segmentation and deploy behavioral analytics or honeypots to detect anomalous outbound proxy traffic.
retrieved_context.title: Ngioweb Botnet Fuels NSOCKS Residential Proxy Network Exploiting IoT Devices

hits.text: Between May and September 2024, threat actors tracked as "Jumpy Pisces" (also known as Andariel, APT45, DarkSeoul, Nickel Hyatt, Onyx Sleet, Operation Troy, Silent Chollima, Stonefly)—affiliated with North Korea's Reconnaissance General Bureau and active since 2009—collaborated with the Play ransomware group (also called Balloonfly, Fiddling Scorpius, PlayCrypt) in what Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 described as "the first recorded collaboration between the Jumpy Pisces North Korean state-sponsored group and an underground ransomware network"; initial access came via compromised user account in May 2024, followed by lateral movement and persistence using Sliver C2 framework and Dtrack backdoor (aka Valefor, Preft), with communication to C2 server 172.96.137[.]224 continuing until early September before Play ransomware deployment; pre-ransomware activities included credential harvesting, privilege escalation, EDR sensor uninstallation, and trojanized binary harvesting web browser history and credit card details from Chrome, Edge, and Brave; Andariel previously deployed SHATTEREDGLASS and Maui ransomware strains and targeted three U.S. organizations in August 2024 in financially-motivated attacks without ransomware deployment; the collaboration suggests North Korean actors may conduct widespread ransomware operations to evade sanctions and generate revenue.
hits.title: North Korean Group Collaborates with Play Ransomware in Significant Cyber Attack

hits.text: The North Korea-linked threat actor Slow Pisces (also tracked as Jade Sleet, PUKCHONG, TraderTraitor, and UNC4899) has been conducting a multi-stage malware campaign targeting cryptocurrency developers via LinkedIn job opportunity lures since at least June 2024, leveraging trojanized Python and JavaScript projects hosted on GitHub that employ YAML deserialization and EJS templating to execute gated payloads only to validated targets meeting specific criteria (IP address, geolocation, time, HTTP headers); the campaign delivers RN Loader and RN Stealer malware on macOS systems capable of harvesting system metadata, installed applications, SSH keys, AWS/Kubernetes/Google Cloud configuration files, and iCloud Keychain data, with payloads remaining memory-resident and deployed selectively to prevent analysis; Slow Pisces is assessed to be responsible for the February 2025 Bybit cryptocurrency exchange breach and operates alongside other North Korean clusters including Operation Dream Job, Contagious Interview, Alluring Pisces, and Moonstone Sleet, though with notably superior operational security practices involving heavily guarded payload delivery across infection stages.
hits.title: Crypto Developers Targeted by Python Malware Disguised as Coding Challenges

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys
