retrieved_context.text: In late 2023, researchers uncovered a sophisticated Taiwan-focused espionage operation in which a China-linked APT actor (likely APT27) hijacked an abandoned Sogou Zhuyin Windows update server—vacated when Sogou ceased Zhuyin support in mid-2022—and weaponized it to distribute a trojanized updater (SHA-256: 3f5c…) that deployed a custom backdoor and Cobalt Strike beacon via HTTP(S) (MITRE T1195.002, T1071.001). This incident underscores the risk of unmaintained update infrastructure in software supply-chain compromises and highlights the need for regular decommissioning audits, code signing validation, and network segmentation to mitigate such persistent threats.

canonical_entities: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
retrieved_context.text: In late 2023, researchers uncovered a sophisticated Taiwan-focused espionage operation in which a China-linked APT actor (likely APT27) hijacked an abandoned Sogou Zhuyin Windows update server—vacated when Sogou ceased Zhuyin support in mid-2022—and weaponized it to distribute a trojanized updater (SHA-256: 3f5c…) that deployed a custom backdoor and Cobalt Strike beacon via HTTP(S) (MITRE T1195.002, T1071.001). Initial access was achieved by swapping the legitimate SogouZhuyinUpdater.exe with the malicious variant, which installed a loader employing code-injection and obfuscation to evade AV detection; post-deployment techniques included Mimikatz for credential harvesting (T1003.001) and encrypted exfiltration of 2 GB of sensitive defense and policy documents from at least five Taiwanese government and research organizations (T1041). This incident underscores the risk of unmaintained update infrastructure in software supply-chain compromises and highlights the need for regular decommissioning audits, code signing validation, and network segmentation to mitigate such persistent threats.
retrieved_context.title: Abandoned Sogou Zhuyin Update Server Hijacked, Weaponized in Taiwan Espionage Campaign

canonical_entities: Palo Alto Networks Cortex XDR Anti-Ransomware
retrieved_context.text: Following the sale of INC ransomware source code in March 2024 and its initial appearance in August 2023, researchers in July 2024 uncovered Lynx ransomware, a Windows-only, C++-based RaaS variant that shares ~48% of INC’s functions (70.8% among common routines) and has been deployed against U.S. and U.K. retail, real estate, architecture, financial and environmental service firms via phishing, malicious downloads and underground forums; employing AES-128-CTR and Curve25519 Donna for encryption with a .lynx extension, it conducts double-extortion by exfiltrating victims’ data (published on lynxblog[.]net under a policy excluding governments, hospitals and non-profits) before encrypting all files by default—killing processes, encrypting network shares and hidden disks, deleting shadow copies and backups, leveraging the Restart Manager API to target in-use files, and printing a OneNote report—then dropping a README.txt ransom note; this evolution of RaaS underscores the need for organizations to adopt robust cybersecurity measures, including anti-phishing training, backup hardening, dynamic and behavioral detections via Palo Alto Networks’ Cortex XDR Anti-Ransomware and Advanced WildFire, and vigilant monitoring of Indicators of Compromise such as published SHA256 hashes to mitigate high-profile, code-reused ransomware campaigns.
retrieved_context.title: Lynx Ransomware: A Rebranding of INC Ransomware

retrieved_context.text: A zero-day VPN vulnerability provided initial access for a sophisticated threat actor who employed publicly available penetration‐testing and exploitation tools—SoftPerfect Network Scanner for network discovery, PsExec to deploy ServeManager.exe (the FiveHands ransomware variant using lattice-based NTRUEncrypt public key cryptography), and SombRAT for remote information theft—alongside RouterScan, grabff.exe, rclone.exe, and s3browser-9-5-3.exe to harvest credentials and exfiltrate data. Once inside, the attacker leveraged Windows Management Instrumentation (T1047) to enumerate and delete Volume Shadow Copies (Inhibit System Recovery, T1490), encrypted files (including those in recovery folders) for impact (T1486), and dropped ransom notes across directories, demanding payment to restore access. Post-encryption activities align with MITRE techniques such as Access Token Manipulation, Boot or Logon Autostart, PowerShell command and scripting interpreter, Domain Trust Discovery, Process Discovery, Screen Capture, and Kerberoasting. The combined use of FiveHands ransomware and SombRAT RAT resulted in both data theft and destruction of backup artifacts, underscoring the need for proactive patch management, network segmentation, strict credential hygiene, and rapid incident response to mitigate novel lattice-based encryption threats.
retrieved_context.title: FiveHands Ransomware Overview

canonical_entities: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
retrieved_context.text: NCC Group’s RIFT team uncovered a sophisticated new FiveHands ransomware variant deployed by an affiliate linked to UNC2447, who gained initial access in June 2021 by exploiting a SonicWall VPN appliance—evidenced by a “command0/Commando” login from source port 4444 (Metasploit default)—then moved laterally via RDP (T1021.001) using the weak password “Remark123!” and PsExec (T1059.003). The actor leveraged publicly available tools—SoftPerfect Netscan and Advanced Port Scanner for network discovery (T1046), AllInOnePasswordRecoveryPro for credential harvesting (T1003.001), Remote Utilities (“Hostclean.exe”) for persistent C2 (T1219), and pCloud (“pCloud.exe”) for exfiltration (T1567.002), caching 10 GB of stolen data under %AppData%\pCloud\CacheCached—to stage and extract sensitive files. The Go-written loader (“Encryptor.exe”) accepts a 16-byte key (captured via RDP bitmap cache and brute force) to decrypt a unique C++ ransomware payload in memory, which uses RSA/AES (Mbed TLS) to encrypt files in blocks (.crypt/.crypt) while excluding system folders and leveraging Windows Restart Manager to breach locked files. This RaaS model (hijacking hardcoded TOR IDs) employs aggressive extortion tactics—spoofed caller ID calls urging prompt payment—and underscores the need for robust VPN log monitoring, RDP restrictions, enforceable command-line auditing, multi-factor authentication, and forensic examination of cloud‐sync caches to detect and mitigate similar intrusions.
retrieved_context.title: Handy guide to a new Fivehands ransomware variant

canonical_entities: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager
retrieved_context.text: Water Ouroboros is a Ransomware-as-a-Service operation that exploits public-facing Oracle WebLogic vulnerabilities (CVE-2019-2725, CVE-2017-10271, CVE-2019-2729) or drive-by installers for initial access (T1190, T1189), then executes remote Windows commands (wmic.exe, bcdedit.exe, wbadmin.exe, vssadmin.exe) to delete backups and disable recovery (T1490, T1562.001) before encrypting fixed, removable and network drives via a Go-based custom routine that uses RTLGenRandom to generate a symmetric key, protects it with embedded RSA public keys (App_ExportKey), appends “.locked” (unless suppressed with –E), excludes over 60 file extensions, and accepts credentials (c {user}:{pass}), logging (–a), non-aggressive (–A) and size filters (–m). Victims find Contact Us.txt ransom notes pointing to a TOR payment site and Hive Leaks data-dump threat. Post-infection, actors maintain access via compromised admin accounts (T1078), disable security tools (PCHunter, ProcessHacker), dump credentials from registry hives (T1003.002), move laterally over RDP/SMB (T1021.001/002), discover assets via AdFind (T1595.002) and exfiltrate data over C&C (SharpRhino RAT/T1071.001, T1041). With 136 incidents in the US and notable impacts on construction, IT, manufacturing and healthcare SMBs, the campaign underscores the need for timely patching, hardened public-facing apps, least-privilege access, MFA, robust backups and advanced threat detection.

canonical_entities: inject the decoded first-stage shellcode into legitimate processes
hits.text: In September 2024, a Winnti-linked APT began targeting trading and brokerage firms by distributing malicious .scr/.pif screen saver files via Skype that use steganographically embedded shellcode to load GodRAT—a new Gh0st RAT variant evolved from the AwesomePuppet backdoor—into legitimate processes. Two loader types (one with XOR-encoded shellcode bytes, one extracting shellcode from JPG images via an expired Valve.exe/SDL2.dll signed binary) allocate memory, inject the decoded first-stage shellcode, decode configuration data (single-byte XOR key 0x63, “godinfo” header), and fetch a UPX-packed GodRAT DLL from C2. GodRAT launches under a “-Puppet” flag in curl.exe or cmd.exe, collects OS, host, AV, process and user metadata, and communicates over zlib-compressed, triple-XOR TCP channels. It supports in-memory plugin injection—deploying a FileManager plugin for file enumeration, manipulation and 7zip-based extraction—and installs Chrome and Edge password stealers in %ALLUSERSPROFILE%. AsyncRAT serves as a secondary fallback implant. Ongoing detections (12 MD5s across Hong Kong, UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia) through August 12 2025 highlight sustained financial credential theft and long-term C2 persistence.
hits.title: Gh0st RAT-based GodRAT attacks financial organizations

canonical_entities: installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry
hits.text: The Lotus Blossom APT (aka Lotus Panda, Billbug, Spring Dragon) has stepped up cyberespionage against APAC government targets by deploying new Sagerunex backdoor variants and abusing Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) for stealthy post-exploitation and lateral movement, enabling remote command execution without additional malware. Initial access methods include spear-phishing, watering-hole attacks and exploiting public-facing application flaws; once inside, operators run reconnaissance commands (tasklist, ipconfig, netstat), harvest credentials with Chrome cookie stealers, compress data via RAR and relay traffic through custom Venom proxies or proxy configurations when direct internet access is blocked. Persistence is achieved by installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry under hijacked service names (tapisrv, swprv) to auto-launch at startup, while command-and-control blends encrypted traffic into legitimate platforms—stolen data uploaded as .rar on Dropbox, commands hidden in Twitter status updates and Zimbra draft emails—evading detection. Organizations are advised to deploy behavior-based EDR for registry and encrypted cloud-service anomalies, implement zero-trust network segmentation, validate defenses with breach-and-attack simulation and maintain robust, regularly tested incident response plans.
hits.title: Lotus Blossom APT Exploits WMI for Post-Exploitation Activities

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
hits.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: hijacks the loading of a legitimate DLL
hits.text: Trend Micro researchers have uncovered a new Chinese-speaking APT dubbed Earth Berberoka (aka GamblingPuppet) that targets online gambling websites on Windows, macOS and Linux by deploying both legacy (PlugX, Gh0st RAT) and novel malware, most notably a five-stage loader called PuppetLoader and a Go-based oRAT. PuppetLoader’s Stage 1 decrypts an initial payload with a flawed RC4 implementation (key “2726c6aea9970bb95211304705b5f595”), then stealthily hijacks the loading of a legitimate DLL (asycfilt.dll) via hooked NTDLL APIs (NtOpenFile, NtMapViewOfSection, RtlPushFrame/RtlPopFrame) to rebase and execute a malicious lz32.dll; Stage 2 drops marker files (CPuppetProcessFileSharer with GUID 78106D5F-CD1A-A8C4-A625-6863092B4BBA, Config.ini encrypted with “whk0q9ogev6ofg8d”), MSVCPX00.dll and BMP stagers; Stage 3’s BasicLoader scans Users\Public directories for 33×11-pixel BMPs containing encrypted payloads; Stage 4’s Core module logs activity via custom RC4-encrypted entries delimited by 0xAABBCCDD and supports -NoModuleLoadDLL and -LoadShellcode flags; and Stage 5’s MainConsole client written in C++ provides interactive shell, file upload/download, process listing, module installation and RDP enumeration over a custom RC4-encrypted UDP protocol with specific packet types (RemoteModuleCommandPacket, FileTransferContent_Packet, InstallModulePacket, etc.). Concurrently, oRAT droppers packaged as an Electron MiMi chat app and a macOS DMG carry AES-GCM-encrypted Go configurations enabling gateway or traffic-forwarder modes and expose HTTP(S)/QUIC routes (e.g., GET/POST /agent/info, /agent/upload) for direct code execution. This multivector, multiplatform campaign highlights the critical need to monitor anomalous DLL load behavior, bitmap steganography, flawed RC4/AES-GCM decryption routines and custom UDP or HTTP traffic on gambling infrastructures.
hits.title: New APT Group Earth Berberoka Targets Gambling Websites With Old and New Malware | Trend Micro (US)

hits.text: New research reveals that over 80,000 Hikvision cameras worldwide remain unpatched against the critical CVE-2021-36260 command-injection flaw (NIST score 9.8/10) disclosed last fall, allowing remote code execution and potential espionage by state-linked groups such as MISSION2025/APT41, APT10 and unknown Russian actors trading stolen credentials on dark-web forums; systemic deficiencies—default or hardcoded passwords, no auto-update mechanism, poor forensics and lack of security-by-design—have left devices in 100+ countries (including the U.S., despite an FCC “unacceptable risk” designation) continuously discoverable via Shodan or Censys and ripe for exploitation, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to inventory IoT assets, change default credentials, deploy available patches and improve visibility and update processes to mitigate geopolitical and operational impact.
hits.title: Cybercriminals Are Selling Access to Chinese Surveillance Cameras | Threatpost

canonical_entities: exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services
harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive
hits.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.
hits.title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

canonical_entities: deployed a webshell on the router’s web server
Credentials from Password Stores: Security Account Manager
hits.text: Dragos researchers, in collaboration with Ukraine’s CSSC, unearthed FrostyGoop—an ICS-specific malware first spotted in April and used in January to disrupt central heating in over 600 Lviv apartment buildings—marking the first known malware to leverage Modbus TCP for read/write operations on operational technology. Attackers gained initial access in April 2023 by exploiting a MikroTik router vulnerability, deployed a webshell on the router’s web server, and maintained persistence via Tor and L2TP tunnels to Moscow-based IPs. After spending months conducting reconnaissance, they extracted credentials by dumping the SAM registry hive in December, then directly issued scripted Modbus commands—read from a JSON configuration file—to publicly exposed ENCO heating controllers, even downgrading firmware to disable monitoring and force inaccurate measurements that halted heating services for nearly two days amid subzero temperatures. This incident underscores the threat posed by internet-exposed ICS devices—over 46,000 globally using Modbus—and highlights poor network segmentation, unpatched ICS CVEs, and the ease with which FrostyGoop’s protocol-agnostic payload can be repurposed against diverse industrial controllers, necessitating immediate network segmentation, firmware monitoring, and patch management in OT environments.
hits.title: ICS malware FrostyGoop disrupted heating in Ukraine, remains threat to OT worldwide

hits.text: Since its emergence in 2013, Iran-linked APT35 (aka Charming Kitten/Phosphorus) has executed a series of high-value espionage campaigns—beginning with a 2014 social-media spying operation—and continued in 2019 with spear-phishing against U.S., French and Middle East academic institutions before Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit seized control of 99 APT35 domains; in late 2020 the group targeted oncology, genetics and neurology researchers in Israel and the U.S. via its “BadBlood” PDF-based spear-phishing campaign, while in 2021 it chained Exchange Server flaws (ProxyShell) for network intrusion and demonstrated TTP overlaps with Momento ransomware (CVE-2021-21972 exploiter); in January 2022 it performed mass Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) scans—over 80 percent of attempts originated in the U.S.—and later deployed a stealthy .NET-based PowerShell backdoor (“PowerLess”) that runs in-process to avoid detection, followed by Hyperscrape, a Windows .NET mailbox exfiltration tool for Outlook, Gmail and Yahoo! that quietly harvests emails once the actor possesses valid credentials or session cookies, and a companion Telegram dump utility; APT35 maintains persistence for intelligence collection or monetizes access when systems lack strategic value, underscoring the need for timely patching, multi-factor authentication and continuous monitoring.

hits.text: ESET researchers disclosed MoustachedBouncer, a Belarus-aligned cyberespionage group active since at least 2014 targeting foreign embassies in Belarus, employing two parallel malware frameworks: the email-based NightClub (SMTP/IMAP C2) and its 2020-onward successor Disco (Go/.NET) delivered via adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) at ISP level—likely leveraging Belarus’s SORM lawful interception—to redirect Windows captive portal checks to a fake Windows Update page. This page loads jdrop.js to prompt a malicious installer, which schedules SMB-delivered OfficeBroker payloads from attacker-injected Google Cloud IPs. Both frameworks support plugins for screenshots, audio recording and file theft. ESET observed compromises of embassies from four continents and assesses medium confidence in state alignment and low confidence in cooperation with Winter Vivern. Recommendations include out-of-band encrypted VPNs to thwart ISP-level interception.

canonical_entities: inject the decoded first-stage shellcode into legitimate processes
retrieved_context.text: In September 2024, a Winnti-linked APT began targeting trading and brokerage firms by distributing malicious .scr/.pif screen saver files via Skype that use steganographically embedded shellcode to load GodRAT—a new Gh0st RAT variant evolved from the AwesomePuppet backdoor—into legitimate processes. Two loader types (one with XOR-encoded shellcode bytes, one extracting shellcode from JPG images via an expired Valve.exe/SDL2.dll signed binary) allocate memory, inject the decoded first-stage shellcode, decode configuration data (single-byte XOR key 0x63, “godinfo” header), and fetch a UPX-packed GodRAT DLL from C2. GodRAT launches under a “-Puppet” flag in curl.exe or cmd.exe, collects OS, host, AV, process and user metadata, and communicates over zlib-compressed, triple-XOR TCP channels. It supports in-memory plugin injection—deploying a FileManager plugin for file enumeration, manipulation and 7zip-based extraction—and installs Chrome and Edge password stealers in %ALLUSERSPROFILE%. AsyncRAT serves as a secondary fallback implant. Ongoing detections (12 MD5s across Hong Kong, UAE, Jordan, Lebanon and Malaysia) through August 12 2025 highlight sustained financial credential theft and long-term C2 persistence.
retrieved_context.title: Gh0st RAT-based GodRAT attacks financial organizations

canonical_entities: installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry
retrieved_context.text: The Lotus Blossom APT (aka Lotus Panda, Billbug, Spring Dragon) has stepped up cyberespionage against APAC government targets by deploying new Sagerunex backdoor variants and abusing Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) for stealthy post-exploitation and lateral movement, enabling remote command execution without additional malware. Initial access methods include spear-phishing, watering-hole attacks and exploiting public-facing application flaws; once inside, operators run reconnaissance commands (tasklist, ipconfig, netstat), harvest credentials with Chrome cookie stealers, compress data via RAR and relay traffic through custom Venom proxies or proxy configurations when direct internet access is blocked. Persistence is achieved by installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry under hijacked service names (tapisrv, swprv) to auto-launch at startup, while command-and-control blends encrypted traffic into legitimate platforms—stolen data uploaded as .rar on Dropbox, commands hidden in Twitter status updates and Zimbra draft emails—evading detection. Organizations are advised to deploy behavior-based EDR for registry and encrypted cloud-service anomalies, implement zero-trust network segmentation, validate defenses with breach-and-attack simulation and maintain robust, regularly tested incident response plans.
retrieved_context.title: Lotus Blossom APT Exploits WMI for Post-Exploitation Activities

Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
retrieved_context.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
retrieved_context.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

canonical_entities: hijacks the loading of a legitimate DLL
retrieved_context.text: Trend Micro researchers have uncovered a new Chinese-speaking APT dubbed Earth Berberoka (aka GamblingPuppet) that targets online gambling websites on Windows, macOS and Linux by deploying both legacy (PlugX, Gh0st RAT) and novel malware, most notably a five-stage loader called PuppetLoader and a Go-based oRAT. PuppetLoader’s Stage 1 decrypts an initial payload with a flawed RC4 implementation (key “2726c6aea9970bb95211304705b5f595”), then stealthily hijacks the loading of a legitimate DLL (asycfilt.dll) via hooked NTDLL APIs (NtOpenFile, NtMapViewOfSection, RtlPushFrame/RtlPopFrame) to rebase and execute a malicious lz32.dll; Stage 2 drops marker files (CPuppetProcessFileSharer with GUID 78106D5F-CD1A-A8C4-A625-6863092B4BBA, Config.ini encrypted with “whk0q9ogev6ofg8d”), MSVCPX00.dll and BMP stagers; Stage 3’s BasicLoader scans Users\Public directories for 33×11-pixel BMPs containing encrypted payloads; Stage 4’s Core module logs activity via custom RC4-encrypted entries delimited by 0xAABBCCDD and supports -NoModuleLoadDLL and -LoadShellcode flags; and Stage 5’s MainConsole client written in C++ provides interactive shell, file upload/download, process listing, module installation and RDP enumeration over a custom RC4-encrypted UDP protocol with specific packet types (RemoteModuleCommandPacket, FileTransferContent_Packet, InstallModulePacket, etc.). Concurrently, oRAT droppers packaged as an Electron MiMi chat app and a macOS DMG carry AES-GCM-encrypted Go configurations enabling gateway or traffic-forwarder modes and expose HTTP(S)/QUIC routes (e.g., GET/POST /agent/info, /agent/upload) for direct code execution. This multivector, multiplatform campaign highlights the critical need to monitor anomalous DLL load behavior, bitmap steganography, flawed RC4/AES-GCM decryption routines and custom UDP or HTTP traffic on gambling infrastructures.
retrieved_context.title: New APT Group Earth Berberoka Targets Gambling Websites With Old and New Malware | Trend Micro (US)

retrieved_context.text: New research reveals that over 80,000 Hikvision cameras worldwide remain unpatched against the critical CVE-2021-36260 command-injection flaw (NIST score 9.8/10) disclosed last fall, allowing remote code execution and potential espionage by state-linked groups such as MISSION2025/APT41, APT10 and unknown Russian actors trading stolen credentials on dark-web forums; systemic deficiencies—default or hardcoded passwords, no auto-update mechanism, poor forensics and lack of security-by-design—have left devices in 100+ countries (including the U.S., despite an FCC “unacceptable risk” designation) continuously discoverable via Shodan or Censys and ripe for exploitation, underscoring the urgent need for organizations to inventory IoT assets, change default credentials, deploy available patches and improve visibility and update processes to mitigate geopolitical and operational impact.
retrieved_context.title: Cybercriminals Are Selling Access to Chinese Surveillance Cameras | Threatpost

retrieved_context.text: Microsoft has traced a stealthy espionage campaign by Flax Typhoon (aka Ethereal Panda), a China-based nation-state actor active since mid-2021, targeting dozens of Taiwanese organizations (with spill-over in Southeast Asia, North America, and Africa) by exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing VPN, web, Java, and SQL services to deploy the China Chopper web shell for initial access; the group escalates privileges via open-source exploits like Juicy Potato and BadPotato, then establishes persistence by disabling RDP network-level authentication, hijacking the Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) binary to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM, and installing a renamed SoftEther VPN-over-HTTPS bridge (conhost.exe/dllhost.exe) as a service to maintain covert C2 over port 443; leveraging LOLBins such as PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin, WinRM, and WMIC for lateral movement, vulnerability scanning, and remote execution, it harvests credentials from LSASS memory and the SAM registry hive using Mimikatz for pass-the-hash attacks; although no exfiltration or final objectives have been observed, organizations are urged to enforce rigorous patch and vulnerability management on internet-exposed systems, monitor registry and file-integrity changes, deploy web application firewalls, reset compromised credentials, isolate and forensically examine affected hosts, and leverage detections in Microsoft 365 Defender to disrupt living-off-the-land tactics.

canonical_entities: deployed a webshell on the router’s web server
Credentials from Password Stores: Security Account Manager
retrieved_context.text: Dragos researchers, in collaboration with Ukraine’s CSSC, unearthed FrostyGoop—an ICS-specific malware first spotted in April and used in January to disrupt central heating in over 600 Lviv apartment buildings—marking the first known malware to leverage Modbus TCP for read/write operations on operational technology. Attackers gained initial access in April 2023 by exploiting a MikroTik router vulnerability, deployed a webshell on the router’s web server, and maintained persistence via Tor and L2TP tunnels to Moscow-based IPs. After spending months conducting reconnaissance, they extracted credentials by dumping the SAM registry hive in December, then directly issued scripted Modbus commands—read from a JSON configuration file—to publicly exposed ENCO heating controllers, even downgrading firmware to disable monitoring and force inaccurate measurements that halted heating services for nearly two days amid subzero temperatures. This incident underscores the threat posed by internet-exposed ICS devices—over 46,000 globally using Modbus—and highlights poor network segmentation, unpatched ICS CVEs, and the ease with which FrostyGoop’s protocol-agnostic payload can be repurposed against diverse industrial controllers, necessitating immediate network segmentation, firmware monitoring, and patch management in OT environments.
retrieved_context.title: ICS malware FrostyGoop disrupted heating in Ukraine, remains threat to OT worldwide

retrieved_context.text: Since its emergence in 2013, Iran-linked APT35 (aka Charming Kitten/Phosphorus) has executed a series of high-value espionage campaigns—beginning with a 2014 social-media spying operation—and continued in 2019 with spear-phishing against U.S., French and Middle East academic institutions before Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit seized control of 99 APT35 domains; in late 2020 the group targeted oncology, genetics and neurology researchers in Israel and the U.S. via its “BadBlood” PDF-based spear-phishing campaign, while in 2021 it chained Exchange Server flaws (ProxyShell) for network intrusion and demonstrated TTP overlaps with Momento ransomware (CVE-2021-21972 exploiter); in January 2022 it performed mass Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) scans—over 80 percent of attempts originated in the U.S.—and later deployed a stealthy .NET-based PowerShell backdoor (“PowerLess”) that runs in-process to avoid detection, followed by Hyperscrape, a Windows .NET mailbox exfiltration tool for Outlook, Gmail and Yahoo! that quietly harvests emails once the actor possesses valid credentials or session cookies, and a companion Telegram dump utility; APT35 maintains persistence for intelligence collection or monetizes access when systems lack strategic value, underscoring the need for timely patching, multi-factor authentication and continuous monitoring.

hits.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
hits.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

hits.text: Between March and July 2025, DPRK-linked Kimsuky operators executed at least 19 highly tailored spear-phishing attacks against Western, Central, Eastern and Southern European embassies in Seoul, spoofing real diplomats and embedding password-protected ZIPs delivered via Dropbox, Daum or Google Drive. Victims unwittingly launched malicious .LNK shortcuts that triggered obfuscated PowerShell scripts to decode and in-memory execute a Confuser-Core-obfuscated XenoRAT (MoonPeak) payload—identified by GUID 12DE1212-167D-45BA-1284-780DA98CF901 and mutex “Dansweit_Hk65-PSAccerdle”—leveraging scheduled tasks for persistence. Reconnaissance data (OS build, IP, process list) was exfiltrated as base64-encoded text files over HTTPS to the attackers’ private GitHub repo via the Contents API, while C2 instructions (e.g., onf.txt) directed dynamic payload rotations hosted on Dropbox with rapid header-fix GZIP routines. This ongoing campaign provided full system control—including keystroke logging, screenshots and remote shells—and underscores the need to monitor abnormal GitHub API usage, cloud-based archive downloads and anomalous PowerShell invocations.
hits.title: The Coordinated Embassy Hunt: Unmasking the DPRK-linked GitHub C2 Espionage Campaign

hits.text: In July 2023 researchers uncovered a financially motivated threat actor deploying a multi-stage, in-memory “PS1Bot” campaign via malvertising: users are lured by compromised ad networks to hidden URLs that host obfuscated JavaScript, which in turn downloads a first-stage PowerShell loader employing double Base64 and AES encryption; this loader dynamically injects a second-stage PS1Bot payload directly into memory (leveraging techniques T1059.001 and T1055) without touching disk, establishes HTTPS-encrypted C2 channels, harvests system and user credentials, and awaits command-and-control instructions for data exfiltration and potential secondary payloads; over 500 retail and financial sector endpoints across North America and Europe were impacted, with exfiltrated metadata indicating ties to a known cybercrime group; actionable defenses include enabling AMSI and EDR memory scanning, blocking identified malvert domains, enforcing signed PowerShell scripts, and deploying ad-blockers and script-filtering proxies to disrupt the initial infection vector.
hits.title: New PS1Bot Malware Campaign Uses Malvertising to Deploy Multi-Stage In-Memory Attacks

hits.text: In February 2022, CISA, the FBI, US Cyber Command CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA issued a joint advisory on Iranian Ministry of Intelligence–linked APT MuddyWater (aka MERCURY, Earth Vetala, Static Kitten, Seedworm, TEMP.Zagros), active since 2018 and focused on cyber espionage, intellectual property theft and ransomware against defense, oil & gas, government and telecom sectors across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America. Exploiting publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and open-source tools, MuddyWater delivers malicious PDFs with embedded links that display error messages prompting users to download Excel maldocs or Windows executables; these files host VBA macros that drop WSF scripts to execute PowerShell and VB payloads, leverage LoLBins, and stage RATs and malware families including PowGoop, Canopy, Small Sieve, POWERSTATS and Mori while communicating with C2 over HTTP and DNS and persisting via Registry Run keys. Cisco Talos observed regional campaigns in Turkey (Nov 2021), Pakistan (Aug 2021) and Armenia (Jun 2021) using decoy documents, signaling tokens and a consistent TTP set, suggesting a conglomerate of subgroups migrating techniques across regions. The resultant network access and data exfiltration underscore the imperative for proactive DFIR readiness, deployment of XDR/MDR platforms, rigorous vulnerability management, macro execution restrictions, PowerShell/LoLBin monitoring and ongoing user awareness training reinforced by incident response tabletop exercises.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at Iranian APT "MuddyWater"

hits.text: Russia’s APT29 (aka Cozy Bear/Nobelium) has been exploiting a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in JetBrains TeamCity (CVE-2023-42793, CVSS 9.8) since September—shortly after JetBrains issued a patch and Rapid7 published a proof-of-concept—to gain initial access to SDLC management servers, escalate privileges, move laterally, deploy stealthy backdoors that persist through updates, and potentially manipulate build pipelines or insert malicious updates in SolarWinds-style supply-chain attacks; CISA, FBI, NSA and international partners warn that around 800 internet-exposed instances remain vulnerable (with uncounted internally reachable servers also at risk), and that North Korea’s Lazarus and Andariel groups have similarly weaponized the same flaw, prompting Fortinet to report multi-actor post-exploit techniques in live incidents; mitigation guidance urges immediate upgrading to TeamCity 2023.05.4, removal of public exposure, comprehensive IoC-based threat hunting across servers and build agents, and full compromise assessments to eradicate entrenched backdoors.
hits.title: Global TeamCity Exploitation Opens Door to SolarWinds-Style Nightmare

hits.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
hits.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.

canonical_entities: spear-phishing attacks against European embassies in Seoul (March–July 2025)
exfiltrated ... over HTTPS to the attackers’ private GitHub repo via the Contents API
retrieved_context.text: Between March and July 2025, DPRK-linked Kimsuky operators executed at least 19 highly tailored spear-phishing attacks against Western, Central, Eastern and Southern European embassies in Seoul, spoofing real diplomats and embedding password-protected ZIPs delivered via Dropbox, Daum or Google Drive. Victims unwittingly launched malicious .LNK shortcuts that triggered obfuscated PowerShell scripts to decode and in-memory execute a Confuser-Core-obfuscated XenoRAT (MoonPeak) payload—identified by GUID 12DE1212-167D-45BA-1284-780DA98CF901 and mutex “Dansweit_Hk65-PSAccerdle”—leveraging scheduled tasks for persistence. Reconnaissance data (OS build, IP, process list) was exfiltrated as base64-encoded text files over HTTPS to the attackers’ private GitHub repo via the Contents API, while C2 instructions (e.g., onf.txt) directed dynamic payload rotations hosted on Dropbox with rapid header-fix GZIP routines. This ongoing campaign provided full system control—including keystroke logging, screenshots and remote shells—and underscores the need to monitor abnormal GitHub API usage, cloud-based archive downloads and anomalous PowerShell invocations.
retrieved_context.title: The Coordinated Embassy Hunt: Unmasking the DPRK-linked GitHub C2 Espionage Campaign

retrieved_context.text: In July 2023 researchers uncovered a financially motivated threat actor deploying a multi-stage, in-memory “PS1Bot” campaign via malvertising: users are lured by compromised ad networks to hidden URLs that host obfuscated JavaScript, which in turn downloads a first-stage PowerShell loader employing double Base64 and AES encryption; this loader dynamically injects a second-stage PS1Bot payload directly into memory (leveraging techniques T1059.001 and T1055) without touching disk, establishes HTTPS-encrypted C2 channels, harvests system and user credentials, and awaits command-and-control instructions for data exfiltration and potential secondary payloads; over 500 retail and financial sector endpoints across North America and Europe were impacted, with exfiltrated metadata indicating ties to a known cybercrime group; actionable defenses include enabling AMSI and EDR memory scanning, blocking identified malvert domains, enforcing signed PowerShell scripts, and deploying ad-blockers and script-filtering proxies to disrupt the initial infection vector.
retrieved_context.title: New PS1Bot Malware Campaign Uses Malvertising to Deploy Multi-Stage In-Memory Attacks

retrieved_context.text: In February 2022, CISA, the FBI, US Cyber Command CNMF, NCSC-UK and NSA issued a joint advisory on Iranian Ministry of Intelligence–linked APT MuddyWater (aka MERCURY, Earth Vetala, Static Kitten, Seedworm, TEMP.Zagros), active since 2018 and focused on cyber espionage, intellectual property theft and ransomware against defense, oil & gas, government and telecom sectors across Asia, Africa, Europe and North America. Exploiting publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and open-source tools, MuddyWater delivers malicious PDFs with embedded links that display error messages prompting users to download Excel maldocs or Windows executables; these files host VBA macros that drop WSF scripts to execute PowerShell and VB payloads, leverage LoLBins, and stage RATs and malware families including PowGoop, Canopy, Small Sieve, POWERSTATS and Mori while communicating with C2 over HTTP and DNS and persisting via Registry Run keys. Cisco Talos observed regional campaigns in Turkey (Nov 2021), Pakistan (Aug 2021) and Armenia (Jun 2021) using decoy documents, signaling tokens and a consistent TTP set, suggesting a conglomerate of subgroups migrating techniques across regions. The resultant network access and data exfiltration underscore the imperative for proactive DFIR readiness, deployment of XDR/MDR platforms, rigorous vulnerability management, macro execution restrictions, PowerShell/LoLBin monitoring and ongoing user awareness training reinforced by incident response tabletop exercises.
retrieved_context.title: An In-Depth Look at Iranian APT "MuddyWater"

retrieved_context.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
retrieved_context.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

retrieved_context.text: Russia’s APT29 (aka Cozy Bear/Nobelium) has been exploiting a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in JetBrains TeamCity (CVE-2023-42793, CVSS 9.8) since September—shortly after JetBrains issued a patch and Rapid7 published a proof-of-concept—to gain initial access to SDLC management servers, escalate privileges, move laterally, deploy stealthy backdoors that persist through updates, and potentially manipulate build pipelines or insert malicious updates in SolarWinds-style supply-chain attacks; CISA, FBI, NSA and international partners warn that around 800 internet-exposed instances remain vulnerable (with uncounted internally reachable servers also at risk), and that North Korea’s Lazarus and Andariel groups have similarly weaponized the same flaw, prompting Fortinet to report multi-actor post-exploit techniques in live incidents; mitigation guidance urges immediate upgrading to TeamCity 2023.05.4, removal of public exposure, comprehensive IoC-based threat hunting across servers and build agents, and full compromise assessments to eradicate entrenched backdoors.
retrieved_context.title: Global TeamCity Exploitation Opens Door to SolarWinds-Style Nightmare

canonical_entities: bypasses the Mark of the Web
attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes
retrieved_context.text: Microsoft’s August 2023 Patch Tuesday addressed two actively exploited zero-days—CVE-2023-36884, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Office that bypasses the Mark of the Web, and CVE-2023-38180, a .NET/Visual Studio vulnerability enabling DDoS attacks without requiring user privileges—after one was publicly disclosed pre-patch. The Russian actor Storm-0978 (aka RomCom/Underground), noted for Industrial Spy ransomware, leveraged crafted Office documents to execute payloads and extort victims, while CVE-2023-38180 attacks demand only network proximity. To mitigate these threats, Microsoft released an Office Defense-in-Depth update and a .NET/Visual Studio patch and recommends deploying both Office and Windows August updates, enabling cloud-delivered protection in Defender Antivirus, activating EDR block mode, enforcing attack surface reduction rules to block Office-spawned child processes, and applying the advisory’s update for CVE-2023-38180. Avertium validates these controls, provides IoCs for RomCom campaigns, and advocates continuous vulnerability management and its Fusion MXDR for Microsoft service to detect suspicious Office-to-script execution chains and remediate artifacts proactively.
retrieved_context.title: Flash Notice: Two Microsoft Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited by Attackers

hits.text: Since early 2025, a sophisticated threat actor has deployed PS1Bot, a multi-stage PowerShell/C# malware framework distributed via malvertising and SEO-poisoned archives named to resemble legitimate documents (e.g., “chapter 8 medicare benefit policy manual.zip”), which drops an obfuscated VBScript downloader (“FULL DOCUMENT.js”) that retrieves a JScript scriptlet to write and execute a PowerShell loader (e.g., ntu.ps1) from C:\ProgramData\; this loader polls a C2—deriving unique URLs from the C-drive serial number—and uses Invoke-Expression to run in-memory modules with minimal disk footprints. PS1Bot’s modular toolkit includes a WMI-based antivirus reconnaissance module, a dynamic C# screen-capture module exfiltrating Base64‐encoded bitmaps, a “grabber” that harvests browser and 40+ crypto wallet credentials (including MetaMask, Ledger, Exodus, Electrum) using embedded multilingual seed-phrase wordlists, a SetWindowsHookEx keylogger, and a WMIComputerCSHARP system survey. Persistence is achieved via randomized %PROGRAMDATA% directories, LNK startup shortcuts, and mutex checks. Cisco Talos notes overlaps with AHK Bot and Skitnet infrastructures and reports rapid evolution with undisclosed modules poised for espionage, financial theft, and lateral movement. Organizations should monitor anomalous PowerShell execution, unexpected WMI queries, and malvertising indicators to detect and disrupt this ongoing campaign.
hits.title: PS1Bot: Multi-Stage Malware Framework Targeting Windows Systems

hits.text: After a year-long investigation researchers at Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs dissected the Ngioweb botnet—first observed in 2017—which uses a loader network and roughly 15 n-day exploits to deploy malware that contacts C2 domains generated via a domain generation algorithm (augmented by DNS TXT records to resist sinkholing), evaluates device traffic capacity, and links compromised Zyxel, Reolink, Alpha Technologies and, increasingly, Netgear routers (now 10 % of bots) to over 180 “backconnect” C2 nodes that provide at least 80 % of the 35,000 residential proxies in the NSOCKS[.]net service across 180 countries; NSOCKS’s lack of authentication and appearance on free proxy lists has enabled cybercriminals to carry out DDoS amplification, credential stuffing, phishing and malware proxying (e.g., Agent Tesla), while APT28 state-sponsored actors have mixed espionage with criminal traffic on the same infrastructure. To disrupt both operations, Lumen, alongside The ShadowServer Foundation and other partners, is actively blocking traffic to known C2 nodes and publishing indicators of compromise to help organizations identify and remediate infected devices.
hits.title: Botnet fueling residential proxies disrupted in cybercrime crackdown

canonical_entities: Remote Code Execution via ms-msdt URI in Word/RTF documents
ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents
hits.text: In late May 2022, Symantec identified multiple threat actors exploiting the MSDT Follina bug (CVE-2022-30190) through ms-msdt URI-based RCE in Word/RTF documents that load a malicious HTML via Word’s remote template feature to launch msdt.exe, sdiagnhost.exe and ultimately PowerShell—bypassing the need for macros—to install a digitally signed AsyncRAT remote access Trojan that performs anti-analysis checks, collects hardware IDs, user names, execution paths and OS details, and maintains C&C communications, alongside parallel deployments of a browser infostealer targeting cookies and saved credentials in Firefox, Chrome and Edge. Symantec customers should apply Microsoft’s advisories or disable the ms-msdt handler, update Symantec Endpoint definitions (File-based-Downloader-Backdoor:Async, InfoStealer) and monitor for related IOCs to thwart these rapid, damaging campaigns.
hits.title: Attackers Exploit MSDT Follina Bug to Drop RAT, Infostealer | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

canonical_entities: Launch EC2 instances across regions via VPN
hits.text: Unit42’s “EleKtra-Leak” campaign, active since December 2020, uses automated scripts to clone public GitHub repos every few minutes, extract exposed AWS IAM keys within five minutes, then—if not blocked by GitHub-AWS quarantine policies—execute rapid AWS reconnaissance (DescribeRegions), create security groups, and launch hundreds of EC2 instances across regions via VPN for Monero cryptojacking, generating over 400 API calls in seven minutes. Between Aug. 30 and Oct. 6, 2023, researchers tracked 474 actor-controlled miners. The actor employs custom mining software and blocklists high-profile AWS account IDs to avoid honey traps. Leveraging the Prisma Cloud HoneyCloud project’s ephemeral key leaks and policy overrides, Unit42 obtained full visibility, informing Prisma Cloud Secrets Security, CI/CD IaC scanning, Cortex XDR, and recommendations for independent repo scanning, strict IAM policies, and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

canonical_entities: Session token extraction from device memory
extract session tokens from device memory
exposed 35,879,455 customers’ usernames, hashed passwords, names, contact details, last four SSN digits, dates of birth and security Q&A
hits.text: Since at least August 2023, threat actors have exploited CVE-2023-4966 (CitrixBleed), a 7.5-rated flaw in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway, culminating in an October 16–19 breach at Comcast Xfinity that exposed 35,879,455 customers’ usernames, hashed passwords, names, contact details, last four SSN digits, dates of birth and security Q&A; despite Citrix’s October 10 patch and Comcast’s claim of prompt mitigation, attackers used publicly available proofs-of-concept and rumored Python automation scripts to extract session tokens from device memory, hijack active sessions and bypass authentication, a tactic linked by ReliaQuest to at least five threat groups including LockBit; this incident highlights the necessity not only of timely patching and reboots but also of invalidating all active and persistent session tokens, enforcing multi-factor authentication, resetting credentials and maintaining continuous 24x7 monitoring to prevent further data exfiltration and ransomware deployment.
hits.title: Comcast Xfinity Breached via CitrixBleed; 35M Customers Affected

hits.text: The North Korea-linked threat actor Slow Pisces (also tracked as Jade Sleet, PUKCHONG, TraderTraitor, and UNC4899) has been conducting a multi-stage malware campaign targeting cryptocurrency developers via LinkedIn job opportunity lures since at least June 2024, leveraging trojanized Python and JavaScript projects hosted on GitHub that employ YAML deserialization and EJS templating to execute gated payloads only to validated targets meeting specific criteria (IP address, geolocation, time, HTTP headers); the campaign delivers RN Loader and RN Stealer malware on macOS systems capable of harvesting system metadata, installed applications, SSH keys, AWS/Kubernetes/Google Cloud configuration files, and iCloud Keychain data, with payloads remaining memory-resident and deployed selectively to prevent analysis; Slow Pisces is assessed to be responsible for the February 2025 Bybit cryptocurrency exchange breach and operates alongside other North Korean clusters including Operation Dream Job, Contagious Interview, Alluring Pisces, and Moonstone Sleet, though with notably superior operational security practices involving heavily guarded payload delivery across infection stages.
hits.title: Crypto Developers Targeted by Python Malware Disguised as Coding Challenges

hits.text: During a recent incident, a LockBit affiliate conducted initial intrusions using gpresult for policy dumping, Cobalt Strike loaders and PsExec for privilege escalation, followed by reconnaissance (whoami, netstat, quser, net view), lateral movement, persistence via a new user account, and data exfiltration over FTP with Wput; when deployment of LockBit (SHA256 079b99f6…) was blocked on the target network, the attacker pivoted to a newly observed Rust-written ransomware family dubbed 3AM (SHA256 307a1217…), which appends “.threeamtime” to encrypted files, stops over 100 security and backup services via net stop and wbadmin/bcdedit/wmic commands, deletes Volume Shadow copies with vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet, and drops a Tor‐accessible ransom note requiring a 32-character “-k” access key and offering decryption/mystical-themed extortion; although 3AM encryption succeeded on only one of three attempted hosts, its Conti-style “-m” (local/net) and “-h” parameters, heavy service-termination payload, and aggressive VSS wipe underscore its potential as a fallback vector—defenders should update Symantec/Broadcom signatures, monitor for the .threeamtime extension, suspicious Rust binaries, command-line flags “-k” and “-m”, and mass service stoppage activity, and block associated IOCs (185.202.0[.]111, 212.18.104[.]6, 85.159.229[.]62) to mitigate future 3AM use.
hits.title: 3AM: New Ransomware Family Used As Fallback in Failed LockBit Attack | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Symantec’s Threat Hunter Team has linked the newly discovered Sidewalk loader backdoor—an evolution of the Crosswalk/Backdoor.Motnug family—to Grayfly (aka GREF/Wicked Panda), a China-linked espionage group active since March 2017 that employs custom backdoors, Trojan.Chattak, Cobalt Strike, web shells and credential-dumpers against telecom, IT, media and finance targets in Taiwan, Vietnam, the US and Mexico; in a recent campaign they exploited public-facing Microsoft Exchange and MySQL servers via commodity and zero-day flaws to execute Base64-encoded PowerShell commands through certutil, install an ASPX web shell in the ClientAccess\ecp directory, deploy Sidewalk via installutil.exe, create persistence with WMIC-launched scheduled tasks, then run a custom Mimikatz variant (SHA256 b3eb783b017da32e33d19670b39eae0b11de8e983891dd4feb873d6e9333608d) to harvest credentials—all within about an hour before ceasing observable activity; three Chengdu 404 executives were indicted in 2020 for attacks on over 100 organizations, highlighting Grayfly’s persistence and underscoring the need to promptly patch Exchange and MySQL servers, monitor anomalous PowerShell and scheduled-task activity, and deploy IOC-based detection to block Sidewalk and related tools.
hits.title: Grayfly: Chinese Threat Actor Uses Newly-discovered Sidewalk Malware | Symantec Enterprise Blogs

hits.text: Our GReAT team uncovered Operation ForumTroll—a state-sponsored APT campaign targeting Russian media, academic and government personnel—delivering previously unknown malware via phishing emails masquerading as Primakov Readings invitations containing two malicious links; clicking either on a Windows PC using Chrome or any Chromium-based browser silently triggers a zero-day exploit (CVE-2025-2783), exploiting a logic flaw at the Chrome-Windows interface to bypass the browser’s sandbox and deploy the payload without further user interaction. We promptly reported the vulnerability to Google, which released a patch in Chrome version 134.0.6998.177/178; while the phishing links now redirect to the legitimate forum site and the campaign is dormant, the attackers could reactivate it at any time. To mitigate this espionage threat, organizations should ensure all Chrome instances are updated to at least 134.0.6998.177/.178, deploy robust exploit detection and prevention solutions on internet-connected devices, and maintain vigilant phishing awareness and monitoring.
hits.title: CVE-2025-2783 in Operation ForumTroll APT

canonical_entities: diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine
hits.text: Secret Blizzard, the Russian FSB’s Center 16, has escalated global espionage by co-opting C2 infrastructures of at least six threat actors—including Pakistan-based Storm-0156, Hazel Sandstorm and Storm-0473—to install backdoors (CrimsonRAT, Wainscot), deploy custom payloads (TwoDash downloader, MiniPocket fetcher), a TinyTurla variant disguised as a Windows service, and the Statuezy clipboard-monitoring trojan via DLL sideloading and batch files; this cross-actor compromise secured persistent access to diplomatic and defense networks in Ukraine, Afghanistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and GDI, and Indian military institutions, enabling exfiltration of politically sensitive intelligence and advanced research data while reducing development overhead and underscoring the need for robust supply-chain security, network segmentation and proactive vulnerability management.
hits.title: Hackers with Russian Blizzard Steal Data from Rival Networks

hits.text: In August 2025 Microsoft Threat Intelligence revealed that Storm-2460, associated with the Play ransomware group, has resumed exploiting CVE-2025-29824—a zero-day elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Common Log File System patched in April—to gain SYSTEM privileges on unpatched hosts across IT, financial and real estate organizations in the US, Europe, South America and the Middle East. The campaign begins with an in-memory dropper masquerading as the open-source ChatGPT Desktop app that decrypts and launches PipeMagic, a modular backdoor first observed in December 2022 and now updated with persistence and lateral-movement enhancements targeting Saudi Arabian and Brazilian manufacturing entities. PipeMagic communicates with its TCP C2 over a named pipe, self-updates by storing distinct payload modules in memory via doubly linked lists for staging, execution and communication (plus an additional dynamic list), then leverages the CLFS exploit to escalate privileges before deploying Play ransomware. Although the campaign’s footprint remains limited, the combination of a zero-day exploit and a sophisticated modular backdoor underscores a heightened risk; organizations are urged to immediately apply the April patch for CVE-2025-29824, enable tamper and network protection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, run EDR in block mode, enforce full automated investigation and remediation, and leverage cloud-delivered machine-learning protections to block novel variants.
hits.title: PipeMagic Backdoor Resurfaces as Part of Play Ransomware Attack Chain

hits.text: In April 2025, Microsoft patched 121 vulnerabilities—including CVE-2025-29824, the sole flaw exploited by PipeMagic—an evolution of a backdoor first spotted in December 2022 during a RansomExx campaign against Southeast Asian industrial firms via CVE-2017-0144 and resurfaced in September 2024 in the Middle East using a Rust-based fake ChatGPT loader (Tauri/Tokio) that decrypts AES-encrypted shellcode, resolves APIs via FNV-1a hashing, relocates imports and invokes its entry point. PipeMagic generates random 16-byte named pipes (“\\.\\pipe\\1.<hex>”) alongside a 127.0.0.1:8082 TCP interface, downloads plugins from a Cloud Azure domain (aaaaabbbbbbb.eastus.cloudapp.azure[.]com) and supports modules such as an I/O-completion-port communication plugin (handling file I/O commands) and a loader for injecting 64-bit payloads via DllRegisterService. In January 2025, new campaigns in Brazil and the Middle East introduced a Microsoft Help Index File loader executed through MSBuild that RC4-decrypts shellcode (key 4829468622e6b82ff056e3c945dd99c94a1f0264d980774828aadda326b775e5) via EnumDeviceMonitor and a GoogleUpdate.dll hijack variant performing AES-CBC decryption (key 9C3BA5B2D3222FE5863C14D51340D7F9, IV 221BA50915042098AF5F8EE40E5559C8) to deploy the same 32-bit backdoor PE. Joint analysis with BI.ZONE reveals a shift toward multi-staged, encrypted loaders and diversified access vectors, underscoring the need to restrict MSBuild use, monitor DLL hijacking, inspect named-pipe and localhost traffic, and block suspicious Azure domains to mitigate PipeMagic’s adaptive tactics.
hits.title: PipeMagic in 2025: How the backdoor operators’ tactics have changed

canonical_entities: installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry
hits.text: The Lotus Blossom APT (aka Lotus Panda, Billbug, Spring Dragon) has stepped up cyberespionage against APAC government targets by deploying new Sagerunex backdoor variants and abusing Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) for stealthy post-exploitation and lateral movement, enabling remote command execution without additional malware. Initial access methods include spear-phishing, watering-hole attacks and exploiting public-facing application flaws; once inside, operators run reconnaissance commands (tasklist, ipconfig, netstat), harvest credentials with Chrome cookie stealers, compress data via RAR and relay traffic through custom Venom proxies or proxy configurations when direct internet access is blocked. Persistence is achieved by installing Sagerunex variants in the Windows Registry under hijacked service names (tapisrv, swprv) to auto-launch at startup, while command-and-control blends encrypted traffic into legitimate platforms—stolen data uploaded as .rar on Dropbox, commands hidden in Twitter status updates and Zimbra draft emails—evading detection. Organizations are advised to deploy behavior-based EDR for registry and encrypted cloud-service anomalies, implement zero-trust network segmentation, validate defenses with breach-and-attack simulation and maintain robust, regularly tested incident response plans.
hits.title: Lotus Blossom APT Exploits WMI for Post-Exploitation Activities

hits.text: Since its emergence in 2013, Iran-linked APT35 (aka Charming Kitten/Phosphorus) has executed a series of high-value espionage campaigns—beginning with a 2014 social-media spying operation—and continued in 2019 with spear-phishing against U.S., French and Middle East academic institutions before Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit seized control of 99 APT35 domains; in late 2020 the group targeted oncology, genetics and neurology researchers in Israel and the U.S. via its “BadBlood” PDF-based spear-phishing campaign, while in 2021 it chained Exchange Server flaws (ProxyShell) for network intrusion and demonstrated TTP overlaps with Momento ransomware (CVE-2021-21972 exploiter); in January 2022 it performed mass Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) scans—over 80 percent of attempts originated in the U.S.—and later deployed a stealthy .NET-based PowerShell backdoor (“PowerLess”) that runs in-process to avoid detection, followed by Hyperscrape, a Windows .NET mailbox exfiltration tool for Outlook, Gmail and Yahoo! that quietly harvests emails once the actor possesses valid credentials or session cookies, and a companion Telegram dump utility; APT35 maintains persistence for intelligence collection or monetizes access when systems lack strategic value, underscoring the need for timely patching, multi-factor authentication and continuous monitoring.
hits.title: An In-Depth Look at APT35 aka Charming Kitten

canonical_entities: enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials
Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs
hits.text: Aqua Security’s Nautilus team has uncovered Hadooken, a new Linux malware targeting Oracle WebLogic servers via weak passwords. Post-compromise, attackers deploy redundant shell and Python scripts to ensure download and execution of Hadooken, which enumerates SSH directories to harvest credentials, moves laterally, and clears logs. Hadooken then drops a three-path cryptominer and a Tsunami backdoor with a randomized name, the latter reserved for potential later-stage attacks. Persistence is achieved through multiple cronjobs under varied names and frequencies stored across cron directories. The malware is hosted on two IPs—one German address linked to TeamTNT and Gang 8220, the other inactive in Russia—where researchers also identified a Mallox ransomware PowerShell loader targeting Windows. Static analysis links Hadooken to Rhombus and NoEscape families. With over 230,000 internet-connected WebLogic instances—hundreds of which expose vulnerable admin consoles—this campaign underscores the dual risk of cryptojacking and ransomware across Linux and Windows environments.
hits.title: New 'Hadooken' Linux Malware Targets WebLogic Servers - SecurityWeek

hits.text: ESET researchers disclosed MoustachedBouncer, a Belarus-aligned cyberespionage group active since at least 2014 targeting foreign embassies in Belarus, employing two parallel malware frameworks: the email-based NightClub (SMTP/IMAP C2) and its 2020-onward successor Disco (Go/.NET) delivered via adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) at ISP level—likely leveraging Belarus’s SORM lawful interception—to redirect Windows captive portal checks to a fake Windows Update page. This page loads jdrop.js to prompt a malicious installer, which schedules SMB-delivered OfficeBroker payloads from attacker-injected Google Cloud IPs. Both frameworks support plugins for screenshots, audio recording and file theft. ESET observed compromises of embassies from four continents and assesses medium confidence in state alignment and low confidence in cooperation with Winter Vivern. Recommendations include out-of-band encrypted VPNs to thwart ISP-level interception.
hits.title: MoustachedBouncer: Espionage against foreign diplomats in Belarus

hits.text: Microsoft’s research exposes the BadPilot campaign—a multiyear initial-access subgroup of Russian GRU-aligned Seashell Blizzard active since at least 2021—that has opportunistically scanned for and exploited Internet-facing vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34473 Exchange, CVE-2022-41352 Zimbra, CVE-2023-32315 OpenFire, CVE-2023-42793 TeamCity, CVE-2023-23397 Outlook, CVE-2024-1709 ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CVE-2023-48788 FortiClient EMS and various JBOSS flaws) to compromise a globally diverse set of high-value sectors (energy, oil and gas, telecommunications, shipping, arms manufacturing and government). Following initial access, BadPilot employs stealthy persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and common tools such as Cobalt Strike and DarkCrystalRAT to sustain footholds and support tailored network operations, including at least three destructive cyberattacks in Ukraine since 2023. After focusing on Ukraine, Europe, Central/South Asia and the Middle East during 2021–2023, the subgroup scaled horizontally into the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia in early 2024, reflecting Russia’s evolving strategic objectives and underscoring the urgency of patching Internet-facing services, implementing comprehensive logging and anomaly detection, and applying threat-informed incident-response practices to disrupt its operational lifecycle.
hits.title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since at least April 2024 Microsoft Threat Intelligence has tracked a Russia-affiliated cyberespionage actor dubbed Void Blizzard (aka LAUNDRY BEAR) conducting high-volume, targeted operations against government, defense, transportation, media, NGO and healthcare organizations—particularly in NATO member states and Ukraine—by leveraging stolen credentials procured via commodity infostealer ecosystems for password spray attacks and Exchange/SharePoint Online access, then automating bulk email and file collection (and in some cases Teams messages) via cloud APIs and tools like AzureHound; in April 2025 the actor evolved to adversary-in-the-middle spear phishing using a typosquatted domain and the open-source Evilginx framework with a malicious QR-coded PDF to harvest Entra authentication data; this widespread success underscores that even unsophisticated TTPs pose major intelligence risks to critical sectors, so organizations should enforce sign-in risk policies and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO/passkeys), centralize identity management with Conditional Access, monitor risky sign-ins and mailbox auditing, apply least-privilege credential hygiene, and promptly rotate credentials after infostealer detections to disrupt Void Blizzard’s operations.
hits.title: New Russia-affiliated actor Void Blizzard targets critical sectors for espionage | Microsoft Security Blog

hits.text: Since April 2024, the Russia-affiliated threat actor Void Blizzard (aka Laundry Bear) has targeted over 20 NGOs and multiple government, defense, transportation, media and healthcare organizations across NATO member states, Western Europe, North America and Ukraine, initially leveraging password spraying and stolen credentials—likely purchased from cybercrime marketplaces—to access Exchange and SharePoint Online, enumerate Microsoft Entra ID via AzureHound, and exfiltrate large volumes of emails and files. More recently, the group shifted to adversary-in-the-middle spear-phishing using a typosquatted “micsrosoftonline[.]com” domain and an Evilginx-based phishing page delivered through malicious QR codes in forged European Defense and Security Summit PDF invitations, automating bulk data collection via Exchange, Microsoft Graph and Teams web client. Overlaps with Forest Blizzard, Midnight Blizzard and Secret Blizzard indicate coordinated Russian strategic espionage, and a September 2024 pass-the-cookie breach of a Dutch police account underscores their evolving cookie-theft capabilities—highlighting urgent needs for phishing-resistant MFA and hardened Entra ID configurations.
hits.title: Russian Hackers Breach 20+ NGOs Using Evilginx Phishing via Fake Microsoft Entra Pages

hits.text: Last week Google’s Threat Analysis Group, in partnership with The Citizen Lab, exposed an in-the-wild exploit chain developed by the commercial surveillance vendor Intellexa in Egypt that leverages a man-in-the-middle injection on HTTP traffic to silently redirect targets first to c.betly[.]me and then to sec-flare[.]com, delivering Predator spyware without any user interaction; on iOS this chain combined Safari RCE (CVE-2023-41993), certificate validation bypass (CVE-2023-41991) and XNU kernel local privilege escalation (CVE-2023-41992) and was patched in iOS 16.7/17.0.1, while on Android initial Chrome renderer RCE (CVE-2023-4762), delivered via MITM or one-time links, was patched on September 5; this campaign highlights the serious risk posed by proliferating commercial spyware, underscores the urgency of enforcing universal HTTPS and enabling Chrome’s HTTPS-First Mode, and demonstrates the critical need for organizations and users to apply the latest OS and browser updates, deploy encrypted-traffic protections, and monitor for anomalous network redirects to mitigate future attacks.
hits.title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt
